ps3__god-of-war-ascension.teaser: A prequel showing Kratos shortly after his family's murder, imprisoned by the Furies.

ps3__fat-princess.article:
A bizarre blend of strategy, platforming action, and team-based multiplayer fun cast players as soldiers trying to kidnap the enemy princess while feeding her cake along the way, gradually making her bigger and harder for the opposing team to carry back. Titan Studios created a playful, brightly colored world inspired by fairy-tale aesthetics, where teams of up to thirty-two players clashed in chaotic battles combining a class system of soldiers, mages, archers, and workers with base-defense elements.

The whole system is designed so that anyone can grasp it within the first minute. Roles don't change through any menu, but simply by putting on a hat at a station near your own castle, so a player can jump between healer, archer, and knight several times within a single match depending on what the team currently needs. Workers chop down trees and gather resources used to upgrade your own stations and unlock stronger class variants, while catapults can launch teammates across the entire map straight into the enemy line. The result is mayhem in which an organized team was obvious at a glance, since without cooperation between workers, healers, and an attacking wave, there was simply no way to carry the princess out of the enemy dungeon.

The concept originally began as a smaller independent project, and Sony helped bring it to completion as a full-fledged multiplayer game distributed through PlayStation Network, making it an example of a successful collaboration between a smaller studio and the publishing power of the platform. Critics praised the originality of the concept and the fun of team cooperation, which helped the game build a loyal community despite its satirically exaggerated central idea. The later expansion Fat Princess: Fistful of Cake for the PSP showed Sony's ambition to build smaller, imaginative titles as a complement to its major exclusive franchises.
ps3__fat-princess.teaser: A bizarre blend of strategy and team action; feeding the princess cake makes her bigger.

ps3__warhawk.article:
A multiplayer action shooter combining infantry combat, tanks and other ground vehicles, and aerial dogfights in Warhawk fighter craft across sprawling battlefields delivered one of the first truly large online-focused titles of the early PS3 era, supporting up to thirty-two players simultaneously across land, sea, and air. Incognito Entertainment built the game entirely around multiplayer with no traditional campaign, emphasizing teamwork between infantry calling for air support and pilots providing covering fire, creating a dynamic different from the ground shooters that dominated at the time.

The key to this was the versatility of the Warhawk fighters, which could switch between fast flight and hovering in place, so the same craft could serve as both an assault plane and a slow floating platform for precision fire into the trenches. On the ground, players captured bases, drove tanks and light vehicles equipped with anti-aircraft weapons, and fought over control points on maps that were unusually large for their time. Combat kept constantly shifting between scales: a lone soldier with a rocket launcher could tip the balance of air superiority, while a single skilled pilot could hold an entire front in check. The game was also one of the first to fully integrate voice communication through a headset included in the box, making coordination a key part of the experience.

Critics praised the variety of the battlefield and the technical execution of the aerial combat, which made Warhawk a favorite platform for community clans and tournaments for several years after release. The included headset was an unusual move at the time, underscoring Sony's emphasis on building a strong online community even before voice communication became the standard for console shooters. The game helped prove that Sony could offer online infrastructure comparable to the competition, and it paved the way for more ambitious online titles on PlayStation Network.
ps3__warhawk.teaser: Multiplayer action with no campaign; infantry battles, tanks, and aerial fighter dogfights.

ps3__motorstorm-pacific-rift.article:
The second entry in the wild off-road series moved its destructive races from a desert canyon into a lush tropical jungle full of volcanoes, waterfalls, and muddy rivers, expanding both the range of environments and the strategic possibilities when choosing between motorbikes, buggies, monster trucks, or rocket-powered ATVs. Evolution Studios improved the physics model for terrain and vehicle destruction, added more dynamic weather, and introduced volcanic activity that directly affected the race, where eruptions or flash floods could change the track quite literally beneath the racers' wheels.

The core of the gameplay remained the risky management of boost. Every vehicle overheats when boost is held too long, and the player must judge the exact moment to let go, since one extra second of acceleration means an explosion and the end of the race. The new tropical setting made this an even more interesting choice, since driving through water cools the engine and opens up room for longer bursts of speed, while hot lava stretches shorten the vehicle's patience instead. Each track also offers several separate routes suited to different vehicle types, so heavy monster trucks crush through vegetation and mud while motorbikes squeeze through narrow mountain trails and bounce off jump ramps. Visually, the game was among the most impressive titles of its time thanks to lush vegetation, particle effects for mud and water, and elaborate lighting.

Critics praised the fun brutality and the technical side of the game, with many reviewers considering Pacific Rift a more balanced and enjoyable experience than the somewhat more chaotic first entry, helped further by the ability to play split-screen with multiple players. MotorStorm: Pacific Rift cemented the series as a beloved arcade alternative to the more realistic Gran Turismo in Sony's portfolio and confirmed Evolution Studios as a respected internal studio specializing in the racing genre, before it later moved on to developing DriveClub.
ps3__motorstorm-pacific-rift.teaser: Destructive off-road racing moved from the desert to a tropical jungle full of volcanoes.

ps4__god-of-war.article:
After years of Greek fury, Kratos relocated to Norse mythology and, for the first time in the series, took on a different role than that of a god-slayer: the role of a father. After the death of his wife Faye, he sets out with his son Atreus on a journey to the highest peak of the nine realms to scatter her ashes, and what begins as a simple errand gradually becomes a journey among giants, trolls, elves, and the Norse gods themselves. Combat was completely reworked: instead of the pair of Greek blades, Kratos received the Leviathan axe, which can be recalled after being thrown, and battles are slower, more tactical, and shown from an over-the-shoulder perspective, with the camera never cutting away throughout the entire game.

The combat system isn't just slower, but built on a different logic altogether. The axe can freeze enemies, throwing the weapon leaves Kratos defenseless and reliant on his fists or shield, and his son Atreus functions as a second weapon, since his arrows interrupt enemies and open up opportunities to attack. Gradually unlocking the earlier Greek blades then gives the player two completely different fighting styles, between fast crowd-clearing strikes and heavy, precise blows. The environment is designed as a semi-open world with returns to previously inaccessible places, a central lake area, and portals to other realms, so the game combines the tight, cinematic pacing of the main story with room for optional challenges, among which the optional battles against the Valkyries stand out.

It was precisely the single unbroken shot, the intricately developed father-son relationship, and a much more personal, mature narrative that made the game one of the most acclaimed titles of its generation, helped further by the talking severed head of Mimir, who accompanies the journey with witty commentary and explanations of Norse mythology. Critics and players alike showered it with awards, including Game of the Year at the 2018 Game Awards. It sold over twenty million copies, the game defined a new standard for the cinematic action-adventure, and paved the way for the sequel Ragnarök. The enhanced PlayStation 5 version only confirmed how timeless it remains.
ps4__god-of-war.teaser: Kratos, for the first time in the role of father rather than avenger of gods; combat and camera rebuilt from scratch.

ps4__marvel-s-spider-man.article:
Insomniac Games earned the trust of Sony and Marvel to craft an original, game-first story about an experienced Spider-Man, eight years into the mask, who battles not only crime in New York but also the balance between the mask and Peter Parker's life. The main villain is Mister Negative, but the true heart of the story lies in the relationship with Mary Jane, Aunt May, and the mentorship of young Miles Morales. Traversal across the New York skyline via web-swinging ranks among the best any game has ever offered.

The entire movement system is built on webs that genuinely attach to buildings, so the player learns the rhythm of swings, wall-bounces, and the acceleration at the lowest point of the arc almost subconsciously, and after a few hours stops using fast travel altogether. Combat blends acrobatics, gadgets, and rapid target-switching in a manner reminiscent of the Batman: Arkham series, but with far nimbler dynamics, where dodging warned by spider-sense matters as much as strikes, and enemies can be tethered to surrounding objects. The open world is densely packed with side activities, research tasks, suits with unique abilities, and boss fights against Rhino, Electro, or Kingpin, while the quieter sections as Mary Jane and Miles shift the pace toward stealth and vulnerability.

The game received an enthusiastic reception, became one of PlayStation 4's best-selling exclusives, and proved that a licensed superhero game can be both artistically ambitious and mechanically flawless. Its success led to the DLC The City That Never Sleeps, the spin-off Miles Morales, and the full sequel Spider-Man 2 on PlayStation 5. Insomniac also demonstrated it could tell an original Marvel story independent of the film universe while still respecting decades of comic-book mythology. The photo mode and the ability to freeze time mid-swing between skyscrapers became an integral part of the experience shared across social media.
ps4__marvel-s-spider-man.teaser: An original story about a seasoned Spider-Man, swinging through Manhattan like never before.

ps4__last-of-us-part-ii.article:
Five years after the events of the first game, Ellie lives in the settlement of Jackson alongside Joel, until a brutal act of violence forces her onto a path of revenge through a devastated Seattle. Naughty Dog took an enormous risk by splitting the narrative between two opposing characters, forcing players to experience the same conflict from both sides and confront uncomfortable questions about the cycle of violence and retribution. The combat system builds on the first game but is far rawer, enemies react to their surroundings and sounds, environments can be used for stealth or frontal assault, and the game shows no restraint in depicting cruelty and its consequences.

Compared to the first game, Ellie gains the ability to dodge, crawl through tall grass and under cars, and navigate far more vertical, permeable locations where combat can be broken off at any moment by fleeing and restarted from another angle. Enemies call each other by name in battle, patrol with trained dogs, and visibly change behavior upon losing a companion, so every skirmish carries an emotional cost the game deliberately stokes. Technically and in terms of performance, it stands as one of the most refined titles of the generation, with facial capture and animation that pushed the bar for interactive storytelling, and an extraordinarily extensive suite of accessibility options that made it a referenced standard for opening up a demanding action title to players with visual or motor impairments.

Reception was extremely polarized, as part of the player community rejected the story's direction, while critics showered it with a record number of Game of the Year awards. The character Abby, whose physical transformation and motivations sparked heated debate even before release due to leaked footage, ultimately became a symbol of the wider controversy over who a player is allowed to sympathize with. Regardless of the controversy, it remains a work passionately discussed to this day, and it confirmed Naughty Dog as a studio willing to risk narrative convention even at the cost of dividing its fanbase.
ps4__last-of-us-part-ii.teaser: A narrative split between two hostile characters forces you to live the conflict from both sides.

ps4__horizon-zero-dawn.article:
Guerrilla Games, until then known mainly for the Killzone shooters, surprised everyone with a complete change of genre and tone. Aloy, an outcast huntress raised outside tribal society, journeys through a post-apocalyptic world a thousand years after the fall of our civilization, where nature is ruled by mechanical creatures resembling dinosaurs and other animals. Combat is built on archery, traps, and tactically shooting the weak points of giant machines, turning every encounter into a miniature puzzle rather than pure action.

The key tool is the Focus device, with which Aloy scans her surroundings, reveals patrol routes and vulnerable spots, and identifies weaknesses to particular elements. The player then chooses the type of arrows, tripwires, or a rope to pull a running machine to the ground, and after clearing special underground complexes, gains the ability to override smaller machines and use them as allies or as mounts. The open world blends tribal mythology with a gradually revealed sci-fi past involving an artificial intelligence named GAIA and a catastrophe called the Faro Plague, so the game works simultaneously as a fantasy adventure and a detective sci-fi story pieced together from the recovered logs of long-dead people.

Visually, it was among the most impressive titles on PlayStation 4 at launch, showing what the console was capable of, while an elaborate photo mode let players capture stunning sunsets over overgrown skyscraper ruins. Critics praised the originality of the concept, the rich lore, and the strength of Aloy as a heroine; the game became one of Sony's most successful new franchises and launched a series continued by Forbidden West. The Frozen Wilds expansion added a snowy mountain range and new machine types, while a later PC release showed that Sony treats its new franchise as a long-term investment it intends to keep returning to beyond its own consoles.
ps4__horizon-zero-dawn.teaser: The creators of Killzone surprised everyone with an open world of mechanical beasts instead of dinosaurs.

ps4__bloodborne.article:
Hidetaka Miyazaki and FromSoftware left the medieval fantasy of the Souls series behind and moved to the gothic city of Yharnam, plagued by a cursed disease that turns its inhabitants into hideous beasts. Instead of a shield and slow blocking, the player is given only a weapon with a transforming form and a firearm to interrupt attacks, which reoriented the entire combat system toward aggression, since the player is rewarded for attacking rather than retreating, thanks to the Rally mechanic that lets lost health be regained through a swift counterattack.

The transforming weapons are the true heart of the gameplay: each has two forms that can be switched mid-combo, so a quick blade morphs mid-animation into a heavy edge with greater reach, letting the player build their own rhythm to fit the situation. The firearm doesn't chip away at health but serves as a precisely timed stagger that opens the way for a devastating melee follow-up, turning every fight into a matter of nerve and timing rather than patient waiting behind a shield. Level design full of shortcuts and interconnected locations is a FromSoftware trademark, but the faster pace and darker atmosphere make Yharnam, with its chapels, alleys, and cathedrals, one of the best-designed environments the studio has ever created. Optional procedurally assembled dungeons then offered dozens more hours for the most persistent players.

The atmosphere draws on both Lovecraftian and Victorian gothic horror, and the world gradually shifts from a hunt for werewolves to cosmic horror filled with strange beings, underscored by the player's growing understanding of Yharnam's hidden side. Critics called the game one of the highlights of the generation, and despite its difficulty it earned an army of devoted fans, further expanded by the demanding The Old Hunters expansion. The lasting absence of a remaster and its status as a Sony exclusive have only heightened the game's cult status and the nostalgic longing for an official return to Yharnam.
ps4__bloodborne.teaser: FromSoftware swapped the shield for a gun; the Rally mechanic rewards aggression.

ps4__uncharted-4-thief-s-end.article:
Nathan Drake, seemingly settled into civilian life alongside Elena, is pulled back into a world of treasure and adventure when his brother Sam resurfaces with a story about the pirate treasure of Captain Henry Avery. In the series' final installment, Naughty Dog bet on its most emotionally mature storytelling yet, tackling questions of family, lies, addiction to adrenaline, and the price adventure exacts on relationships.

Action sequences combine platforming, cover-based shootouts, and, for the first time, a grappling rope enabling more dramatic movement and vertical combat, while more open locations in Madagascar offer greater freedom than the series' earlier linear installments, including longer stretches driving a winch-equipped off-road vehicle. Stealth received a fully realized form for the first time, with tall grass, enemy marking, and the option to advance silently through entire arenas, letting the player choose between a cinematic firefight and patiently picking off patrols. Quieter chapters, meanwhile, unfold entirely without combat, relying on exploring a house, conversations, and memories, lending the series - previously built mainly around action - an unexpectedly personal tone. Visually and technically, it was one of the most spectacular titles of the generation, with cinematic direction approaching the quality of a Hollywood adventure film.

Critics praised the dignified and emotionally powerful farewell to the series along with the overall polish of the gameplay; the game earned numerous Game of the Year awards and is considered one of the high points of the action-adventure genre on PlayStation 4. The character Nadine Ross and the new villain Rafe Adler brought a fresh perspective on treasure hunters' motivations to the series' finale, while an epilogue set years later with daughter Cassie showed Drake finally settled down, giving players an emotionally satisfying farewell after four installments. The multiplayer component and the standalone expansion The Lost Legacy, starring Chloe Frazer and Nadine Ross, further expanded the world beyond the main story.
ps4__uncharted-4-thief-s-end.teaser: Nathan Drake's final chapter, with the series' most mature story and cinematic pacing of action.

ps4__ghost-of-tsushima.article:
The year is 1274; the Mongol invasion is ravaging the island of Tsushima, and the samurai Jin Sakai, one of the few survivors of his clan, must choose between the honor-bound path of bushido and the ruthless, covert tactics that are the only hope of defeating an overwhelming enemy. Sucker Punch, until then known mainly for Infamous, created an open world inspired by Japanese samurai films, where the wind literally points the way to the next objective instead of traditional maps and markers.

Combat unfolds in tense one-on-one duels as well as chaotic skirmishes, with the player switching between combat stances depending on the enemy type and gradually combining open confrontation with ninja tools such as smoke bombs or a bow. A signature feature is the opening standoff, in which Jin challenges a group of enemies himself and, with a single precise draw of the sword, cuts down several of them before the actual battle even begins. Exploring the island isn't driven by a quest list but by curiosity: smoke over a burned village, a flock of birds, or a fox by a forest shrine lead the player to camps, hot springs, and bamboo-cutting challenges that gradually increase Jin's resolve and combat skills. The visual stylization, with fields of red grass, maple forests, and the black-and-white grainy Kurosawa cinema mode, made the game one of the most visually striking titles of the generation.

The game became a commercial hit, received numerous awards for its artistic direction, and paved the way for the multiplayer mode Legends as well as the sequel Yotei. Jin is also one of the few major games fully dubbed in Japanese with matching lip movement, which, combined with traditional music and quiet, contemplative moments by the campfire composing haiku, gave the experience an unusually meditative tone compared to typical open worlds. The Iki Island expansion added a new island and revealed Jin's past tied to his father, deepening the hero's psychological dimension.
ps4__ghost-of-tsushima.teaser: An open world inspired by samurai films, where the wind, not a map, points the way to your destination.

ps4__death-stranding.article:
After leaving Konami, Hideo Kojima founded his own studio and created a game that defies classification: Sam Bridges, played by Norman Reedus, delivers packages across a fractured United States after a mysterious catastrophe called the Death Stranding opened a gateway between the world of the living and the dead. The very act of walking is the core of the gameplay, as the player must contend with terrain, cargo weight, character fatigue, and invisible entities called BTs, while an online cooperation network lets players share ladders, ropes, and structures with other players without ever meeting them directly.

Few major games place such emphasis on preparation before setting out: how cargo is stacked on the back affects balance, controller triggers are used to steady the load when stumbling, and crossing a shallow river becomes a tense trial. Progressing through the game means connecting further settlements to the so-called chiral network, unlocking not only the story but also the ability to build roads, elevators, and cable cars that other players contribute to as well. A route someone painstakingly carved out thus eases the way for complete strangers, with the only form of contact remaining left-behind signs and likes. A star-studded cast including Mads Mikkelsen and Léa Seydoux, plus a distinctly melancholic soundtrack, only heighten the bizarre, surreal tone of a story about isolation, connection, and American division.

Reviews were split between enthusiasm for the bold, meditative gameplay and criticism of its slow pace, yet the game built a strong fanbase and became a symbol of artistically uncompromising work within the mainstream industry. The term "strand game," coined for it, refers to connecting isolated people through invisible threads of cooperation, a theme that proved unexpectedly timely just before the worldwide pandemic isolation. The expanded Director's Cut edition and its sequel only confirmed that Kojima had found an audience willing to follow him.
ps4__death-stranding.teaser: Kojima's game, where the core mechanic is simply walking with cargo across a devastated USA.

ps4__days-gone.article:
Former outlaw biker Deacon St. John survives in post-apocalyptic Oregon two years after a pandemic broke out, turning most of humanity into Freakers - fast, unpredictable zombies that travel in the hundreds as so-called Hordes. It is precisely these massive Hordes, which must be dealt with tactically using traps, incendiary bottles, and terrain, that rank among the game's most compelling elements, setting it apart from other zombie titles. The motorcycle isn't just a means of transport but a survival mechanic in its own right, since it burns fuel, wears down, and requires maintenance, deepening the sense of fragility in a world with no rescue in sight.

The world reacts to time of day and weather; at night and in the rain the infected are faster and more numerous, and Hordes move between nests and water sources on their own schedule, so attacking one is always a planned operation with an escape route and an ammunition supply. Materials for explosives, bandages, and silencers are gathered continuously from abandoned houses and vehicles, and upgrades for the motorcycle and weapons are bought with reputation earned among various survivor camps, forcing the player to choose whom to serve. The sprawling Oregon landscape, with its dense forests, volcanic plains, and abandoned mountain towns, offered an unusually American, rugged alternative to the European or Asian post-apocalyptic settings common in the genre.

The story tackles themes of loss, guilt, and brotherhood among biker clans, though critics viewed the narrative as less original than the technical execution of the horde battles. The game had performance issues and bugs at launch, which hurt its initial reviews, but gradual patches and later releases on other platforms earned it a reputation as an underrated gem with one of the best zombie-horde concepts of the generation. Despite solid sales, Bend Studio decided not to develop a sequel, leaving the game a closed but well-regarded experiment for Sony.
ps4__days-gone.teaser: Massive hordes of hundreds of zombies force you to use traps and terrain tactically; the motorbike is almost a character.

ps4__detroit-become-human.article:
**Detroit: Become Human**, created by David Cage and Quantic Dream, is set in 2038, when androids perform all manual and service labor for humanity, until some of them begin to awaken with their own consciousness. The player alternately controls three androids - Connor, a detective hunting deviants; Kara, a caregiver protecting a child from a violent father; and Markus, who becomes the face of the android revolution - and their fates gradually intertwine without ever fully merging into a single storyline.

The game relies on extensive story branching through quick-time events and decisions, where practically any character can die at any moment and the story simply continues, making every playthrough a unique experience recorded in clear flowcharts after each chapter. The controls follow the studio's tradition: character movement is complemented by contextual gestures using the DualShock 4's sticks and touchpad, so that even mundane actions like tidying an apartment or treating a wound carry physical weight. Connor also offers a distinctive crime-scene analysis mechanic, letting the reconstructed sequence of events be replayed forward and backward, while the choice between a peaceful and a violent android revolution in Markus's storyline gives the player a genuine sense of responsibility for the fate of an entire species.

Themes of slavery, civil rights, and artificial intelligence are handled with varying degrees of subtlety, but the visual production and motion-capture performances rank among the best in the field - detailed facial expressions, lighting work, and Detroit's rainy, neon-cold appearance create a convincingly near future. Critics praised the ambition and technical craftsmanship, players embraced the enormous replayability, and the game became one of Quantic Dream's most successful titles and proof that interactive drama has a solid place on PlayStation 4. With this title, the studio finally shook off its reputation as the creator of interesting but mechanically fragile experiments from earlier games like Heavy Rain or Beyond: Two Souls.
ps4__detroit-become-human.teaser: Three androids, three intertwined fates, and choices that branch the story into many endings.

ps4__ratchet-and-clank.article:
**Ratchet & Clank** came about when Insomniac Games used the production of a feature-length animated film as an opportunity to remake its own 2002 debut into a modern reboot that works both as a film tie-in and as a new entry point into the series for PlayStation 4 players. The story follows the meeting of the Lombax Ratchet and the robot Clank, who accidentally get caught up in the scheme of the evil Emperor Drek to destroy planets to build a new homeland, and must team up with the disbanded group of heroes known as the Galactic Rangers.

The core remains the proven combination of platforming jumps and shootouts with extravagant weapons, such as the Sheepinator that turns enemies into sheep or the Groovitron that forces an entire room to dance, with each weapon gradually upgrading through use and gaining a more powerful form. Combat demands constant lateral movement, dodging, and quick switching of the arsenal depending on the enemy type; interspersed between firefights are hoverboard sections, starfighter flights, and small logic puzzles in which the player controls Clank's helper bots. Level design is more streamlined and accessible for a new generation of players compared to the original, with less punishing checkpoint placement, without losing the appeal of returning to earlier planets with newly acquired gear.

Visually, the game harnessed the full graphical power of PlayStation 4 for a colorful, animated style comparable to Pixar-level production. Fast animated cutscenes flowing seamlessly into gameplay without visible loading screens showed just what the console was capable of in terms of smooth transitions between cinematic and playable sections. Critics praised the return to humor and inventiveness without sacrificing accessibility for newcomers, and the game became both a successful standalone title and convincing proof that classic franchises can be sensitively modernized, paving the way for the more spectacular Rift Apart on PlayStation 5. The accompanying animated film failed to win over critics or audiences to any great degree, but the game itself made clear that Insomniac retains firm creative control over this classic franchise.
ps4__ratchet-and-clank.teaser: A modern reboot of the series' 2002 debut, filmed alongside an animated movie.

ps4__gran-turismo-sport.article:
After several years of waiting and a delayed development cycle, Polyphony Digital delivered the seventh installment of the legendary series with **Gran Turismo Sport**, this time with a marked shift toward online competition and esports at the expense of the traditional career mode. Sport Mode, with its clearly defined system of Driver Rating and Safety Rating, became the backbone of the game and was developed in collaboration with the FIA, enabling official championship series to be run directly within the game.

The driving physics model remained true to the series' philosophy - precise, realistic car behavior on track, where any premature stab of the throttle in a corner immediately results in a loss of grip. The rating system pairs drivers of similar speed and similar levels of consideration into the same race, making online driving feel more disciplined than in typical racing games; prescribed braking points and training challenges, meanwhile, help newcomers understand the ideal racing line. These were complemented by the photorealistic Scapes mode and the Livery Editor for custom bodywork designs, which let players design vehicle liveries with incredible precision and share them with the community, producing an extensive library of creative designs far beyond what the developers originally intended.

A smaller selection of tracks and cars compared to previous entries, along with the missing offline career mode at launch, disappointed part of the fanbase, but gradual free updates significantly expanded the content - adding a career mode along with dozens of new tracks and cars, so that by the end of its lifespan the game offered a much more complete experience than at release. Technically, it was one of the cleanest-looking games on PlayStation 4, with meticulously lit car models and HDR support. The game became Sony's flagship title for simulation racing on the console, cemented its position in professional esports through the FIA Gran Turismo Championship, and proved that the series holds its own even in an era of online-focused live-service titles.
ps4__gran-turismo-sport.teaser: The series' first focus on online competition; Sport Mode was created in collaboration with the FIA.

ps4__persona-5.article: A group of Tokyo students led by the protagonist nicknamed Joker lead a double life - ordinary high school students by day, and by night the Phantom Thieves of Hearts, who infiltrate Palaces, twisted manifestations of the corrupted subconscious of corrupt adults, and steal their distorted hearts to force them into repentance. Atlus combined social simulation - building relationships with characters called Confidants, managing the school-year calendar, part-time jobs, and hobbies - with turn-based dungeon crawling, where the player collects and fuses Personas, manifestations of one's own inner self in the style of tarot archetypes. The game's iconic visual style, with its red-and-black menu design, Shoji Meguro's jazz soundtrack, and stylized animated direction, transformed the Persona series from a niche JRPG into a global phenomenon. The story, about young people rebelling against a corrupt society and hypocritical authority figures, resonated with players around the world. Critics called it one of the best JRPGs of all time, the game received an expanded Royal edition, an anime adaptation, and crossover spin-offs, and it definitively catapulted Atlus and its Persona brand into the mainstream. The theme of a group of friends fighting the systemic corruption of the adult world in their spare time resonated especially with a younger generation of players weary of authoritarian institutions, and characters like Ryuji, Ann, and the mysterious talking cat Morgana became icons of pop culture even outside the gaming community. Boss battles against corrupted figures, full of dramatic Palace transformations, also showed just how powerfully visual design can reinforce a game's thematic message.
ps4__persona-5.teaser: A double life for students: school by day, stealing the hearts of corrupt adults by night.

ps4__nioh.article:
Team Ninja, known for the Ninja Gaiden series, crafted with **Nioh** its own take on the soulslike genre, set in a fictionalized version of Sengoku-era Japan where the real historical English sailor William Adams becomes entangled in battles against samurai, yokai demons, and supernatural forces.

The combat system is built around three stances - high, mid, and low - each offering a different balance of attack power, reach, and speed, and players can switch between them even mid-combo. The second pillar is the Ki Pulse mechanic, allowing quick stamina recovery with a precisely timed button press after an attack; mastering this rhythm separates players who struggle with the game from those who master it. An elaborate equipment system with randomly generated weapon and armor traits draws inspiration from looter RPGs like Diablo, setting the game apart from FromSoftware's austere approach, and an extensive roster of optional missions lets players endlessly refine their gear, making the game a beloved endgame farming destination.

The difficulty is notoriously high and demands patient mastery of timing, but rewards players with a deep build system and a variety of playstyles, from a swift katana to a heavy hammer. Yokai such as the giant spider-woman Nure-onna or the fiery demon Enki give boss fights a visual and mechanical identity distinct from the Europe-flavored Souls games, drawing directly on Japanese folklore; pools of dark yokai energy on the battlefield also alter stamina recovery rules, forcing players to think about where they stand. The historical backdrop of civil wars, accompanied by drums and flutes in the score, lends missions a grim, cold gravity rarely seen in action RPGs of the time. Critics praised the original combination of soulslike difficulty with Japanese historical themes and rich loot, the game built a devoted fanbase, and it received a successful sequel, Nioh 2, which further developed the stance mechanics and yokai abilities.
ps4__nioh.teaser: A soulslike set in the Sengoku period with three sword stances and merciless difficulty.

ps4__shadow-of-colossus.article:
Bluepoint Games, a studio specializing in remakes and remasters, rebuilt Fumito Ueda's 2005 classic **Shadow of the Colossus** completely from the ground up on a modern engine while preserving every detail of the original design. A young man named Wander rides his horse Agro into a forbidden land to revive a dead girl, Mono, and the only price for this miracle is the killing of sixteen giant, majestic colossi scattered across an empty, melancholic landscape.

Instead of ordinary enemies, each colossus is a puzzle in itself - the player must find weak points, climb the giant's fur or stone body, and drive a sword into marked spots while the world shudders around them. Climbing consumes stamina and the colossus tries to shake the rider off, so the player must seek moments of calm to catch their breath; reflecting sunlight off the sword helps locate weaknesses. There are no cutscenes or side quests in the game, only long, solitary rides across the landscape that lend each encounter a ritual weight. It was precisely this combination of acrobatic climbing, the epic scale of the opponents, and a quiet, almost wordless story about the price we pay for love that made the original game one of the most influential titles in history.

The animalistic, almost mythological presence of the colossi, who often seem to defend themselves rather than attack aggressively before the player strikes, evokes in many players a sense of guilt over killing them - precisely the effect Fumito Ueda intended. The remake delivered photorealistic graphics, reworked lighting, and a smooth sixty frames per second while preserving the soul of the original, and added a photo mode and a new, even harder difficulty setting. Sound remained as essential as visuals: the colossi's thudding footsteps, the sudden silence after their fall, and the mournful orchestral theme turn every victory into something closer to a funeral than a triumph. Critics praised it as a model example of a remake, and the game reached both nostalgic veterans and an entirely new audience unfamiliar with the original PlayStation 2-era title.
ps4__shadow-of-colossus.teaser: A ground-up remake of Fumito Ueda's classic; no ordinary enemies, just sixteen colossi.

ps4__witcher-3-wild-hunt.article:
Geralt of Rivia, a witcher and monster hunter for hire, journeys through the war-torn Northern Kingdoms in **The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt**, the final and most expansive chapter of the Polish trilogy, searching for his adoptive daughter Ciri, who is being hunted by the supernatural Wild Hunt. CD Projekt Red created one of the largest and most densely crafted open worlds of its time, where even minor side quests usually conceal morally ambiguous stories worthy of the main plot, from village curses to political intrigue between Nilfgaard and Temeria.

The combat system combines two swords for human and monstrous opponents, Signs - magical attacks like the fiery Igni or the protective Quen - potions, and alchemy, with preparation paying off on higher difficulties: reading the bestiary, coating the blade with the right oil, and setting out only in the right weather. The Witcher Sense turns monster hunting into a small detective investigation involving tracks and witness interrogations. Gwent, a card minigame scattered across taverns across the continent, became so popular that it later spun off into its own standalone title.

The expansions Hearts of Stone and especially Blood and Wine, set in the sunny region of Toussaint, rank among the best-reviewed expansions in the genre's history. The sorceress Yennefer, Ciri's friend Triss Merigold, and even the horse Roach became an inseparable part of pop culture, while morally ambiguous choices, such as the fate of Novigrad and its witch hunts, showed that a fantasy RPG can tackle political and ethical questions just as pressing as serious literature. The game won countless Game of the Year awards, sold tens of millions of copies, inspired a successful Netflix series, and is still considered one of the gold standards of the open-world RPG genre. CD Projekt Red also supported the game for years with dozens of free content updates, earning it enormous respect from the gaming community.
ps4__witcher-3-wild-hunt.teaser: The most sprawling open world of its time, where even minor quests hide moral dilemmas.

ps4__red-dead-redemption-2.article:
A prequel to Red Dead Redemption, **Red Dead Redemption 2** follows Arthur Morgan, a member of the Van der Linde gang, at a time when the Wild American West is slowly giving way to modernization, industrialization, and ever-growing government pressure on criminal groups. Rockstar Games built an enormous open world with an incredible density of detail - horses have their own personalities and must be tamed and cared for, food and hygiene affect stats, NPC dialogue reacts to the player's clothing and behavior, and even minor interactions in towns feel alive and unscripted.

The player isn't limited to a single conversation button: every character can be approached with a greeting, a threat, or an apology, turning an ordinary encounter on the road into a small, open-ended situation. The gang's camp functions as a living organism that must be supplied through hunting and money, and the honor system changes how towns and Arthur's own companions react to him. Details like a gradually growing unkempt beard, visible bloodstains on clothing after a shootout, or real depletion of wildlife from overhunting show just how far Rockstar was willing to go to simulate the consequences of the player's actions.

The story focuses on themes of loyalty, honor, and the inevitable end of a certain way of life, with Arthur ranking among the best-written and most human protagonists in Rockstar's history; the epilogue featuring John Marston, tying the game back to the first installment of the series, gives the entire story a sense of a closed, tragic circle. Although the game's pacing was too slow for some players and its controls less streamlined than the competition, its technical precision, music, and the atmosphere of misty mornings and snow-covered mountains catapulted the game among the absolute peaks of its generation. Critics gave it near-perfect scores, it ranks commercially among the most successful video games of all time, and the online multiplayer mode Red Dead Online has secured it a long lifespan.
ps4__red-dead-redemption-2.teaser: A massive open world with incredible density of detail, where even caring for your horse has its own rules.

ps4__grand-theft-auto-v.article:
Rockstar North moved its series with **Grand Theft Auto V** into the fictional Los Santos, a caricature of Southern California, and for the first time in the main series offered three playable protagonists - former robber Michael, street gangster Franklin, and the unpredictable psychopath Trevor - between whom players can switch at any time, even during action, enabling more sophisticated planned bank robberies and heists.

Those heists form the core of the game's structure: each is prepared by choosing an approach, hiring helpers of varying quality, and gathering equipment, and switching between characters during the action itself works like a film cut, letting the player take control of one hero while another covers the retreat. Each character also has a unique special ability, from slowing down time during shootouts to increased resilience in close combat. At release, the open world ranked among the largest and most lively ever made, full of satire on American consumer society, celebrity culture, and politics, and offered an enormous range of side activities from stock trading to golf, tennis, or diving.

The transition to PlayStation 4 in 2014 brought a graphical upgrade, denser traffic and vegetation, and an entirely new first-person perspective, but true longevity for the title came from the online multiplayer Grand Theft Auto Online, which became one of the most profitable products in the history of the entertainment industry and, through regular updates featuring heists, races, and raids, turned the game into a practically endlessly alive world. Radio stations with original hosts, parody ads for fictional products, and a limitless number of small details in the streets of Los Santos still reveal new jokes to players even after years of exploration. Critics gave the game near-unanimous praise for its scope, humor, and technical execution, and the title remains a commercially active phenomenon more than a decade later.
ps4__grand-theft-auto-v.teaser: The series' first three playable protagonists, switchable even in the middle of the action.

ps4__elden-ring.article: FromSoftware, working with fantasy author George R. R. Martin, who designed the world's mythology and backstory, abandoned the linear, interconnected level design of its earlier Souls games in favor of the sprawling open world of the Lands Between, shattered after the breaking of the titular Elden Ring and the murder of the Golden Order. Playing as the Tarnished, one of many who have lost their grace, the player journeys through a land full of catacombs, castles, and legendary demigods, and thanks to the horse Torrent and a far more open progression structure, can choose the order in which to face challenges, unlike the studio's stricter earlier titles. The combat system expands the tried-and-true formula with spells, Ashes of War that let players customize weapon abilities, and spirit summons for tougher boss encounters. The scope, artistic direction, and thoughtful balance of freedom against difficulty earned the game near-unanimous praise from critics and players alike, along with a record haul of Game of the Year awards. Commercially, it became one of FromSoftware's fastest-selling titles, brought the soulslike genre to a much wider audience, and the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion only confirmed the game's exceptional standing. The freedom offered by legendary weapons such as the Rivers of Blood sword, explosive incantations, and a highly variable build system allowed for wildly different playstyles, from purely knightly combat to ranged magic attacks, letting the game win over even players who had previously avoided the Souls titles because of their difficulty. The extensive collaboration with George R. R. Martin also gave the world of the Lands Between an unusually rich background full of tragic demigod bloodlines that players gradually uncover through fragmentary item descriptions.
ps4__elden-ring.teaser: The open world of the Lands Between, its mythology co-created with author George R. R. Martin.

ps4__dark-souls-iii.article:
The final installment of the original trilogy, **Dark Souls III**, brings players into Lothric, a kingdom on the verge of collapse, where eras and beings from the series' past games intertwine - the First Flame is fading, and undead Lords of Cinder are being torn from their graves to rekindle it.

FromSoftware sped up combat compared to the second installment, bringing it closer to the more aggressive style of Bloodborne: enemy attacks come in longer, harder-to-read combinations, and dodging is more often the right answer than blocking. A new addition is Weapon Arts, allowing each weapon a unique special attack that consumes mana, giving even ordinary swords their own personality and expanding the space for character builds. Level design returned to the ingeniously interconnected architecture of the first game, where shortcuts unlocked deep within a level lead back to a bonfire and reshape the sense of space, wrapped in a dark, gothic aesthetic of burning cathedrals and crumbling castles.

It is accompanied by some of the most demanding boss fights in the entire series, including the legendary battle with the Nameless King, where the first phase atop a dragon tests both patience and camera control. As a closing chapter for the whole trilogy, the game also functions as a nostalgic celebration with many references to the first installment and its characters; Siegward of Catarina, a comical yet deeply human companion, ranks among the most beloved figures in the fan community and shows that even in a grim, dying apocalypse FromSoftware can find room for touching humor. The expansions Ashes of Ariandel and The Ringed City added entirely new areas and some of the toughest fights in the series, providing a dignified farewell to the trilogy. Technically, it was the most stable installment in the series, with significantly shorter loading times after death than on older consoles - a crucial change in how punishment feels for a game built on dozens of repeated attempts. Critics received it as a dignified and most polished conclusion, and players praised the return to a harder, more interconnected structure; it is still considered one of the high points of the studio's entire soulslike output.
ps4__dark-souls-iii.teaser: The trilogy's final entry sped up combat toward Bloodborne's more aggressive style.

ps4__sekiro-shadows-die-twice.article:
With **Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice**, FromSoftware abandoned the stat and build systems typical of the Souls series and created a much more direct, yet mercilessly demanding action game set in fictional feudal Japan. The player controls a one-armed shinobi who must rescue his young lord, and the core combat mechanic isn't stamina management for attacks but a posture system - fights are won by aggressively deflecting attacks with a katana until the opponent's posture breaks, allowing a lethal Shinobi Execution strike.

The verticality of the level design allows, thanks to a grappling hook, free movement across rooftops and cliffs, which combined with prosthetic arm tools - an axe that shatters shields, a fire-spewing device, or an opening umbrella - offers a more flexible approach to both stealth and confrontation than the studio's earlier titles. The player can quietly eliminate weaker guards from above, gaining an advantage before a boss fight, and the ability to resurrect once on the spot of death changes the rhythm of trial and error. The difficulty is downright extreme and demands mastering precise parry timing rather than dodging, which put off some players but also delivered an unprecedented sense of satisfaction from defeating bosses like Genichiro or Isshin.

An environment inspired by the Sengoku period, full of castle towers, snow-covered temples, and a mystical underworld inhabited by supernatural beings, offers a visually distinct palette from the studio's Europe-flavored games, and sound design featuring the sharp clang of a deflected blade serves as precise feedback for the entire combat rhythm. Compared to earlier titles, Sekiro also avoids optional builds and skill trees in favor of a strictly balanced combat design, which made it more accessible for viewing as a competitive discipline among skilled players. Critics praised the game as a masterwork of combat design, and it won Game of the Year 2019 at The Game Awards.
ps4__sekiro-shadows-die-twice.teaser: Combat is decided by the posture system, not stamina or builds; FromSoftware's most merciless game.

ps4__monster-hunter-world.article:
With **Monster Hunter: World**, Capcom departed for the first time from the series' traditional division into small mission-based areas and created a truly seamless open world, the New World, where the Hunters' Guild sets out to investigate the migration of giant monsters and their ecosystem.

The heart of the game remains the hunt itself - the player chooses from fourteen distinct weapon types, from heavy hammers to complex hunting horns, each with its own set of combos, speed, and rhythm, so switching weapons is almost like playing a new game. The hunter tracks the trails and behavior of monsters such as the flagship, T-Rex-like Anjanath or the majestic dragon Nergigante, tags them with the flying Scoutfly insect, and forges ever stronger gear from the materials gathered. Fights last dozens of minutes, monsters limp, flee to their lairs, and can have their tail severed or specific body parts damaged, changing not only their behavior but also their loot. The new seamless environment also lets monsters interact with each other and their surroundings, creating emergent situations where two beasts clash right in front of the player.

The base of Astera serves as a social hub between expeditions, where players can cook meals granting temporary bonuses, trade with other hunters, and plan joint expeditions for up to four players. More accessible controls, a clearer interface, and modern graphics compared to earlier, exclusively handheld installments opened the series to a massive Western audience that had previously overlooked it. The subsequent major expansion Iceborne added the snowy region of Hoarfrost Reach and a new, even tougher monster named Velkhana, extending the game's lifespan by years of additional content. Critics praised the depth of its systems while remaining accessible to newcomers, and the game became the best-selling title in Capcom's history, definitively catapulting Monster Hunter into the global mainstream.
ps4__monster-hunter-world.teaser: For the first time, a truly seamless open world instead of separate mission zones.

ps4__final-fantasy-xv.article:
After years of turbulent development under the original title Final Fantasy Versus XIII, the fifteenth numbered entry was released as **Final Fantasy XV**, a road-trip story about Prince Noctis and his three childhood friends journeying across the kingdom of Lucis so that Noctis can marry Lunafreya and save his homeland from the invading empire of Niflheim.

Combat plays out in real time with the ability to warp-strike toward weapons lodged in enemies or thrown onto terrain above the battlefield, giving fights a distinctive verticality; holding a button lets the character defend automatically while the player focuses on timing counterattacks and coordinating with companions, whose special abilities can be switched to at any time. The game's greatest strength is the group of friends itself - their banter while riding in the convertible Regalia, campfire nights, photographs taken by Prompto, and shared cooking that grants specific bonuses for the next day create a fresh, human dynamic unusual for an epic fantasy story.

Development was marred by an incomplete final storyline, which Square Enix later filled in through DLC episodes and the animated film Kingsglaive, sparking mixed critical reactions regarding narrative cohesion. The open first half of the game, with highways, roadside diners, and a distant silhouette of a castle on the horizon, also sharply contrasts with the more linear, darker second half, fueling discussion about uneven pacing. Square Enix continued to adjust and expand the game for years after release, making it one of the first major Japanese titles developed essentially as a live service. Visually, it was one of the most technically demanding titles on PlayStation 4, with vast plains, dynamic weather, and a day-night cycle after which noticeably stronger monsters appear. Despite these reservations, the game became commercially successful, praised especially for its atmosphere of friendship and open world, and nighttime camping with guitar playing, fishing, and cooking remains one of the most fondly remembered moments in the entire series. It showed that even a serious fantasy epic can find room for sincere, almost brotherly warmth between its characters.
ps4__final-fantasy-xv.teaser: A road trip story about a prince and his three childhood friends, after years of turbulent development.

ps4__final-fantasy-vii-remake.article:
With **Final Fantasy VII Remake**, Square Enix boldly decided not to retell the 1997 classic in a single game, but instead to expand only its opening section set in the city of Midgar into a full-fledged, several-dozen-hour title, supplemented with new characters, side content, and mysterious beings called Whispers that hint at a departure from the boundaries of the original story.

The combat system abandoned the turn-based mechanics of the older installments in favor of a real-time action system combined with tactical pausing for selecting spells and abilities via Materia, linking the dynamics of modern action with the tactical depth of classic JRPGs. Basic attacks fill an ATB gauge, spending it triggers abilities in slowed time, and the player switches between party members, each with a different role - Cloud's switchable stance, Tifa's rapid combo-based aggression, Barret's ranged fire support. Enemy weaknesses lead to staggering them and a brief window for a devastating combo, so even an ordinary fight carries the rhythm of a small tactical puzzle.

Cloud Strife, Tifa, Aerith, and Barret all received deeper characterization and fully voiced dialogue, with Aerith in particular getting much more screen time, sparking tense anticipation among fans of the original regarding her fate given the Whispers' role in preventing deviation from the original script. Nobuo Uematsu's iconic soundtrack was rearranged with an orchestral emphasis while preserving its signature motifs. Midgar's skyscrapers and slums were fleshed out to an unprecedented level of detail, turning what was roughly a five-hour opening in the 1990s classic into a self-contained world with its own political and social subtext. Critics praised the combat and the emotional depth of the relationships, though stretching out a short section drew questions about pacing from some fans; commercial success then paved the way for the sequel, Rebirth.
ps4__final-fantasy-vii-remake.teaser: Just the opening chapter of the 1997 classic, expanded into dozens of hours of a full-fledged game.

ps4__nier-automata.article:
The pairing of visionary writer Yoko Taro and the action specialists at PlatinumGames delivered, in **Nier: Automata**, a story about combat androids 2B, 9S, and A2, who fight in humanity's proxy war against alien machines on a devastated Earth, unaware of just how deeply distorted the truth about their mission really is.

Combat combines hack-and-slash sword fighting with bullet-hell shootouts using flying Pod units, letting PlatinumGames bring its signature fluid action into an RPG framework. The game constantly toys with the camera: the perspective shifts without warning from third person to a side-scrolling platformer or a classic top-down shoot-em-up, so the player moves through several genres within a single mission. Characters aren't upgraded through levels alone but through plug-in chips that take up space in shared memory - players can sacrifice part of the interface, such as the health bar or minimap, in exchange for greater combat power, a typically audacious idea from Yoko Taro.

The game is famous for its structure of several successive playthroughs - the second and third runs reveal the same events from another character's perspective or entirely new chapters, while questions of consciousness, mortality, and the meaning of existence form the philosophical core of the narrative; the game also contains a number of hidden, unconventional endings, including sequences with no gameplay at all. The emotive soundtrack, sung in an invented language, ranks among the most acclaimed in the gaming industry and amplifies the melancholic tone of a dying planet, while the design of 2B, inspired by a gothic military uniform and a blindfold symbolizing suppressed emotion, became one of the most recognizable visual concepts of the decade. Empty, nature-overgrown ruins of human cities, abandoned amusement parks, and rusting factories don't merely serve as scenery but as a quiet commentary on what remains after civilization. Critics praised the unusual combination of deep philosophical reflection with satisfying action, the game became an unexpected commercial and critical hit, and it firmly established Yoko Taro as one of the most distinctive creators in the Japanese gaming industry.
ps4__nier-automata.teaser: A pairing of writer Yoko Taro and PlatinumGames; combat blends swordplay with bullet-hell.

ps4__metal-gear-solid-v-phantom-pain.article:
The last game made by Hideo Kojima under the Konami banner, **Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain** introduces Venom Snake, awakened from a nine-year coma after an explosion, into the vast open environments of Afghanistan and Angola, where he builds a private army, Diamond Dogs, and seeks revenge against the organization XOF, which destroyed his previous base, Mother Base.

For the first time, the series abandoned its linear mission structure in favor of a truly open world, where the player plans infiltrations using prior binocular reconnaissance, a reprogrammed robot, canine companion D-Dog, sniper Quiet, or direct combat deployment. The Fulton Recovery system allows soldiers, animals, and vehicles to be extracted straight to base via balloon-based extraction, so every specialist captured through stealth strengthens the player's own development division. Enemy garrisons also adapt: those who shoot too often for the head start running into helmets, those who attack at night encounter guards with night-vision goggles. Time of day and weather change the entire approach, since a sandstorm can conceal a movement that would trigger an alarm in broad daylight.

Narratively, the game is unusually fragmentary and deliberately leaves key moments unresolved, sparking discussions about the unfinished state of the release due to Kojima's split from Konami during development; the divisively received second half, whose chapters ended up largely repeating earlier missions at higher difficulty, remains a lasting source of speculation. The character of Quiet, a sniper who communicates without words, along with building a private army through base management, linked action infiltration with elements of strategic planning previously unseen in the series. Technically, it was one of the smoothest titles of its generation: the Fox Engine handled vast regions at a stable frame rate with virtually no loading screens between missions and base. Despite the reservations mentioned, critics praised the sophistication of its stealth mechanics and the freedom of approach to missions as one of the high points of the genre, the game became commercially immensely successful, and it is still viewed today as a dignified, if bittersweet, farewell from its creator to his own legendary series.
ps4__metal-gear-solid-v-phantom-pain.teaser: Hideo Kojima's last game under Konami, and the series' first entry with a truly open world.

ps4__resident-evil-2.article:
Capcom did not treat the remake of **Resident Evil 2** as a mere graphical update to the 1998 classic, but completely reworked the level design, the over-the-shoulder camera system, and the pacing of the game using the RE Engine, which also powered the modern Resident Evil 7.

Leon Kennedy and Claire Redfield make their way through the Raccoon City police station overrun by a zombie outbreak caused by the T-virus, while the merciless, practically indestructible Mr. X, a giant pursuer that reacts to the player's noise, adds a permanent tension the original game never had - his heavy footsteps heard a floor above turn even a routine trip for a key into a nerve-wracking decision. Limited ammunition and inventory space force the player to choose between fighting and fleeing; zombies can take several headshots without going down, so it often pays to simply go around them and remember which routes are already blocked. The key-and-symbol puzzles remain faithful to the spirit of the original survival horror classic.

The new, elaborate model of the police headquarters, with its many interconnected corridors and rooms that the player gradually memorizes, showed just how strongly familiarity with the environment can heighten the tension of repeated encounters with Mr. X. The visual presentation, with photorealistic lighting, wet reflective surfaces, and precise sound design, amplifies the claustrophobic atmosphere of the station and its adjoining sewers, while the added alternate scenarios of the so-called second playthrough for both Leon and Claire offered plenty of content for repeat play. Capcom also kept the two-protagonist structure, whose paths sometimes intertwine and sometimes diverge, so the player sees the same catastrophe from two angles and only pieces together the full picture of Raccoon City's fall by playing both. Critics called the remake a model example of how to properly modernize a classic without losing its identity, and its commercial success convinced Capcom to continue with the remakes of Resident Evil 3 and 4, as well as to restore confidence in the series as a whole.
ps4__resident-evil-2.teaser: A remake of the 1998 classic, rebuilt from the ground up with an over-the-shoulder perspective.

ps4__resident-evil-7-biohazard.article:
After several entries that pushed the series toward the action genre, Capcom returned to the roots of claustrophobic survival horror with **Resident Evil 7: Biohazard**, while also shifting to a first-person perspective for the first time in the main line. Ethan Winters arrives at the decaying Baker family estate in the Louisiana bayous to search for his missing wife Mia, and finds himself held captive by a seemingly indestructible, violent family influenced by a parasite called the Mold.

The first-person view fundamentally changes the rules: the player cannot see around corners, must carefully lean to peek, and sound becomes the primary source of information about where the pursuer currently is. The estate is designed as a classic Resident Evil labyrinth full of locked doors, sought-after keys, and item boxes for storage, so the limited resources and the unpredictable, terrifying family patriarch Jack Baker create an atmosphere closer to horror classics like The Texas Chain Saw Massacre than to the series' earlier, more action-oriented entries. The game also supported full playability in virtual reality on PlayStation VR, which heightened the sense of physical presence in the terrifying environment to the point that, for many players, it became the most intense VR experience of the generation.

The grotesque, larger-than-life Baker family - with father Jack, mother Marguerite spawning swarms of insects, and son Lucas obsessed with traps - creates a gallery of unforgettable villains, with Jack becoming one of the most iconic characters in the entire series. A demo called Beginning Hour, released months before the full game, built extraordinary anticipation and became a viral phenomenon in its own right thanks to its hidden secrets and mysteries. Critics praised the return to a slower, tenser pace as a refreshing change for the series after years of leaning into action, the game became commercially very successful, and it relaunched Resident Evil as a respected horror brand, which subsequent entries and remakes went on to build upon.
ps4__resident-evil-7-biohazard.teaser: A return to claustrophobic horror, and the series' first entry in first-person perspective.

ps4__doom.article:
After years of experimenting with slower, cover-based shooters, id Software returned with **Doom** to the fast, brutal core of its original 1993 masterpiece. The Doom Marine wakes up on Mars amid a demon invasion triggered by Argent energy mining, and his only answer is unstoppable forward momentum.

The game actively penalizes passive hiding behind cover and rewards aggressive advancement through the Glory Kills mechanic, where brutal finishing blows on weakened enemies restore health and ammo - health packs are practically never picked up, they are earned through attacking, so the only way to survive is to charge into the thickest crowd. Movement speed, the double jump, and fluid switching across an arsenal ranging from the shotgun to the legendary chainsaw create a sense of unstoppable power the genre had lacked for years; the arenas are designed as open, circular spaces with elevated tiers, where enemies close in from all sides and the player circles along the edges. The levels also hide secret chambers and references to classic maps from the nineties, rewarding thorough exploration.

Mick Gordon's metal soundtrack, with its aggressive synthesizer riffs, became an inseparable part of the game's identity and reacts directly to the intensity of combat. The multiplayer and cooperative modes received a more lukewarm reception from critics than the campaign itself, but the SnapMap editor let the community create its own levels and game modes. Critics and players alike praised the return to pure, adrenaline-fueled shooting as a refreshing contrast to the slower, story-driven shooters of the time, and the game became one of the most successful brand reboots, paving the way for the even more extreme sequel Doom Eternal. With this title, the studio proved, after years of experiments like the controversial Doom 3, that it understood exactly what made the original so unforgettable.
ps4__doom.teaser: A return to the fast, brutal core of the 1993 original after years of slower shooters.

ps4__doom-eternal.article:
In the sequel **Doom Eternal**, id Software raised the pace and complexity of the combat system to the point where the game became an almost dance-like, micromanaged adrenaline experience. The Doom Slayer now fights a demon invasion striking Earth itself, while the game expands the Slayer's mythology from a silent symbol of fury into a character with his own elaborate history.

The key change is the forced weapon-switching based on enemy type and a deliberate scarcity of resources - the chainsaw refills ammo, the flame belch strips armor from demons, and Glory Kills restore health, forcing the player to constantly cycle between offensive tools instead of relying on a single favorite weapon. Every tougher enemy also has a weak point best exploited with a specific tool, turning the fight for survival into a clever puzzle-like decision about the order in which to eliminate opponents in each arena. The more vertical, platforming-oriented level design, with double jumps, air dashes, and a grappling hook chain, adds almost platformer-like elements to movement, which some series veterans saw as a departure from the first reboot's purely grounded action.

Visually, the game abandoned the grey Mars in favor of more colorful hellish cathedrals, ice fortresses, and ruined earthly cities, giving it a more comic-book-like, vibrant tone. Mick Gordon's soundtrack again heightens the intensity, though his subsequent public dispute with id Software over the final mix caused controversy. The Ancient Gods expansions extended the Slayer's story with a more cosmic mythology reaching back to the very origin of the hellish forces. Despite a noticeably steeper difficulty curve, critics praised the game as one of the best-crafted action shooters of the generation, and under id Software's guidance the Doom series firmly established itself as the technical and design benchmark for the entire fast-paced first-person shooter genre.
ps4__doom-eternal.teaser: The sequel sped combat up into an almost dance-like, micromanaged experience.

ps4__destiny.article:
**Destiny** is the project through which Bungie, creator of the legendary Halo, bet on merging a first-person shooter with an MMO structure and treating the game as a long-term service, following its departure from Microsoft. Guardians defend the last human city, protected by the mysterious Traveler, against dark forces spread across the solar system, with gameplay combining the precise, satisfying shooting typical of Bungie with a loot system inspired by MMO titles - colorful light spraying from fallen enemies that instantly signals the rarity of the loot. Each of the three Guardian classes, Titan, Hunter, and Warlock, offers its own set of abilities and supers, so players naturally specialize and complement each other in a group.

The Vault of Glass raid, requiring six players to coordinate without any in-game explanation of its mechanics, became an iconic example of the community discovering, documenting, and sharing strategies on its own. A whole layer of guides, spreadsheets, and voice channels grew up around the game, without which the hardest content was practically impossible to clear. Visually, the game bet on monumental, silent ruins of abandoned colonies on the Moon, Mars, and Venus, which, combined with the subdued ambient soundtrack, create a peculiar feeling of loneliness even in the middle of a shared expedition.

At launch the game faced criticism for its thin, underdeveloped story and repetitive endgame content, yet players poured enormous numbers of hours into it thanks to its addictive shooting core and the social aspect of clans and shared patrols. The design of the weapons and their satisfying visual and audio feedback on impact still stands among the genre's benchmarks today, a testament to the experience gathered over years of developing the Halo series. Successive expansions - The Dark Below, House of Wolves, and especially the extensive The Taken King - substantially reworked the character and reward systems, helping to turn initial disappointment into a respected game-as-a-service, which lasted until the full sequel Destiny 2 and defined the looter-shooter genre for the entire next decade.
ps4__destiny.teaser: The creators of Halo combined a first-person shooter with the MMO structure of a game as a service.

ps4__overwatch.article:
**Overwatch** arose from the wreckage of the cancelled ambitious MMO project Titan, from which Blizzard Entertainment reworked part of the concepts into a team-based shooter built around heroes with distinct abilities, roles, and personalities, ranging from attackers and defenders to support and tank characters. The game's key strength was its colorful, accessible visual style and a carefully polished roster of characters like Tracer, Reinhardt, or Mercy, each offering a completely different play experience and requiring team synergy rather than individual skill. Matches take place on compact maps with clearly readable objectives, whether capturing a point or escorting a payload, and last only a few minutes, so the game rewards quick reading of the situation and immediate reshuffling of the team composition. The ability to switch heroes mid-match also turned character selection into an ongoing tactical decision rather than a one-time choice at the start.

Blizzard supplemented the game with a rich world told primarily outside the game itself - animated short films and comics that built players' emotional connection to the characters without a traditional single-player story. Fan creations, from cosplay to fan art, reached a scale for characters like D.Va or Genji comparable to popular comic-book universes, which was unprecedented for a purely multiplayer game without a classic campaign. Seasonal events, cosmetic rewards with no impact on gameplay, and regular balancing kept the community active for years, while the Overwatch League esports scene tried to establish the team shooter as a spectator sport.

Critics praised the brilliant game design and accessibility, the game became a cultural phenomenon and defined the modern shape of hero-based team shooters before the arrival of the sequel Overwatch 2. Over time, however, it became clear that maintaining balance among dozens of distinct heroes is enormously demanding, and the constant balancing updates became both a strength of the long-term support and a recurring source of community frustration. On PlayStation 4 the game maintained smooth performance and stable input response, which is essential for such fast-paced shootouts, and today it is remembered as the moment when a team shooter became colorful, friendly fun open to everyone.
ps4__overwatch.teaser: Born from the wreckage of the cancelled MMO project Titan as a team-based hero shooter.

ps4__fortnite.article:
**Fortnite** began at Epic Games as a cooperative defense against zombie hordes called Save the World, but the real phenomenon arrived only with the free-to-play Battle Royale mode, where a hundred players compete for survival on a shrinking map until only one winner remains. Real-time building from harvested wood, stone, and metal set Fortnite apart from competing battle royale titles like PUBG and added another layer of tactical depth to the gameplay, enabling instant defensive and offensive structures right in the middle of a firefight. Gathering materials with a pickaxe, quickly switching between building pieces, and so-called wall editing created an entirely new skill ceiling, where the difference between a casual and a top-tier player is made.

A stylized, clearly readable visual style with bold colors and cartoonish proportions let the game run on an enormous range of devices, including older consoles and mobile phones, opening it up to an audience the more realistic competition never reached. The free-to-play model, with cosmetic skins, seasonal battle passes, and regularly changing map lore, turned the game into a massive cultural platform reaching far beyond gaming itself - in-game concerts by artists like Travis Scott attracted tens of millions of simultaneous viewers. Crossovers with characters from Marvel, Star Wars, and other franchises turned the game's island into a kind of universal cultural stage where fictional worlds that would otherwise never meet come together.

Regular, literally seasonal resets of the map through so-called in-game events kept players' attention for years and became a model for the entire live-service genre of the following decade. Accessibility and a constant stream of new content made Fortnite one of the most profitable and culturally influential titles in history, beloved across generations from children to adult players. The phenomenon spread beyond video games and became part of pop culture, fashion, and the music industry, and it still stands today as a textbook example of how a single spin-off game mode can grow into a long-lived digital space.
ps4__fortnite.teaser: A battle royale where real-time building set the game apart from PUBG and others.

ps4__rocket-league.article:
**Rocket League** built on Psyonix's lesser-known game Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars with a seemingly simple concept - soccer played by rocket-powered cars on an enclosed arena pitch - and turned it into one of the most successful independent titles of the generation. The car physics model lets players jump, fly using boosters, and pull off acrobatic mid-air hits on the ball, creating an almost endless space for mastering advanced techniques like aerial passes or full-field defensive saves.
