Managing the boost pads scattered across the pitch, rotating with the team, and reading the ball's bounce off the walls turn every match into a fast tactical game, even though the rules can be explained in a single sentence.

Easy initial controls combined with a huge skill ceiling let the game function equally well as relaxed fun for casual players and as a respected esports discipline with professional leagues and tournaments watched by millions of viewers. The Rocket League Championship Series was among the first stably funded leagues for an independent title and helped prove that esports need not be reserved for major publisher brands. Matches are also an ideal length for viewing, about five minutes of pure playtime, with a clearly readable score and effective multi-angle instant replays of goals.

On PlayStation 4 the game ran at a high frame rate, which is absolutely essential for a title dependent on precisely timed hits, and the switch to a free-to-play model in 2020 further expanded the player base across platforms thanks to full cross-play. Crossover cosmetics with licenses like Batman, Ghostbusters, or Portal showed an unusual flexibility for a sports-arcade genre that otherwise stays purely focused on the gameplay itself. Critics praised the elegant, seemingly simple concept hiding a deep skill curve, and the game became a model example of how a simple idea can create a long-lasting cultural phenomenon.
ps4__rocket-league.teaser: Football played with rocket-powered cars in an enclosed arena, turned into a genuine esports phenomenon.

ps4__hollow-knight.article:
**Hollow Knight** was created by the small Australian studio Team Cherry, essentially just a handful of people, as a sprawling metroidvania set in the decaying underground insect kingdom of Hallownest, plagued by a mysterious infection. The nameless knight travels through interconnected caverns, catacombs, and gardens full of atmospheric, hand-drawn environments, and the level design rewards patient exploration, with the player charting the area's map themselves using purchased cartography equipment instead of an automatically revealed map. The charm system, through which the player fills a limited number of slots, also functions as a light form of build customization, letting them lean into faster healing, longer weapon reach, or silent movement.

The combat system combines precise platforming jumps with magic called Soul, charged by hitting enemies and then usable for healing or special attacks, while the difficulty of boss fights like Nightmare King Grimm ranks among the hardest in the genre. Losing currency on death and having to return to the site of the fall to reclaim one's own shade create a tension reminiscent of the Dark Souls series, with which Hollow Knight also shares its manner of storytelling: characters such as the mysterious Hollow Knight, the combative Hornet, or the tragic ruler of Hallownest form an elaborate mythology that players piece together from fragments and found scraps. A melancholic yet occasionally gently humorous atmosphere, complemented by Christopher Larkin's orchestral soundtrack, creates an unmistakable mood.

Critics showered the game with praise for the scope of its content, the depth of its combat, and its artistic cohesion despite a low budget, and it became one of the most beloved independent titles of the decade, fueling enormous anticipation for the long-delayed sequel Silksong. Free expansions like Hidden Dreams and Godmaster were also added by the studio long after release at no cost, earning it a reputation as an unusually generous and player-devoted development team. Today Hollow Knight is cited as proof that a hand-drawn game from a handful of people can boldly compete with the output of major publishers in both the scale of its world and the care of its craftsmanship.
ps4__hollow-knight.teaser: A sprawling metroidvania made by a handful of people from the Australian studio Team Cherry.

ps4__celeste.article:
**Celeste** is a precision platformer by Maddy Thorson and her small team about a young woman named Madeline who decides to climb Mount Celeste, and along the way faces not only deadly difficult jump sequences but also her own anxiety and depression, embodied by a dark version of herself. The controls are tuned down to the last detail - a double jump, a dash in the chosen direction, and wall climbing give the player precise tools capable of handling even the toughest passages, while the game generously offers instant respawns with no penalty for frequent dying, removing the frustration usually associated with difficult platformers. Every screen functions as a self-contained puzzle with one clean solution, so even after hundreds of falls the feeling remains that the mistake was always the player's own.

A pixel-art visual style with a distinct color palette for each chapter and music by Lena Raine that shifts with the situation give the whole experience an emotional rhythm. Alongside the main campaign, the game also offers extremely demanding B-Side and C-Side levels for players craving an even greater challenge, while an optional Assist Mode lets the game be slowed down or grants extra dashes so that truly everyone can reach the story. The side character Theo, met along the way up the mountain, and the narrator called Granny lend a sense of human warmth and companionship to what would otherwise seem a solitary climb.

The story sensitively and honestly addresses themes of mental health, self-acceptance, and overcoming one's own inner demons without lapsing into cheap sentimentality, and the final revelation of dark Madeline's true nature offers one of the most powerful treatments of this theme in the video game medium. Critics praised the flawless controls, the thoughtful level design, and the emotional depth, the game won Best Independent Game at the Game Awards, and it is still considered one of the best-crafted platformers of the modern era. The free Farewell expansion, released a year after the game, added an even more demanding and emotionally intense conclusion to Madeline's entire story.
ps4__celeste.teaser: A precision platformer about climbing a mountain, a journey that serves as a metaphor for anxiety and depression.

ps4__cuphead.article:
**Cuphead**, created by brothers Chad and Jared Moldenhauer of Studio MDHR, staked everything on a completely unique visual concept - the entire animation was hand-drawn and hand-painted using techniques imitating rubber-hose American cartoons from the 1930s, complemented by a period jazz swing soundtrack recorded by live musicians. Cuphead and his brother Mugman, after losing a bet with the Devil, must pay off their debt by collecting souls from a gallery of bizarre bosses scattered across a stylized map, which makes the game primarily a series of intense boss fights interspersed with classic run-and-gun levels.

Every fight requires memorizing attack patterns and precise dodging, the parry mechanic for deflecting pink objects further expands the defensive options while also charging a super attack, and the difficulty ranks among the notoriously high even for experienced genre players. Optional ammunition types, charms, and various shot variants let the player tailor their approach to a specific opponent, so defeating the toughest bosses is as much a matter of proper preparation as of reflexes. Cooperative two-player gameplay also let extremely demanding fights be shared between two people, so the game also worked as a beloved social activity beyond a purely solo experience.

Development itself took the Moldenhauer brothers nearly seven years and required selling the family home to help finance the project, which, after release and massive commercial success, turned into a legendary story of independent game creation. The unmistakable visual style drew attention even beyond the core gaming community, and the game became a symbol of how strongly an art direction can define the identity of an independent title. Critics praised both the breathtaking animation and the precision of the boss designs, and commercial success led to the Delicious Last Course expansion as well as its own animated series. Today Cuphead comes across as a title that cannot age, because its look was already deliberately ninety years old at the time of release.
ps4__cuphead.teaser: Hand-painted animation in the spirit of 1930s rubber-hose cartoons, with boss fights that spare no one.

ps4__hades.article:
**Hades** combined Supergiant Games' signature emphasis on storytelling and music with the roguelike genre: Zagreus, son of the god of the underworld, Hades, repeatedly attempts to escape the underworld for Mount Olympus in search of his mother Persephone, and each death sends him back to the start with a new selection of weapons and divine boons from figures of Greek mythology such as Zeus, Athena, or Ares. The key innovation is the fusion of the repeated dying typical of the roguelike genre with a fluid, continuously evolving narrative - characters remember previous attempts, new dialogue is revealed, and relationships deepen with every further fall, turning the frustration of failure into meaningful narrative progress.

The combat system offers six distinct weapons, each of which changes dramatically depending on the chosen combination of bonuses, guaranteeing enormous variability between individual runs; in an isometric view, the player fluidly combines a fast attack, a special move, a ranged ability, and an evasive dash. Permanent upgrades purchased between runs, along with the option to voluntarily raise the difficulty in exchange for better rewards, let everyone set their own pace of progression. A visual style drawing on Greek vase painting and comic-book aesthetics, together with an excellent soundtrack by Darren Korb, further heighten the atmosphere.

The voice performances, including the charismatic narrator Hades voiced by Logan Cunningham, give even the smallest characters of the underworld an unmistakable personality, while Zagreus's relationship arcs with characters like Megaera or Thanatos offer an unusually intimate look at Greek mythology. Hades also became one of the first titles to successfully use a long-term, community-followed early access development process on the Epic Games Store before its full release. Critics showered the game with nearly unanimous praise and a string of Game of the Year awards, firmly establishing the roguelike genre in mainstream awareness and opening the door to a sequel.
ps4__hades.teaser: A roguelike where dying moves the story forward; Greek mythology takes the lead roles.

ps4__disco-elysium.article:
**Disco Elysium** by Estonian studio ZA/UM is a game without a single fight in the traditional sense - the player wakes up as an amnesiac detective in the depressing port town of Revachol and must solve a murder, armed with nothing but dialogue, persuasion, and introspection. Instead of weapons and hit points, the game relies on an extensive skill system such as Logic, Empathy, or Electrochemistry, which speak directly to the player as inner voices commenting on the situation, creating a unique sense of the protagonist's fragmented, unreliable mind. Dice rolls decide the success of lines and minor actions, and failure is often as interesting as victory, since it pushes the story in an unexpected direction.

The so-called Thought Cabinet system, in which the player literally internalizes ideas that affect his abilities and worldview, is one of the genre's most original mechanics, letting the detective develop even outright bizarre or self-destructive personality traits. The hand-painted, oil-painting-like graphics and the subdued, atmospheric soundtrack give Revachol the look of a rundown postwar town, where crumbling plaster equals crumbling ideals. The political spectrum from communism to fascism, existential crisis, and dark humor are handled with a literary quality comparable to serious fiction, which makes the game function more like an interactive novel than a classic RPG.

The 2021 Final Cut version brought full voice acting of all dialogue to PlayStation 4 along with new content, turning what was originally a text-heavy title into an experience accessible even from the couch. The fact that the game was written by a team with roots in an artistic collective with a literary background shows in an unusually open and unsentimental reflection on politics, class, and personal failure, still a rarity in video games. Critics praised it with extremely high scores for its originality of writing and systemic design, the game won a string of prestigious awards for its script, and it established ZA/UM as one of the most distinctive studios in the contemporary RPG scene.
ps4__disco-elysium.teaser: An RPG without a single fight — you solve the detective mystery through words and your own fractured psyche.

ps4__cyberpunk-2077.article:
**Cyberpunk 2077** marked CD Projekt Red's move, after the triumph of The Witcher 3, from fantasy to the dark, neon-lit Night City, a metropolis full of corporate greed and technological transhumanism, where mercenary V teams up with the digital ghost of legendary rocker Johnny Silverhand, stored in his own mind thanks to a dangerous biochip. The game combines a first-person view with RPG elements, lets the player customize their build through cybernetic implants, hacking, or direct confrontation, and offers extensive branching of dialogue and missions depending on the chosen approach. The city's division into districts with their own architecture, gangs, and social climate makes Night City one of the most densely built game cities ever.

The release on the older console generation was marred by serious technical problems - frequent crashes, bugs, and insufficient optimization led to the game's temporary removal from the PlayStation Store and a wave of criticism directed at overly ambitious marketing. The extensive fixes that followed, the next-gen update, and the Phantom Liberty expansion featuring Idris Elba gradually turned public opinion around, and the game became a respected title whose atmosphere, main story, and performances are still praised today. The Cyberpunk 2077 case became a textbook example of how a long road to redemption can turn disappointment into an acclaimed comeback.

Keanu Reeves's performance as Johnny Silverhand, shot with dedication comparable to Hollywood productions, remains one of the game's strongest assets since launch, while Night City's visual design, inspired by the classic cyberpunk genre of the eighties, set a new aesthetic standard for the entire genre. The accompanying anime series Edgerunners by studio Trigger also brought a new audience to the game and indirectly helped turn public opinion in the title's favor. Years later, Cyberpunk 2077 feels like a game whose greatest strength was never the technology, but its story about the finiteness of life in a city that promises immortality.
ps4__cyberpunk-2077.teaser: After The Witcher, CD Projekt Red bet on neon-lit Night City and Keanu Reeves as Silverhand.

ps4__assassin-s-creed-origins.article:
**Assassin's Creed Origins** reshaped, after a year-long break for the series, Ubisoft Montreal's action-adventure with cover and counterattacks into a full-fledged action RPG with enemy levels, a skill tree, and loot, laying the foundation for the franchise's modern direction. Bayek, an Egyptian Medjay serving the pharaoh, sets out for revenge in Ptolemaic Egypt under Cleopatra's rule against a mysterious organization whose roots ultimately explain the very origin of the Assassin brotherhood, making the game function as the mythological beginning of the whole series. The new combat system with distinct weapon types, a bow, and blocks instead of automatic counters brought the game closer to the Souls genre and The Witcher.

The vast, meticulously reconstructed map of ancient Egypt, from Alexandria to desert oases, is one of the series' most impressive settings; the player traverses it on horseback and camel, sails the Nile, and exploration is aided by the eagle Senu, which replaced the classic synchronization towers as a tool for marking targets. The reconstruction of the Lighthouse of Alexandria, the Great Library, and the pyramids of Giza was created in collaboration with historians and Egyptologists, which is why the educational Discovery Tour mode, exploring the world entirely without violence, is still used in school history classes today.

Bayek's discovery of his own role in an ancient conflict between the Order of the Ancients and the future Assassins gave meaning to a decade's worth of previously disjointed hints about the series' ancient origins, and his relationship with his wife Aya is among the best-written threads in the entire brand. Critics praised the strong revival of a stagnating series, the scope of the world, and the depth of the systems; the game became commercially very successful and launched a new RPG era continued by Odyssey and Valhalla. On PlayStation 4, the sprawling Egypt took a toll on the frame rate, but the views from pyramid tops at sunrise remain among the visually best that generation had to offer.
ps4__assassin-s-creed-origins.teaser: A series reboot that turned cover-based action into a full-fledged RPG with a skill tree.

ps4__assassin-s-creed-odyssey.article:
**Assassin's Creed Odyssey** deepened the RPG direction started in Origins and set the game in ancient Greece during the Peloponnesian War between Sparta and Athens, where for the first time in the series the player could choose between two protagonists - the mercenary Alexios or the mercenary Kassandra - with fully voiced dialogue choices affecting the story's course and its ending. The vast map, encompassing hundreds of islands of the Aegean Sea, is connected by sea travel in the style of earlier series entries like Black Flag, complemented by grand naval battles and massive clashes between the armies of Sparta and Athens that the player can actively join.

The RPG systems offer greater freedom in building a character based on stealth kills, archery, or direct combat, romantic relationships with side characters, and a mercenary system that hunts the player according to their notoriety, so slaughtering guards has tangible consequences hours later. The so-called Odyssey Plus system later let players freely adjust the difficulty of individual combat and story elements, Ubisoft's response to criticism over the balance of RPG systems against the series' more traditional style. The scope of content and the game's length are among the largest in the entire series, which sparked some players' discussions about padding and the presence of microtransactions.

The Fate of Atlantis expansion additionally transported players to the fully fantastical setting of mythical Atlantis and the Greek underworld, showing Ubisoft's willingness to experiment with mythological elements far beyond historical realism. Visually the game bet on a vividly colored, postcard-like Greece with olive groves, marble, and turquoise sea, thanks to which even simple sailing between islands becomes entertainment in its own right. Critics praised the elaborate world, Melissanthi Mahut's performance as Kassandra, and the depth of the RPG mechanics; the game became one of the commercially most successful entries in the series.
ps4__assassin-s-creed-odyssey.teaser: Ancient Greece, two selectable protagonists, and for the first time fully voiced dialogue choices.

ps4__marvel-s-spider-man-miles-morales.article:
**Marvel's Spider-Man: Miles Morales** was Insomniac Games' use of the success of its first Spider-Man to create a more compact but narratively focused spin-off about young Miles Morales, who at Christmas takes on the responsibility of protecting New York while Peter Parker goes on vacation, and faces both the energy corporation Roxxon and his own struggle to master his newly gained bioelectric powers. Miles has a different combat style than Peter - his invisibility and electrifying Venom strikes offer a different tactical dynamic from the original, while the smaller, snow-covered version of Manhattan allowed the developers to focus on density of detail rather than sheer size.

Swinging on webs remained just as smooth and addictive as in the first game, and the new acrobatic animations reflect Miles's inexperience as well as his street-inspired, dance-tinged personality. The game also served as a technology showcase for the PlayStation 5's capabilities with ray tracing and near-instant loading, though it also released on PlayStation 4, where it retained an impressive look for a snow-covered metropolis. The Christmas atmosphere of Harlem, with decorations and festive lighting, gave the game a different mood from the first game's summery tone.

The story sensitively explores themes of growing up, family loss, and the responsibility Miles takes on as a young Black hero in a role that significantly enriched superhero media representation, and the community dimension, where the hero defends his own neighborhood and its residents, strengthens the story's more personal, local tone. Critics praised the emotional depth despite the shorter length and the excellent combat system; the game was commercially successful and cemented Miles as a distinct character alongside Peter Parker. The short but intense campaign also proved that a spin-off need not be seen as an inferior add-on, but as a full-fledged, thoroughly polished experience in its own right.
ps4__marvel-s-spider-man-miles-morales.teaser: A compact Christmas-set spin-off about the young successor with bioelectric powers.

ps4__journey.article:
**Journey** was created by thatgamecompany, a studio that had already built a reputation with the meditative titles Flow and Flower, as a short but exceptionally emotional journey without a single word, dialogue, or any text explaining the plot. A figure clad in a red cloak crosses an endless desert toward a beam of light shining from a distant mountain, with walking, jumping, and brief gliding via a lengthening scarf - collected from scattered ancient cloth - as the only forms of movement. The controls fit onto two buttons, and the game never explains what the player is supposed to do - direction is dictated solely by the composition of the landscape and the light on the horizon.

A completely unique element is anonymous online cooperation - during the journey, the player randomly encounters other real players with no possibility of text or voice chat, the only means of communication being a musical tone, which creates an unexpectedly intimate bond between strangers sharing the same path. Because fellow players' names only appear in the closing credits, the companion remains an anonymous silhouette throughout, to whom players nonetheless form a surprisingly strong attachment. The visual style with rippling sand resembling a water surface and Austin Wintory's orchestral soundtrack, later nominated for a Grammy, amplify the emotional impact of the roughly two-hour experience.

Critics showered the game with an unprecedented number of Game of the Year awards despite its unusually short length and lack of traditional game objectives, and Journey became one of the central arguments in the era's debate over whether video games can be art. The remastered version for PlayStation 4 from 2015 brought the game to a new generation of players in higher resolution and with a smoother frame rate. To this day it's cited as proof that video games can tell stories in a purely emotional language rather than a textual one, and as a title that can be finished in a single evening yet stays in memory for years.
ps4__journey.teaser: A short, moving wordless journey from the creators of Flow and Flower; a game full of beauty.

ps4__dreams.article:
**Dreams** pushed Media Molecule, the creator of LittleBigPlanet, and its concept of player-made content to an entirely new level with a tool that lets players create practically anything - from platformers to shooters to music videos and cinematic demos - using an intuitive sculpting interface controlled with the Move motion controller or a standard gamepad. Modeling works by shaping and blending matter in three-dimensional space, complemented by tools for animation, logic, music, and sound, so a single person can handle the entire production pipeline of a small game.

The game itself offers a short, dreamlike campaign called Art's Dream as a showcase of the engine's capabilities, but the real core of the experience is the community ecosystem, which lets millions of players share, remix, and rate each other's creations, forming an ever-growing library of community-made content. The Dreamiverse system let players browse created content by genre, popularity, or community recommendation, creating an environment closer to a curated gallery than a typical video game menu. Media Molecule also regularly selected and promoted exceptional player creations, inspiring real artistic and gaming careers and showing just how far a tool can be pushed beyond its creators' original vision once placed in the community's hands.

The technical sophistication of the tools allowed for surprisingly elaborate projects, including complete JRPGs, horror adventures, and experimental music, making Dreams function more as a creative platform than a traditional video game. Despite the technical brilliance and enthusiastic response from the creative community, the game remained somewhat niche for the wider mainstream audience due to its steep learning curve and the fact that results were tied to a single platform. Critics praised the incredible ambition and possibilities of the tool, and Dreams is still cited today as proof of the creative potential the PlayStation 4 hardware was able to unlock.
ps4__dreams.teaser: A tool for creating anything from Media Molecule — platformers, shooters, and even film demos.

ps4__gravity-rush-2.article:
**Gravity Rush 2**, the sequel to the originally handheld PS Vita game, brought Kat, a girl with the mysterious ability to manipulate gravity, into a full-fledged console adventure with a significantly expanded world of floating cities inspired by French Art Nouveau and Victorian architecture. The core mechanic remains the ability to change the direction of gravity, letting Kat literally walk on walls and ceilings or fall upward, creating a completely unique sense of spatial orientation unmatched by other action-adventures. The sequel additionally added two alternative gravity styles, heavy and light, letting the player change the strength and speed of attacks and movement depending on the situation.

The story continues the first game and deepens the mythology of the world of Hekseville and the relationships between Kat and her companions, while the playful, comic-book- and anime-inspired visual style, hand-drawn cutscenes, and Japanese voice acting give the game an unmistakable identity. The photo mode and the ability to freely fly the camera around the vast floating islands of Hekseville and the new city of Jirga Para Lhao gave players room to admire the unusual architecture of the environment from angles no other game offered. Orientation in space is confusing at first, but once the player gets used to it, simply moving through the city becomes one of the greatest joys of the whole game.

Despite its technical and design originality, the game did not achieve commercial success matching the effort invested, which became one of the factors leading to the later closure of Sony's Japan Studio. The end of Japan Studio in 2021 put a definitive end to hopes for a third installment, making Gravity Rush 2 the series' last major entry and one of the last strongly Japanese-flavored first-party Sony projects. Critics praised the unique movement system and aesthetics, earning the game cult status as a commercially overlooked gem of the PlayStation 4 generation.
ps4__gravity-rush-2.teaser: The sequel to the game about a girl who controls gravity; walking on the walls and ceilings of an Art Nouveau city.

ps4__until-dawn.article:
**Until Dawn** was created by Supermassive Games as an interactive horror built on the motifs of slasher films like Halloween or Friday the 13th, in which a group of eight young friends spend a night at a remote mountain lodge one year after a tragic accident marred their previous visit, and must face a mysterious threat hidden in the surrounding woods. The game's key concept is the butterfly-effect mechanic - almost every decision, dialogue choice, or successfully completed quick-time event can influence which characters survive until morning, with any of the eight main characters able to die unexpectedly at any time regardless of their apparent importance to the story.

The game cannot be reloaded to undo a bad decision, so even a minor failure in reacting to a prompt remains a permanent part of the player's story, and the mechanic of holding the controller perfectly still during moments when a character is hiding can ratchet up tension more than most classic jump scares. The game hired recognizable acting talent including Hayden Panettiere and Rutger Hauer, whose motion-capture performances heightened the cinematic atmosphere of a B-movie horror with a serious undertone, while the fixed, cinematically composed camera angles evoke classic survival horrors of the nineties.

The mysterious psychiatrist Dr. Hill, who comments on the player's decisions through a metaphorical torture chamber between chapters, adds an unusual self-reflexive layer about one's own role as both viewer and participant in a horror story. Choosing between seemingly insignificant actions, such as discarding or keeping a weapon, can have unexpectedly far-reaching consequences later in the game, making replays feel almost like a detective investigation of one's own past decisions. Critics praised the tense atmosphere, humor, and ambition of the branching narrative; the game was commercially successful and inspired Supermassive to create further anthology horror titles in The Dark Pictures series.
ps4__until-dawn.teaser: An interactive slasher horror where the butterfly effect decides who in the group survives the night.

ps4__horizon-forbidden-west.article:
**Horizon Forbidden West** expanded Guerrilla Games' successful first-game concept into a much more varied environment along the American west coast, from the flooded ruins of San Francisco to desert canyons and dense rainforests, while Aloy continues searching for the cause of a mysterious blight decimating the planet's remaining vegetation and uncovers ever darker secrets of an ancient civilization. The combat system against mechanical creatures was enriched with new weapons, a diving ability, exploration of underwater locations, and a more elaborate system of dismantling and using parts from defeated machines against other enemies.

A new gallery of machines, including the massive Tremortusk and the predatory Slitherfang, further expands the tactical depth of combat based on finding weak points, which the player targets with a bow and various types of ammunition after scanning the target. A new gliding wing and grappling hook system allows for much more vertical and acrobatic movement across the landscape than in the first game, while the underwater locations bring an entirely new type of puzzles and battles with aquatic machines. The story deepens Aloy's relationships with new and old allies and expands the world's mythology by revealing the fate of the rest of humanity outside America.

Critics praised the visual presentation, variety of environments, and improved combat mechanics as a worthy sequel to the acclaimed first game; the game was commercially successful and cemented Horizon as one of Sony's key modern franchises. The fact that the game released simultaneously on both PlayStation 4 and 5 despite its enormous technical demands showed Guerrilla Games' determination not to leave the older console generation and its players without access to the sequel of a beloved series. Even on older hardware, the vistas of overgrown skyscrapers and herds of machines roaming the landscape remain among the most visually striking scenes that PlayStation 4 managed in its final phase.
ps4__horizon-forbidden-west.teaser: Aloy continues her journey among mechanical creatures in a far more varied coastal setting.

xbox-one__halo-5-guardians.article:
**Halo 5: Guardians** was Xbox One's flagship title and clear proof that 343 Industries could keep the Bungie-founded series alive even after its creators' departure. The campaign for the first time puts the four-member Fireteam Osiris, led by Agent Locke, front and center, as they hunt the renegade Master Chief and his Blue Team. The narrative is more fragmented and less focused than before, yet it offers grand environments, new Promethean creatures, and a well-executed squad ability system - the player can issue orders to teammates, be revived by them, or send them to a signaled target. The campaign can also be played entirely in online co-op with up to four players, a first for the series.

New sprint, boost dodge, ground pound, and stabilized hover-while-aiming abilities significantly sped up movement and turned battles into a more acrobatic affair than in previous installments, without losing Halo's signature rhythm where an enemy first loses its shields and only then its life. But the title's main draw became its multiplayer: the classic Arena mode returned to fast, symmetrical arena combat without outside loadouts, while the massive Warzone mode combined twelve-on-twelve players with AI enemies, bosses, and a card system letting players unlock weapons and vehicles with in-game currency.

The graphics engine achieved native 1080p resolution on Xbox One at a stable 60 frames per second, a rare standard among console shooters in 2015, albeit at the cost of dynamically scaling resolution in the most demanding scenes. Despite criticism from fans over the missing split-screen co-op and a somewhat uneven story, Halo 5 remains the technically most polished multiplayer Halo of the generation and proof of the brand's viability under new leadership. Today it's remembered as the installment that pushed the series toward fast modern action while also showing just how sensitive the Halo community is to any change to its traditions.
xbox-one__halo-5-guardians.teaser: The flagship of the Xbox One; for the first time, the four-member Fireteam Osiris takes center stage.

xbox-one__halo-master-chief-collection.article:
**Halo: The Master Chief Collection** was, upon its release in November 2014, the most ambitious collection in the history of console shooters - it bundled remastered Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary, Halo 2 Anniversary, Halo 3, and Halo 4 into a single package with reworked graphics, a unified menu, and combined multiplayer featuring over a hundred maps. Players could switch on the fly between the original graphics from the Xbox and Xbox 360 consoles and newly created high-resolution models, which for Halo 2 Anniversary meant completely redone cutscenes by studio Blur. The campaigns of all four games could be played in online and local co-op with up to four players, across all difficulties including the legendary Legendary.

The collection also offered playlists compiled across the individual games, such as a sequence of vehicle missions or a showcase of the series' toughest moments, and a challenge system that gave the old campaigns a reason for repeat playthroughs. However, the launch was plagued by notorious server infrastructure problems that essentially paralyzed multiplayer for months, earning 343 Industries a public apology and a subsequent free content expansion as compensation.

Over the years, though, MCC became one of the generation's most supported titles: it gained mod support, cross-platform play with PC, 4K textures for Xbox One X, improved controls, and the additional Halo 3: ODST, including its campaign and Firefight mode. For a generation of players who never played the original titles on older hardware, the collection represented the only reasonable way to experience the entire arc of Master Chief's story, from the fall of Reach to the fight against the Didact, in a single package for the price of one full game. Today it stands as a model of how classic series should be cared for, and at the same time as a reminder that not even the best intentions can save a launch that goes technically wrong.
xbox-one__halo-master-chief-collection.teaser: The most ambitious shooter collection of 2014 — four Halo games in one package.

xbox-one__gears-of-war-4.article:
**Gears of War 4** marked the handover of the reins from Epic Games to the newly founded studio The Coalition, and at the same time a generational leap in the story, twenty-five years into the future. The new lead character is JD Fenix, Marcus's son, who alongside Kait Diaz and Del Walker fights not only the new threat known as the Swarm, but also the authoritarian COG government he once served as a soldier. The return of an older Marcus to the plot gives the narrative a more personal, family-driven dimension that the original trilogy lacked, and a darker, less parodic tone underscores the sense that the war on Sera never truly ended.

The core of the series remained untouched — the cover system, the brutal chainsaw Lancer, active reload, and the emphasis on team tactics in the cooperative campaign. The Coalition added a dynamic tornado that reshapes the battlefield, tears away cover, and sweeps enemies away, along with new robotic opponents called DeeBees, whose behavior differs markedly from the organic Swarm: they break apart piece by piece, are harder to finish off, and force players to change the rhythm of firefights. The Unreal Engine 4 graphics engine pushed the series to a new visual level on Xbox One, with detailed textures, realistic lighting, and elaborate weather particle effects; the scenes where a windstorm tears apart sheet-metal structures and reshapes the passability of an entire arena rank among the campaign's most striking moments.

The multiplayer offered the classic Versus mode as well as a reworked Horde with ten character classes, their upgrades, and the placement of defensive structures around the mobile Fabricator, turning the cooperative mode into a game of role division and resource management. A new collectible card system for weapons, skills, and skins became the foundation of the reward economy for later entries in the series as well. The game was also among the first titles to fully support Xbox Play Anywhere, letting players enjoy it on both console and PC with a single purchase and shared progress. Gears of War 4 thus proved that the series could work without its founders, and laid a solid foundation for the rest of the new trilogy.
xbox-one__gears-of-war-4.teaser: The reins pass to new studio The Coalition; the story jumps 25 years forward, with JD Fenix.

xbox-one__gears-5.article:
**Gears 5** shifted the series' narrative from JD Fenix to Kait Diaz, whose visions and family past lead her straight into the heart of the mystery surrounding the Swarm and the enigmatic Locust. For the first time in the series' history, the campaign offered a partially open world — snowy plains and sand deserts can be explored on a sail-sled and later on the wheeled Skiff hovercraft, gathering side quests, treasures, and upgrades for the little robot Jack, whom the player controls and who can invisibly stun enemies or steal their weapons. Jack can also be handed over to a co-op partner, so even a support role has full meaning in cooperative play.

With this move, The Coalition noticeably enriched the game's pacing without abandoning the core cover-based shooting and brutal execution animations the series is built on: the open areas serve as breathing room between carefully directed corridor firefights. Visually, it is one of the most striking titles of the generation, with photorealistic snowy environments running even on the base Xbox One at a solid frame rate, while the Xbox One X pushed the game to a substantially higher resolution. Snowstorms, swirling dust, and vast vistas give the campaign an unusually melancholic atmosphere, underscored by a subdued orchestral score.

The multiplayer expanded the beloved Horde mode with five playable factions and an elaborate skill tree, added a new PvP mode called Escalation aimed at the esports scene, and also offered the cooperative Escape mode, in which a trio of players flee a hive ahead of spreading toxic gas. The game launched simultaneously on Xbox One and Windows 10 as part of Xbox Play Anywhere and Xbox Game Pass, reaching a record number of players right on release day. It subsequently received free updates for years afterward with new characters, maps, and operations, keeping an active community for a long time. Gears 5 is regarded as one of the high points of the whole series and firm proof of The Coalition studio's creative maturity.
xbox-one__gears-5.teaser: The series' first partially open world; the narrative shifts focus from JD Fenix to Kait Diaz.

xbox-one__forza-horizon-2.article:
**Forza Horizon 2** moved the fictional car festival from Colorado to sunny southern Europe, specifically to a setting inspired by France and Italy, and delivered an open world with no loading screens between drives. Playground Games used the new ForzaTech engine, shared with the main Motorsport series, which gave the game a more realistic weather model, including storms that change road grip in real time. For the first time, the festival was split into several separate hubs, between which the player freely drives across vineyards, coastal roads, and mountain switchbacks, with traffic and non-playable drivers reacting more naturally to the player's actions than before.

A key change from the first game was the ability to leave the road practically anywhere — fields, dirt tracks, and dry riverbeds became shortcuts, and the game actively encouraged players to seek them out. The car roster totaled over two hundred licensed vehicles, from ordinary hatchbacks to supercars like the Bugatti Veyron, each with a finely modeled interior and a fully usable cockpit view. A new feature was the Drivatar system, which projected the driving style of the player's friends, controlled by artificial intelligence, into the world, making it possible to race against virtual copies of real people even offline.

The game supported seamless switching between the solo campaign and online multiplayer while driving, without interruption or menus, a revolutionary approach to open-world racing games at the time; a group of friends could meet in one shared world and move between individual events together. The atmosphere was rounded out by a lineup of radio stations with a varied musical selection and the festival's easygoing summer tone, which defined the series for years to come. Although the game also came out on Xbox 360 in a different, separately developed version, it was the Xbox One version that made full use of the new console's power and set the bar for the visual and atmospheric quality of every subsequent Horizon entry.
xbox-one__forza-horizon-2.teaser: The car festival moves from Colorado to southern Europe; more realistic weather, no loading screens.

xbox-one__forza-horizon-3.article:
**Forza Horizon 3** moved the festival to Australia and became the first entry in the series where the player figures not merely as a participant but directly as the director of the entire Horizon festival. The open world offered an extraordinary variety of settings, from tropical rainforests through outback deserts to the metropolitan Surfers Paradise, all connected seamlessly with no loading. New to the series were four specialized hubs focused on off-road, drifting, aerial stunts, and classic championships, whose development the player plans out themselves, deciding which direction their version of the festival will take.

Thanks to the power of the Xbox One and especially the Xbox One X, which supported the game in 4K resolution, Playground Games pushed the visual quality to a new level with dense vegetation, realistic lighting, and a dynamic day-night cycle. A nighttime setting and storms with real lightning affecting visibility were added, so the same route feels like two entirely different places at dawn and in a heavy downpour. The game was the first in the series to support full four-player cooperative play in the open world and offered a robust Blueprint route editor, which the community used to create their own races and share them worldwide.

The car roster exceeded three hundred fifty vehicles, and the radio stations offered a genre-diverse lineup from electronic music to rock, with the player also able to build their own station. The Hot Wheels expansion, with a closed track full of orange ramps and loops, showed just how well the series' open world gets along with pure arcade fantasy, while Blizzard Mountain added a snowy mountain setting. Forza Horizon 3 is still considered by many reviewers to be the peak of the series thanks to its perfect balance between arcade driving feel, technical depth, and the atmosphere of an endless summer vacation that made the series famous. Its later removal from digital stores due to expired licenses has also made it a title that's now hard for new players to get hold of.
xbox-one__forza-horizon-3.teaser: For the first time, the player is directly the director of the Horizon festival; variety ranging from rainforests to a big city.

xbox-one__forza-horizon-4.article:
**Forza Horizon 4** brought the series to Great Britain and introduced a major new system feature — dynamically changing seasons, where the entire open-world map transforms every week from snowy winter through blossoming spring and lush summer to autumn leaves, with each season changing road grip, available routes, and the look of the environment. In winter a lake freezes over, opening up a route otherwise inaccessible; in autumn, muddy dirt roads punish too heavy a right foot. With this, Playground Games created a living world that keeps evolving without the player having to wait for the next expansion.

For the first time, the Horizon festival functions as a shared open world, where players encounter other live participants directly while driving, without having to enter separate lobbies, creating a sense of a genuinely living automotive community. The car roster exceeded four hundred fifty vehicles, a housing system let players buy homes across the map and unlock bonuses through them, and the new Horizon Life framework offered leisure activities beyond racing, including winter fun and collectible challenges. Forzathon Live events were also added — time-limited community tasks with an immediate reward that connected players across the world in real time.

The visuals on Xbox One X reached native 4K resolution with rich vegetation changing according to the season, while the base Xbox One held a steady thirty frames per second. The driving model remained true to the series' arcade-leaning but technically honest approach, in which every car handles noticeably differently, while the game never punishes newcomers, since difficulty and assists can be tuned almost however one likes. Forza Horizon 4 is still cited as one of the most successful and longest-supported titles of the entire generation, with regular content updates for years after release, and for many players it remained the main reason to get an Xbox One in the first place.
xbox-one__forza-horizon-4.teaser: Dynamic seasons change the entire map every week — winter, spring, summer, and autumn.

xbox-one__forza-motorsport-5.article:
**Forza Motorsport 5** was an Xbox One launch title and the first showcase of what the new generation would bring to simulation racing. Turn 10 Studios used the new console's power for photorealistic lighting of cars and tracks, while laser scanning of the road surface allowed the precise capture of asphalt imperfections on real circuits like Silverstone, Spa-Francorchamps, or Laguna Seca. Cars received fully modeled interiors, and the cockpit view became a fully viable option for wheel-and-pedal play as well. Running at 1080p at a steady sixty frames per second was a non-negotiable requirement for the series, to which Turn 10 subordinated a number of visual compromises.

New was a reworked Drivatar system, using cloud computing power for the first time to generate opponents that learn from real players' driving style and then race against them even in their absence. The damage model and physics grew noticeably more precise compared to previous entries, as did tire behavior and wear over longer races, so racing strategy began to matter even outside the narrow circle of hardcore simulation fans. The engine sound recordings, which Turn 10 captured directly from real cars on the circuits, remained technically unmatched and defined the honest, simulation-focused approach of the Motorsport brand in contrast to its more arcade-leaning sister series, Horizon.

At launch, the game suffered from a limited selection of cars and tracks due to the short development cycle dictated by the new console's launch, leading to criticism of the pricing policy for additional content sold as car packs, as well as of the reward economy, which developers had to adjust after release. Many players also missed favorite circuits from previous entries. Forza Motorsport 5 thus mainly served as a showcase of the Xbox One's graphical possibilities right at the console's launch, and as the technical foundation on which later entries in the series built the content it itself lacked.
xbox-one__forza-motorsport-5.teaser: A launch title for the Xbox One; laser-scanned tracks and photorealistic car lighting.

xbox-one__forza-motorsport-6.article:
**Forza Motorsport 6** fixed most of the shortcomings that plagued the launch fifth entry, offering substantially richer content right from the start — more than four hundred fifty cars and over two dozen circuits, including a newly rendered track in Rio de Janeiro. The return of beloved tracks from previous entries and a wider selection of both historic and modern cars gave the career mode noticeably more staying power from the very first minute compared to its predecessor. Turn 10 Studios improved the weather system, which now included night races with realistic headlight lighting and rain with puddles affecting tire grip, forcing players to hunt for the dry line, a first in the series' history.

The Drivatar system underwent further refinement of its AI behavior, better simulating the aggression and mistakes of real players, whose data the opponents learned from, so the starting grid felt less like a scripted train and more like a race against people. The game placed emphasis on a return to an honest economy without microtransactions following criticism of the previous entry, offering more generous rewards for driving and a more elaborate career structure divided into seasons by car type. Mod cards were also added, letting players increase their earnings in exchange for tougher race conditions, such as disabled assists or a worse starting position.

The multiplayer supported races with up to twenty-four players simultaneously and also offered modes dedicated to specific series, such as Le Mans prototypes or American muscle cars. Visually, the game ran at 1080p and a steady sixty frames per second, which, together with its elaborate engine sound design, placed it among the technically most advanced racing simulations of the generation; the deep assist options also let the game be tuned from relaxed arcade driving to raw simulation without any aids whatsoever. Forza Motorsport 6 is therefore seen by many fans as the series' return to its roots of honest, content-packed simulation racing.
xbox-one__forza-motorsport-6.teaser: Fixed the launch title's flaws; over 450 cars and richer content from the very start of the career.

xbox-one__forza-motorsport-7.article:
**Forza Motorsport 7** was the last entry in the main simulation series on Xbox One and also the most extensive one — it offered over seven hundred licensed cars and more than thirty tracks, including the return of the iconic Nürburgring Nordschleife circuit. Turn 10 Studios made full use of the Xbox One X's power for native 4K resolution at sixty frames per second, making the game one of the visually most impressive racing simulations of the generation, with dynamic weather including storms, fog, and changing daylight affecting traction.

A new track conditions system allowed variable weather to be set directly for individual career races, increasing variety and difficulty; driving in a downpour on the Nordschleife ranks among the most demanding experiences console racing offered at the time. The career mode connected individual car series into a comprehensive cross-section of automotive history, from formula cars to legendary muscle cars, divided into progressively unlocked league tiers. The game also offered full support for wheels and pedals as well as an elaborate livery editor, with which the community created and shared thousands of custom car designs.

The collectible reward-crate system, in which players unlocked cards with cars, add-ons, and modifiers for race wins, caused controversy; due to its resemblance to loot boxes and a planned link to paid currency, it became a target of sharp criticism, and Turn 10 eventually removed the microtransactions from the game. Despite this controversy, the driving physics, the Drivatar system, and the audiovisual treatment of the engines remained at the absolute top of the genre, and the game kept its reputation as the most extensive console simulator of its time. Forza Motorsport 7 thus defined, through its sheer scope, the peak of the brand's simulation focus before the series went quiet for several years and returned only as a reboot on the next console generation.
xbox-one__forza-motorsport-7.teaser: The last entry in the series on Xbox One; over 700 cars and native 4K at 60 frames per second.

xbox-one__sunset-overdrive.article:
**Sunset Overdrive** was a wild exclusive from California-based studio Insomniac Games, which, after years of working with Sony, took on a game for the rival platform for the first time. It takes place in the fictional city of Sunset City, flooded after a catastrophic accident involving an energy drink with mutants called OD, and it bets everything on a completely loose, self-ironic tone full of fourth-wall breaks, pop-culture references, and brightly colored, comic-book-styled visuals. The player character is fully customizable, from gender through hairstyle to absurd costumes, so character creation itself joins in on the game's joking tone.

At the core of the gameplay is a movement system reminiscent of extreme sports — the player grinds along power lines and railings, bounces off trampolines, awnings, and billboards, and remains constantly airborne, avoiding damage while charging up bonus weapon abilities. Stopping practically means losing, so the game forces continuous, fluid movement through the city, and combat turns into more of a choreography than a firefight. The arsenal includes absurd inventions, from vinyl records fired as sharp projectiles to a cannon launching explosive teddy bears, and the longer the player stays in motion, the higher the combo score and bonuses they earn.

The game also included the eight-player cooperative Chaos Squad mode, in which players together face waves of enemies and bosses across the open city, with results feeding back into the solo campaign. Insomniac Games bet on humor instead of a serious tone, setting itself apart markedly from competing open worlds, and a punk-rock soundtrack keeps pace as high as the gameplay. Sunset Overdrive, thanks to its originality and energetic gameplay, became one of the most cited true exclusives of the early Xbox One era, even though it commercially never reached the level of the platform's big action brands.
xbox-one__sunset-overdrive.teaser: A crazy exclusive from Insomniac Games; a self-mocking tone and a fight against OD mutants.

xbox-one__ori-and-blind-forest.article:
**Ori and the Blind Forest** is a fairy-tale-beautiful platformer from Austrian studio Moon Studios, combining hand-painted backgrounds inspired by Studio Ghibli's animated films with precise metroidvania design. The story follows an orphaned forest spirit named Ori and his light companion Sein, who set out to save the dying forest of Nibel after a devastating storm robbed it of life. The emotionally powerful opening, without a single line of dialogue, in which Ori loses his guardian Naru, ranks among the most cited moments of the whole generation and sets the tone for a game that tells its story purely through image, movement, and music.

Gameplay gradually unlocks new abilities such as a double jump, a gliding dash, or Bash, which lets the player bounce off an enemy projectile and launch themselves in the opposite direction; it is this ability that turns movement into true acrobatics and opens up returns to previously inaccessible parts of the interconnected world, as is typical for the metroidvania genre. A key element of the difficulty is the save system built around the Soul Link ability, which the player activates at will at the cost of an in-game resource, forcing tactical decisions in the middle of dangerous passages. Escape sequences, such as the flooding Ginso Tree, rank among the genre's most demanding and, at the same time, most memorable scenes.

The music was composed by Gareth Coker, and the orchestral pieces accompanying key scenes rank among the decade's most acclaimed game soundtracks, since they weave dynamically together with what's happening on screen. A year later, an expanded Definitive Edition was released with new areas, abilities, a faster travel option, and better-balanced difficulty. Ori and the Blind Forest proved that Microsoft could also support smaller artistic projects alongside its big action exclusives, and it became one of the most beloved titles on the whole platform, as well as a gateway into the genre for a great many players.
xbox-one__ori-and-blind-forest.teaser: A hand-painted metroidvania inspired by Studio Ghibli; the emotional story of a forest spirit.

xbox-one__ori-and-will-of-wisps.article:
**Ori and the Will of the Wisps** built on the success of the first game with a substantially larger and more elaborate world, new gameplay mechanics, and a more emotional, more mature story. After the hatching of the owl chick Ku, Ori sets out on a journey to the lost forest of Niwen to save the dying tree of life, with the main threat being the disfigured owl Shriek, whose own tragic fate lends the story an unusual degree of empathy even for its antagonist. The narrative again unfolds almost entirely without words, through gestures, glances, and music alone, and yet manages to be even more striking than in the first game.

Moon Studios expanded the combat system with a genuine arsenal of weapons such as a sword, a bow, and a hammer, pushing the game closer to the action genre and away from its predecessor's purely contemplative platforming. The world is considerably more open, with side quests, merchants, a gradually built-up little village, and an upgrade system using shards that the player freely equips according to their playstyle. A new automatic save system replaced Sein's manual activation, making demanding passages accessible to a broader audience without losing tension, and full-fledged boss fights were also added, something the first game lacked entirely.

Visually, it is one of the most aesthetically accomplished titles of the generation, with picturesque biomes ranging from flooded caves to desert dunes, and with striking escape sequences in which the whole screen turns into a chase on the edge of the player's reflexes. Once again, they are accompanied by a gripping orchestral soundtrack by Gareth Coker, who manages to move from quiet melancholy to a full orchestra within a single scene. The game launched simultaneously on Xbox One and PC as part of Xbox Game Pass, reaching a record number of players right at release, though it was initially plagued by performance issues that the developers gradually fixed. Ori and the Will of the Wisps is considered one of the high points of the metroidvania genre for the entire decade.
xbox-one__ori-and-will-of-wisps.teaser: It follows up with a bigger world and a more mature story; empathy works even for the villain.

xbox-one__cuphead.article:
**Cuphead** is a visually utterly unique run-and-gun platformer from the Canadian brother duo Chad and Jared Moldenhauer, whose entire graphics were hand-drawn and animated using the same process as the rubber-hose cartoon grotesques of the 1930s, including watercolor backgrounds and a live-recorded jazz score. The story, in the spirit of period cartoons, follows the brothers Cuphead and Mugman, who lost a bet with the Devil and must collect debts for him from a colorful roster of bosses scattered across an island map, which the player navigates in a simple top-down view similar to classic platformers.

At the core of the gameplay are intense boss battles against giant enemies with multiple transformation phases, requiring precise memorization of attack patterns, perfect timing of parries on pink-colored objects, and strategic selection of weapons, super moves, and charms before each attempt. The game is renowned for its extremely high yet fair difficulty, where every failure stems from a player's mistake rather than chance, placing it alongside classic arcade bullet-hell titles. Besides the boss fights, it also offers classic run-and-gun platforming levels, and it can be played from the start by two people in local co-op, though the screen becomes even more chaotic that way.

Development took nearly seven years, and its hand-drawn animation process was enormously labor-intensive, which is reflected in a unique atmosphere unmatched by any other title, where every frame looks like a cel from an old film reel. Cuphead became a commercial and critical phenomenon and one of the most striking indie games of the entire generation; it was later released on other platforms as well and got its own animated series. The later The Delicious Last Course expansion added a new playable character, Ms. Chalice, along with another set of inventive bosses that expand the otherwise compact but immensely dense content of the base game.
xbox-one__cuphead.teaser: Hand-drawn and animated like 1930s cartoons, with live-recorded jazz.

xbox-one__sea-of-thieves.article:
**Sea of Thieves** is a shared pirate adventure game from legendary British studio Rare, in which crews of up to four players sail the open seas together, hunt for treasure, battle other ships, and face supernatural threats like skeleton fleets or a giant kraken. The choice of vessel — between a nimble sloop for solo players, a mid-sized brigantine, and a mighty galleon — determines how many hands are needed on deck and how cautiously a player has to behave at sea. The world is shared, so any sail on the horizon can mean a trading partner or the end of a long-planned expedition.

The game places extreme emphasis on the crew's physical cooperation — one player must man the helm, another trim the sails according to the wind, a third bail water from a leaking hull, and a fourth navigate using the map spread out on the table below deck, with all communication happening primarily by voice. This is exactly what gives rise to unique emergent stories, where a perfectly prepared voyage collapses because of a single unpatched hole, or conversely ends in triumph after an unexpected fight over someone else's chest. The art style combines a stylized, painterly water surface with an advanced sea physics simulation that reacts to weather and player actions in real time, and a stormy night on a raging ocean ranks among the most striking scenes of the entire generation.

At its 2018 launch, the game was criticized for a lack of long-term content and repetitive tasks, but this changed fundamentally thanks to free regular updates and the narrated Tall Tales campaigns, which gradually added elaborate quest lines, new factions, and crossovers with other brands like Pirates of the Caribbean and Monkey Island. The game supports crossplay between Xbox and PC and is one of the longest and most actively supported titles in Microsoft's entire history. Sea of Thieves thus transformed from a shaky launch into one of the defining social experiences of the entire console generation.
xbox-one__sea-of-thieves.teaser: A shared pirate adventure for four players, where a giant kraken lurks at sea too.

xbox-one__state-of-decay-2.article:
**State of Decay 2** is a survival game about surviving a zombie apocalypse, in which the player doesn't manage just one character but an entire community of survivors, whose members have their own personalities, skills, relationships, and risk of permanent death. Players switch freely between characters, and each one wears down from fatigue and injuries, so it's necessary to rotate them like a real team. Undead Labs expanded the concept of the first game with cooperative play for up to four players, who together build a fortified base, scavenge supplies from abandoned buildings, and face growing threats including mutated zombie types.

A key element is the permanent death of characters — if a beloved community member dies, it's for good, which lends even minor grain-sack runs a high degree of tension and personal investment. Noise also attracts attention, so gunfire tends to be a last resort, while quiet work with blunt weapons or sneaking past patrolling infected pays off more. The game offers three sprawling open maps with different terrain and dangers, between which the whole community can migrate if the current base becomes unsustainable, and a new addition was so-called blood plague hearts — infection sources that must be located and destroyed.

The game's economy revolves around gathering resources, upgrading the base, and managing the morale of survivors, who can fall ill, get injured, or quarrel with each other over scarce resources and, in extreme cases, even leave. The technical side was criticized at launch for unstable framerates and graphical shortcomings, but the core gameplay built around improvised survival and community-building won over a loyal player base, and the game received numerous updates as well as an expanded edition. State of Decay 2 remains to this day one of the few open-world survival titles with such a deep emphasis on the social dynamics of a survivor group.
xbox-one__state-of-decay-2.teaser: A survival game where you don't control a hero, but an entire community with its own relationships and weaknesses.

xbox-one__quantum-break.article:
**Quantum Break** is a unique hybrid of third-person action and television series from the Finnish studio Remedy Entertainment, famous for titles like Max Payne and Alan Wake. The story follows Jack Joyce, who gains the ability to manipulate time-space after an accident during a time experiment, while the world around him gradually collapses due to so-called time fractures freezing the surroundings mid-motion. The game's strongest idea is precisely these frozen locations — a collapsed bridge or a falling container ship turns into a platforming puzzle, in which time moves only in brief flickers.

The gameplay combines cover-based shooting with striking time powers, letting the player trap enemies in a slowed-down bubble, dash forward as a blurred shadow, teleport behind opponents, or create a protective shield around themselves. Firefights therefore unfold in constant motion, and cover serves more as a moment to catch one's breath than a place to wait things out. The visual side used advanced particle effects and lighting to visualize frozen time and was among the technically most ambitious on Xbox One, though at the cost of a softer, blurrier image that divided contemporary reviews.

The game's most distinctive feature is its connection to a live-action television series of four long episodes, told from the perspective of the antagonist Paul Serene, whose content changes based on decisions the player makes at the end of each game chapter. The cast included well-known actors such as Shawn Ashmore, Aidan Gillen from Game of Thrones, and Lance Reddick, who lent the characters both face and voice. Although the concept of linking the game to the series divided critics and some players tended to skip the episodes, Quantum Break remains a bold experiment and a showcase of Remedy's creative ambition within Microsoft's exclusive portfolio.
xbox-one__quantum-break.teaser: A hybrid of action game and TV series from the creators of Max Payne and Alan Wake, featuring time manipulation.

xbox-one__recore.article:
**ReCore** was created through a collaboration between the Texas-based Armature Studio, founded by former developers of the Metroid Prime series, and the legendary Japanese creator Keiji Inafune, associated with the Mega Man series. The game takes place on the desert planet Far Eden, where humanity relocated after Earth became uninhabitable, and follows engineer Joule Adams as she wakes from cryosleep into a world ruled by hostile robots and buried under drifts of sand.

Joule travels the planet with a crew of robotic companions in animal forms — the dog-like Mack, the spider-like Seth, and the bird-like Duncan — each offering different abilities for movement and combat, and switchable on the fly: one digs objects out of the sand, another climbs along rails, and a third smashes through obstacles. The combat system is built around color-coding enemies by core type, which must be weakened with a correspondingly colored shot before it can be ripped out with a rope as a trophy and used to upgrade the player's own robots. The open world combines platforming sections with double jumps and dashes in the Metroidvania tradition with action combat and a light system for building robots from found parts.

At launch, the game suffered from technical problems including disproportionately long loading times and an unfinished feel in its final areas, where the ending required gathering a large number of cores and felt more like padding out playtime. This led to a mixed reception despite a strong artistic concept, likeable main characters, and an unusually fluid feel of movement that the studio's history with the Metroid Prime series certainly did not lack. A later expanded version addressed some of the criticism. ReCore nonetheless remains an interesting example of collaboration between Western and Japanese development approaches within Microsoft's exclusive program, and a reminder of how thin the line is between an original idea and unrealized potential.
xbox-one__recore.teaser: Desert sci-fi from former Metroid Prime creators and the father of Mega Man, Keiji Inafune.

xbox-one__killer-instinct.article:
**Killer Instinct** was a launch title for Xbox One and a surprising reboot of the legendary fighting series from the nineties, this time developed not by the original Rare but by Double Helix Games and, in later seasons, Iron Galaxy, with Microsoft Studios itself taking the project under its wing. The game stood out with an unusual free-to-play business model, letting players try one regularly rotating character for free and unlock others individually or by buying the complete package, which was unusual for an exclusive console fighting game at the time. Thanks to this, even someone who would never pay full price for a fighting game got to try it.

The combat system built on the signature combo-breaker mechanics of the original series — long, lightning-fast chained damage combos can be interrupted by a precisely timed counter-hit matching the strength of the attack the opponent is currently using, while the attacker in turn can defend with a so-called counter breaker. Combat thus becomes a game of bluffing and reading the opponent, where understanding timing matters more than simple combo memorization. The game also offered an exceptionally thorough training and tutorial mode, still cited today as a model for how the genre should teach newcomers.

The roster included both returning classic fighters like Jago, Sabrewulf, and Glacius, as well as entirely new additions and later guest characters from other franchises, including General RAAM from Gears of War, the Arbiter from Halo, and Rash from Battletoads. The game received regular seasonal updates for years with new fighters, improved graphics, and reworked arenas, making it one of the longest-supported titles on the whole platform, aided by an aggressive electronic soundtrack that reacted to the flow of combat. Killer Instinct is still valued today as a technically deep, community-beloved fighter and proof that Microsoft can revive even long-forgotten franchises from its history.
xbox-one__killer-instinct.teaser: A restart of the 90s fighting game as an Xbox One launch title, free-to-play for the first time.

xbox-one__rare-replay.article:
**Rare Replay** is a monumental celebration of thirty years of history of the British studio Rare, bringing together thirty full games from across its output, from the eighties to the more recent era, all for the price of a single standard title. The collection includes eight-bit classics like Jetpac and Atic Atac, titles from the era of home computers and Nintendo consoles, the golden age on the Nintendo 64 with games like Banjo-Kazooie, Blast Corps, Jet Force Gemini, and Perfect Dark, and closes with more modern additions like Viva Piñata or Kameo: Elements of Power from the early Xbox 360 era. The titles are moreover arranged chronologically on a timeline, so simply browsing the menu functions as a tour through the studio's history.

Each game runs via emulation directly on Xbox One and is accompanied by archival interviews with the creators, concept materials, and so-called Snapshots — short, custom-designed challenges derived from individual games that let players sample even titles that would otherwise require hours of play. The emulation also adds modern conveniences like rewinding time and quicksaving, thanks to which even merciless eight-bit games are finally completable without memorizing every screen. Unfortunately, for licensing reasons the collection does not include the studio's most famous titles like GoldenEye 007 or the Donkey Kong Country series, whose rights are held by other companies.

Rare Replay thus functions as an interactive museum of game development, showing in one place how a single studio managed to adapt to several generations of hardware and to genre trends alike — from simple arcade games through platformers and shooters to experiments in raising virtual creatures. For fans of retro gaming, it's a unique opportunity to experience the history of one of the most influential British studios in an authentic and legally available form on a modern console, which makes Rare Replay a significant entry for this retro-gaming-focused site as well.
xbox-one__rare-replay.teaser: Thirty games from Rare's history in one collection for the price of a single game — from Jetpac to Banjo-Kazooie.

xbox-one__crackdown-3.article:
**Crackdown 3** was a long-delayed sequel to the cult open-world series about a super-agent fighting criminal organizations in the stylized city of New Providence, with Terry Crews as agent Isaiah Jones as the main star of the marketing campaign. The game retained the series' signature vertical gameplay built around collecting so-called Agility Orbs, thanks to which the player's character gradually gains the ability to jump to ever greater heights, turning exploration of the open city into almost a platforming discipline and the blinking orbs on rooftops into one of the most addictive collectible loops in the genre.

Combat combines shooting from a varied arsenal of weapons with comfortable auto-aim and a super-strength ability allowing the player to lift vehicles and pieces of the environment and hurl them at enemies. Progression is free-form: the city is controlled by divisions of the Terra Nova corporation, and the player chooses which parts of their structure to dismantle first, since eliminating subordinates weakens their superiors. The main draw was meant to be environmental destruction technology powered by Microsoft Azure cloud computing, enabling real-time demolition of entire buildings, but this feature ultimately ended up confined solely to the standalone multiplayer mode Wrecking Zone, while the single-player campaign offers destruction only to a very limited degree.

Development of the game took nearly five years and was accompanied by repeated delays and changes on the development teams' side, which showed in a somewhat dated graphical presentation compared to competitors of its release year and in a sense that the game arrived a generation late. Nevertheless, Crackdown 3 retained the lighthearted, arcade-style fun that made the series famous back in 2007, offering full open-world cooperation full of vertical challenges, and thanks to its release directly into Xbox Game Pass, it was ultimately tried by far more players than would have bought it.
xbox-one__crackdown-3.teaser: Open-world action with Agility Orbs to collect for higher jumps; Terry Crews was the face of the campaign.

xbox-one__titanfall.article:
**Titanfall** was the debut title of Respawn Entertainment, founded by former Call of Duty creators Vince Zampella and Jason West, and became one of the most anticipated exclusives of the early Xbox One era. The game combines fast infantry shooting with wall-running parkour movement and double jumps with massive bipedal mechs called Titans, which the player calls down to the battlefield after a countdown and either personally pilots or lets fight autonomously.

The switch between the agile pilot and the ponderous but devastating power of a Titan creates unique dynamics, where experienced players can attack Titans from behind, rip the fuel cell out of their hull, jump out of the cockpit on the run, and become vulnerable infantry again. The maps were designed with two layers at once — ground-level streets and halls for the mechs, and a tangle of rooftops, walkways, and walls for the pilots — so the same arena offers two different games simultaneously, and escaping a Titan simply means jumping somewhere it can't reach. The feel of the shooting, and especially of the movement, was exceptionally polished and still ranks among the best the genre has offered.

The game was purely multiplayer, without a classic single-player campaign; the story played out through radio chatter and scripted events happening directly during network matches divided into two factional campaigns. Respawn Entertainment also relied heavily on Microsoft Azure server infrastructure, among other things for the behavior of the non-player soldiers who fill the battlefield and give less experienced players opportunities for easier kills and a faster Titan call-in. Despite the lack of offline content and a gradually thinning player base, Titanfall became an influential title that defined the trend of fast, acrobatic multiplayer design and paved the way for a more successful sequel two years later.
xbox-one__titanfall.teaser: Respawn's debut combines wall-running parkour with piloting giant Titan mechs on the battlefield.

xbox-one__titanfall-2.article:
