**Titanfall 2** fixed the main shortcoming of the first game by adding a full single-player campaign, which, despite its modest length, went down as one of the best-rated story shooters of the generation. The campaign follows foot soldier Jack Cooper, who unexpectedly becomes the pilot of a Titan named BT-7274 after his mentor's death, and their gradually built relationship between human and artificial intelligence gives an otherwise action-focused game unexpected emotional depth. Communication with BT happens through simple dialogue choices and the handing over of weapon modules, so within a few hours the war machine becomes a genuine character rather than just a walking vehicle.

The campaign's level design excels in creative puzzles involving time manipulation via a device that jumps between the past and present of the same location, repeatedly praised by critics as one of the most inventive game ideas of the year. Just as inventive are missions built around moving factory-line modules or a controlled fall from a great height, and the game practically never reuses an idea twice, preferring to set it aside after a single mission. The core of the controls remains the pilot's movement — wall-running, sliding, and double jumps keep the pace so high that the player rarely touches the ground for more than a moment.

The multiplayer retained the core parkour movement and infantry-versus-Titan combat of the first game but enriched it with six distinct Titan classes with their own abilities and loadouts, a more elaborate pilot equipment system, and new game modes. Respawn Entertainment unfortunately released the game in the same week as Battlefield 1 and Call of Duty: Infinite Warfare, which significantly damaged its sales despite excellent reviews, and it became one of the most-cited cases of poor marketing timing in the games industry. Over the years, thanks to word of mouth, Titanfall 2 built a strong cult following and is now retrospectively considered one of the best-designed shooters of the entire console generation.
xbox-one__titanfall-2.teaser: The added campaign with the robot BT-7274 ranks among the best-reviewed shooters of the generation.

xbox-one__witcher-3-wild-hunt.article:
**The Witcher 3: Wild Hunt** is a sprawling fantasy RPG from the Polish studio CD Projekt RED, which closes out the story trilogy about witcher Geralt of Rivia and his search for his missing adoptive daughter Ciri amid an invasion of the supernatural Wild Hunt. The game offers a vast, aesthetically varied open world ranging from the swampy villages of Temeria through the island region of Skellige to the metropolis of Novigrad, threaded with hundreds of side quests whose narrative quality often matches the main storyline and which became famous for morally ambiguous decisions with no clearly good solutions. It is precisely the witcher contracts — which begin as ordinary investigations in a village and end in the revelation of a far more uncomfortable human truth — that players remember most vividly from Wild Hunt.

The combat system combines sword fighting in two stances, alchemical potions and sword oils, and a set of five signs — magic spells like Igni or Quen — while Gwent, a card minigame expanded with its own factions and card collecting, became so popular that it later earned its own standalone sequel. Preparation for the hunt is matched by a bestiary in which monster weaknesses are recorded, guiding the player to choose the right oil and trap before a fight.

On Xbox One, the game ran at a native 900p resolution, a small price paid for the sheer scale and density of the world's content, while the Complete Edition release unified the base game with the Hearts of Stone and Blood and Wine expansions, the latter comparable in scope to a full standalone game. The overall impression is also shaped by artistic design rooted in Slavic folk motifs and music combining period instruments with female vocals, giving each region its own sonic identity. The Witcher 3 has won more than two hundred fifty Game of the Year awards and is widely regarded as one of the most significant RPGs of all time, even outside the Xbox platform.
xbox-one__witcher-3-wild-hunt.teaser: A vast fantasy RPG about Geralt of Rivia and one of the most admired open worlds.

xbox-one__red-dead-redemption-2.article:
**Red Dead Redemption 2** is a sprawling western from Rockstar Games which, as a prequel to the original 2010 game, tells the story of the decline of the Van der Linde gang and its member Arthur Morgan at the twilight of the Wild West. The game excels through unprecedented attention to detail in its open world — from animals reacting to weather and seasons, through physically simulated horse coats and mud sticking to clothing, to a dynamic honor system that affects how townspeople react, which dialogue options are available, and how individual missions end. The game's pace is deliberately slow: characters mount their horses with full animations, weapons must be cleaned, and food prepared, turning ordinary travel across the landscape into a standalone experience.

The narrative gradually uncovers the internal breakdown of Arthur's group against the backdrop of the end of the gang era and the rise of industrialization, with the main character undergoing one of the best-written character arcs in the history of video games. The gameplay includes cover-based shooting similar to previous Rockstar titles, hunting and skinning animals, poker and other minigames, and an elaborate camp economy system that the player finances by donating loot. The camp also serves as a narrative hub — its members talk, argue, and change their tone between missions depending on how the group is faring.

The online mode, Red Dead Online, released separately after launch, offered a persistent multiplayer world with its own professions like bounty hunter or trader. On Xbox One, the game required installing over a hundred gigabytes of data and ranked among the most technically demanding titles of the generation, which showed in long installations and a noticeable strain on older console models. The result justified it, though: the lighting, fog handling, and time-of-day transitions ranked among the best the console generation had to offer. Red Dead Redemption 2 is generally ranked among the most ambitious and elaborate video games of the entire decade.
xbox-one__red-dead-redemption-2.teaser: A western from Rockstar with obsessive attention to detail, from horse fur to weather.

xbox-one__grand-theft-auto-v.article:
**Grand Theft Auto V**, originally released for Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3, arrived in a reworked form on Xbox One as well, with improved graphics, denser traffic, new wildlife, and an expanded range of content for the online mode. The game takes place in the fictional metropolis of Los Santos and its surroundings, inspired by Southern California, and as the first entry in the series offers a story told from the perspective of three different protagonists — former bank robber Michael, street gangster Franklin, and unpredictable Trevor — between whom players can switch at any time during gameplay, allowing heists to be followed from multiple angles at once. It's precisely the big heists that rank among the campaign's highlights — the player chooses an approach, hires helpers with different skill sets, and bears the consequences of their decisions right through to the execution of the job itself.

The open world ranks among the largest and most detailed in the history of the gaming industry, with an elaborate stock-market economy that can be influenced through decisions made during main missions, and it offers dozens of side activities from golf and tennis to skydiving. The Xbox One console version additionally added an optional first-person perspective, which completely reworked vehicle and shooting controls and essentially offered a second way to experience the entire game.

The multiplayer mode Grand Theft Auto Online gradually evolved from a supplementary add-on into a standalone, commercially the most successful online world from Rockstar Games, regularly expanded with new content, vehicles, and story updates throughout the entire Xbox One generation. The game also became known for its sophisticated, often sarcastic satire of American consumer society, media, and celebrity culture, which permeates radio stations, billboard advertisements, and side characters alike. Grand Theft Auto V became one of the best-selling entertainment products in history across all media, not just video games, and even years later it remains among the most-played titles on the charts.
xbox-one__grand-theft-auto-v.teaser: A re-ported version of the action game with three protagonists, with denser traffic and improved graphics.

xbox-one__elden-ring.article:
**Elden Ring** is an open-world action RPG from Japanese studio FromSoftware, created in collaboration with fantasy author George R. R. Martin, who crafted the mythological backdrop of the shattered Elden Ring and its scattered wielders of power. The game brings the series' signature unforgiving difficulty and deliberate combat from Souls and Bloodborne into the vast open world of the Lands Between, where the player is free to explore from the very start, discovering hidden caves, catacombs, and legendary bosses in any order without linear guidance. The simple ability to bypass a tough opponent and return later fundamentally changed the accessibility of the whole franchise.

A key element is the game's surprisingly generous yet unobtrusive help system: cryptic messages left on the ground by other players, summonable spirit companions, and the horse Torrent, which makes both fast travel and fighting giant bosses far easier. The character-building system offers extreme freedom between swords, spells, fire abilities, and hybrid styles, with each weapon carrying its own unique movesets and so-called Ashes of War for further customization. The storytelling remains traditionally fragmented and hidden in item descriptions, so players piece the lore together among themselves rather than through explicit dialogue.

On Xbox One the game ran in a more limited form due to the engine's demands, though it fully showed off its visuals on newer hardware; even so, it kept the impressive vistas the studio uses in place of conventional objective markers. Elden Ring won over three hundred Game of the Year awards and is widely regarded as one of the most significant and influential RPGs in the history of the medium, defining the soulslike genre for the decade to come. The later Shadow of the Erdtree expansion added an entirely new, sprawling region with its own story and boss gallery comparable in scope to a smaller standalone game.
xbox-one__elden-ring.teaser: FromSoftware's open world with mythology by George R. R. Martin and Souls-level difficulty.

xbox-one__doom.article:
**Doom** from 2016 was a triumphant reboot of id Software's legendary series, which after the disappointment of Doom 3 returned to its roots of brutal, breakneck demon-slaying on Mars and in Hell itself. The game builds on a philosophy of push-forward combat, where the player is actively encouraged to charge straight into enemy waves rather than hide behind cover, since the Glory Kill system lets brutal finishing moves on staggered demons instantly refill health and ammo. There's no automatic health regeneration and no conventional reloading, so the player has no reason to retreat and the game keeps pushing them forward.

The arsenal includes the iconic Super Shotgun, a chainsaw for carving enemies into ammo, and the series' undisputedly most iconic weapon, the BFG9000, with each weapon moddable via two distinct upgrade paths depending on preferred playstyle. The level design combines fast, vertical arenas full of hidden secrets with nods to the classic nineties titles, such as secret levels accessible only through retro-styled portals. Collecting figures, runes, and Praetor Suit upgrades also gives exploration a purpose beyond combat itself, rewarding players who don't settle for the shortest path to the next elevator.

Mick Gordon's accompanying soundtrack, with its aggressive metal-industrial sound that reacts to the flow of combat, became one of the most iconic game soundtracks of the decade and, for many players, is inseparable from the game itself. The multiplayer component and the SnapMap editor were received more mixedly than the single-player campaign, which on its own definitively restored players' faith in the Doom brand and paved the way for the even more successful sequel Eternal four years later. On Xbox One the game maintained smooth performance, which matters more for a shooter this fast than texture detail, and it still feels fresh today.
xbox-one__doom.teaser: A return to the roots of brutal action; the Glory Kill system turns combat into an aggressive, attacking dance.

xbox-one__doom-eternal.article:
**Doom Eternal** takes the concept of its 2016 predecessor to an even more extreme, faster, and mechanically more complex place, turning the player into a literal mobile fortress constantly juggling health, ammo, and armor across three interlinked resources. The chainsaw now requires fuel and becomes the key tool for replenishing ammo, the flamethrower mounted on the Doomguy's back generates armor when hitting burning enemies, and Glory Kill finishers remain the main source of health, forcing constant aggressive movement around the arena instead of waiting things out.

Combat is also built around knowledge of specific weak points—many tougher demons can be quickly neutralized by shooting off a particular body part or piece of equipment, turning a fight into a kind of rapid-fire puzzle solved at full speed. The level design opens up to platforming elements for the first time in the series: double jump, dash, and wall-climbing extend the battlefield into the vertical plane, which the player must actively use to keep distance from attacking demons. Between arenas, the game varies the pace with secret rooms, challenges, and collectibles hidden behind dexterity sequences.

The story, previously an afterthought, this time takes on a surprisingly elaborate mythological scope with its own deep lore, cutscenes, and an extensive database of entries detailing the history of the hellish invasion and the Doom Slayer's own role as a legendary figure. Visually, the game shifted away from gray sci-fi toward more colorful, almost comic-book environments ranging from flooded cities to heavenly fortresses. Mick Gordon's soundtrack once again defined the series' aggressive sound, though its release was accompanied by a public dispute with id Software. The game's difficulty ranks among the toughest in the modern shooter genre, which the hardcore fanbase appreciated even as it mildly discouraged casual players used to the previous game's gentler approach.
xbox-one__doom-eternal.teaser: An even faster and more complex sequel, where the chainsaw solves ammo shortages.

xbox-one__resident-evil-2.article:
**Resident Evil 2** is a complete remake of the 1998 classic, which Capcom built on the modern RE Engine and transformed from fixed camera angles into a fluid over-the-shoulder view, without losing the claustrophobic horror atmosphere of an infested Raccoon City. The player takes on either rookie police officer Leon S. Kennedy on his first night shift, or student Claire Redfield searching for her brother, with both scenarios—so-called Scenario A and B—offering interlinked yet distinct perspectives on the same zombie- and mutated bio-organic-weapon-filled night.

A key innovation is the enemy known as Mr. X, a giant trench-coated pursuer who, once a certain point in the game unlocks, roams the police station freely and continuously, actively hunting the player, creating tension entirely different from classic scripted jump scares. His heavy footsteps, audible through walls, became one of the most-cited sound motifs of modern horror and force the player to plan both their route and their escape route ahead of time. The zombies themselves also take a surprising amount of punishment, and individual shots visibly tear their flesh, so the player weighs whether every opponent is even worth the bullet.

A system of limited ammo, key-and-puzzle-item conundrums, and a sophisticated inventory with limited capacity carries on the traditional survival horror design of the original series, while realistic lighting and detailed character models give the horror unprecedented visual intensity. The police station itself functions as an interconnected labyrinth full of shortcuts that gradually open up to the player, turning the repeated back-and-forth from a chore into a routine; the map system from the original also returns, color-coding rooms that still have something left to collect. The game also includes bonus scenarios with Ada Wong and Hunk as unlockable content after completion. The Resident Evil 2 remake is widely regarded as one of the best-executed remakes in the history of the medium and defined the direction the series' subsequent remakes would take.
xbox-one__resident-evil-2.teaser: A remake of the 1998 classic with an over-the-shoulder view instead of fixed cameras.

xbox-one__resident-evil-7-biohazard.article:
**Resident Evil 7: Biohazard** marked a decisive turn for the series back to pure horror atmosphere after several more action-oriented entries, achieved through a fundamental shift in perspective to first-person, which intensifies the sense of immediate danger. The player steps into the role of Ethan Winters, who after years of searching for his missing wife Mia finds her in the decrepit, mold- and rot-overgrown mansion of the Baker family in remote Louisiana, where he faces mutated family members endowed with near-indestructible regeneration.

The level design returned to the series' traditional roots with an interconnected, enclosed environment full of locked doors requiring specific key items, limited ammo, and careful inventory management, while the game also supported a full experience in virtual reality on the PlayStation VR platform, though the Xbox One console version offered conventional controls. Combat is deliberately slow and uncomfortable: Ethan is not a soldier, weapons reload clumsily, and the knife attack serves mostly as a last resort. Healing via mixed fluids and saving progress on cassette tape recorders further give the game an old-fashioned rhythm.

The atmosphere combines a found-footage aesthetic of videotapes the player discovers and plays back as flashbacks revealing the family's previous victims, with a claustrophobic cat-and-mouse game against patriarch Jack Baker in the game's first half. The soundtrack relies more on silence, creaking wood, and distant footsteps than on music, keeping tension alive even in rooms where nothing is happening, and the safe rooms with their music box feel like genuine relief. The RE Engine graphics engine debuted here and set the visual standard for all of Capcom's following titles for several years. Resident Evil 7 is considered a successful return of the series to its horror roots and one of the most frightening mainstream titles of its generation.
xbox-one__resident-evil-7-biohazard.teaser: A return to pure first-person horror in the decaying mansion of the Baker family.

xbox-one__monster-hunter-world.article:
**Monster Hunter: World** was a breakthrough entry for the long-running, historically Japan-focused series, opening it up fully to Western audiences for the first time thanks to seamlessly connected hunting grounds without the earlier division into separate zones, and a clearer, more accessible explanation of its complex systems for newcomers. The player becomes a hunter attached to a research commission investigating the periodic migration of ancient dragons in the New World, with the core of the game remaining the hunt for giant monsters using fourteen distinct weapon types, from massive Great Swords through nimble Dual Blades to Hunting Horns that support allies with musical buffs.

Each weapon has its own set of moves, speed, and way of maintaining an advantage, making weapon choice feel more like picking a character class than swapping out equipment. After successfully hunting a monster, the player gathers its materials to craft new armor and weapons, creating the signature hunt-and-craft loop that made the series famous, especially in Japan, well before this installment. The hunt itself begins with preparation: the player tracks footprints, uses scent to locate prey, and sets traps or stun bombs.

A new feature was the dynamic weather and ecosystem, in which various monsters can attack one another, something the player can exploit tactically by luring a larger predator onto their opponent. Cooperation among up to four hunters on a single expedition dramatically eases the fight against the toughest monsters and forms the core of the series' social experience. Visually, the game showed surprisingly dense, lively environments even on Xbox One, albeit at the cost of occasional frame drops during the busiest fights. The hub of Astera also serves as a shared gathering place where hunters meet, upgrade their gear, and plan the next expedition. The later Iceborne expansion added new snowy regions, monsters, and mechanics. Monster Hunter: World became the best-selling title in Capcom's history and dramatically expanded the brand's global popularity beyond Japan.
xbox-one__monster-hunter-world.teaser: The entry that finally opened up the Japanese series to the West with seamless hunting grounds.

xbox-one__assassin-s-creed-origins.article:
**Assassin's Creed Origins** marked a fundamental transformation of Ubisoft's long-running series from an action-platformer with stealth elements into a full-fledged action RPG with an elaborate leveling, gear, and skill tree system. The story returns to ancient Egypt at the twilight of Ptolemaic rule and for the first time tells the so-called origin of the Assassin Brotherhood through the medjay Bayek of Siwa and his wife Aya, whose personal quest for revenge gradually grows into the founding of the secret Order of the Hidden Ones.

The open world reconstructs Egypt with unprecedented care, from the Library of Alexandria through the pyramids of Giza to the Nile Delta, and the developers also added a free educational mode, Discovery Tour, allowing players to walk through historical locations without combat or enemies, accompanied by expert commentary from ancient Egypt specialists. The environment changes significantly by region: the green farmland along the Nile stands in sharp contrast to the empty desert, where mirages and sandstorms appear.

The combat system abandoned the earlier simple blocking-and-countering in favor of a more complex system based on dodging, various weapon types with specific speed and damage, and enemy levels the player must avoid if underleveled for them. Weapons and bows also now come in several rarity tiers with their own bonuses, bringing the game closer to looter-game logic for the first time in the series. A new ranged ability via the eagle Senu allows scouting terrain and marking enemies from above, which became a permanent fixture of subsequent series entries. Optional arena fights, chariot races, and the hunt for exceptionally powerful enemies then offered post-completion content, as did expansions devoted to the pharaohs and the fate of Bayek's family. Assassin's Creed Origins is generally regarded as a successful relaunch of the brand after a year-long break and a template for the series' subsequent RPG-focused entries.
xbox-one__assassin-s-creed-origins.teaser: The series' transformation into an action RPG with a skill tree; the story of the brotherhood's origins in Egypt.

xbox-one__assassin-s-creed-odyssey.article:
**Assassin's Creed Odyssey** deepened the RPG direction the series took with the previous entry, Origins, and transported the player to ancient Greece against the backdrop of the Peloponnesian War between Athens and Sparta. For the first time in the series, the game offered a full choice between two main protagonists, the mercenary Kassandra or the mercenary Alexios, whose fate as descendants of King Leonidas gradually reveals both a tangled family tragedy and a conspiracy by the mysterious Cult of Kosmos manipulating the entire war from behind the scenes. Both versions of the main character are fully voiced, and Kassandra earned notably stronger acclaim among players for her performance.

The scale of the open world grew dramatically to encompass dozens of islands across the Aegean Sea connected by a ship, on which the player can recruit a crew and fight naval battles similar to earlier pirate-themed entries in the series. Combat abandoned the classic hidden blade as a guaranteed one-hit kill tool, replacing it with a set of active abilities, from 300-style kicks to rain-like arrow volleys that charge up through successful attacks. The mercenary system also means that after a committed crime, the player is hunted by increasingly powerful opponents with their own weaknesses and rewards.

A dialogue system with branching choices and several distinct endings represented a major novelty for the series toward full-fledged RPG storytelling, where the player's decisions genuinely affect the fates of side characters and the story's ultimate direction. The Battle of Thermopylae and a massive faction-war system, in which the player influences which side controls a given region by recruiting mercenaries and taking part in battles, ranked among the most ambitious systems in the entire series. Subsequent expansions about family legacy and about Atlantis added mythological, supernatural elements, pitting the player against beings from Greek myth. Critical reception was very favorable, though some criticized the need to grind experience between main missions at length. Thanks to its scale and length, Assassin's Creed Odyssey is considered one of the most expansive titles of the entire Xbox One generation.
xbox-one__assassin-s-creed-odyssey.teaser: Ancient Greece and the Peloponnesian War; for the first time in the series, a choice between two protagonists.

xbox-one__destiny-2.article:
**Destiny 2** is a sci-fi looter shooter from Bungie, creators of the original Halo series, combining fast, precisely tuned shooting with a long-term loop of collecting ever-better gear and gradually building up one of three Guardian classes—Titan, Hunter, or Warlock. The story picks up from the first game with the destruction of humanity's last bastion, the Tower, by the invading Red Legion force led by Dominus Ghaul, forcing the player to rebuild the Guardians' strength from scratch.

The game stands out for its elaborate, regularly refreshed world with dynamic public events, demanding six-player raids requiring complex mechanical coordination, and the competitive Crucible mode for PvP-focused players. The raids in particular became the title's high point: without voice communication and role division they are practically impossible to complete, and their first clears are followed by the community like a sporting event. The key draw remains the tangible, satisfying feel of the shooting, which critics and players alike have long called one of the best in the genre, complemented by a sophisticated system of classes, grenades, and supercharged ultimate attacks.

Bungie gradually moved from paid expansions to a seasonal content model and eventually to the free base game New Light, making the game accessible to a far wider audience, though at the cost of repeated criticism for removing older content from the game. Expansions such as Forsaken, Shadowkeep, and Beyond Light gradually expanded the game's mythology around the Darkness and the Light as opposing cosmic forces and added new areas and abilities. The game's lasting atmosphere is also helped by its orchestral music and art direction blending sci-fi with almost sacral motifs, making even ordinary hunting grounds feel more like pilgrimage sites than shooter backdrops. Destiny 2 became one of the longest continuously live-supported online titles on Xbox One, with an active community lasting years after release.
xbox-one__destiny-2.teaser: A sci-fi looter shooter from the creators of Halo, with precise shooting and the chase for better gear.

xbox-one__overwatch.article:
**Overwatch** is a team-based hero shooter from Blizzard Entertainment that became one of the most influential multiplayer titles of the decade thanks to its colorful, distinctly stylized cast of heroes, each offering a completely different playstyle, from tanking through support to highly mobile damage dealers. The game emphasizes team synergy of abilities over individual performance, with objective modes like payload escort, point control, or a hybrid combination of both requiring constant communication and adapting the team composition to the situation on the battlefield.

A crucial feature is the ability to switch heroes at any time after death, turning every match into an ongoing tactical puzzle—a different lineup is needed against an enemy hiding behind a shield than against fast flankers going around the side. Ultimate abilities charge up gradually and their interplay decides entire engagements, so experienced teams deliberately hold and unleash them together. The visual design draws on an animated aesthetic with clearly distinguishable character silhouettes, making it easy to quickly recognize enemies and allies amid chaotic fights. Voice lines serve the same purpose, letting players identify a triggered ultimate ability even before they see it.

Blizzard built a rich story universe primarily through animated shorts and comics released outside the game itself, while narrative elements within the game remained minimal, one of the most common complaints from players. Seasonal events like the Summer Games or Halloween specials brought themed game modes and cosmetic rewards without affecting the game's balance. The competitive scene grew all the way to the founding of a full-fledged professional Overwatch League with city-based franchises modeled on traditional sports leagues, an unprecedented step for esports. Overwatch on Xbox One defined the hero shooter genre for years to come and inspired numerous competing titles.
xbox-one__overwatch.teaser: A team-based hero shooter that defined the genre with a colorful cast and role synergy.

xbox-one__rocket-league.article:
**Rocket League** is a phenomenally successful blend of arcade soccer and racing, in which players control rocket-powered cars trying to score a giant ball into the opponent's goal on an enclosed, arena-like pitch. Psyonix, formerly a small independent studio behind the less successful predecessor Supersonic Acrobatic Rocket-Powered Battle-Cars, created an incredibly accessible yet mechanically endlessly deep game, where the most skilled players pull off aerial dribbles, precise cannon shots, and so-called ceiling shots off the arena's roof.

The rules fit into a single sentence and the controls into a handful of buttons: throttle, jump, boost, and air tilt. It's the physics that hold the whole game together—the ball behaves predictably, bounces are consistent, and every goal feels like the player's own doing, not luck. Matches last five minutes and only end once the ball touches the ground, which is how last-second equalizers and the resulting overtime became the title's trademark. That short match length is exactly what made Rocket League a game players return to for even ten minutes between other titles.

The game debuted for free as part of the PlayStation Plus subscription, but its major commercial success and massive social-media buzz quickly catapulted it to all major platforms including Xbox One, where it supported crossplay across PC and other consoles as one of the very first major titles to do so. The cosmetic system of cars, trinkets, banners, and color effects with no impact on gameplay became a template for the so-called battle pass model later adopted by numerous other games such as Fortnite. Rocket League's competitive scene grew into one of the most-watched esports disciplines with its own professional league, the RLCS. Psyonix gradually converted the game into a fully free-to-play title in 2020, further expanding its already massive player base across console generations.
xbox-one__rocket-league.teaser: Football with rocket-powered cars from small studio Psyonix; easy to understand, endlessly deep.

xbox-one__hollow-knight.article:
**Hollow Knight** is a sprawling, hand-drawn metroidvania from the small Australian studio Team Cherry, whose depth, atmosphere, and unforgiving difficulty outshone much larger productions and made it one of the defining independent titles of the entire decade. The game casts the player as a nameless knight exploring the vast, interconnected underground kingdom of Hallownest, inhabited by insect creatures afflicted by a mysterious sickness called the Infection.

The world is designed with admirable interconnection of shortcuts, hidden chambers, and optional areas, and the game relies almost entirely on visual storytelling and fragmentary dialogue rather than explicit text, lending the whole story a melancholic, mysterious atmosphere. The approach to orientation is also unusual: the map isn't drawn automatically—the player must buy it from the cartographer Cornifer and fill it in only at benches, so entering a new area always means a moment of genuine disorientation.

The combat system combines precise platforming with strikes from a weapon called the Nail, a simple yet merciless attack mechanic, and gradually unlocked abilities like double jump, dash, or wall jump typical of the metroidvania genre. The healing system requires strategically pausing mid-fight to convert soul gathered from previous attacks, raising the risk and tension of every encounter with enemies and bosses. Players craft their own playstyle using charms with a limited number of slots, which alter weapon reach, healing speed, and movement style. Christopher Larkin's captivating orchestral score gives each area its own mood, from quiet melancholy to boss-fight urgency. Team Cherry supported the game long-term with free expansions adding new areas, bosses, and game modes, making it an unusually content-generous title for a fraction of the cost of bigger productions. Hollow Knight is generally ranked among the best metroidvanias in the genre's history.
xbox-one__hollow-knight.teaser: A hand-drawn metroidvania from a small Australian team, whose depth shames big-budget productions.

xbox-one__hades.article:
**Hades** is a roguelike action game from American studio Supergiant Games, set in the Greek underworld and following Zagreus, son of the god Hades, who repeatedly attempts to escape his subterranean home for the surface, with every failed attempt sending him back to the start with a new set of weapons and abilities. The genre's key innovation is a sophisticated narrative system in which the character dies and comes back to life many times over as part of the core game design, yet instead of feeling repetitive, this death serves as a natural narrative framework for gradually unfolding dialogue with the gods of Olympus and the inhabitants of the underworld, so the player genuinely falls in love with uncovering a rich, fully voiced story bit by bit.

The combat system offers six distinct weapons ranging from a sword to a bow to an unconventional shield, each controlling completely differently, while the system of so-called Boons, gifts from gods like Zeus, Athena, or Aphrodite, lets players combine abilities between runs to create unique synergistic builds. Combat itself is fast and readable, built around a forward dash, a light and heavy attack, and one unlockable skill, so all the depth shifts into deciding which boons to accept.

Between escape attempts, the player invests gathered resources into permanent upgrades and into improving his father's house, so even a failed run pushes progress forward. The visual style combines hand-painted characters with a dark yet colorful underworld setting, accompanied by Darren Korb's distinctive, genre-spanning soundtrack that blends rock guitars with ancient motifs. The underworld's characters also react to the player's progress, changing their lines depending on the chosen weapon and on who last defeated them. Hades launched on Xbox One after a successful stint in Early Access on PC and is widely regarded as one of the best-received titles of the entire generation, even outside the narrow circle of independent games.
xbox-one__hades.teaser: An action roguelike about escaping the underworld; death isn't the end, just a trip home for another attempt.

xbox-one__celeste.article:
**Celeste** is a precise, extremely demanding platformer from Canadian studio Matt Makes Games, whose heroine Madeline attempts to climb the fictional Mount Celeste, her physical journey gradually revealing a much deeper, honest story about anxiety, depression, and self-acceptance, embodied literally by the heroine's dark shadow double. The gameplay is built on perfectly tuned jump, air-dash, and wall-climb controls, with each level constructed as a carefully designed puzzle demanding precise timing and spatial awareness, compared by critics to the classic Super Meat Boy for its merciless yet fair difficulty.

The game is divided into single-screen challenges that restart almost instantly upon death, turning dozens of failures into a smooth learning process rather than a source of frustration. Each chapter also introduces its own mechanic, from moving blocks through wind currents to mirror reflections of the heroine, and once it's exhausted the game drops it, so the challenges never repeat in the same form. The game also includes an assist mode allowing players to slow the game down, add infinite dashes, or unlimited stamina, opening up an otherwise extremely demanding experience to players who would otherwise hit high difficulty as a wall, without it being viewed as cheating.

Side collectibles called strawberries and hidden B-side levels with even more demanding design offer experienced players dozens more hours of content beyond the main story. The accompanying chiptune-orchestral soundtrack by Lena Raine ranks among the most acclaimed game music of the decade and on its own underscores the emotional arc of the story, as the main theme returns in transformed form depending on how Madeline is faring. Celeste is generally regarded as one of the best-written and most precisely crafted platformers of the entire console generation.
xbox-one__celeste.teaser: A precise, demanding platformer about climbing a mountain and about anxiety; the heroine is pursued by a dark shadow.

xbox-one__cyberpunk-2077.article:
**Cyberpunk 2077** is a sprawling sci-fi RPG from Polish studio CD Projekt RED set in the dystopian Night City, where the player, as a mercenary named V, builds a career through a combination of shootouts, hacking, and an extensive dialogue system with several distinct paths for solving quests depending on the character's chosen starting lifestyle. The central storyline follows V, into whose mind a digital remnant of the legendary rocker and fighter Johnny Silverhand, portrayed by Keanu Reeves, becomes implanted after a failed heist, gradually taking control of the protagonist's body, creating a unique dynamic of two consciousnesses sharing one body.

Night City itself ranks among the most impressively designed game cities ever: vertical construction, neon advertising, and layers of slum blocks beneath luxury towers create a setting that functions as a character of the story in its own right. The atmosphere is significantly boosted by music split between radio stations and bands created specifically for the game. Most of the experience takes place from a first-person perspective including dialogue, keeping the player inside the scene even in moments of pure conversation.

On Xbox One and Xbox One X, the game's launch was among the most controversial in the history of the games industry due to serious technical issues, frequent crashes, and low frame rates, which led to the game being temporarily pulled from the PlayStation digital store and a public apology from the studio along with refund offers. Subsequent years of intensive fixes, patch 1.5, and the extensive Phantom Liberty expansion with a new story thread and Idris Elba in the lead role fundamentally transformed the game's reputation toward much more positive reception. The core gameplay, built on a deep RPG system of cyberware, hacking, and variable combat styles, remained praised throughout as one of the most ambitious gaming fantasies of the generation, as was the quality of the side quest writing.
xbox-one__cyberpunk-2077.teaser: A sprawling RPG set in Night City from CD Projekt RED, with hacking and a digital ghost in your head.

xbox-one__fallout-4.article:
**Fallout 4** is a sprawling post-apocalyptic RPG from Bethesda Game Studios that takes players to a devastated Boston two hundred years after nuclear war, where the sole survivor from Vault 111 searches for a kidnapped son after witnessing the murder of a spouse. The series offered for the first time a sophisticated settlement-building system, where the player constructs entire functioning communities of survivors from scavenged junk, complete with farms, defensive fortifications, and shops, which became one of the most discussed and time-consuming systems in the entire game.

The combat system integrated shooter elements with the classic bullet-time V.A.T.S. system, allowing time to slow down for precise targeting of enemies' specific body parts, while extensive crafting allowed nearly every weapon and piece of armor to be modified using dozens of components. Collecting seeming junk gained new meaning, since disassembled adhesives and cables became materials for upgrades. Power armor also became a standalone vehicle powered by fusion cores, which the character climbs into and which significantly changes the pace of combat.

The open world of the Commonwealth is dotted with hundreds of locations, from abandoned cities through military bases to bizarre side quests, with the player's guides ranging from robots and mutants to their own dog, Dogmeat. The choice between factions like the Brotherhood of Steel or the Institute then determines the story's ending and is mutually exclusive. Bethesda also supported the game with the Automatron, Vault-Tec Workshop, Far Harbor, and Nuka-World expansions, of which Far Harbor rivaled a smaller standalone game in scope. Fallout 4 on Xbox One was among the best-selling and longest-played titles of the entire generation despite the technical imperfections of the Creation engine. The game also supported mods directly in the console environment, a significant novelty for the Xbox One platform at the time, letting players install community content without needing to own a PC.
xbox-one__fallout-4.teaser: Post-apocalyptic Boston with the series' first elaborate settlement-building system made from scavenged junk.

xbox-one__dark-souls-iii.article:
**Dark Souls III** is the final entry in the legendary trilogy from Japanese studio FromSoftware, unifying the themes and aesthetics of the previous two games into the dark, dying world of Lothric, where the last flame is guttering out and undead Ashen Ones are summoned to rekindle it. The world feels like ruins piled on ruins, and the player constantly senses they're arriving at the very end of a long story, of which only wreckage and madmen remain. The combat system picked up the pace compared to the second entry, moving closer to the swifter, more aggressive action inspired by sister series Bloodborne, while retaining the series' characteristic emphasis on precise dodge timing, stamina management, and uncompromising punishment of carelessness with death, after which the player loses all accumulated souls unless they manage to return to the spot where they died.

A new addition is special weapon abilities called Weapon Arts, which add a unique special attack powered by a dedicated gauge to almost every sword, spear, or axe, significantly expanding character-building options. The level design links sprawling, vertically rich locations full of shortcuts leading back to bonfire rest points, while the boss gallery, including the legendary fights against Iudex Gundyr or the Abyss Watchers, ranks among the best designed in the entire series; most of these encounters have two phases, and the second usually completely transforms the rhythm of the fight. The game continues the tradition of minimalist, environmental storytelling, where most of the story is revealed through item descriptions and fragmentary dialogue from non-player characters rather than direct cutscenes.

Two expansions, Ashes of Ariandel and The Ringed City, added new areas and closed out the series' entire mythological arc with callbacks to the first game. Dark Souls III is generally regarded as the most balanced and technically most polished entry of the entire Souls trilogy, and a dignified farewell to the saga before the studio moved on to new franchises. Today it serves as an ideal entry point into the souls-like genre — tough enough to keep its reputation, yet more readable and smoother than its predecessors.
xbox-one__dark-souls-iii.teaser: The conclusion of FromSoftware's trilogy, the dying world of Lothric as a ruin piled on ruins.

xbox-one__sekiro-shadows-die-twice.article:
**Sekiro: Shadows Die Twice** is an action-adventure from FromSoftware set in a fictional feudal Japan of the late Sengoku period, which significantly departs from the Souls series' earlier character-building system in favor of a single, fixed protagonist, a one-armed ninja named Wolf, protecting a young lord whose mysterious bloodline grants immortality. The key new feature is a posture/balance system, where the goal of combat isn't primarily to deplete an opponent's health but their stability through precisely timed deflections, creating an intense, swordfight-like rhythm of combat that resembles a katana duel more than classic action-RPG battles. The game therefore doesn't reward carefully circling an enemy, but constant pressure.

The player's prosthetic arm allows equipping various tools such as a grappling hook for vertical movement across rooftops, an axe against shield-bearing enemies, or a fire device against animal opponents, adding a tactical layer beyond swordplay itself. The grappling hook in particular fundamentally changes level structure: locations are built vertically, the player moves across rooftops and branches, bypasses patrols, and can use stealth kills to weaken bosses even before the fight itself begins. The resurrection system allows one immediate revival right at the spot of death in the middle of combat, opening up risky but often crucial tactical options in fights against the game's toughest bosses. Visually, the game relies on a muted palette of autumnal Japan, fog, snow, and a soundscape built from traditional instruments.

The game won Game of the Year at The Game Awards 2019 and is generally regarded as the most demanding yet most precise action title from FromSoftware, proving that the studio could craft a great game even outside the established Souls formula. One of the loudest debates of its time erupted around its difficulty, since Sekiro offers none of the usual escape routes in the form of summoned help or character rebuilding — the player must master exactly one combat language. Today Sekiro is seen as the purest design in the studio's portfolio.
xbox-one__sekiro-shadows-die-twice.teaser: Feudal Japan and a new posture-balance system instead of the Souls-style character building.

xbox-one__metal-gear-solid-v-phantom-pai.article:
**Metal Gear Solid V: The Phantom Pain** was the final entry by legendary creator Hideo Kojima in the Metal Gear Solid franchise and also its first genuinely open world, set in the mountains of Afghanistan and the savannas of Angola in the mid-1980s. The game follows Punished Snake, who after a nine-year coma sets out for revenge against the organization Cipher while also building his own mercenary army, Diamond Dogs, funded precisely by resources and prisoners found and extracted directly in the field via the iconic Fulton Recovery balloon system. The structure is mission-based, but each mission is essentially an open puzzle: the player chooses their own arrival time, drop point, loadout, and companion, whether a dog, the sniper Quiet, or a robotic horse.

Stealth infiltration reached unprecedented systemic depth in this entry — dynamic weather, a day-night cycle, and enemies reacting to the player's tactics by installing anti-headshot helmets or reinforcing patrols after repeated infiltrations create a genuinely reactive simulation where no two missions play out the same way. The player's base, Mother Base, develops by gathering personnel and resources, with individual units specialized in combat, reconnaissance, or development able to be combined for more efficient operations. Controls are incomparably smoother than in earlier series entries, since Snake finally moves and aims like a character from a modern action game.

The game shipped unfinished due to Kojima's falling-out with Konami, which showed most clearly in a rushed second act and a missing final chapter, yet the core gameplay and the technical sophistication of the Fox Engine remain generally regarded as among the best in the entire series and the whole stealth-action genre. The Fox Engine ran remarkably stably on Xbox One even during sprawling scenes, and the lighting of desert plains ranked among the visual highlights of the time. Today The Phantom Pain is viewed with mixed feelings: as a torso of a story, yet at the same time as one of the best-designed action sandboxes ever made.
xbox-one__metal-gear-solid-v-phantom-pai.teaser: Kojima's last Metal Gear Solid and the series' first truly open world.

xbox-one__battlefield-1.article:
**Battlefield 1** marked DICE's bold return to the World War I era after previous entries had long focused on modern and near-future conflicts, delivering one of the most striking audiovisual portrayals of that conflict in video games ever. The opening sequence alone, in which the player progressively dies as one soldier after another while their names and dates appear on screen, made it clear the game didn't want to be a typical gung-ho shooter. The single-player campaign split its narrative into several standalone stories called War Stories, each following a different character and front, from a tank crewman at the Battle of Cambrai through an Italian mountain soldier to a British fighter pilot, emphasizing the human, personal tragedy of the great conflict rather than a single linear campaign.

Multiplayer, the series' key focus, offered massive battles of up to sixty-four players on sprawling maps with destructible environments, dynamic weather including sandstorms, and legendary Behemoth vehicles like an airship or an armored train, activated for the team in a significantly worse match position. Alongside classic Conquest and Rush modes came Operations, long multi-map battles with a gradually shifting front line that best captured the war's trench-warfare character. Weapons and equipment faithfully reflected the more primitive but brutal nature of World War I weaponry, from bayonet charges through gas attacks to cumbersome early tanks, and the inaccuracy of period rifles pushed players into closer, riskier combat.

The Frostbite graphics engine achieved on Xbox One one of the most striking renderings of wartime chaos of the generation — the sound of artillery and villages turning into muddy wastelands became the game's signature. Battlefield 1 is generally regarded as one of the best-received entries in the entire series thanks to its atmosphere, theme, and technical execution. The game stayed alive for a long time thanks to expansions bringing new nations and maps, and many players still consider it the last truly great old-school Battlefield.
xbox-one__battlefield-1.teaser: DICE's bold return to World War I, with an impressive portrayal of the conflict.

switch__legend-of-zelda-breath-of-wild.article:
When Nintendo launched the Switch in 2017, it needed a title that would define the new generation — and **Breath of the Wild** fulfilled that task completely. The game radically rewrote the series' rules: linear dungeons were replaced by a vast open Hyrule where, from the first minute, the player can go anywhere and climb any mountain to see what happens. The philosophy of the chemistry engine meant fire ignites grass, metal attracts lightning, and wooden weapons burn — the world reacts to physics as consistently as it does to scripts. This very consistency is the core of the whole game: almost any solution the player thinks of works, and the game rewards them for their own idea instead of forcing them to find the single intended path.

Link wakes up after a hundred years of sleep with no memories, with a single task: defeat Calamity Ganon, who holds Princess Zelda at bay inside the castle. Along the way he needs to overcome four Divine Beasts controlled by the spirits of ancient heroes, gather hearts and stamina across hundreds of shrines, and survive in a harsh wilderness full of monsters, weather, and hunger. The weapon durability system, where weapons break after a few fights, was one of the most discussed elements of the game, but it also forces the player to constantly improvise and not hoard gear for later. Stamina while climbing and paragliding, meanwhile, turns the landscape into a puzzle — every hill becomes a question of whether the player even has the strength to reach the top.

The game's openness was staggering at launch — the developers themselves admitted they wanted the player to theoretically be able to go straight for the final boss. The visual style, combining cel-shading with a watercolor palette, has aged remarkably well, and the music, sparse and ambient, built on lonely piano motifs, heightens the sense of being lost in a vast world. Breath of the Wild received dozens of Game of the Year awards and is still cited today as one of the most influential titles of the decade, one that inspired countless open-world games across the entire industry — from Japanese action RPGs to major Western productions that, following its lead, began stripping icons from maps and letting players discover the world with their own eyes.
switch__legend-of-zelda-breath-of-wild.teaser: An open Hyrule you can go anywhere in from the very first minute; a game that redefined the entire series.

switch__legend-of-zelda-tears-of-kingdom.article:
The sequel to Breath of the Wild had a tough job — surpassing a game that had redefined the entire genre. **Tears of the Kingdom** managed it above all thanks to a new set of abilities that change how the player thinks about the game space. Ultrahand allows combining objects into custom contraptions — rafts with fans, vehicles with weapons, bridges over chasms — and players' creativity quickly outpaced even the developers' wildest imaginations. It's complemented by Fuse, which combines a weapon with any object to turn a stick and a boulder into a mace, and Ascend, which lets you pass through a cave ceiling straight to the surface. Together they form a toolkit that turns every obstacle into an open question instead of a task with a single solution.

This time Link travels not only across the surface of Hyrule, but also up into the floating Sky Islands and down into the sprawling Depths, a dark mirror world underground ruled by danger and a lack of light. The story follows on from earlier events: a mysterious dark force awakens an ancient evil named Ganondorf, and Princess Zelda again disappears, this time under far more mysterious circumstances tied to the kingdom's ancient history. The game keeps the philosophy of a physics toy but expands it with building and assembling contraptions, and technically it's a remarkable feat — the Switch manages to compute the collisions and propulsion of players' homemade inventions without falling apart.

The world is essentially the same as in its predecessor, but thanks to the vertical layer, the transformed landscape, and reworked shrines it feels completely new; ruins fallen from the sky and new caves change even places the player knew by heart. Critics showered the game with top scores, and many called it even more ambitious than its predecessor, even though at its core it's the same gameplay skeleton. Tears of the Kingdom proved that Nintendo can surprise again even within its own, seemingly exhausted formula, and it also became one of the last major titles to squeeze the original Switch's true maximum out of it.
switch__legend-of-zelda-tears-of-kingdom.teaser: A sequel that surpasses Breath of the Wild with a new Ultrahand ability for building machines.

switch__super-mario-odyssey.article:
**Super Mario Odyssey** brought Mario back to the style of 3D sandbox platformers that last shone in Super Mario 64 and Sunshine, but pushed the concept even further thanks to the magical cap Cappy. Cappy lets Mario possess almost any character or object in the world — from a frog through a tank to Bowser himself — and each such possession brings unique mechanics and puzzle solutions. That's the heart of the game's charm: each new ability appears, the player has fun with it for a while, and it's soon swapped for another, so the pace never grows stale and the game doesn't need classic upgrade-collecting.

The story is classically simple: Bowser has kidnapped Princess Peach and is preparing a forced wedding with her, while Mario and Cappy chase his airship Odyssey across a series of themed kingdoms, from the desert Sand Kingdom through the culinary Luncheon Kingdom to the photorealistic metropolis of New Donk City. The contrast between cartoonish Mario and the realistic-looking city inhabited by humans sparked heated debate when the game was revealed, but in the end it works as a refreshing visual experiment. The game emphasizes collecting Moons, of which there are dozens to hundreds in each kingdom, encouraging a free exploratory pace without the need for linear progression — the player can leave a kingdom practically at any time and return whenever they want.

Odyssey is also marked by extremely precise controls and total camera freedom, making it one of the technically most cohesive 3D platformers ever; jumps, flips, and cap throws can be chained into fluid combos, on which the entire speedrunning community has built its existence. The music, led by the central song Jump Up, Super Star!, ranks among the catchiest in the series' history, and its live-sung version was something entirely new for Mario games. Critics and players alike embraced the game as one of the peaks of the genre and as a title that, shortly after launch, showed what the Switch was capable of; after finishing the main story, an extensive postgame full of the toughest challenges awaits.
switch__super-mario-odyssey.teaser: Cappy lets you possess almost anything in the world — from a frog to a tank; 3D Mario at its very best.

switch__mario-kart-8-deluxe.article:
**Mario Kart 8 Deluxe** is an expanded version of the 2014 Wii U game, but on Switch it became such a dominant phenomenon that it now ranks among the best-selling video games in history. It adds all released DLC content, new racers and tracks, restores the battle mode with full-fledged arenas, and introduces two-player-per-kart racing, where one player steers and the other throws items. New assist features — Auto-Steer and Smart Steering — also made the Deluxe version a game a complete newcomer or child can handle without ruining the match for everyone else, which significantly contributed to its reputation as the ideal party game.

The foundation remains unchanged and immensely catchy: eight players duke it out on tracks full of shortcuts, anti-gravity sections, and classic obstacles like banana peels, shells, or the dreaded blue shell, which can flip an entire race in the final second. Anti-gravity isn't just a visual effect — the track curves along walls and ceilings, and bumping into an opponent in this mode speeds up both parties, so it pays to race in a pack. The roster includes dozens of characters from the Mario universe and beyond, each with its own stats affecting speed, acceleration, and weight, which combined with tuning the kart body, wheels, and glider creates a surprisingly deep build system that the tournament scene dissects down to the last digit.

In 2022 the game also received the paid Booster Course Pass expansion, which gradually added another 48 tracks from previous series entries in reworked graphics, pushing the total number of courses to a record number. Technically it's one of the cleanest titles on Switch — it holds a stable frame rate even in split-screen and looks practically as good in handheld mode as on a TV. It's precisely the combination of simple rules, chaotic multiplayer, and a huge amount of content that made Mario Kart 8 Deluxe an evergreen that has held its place at parties and professional tournaments alike for over seven years, and it still sells in the millions every year.
switch__mario-kart-8-deluxe.teaser: The best-selling racing game of all time; DLC tracks, revived battle mode, and two players on one kart.

switch__super-smash-bros-ultimate.article:
**Super Smash Bros. Ultimate** is a grandiose celebration of the entire history of video games, led by designer Masahiro Sakurai, who promised that everyone would be here – and he really did gather absolutely every character who has ever appeared in the Smash series, from Mario and Link through Pikachu to Solid Snake and Sonic the Hedgehog. Over the years, the game expanded its roster with paid fighters through the Fighters Pass, bringing in completely unexpected faces such as Sephiroth from Final Fantasy VII, Steve from Minecraft, Kazuya from Tekken, or Sora from Kingdom Hearts, and the final fighter roster exceeded ninety characters. Each of them received their own set of moves and animations, which makes Ultimate a project whose scope is unique in the fighting genre.

The core gameplay stays faithful to the series: it's a platform fighter where the goal isn't to zero out an opponent's health bar, but to increase their damage percentage and then knock them off the screen. This simple principle is also the reason the game works on two completely different levels – as chaotic fun for four people on the couch with random items, and as a tightly tuned one-on-one duel without any distracting elements. Ultimate adds an elaborate single-player mode, World of Light, with an expansive challenge map and hundreds of spirits inspired by characters from across the entire games industry, whose traits can be combined into custom builds.

The game also excels as a spectated esports title thanks to its deep movement system and an active community that holds tournaments around the world. The visuals, a soundtrack numbering in the thousands of tracks, and a huge selection of arenas make Ultimate arguably the most comprehensive crossover title in video game history and the flagship of Switch multiplayer. The game's online side, on the other hand, was long a target of criticism for its unstable connection, so the competitive scene made do with its own unofficial solutions for years and tournaments were preferentially played live. Even so, Ultimate remains a game that you just need to turn on, and any group of people instantly knows what to do.
switch__super-smash-bros-ultimate.teaser: Sakurai's celebration of gaming history — practically everyone the series ever had shows up.

switch__splatoon-2.article:
**Splatoon 2** brought a refreshingly colorful alternative to traditional shooters onto the Switch. Instead of eliminating opponents, the goal is to cover as much territory as possible in your own team's ink, which makes the game a more strategic and accessible experience than classic arenas – even a player who doesn't hit anyone can win the match for their team by diligently painting the floor. Players, in the form of humanoid squid-kids called Inklings, can transform into cephalopods and in this form move lightning-fast through their own color across walls and floors, creating a unique rhythm between attack and tactical maneuvering. Ink serves simultaneously as ammunition and as terrain, so shooting, movement, and territory capture are all one and the same activity in this game.

Besides four-versus-four Turf War matches, the game offers ranked Ranked Battles with variations like Rainmaker or Tower Control, as well as a full-fledged single-player campaign set in the underground Octo Valley, where the Inklings face an army of Octarians; the campaign also serves as an excellent tutorial for controls and the individual weapon types. The off-battlefield layer deserves special attention too: the capital city of Inkopolis Square has its own music industry with idol bands, whose songs accompany the seasonal Splatfests – massive community events where players split into two sides based on their preferred theme and compete for the honor of their team.

The second installment added new weapons, such as the Splat Roller and the Dualies pistols with a dodge roll, and expanded the offering with the cooperative Salmon Run mode, in which four players fend off waves of salmonid monsters and collect their eggs. The paid Octo Expansion then offered a series of very difficult trials and a surprisingly dark story that earned a reputation as the best content in the entire game. Splatoon 2 became one of the pillars of the early Switch library, exceptionally popular especially in Japan, and cemented the series' reputation as the most distinctive new brand Nintendo has created in the last decade.
switch__splatoon-2.teaser: A colorful alternative to shooters — the team that paints more territory wins, not the one with more kills.

switch__splatoon-3.article:
**Splatoon 3** moves the action from Inkopolis to the sunny coastal town of Splatsville in the Splatlands region, where Inklings and the newly playable Octolings converge from all around. Visually, it's a shift toward a rougher, desert-like, street-fashion-soaked style that suits the series and sets it apart from its more cleanly colorful predecessors. The core gameplay remains faithful to the series – painting territory in your own color, transforming into a cephalopod for quick movement, and competing in team Turf War matches and ranked modes – but Splatoon 3 adds a new weapon class, the Stringers (ink bows), and the Splatana, wide wiper blades for close combat, noticeably broadening the range of possible playstyles.

Also new is Tricolor Turf War, a three-team match that appears during Splatfests. The single-player campaign, Return of the Mammalians, is the most expansive in the series and tells a darker story about a strange furry entity controlling the inhabitants of the Splatlands, with a visually spectacular finale. The cooperative monster-wave mode Salmon Run, popular from the previous installment, has become a permanent part of the game instead of limited time windows, allowing it to be played anytime, and the collectible card game Tableturf Battle was added, translating the territory-capturing principle onto a board and becoming a surprisingly addictive side pastime.

Splatfests were revised into a three-way clash, pitting three factions against each other instead of two, and the game regularly receives new weapons, maps, and cosmetic items through seasonal updates as well as the paid Side Order expansion, which offers a roguelite challenge with the heroine from Octo Expansion, Agent 8. The developers also gradually improved connection quality and the speed of returning to the game after a match, things the community had long criticized in previous installments. Splatoon 3 became one of the fastest-selling titles in Japan and confirmed that Nintendo managed to build the original brand into a mainstay with a loyal community outside of the traditional Mario and Zelda franchises.
switch__splatoon-3.teaser: The Inklings in sunny Splatsville; rougher visuals, the same addictive painting action.

switch__animal-crossing-new-horizons.article:
**Animal Crossing: New Horizons** launched in March 2020, at the exact moment the world got stuck in lockdowns because of the pandemic, and it became an unexpected cultural phenomenon and refuge for millions of players. The game leaves behind the series' established towns and puts the player in the role of the first resident of an uninhabited island, who, with the help of the raccoon-run company Tom Nook, gradually builds it up from scratch – from a tent through their own house to an extensive village full of animal neighbors. Progress isn't driven by experience or levels but by small tasks and mortgage installments, creating a calm, gentle rhythm where nothing is ever on fire.

A key element is real time: the game runs according to the actual date and clock, seasons, holidays, and the day-night cycle all change, which supports a long-term, meditative rhythm of play rather than a chase after a goal. The new terraforming mechanic allows you to change the terrain, build bridges and ladders, and move entire rivers, so every island has a completely unique look reflecting its owner's taste; the community around sharing island designs became its own phenomenon on social media. Gathering fruit, catching fish and bugs for the museum, crafting furniture using DIY recipes, and visiting neighboring islands via Nintendo Switch Online form the core of an endless loop of activities, complemented by the turnip exchange, the one genuinely tense part of the game.

The game also allows for rich creative expression through a clothing and pattern design tool, with which players crafted everything from paving tiles to replicas of designer outfits. Thanks to its soothing atmosphere, gentle acoustic music that changes every hour, cute graphics, and the absence of any pressure to perform, New Horizons became a symbol of the pandemic era and one of the best-selling exclusive Switch titles ever. Subsequent free updates added characters like café owner Brewster or musician K.K. Slider, and the paid Happy Home Paradise expansion added design work on other residents' vacation homes.
switch__animal-crossing-new-horizons.teaser: Released right into lockdown and became a phenomenon; building an island from scratch with Tom Nook.

switch__super-mario-maker-2.article:
**Super Mario Maker 2** brings to Switch an idea that proved on Wii U just how powerful a tool can arise from simple platforming building blocks. The game gives players the full set of tools Nintendo itself used for decades to build Mario platformers – from the classic Super Mario Bros. style through New Super Mario Bros. to 3D World – and lets them design their own levels by dragging blocks, enemies, and mechanisms directly on the touchscreen. Each style doesn't just change the graphics but also the jump physics and enemy behavior, so the same design plays completely differently in a different style.

New compared to the first game is a nighttime palette that changes the rules of individual worlds, water currents, slopes, linked On/Off switches, and above all a full-fledged Story Mode, in which Mario helps rebuild Princess Peach's castle across more than a hundred hand-designed levels from Nintendo itself – these also serve as an excellent showcase of everything the editor can do. The online community aspect remains the heart of the game: players upload their own creations to a global server, rate them with a thumbs up, work through difficulty leaderboards in Endless Challenge mode, and compete in online multiplayer races across community levels.

The editor is remarkably deep and allows creating not just traditional jumping segments but also complex logic puzzles, auto-scrollers, escape rooms, or music sequencers that exploit the game's physics in ways the developers hardly intended. This layer of ingenuity is exactly what made Mario Maker 2 a phenomenon on streaming platforms, where watching desperate attempts to beat extremely difficult kaizo levels became entertainment in its own right. Thanks to its huge and creative community, the game contains effectively endless content that continues to grow to this day, and it has become a favorite tool for speedrunners and creators of custom minigames built purely from Mario's building blocks.
switch__super-mario-maker-2.teaser: Nintendo handed players the toolkit it used to build Mario platformers for decades.

switch__luigi-s-mansion-3.article:
**Luigi's Mansion 3** puts the timid Luigi in the role of the main hero, who, with the help of the upgraded Poltergust G-00 vacuum, must face an army of ghosts in the luxurious Last Resort hotel, where he was invited on vacation along with Mario, Peach, and friends. The trap was set by the sinister painter King Boo, whose magic portrait pulled the whole group into a trap and turned the hotel into a nest of ghosts scattered across its floors, each of which has its own visual theme – from a kitchen through an art floor to a frozen swimming pool. The hotel's structure is also a clever pacing solution: each floor works as a separate episode with its own puzzle and boss, so the game never turns into repetition.

The gameplay combines exploration and puzzle-solving using a flashlight and vacuum with tense combat sequences against ghosts, which must first be stunned with a flash and then sucked up. New moves were added too, such as a vacuum slam or a burst of exhaust air, giving fights against larger groups of ghosts noticeably better pacing than in previous installments. New is the companion Gooigi, a gelatinous copy of Luigi, who can be controlled by a second player in co-op or switched to solo for solving puzzles that require two characters at once, though Gooigi can pass through grates but is vulnerable to water and sharp objects. The game also offers robust multiplayer modes, ScareScraper and ScreamPark, for up to eight players locally and online.

Visually, it's one of the technically most impressive titles on Switch thanks to detailed animations, playful lighting, soft shadows, and comic-book-like character expressions – Luigi's terrified faces rank among the best things Nintendo's animators have ever shown. Almost every piece of furniture is interactive, so vacuuming curtains, pillows, and trash is entertaining in its own right. Critics praised the humor, the creativity of the boss fights, and the solid length of the campaign, making Luigi's Mansion 3 one of the best-reviewed titles in the series and a favorite choice for players looking for a lighter but visually rich action-adventure.
switch__luigi-s-mansion-3.teaser: Luigi and his Poltergust vacuum clean out a haunted hotel split into themed floors.

switch__pokemon-sword-and-shield.article:
**Pokémon Sword and Shield** marked the main Pokémon series' debut on a home console and, at the same time, the first fully 3D open environments in mainline games. The story takes trainers to the Galar region, inspired by Great Britain, where the challenge for the league also becomes a journey full of gym battles taking place in front of a roaring crowd in giant stadiums – enabled by the new Dynamax mechanic, which temporarily enlarges a Pokémon to gigantic proportions and, in even rarer cases, transforms its appearance through Gigantamax. The football-like, sporting atmosphere of the whole league gave the series a new flair: gym battles feel like sold-out matches, complete with fans, uniforms, and anthem-like songs.

The open Wild Area was a novelty for the series: a sprawling meadow full of randomly roaming wild Pokémon and changing weather that affects which species appear, plus a free camera the series hadn't known until then. This is also where cooperative Max Raid Battles are focused, in which four players team up to take on a single giant Pokémon. The game also introduced new Galarian forms of familiar Pokémon adapted to the local environment and expanded the Galar League's roster of trainers with more distinctive personalities, including rival Hop and champion Leon.

The release was accompanied by controversy over the so-called Dexit – for the first time in the series' history, it wasn't possible to transfer all Pokémon from previous generations, which divided the fanbase and sparked debate about how far the series can grow. Even so, the game sold exceptionally well, and two expansions, Isle of Armor and Crown Tundra, added new areas, legendary Pokémon, and characters. Sword and Shield showed where the series could head on more powerful hardware and paved the way for even more open successors. The side mode of cooking curry at the campfire added an unexpectedly beloved pastime, letting players spend time with their team outside of battles.
switch__pokemon-sword-and-shield.teaser: The first mainline Pokemon in a fully 3D open environment; Dynamax turns battles into giant clashes.

switch__pokemon-legends-arceus.article:
**Pokémon Legends: Arceus** is the most radical experiment in the history of the mainline Pokémon series. Instead of turn-based battles in the grass and linear towns, it offers a semi-open world set in the distant past of the Hisui region, the predecessor of today's Sinnoh, where the player, as a member of the newly founded Survey Corps, maps unexplored wilderness and compiles the first Pokédex. There's also a crucial shift in tone: at this point in time, people don't yet know Pokémon and are afraid of them, so the game tells a story of discovery and the slow building of trust between two worlds instead of a sporting challenge.

Catching Pokémon happens directly in real time without switching to a separate battle screen – the player sneaks through the landscape, throws Poké Balls at unsuspecting creatures or first weakens them in battle, and a botched attempt can spook an entire herd. Additionally, aggressive Pokémon can now attack the player directly, who can then faint and lose some of the items they've collected, adding unusual tension to exploration. The battles themselves remain turn-based, but sped up and supplemented with new Strong and Agile attack styles that change the turn order and damage amount, so even familiar moves are used differently than before.

The world is divided into several vast areas with different biomes, from volcanic plains to snowy mountains, and the player returns between them to the central Jubilife Village, where gear upgrades and missions for the local residents take place. A special chapter belongs to the so-called noble Pokémon, giant enraged creatures the player faces in action battles involving dodging and throwing healing balms. The story escalates with a darker twist involving the mythological Pokémon Arceus, the creator of the universe. Critics praised Game Freak's courage in abandoning decades-old series conventions, despite technical shortcomings in the form of simpler graphics and occasional frame-rate drops. Legends: Arceus became one of the fastest-selling Pokémon games in history and hinted at the direction the series might take next.
switch__pokemon-legends-arceus.teaser: The series' most radical departure from formula — an open wilderness instead of turn-based battles in the grass.

switch__pokemon-scarlet-and-violet.article:
