Technically, it's a striking spectacle with massive city locations and thoughtful lighting, and the music, alternating chamber motifs with choir, is among the strongest aspects of the whole production. Reviews praised the production values, the storytelling, and the combat, while criticism was aimed at the more linear structure and at how side quests often just fill in the world's background. Today, Final Fantasy XVI is a clear choice for players seeking mature fantasy with an emphasis on action, who are willing to part ways with the series' classic form.
ps5__final-fantasy-xvi.teaser: The darkest and most action-heavy entry in the series; Eikons also serve here as weapons of mass destruction.

ps5__baldur-s-gate-3.article:
**Baldur's Gate 3** brought console gamers a classic Dungeons & Dragons tabletop RPG on a scale the genre hadn't seen in a long time. At the outset, the hero is infected by a parasite that threatens to transform him into something entirely different, and the search for a cure leads through forests, swamps, subterranean realms, and the city of Baldur's Gate itself. Players can create a character from a wide range of races and classes, or take control of one of the prepared companions, each with their own motivations, secrets, and opinions about the hero's decisions.

Combat is turn-based, following the fifth edition rules, with dice rolls, actions and bonus actions, terrain height, and plenty of room for ingenuity. Practically every problem has more than one solution: it can be negotiated, bypassed with a spell, solved through a quiet break-in, or simply set on fire. The game's strength lies in accounting for approaches other RPGs wouldn't allow — killing an important character, sacrificing an ally, or a completely unexpected dice roll outcome. Co-op for up to four players, including split-screen on a single console, is one of the few ways to experience an RPG of this scale together. The environment also plays its part: burning oil, knocking an opponent off a height, or a frozen floor can decide a fight just as reliably as a well-chosen spell.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs smoothly, and fast loading helps considerably given how often you revisit saved positions; gamepad controls got their own radial menus and were designed from the ground up rather than simply ported from the PC version. The storytelling is backed by an extensive voice cast and directed dialogue, and the music, alternating chamber motifs with songs, has an unusually strong identity. Reception was extraordinary, and the game noticeably raised expectations for choice-driven possibilities in modern RPGs. Today it's a staple in the library of anyone who loves narrative-driven games — just be prepared for dozens of hours and an appetite for reading. The screen also fits a journal, map, and inventory without shrinking the text, which for a game with this many items is no small feat.
ps5__baldur-s-gate-3.teaser: An RPG built on Dungeons & Dragons rules, on a scale the genre hadn't seen in a long time.

ps5__cyberpunk-2077.article:
**Cyberpunk 2077** received a native PlayStation 5 version in 2022, by which time it already had a rocky launch and a long string of fixes behind it. The player takes on the role of a mercenary named V, who craves a reputation in the megalopolis of Night City, and instead unwittingly gets the personality of the long-dead rebel Johnny Silverhand, played by Keanu Reeves, uploaded into their head. What follows is at once a crime story, a meditation on identity, and a tour of one of the most densely populated open worlds ever made.

The game combines a first-person shooter with RPG character building: implants alter the body's abilities, hacking programs let you take out cameras and enemies remotely, and most missions can be completed quietly, through force, or via the net. The side jobs are among the best-written content the genre offers, and several of them outshine the main storyline. The major 2.0 update overhauled the skill trees, police behavior, and vehicle combat, changing the game enough that it's worth returning to even for those who played it earlier. A character can be built as a stealthy hacker, an armored brawler with arm implants, or a sniper, with the choice reflected in the dialogue options available.

The native PS5 version added a ray-tracing mode as well as a smooth-performance option, fast loading, and haptic feedback that distinguishes individual weapons. Driving around the city gained pursuits and motorcycle combat in later updates. Night City glows with neon, holograms, and advertising to the point that simply walking the streets works as an experience in itself, and the soundtrack blending industrial, synth music, and rock tracks from fictional bands is among what players remember longest. Reception shifted over time from disappointment to acclaim, helped by the Phantom Liberty expansion. Today, Cyberpunk 2077 is often cited as an example that even a very troubled launch can be fixed through persistent work.
ps5__cyberpunk-2077.teaser: Mercenary V shares their head with a digital copy of Johnny Silverhand, played by Keanu Reeves.

ps5__persona-5-royal.article:
**Persona 5 Royal** arrived on PlayStation 5 as the expanded version of one of the most beloved modern JRPGs, bringing with it the story of high schoolers who deal with everyday worries by day and enter the minds of corrupt adults by night. The hero arrives in Tokyo with a probationary sentence he didn't deserve, and together with a group of outcasts founds the Phantom Thieves, a band that steals criminals' twisted desires by plundering the treasure at the root of that corruption from within their hearts.

The game splits into two tightly linked halves. In the city, a calendar runs its course: the player goes to school, works, studies, and above all builds relationships with characters who soon unlock new abilities in combat. The other half consists of exploring Palaces, stylized dungeons full of puzzles and stealth, where turn-based battles emphasize finding enemy weaknesses and chaining attacks across the whole party. Collecting and fusing Personas, beings that serve as both spells and passive abilities, gives the system surprising depth. The Royal version also adds new characters and an entire final act. Time pressure is real, too: every Palace has a deadline it must be cleared by, so the player is constantly weighing what they can still fit in.

The console version on PS5 stands out above all for its smooth visuals and fast loading, which benefits a game built on hundreds of short transitions between locations. Visually, it's one of the most distinctive works out there: the red-and-black interface is animated in its own right and has become a template copied by a whole host of imitators. Shoji Meguro's soundtrack, blending acid jazz with funk and vocals, ranks among the highest-rated in the genre. Critics received the game excellently, and its influence shows in how many newer JRPGs have adopted the calendar-and-relationships structure. The console version also includes previously released expansions, making it the most complete version of the game available. Expect a very long experience, but one that pays off with every hour.
ps5__persona-5-royal.teaser: An expanded version of the beloved JRPG about the Phantom Thieves, who steal people's twisted desires.

ps5__metaphor-refantazio.article:
**Metaphor: ReFantazio** was created by the team behind the Persona series and transplanted its proven formula into a fantasy world full of races, prejudice, and politics. The kingdom has lost its ruler, and the successor is to be chosen through an unusual election that anyone can enter. The hero enters it with his own hidden goal: to save the cursed crown prince. The story openly tackles discrimination, fear of otherness, and how easily a crowd can be swayed by a simple answer, making it unusually mature material by the genre's standards.

The gameplay is again built around a calendar: the path to the election has a fixed deadline, so every day the player must decide whether to head into a dungeon, strengthen bonds with companions, or cultivate virtues that unlock further options. Combat combines fast dispatching of weaker enemies directly in the field with a turn-based mode for serious encounters, where exploiting weaknesses and switching archetypes decides the outcome. Archetypes are this world's equivalent of classes; they can be developed, combined, and can pass abilities between one another, giving party building plenty of room for experimentation. Travel between cities happens inside a strange walking colossus, which serves as a mobile base and also as a place to read, cook, and rest.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs smoothly with virtually no waiting, which matters a great deal for a title with so much movement between city, road, and dungeon. Visually, it commits to strong stylization, with a stamped, almost paper-like interface and inventively ugly enemy designs; Shoji Meguro's music adds choral singing in a constructed language that players remember after the very first battle. Critics received the game very warmly, often calling it one of the best JRPG titles of its era. Difficulty can be freely adjusted, so even a player still getting used to turn-based combat can handle it. For PS5 owners who enjoy turn-based combat and don't mind a substantial amount of reading, it's a clear recommendation.
ps5__metaphor-refantazio.teaser: From the Persona team; a fantasy about choosing a successor to the throne and a hidden fight against discrimination.

ps5__like-dragon-infinite-wealth.article:
**Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth** sends the eternal idealist Ichiban Kasuga from the streets of Japan all the way to Hawaii, where he searches for the mother he never knew. Alongside him, the game tells a second storyline with Kazuma Kiryu, the series' longtime face, who this time confronts his own past as well as a very personal threat. Alternating between the two perspectives gives the whole game an unusual emotional range: one half is optimistic and playful, the other bids farewell to an era players have followed for two decades.

Combat remains turn-based, as the series established in the previous installment, but has gained greater freedom of movement around the arena, which favors attacks from behind and the use of objects in the environment. Characters change jobs, which determine their abilities and appearance in combat, and combined with the bonds between party members, a surprisingly deep system emerges. As always, the main story is surrounded by a huge amount of side content: building your own island, a collectible game with strange little figures, a dating app, karaoke, arcade minigames, and dozens of street stories that mix absurd humor with unexpectedly serious themes. Combat also rewards knowledge of the surroundings, since a bicycle, a traffic cone, or a wall behind an enemy can multiply the damage dealt.

On PS5, the game runs smoothly, loading between districts is short, and Hawaii is among the most colorful settings the series has ever had. The sound relies on strong combat music and very good voice performances in both Japanese and English, with the Hawaiian sections accompanied by English-speaking characters and the game playing with how Ichiban communicates in a foreign land. Reviews received the game very well, praising especially Kiryu's story and the sheer amount of content, with occasional pacing fragmentation cited as a drawback. New players are advised to have at least a rough idea of the previous installment, since there are truly a great many callbacks to earlier events that the game relies on. But whoever is looking for a long PS5 game that alternates between laughter and heartbreak will find one of the most generous offerings here. Anyone wanting to see everything can easily spend a hundred hours with it.
ps5__like-dragon-infinite-wealth.teaser: Ichiban Kasuga searches for his mother in Hawaii, joined by the legendary Kazuma Kiryu.

ps5__dragon-s-dogma-2.article:
**Dragon's Dogma 2** picks up more than a decade later, continuing the cult action RPG and once again casting the player as the Arisen, a person whose heart was taken by a dragon and who sets out to both revive and avenge the world. This time the open world encompasses two rival realms, a human kingdom and a land of feline inhabitants, and the journey between them matters as much as the destination. The game deliberately doesn't hand out fast travel for free: trekking along a road where a band of goblins might attack at any moment, or an ogre might come down from a hillside, forms a substantial part of the experience.

The series' main distinguishing feature remains the pawns, artificial companions the player either creates or borrows from other players online. Pawns learn from the player's playstyle, advise on where to go, and carry their accumulated experience back to their creator. Combat combines fast-paced action with vocations ranging from warrior through archer to mage, and in encounters with large enemies you can literally climb onto their bodies and stab at their weak points. The emphasis on physics, character weight, and use of the environment makes every fight feel a little different from the last. The chosen vocation can also be switched in larger cities, so a single character can gradually go through several completely different combat styles.

The game runs on the RE Engine and on PS5 offers detailed lighting, a grounded view of the world, and a realistic day-night cycle in which night is genuinely dark and dangerous. After release, criticism emerged over uneven performance, especially in cities, along with reservations about how the game handles saving and paid convenience items. Even so, most reviews received it positively, precisely for its uncompromising approach and for feeling unusual amid the current flood of open-world titles. The strongest experience is nighttime travel with a lantern, when you can only see a few meters around you and every sound from the forest spells trouble. Today it's a title for players who want adventure rather than a quest checklist.
ps5__dragon-s-dogma-2.teaser: An open-world action RPG where traveling the land is dangerous and fast travel isn't free.

ps5__tales-of-arise.article:
**Tales of Arise** marked a major reset of look and tone for the long-running Tales series. The story unfolds on two connected planets, where one civilization has oppressed the other for three hundred years, stripping it of its resources. The hero is a man without memory who feels no pain and wears an iron mask; his counterpart is a girl from the oppressors' realm whom no one can touch without being harmed themselves. From this seemingly simple premise, the game gradually builds a story about retribution, guilt, and how hard it is to find reconciliation between peoples.

Combat continues the series' tradition: it plays out in real time, with the player controlling one character and unleashing chains of attacks and special abilities while the rest of the party acts according to set behavior. New this time are combined attacks with individual companions, which reward good timing, and a much clearer system for managing resources used for spells. Outside combat, there's cooking, fishing, gathering materials, and above all short scenes between characters, which have always been among the series' best moments and here too deepen the bonds within the party. Enemies have resistances based on elements, and the right party member can cut a long fight down to a few seconds.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs at high resolution and smoothly, and its art style, combining anime characters with painterly backgrounds, really shines on a big screen. Motoi Sakuraba's music alternates orchestral themes with rock inserts during battles. Critics received the game as the best entry in the series in a long time, praising especially its presentation and more serious storytelling, with objections aimed at a weaker second half and repetitive environments. The interface and pacing also shed much of the sluggishness earlier installments in the series suffered from, and loading on PS5 is virtually instant. For a player who wants a classically structured JRPG on PS5 without dozens of hours of side content, it's a very good choice.
ps5__tales-of-arise.teaser: A JRPG with a striking visual reboot of the series; a story of two civilizations at war.

ps5__kingdom-come-deliverance-ii.article:
**Kingdom Come: Deliverance II** continues the story of the blacksmith's son Henry against the backdrop of the Bohemian lands in the early fifteenth century, during the conflict between Wenceslas IV and Sigismund of Luxembourg. The game holds to a realistic approach with no dragons or magic: the world is made up of real places, ordinary villages, castles, and a city where you can get lost in alleys between craftsmen's workshops. The story works from the premise that the hero isn't a hero from the start, letting the player earn skill, education, and the respect of those around him.

The progression system has no classic classes: skills grow through what the player actually does, so horseback riding, blacksmithing, alchemy, persuasion, and swordplay all improve with practice. Combat is deliberately demanding, based on attack directions, blocking, and the advantages of specific weapons against given armor. Alongside that, the game features stealth, lockpicking, brewing potions by an authentic process, and the fact that a dirty or drunk hero will come across differently to people. Side quests often take the form of small mysteries with several possible solutions. Part of the world is also the characters' daily routine — they go to sleep, to work, and to the tavern — so theft or an assault has genuine witnesses and consequences.

On PlayStation 5, the game took advantage of stronger hardware for noticeably more stable performance than the first installment had on the older generation, along with fast loading of its sprawling world. The atmosphere is helped by restrained lighting, changeable weather, and music built on period instruments and choral singing. Reviews received the game very well, praising especially the storytelling, the wealth of options, and the care taken over period detail. For Czech players, the familiar home setting and full Czech dubbing carry particular value. Those unfamiliar with the first installment get a sufficient recap of prior events at the start. Expect a slower start and a game that rewards patience far more than quick reflexes.
ps5__kingdom-come-deliverance-ii.teaser: A Czech RPG without dragons or magic — a realistic Middle Ages during the conflict between Wenceslaus IV and Sigismund.

ps5__hogwarts-legacy.article:
**Hogwarts Legacy** fulfilled an old gamer wish for an open-world wizarding school game, setting it in the nineteenth century, long before the events of the well-known books. The player creates their own student, who enrolls straight into the fifth year and simultaneously discovers that they can see ancient magic no one else perceives. The main storyline leads to a mystery hidden beneath the school, but around it spreads an entire region with villages, caves, poacher camps, and guarded chests that will keep players occupied for dozens of hours.

Combat is fully action-based: the player assigns spells to buttons, combines attacks to break shields, lifts enemies into the air, and supplements them with potions and plants from their own greenhouse. Outside of combat, they attend classes, solve puzzles, fly on a broomstick and on winged creatures, and manage the Room of Requirement, a customizable space of their own where they keep rescued magical animals and craft equipment. Choosing a house affects the common room and a handful of quests, but the main story remains shared. There are also flying lessons, duels with wizards in an arena, and collecting pages from books that expand knowledge about the world.

On PlayStation 5 the game offers several visual modes, including one with ray tracing, and fast loading that helps a lot given how intricate the building is. Its strongest asset is precisely the depiction of the castle itself: moving paintings, shifting staircases, and detailed interiors rank among the best-designed things licensed games have offered. The transition between the castle and the open countryside happens without visible loading, and the music builds on familiar themes without merely repeating them. Reviews were mostly positive, with reservations about repetitive side activities and a story that doesn't reach the quality of its setting. For fans of the source material, though, it's the closest possible approximation of what actually studying at such a school might be like.
ps5__hogwarts-legacy.teaser: An open world of 19th-century Hogwarts, long before the story of the Harry Potter books.

ps5__resident-evil-4.article:
**Resident Evil 4** is a remake of one of the most influential action games of all time, and Capcom approached it with a real feel for what made the original so special. Leon S. Kennedy heads to a remote European village to find the kidnapped president's daughter, Ashley Graham, and instead of ordinary villagers encounters the fanatical cult Los Illuminados, whose members are controlled by a parasite. The structure stays faithful to the original — village, castle, island — but the individual locations are larger, more interconnected, and full of side quests, treasures, and hidden shortcuts, so the playthrough feels more like an expedition than a series of arenas.

The combat system underwent the biggest transformation. Leon can now move while aiming, sneak, and silently dispatch enemies with a knife, except the knife has its own durability and is also used for parrying attacks and escaping grabs. This creates a rhythm where you're constantly weighing shooting, blocking, and dodging against your remaining supplies. The Merchant again buys and upgrades gear, adds quests for rewards, and ammo crafting turns every material you find into a decision. Ashley no longer has her own health or inventory, which makes escorting her far less frustrating. On PlayStation 5 the game runs on the RE Engine with optional ray tracing, smooth performance, and dense haptic feedback that makes the shotgun and pistol feel distinctly different.

The atmosphere leans on darkness, rain, and fog; the music only kicks in during tense moments, leaving the rest to the sound of footsteps and the muttering of the Ganados. Reception was enthusiastic, and the game quickly ranked among the best-reviewed remakes of its time. The original's influence on the over-the-shoulder genre is well known, and this new version shows that its language is still very much alive. The Separate Ways add-on with Ada Wong and the free Mercenaries mode extend its lifespan well beyond a single playthrough. A standalone expansion mode for PS VR2 also lets players experience the whole campaign in first-person virtual reality, where weapons are reloaded by hand and the knife is wielded with genuine motion — it's a different experience, yet still the same game.
ps5__resident-evil-4.teaser: A remake of one of the most influential action games ever; faithful in spirit, rebuilt in the details.

ps5__dead-space.article:
**Dead Space** brings players back aboard the mining ship USG Ishimura, where engineer Isaac Clarke searches for his girlfriend and instead of the crew finds Necromorphs — mutated bodies that must literally be dismembered piece by piece. The remake of the original 2008 game keeps the entire narrative skeleton and its legendary emphasis on strategic dismemberment, where you aim at limbs instead of the head, but rebuilt everything around it from the ground up. The Ishimura is now one continuous location without loading screens, connected by tram and elevators, so you return to earlier decks with new access privileges and discover what you previously had to bypass.

Gameplay rests on the plasma cutter, kinesis, and stasis. Kinesis can pick up and hurl even severed enemy limbs, stasis slows down both attacks and mechanisms, and the ammo economy forces you to choose between spending rounds or improvising with your surroundings. Enemies have an elaborately layered anatomy, so exposing muscle and bone functions as readable feedback. A new system dynamically changes the presence of enemies and sounds based on your progress, so a walk down a familiar corridor never repeats the same way twice. Isaac also now speaks, which changes his relationship with the crew and with the ship. On PlayStation 5 the game looks very impressive thanks to lighting, volumetric fog, spatial audio, and haptics that transmit the cutter's vibration into your hands.

The whole interface remains diegetic — health displayed on the suit's spine, inventory shown as a hologram — which means the game never pauses to interrupt itself. The soundtrack works with silence, industrial creaking, and sudden string outbursts. Reception was very positive, and the remake is often cited as an example of how to modernize a classic without losing its identity. The original's influence on space horror action is undeniable, and this version is now the best way to experience the Ishimura for the first time. Those who know the original by heart will appreciate small changes to quest layout and an expanded Nicole storyline that gives the ending noticeably more weight, as well as a single-life highest difficulty for anyone wanting a true test of nerve.
ps5__dead-space.teaser: A remake of the classic space horror; strategic dismemberment of the Necromorphs remains its heart.

ps5__callisto-protocol.article:
**The Callisto Protocol** takes players into Black Iron Prison on Jupiter's moon Callisto, where pilot Jacob Lee finds himself behind bars after a crash just as the inmates begin transforming into deformed Biophages. The game was made by a studio led by one of the creators of the original Dead Space, and the lineage shows at every step — from tight crawlspaces and shafts to brutal death animations to an industrial aesthetic where the biggest enemy is confined space itself. Progression is markedly more linear than in related titles, and the game focuses on the pacing of one long, filthy way out.

Combat unusually leans on melee. A baton is paired with a dodge system in which tilting the stick lets you evade blows before countering, ideally with a combination of a strike and a quick shot to an exposed weak point. The key gadget is the GRP gravity glove, which lets you hurl enemies into fans, presses, or spikes, so the environment itself functions as a weapon. Ammo is scarce, upgrades happen at vending machines, and mutating enemies force you to shoot off their sprouting tendrils before they turn into a stronger form. On PlayStation 5, the biggest draw is the visuals: photogrammetric character models, wet surfaces, volumetric lighting, and highly detailed facial animation.

The atmosphere is helped by minimalist sound, booming bass, and an almost total absence of music in passages where you sneak past blind enemies. Reception was more mixed than expected — criticism targeted the repetitive combat structure and the heavy-handed use of death scenes, while praise went to the craftsmanship and dense atmosphere. Later updates added new difficulty levels and a New Game Plus mode, and the Final Transmission add-on finishes telling the story. Today it's a short but intense showcase for sci-fi horror fans. The additional content also brought a wave-based mode facing an endless tide of Biophages, so the game doesn't end with the credits. Anyone looking mainly for a visual experience who doesn't mind being led by the hand will find here one of the filthiest and most tactile space stations of recent years.
ps5__callisto-protocol.teaser: A survival horror from a co-creator of Dead Space; cramped shafts and brutal death animations.

ps5__alan-wake-2.article:
**Alan Wake 2** arrives thirteen years later and turns an adventure-action game into a full-blooded survival horror centered on two lead characters. FBI agent Saga Anderson investigates ritual murders near the town of Bright Falls, while writer Alan Wake is still trying to write his way out of the dark place where he got trapped at the end of the first game. Both storylines can be switched between almost freely, and their events intertwine, so the narrative feels like a spiral in which motifs keep returning, each time in a different light.

Gameplay rests on limited ammunition, a flashlight that first strips enemies of their protective shadow, and two original mental spaces. Saga assembles evidence on a board and profiles suspects in her Mind Place, while Alan rewrites scenes in the Writer's Room, literally altering the shape of the New York streets around him. On top of that come light-based puzzles, gathering supplies, and exploring both forest and urban locations. On PlayStation 5 the game ranks among the most technically impressive titles of the generation — lighting, volumetric fog, digitized actor faces, and a smooth blend of live-action footage with the engine create images that are sometimes hard to distinguish from film.

The atmosphere is slow, oppressive, and full of Nordic silence, interrupted by radio broadcasts and found manuscripts. Music plays an extraordinary role: every chapter ends with a song, and one of the most acclaimed sequences in the whole game plays out as a full-blown musical number. Critics received the game enthusiastically, praising it especially for its direction, art direction, and the courage to tell a non-linear story; the commercial launch was initially slower due to being exclusively digital. Today, Alan Wake 2 is regarded as Remedy's recommended peak and a gateway into their interconnected universe, which is also joined by two story expansions. Gathering supplies is deliberately scarce, and the game often encourages you to run past enemies rather than kill them, which is a major shift compared to the first game. This is helped further by exceptional spatial sound work, where the whisper of the Dark Presence comes precisely from the direction you aren't looking.
ps5__alan-wake-2.teaser: After 13 years, a full-blooded horror about two characters whose stories intertwine.

ps5__silent-hill-2.article:
**Silent Hill 2**, remade by Bloober Team, once again tells one of the most powerful stories in horror gaming history. James Sunderland receives a letter from his wife, who has been dead for years, and heads to the fog-shrouded town of Silent Hill to look for her. What he meets along the way — nurses, faceless creatures, and above all Pyramid Head — is no random bestiary but a mirror of his own guilt. The remake preserves the structure of the original game, expands it with new sections of locations and puzzles, and keeps the pacing deliberately slow.

The camera has moved over the shoulder, making combat and exploration feel more immediate. James moves heavily, both his pipe and firearms have noticeable weight, and enemies withstand an uncomfortable number of hits, which sustains a feeling of desperate improvisation rather than action-game confidence. Ammo and healing items are limited, puzzles have their own adjustable difficulty separate from combat, and exploring the apartment buildings, the hospital, and the prison rewards you for reading notes. On PlayStation 5 the game runs on Unreal Engine 5, and the fog that once masked technical limitations has become a full-fledged artistic tool here — it swallows the flashlight's light, changes silhouettes, and turns empty streets into an endless space.

The sound design is essential: the music was composed once again by Akira Yamaoka, and his combination of guitar melodies and industrial noise holds the whole mood together, while the radio crackles as an enemy approaches. Reception was significantly better than many expected after years of uncertainty, and the game became one of the best-reviewed horror titles of the year. The original's influence on psychological horror is beyond question, and this version makes it accessible to a generation that can barely reach the original anymore. Several endings additionally reward repeated playthroughs. Anyone looking for purely action-driven horror may be disappointed by the slow pace and the game's unwillingness to explain anything; but that is precisely where its strength lies. Silent Hill 2 remains a story about grief and guilt in which the monsters are a metaphor, and the modern version dilutes none of that.
ps5__silent-hill-2.teaser: A remake of one of the most powerful horror stories ever; Pyramid Head as a mirror of guilt.

ps5__deathloop.article:
**Deathloop** builds on a simple yet immensely clever premise: hitman Colt wakes up on the island of Blackreef trapped in a single day that repeats endlessly, and the only way out is to kill eight so-called Visionaries within a single run. The problem is they never stay in the same place at the same time, so the game isn't about shooting — it's about planning. The day is split into four phases and four areas, among which you choose where to go, and every choice irreversibly moves the clock forward.

The loop functions as a knowledge puzzle. On every run you gather clues, passwords, schedules, and ideas for how to get two targets in the same place, and you keep this knowledge even after death. Weapons and abilities only carry over between days if you charge them with a special resource, so even your gear is at risk. Meanwhile Arkane offers its typical immersive-sim freedom: teleportation, invisibility, linking enemies to a shared fate, silent approach, or a loud firefight. A special layer comes from Julianna, a rival defending the loop — she can be controlled by the computer, or another player can slip into your game instead, which disrupts even the most confident plan.

Visually it's a fresh mix of sixties spy aesthetics, brutalist architecture, and a jazz soundtrack that lends the island a cool elegance. The banter between Colt and Julianna ranks among the best writing Arkane has ever produced, and it keeps the mood alive even after several restarts. The game launched as a timed console exclusive for PlayStation 5 and received very good reviews for its idea and craftsmanship, with reservations about enemy AI. Today it's considered one of the most interesting experiments with the time-loop concept in the shooter genre. This is helped further by an excellent feel for the weapons, each with distinctly different weight and sound, and a clear interface that automatically keeps a record of discovered leads, so players don't have to rely on their own notes. Thanks to that, putting together the perfect plan lands as a genuine victory.
ps5__deathloop.teaser: A hitman stuck in one endless day; the game favors planning over shooting.

ps5__ghostwire-tokyo.article:
**Ghostwire: Tokyo** begins the moment nearly every person vanishes from the streets of Shibuya, leaving behind nothing but piles of clothing. The player takes control of a young man named Akito, whose body shares space with the spirit of an unyielding detective called KK, and together they venture into a fog-shrouded city full of visitors from another world — headless schoolgirls, men with umbrellas, or giant scissor-wielding women. Tango Gameworks left pure horror behind here and created a first-person action-adventure that leans more on occult atmosphere and Japanese folklore than on jump scares.

Instead of guns, you use Ethereal Weaving — hand gestures that unleash currents of wind, fire, and water. Combat looks like a wizard's shooter: you weaken an enemy, expose their core, and tear it out with a single motion. This is complemented by sacred bows, paper talismans for stunning or turning invisible, and the purification of torii gates, which uncovers more of the map. Shibuya is faithfully recreated and full of small tasks — collecting souls into paper katawaguruma, feeding dogs that lead you to treasure, and shopping at convenience stores run by cat-like nekomata. On PlayStation 5 the game shines with neon lighting, reflections on wet asphalt, and smooth transitions between display modes; spatial audio, meanwhile, masterfully handles whispering behind your back.

The music blends traditional Japanese instruments with electronica, creating together with the depopulated city a feeling of a solitary pilgrimage. Reception was cooler than the setting deserved — praise went to the atmosphere, the environment, and the imaginative bestiary, while criticism targeted repetitive side content. The free Spider's Thread update later added new enemies, areas, and a standalone roguelike mode. Today Ghostwire: Tokyo is recommended mainly for those who want to explore an empty Shibuya and let themselves be guided by folklore. It also helps that the game doesn't take itself entirely seriously — amid the tense scenes there's room for humor and for quiet moments on rooftops above the empty city.
ps5__ghostwire-tokyo.teaser: A Shibuya emptied of people, full of ghosts and yokai; an action adventure rather than pure horror.

ps5__doom-eternal.article:
**Doom Eternal** arrived on PlayStation 5 as a free upgrade for owners of the previous version and turned an already breakneck shooter into a technical delicacy. This time the Doom Slayer defends an Earth overrun by demons, and his campaign leads from demolished cities through hellish fortresses all the way to cosmic temples. The story is deliberately over-the-top, full of codex entries and mythology, but what matters is what happens between the shots — and that's one of the most elaborate combat systems any shooter has ever offered.

At its core lies a closed resource loop. The chainsaw restores ammo, brutal finishing moves drop health, and the flamethrower shakes armor loose from enemies. So you can't retreat into a corner and hide — instead you must constantly attack, clear arenas using the double jump and quick dash, and switch weapons on the fly to exploit each demon's weak points — shoot off the mancubus's cannon, the arachnotron's turret, lob a grenade straight into a cacodemon's maw. The result is something between a shooter and a rhythm game. On PlayStation 5 the game runs in high resolution with up to 120 frames per second, ray tracing has been added, and loading takes a fraction of the previous time, so you're back in the fight instantly after death.

Mick Gordon's soundtrack combines crushing guitars with electronics and is an integral part of the pacing, while the visual style leans on saturated colors far removed from grey shooters. The game received excellent reviews and sparked a healthy debate, since its emphasis on resource management and puzzle-like arenas was noticeably tougher than its predecessor's. Its influence on modern fast-paced shooters is clearly visible, and the two-part expansion The Ancient Gods adds an even harder challenge for those who've mastered the basics. There's also a competitive mode and an extensive collection of secret rooms, toys, and references to older entries in the series, rewarding exploration of the levels between battles. Anyone looking for a shooter that won't let you catch your breath for even a second won't find many better choices on PlayStation 5.
ps5__doom-eternal.teaser: An extremely fast-paced shooter full of demons; combat between shots is choreographed like a dance.

ps5__hitman-3.article:
**Hitman 3** concludes the World of Assassination trilogy and is also its most confident entry. This time Agent 47 settles accounts with the mysterious organization Providence, and his journey leads from a skyscraper in Dubai through an English manor, a Berlin club, rainy Chongqing, and an Argentine winery estate to a night train in the Carpathians. Each location is a clockwork mechanism full of characters on fixed schedules, and the player enters it as an uninvited guest who must find a crack in the machinery.

The principle remains untouched: disguises, patient observation, coincidences that look like accidents. New this time is a camera for scanning locks and terminals, and above all a complete mission conceived as a detective mystery, in which 47 investigates a murder and can expose the killer — or simply walk his own path. The game can import all the locations from the previous two entries, turning it into one enormous collection of sandboxes with challenges, contracts, and rotating targets whose exploration takes dozens of hours. On PlayStation 5 it impresses with fast loading, stable performance, and especially interior lighting; the Dubai heights and Berlin strobe lights rank among the best-looking scenes in the series.

The atmosphere thrives on the contrast between cold professionalism and the near-comedic absurdity that arises when the player decides to improvise. The music is understated, with tension built more by ambient noise and crowd voices. Critics received the game very well, and many called it the best entry in the entire trilogy, praised above all for its level design. A later PS VR2 version offered first-person stealth, and the whole trilogy has been merged into a single package, making entry into Agent 47's world easier than ever. Alongside the story missions, the game is kept alive by regularly returning targets available only for a limited time and player-made contracts, which keep familiar locations constantly changing. It's precisely this bottomless replayability that makes Hitman a series worth returning to for years.
ps5__hitman-3.teaser: Concludes the World of Assassination trilogy; every location is a clockwork mechanism full of characters.

ps5__metro-exodus-complete-edition.article:
**Metro Exodus Complete Edition** is a version of the post-apocalyptic shooter built directly for the new consoles, and in many ways it's a textbook modernization. Artyom ventures out of the Moscow metro for the first time, into the contaminated land, and together with the crew of the steam locomotive Aurora travels across Russia over the course of a year. The structure alternates tight corridor chapters with sprawling semi-open areas, where you choose the order of objectives yourself, search for supplies, and decide whether to shoot your way through an enemy camp or slip past it.

The gameplay is uncompromisingly survival-focused. Ammunition is crafted from scavenged parts right in your backpack, gas mask filters have a limited lifespan, the mask cracks and gets dirty, the flashlight recharges with a hand dynamo, and weapons foul up until you clean and reassemble them at a workbench. The pace is governed by the day cycle and weather — night favors stealth but wakes more dangerous creatures. The game also quietly remembers how you treat people and changes the ending accordingly, without ever offering an explicit choice. On PlayStation 5 it gained full ray-traced global illumination, a sharper image, and smooth performance, making the exits from the tunnels into daylight feel exceptionally powerful. The package includes both story expansions, The Two Colonels and Sam's Story.

The atmosphere draws on Dmitry Glukhovsky's original novel and combines hopelessness with a strange nostalgia; the music is restrained, and the space is filled with wind, the crackle of a Geiger counter, and the voices of fellow travelers on the train. Reception was very positive, and the enhanced version is often cited as one of the first titles to fully showcase the possibilities of ray tracing on consoles. Today it ranks among the most atmospheric shooters you can play on PlayStation 5. The campaign runs about fifteen hours, considerably more with the expansions, and rewards slow, careful play — anyone who rushes ahead misses most of what's best, since a substantial part of the story unfolds in conversations by the fire and in small details scattered throughout the train cars.
ps5__metro-exodus-complete-edition.teaser: Artyom heads out of the metro for the first time; corridors alternate with sprawling open areas.

ps5__dying-light-2-stay-human.article:
**Dying Light 2 Stay Human** moves zombie parkour to Villedor, the last great city to survive the pandemic, and puts the player in the shoes of Aiden, a wanderer searching for his sister. The city is built vertically: rooftops, walkways, wind turbines, and unfinished skyscrapers form one giant jungle gym you move through without interruption. By day the streets belong to people while the infected hide in dark buildings; by night the ratio reverses and a hunt begins outside, with packs of fast mutants chasing you down.

The gameplay rests on two separate skill trees — parkour and combat — which develop independently and turn movement from cautious climbing into fluid vaulting across entire blocks. Weapons are improvised, wear down, and can be upgraded with electric, fire, or freezing modifiers, making combat both brutal and tactical. Over all of this sits a decision system: assigning a water tower or power plant to one of the factions permanently changes the look of a district, adding either traps and combat aids or trampolines and ropes for parkour. The entire campaign can be played in co-op with up to four players. On PlayStation 5 the game offers both high-resolution and high-performance modes as well as, later, smoother variants; the lighting of nighttime streets and the dynamic transition from day to night rank among its greatest strengths.

The atmosphere swings between the tourist-view calm of a lookout tower and sheer panic while fleeing a horde. The music stays subdued until a chase begins, then turns into an adrenaline-fueled track. Reception was good, with reservations about the writing and the game's technical state at launch, which Techland has long since fixed and expanded with dozens of updates as well as the Bloody Ties add-on. Today the game is considerably more polished and remains the best parkour experience of its kind. It also offers several endings depending on key decisions, and a map whose complete conquest can easily take fifty hours, especially if you venture out at night in search of rare gear hidden in the most heavily guarded buildings.
ps5__dying-light-2-stay-human.teaser: Zombie parkour in a vertical city; humans rule by day, the infected by night.

ps5__sifu.article:
**Sifu** is a revenge story split across five long levels and a single life that shortens with every defeat. A young fighter loses his father in an attack by five assassins and sets out to find them one by one; he has, however, a magic talisman that puts him back on his feet after death — at the cost of years. Every revival adds age, and with it the strength of your blows grows while your health pool shrinks, and once you cross the age of seventy, everything ends. The game thus turns the death counter into both a narrative and a mechanical engine.

The combat system draws on the Pak Mei style of kung fu and is unusually deep. The key is the balance meter: an opponent's attacks can be blocked, but blocking fills up the structure meter, so it's necessary to deflect blows with precise parries, dodge with a crouch or sidestep, and interrupt strings with your own combos. The environment plays a role, since you can slam an enemy against a wall or railing, and objects like poles and bricks serve as temporary weapons. Unlocking abilities is permanent only if you buy the same skill several times, which pushes players to replay already-mastered levels aiming to clear them younger and with fewer mistakes. On PlayStation 5 the game runs very smoothly, which is essential for combat timed this precisely.

Visually it's a stylized tribute to Hong Kong action films — long takes, a passage through a neon-lit club, a painterly scene in a museum. The music mixes electronics with drums and underscores the rhythm of the fights. Reception was very positive, and the game earned a reputation as a demanding but fair title; later updates added optional difficulty settings, modifiers, and an arena mode, opening it up to less patient players as well. Today Sifu is one of the few games that genuinely teaches a martial art instead of just button-mashing. A skilled player can clear the five levels in a single afternoon, but this is a game where the first playthrough is only the beginning — the real goal is to go back and clear it clean, young, and without losses.
ps5__sifu.teaser: Revenge across five lives — each revival adds years, strength, and an approaching end at age 70.

ps5__warhammer-40-000-space-marine-2.article:
**Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine 2** brings Captain Titus back to the front line after many years and lets the player experience what it's like to be a Space Marine facing an endless tide of Tyranids. The campaign follows the fight for planets being swallowed by the swarm and alternates massive battle scenes with underground corridors; it can be played solo or with three, since Titus is joined by two other brothers of the Ultramarines chapter. The narrative doesn't try to be subtle — it's a loud, bombastic war opera, exactly as one would expect from this universe.

Combat combines shooting and melee into one fluid whole. Bolters and plasma weapons shred distant targets, swords and hammers clear the surroundings, and the key mechanic is parrying followed by a shot that replenishes your armor. Health regenerates only through executions, so defense means offense. The engine can throw enormous numbers of enemies onto the screen, pouring over rocks and climbing walls, and this sight of a living tide is the game's biggest draw. Outside the campaign the title offers co-op Operations for three players with their own classes and gear progression, plus the competitive Eternal War mode. On PlayStation 5 the game feels spectacular thanks to sprawling vistas, dense effects, and haptics tuned perfectly to every weapon.

The sound is appropriately over-the-top — booming choirs, wailing sirens, the swarm's screech — and together with the empire's architecture creates the intended crushing impression. Reception was very positive, and the game became one of the most commercially successful titles of its brand, praised especially for its weapon feel and scale of battles. Support continued with further Operations and enemies, and today it's the best way to experience Warhammer 40,000 as pure action. The campaign takes around ten hours, but co-op Operations and the gradual unlocking of each class's gear extend its lifespan many times over, especially with a steady squad. Higher difficulties then demand teamwork and reliable parrying, so the game gradually shifts from a loud spectacle into an honest cooperative challenge.
ps5__warhammer-40-000-space-marine-2.teaser: A Space Marine against an endless wave of Tyranids; playable solo or with two others.

ps5__devil-may-cry-5-special-edition.article:
**Devil May Cry 5 Special Edition** was among the games available right at the PlayStation 5 launch and served as an ideal showcase of what the new console could do. At its core is the return of the cult action series to Red Grave City, where a demonic tree has grown out of the ground and the demon Urizen threatens the entire world. The player alternately controls three characters: young hunter Nero with his interchangeable mechanical arms, the ever-sharp Dante with his four combat styles, and the mysterious V, who lets his summoned beasts fight while he himself only finishes off weakened enemies.

The heart of the game is the style rank. Varied, uninterrupted combos raise your grade from D all the way to the legendary SSS, along with the feeling that you've finally grasped the rhythm. Nero switches between Devil Breakers with different abilities, Dante changes both style and weapon within a single combo, and V keeps his distance while directing his panther and bird. The Special Edition additionally adds playable Vergil with his own set of attacks and the technique of splitting into two bodies, the Legendary Dark Knight difficulty with an enormous number of enemies on screen, and a Turbo mode that speeds up the entire game. On PlayStation 5 it gained ray tracing and a high-frame-rate mode, which matters most for action this fast.

The atmosphere is deliberately over the top — a rock soundtrack with vocals that intensify as your style rank rises, chatty characters, and scenes practically tailor-made for highlight reels. The original game was received brilliantly and is often described as the series' return to form, and the special edition added exactly what fans wanted most. Devil May Cry's influence on the entire stylish-action genre is well known, and the fifth entry still serves as its benchmark today: accessible on a first playthrough, practically bottomless for anyone who wants to play well. Alongside the campaign it offers the Bloody Palace, a hundred floors of timed combat, and an extensive skill tree for each character separately, so unlocking and mastering every move alone takes dozens of hours.
ps5__devil-may-cry-5-special-edition.teaser: A PS5 launch title; three playable characters, including Nero with his mechanical arms.

ps5__gran-turismo-7.article:
**Gran Turismo 7** brought the series back to where it was strongest: a patient, almost encyclopedic celebration of automobiles. The player starts with one ordinary car and, through a menu of nodes called the Café, completes collection tasks that gradually guide them through the history of individual brands and body-style classes. Around this stretches the familiar structure of license tests, championships, and endless tuning, as you adjust gear ratios, spring stiffness, and tire compound in the garage. The driving model sits somewhere between simulation and an accessible arcade approach: the car feels properly weighty, yet the game offers so many assists that even someone who otherwise doesn't play racing games can find their footing. The economy of collecting is just as important as the driving itself, since every new car unlocks another branch of competitions.

On PlayStation 5 the game shows for the first time what fast storage and controller haptics allow the new console to do. Track loading is a matter of an instant, the DualSense's adaptive triggers mimic brake lock-up and wheel slip, and the haptics convey surface texture and curb impacts. Visually the title combines a sharp, high-resolution image with ray tracing in replays and car showcases, while an alternative mode prioritizes smoothness. Especially notable is the modeling of weather and time of day, where during longer races the track temperature changes and with it the tires' behavior. The soundtrack ranges from calm jazz in the menus to electronic music during races, keeping the series' characteristically soothing tone.

Reception was mixed. Reviewers praised the content, presentation, and technical execution, while part of the player base loudly criticized the reward economy and the requirement for a constant server connection; the studio responded with repeated adjustments and long-term additions of cars and tracks. The game's influence is evident in how it raised the bar for racing-title presentation. Today Gran Turismo 7 feels like a living catalog of car culture you can return to in doses: it offers both the calm of focused tuning and the tension of sharp online championships, and it's one of the strongest arguments for hooking a wheel up to a PlayStation 5.
ps5__gran-turismo-7.teaser: A patient, encyclopedic celebration of cars — from a single vehicle through brand history to tuning.

ps5__f1-23.article:
**F1 23** is the year the Codemasters-developed series returned to storytelling while also polishing the issues that plagued its predecessors. Alongside the classic career mode, where the player signs with a real team, and the My Team mode dealing with budget, part development and driver recruitment, the story campaign following fictional racers behind the scenes of the queen of motorsport made its return. It is precisely this campaign that gives the otherwise cold simulator a human dimension: dialogues, team intrigue and decisions affecting the mood in the garage play out between races. Anyone who just wants to drive has quick weekends, time trials and extensive race length settings at their disposal.

The handling model received adjustments to car behavior under braking and at low speeds, so the car feels more predictable at the edge of grip and forgives small mistakes more readily. A wide range of assists and a helper layer for gamepad players allow the difficulty to be set anywhere from casual Sunday arcade driving to a hardcore simulation without support systems. On PlayStation 5 the game runs smoothly with short loading times, the adaptive triggers make locking brakes noticeably felt, and the haptics distinguish smooth asphalt from vibrations over kerbs. Sound is one of the game's strongest aspects: hybrid power units, the engineer's radio calls and pit lane noise create a convincing broadcast-like atmosphere.

Reception was noticeably warmer than for the previous entry, mainly thanks to the return of the story campaign and more sensitive handling. Criticism traditionally targeted the fact that it is a yearly iteration building on a proven foundation rather than a bigger revolution, along with microtransactions in add-ons. For the genre the series matters because it keeps licensed motorsport in a shape that holds up both for fans of TV broadcasts and for players with a wheel and three monitors. Today F1 23 works as a solid entry ticket into the world of Formula 1 for anyone who wants to race fast, and as a decent foundation for league racing with friends.
ps5__f1-23.teaser: The return of a story campaign to the F1 series; a human dimension for an otherwise cold simulator.

ps5__need-for-speed-unbound.article:
**Need for Speed Unbound** is the boldest visual experiment this series has allowed itself in recent years. Realistically scanned cars are accompanied by hand-drawn effects in a graffiti and comic-book style: a marker-drawn cloud of smoke trails from the wheels, illustrated wings flutter behind the car while drifting, and nitro is accompanied by a popping illustration. The player starts as a young man from the street whose car has been stolen, and over the course of an in-game week works their way up to a big city race. Each day is split into a day and night shift, between which earned money is wagered, bodywork is repaired, and above all the level of police attention is watched, because getting arrested costs the player everything they've earned.

The driving model stands firmly in arcade territory: drifting is the basis of every corner, boost fills up through risky driving, and car building allows tuning everything from dampers to how the car responds to the throttle. A strong point is the customization, where you can change not only colors and add-ons but also animated effects and marks that remain on the road while driving. On PlayStation 5 the game runs at a high frame rate, which matters greatly during fast night chases on wet asphalt, and the controller's haptics dose out the feeling of grip as well as impacts with police cars. The soundtrack is built on contemporary hip hop and electronic music, and together with the visual style it sets the game's overall tone.

Reception was mixed. The visual style found both enthusiasts and detractors; critics praised the boldness and the night chases but pointed to uneven police difficulty and overly talkative characters. For the genre the title matters because it showed a way out of photorealistic monotony and proved that stylization can be a racing game's main draw. Today Unbound feels like a fast, loud and distinctly urban affair best played in shorter sessions: the moment the player, car loaded up, cuts through the night city with three police cars on their tail ranks among the most tense chases on console.
ps5__need-for-speed-unbound.teaser: Realistic cars with hand-drawn graffiti effects — smoke, wings, comic-book nitro.

ps5__hot-wheels-unleashed.article:
**Hot Wheels Unleashed** turned a familiar toy into a surprisingly seriously made racing title that still keeps the childlike joy of the orange plastic track. Races take place in environments blown up to giant scale, so tracks run across shelves in a garage, around a desk in an office, or across a skatepark, and they include loops, magnetic sections and hazards such as a giant spider or fire traps. Every car has its own weight, grip and boost supply, which is replenished by drifting, so there is a noticeable difference between models. The collecting side is just as important as the racing itself: new cars are obtained from blind boxes, upgraded and displayed in your own virtual collection.

The strongest part of the game is the track editor. The player gets the same pieces the official circuits are built from, can arrange them in space, anchor them to furniture, and share the result with others. This is exactly what has given the game its long lifespan. On PlayStation 5 the title runs smoothly with a crisp image that shows off well on the glossy plastic bodywork and floor reflections, and loading between races is short. The controller's haptics signal driving over a piece joint as well as loss of grip, and the adaptive triggers highlight the moment the car leaves a magnetic section. The audio side relies on upbeat electronic tunes and the characteristic whir of plastic wheels.

Reception was surprisingly warm: reviewers praised the precise controls, the idea of an enlarged environment, and above all the editor, though they criticized the repetitive career structure and the way new cars are obtained. For the genre the game matters because it brought arcade racing with small vehicles, long absent from the mainstream, back into the spotlight. Today Hot Wheels Unleashed feels like an ideal title for split-screen play or short evening sessions, where a few minutes are enough to once again want to build your own loop across the whole room.
ps5__hot-wheels-unleashed.teaser: Tracks from the famous toy scaled up to giant proportions — across shelves, desks, and a skatepark.

ps5__crew-motorfest.article:
**The Crew Motorfest** moved the open-world racing series from an entire continent to a single Hawaiian island and, in doing so, gained exactly what previous entries lacked: focus. Oahu offers volcanic slopes, rainforest, beaches and the city streets of Honolulu, all connected into a single map you can drive across without loading. The content is organized into themed playlists, short series of races each devoted to a single subject: the Japanese tuning scene, American muscle cars, endurance racing, electric vehicles or off-road machines. Each playlist has its own presentation, its own music and its own narrator, so it feels like a self-contained smaller festival within the larger event.

Besides cars, the game offers motorcycles, boats and planes, and switching between them is part of some competitions, where a car turns into a boat while driving along a beach and then into a plane. The driving model is arcade-style but distinguishes between surface types and vehicle categories enough that tuning gears and suspension actually matters. On PlayStation 5 the game runs smoothly, with short loading and pleasantly detailed vegetation and water surfaces; adaptive triggers distinguish off-road driving from asphalt, and haptics convey the spray of waves during a race at sea. Engine sound blends with a varied musical lineup that changes according to the playlist currently being played.

Reviews received the game as a significant improvement over its predecessor, praising the clear structure, the island atmosphere and the variety of the vehicle roster, while criticizing the weaker story framing and the at times overly forgiving difficulty. For the genre the title matters in how elegantly it solves the problem of open-world racing games: instead of an endless list of icons on the map, it offers curated blocks that have a beginning and an end. Today Motorfest feels like a relaxed, sunny and surprisingly substantial affair, suited both to short evening drives and to long evenings spent collecting cars.
ps5__crew-motorfest.teaser: An open world narrowed down to a single Hawaiian island; content divided into themed playlists.

ps5__tony-hawk-s-pro-skater-1-2.article:
**Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 1 + 2** is a remake of two pivotal skateboarding games from the turn of the millennium that preserves their exact gameplay while dressing it in modern graphics. All the original skateparks, from the warehouse through the school to the mall, have been rebuilt from the ground up, but the layout of obstacles and the placement of the collectible S-K-A-T-E letters match the originals. The goal of each run is to complete a list of tasks within a two-minute time limit: reach a score threshold, find a hidden object, break certain objects. Controls are built around chaining tricks, grinds and manuals into a single long combo, broken by a single badly landed jump.

The remake added mechanics from later entries in the series, so both revert and rail-riding in either direction are available, and it expanded custom skater creation as well as the skatepark editor, in which you can build your own parks and share them with others. The PlayStation 5 version benefits from a high frame rate, essential for a game built on precise timing, and from near-instant restarting of a run, so repeated attempts at the perfect combo aren't slowed down. The soundtrack combines the original punk and hip hop tracks that made the series famous with new additions, and is a key part of the atmosphere: the music sets the pace just as much as the two-minute countdown.

Reception was very warm. Reviewers praised the fact that the remake understood why the original games worked and didn't try to rewrite them, only polish them; criticism targeted later changes to online services and the absence of a sequel. The original games' influence on the genre was enormous, as they defined an entire wave of combo-based sports arcade titles, and this remake showed that their system is still very much alive. Today Pro Skater 1 + 2 stands as one of the best-executed revivals ever: instantly understandable, hard to fully master, and one keeps coming back to the perfect two-minute run long after finishing the game.
ps5__tony-hawk-s-pro-skater-1-2.teaser: A remake of two classics from the turn of the millennium; the same gameplay, modern graphics.

ps5__riders-republic.article:
**Riders Republic** is an open playground for extreme sports that combines mountain biking, downhill skiing and snowboarding, wingsuit flying and rocket-powered jetpacks into one giant map made up of environments inspired by American national parks. The player moves freely across it and can switch from a bike to skis at any moment, or dive off a cliff in a winged suit. The content is split into career branches by discipline, each with its own races, trick contests and star challenges, and progress unlocks better gear. Alongside regular racing, the game offers mass starts with dozens of players at once, in which the field squeezes through a narrow forest and every fall costs several places.

Controls are arcade-like and forgiving: the player focuses on line choice, leaning before a jump, and chaining tricks in the air, with two trick schemes available depending on whether one wants precision or simplicity. On PlayStation 5 the game runs at a high frame rate and with long draw distance, essential when flying a wingsuit just above the slope, and loading times for transfers between distant points on the map are short. The controller's haptics distinguish powder from ice and gravel, and the adaptive triggers give tangible feedback when braking on a bike. Wind sound and a soundtrack built on energetic electronic music and rock reinforce the sense of speed.

Reviews praised the variety of disciplines, the generous map and the mass races, but criticized the chatty presentation, the aggressive offer of paid add-ons, and an at times chaotic interface. For the genre the game matters because it took the open-world model and applied it to sports that were previously tied to individual tracks. Today Riders Republic feels like a fast-paced, sociable pastime that works best in a crowd with other players: the moment fifty people set off from a mountaintop at once, and some of them turn into flyers halfway down the run, the game delivers a scene you won't find anywhere else.
ps5__riders-republic.teaser: A giant playground for extreme sports — bike, skis, and wingsuit all on one open map.

ps5__mlb-show-21.article:
**MLB The Show 21** is the year in which the long-running baseball series first made it beyond PlayStation consoles while also taking advantage of new-generation hardware. The foundation remained proven: a single-player career mode starting in the lower leagues and working its way up to the majors, full club management including budget and player trades, and a collecting mode where cards are combined into your own lineups to play against others. This year's novelty was the option to run a career player as two-way, meaning both pitcher and hitter at once, reflecting changes in real baseball.

Gameplay offers several levels of depth. Batting and pitching can be controlled with a simple button press, by aiming into a zone, or with full analog stick movement, so the player chooses between quick fun and practiced precise timing. On PlayStation 5 the game benefits from short loading times, higher resolution and more detailed stadium models, complemented by a custom ballpark editor that lets you build an arena your own way. Adaptive triggers and haptics convey the difference between a clean bat contact and a hit near the edge of the wood. The presentation imitates a TV broadcast, including commentary, statistics and shots of the stands, and the between-inning music draws on a wide mix of rock and hip hop.

Reception was good; reviewers praised above all the accessibility for new players and the scope of content, but criticized the heavy emphasis on the collecting mode and its economy. The title holds a special place for the genre: for a long time it was the only seriously made baseball simulation on the market, and its move to multiple platforms opened the sport to a wider audience. Today MLB The Show 21 feels like a calm, almost meditative sports game that rewards patience and careful reading of the situation; anyone who works through the rules will find one of the best-crafted sports simulations of its time.
ps5__mlb-show-21.teaser: The baseball series steps outside PlayStation for the first time; career, franchise, and a card-collecting mode.

ps5__ea-sports-fc-24.article:
**EA Sports FC 24** is the first entry in the long-running football series to be released without the FIFA name, and it therefore draws extra attention to whether anything has actually changed under the new title. The foundation consists of the familiar range of modes: manager and player career, quick matches, online competitions and, above all, the collecting mode built around assembling a team from cards, which remains by far the most-played part of the game. This year's novelty was the introduction of player styles, traits derived from real-world data that give individual footballers concrete abilities, such as a long-range shot, a precise long pass, or tireless off-the-ball runs.

On the pitch, the changes show up mainly in player movement and in the battle for the ball. An animation system built on real-match motion capture makes transitions between running, turning and shooting smoother, and defending feels somewhat more disciplined than in previous years. The PlayStation 5 version offers higher resolution, smooth visuals and more detailed player and stadium models, along with short loading and haptic feedback that distinguishes a clean volley from a rash tackle. The presentation imitates a TV broadcast, including cameras, graphics and stadium atmosphere, and the soundtrack traditionally serves as a showcase of the current global music scene.

Reception was mildly positive: reviewers praised the player styles and the greater differences between individual footballers, but repeatedly criticized the collecting mode's dependence on purchases and the slower development of career modes. The series' influence on the genre is undeniable, given that for decades it has defined what football looks like on consoles, and its yearly cycle shapes the entire sports game market. Today FC 24 feels like a reliable, content-packed football game that shines brightest in matches against a friend on the same couch, where its greater emphasis on player individuality is genuinely noticeable.
ps5__ea-sports-fc-24.teaser: The first entry in the football series without the FIFA name; the question is what actually changed under the new title.

ps5__stray.article:
**Stray** tells the story of a stray cat that falls into an underground city inhabited by robots and must find a way back to the surface. The player controls the cat directly, with everything that entails: leaping across ledges and air-conditioning units, squeezing through narrow crawlspaces, sleeping on warm pipes, knocking over cans, and scratching carpets. Along the way it's joined by a small flying droid named B-12, who translates the local inhabitants' language, carries objects, and handles the things a cat's paws simply can't. Progression alternates between calm exploration of the streets, simple puzzles built around vertical movement, and a few tense chases where you must flee from parasitic creatures.

The game's greatest strength is its setting. The neon city, hemmed in between walls, is packed with detail — makeshift shelters, flickering signs, and robotic inhabitants who have built their own imitation of human life. On PlayStation 5 the game runs smoothly, with a crisp image and convincing lighting that turns the narrow alleys into the title's strongest visual moments, and loading is nearly instant. The controller's haptics convey both purring and impacts on metal, and the button dedicated to meowing has become a small legend. The soundtrack blends electronica with meditative pads, making the city feel both cozy and melancholy at once.

The game was received exceptionally warmly, praised for its atmosphere, its original perspective, and for not overstaying its welcome — a full playthrough takes one long evening session. Criticism focused on the simplicity of the puzzles and the fact that the second half is more linear than the opening. The title's influence can be seen in the renewed interest it sparked in smaller, atmospheric games built around an unusual protagonist. Today Stray feels like a precisely measured experience that can be recommended even to people who don't normally play games, one that got far more out of a cat's-eye view than mere cuteness.
ps5__stray.teaser: A stray cat in an underground robot city; control includes everything a cat would do.

ps5__hades.article:
**Hades** is an action roguelike about Zagreus, son of the god of the underworld, who is trying to escape his father's realm and reach the surface. Every attempt follows the same room structure, but the contents and layout change each time, and after each death the hero returns home to try again. These returns are the heart of the game: between runs, relationships with the underworld's inhabitants deepen, gathered resources are spent on permanent upgrades, and new weapons are unlocked, from a sword to a bow to a thrown shield. During each escape attempt the player collects boons from the Olympian gods that alter how attacks behave, and their combinations produce a different-feeling build every time.

Combat is fast, readable, and built around dodging at the right moment; the difficulty is high, but every death pushes the story forward, so failure never feels like wasted time. The narrative is assembled from thousands of short dialogue lines that react to whatever just happened, gradually revealing a family drama rather than a single ending. Visually the game rests on hand-drawn portraits and a rich color palette for each region of the underworld, while the music combines rock guitars with Greek stringed instruments and ranks among the most praised game soundtracks of recent years. The PlayStation 5 version offers a high frame rate, near-zero loading between rooms, and haptic feedback that distinguishes each weapon.

Reception was extraordinary; the game collected numerous awards and became a textbook example of how to combine randomly generated progression with a tightly written story. Its influence on the genre is clear — many later roguelikes adopted the idea that death should advance both the narrative and permanent progression. Today Hades feels like an almost flawlessly balanced title that's hard to put down after just one run, and the best entry point into a genre that can otherwise be unforgiving.
ps5__hades.teaser: An action roguelike about escaping the underworld; death isn't the end, just a trip home for another attempt.

ps5__kena-bridge-of-spirits.article:
**Kena: Bridge of Spirits** is the adventure of a young spirit guide who arrives in an overgrown mountain village to help trapped spirits find peace while cleansing the land of corruption. The structure combines a semi-open world with linear stretches: the player moves through forests, shrines, and flooded ravines, solves puzzles built around manipulating the environment, and fights the guardians of corrupted sites in arena encounters. A key part of the game are the Rot, small black creatures the heroine collects, which in return clear obstacles, carry objects, distract enemies, or boost her attacks. The more you find, the more capable your little band becomes.

Combat is surprisingly tough. Kena wields a staff usable for melee attacks and as a bow, along with a shield that consumes energy and several abilities tied to the Rot; enemies must be read, dodged at the right moment, and engaged at varying distances, so boss fights in particular can take several attempts. Visually the game benefits from the studio's animation background and looks like a feature animated film: soft lighting, expressive character faces, and lush vegetation rank among the best-looking things seen in the early years of PlayStation 5. The console version offers both a higher-resolution mode and a smoother-performance mode along with short loading times. Music built on orchestra and Balinese percussion gives the whole thing a ceremonial, at times wistful tone.

Reviews praised the art direction, the atmosphere, and the surprising difficulty of the combat, but criticized a somewhat conventional story and a repetitive quest structure in the second half. For the independent scene, the title matters because it showed a small studio could deliver a game with production values on par with major publishers. Today Kena feels like a kind, visually exceptional adventure suited to players looking for something between a fairy tale and a real challenge, and one that still ranks among the best-looking things on this console even years later.
ps5__kena-bridge-of-spirits.teaser: A spirit guide moving between a semi-open world and temples; puzzles and combat with the Rot at her side.

ps5__sea-of-stars.article:
**Sea of Stars** is a turn-based RPG that deliberately follows in the footsteps of classic Japanese games from the nineties while stripping away their most annoying habits. Two young heroes wielding the power of the sun and the moon set out to stop a threat spreading across the world, gathering more companions with their own abilities and histories along the way.
