Combat is turn-based but demands attention: every attack and block has a timing window for a precise button press that boosts its effect or reduces damage taken, and enemies telegraph a sequence of damage types before a powerful spell that must be broken before the attack lands.

The game takes place in a world you move through with surprising freedom: the heroes climb ledges, leap chasms, and swim across rivers on their own, so exploration is never held back by invisible walls. There are no random battles, no endlessly repeated grinding for experience, no shopping for potions in endless rounds — instead there's a campsite where you cook food and smoothly replenish your resources. Visually it's pixel art with dynamic lighting and shading that pushes the classic aesthetic somewhere the original games never reached. On PlayStation 5 the game runs without a hitch, with instant loading and very fast switching between the map and combat. The music leans on melodic themes in the spirit of old JRPGs and ranks among the strongest parts of the whole package.

Reception was very positive: reviewers praised the art direction, the combat system, and its consideration for the player's time, though some found the story too straightforward and the difficulty too low. For the genre, the title matters because it showed how to modernize the classic JRPG without losing what made people love it in the first place. Today Sea of Stars feels like a pleasantly long, gentle, and visually enchanting journey that works just as well for old-timers as for new players.
ps5__sea-of-stars.teaser: A turn-based RPG that follows in the footsteps of 90s classics without their most annoying habits.

ps5__dave-diver.article:
**Dave the Diver** is an unusual blend of two completely different games. By day, the player dives the good-natured Dave into a mysterious blue hole, harpooning and netting fish, gathering resources, and dodging sharks, with each descent a single run limited by oxygen and backpack space. By night, the catch becomes the menu of a small sushi restaurant that must be run: the player sets prices, hires staff, upgrades kitchen equipment, and personally serves tea and delivers plates to guests during the rush hour. The two halves are interlinked, since the restaurant's success funds better diving gear, which in turn opens up deeper and more dangerous parts of the ocean.

Around this core the game keeps piling on more ideas: growing rice, farming fish, photographing marine species, cooperating with an undersea tribe, minigames parodying other genres, and story twists with an adventurous flavor. This constant switching between activities is exactly why the title holds your attention for dozens of hours without ever feeling repetitive. Visually it rests on detailed pixel art with an enormous number of animations and broadly comic-book humor that never takes itself seriously. On PlayStation 5 the game runs completely smoothly, with short loading between day and night, and the controller's haptics dole out resistance when reeling in a bigger fish. The music shifts with the time of day, from calm underwater pads to upbeat restaurant themes.

The game was received very well and became one of the most talked-about surprises of its time, praised for its sheer amount of content, its pacing, and its sense of humor; criticism pointed to the later stages leaning more heavily into restaurant management than some players would like. The title's influence can be seen in renewed interest in games that combine two unrelated systems. Today Dave the Diver feels like an unusually generous and relaxing experience where you often find that the promised single dive stretched into an entire evening.
ps5__dave-diver.teaser: An unusual mix: diving into a blue hole by day, running a sushi restaurant by night.

xbox-series__halo-infinite.article:
**Halo Infinite** brought Master Chief back as the flagship title of the Xbox Series X|S generation, and also became the first entry in the series to abandon the tight corridor structure in favor of an open world. Zeta Halo is shattered into pieces, and the player moves freely across its surface: capturing Banished bases, freeing captured marines, taking out named commanders, and along the way passing through classic closed-off missions that harken back to earlier entries. The key new addition is the Grappleshot, a hook that changes the pace of firefights — letting you pull yourself onto a rocky ledge, rip a weapon from an enemy's hands, or literally latch onto a passing vehicle. The gunplay retained the series' trademark weight, where every shield hit has an audible and tactile response, and fights unfold in long improvised loops rather than quick exchanges.

Technically it was a showcase for the new hardware. The campaign runs at a high resolution with the option of a smoother mode, and multiplayer on Series X targets a very high frame rate, which is essential for a competitive arena shooter. The multiplayer component was also released for free as a standalone free-to-play title, making it accessible even to owners of the cheaper Series S. Visually the game bet on a clean, colorful, and slightly retro design close to the original trilogy, where the ring's lush greens meet the metallic structures of the Forerunners. The music returns to iconic choral themes, supplemented with more understated, atmospheric passages that play while traveling through the landscape.

Reception was mixed in both good and bad ways. The campaign and the multiplayer's core shooting mechanics earned praise as a return to form for the franchise, while the surrounding live-service model, the pace of content additions, and missing features drew criticism the developers kept responding to for many months after launch. Today Halo Infinite feels like a game that only gradually realized its potential: the moment-to-moment gameplay ranks among the best the franchise has offered, and the open ring gives Halo's old rituals a pleasantly loose breathing room.
xbox-series__halo-infinite.teaser: Master Chief returns and, for the first time, leaves the corridors for the open world of the Zeta Halo ring.

xbox-series__forza-horizon-5.article:
**Forza Horizon 5** moved the traveling car festival to Mexico and, right from launch, became the most striking showcase for the Xbox Series X|S consoles. The map is built on contrasts: a single drive can take you through a tropical jungle with temple ruins, up a snow-capped volcano slope, across a dusty desert, and finish in the narrow streets of a colonial town. The structure stayed true to the series — the player earns points across different branches of activity, unlocks new festival hubs, races on circuits and off-road, completes speed zones and stunt jumps, and along the way tackles Horizon Stories, short themed episodes. A major addition is the EventLab editor, which lets you build custom tracks and game modes and share them with others, so the game's content grew far beyond what the developers themselves put into it.

Technically it's a showpiece title for the new generation. On Series X you can choose between a higher-resolution mode and a smoother-performance mode, SSD loading cut waiting times to a minimum, and fast travel is practically instant. Seasons change on a weekly cycle for all players at once, so the world regularly transforms — rain floods riverbeds, the desert scorches in summer, and stormy skies over the coast look straight out of a documentary. Engine sound is recorded with obsessive care, and the radio stations cover everything from electronica to classical music, a traditional hallmark of the series.

Critics received the game exceptionally warmly, praising both the depiction of the Mexican landscape and the unprecedented attention to accessibility, including sign-language interpretation in story sequences. Forza Horizon 5 also became a symbol of the Game Pass strategy: a huge, technically polished blockbuster available on subscription from day one. Even years later it feels like the most comfortable arcade ride on the market — it doesn't matter whether you spend ten minutes with it or ten hours.
xbox-series__forza-horizon-5.teaser: A car festival in Mexico; a single drive links jungle, volcano, desert, and an old city.

xbox-series__starfield.article:
**Starfield** is Bethesda Game Studios' first entirely new franchise in a full twenty-five years, and also the biggest exclusive the Xbox Series X|S consoles have received. The player starts as a nameless miner who touches a mysterious artifact and soon joins Constellation, the last group of explorers seeking answers to what these artifacts actually are. From there unfolds a structure the studio has honed since the days of Morrowind: a main storyline, sprawling faction narratives — space marines, pirates, corporate intrigue — and hundreds of small tasks you can lose yourself in for dozens of hours. The novelty here is the universe itself: over a thousand landable planets, resource mining, building your own outposts, and above all a ship editor where hulls, engines, and weapon systems can be assembled module by module.

On Series X the game bet primarily on stability; at launch it ran at a locked lower frame rate, and only later updates added an optional smoother-performance mode. Visually the most striking elements are ship and station interiors, the handling of light and materials, while the procedurally generated planet surfaces serve more as a backdrop for exploration than a hand-crafted experience. The music works with silence and broad orchestral passages closer to serious 1970s sci-fi than to action-packed space adventure, and together with the utilitarian design of the technology creates a restrained, believable atmosphere.

Reception was divided. Reviewers praised the sheer volume of content, the writing of the faction storylines, and the idea of New Game Plus becoming a direct part of the story, but criticized the fragmented travel between loading screens and the emptiness of the randomly generated moons. Today, after a series of major updates and expansions, Starfield feels like a classic Bethesda RPG transplanted into space — slower and colder than Skyrim, but with enormous room for players who enjoy building their own story.
xbox-series__starfield.teaser: Bethesda's first new franchise in twenty-five years; a miner with an artifact searches for answers.

xbox-series__senua-s-saga-hellblade-ii.article:
**Senua's Saga: Hellblade II** takes to the extreme the idea that a game can be short, tightly focused, and still unforgettable. Senua travels to tenth-century Iceland to stop the slavers who ravaged her home, and along the way she encounters giants, superstition, and her own psychosis, which never stops whispering in her ear. The gameplay is deliberately minimalist: trekking through raw landscapes, solving perspective puzzles where you must turn your view so that broken shapes align into a symbol, and one-on-one duels. These play out in tight over-the-shoulder framing, with a clear rhythm of strike, block, and dodge, feeling more like choreography than a combo-driven system — which makes every exchange feel brutal and personal.

Technically, it's one of the most impressive games of the entire generation. Both characters and locations were created through photogrammetry of real actors and places, the image is cinematically framed in a wide aspect ratio, and it runs at a locked thirty frames per second, which the studio explained as an effort to preserve the filmic quality of every shot. Sound is absolutely essential: the binaurally recorded voices Senua hears circle around the player's head, creating an unsettlingly intimate experience for which headphones are practically mandatory. The music blends Nordic vocals, percussion, and industrial noise, receding in quiet passages to nothing but breath and wind.

Reviews praised the audiovisual craft, the acting, and the sensitive handling of mental illness; criticism targeted the simplicity of the gameplay and the linearity that leaves players little room for their own decisions. Hellblade II thus sits on the border between a game and an interactive film, and it's best approached that way. Those who tune into it get five to seven hours of extraordinarily intense spectacle; those looking for rich action mechanics will leave disappointed. The title's influence is mainly technical — it showed just how far you can push the believability of the human face and real-time lighting on a mainstream console.
xbox-series__senua-s-saga-hellblade-ii.teaser: Short, tight, and unforgettable; Senua crosses 10th-century Iceland against slavers.

xbox-series__microsoft-flight-simulator.article:
**Microsoft Flight Simulator** arrived on Xbox Series X|S in the summer of 2021 and became the first truly full-fledged civilian flight simulator that made sense on a console. Its main appeal lies in its scale: the game reconstructs the entire planet from satellite and aerial imagery, uses machine learning to compute the shapes of buildings and trees from it, and streams detailed data from the cloud based on wherever you happen to be flying. You can therefore take off from an airfield in your own region, fly over your own house, and head toward the Alps or Manhattan. Everything is available, from a small Cessna through turboprop aircraft to airliners, along with training lessons for complete beginners, a system of challenges, and free flight without any rules at all.

Bringing it to console was the technically most demanding part of the project. Gamepad controls received a thoughtfully designed layout and assistance features that can gradually be turned off as the player gains confidence, while support for real yokes and pedals was retained. Series X handles high resolution and a rich level of detail, Series S works with reduced parameters, but the flying experience itself remains the same. Weather and air traffic can be switched to real-time data, so a cloud over Prague in the simulator matches the cloud over Prague outside your window, and night flights over lit-up cities rank among the most beautiful images of the generation.

Reviewers welcomed the game with enthusiasm, praising above all how it turned into more of a calm form of tourism than a dry technical discipline. A huge community of aircraft and airport creators has also grown up around the simulator, and their creations have reached console players too, through the store. Today Flight Simulator remains a one-of-a-kind title: it has no rival, offers practically endless content, and works equally well as a demanding hobby and as a meditative spectacle of the world from above. The steady addition of new regions and aircraft through updates also means you can return to the game months later and each time discover something new in it.
xbox-series__microsoft-flight-simulator.teaser: The first full-fledged flight simulator on a console; it reconstructs the entire planet from imagery.

xbox-series__forza-motorsport.article:
**Forza Motorsport** from 2023 is not another numbered installment but a reboot of the brand, meant to place Forza's circuit-racing branch on the foundations of a new generation. The career mode is arranged into series called the Builders Cup, in which the player isn't racing just for position but mainly developing a specific car: driven kilometers, clean corners, and overtakes earn points that can be spent on individual parts. The car thus improves alongside the driver, and upgrades are a matter of work put in rather than wallet size. A key new feature is also more detailed tire physics and changing conditions, where track temperature and grip shift during a race, so the ideal line in the final third looks different than in the first.

Technically, the game bet on a combination of high frame rate and ray tracing, which works on Series X even during actual driving, not just in garage inspections. A dynamic day cycle changes how tracks are lit, wet asphalt reflects the lights of the pit lane, and the car models rank among the most detailed in the genre. Sound remains a strong point: engines are recorded from real machines, and the difference between a naturally aspirated six-cylinder and a turbocharged four-cylinder is audible immediately. Assist features range from a fully assisted mode for newcomers to bare-bones driving without any support at all.

Reception was cooler than Microsoft had hoped. Reviewers praised the handling model, the tire work, and the visuals, but criticized long holdups in the progression system, technical issues at launch, and a rather sparse track selection compared to earlier entries. Many of these complaints eased over subsequent updates. Today Forza Motorsport is a solid choice for players who want to find an honest simulator beneath an arcade-like surface, and together with Forza Horizon it shows well just how differently the racing genre can be approached. The online portion, moreover, keeps order thanks to a safe-driving rating, so races don't end in a pile-up in the very first corner, and players get matched with similarly minded opponents.
xbox-series__forza-motorsport.teaser: A relaunch of the brand with the Builders Cup career, focused mainly on developing a specific car.

xbox-series__psychonauts-2.article:
**Psychonauts 2** is a sequel that was sixteen years in the making, yet feels as if only a single year had passed between the two entries. Raz has just been accepted among the Psychonauts and, instead of heroic missions, faces an internship, paperwork, and his colleagues' distrust — and above all, a series of expeditions into other people's minds. That's the heart of the game: each mind is a self-contained world with its own visual concept, from a hospital scene turned into a concert stage to a cooking competition where the ingredients are thoughts. In between, Raz uses telekinesis, pyrokinesis, levitation on a ball, or mental links, combining individual abilities both in combat and while jumping and solving small puzzles.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly at high resolution, and fast loading helps the pacing, since transitions between minds happen often. The visuals rely on a bold cartoonish style that changes with each level depending on what the given character is suffering from, so the game never visually repeats itself. The music draws on jazz, orchestral scoring, and psychedelia, precisely mirroring the madness of each mind. Character animation and facial expressions rank among the best the genre has to offer, and together with witty dialogue they form the main draw.

Reviews were unequivocally enthusiastic, praising not just the humor and inventiveness but especially the way the game talks about anxiety, trauma, and addiction — with empathy, without oversimplification, and without turning mental struggles into entertainment at someone else's expense. That's exactly where Psychonauts 2 remains influential: it showed that a colorful platformer can carry a serious subject without losing its lightness. Today it's one of the most welcoming games in Xbox's library and a great entry point for anyone who thinks platformers no longer have anything to say. Its accessibility helps too: combat difficulty can be lowered at any time, so anyone mainly interested in the story doesn't need to fear being stopped by a single tough spot. Those who like collecting, on the other hand, will find plenty of hidden details in every mind.
xbox-series__psychonauts-2.teaser: A sequel after sixteen years of waiting that feels like it arrived after just one.

xbox-series__pentiment.article:
**Pentiment** is the most unusual game Obsidian Entertainment has ever released, and at the same time one of the strongest proofs that Xbox exclusives don't have to be grand blockbusters. It takes place in the Bavarian foothills at the start of the sixteenth century, at a time when the old nobility, monastic learning, and peasant everyday life are beginning to rub dangerously against each other. The player leads the illuminator Andreas Maler, whose stay at the abbey scriptorium lands him in the middle of a murder — and over the course of a few tense days he must question people, observe, compare testimonies, and finally point to the culprit, even though he can never be entirely certain. The game deliberately doesn't allow you to check every lead: time passes, and whatever you didn't get to, you'll never find out.

The visuals are the main star. Everything looks like a page from a medieval manuscript and an early-modern printed book — characters have outlined contours, the backgrounds are decorated with ornaments, and the lettering in the dialogue changes depending on who is speaking, so an educated monk speaks in a different script than an illiterate peasant. The sound works with the scratching of a quill, period instruments, and the silence of the countryside. There is no combat in the game whatsoever; all the tension is carried by conversation and the decision of whom to believe.

The story spans decades and, across three acts, shows how a single hasty accusation can mark an entire village for generations to come. Critics received the game excellently, praising above all its historical honesty, its writing, and its courage to turn a detective story into a study of community and memory. On Xbox Series X|S it runs without any demands and is also well suited to play in short sessions. Today Pentiment is among the titles recommended even to people who don't normally play games — it's more a good historical book you can live through than a traditional video game. Replaying it, moreover, reveals how many details stayed hidden the first time around — the choice of the hero's past and education changes which subjects he understands, and thereby also which questions he can even ask. Few titles can so convincingly show that truth is, above all, a matter of storytelling.
xbox-series__pentiment.teaser: Obsidian's most unusual game — a drawn story of guilt and memory in a Bavarian town.

xbox-series__grounded.article:
**Grounded** was born from a simple idea: what if a group of kids shrank to the size of an ant and had to survive in an ordinary backyard. Blades of grass become logs, a drop of dew becomes a water supply, and an ordinary spider becomes a nightmare you can only run from. The player gathers resources, builds shelters and later sprawling bases, crafts weapons from ant mandibles, brews potions from mushrooms, and gradually pushes deeper into the yard — toward the pond, the trash pile, the dark tunnels underground. There's a story thread explaining who's behind the shrinking, and the whole game can be played in co-op with up to four people.

Technically, Grounded bets on a readable, stylized look with bold colors instead of photorealism, which helps it keep a smooth pace even when dozens of bugs are swarming on screen. On Series X|S the game loads quickly, and switching between visual and performance modes lets you fine-tune the experience to taste. Sound is unusually important: buzzing, crackling, and rustling hints at what's approaching through the grass, and at night the yard turns into a truly unpleasant place. The developers also thought of arachnophobes and added a slider that gradually strips detail from spiders down to harmless spheres.

The game first came out in early access and reached its full version in 2022, when the complete story and ending arrived. Reviews praised the concept, the clear base-building, and above all how well it works within a group of friends; complaints targeted repetitive activities in the later stages. Today Grounded is one of the most accessible survival games out there — deep enough for genre veterans, yet friendly enough that a younger player can stick with it too. After release, the game kept receiving updates with new areas, enemies, and building options, so a return trip is worthwhile even for those who tried it in its early versions. And if there's one thing Grounded does unmatched, it's shifting scale: after a few hours, you look at an ordinary backyard in a completely different way.
xbox-series__grounded.teaser: A group of kids shrunk to ant size survives in a backyard; a blade of grass is a log.

xbox-series__hi-fi-rush.article:
**Hi-Fi RUSH** appeared completely out of nowhere — it was announced and released on the very same day — and within a few hours it became one of the most delightful surprises of the entire generation. The player controls Chai, an aspiring musician, who during a corporate experiment gets an audio player lodged in his chest, turning him into a system defect that the Vandelay corporation wants removed immediately. The core of the gameplay is action-brawling in the spirit of classic Japanese action games, except everything runs on the rhythm of the soundtrack: hits land harder when timed to the beat, dodges and blocks are counted in measures, and even the environment — presses, cranes, traffic lights — moves precisely to the music.

Visually, it's a hand-drawn comic brought into three dimensions, with bold outlines, saturated colors, and animation that plays with caricature. That very style is what let the game run exceptionally smoothly on Series X|S, which is a necessity for rhythm-based action — any stumble would ruin the timing. The sound mix is the star: the soundtrack blends original compositions with licensed rock tracks, and during boss fights the music adapts to how the battle is going. For players who don't feel the rhythm, the developers added visual aids and an assist mode, so the game shuts nobody out.

Reviewers were thrilled by how elegantly it managed to combine two genres that usually have nothing to do with each other, as well as by its light, self-deprecating humor. Hi-Fi RUSH quickly became a textbook example of what a mid-sized project released straight into a subscription service can achieve. Today it still feels fresh and is an ideal choice for anyone who wants a smoothly flowing campaign from an action game without unnecessary padding, clearly readable combat, and a soundtrack you'll still be humming long after finishing it. The campaign is rounded out by allies with their own moves in combat, gradual unlocking of new techniques, and arena challenges for those who want to truly master the system. The future of Tango Gameworks was uncertain after release, which only makes the game stand out more as a reminder that originality pays off.
xbox-series__hi-fi-rush.teaser: Announced and released the same day; rhythm action where combat syncs to the beat of the music.

xbox-series__indiana-jones-and-great-cir.article:
**Indiana Jones and the Great Circle** is an adventure set between the films Raiders of the Lost Ark and The Last Crusade, telling of a mysterious circle of sacred sites scattered across the globe. The game bets on an unusual solution: exploration and combat play out in first person, while climbing, cutscenes, and the most intense moments switch to third person. Indy is no soldier — a gun is very much a last resort; fists, improvised objects, and above all the whip work far better, letting you disarm an opponent, pull yourself up to a ledge, or sweep a guard's legs out from under them. A large part of the game consists of quietly sneaking past guards, solving puzzles in tombs, and leafing through a notebook full of notes and photographs.

The individual areas — the Vatican, Egyptian deserts, Himalayan heights, or the Thai jungle — are designed as semi-open playgrounds, where alongside the main storyline lie optional tasks, lost artifacts, and plenty of nooks rewarding curiosity. On Xbox Series X|S the game runs on the studio's proven engine with excellent lighting and ray tracing, so shafts of dusty light in underground temples rank among the most beautiful images of the year. The music quotes the iconic fanfare motif only sparingly, so that each use carries weight, and the lead character's voice acting comes across very convincingly close to the film original.

Critics received the game excellently, praising above all its faithfulness to the source material's tone — the game is adventurous, funny, and, at the right moment, serious, without trying to be a modern action shooter. It also showed that MachineGames can do something other than fast-paced action. Today it's one of the best licensed games of recent years and a title that can delight even players who have no attachment to the Indiana Jones brand at all. There's also a camera used to document finds, and a system of small rewards for completed challenges that makes it worthwhile to explore areas off the main path too. Difficulty, moreover, can be set separately for combat and for puzzles.
xbox-series__indiana-jones-and-great-cir.teaser: An adventure between Raiders of the Lost Ark and The Last Crusade; played in first person.

xbox-series__avowed.article:
**Avowed** takes players into the world of Eora, the same setting Obsidian Entertainment built in the isometric Pillars of Eternity games, but this time from a first-person perspective with a strong emphasis on direct action. The protagonist is an envoy of the empire who arrives on a sprawling archipelago called the Living Lands to investigate a strange plague that is changing both people and animals. The fact that crystals are growing out of their face and a foreign voice speaks inside their head does nothing to make the situation easier. Combat rests on free combination of both hands — one might hold a sword, the other a pistol or a magic staff — and the game never forces players into a fixed class; the build can be reshaped and experimented with throughout the playthrough.

The world isn't one giant map but several large, hand-built regions, which plays to Obsidian's strengths: instead of empty expanse it offers density — hidden caves, notes, camps and side threads that almost always lead somewhere. Companions have their own opinions on how you deal with local factions and chime in even in the middle of conversations. It's the dialogue, and the option to resolve situations through cunning, persuasion or knowledge of the surroundings, that sets the game apart from purely action-focused RPGs. Visually it leans on a rich, slightly stylized palette with lush vegetation and strange fungal formations that make the Living Lands feel genuinely exotic.

On Xbox Series X|S the game offers a choice between image fidelity and smoothness and technically ranks among the more solid releases Microsoft has put out in recent years. Reviews were positive — praising the writing, the freedom in character building and the inventive world, while criticism focused on a less flexible faction system and the fact that the game doesn't reach the scale of its biggest competitors. As a mid-sized RPG built with honest craft, though, it works excellently. Magic combat comes off especially well: spells can be chained with weapons, the environment reacts to fire and frost, and the strongest hits require careful timing, bringing combat closer to an action game than a mere skill rotation. Anyone who fell in love with Pillars of Eternity will also appreciate the many references to earlier events in Eora.
xbox-series__avowed.teaser: A return to the world of Eora from Pillars of Eternity, this time in first person.

xbox-series__south-of-midnight.article:
**South of Midnight** is a fairy tale from the American South unlike anything usually seen in games. After a devastating storm, the heroine Hazel sets out to find her mother and discovers along the way that she belongs to the so-called Weavers — people able to see and mend the threads the world is woven from. The landscape of swamps, flooded houses and abandoned little towns is full of creatures out of local folklore, driven mad by unprocessed grief and old wrongs, and Hazel must either unravel them or help them find peace. The gameplay combines brisk platforming — swinging along thread-ropes, double jumps, pulling yourself forward — with combat in which enemies are first weakened and then literally unwoven.

The strongest element is the visual style. Character and creature animation deliberately skips frames, so the whole game looks like a stop-motion puppet film, and this trick lends even calm scenes an unsettled, dreamlike undertone. Add to that landscapes full of moss, cypress trees and rusting metal, mist over the water, and lighting that borrows its colors from Southern sunsets. The music rests on blues, gospel and folk ballads; every major enemy has its own song telling its story, and it's precisely these songs that make the game a long-remembered experience.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly and also offers a smoother-framerate mode, with the stylization letting it look great without extreme hardware demands. Reviews highlighted the atmosphere, the music and the sensitive handling of themes of loss and family memory, while criticism leaned toward the simplicity of combat and the linearity of the levels. As a mid-length, well-told adventure with a distinctive cultural grounding, though, South of Midnight ranks among the most personal titles Xbox Game Studios has released. The chapters are also short and play well over an evening, so the game never starts to feel like a chore. Worth noting too is the narrative framing device, with a character commenting on events like a folk storyteller, which holds the whole thing together like a collection of connected legends.
xbox-series__south-of-midnight.teaser: A fairy tale from the American South about Weaver, a girl who mends the threads the world is woven from.

xbox-series__age-of-mythology-retold.article:
**Age of Mythology: Retold** is a thorough revival of the 2002 strategy game that always held a special place within the Age of Empires series — instead of historical armies, it features mythical heroes, giant monsters and direct interventions from the gods. Players gather wood, food, gold and, crucially, favor, whose method of collection differs for each culture, and choose one of the offered gods at each advance through the ages. This unlocks divine powers such as earthquakes, meteor showers or turning enemies into pigs, along with specific mythical units. It's exactly this choice that makes every match feel a little different and keeps the strategy fresh even after twenty years.

The remake didn't just redraw the textures: it brought entirely new models, lighting, dynamic weather and reworked bodies of water, a clearer interface and a range of gameplay tweaks, including adjustments to economy management and unit behavior. The campaign following Arkantos remains intact, only fully rebuilt, and is supplemented with content from the original expansion featuring Norse and Atlantean themes, plus other cultures added after release. The major new addition is the console version — gamepad controls were designed with an awareness that strategy games of this type traditionally struggle on consoles, and it offers smart switching between unit groups and production buildings.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly and supports cross-play with PC players, so the community stays undivided. The reception was warm; reviewers praised the respect shown to the original, the quality of the remake, and the fact that the game didn't simplify what always set it apart. For newcomers it's one of the most accessible classic real-time strategy games out there, and for veterans it's a return that didn't betray their memories. Alongside the campaigns, the game offers classic skirmishes against the AI, ranked multiplayer and a map editor, so its lifespan is measured in hundreds of hours. And it's precisely the mythical units that remain what sets it apart from the rest of the series: a giant cyclops or a sea serpent can turn a battle around, but a well-timed divine power can do so far more dramatically.
xbox-series__age-of-mythology-retold.teaser: A revival of the 2002 strategy game, where mythical heroes and gods take the place of armies.

xbox-series__ori-and-will-of-wisps.article:
**Ori and the Will of the Wisps** accompanied the launch of the Xbox Series X|S consoles as one of the first titles enhanced for the new hardware, and it still ranks among the most beautiful games running on them. The story continues the tale of the small spirit of light, Ori, who sets out to find the owlet Ku and in the process reaches the withering land of Niwen, plagued by spreading darkness. The structure is classic metroidvania: the map opens up gradually as the hero gains new abilities — an air jump, a sword strike, a spear, a grappling hook or the ability to swim through sand — and older areas transform into entirely new paths thanks to them. Compared to the first game, combat has been noticeably toughened up, with the addition of heroic trials, full-fledged bosses and a system of charms that lets players build their own playstyle.

On the new generation the game runs at high resolution and with a considerably higher frame rate, which for a game built on split-second precision jumps and dodges is no mere cosmetic touch but a tangible difference in control. Hand-painted backgrounds with several layers of depth, light filtering through roots, and delicate particle effects create the impression of a moving illustration. The music is purely orchestral, built around piano and strings, and during the chases where ruin pursues Ori across an entire level, it becomes an utterly gripping accompaniment.

Critics received the game enthusiastically, praising above all how it managed to expand the scope without losing the fragility and emotional power of its predecessor — the story's ending ranks among the strongest moments in the genre. Today Ori and the Will of the Wisps is a required stop for anyone who loves platformers, and at the same time proof that a relatively small team can create a game with the visual and musical polish of major productions. Alongside the main story, the game offers side quests for the village's inhabitants, racing trials against spirits and a number of hidden nooks with upgrades, so there's still reason to return after finishing it. The difficulty is well balanced, too: the game can put up a real fight, but thanks to generous saving it never punishes unfairly.
xbox-series__ori-and-will-of-wisps.teaser: The sequel about the spirit of light searching for the owlet Ku; one of the most beautiful games of the generation.

xbox-series__elden-ring.article:
**Elden Ring** took the proven formula of Soulslike games and spread it across an open world that makes no effort to hold the player's hand. The Lands Between is a landscape of scorched plains, flooded catacombs, abandoned castles and crypts, into which the game drops you without arrows or a quest list. The storytelling is built from item descriptions, sparse dialogue, and above all from what can be seen on the horizon: something strange in the distance, a path leading to it, and a reward in the form of a dungeon, a boss, or a piece of gear that rewrites your entire build. Combat remains methodical and merciless, but it's joined by the horse Torrent, a jump, full-fledged stealth, and such a range of spells and weapons that two playthroughs can look completely different.

On Xbox Series X|S the game benefits above all from fast loading, since death comes often here and the reload afterward takes only a moment. The consoles offer a frame-rate-priority mode and a resolution-priority mode, to which a later update added optional ray tracing for shadows and reflections. On the more powerful model the game runs essentially stable, on Series S the resolution is lower, but the experience remains complete. The visual side doesn't rely on raw technical power but on architecture and light: the golden glow of Erdtree streams, mist over swamps, and giant forces sleeping somewhere beneath the earth. The music is heard almost exclusively during boss fights, and precisely because of that, the orchestral choir feels like an event when it does arrive.

The reception was extraordinary, and the game collected a record number of Game of the Year awards. Its influence on the genre is visible immediately: open worlds began experimenting with how little information players actually need, and a number of studios have tried to replicate the combination of free exploration and brutal combat. Today Elden Ring feels like an exceptionally complete package, especially with the Shadow of the Erdtree expansion, which adds another sprawling region. It isn't a game for everyone looking to unwind after work, but whoever lets themselves get pulled in loses dozens of hours in the Lands Between without ever feeling like they're just going through the motions.
xbox-series__elden-ring.teaser: The Souls formula spread across an open world that doesn't hold your hand.

xbox-series__cyberpunk-2077.article:
**Cyberpunk 2077** drops players into Night City as a desperate nomad, a corporate errand-runner, or a street kid into whose head the digital imprint of a dead rock legend gets implanted. That's where the game's central tension comes from: time pressure, personal disintegration, and a city that offers far more distraction than is healthy. It plays as a first-person shooter with a deep RPG layer on top. Cybernetic implants change the style of play far more radically than mere stat numbers: one player might slip through a building via networks and disable cameras, another might blast through a wall, and a third might cut their way close-up with a monofilament whip. The side character quests rank among the best-written content in modern RPGs.

On Xbox Series X|S, the game arrived in native form only in 2022, when a major update brought improved lighting, denser traffic, and performance and quality modes including ray tracing. It's precisely this version that finally matches how the city was supposed to look from the start: rain on neon signs, reflections in shop windows, and crowds that feel dense. Loading is short thanks to the SSD, and fast travel is essentially instant. The sound design is by far the strongest part of the atmosphere — radio stations, synthesizer loops, and aggressive guitar tracks define the mood of each district just as much as the architecture does.

The game's 2020 launch was marred by technical problems, especially on the older console generation, and the brand went through a very rough period as a result. The following years, however, brought a fundamental overhaul of the police system, skills, and cybernetic gear, and with the Phantom Liberty expansion, a cohesive espionage story that many consider the high point of the entire game. Today Cyberpunk 2077 is a showcase of what a long-term fix of a major project looks like. Anyone picking it up now gets a vast, technically solid, and remarkably well-written RPG whose greatest strength remains the city itself.
xbox-series__cyberpunk-2077.teaser: Night City through the eyes of a mercenary carrying the digital imprint of a dead rock legend in his head.

xbox-series__baldur-s-gate-3.article:
**Baldur's Gate 3** is an attempt to translate the rules of tabletop Dungeons & Dragons into a video game without losing the freedom that defines the tabletop experience along the way. The premise is classic: a party of adventurers with a parasite in their heads seeks a way to get rid of it, and in doing so uncovers a conspiracy reaching all the way up to the gods themselves. Combat is turn-based on a grid, with a dice roll for every action, and the environment is fully interactive — barrels of oil, height differences, objects you can push, spells that reshape the terrain. Crucially, the game accounts for genuinely unconventional solutions: killing an important character, sabotaging your own quest, or bypassing an entire chapter is a legitimate path, and the story adapts accordingly.

The Xbox Series X|S version launched at the end of 2023 and is fully featured, including multiplayer co-op. The Series X even handles split-screen mode, while on the Series S this option is limited, which was the biggest technical hurdle during development. Controls adapted for the gamepad are surprisingly comfortable: radial menus, smart spell targeting, and clear action queues. Loading of the extensive areas is short thanks to the SSD, which is no small feat for a game with this much data. Visually, the game leans on detailed faces and acting work, since a substantial part of the experience takes place in dialogue; the orchestral score stays discreetly in the background and only steps forward at moments when an event truly carries weight.

The reception was enthusiastic, and the game picked up numerous Game of the Year awards. Its influence is felt in how it raised expectations around reactivity — after it, it's harder to defend an RPG where choice means nothing more than a different line of dialogue. Today Baldur's Gate 3 feels like an exceptionally generous title: three sprawling acts, hundreds of hours of content across replays, and a party of characters with their own goals and opinions about what you do. For players who were wary of turn-based combat, it also happens to be the best available introduction to the genre.
xbox-series__baldur-s-gate-3.teaser: Perhaps the most faithful translation of Dungeons & Dragons rules into a video game; freedom without compromise.

xbox-series__resident-evil-4.article:
**Resident Evil 4** in its 2023 form isn't just a redrawn original but a rebuild that preserves the pacing of its source while rewriting nearly every situation. Leon S. Kennedy heads to a remote Spanish village to find the president's daughter, and instead of zombies he's greeted by villagers controlled by a parasite, who can open doors, flank him, and work together. The game rests on resource management: every round of ammunition counts, a limited-space case forces you to choose between healing items and munitions, and the merchant offers weapon upgrades that fundamentally change your playstyle. New additions include a knife with its own durability, full-fledged parrying, and the option to proceed quietly, turning what was an action game into a surprisingly tactical affair.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs on the RE Engine and ranks among the technically cleanest titles of its generation. There's a higher-resolution mode and a smoothness-priority mode, optional ray tracing, and very fast loading. Lighting is the real star: the cone of a flashlight in caves, flickering torches in the church, and scenes where darkness isn't just an effect but an obstacle. Sound works with space — footsteps overhead, distant calls of villagers, and sudden silence that announces the arrival of an unexpected foe. The music enters sparingly, which only makes it hit harder during the chases.

The 2005 original, with its over-the-shoulder view, practically defined the modern third-person action game, and its influence can be seen in dozens of successors. The new version pulled off something rare: it embraced changed player expectations without giving up the source material's rough pacing and playfulness. Both critics and players received it very well, and it regularly comes up in discussions of the best remakes ever made. Today it's one of the most easily recommendable games on Xbox Series X|S: just the right length, well paced, and even after finishing it, tempting you back for another run on a harder difficulty.
xbox-series__resident-evil-4.teaser: A rebuild of the classic that preserves the original's rhythm while rewriting almost every scene.

xbox-series__yakuza-like-dragon.article:
**Yakuza: Like a Dragon** is the boldest turning point in the entire series — instead of action-brawling, it delivers a full-fledged turn-based JRPG, and instead of the taciturn Kazuma Kiryu, the hero is Ichiban Kasuga, a warm-hearted member of a lowly clan who, after eighteen years in prison, discovers that no one was waiting for him. Ichiban grew up on classic Japanese RPGs, so he imagines his own life as a party adventure: random passersby turn into monsters in his head, city jobs work like character classes, and special attacks look exactly as absurd as he'd wish. Thanks to this, the turn-based combat never feels like a compromise, but like a joke that holds the whole game together.

The game launched alongside the Xbox Series X|S and was one of the first titles to show off the new console's potential: higher resolution, smoother performance, and very short loading times when moving between streets and battles. Players who started on the older generation could carry their progress over. Yokohama's setting is dense and full of detail — arcades, restaurants, shops, karaoke, go-kart races, and dozens of other distractions that together take up more time than the main story. The music mixes jazz, rock, and bombastic battle themes, and the karaoke minigame turns into an attraction all its own.

Before this entry, the series held cult status in the West; this title in particular significantly widened its audience, since the turn-based system also appealed to players who never clicked with the earlier action combat. Critics especially praised the script, which can shift within moments from a grotesque gag to a very serious thread about poverty and exclusion. Its influence shows in the fact that the studio continued in this form with later entries as well. Today it's a great entry point into the whole Like a Dragon universe: the story stands on its own, the game explains the necessary context, and its scope will easily fill dozens of evenings.
xbox-series__yakuza-like-dragon.teaser: A bold turn for the series toward turn-based JRPG; kind-hearted Ichiban takes over from Kiryu.

xbox-series__metaphor-refantazio.article:
**Metaphor: ReFantazio** is a fantasy JRPG from the creators of the Persona series, who have carried their proven formula over from a Japanese city into an invented realm full of tension between human tribes. The king is dead, and his successor is decided by a nationwide election that anyone can enter — including a hero from a despised lineage who is trying to save a cursed prince. The game combines a calendar and time-management system, in which you decide who gets your afternoons, with turn-based battles built around exploiting enemy weaknesses. The key mechanic is the archetypes, i.e. job classes that can be swapped, combined, and developed into specialized branches; relationships with characters unlock further archetypes and force the player to plan ahead.

On Xbox Series X|S, the game launched simultaneously with the other platforms and has been available on subscription from day one. It runs very smoothly, loading times are short, and quick navigation through the menus is part of the enjoyment — Atlus is known for treating its user interface as an art form in its own right, and here too every menu is animated, crisp, and full of motion. The art style mixes medieval paintings, collage, and expressive typography; the enemies resemble dark engravings more than classic fantasy monsters. The music is one of the most distinctive elements: choral singing in a non-existent language, along with drums and brass, creates a sound that differs sharply from ordinary fantasy scores.

Reception was very strong, and the game emerged as one of the leading contenders for game of the year. It was praised above all for the courage to transplant Persona's rhythm into a fantasy setting, and for how it handles themes of prejudice and fear of the unfamiliar without slipping into preaching. Its influence on the genre lies mainly in proving that a time-management system can work outside a school setting as well. Today, Metaphor: ReFantazio is one of the best ways to play a big Japanese RPG on Xbox — it's extensive, yet surprisingly well explained even for genre newcomers.
xbox-series__metaphor-refantazio.teaser: A fantasy JRPG from the creators of Persona; a calendar, journals, and the choice of a new king in a threatened realm.

xbox-series__plague-tale-requiem.article:
**A Plague Tale: Requiem** continues the story of siblings Amicia and Hugo, who flee a France ravaged by war and plague, heading south in search of a cure for the boy's curse. The core of the gameplay is stealth: the player skirts patrols, draws attention away, douses and lights fires, and mixes projectiles of various effects into the sling. Compared to the previous entry, there's more freedom — a crossbow, the option of open confrontation, and environments that offer more than one path. The strongest mechanic remains light: rats are afraid of fire, so every torch, bonfire, and spark serves as both weapon and compass, and the scenes where a black tide floods through the streets rank among the most tense moments of their generation.

The game released only for the new console generation, and on Xbox Series X|S that shows. The rat-swarm simulation runs at a scale older hardware couldn't handle, and combined with the very detailed environments of southern France and the Mediterranean, it becomes one of the visually strongest titles of its year. The game was initially locked to thirty frames per second, but a later update added a performance mode favoring smoothness. Thanks to the SSD, loading is short, which, in a game with frequent section retries, contributes to a smoother overall experience. The orchestral score leans on strings and female vocals, carrying the mood from calm moments on the beach all the way to a tragic climax.

Critics received the game very well, especially for its storytelling and the relationship between the two siblings, which gradually shifts over the course of the game. Criticism was aimed at its linearity and at the fact that the stealth sometimes punishes experimentation. The title's influence lies mainly in demonstrating room for mid-sized European productions that don't compete on scale but on direction and atmosphere. Today, Requiem feels like a tight, emotionally demanding experience: it doesn't stretch into hundreds of hours, but players remember its ending long after finishing it. It's also one of the few games unafraid to lead the player toward uncomfortable conclusions instead of offering easy absolution.
xbox-series__plague-tale-requiem.teaser: A stealthy sequel to the story of siblings Amicia and Hugo, with greater freedom in combat.

xbox-series__star-wars-jedi-survivor.article:
**Star Wars Jedi: Survivor** continues Cal Kestis's story several years after the events of the first game, finding him a tired, battle-hardened knight who no longer has illusions about how easily the Empire can be resisted. Combat draws on the schooling the soulslike genre has taught players: parrying at just the right moment, stamina management, and bosses whose attacks you have to learn. New this time are combat stances — a double-bladed lightsaber, a lightsaber paired with a blaster, a cross-guard stance, and more — that can be switched between to build your own style. Exploring the planets is metroidvania in the truest sense: new abilities open up previously inaccessible paths, and it pays off to go back.

On Xbox Series X|S, the game offers a visual mode including ray tracing as well as a mode favoring smoother performance. Its launch was plagued by performance issues, especially on PC, and subsequent updates focused specifically on stability; on consoles, the situation improved significantly during the first few months. Visually, it's one of the most beautiful games in the entire Star Wars universe — the planet Koboh, with its rocky massifs, dusty little town, and sunsets, feels like a place you could actually live. The sound design uses the series' iconic motifs but doesn't rely on them blindly; its own orchestral themes keep the tension up even away from familiar territory.

Reception was mostly very good, with praise going especially to the characters' growth, the broadened combat system, and a far bolder world structure compared to the first game. Reservations were aimed at its technical state at launch and at the occasional emptiness of large areas. Its influence shows in how licensed action games began drifting away from corridors and toward interconnected worlds with gradual unlocking. Today, after patches, Jedi: Survivor is one of the best reasons to pick up a Star Wars game on Xbox Series X|S, even for players who've only followed the films casually.
xbox-series__star-wars-jedi-survivor.teaser: Soulslike combat tailored to fit; a tougher, more seasoned Cal Kestis gains new combat stances.

xbox-series__lies-of-p.article:
**Lies of P** takes the fairy tale of Pinocchio and transposes it to the dark city of Krat, where puppets have risen up against their creators and disease has flooded the streets. The player controls the puppet P, who is searching for his creator and along the way must decide whether to tell the truth or lie — and it's the lies that bring him closer to humanity, which affects the ending. The gameplay openly draws on Bloodborne: quick dodges, an aggressive pace, and a boss at the end of each area that tests your patience. Its own contribution lies in a mechanical arm with swappable attachments, the ability to combine weapon blades and handles into custom builds, and a perfect-block system that, with the right timing, destroys enemy weapons.

On Xbox Series X|S, the game runs on Unreal Engine, maintains high smoothness, and offers short loading times, which is essential for a game built around constant dying. The art direction is one of the title's strongest aspects overall: Art Nouveau facades, gas lamps, opulent hotels wrapped in grime, and mechanical monsters that come across as both fragile and terrifying at once. The music works with piano, strings, and singing in bars where the player can rest for a moment; the contrast between a calm song and a massacre a few rooms further ranks among its most memorable moments. The game was available on subscription from launch, which helped it spread quickly among players.

Reception was surprisingly strong — critics expected less from a title that openly declares its FromSoftware inspiration, and the game won them over with both its combat and its visual side. Reservations were aimed mainly at the difficulty of some bosses at launch, which later updates smoothed out. Its influence on the genre lies in showing that soulslike is no longer the exclusive domain of one studio and that a game can find its own voice within it. Today, Lies of P is one of the best ways to try the genre, especially for players who enjoy a fast, aggressive combat style.
xbox-series__lies-of-p.teaser: A dark take on Pinocchio in the spirit of Bloodborne; lying paradoxically brings the hero closer to humanity.

xbox-series__assassin-s-creed-valhalla.article:
**Assassin's Creed Valhalla** moves the series into the ninth century, when Norse clans arrive on the British Isles in search of new land. The player leads Eivor, chieftain of the Raven Clan, and alongside raiding expeditions also manages her own settlement, Ravensthorpe, which grows according to which buildings and people are brought into it. The game's structure is assembled from regional story arcs: in each shire, a dispute between local rulers is resolved, alliances are forged, and only gradually does the picture of the whole island come together. Combat is slower and heavier than in earlier entries, with an emphasis on two-handed weapons, dual-wielding, and abilities unlocked on an extensive skill tree.

The game launched alongside the Xbox Series X|S and was one of the first titles to show off the benefits of the new generation: higher resolution, greater draw distance, smoother performance, and noticeably shorter loading times than on the older console. The settings of England and Norway rank among the best-realized in the entire series — mists over the marshes, crumbling Roman buildings overgrown with ivy, and monasteries perched on cliffs. The music mixes Nordic wind instruments and drums with ambient textures, complemented by shipboard singing during river voyages, one of the strongest atmospheric ideas in the whole game.

Reception was good, the game gained a large player base, and received several extensive expansions, including arcs set in Ireland and France. Critics praised the settings and settlement management, while criticism was aimed at the enormous scale, which also means repetition of the same activities; completing everything takes a very large number of hours. After this entry, the series headed back toward tighter titles, meaning Valhalla essentially closed out the era of sprawling RPGs. Today, it's a game for those who want a long-term setting to return to evening after evening; those looking for a tight adventure should reach for something else. But precisely thanks to its volume of content and low price during sales, it remains one of the most frequently recommended entry points into the series on the new console generation.
xbox-series__assassin-s-creed-valhalla.teaser: The series' Viking detour, featuring the building of your own settlement and regional story arcs.

xbox-series__dying-light-2-stay-human.article:
**Dying Light 2 Stay Human** builds on the combination its predecessor practically invented: first-person parkour, melee combat, and a day that turns into a run for your life at night. The city of Villedor is the last great settlement of surviving civilization, and its rooftop landscape is the main playground — the player jumps, slides, uses a paraglider and a grappling hook to avoid the streets, which belong to the infected after dark. Combat is brutal, built around improvised weapons with limited durability and custom modifications. A crucial layer is decision-making: handing a water tower, power plant, or bridge over to one faction permanently changes the look of a district as well as which equipment becomes available.

On Xbox Series X|S, the game offers several modes — with an emphasis on resolution, on smoothness, and an optional ray tracing mode for global illumination that affects the atmosphere more than usual: dark interiors without light are genuinely dark. Loading is short, and the game supports co-op for up to four players, which makes it one of the best titles for evenings spent together. Sound is key to the tension — growling in a corridor, noise while fleeing across rooftops, and music that surges sharply during a chase and drops back into silence after you escape.

Reception was good, though mixed: praise went to the movement, which ranks among the best in the genre, and to the scale of the city, while criticism was aimed at the writing of the main storyline and at technical bugs at launch. Techland, however, supported the game long-term, and the following years brought major updates, including reworked weapon combat and expansions. The title's influence shows in how first-person movement became a game discipline of its own, even outside purely action-focused games. Today, Dying Light 2 is a sprawling package that pays off especially for players seeking long-term co-op fun. The first few hours can feel awkward until you get used to the movement and unlock the paraglider, but once you start reading the city as a system of roofs and ledges, crossing half the map turns from a chore into the best part of the whole game.
xbox-series__dying-light-2-stay-human.teaser: First-person parkour that turns the city into a fight for survival against the infected at night.

xbox-series__hogwarts-legacy.article:
**Hogwarts Legacy** places the player in the nineteenth century, long before the events of the well-known books, and lets them begin their studies at Hogwarts straight into the fifth year, with an unusual ability to sense ancient magic. The school itself is the main attraction: moving staircases, paintings that comment on events, secret passages, and classrooms where lessons in potions, herbology, or spellwork take place. Combat is fast-paced action built around combining spells according to an opponent's colored shield type, dodging, and correct timing; the player assembles their own spell loadouts and upgrades them through a gear system. Beyond the castle, an open landscape unfolds with Scottish hills, villages, and caves.

On Xbox Series X|S, the game offers a mode with higher resolution and ray tracing as well as a mode favoring smoothness; the version for the new consoles launched earlier than the one for the older generation. Hogwarts' setting is a showcase of just how important lighting is — candles in the Great Hall, reflections on wooden floors, and stained glass all feel convincing, and many players spend their first few hours simply wandering the corridors. The sound design uses its own orchestral score, which draws on the series' familiar style without merely repeating the film themes, and shifts smoothly across the castle's different areas.

The game became one of the commercially most successful titles of its year, even though its release was accompanied by public debate connected to the author of the original source material. Critics praised above all the depiction of the school and the combat, while criticism was aimed at repetitive side quests and at the fact that the school routine fades into the background after a few hours. The title's influence lies mainly in proving that licensed open worlds can build on setting rather than action. Today, Hogwarts Legacy is a comfortable, visually strong game that works best for those who simply want to live out a year at Hogwarts.
xbox-series__hogwarts-legacy.teaser: An open world of Hogwarts a century before the books; a living school with moving staircases.

xbox-series__clair-obscur-expedition-33.article:
**Clair Obscur: Expedition 33** is a French RPG that borrows the shape of Japanese turn-based games and fuses it with an art style inspired by the belle époque. The starting premise is chilling: every year a number appears on a distant monolith, and everyone who has reached that age vanishes. Expedition 33 sets out to destroy the monolith, fully aware that the previous thirty-two expeditions never returned. Combat is turn-based, but it demands active participation even outside your own turn — every enemy attack can be dodged or parried at the right moment, turning defense into a skill-based discipline in its own right. Characters develop through a system of items that alter how their abilities behave, and each has its own distinct combat mechanics.

On Xbox Series X|S the game launched simultaneously with the other platforms and was available on subscription from day one, which gave it an extremely fast reach. It runs on Unreal Engine 5, offers both a quality and a performance mode, and holds up technically even on Series S. Visually it is one of the most distinctive titles of recent years: landscapes look like painted canvases, a city shrouded in mist dissolves into particles of light, and enemies take shapes that keep their distance from generic fantasy. The music is singled out especially often — piano, strings, vocals in French as well as wordless singing that, in combination, define the whole mood by swinging between calm and sudden bombast.

Reception was extraordinarily strong, and the game quickly became one of the most talked-about titles of the year, especially thanks to its character writing and an ending that leaves the player with a difficult decision. It was also praised for how a relatively small studio managed to deliver a game of this caliber. Its influence is already visible in how it has revived interest in turn-based combat with a reflex-based element. Today, Clair Obscur: Expedition 33 is one of the easiest games to recommend on Xbox Series X|S to anyone who loves strong storytelling.
xbox-series__clair-obscur-expedition-33.teaser: A French turn-based RPG with a painted belle époque world and a chilling starting premise.

xbox-series__dirt-5.article:
**Dirt 5** was among the titles that accompanied the launch of Xbox Series X|S, and it shifted away from its more simulation-leaning predecessors toward colorful arcade racing. Instead of narrow rally stages, it offers wide circuits in icy Scandinavia, snow-covered New York streets, or Chinese canyons where packs of cars rub shoulders side by side. The handling model is forgiving, slides hold for a long time, and contact with rivals is part of the fun. The career mode is split into series spanning disciplines from rallycross through buggies to big trucks, accompanied by a narrated radio show that comments on the player's progress between races.

Technically it was one of the first showcases of what the new generation could do: on Series X you can choose a mode targeting 120 frames per second, which for arcade off-road driving means noticeably more readable car responses. Changeable weather and time of day are not just window dressing — mud gradually gets churned up, tire tracks appear in snow, and night stages lit only by headlights are among the game's strongest moments. The soundtrack leans on loud modern electronic music and rock, so the music underscores the pace rather than merely accompanying it.

Contemporary reception was mildly positive: reviewers praised the visuals, the smoothness, and the Playgrounds mode, in which players build their own stunt arenas and share them with others, while criticism targeted the shallower handling model and a less inventive career structure. In the history of the Dirt brand this is more of a detour than a continuation of the line built on faithful rally racing. Today it works as an undemanding racing title to reach for when you want a quick dose of driving without having to memorize the track by heart. On Series X|S it still looks good, and the smoothness in high-frame-rate mode is one of the things helping it age more slowly than one might expect. It will especially appeal to anyone wanting to race in pairs on one screen, since split-screen multiplayer on consoles has gradually become rarer.
xbox-series__dirt-5.teaser: A colorful arcade detour from the otherwise simulation-focused Dirt games; wide circuits instead of narrow stages.

xbox-series__need-for-speed-unbound.article:
**Need for Speed Unbound** attempts to revive street racing with a bold visual idea: photorealistic cars are accompanied by hand-drawn effects that burst from the bodywork like graffiti during drifts, nitrous boosts, or jumps. The result feels like a comic book projected onto an otherwise realistic city, Lakeshore, modeled on an American metropolis with industrial districts, bridges, and wide boulevards. The game builds on a weekly cycle: daytime races pay less, nighttime ones are lucrative, but with every win police interest grows, and the player has to judge when to retreat to the garage and bank the money.

The handling model is classically arcade-style with an emphasis on drifting, with tuning that can be shifted from grippy setups all the way to cars that slide into a drift at every touch of the throttle. Car customization is extensive, covering not just parts and paint but also the animated effects around the wheels and the player's own avatar. On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly at high resolution, and the stylization benefits it technically too — sharp outlines and bold colors work better than an attempt at pure realism. The soundtrack is carried by modern hip hop and electronic music that fits the street atmosphere of nighttime chases.

Reception was mixed to mildly positive. Praise went to the visual style, which after years gave the series its own face, and to the tense risk system when fleeing the police; criticism targeted story clichés, the difficulty of later races, and an uneven career pace. For the series it was a bold step that showed stylization can be its strongest weapon. Today it stands as a racing game with a clearly defined identity — it doesn't try to compete with simulations or open festival worlds, but offers tight nighttime driving with the adrenaline of a chase. Anyone who loves fast drifts and high stakes will get exactly this kind of fun. It works especially well in smaller doses, when one completed night cycle with an escape from patrol cars is a self-contained story in itself.
xbox-series__need-for-speed-unbound.teaser: Street racing with comic-book graffiti effects that burst from the bodywork during a drift.

xbox-series__call-of-duty-black-ops-cold.article:
**Call of Duty: Black Ops Cold War** arrived alongside the launch of the new console generation and took players into the 1980s, into a world of espionage operations and mistrust between superpowers. The campaign continues the line of the first Black Ops and, alongside the usual action set pieces, offers quiet missions, interrogations, and decisions that change the ending of the story. New was a customizable protagonist with several selectable abilities and several missions built around gathering evidence, where the player pieces clues together and decides how to proceed. The pace is brisk, the campaign can be finished over a few evenings, but it offers motivation to replay it for the alternate endings.

Multiplayer sticks to the proven formula of fast matches on compact maps, a loadout system, and killstreak rewards, joined by larger vehicle-based modes. Alongside it stands the cooperative Zombies mode, which in this installment opened its storyline to new players and offered clearer rules along with the option to bail out of a map at any time. On Xbox Series X|S a mode targeting 120 frames per second is available, which for a competitive shooter means noticeably more precise aiming, and SSD loading eliminated long waits between matches. The visuals lean on striking lighting and dense weapon sound design.

At the time the game was received mostly favorably, with the campaign earning praise for its narrative boldness and its willingness to experiment with form, while some players criticized the shorter length and balance changes to multiplayer after launch. The link to the free battle royale mode, into which weapons and progress carried over, confirmed at the time the direction the whole brand was heading. Today it stands as a solid entry among modern military shooters, its campaign among the more interesting in the series' recent history, even though the online portion has long since been replaced by newer installments. That is precisely why it's worth revisiting — mainly for the story and the cooperative zombie maps, which work independently of how many players are currently looking for a match.
xbox-series__call-of-duty-black-ops-cold.teaser: A Cold War espionage campaign with stealth missions and decisions that change the ending.

xbox-series__sniper-elite-5.article:
**Sniper Elite 5** sends sniper Karl Fairburne into occupied France in 1944, where he must uncover a secret Nazi project. Over the years the series has built its own subgenre: it's not about fast action but about patiently observing a sprawling map, tracking patrol routes, and deciding whether to remove a target quietly with a knife, a silenced pistol, or a risky long-range shot. Bullet-drop calculations factor in distance, wind, and gravity, and on higher difficulties the game doesn't show exactly where the bullet will land. Ambient noise, such as a generator's hum or artillery fire, serves as cover for uncovered shots.

The maps in this installment are noticeably more open than before and offer several routes to the objective, including optional tasks that shift the balance of power. A more elaborate weapon customization system was added, letting players swap barrels, magazines, and optics to suit their playstyle. The series' signature X-ray camera accompanying successful hits remains, only in more detailed form, which is also why the game is definitely not for children. On Xbox Series X|S it shows longer draw distances on large maps, stable performance, and fast loading, so retrying a failed approach doesn't punish you with waiting.

An interesting feature is the invasion mode, in which another player joins your ongoing mission as an enemy sniper, turning a calm approach into a nerve-wracking cat-and-mouse game. Alongside that, cooperative play is available for the whole campaign, as are competitive modes. Reviews received the game favorably as the best or one of the best entries in the series, praising the greater map freedom and variety of approach, with criticism aimed at the routine story and enemy AI. Today Sniper Elite 5 represents perhaps the most complete form of a genre built on a single, well-prepared shot — and on the long minutes of silence that precede it. It also offers newcomers enough tools to ease into the patient playstyle without having to start on the hardest difficulty.
xbox-series__sniper-elite-5.teaser: A patient tactical sniper game set in France, 1944; wind and gravity affect the bullet's flight.

xbox-series__s-t-l-k-e-r-2-heart-of-chor.article:
**S.T.A.L.K.E.R. 2: Heart of Chornobyl** is the long-awaited return to the Zone around the Chernobyl power plant and one of the few major titles to launch on console exclusively for Xbox Series X|S. The game blends a first-person shooter with survival elements: the player tracks hunger, fatigue, equipment condition, and radiation exposure, and every trip deeper into the Zone means deciding what to carry. Space-warping anomalies, packs of mutants, and hostile factions force careful route planning, since even an ordinary firefight can end with an empty magazine and a broken weapon hundreds of meters from the nearest shelter.

The open world is vast and deliberately inhospitable, with abandoned villages, industrial complexes, and underground facilities where the pace shifts into claustrophobic horror. Artifacts hidden within anomalies are the main economic motivation, but carrying them comes at the cost of radiation exposure. Technically the game runs on Unreal Engine 5 and offers impressive lighting, fog, and dynamic weather; storms and nighttime treks without a flashlight rank among the game's strongest atmospheric moments. Sound carries the tension — the crackling of the detector, distant footsteps, and wind in the treetops do more than any music could.

Development took place under extraordinarily difficult conditions following Russia's invasion of Ukraine, when the studio had to relocate part of its work abroad, and the mere completion of the project was met with respect. Contemporary reviews were positive but cautious, given the game's technical state at launch and bugs that were fixed through extensive updates. The influence of the original trilogy on the Eastern European school of survival games is unmistakable, and the second installment continues in that spirit. Today it stands as one of the most distinctive major titles of this generation: demanding, at times uncomfortable, but with an atmosphere hard to find elsewhere. Anyone who accepts its rules and stops expecting the Zone to be forgiving will get an experience that big studio shooters rarely offer — a game in which returning to the trader with a full backpack of artifacts is a genuine victory.
xbox-series__s-t-l-k-e-r-2-heart-of-chor.teaser: The long-awaited return to the Zone; a shooter mixed with harsh survival and anomalies.

xbox-series__atomic-heart.article:
**Atomic Heart** builds on an alternate version of history in which the Soviet Union mastered robotics in the 1950s and built a utopian society full of automatons — until the machines turn against people. The player takes on the role of an agent sent into a sealed scientific complex and progresses through a mix of shooting, melee combat, and abilities granted by a special glove. It can freeze enemies, lift them into the air, or strike them with electricity, and combining force and element forms the basis of the combat system.
