**Arcanum: Of Steamworks and Magick Obscura** is an isometric RPG from 2001 that placed the player in a world straddling fantasy and the industrial revolution – elves and dwarves live here alongside steam engines, steam-powered weapons, and the first automobiles. The central idea of the game is the tension between magic and technology: the more a character focuses on one area, the worse they become at the other, forcing the player to think from the start about which direction their development will take. Character creation is deep and recalls earlier classic CRPGs – a wealth of attributes, skills, and abilities allows the player to build a warrior, a mage, a technician, or anything in between, with these choices also reflected in how the talking inhabitants of individual towns and settlements react to the player.

The game offers a choice between turn-based and real-time combat systems, an open world with numerous side quests, and a strongly branching dialogue structure, where decisions genuinely change the course of the story and relationships with factions divided precisely along the lines of their relationship to magic and technology. The game also includes an extensive crafting and item-improvement system, from alchemical potions to mechanical prosthetics and firearms, so the player can also shape their character through crafting skills. Technically, Arcanum suffered on release from a number of bugs and rough edges that put off some players, but gradual unofficial and official fixes turned it into a stable and playable title. The atmosphere is rounded out by melancholic music and a distinctive humor combining Victorian aesthetics with fantasy tropes, with the world feeling believable precisely because of the tension between the old and the new order.

Even after all these years, Arcanum remains among the cult classics of the genre – its freedom of choice and inventive world are still rated higher today than many more polished but more conventional RPGs. For fans of old-school CRPGs, it still represents a game worth returning to, especially for the way it uncompromisingly confronts the player with the consequences of their own decisions.
pc-modern__arcanum-of-steamworks-and-mag.teaser: An isometric RPG straddling fantasy and industry, where magic and technology get in each other's way.

pc-modern__mafia.article:
**Mafia** from 2002 introduced players to the fictional metropolis of Lost Heaven at the turn of the 1920s and 1930s, during Prohibition and gang wars. The player takes on the role of taxi driver Tommy Angelo, whom chance draws into the service of a mafia family, and gradually guides him through a story about loyalty, power and their price. Unlike the popular action sandboxes of the time, Mafia was built on a linear, cinematically told story, where the open city served more as a backdrop than a playground for chaotic mayhem, even though between missions the player could drive through the streets and take in the shops or police patrols. The narrative itself is moreover framed as the confession of an aging Tommy to a detective, which lends the story a tinge of inevitability and sorrow.

In terms of gameplay, the game combines cover-based shooting, driving period automobiles with fairly realistic physics, and completing well-crafted missions, some of which — such as the notoriously difficult speed-limited race — have stuck in the memory of an entire generation of players. The individual chapters play out across varied settings, from docks and warehouses to lavish villas, while the game gradually reveals how deeply Tommy becomes entangled in the world of organized crime. The atmosphere is rounded out by carefully directed camera work, voice acting and a jazz soundtrack, which made Lost Heaven feel like a believably living world of the 1930s. The graphics were above average for their time, and the technical execution demonstrated the ambitions of what was then a little-known Czech studio, which earned international respect thanks to Mafia.

Mafia became one of the defining titles of the story-driven action genre with a city as backdrop, significantly influenced the direction of similar games over the following decade, and is still considered one of the best games ever made in the Czech Republic. The later 2020 remake only confirmed how strongly the story still resonates years later and how well it holds up against modern productions.
pc-modern__mafia.teaser: The cinematically told story of cab driver Tommy in gangster-era Lost Heaven; the counterpoint to sandbox games.

pc-modern__mafia-ii.article:
**Mafia II** built on the success of the first game in 2010 and transported players to the fictional Empire Bay, this time spanning the period from World War II to the 1950s. The main character is Vito Scaletta, a veteran who, upon returning from the front, gets involved in organized crime to pay off family debts, and together with his friend Joe gradually rises through the ranks of the local family, having to choose between loyalty to friends and his own conscience. The story again relies on linearly told missions with an emphasis on cinematic presentation, dialogue and relationships between characters, while the open city serves mainly as an atmospheric backdrop between chapters. Both Vito and Joe are portrayed as believable characters with their own weaknesses, so the player ultimately understands their decisions and mistakes without necessarily condoning them.

The gameplay combines cover-based shootouts, driving period vehicles, and occasional quieter passages devoted to building relationships and atmosphere, complemented by small period details such as paying off fines to policemen or listening to the radio with period news and advertisements. Visually, the game benefited from significantly more elaborate depictions of interiors, weather and time of day than its predecessor, and was accompanied by a licensed period soundtrack that further enhanced the illusion of postwar America. Some players and reviewers at the time criticized the reduced emphasis on side content and the openness of the world compared to what the first game offered, yet the story and atmosphere were largely received positively.

Even years later, Mafia II retains its reputation as a quality story-driven game with a strong atmosphere and ranks among the titles that showed a Czech studio could create a game with a powerful emotional impact even amid strong competition, albeit at the cost of less freedom than more open rivals offered. For many players, the ending of the story remains one of the most powerful moments of the entire series.
pc-modern__mafia-ii.teaser: After the war, Vito Scaletta gets drawn into crime in Empire Bay; loyalty or survival.

pc-modern__operation-flashpoint-cold-war.article:
**Operation Flashpoint: Cold War Crisis** from 2001 brought a completely new level of military realism to PC. Instead of the arcade-style shooters common at the time, it offered a sprawling island battlefield where a fictional Cold War conflict plays out across forests, fields and villages on a scale no game had managed before. The player switches between the roles of infantryman, driver and pilot, and must reckon with realistic ballistics, limited endurance, and the fact that a single poorly aimed shot often means instant death, regardless of how many hours the player has invested in the character. The available vehicles range from simple off-road vehicles through tanks to helicopters, each requiring a different amount of patience and practice to operate.

The campaign is divided into chapters told gradually from the perspective of several soldiers on both sides of the conflict, complemented by an extensive mission editor that allowed the community to create its own scenarios and campaigns for many years afterward. The battlefield includes open plains, forests and villages, where using terrain cover and coordinating advances with a subordinate unit is essential, since a direct attack across open ground usually ends in swift defeat. The graphical rendering of the landscape was impressive for its time, though it came at the cost of high hardware demands. The sound design and dense atmosphere of the battlefield, where combat could take place at distances of hundreds of meters, created the feeling of an actual military operation rather than action entertainment.

The game from Czech studio Bohemia Interactive laid the foundation for an entire series of military simulators, and its legacy is evident in the later Arma titles and in the whole genre of realistic military games. It is still considered a pioneering title that defined what a truly open and believable virtual battlefield can look like, and many of its design principles remain in use throughout the series to this day.
pc-modern__operation-flashpoint-cold-war.teaser: A new level of military realism; the role of infantryman, driver, and pilot on a vast island.

pc-modern__vietcong.article:
**Vietcong** from 2003 took players into the jungles of Vietnam in the role of a commander of a small unit of American soldiers. Unlike many war shooters of the time, the game emphasized tactics, movement through dense vegetation with limited visibility, and cooperation with subordinates, who could be given orders to advance, take cover or open fire. The environment of dense jungles, villages and underground tunnels created a claustrophobic, tense atmosphere where the enemy was often heard before being seen, and where careless movement across open terrain easily led to a swift end to the mission. The player could give their squadmates basic instructions for advancing and firing, which turned individual skirmishes into small tactical operations rather than chaotic firefights.

The game's sound design was among its greatest strengths — period rock music playing from military transistor radios reinforced the sense of time and place, while jungle sounds, distant gunfire and crackling radios built tension even during quieter passages. Missions led players through rice paddies, abandoned villages and a network of tunnels used by the enemy, and the game did not shy away from depicting civilian casualties and the moral ambiguity of the whole conflict. The graphics were of a high standard for their time, especially in terms of the density of the vegetation and lighting, which made the jungle feel dense and disorienting, much as it probably was in reality. The game from Czech studio Pterodon was among the first to seriously and thoroughly address the conflict in Vietnam, including its morally ambiguous aspects.

Thanks to its atmosphere and tactical approach, Vietcong earned devoted fans even abroad and is still remembered as one of the most authentic war experiences of its time, despite being a game with pronounced violence corresponding to the conflict it depicts.
pc-modern__vietcong.teaser: Tactics and limited visibility in dense Vietnamese jungle instead of the usual war-game arcade action.

pc-modern__arma-2.article:
**Arma 2** from 2009 expanded the military simulator concept from Operation Flashpoint to even greater proportions. The vast fictional country of Chernarus, with tens of square kilometers of terrain, villages and towns, offered room for combined operations of infantry, armored vehicles and aircraft within a single mission. The game retained an uncompromising approach to realism — weapons, ballistics and unit behavior are governed by elaborate simulation rules, making it more of a virtual military training exercise than relaxing entertainment, requiring the player to account for range, projectile drop and visibility over long distances. Enemy artificial intelligence reacts to sounds and terrain cover, so even a single firefight can require careful planning of the advance.

The campaign takes the player through the conflict in Chernarus, but the game's true strength always lay in its mission editor and modifications, which allowed the creation of custom scenarios ranging from small skirmishes to large multiplayer operations for dozens of players coordinated by voice communication. The variety of available vehicles, from jeeps through armored personnel carriers to attack helicopters, gave players enormous freedom in their own approach to completing assigned objectives. It was from Arma 2 modifications that the survival mode phenomenon DayZ emerged, which later became independent and influenced the entire survival game genre built on resource scarcity and the threat posed by other players. Technically, the game was demanding on hardware at release and not always perfectly optimized, which nevertheless did not prevent it from becoming one of the most discussed titles of its time.

The legacy of Arma 2 lives on today both in the series' sequels and in the enormous community of modification creators, who managed to draw content from it far beyond the original intentions of its creators at Bohemia Interactive, ranging from civilian simulations to entirely new game genres.
pc-modern__arma-2.teaser: An uncompromising military simulation across the vast landscape of Chernarus, spanning hundreds of square kilometers.

pc-modern__machinarium.article:
**Machinarium** from 2009 is a point-and-click adventure in which a small robot tries to rescue his robotic girlfriend and his home city from a gang of villainous machines. The entire game is told without words — the story and characters' emotions are conveyed only through picture bubbles and expressive body language, making the game understandable regardless of language barriers. The gameplay is built on classic logic puzzles and combining objects, complemented by optional hints for players who get stuck, as well as short minigames hidden within more complex tasks. The pace of the game is deliberately slower and contemplative, giving the player room to explore the surroundings and let the atmosphere sink in before tackling the next puzzle, often rewarded with a small side scene that has nothing to do with the main task.

The visual style, featuring a hand-drawn, slightly rusted industrial world, is among the game's most striking features — every screen feels like a carefully considered illustration full of details that can be explored at length regardless of the current puzzle. The music was composed by musician Tomáš Dvořák, performing under the name Floex, and his ambient, melancholic tracks significantly contributed to the overall atmosphere of loneliness and hope that accompanies the game from the opening scene to its final climax. Machinarium from studio Amanita Design was among the first independent adventure games to capture the attention of a wide international audience as well as expert critics, helping to pave the way for other smaller European studios.

The game became one of the most successful Czech gaming exports and is still held up as an example of how to tell a touching story purely through visual means, without a single spoken or written sentence, while still allowing the player to feel joy and sadness just as strongly as in games with extensive voice acting.
pc-modern__machinarium.teaser: A wordless story told through picture bubbles; a little robot saves both the city and his girlfriend.

pc-modern__samorost-3.article:
**Samorost 3** from 2016 is another point-and-click adventure from studio Amanita Design, this time with a much larger and more elaborate world than its predecessors. The player takes on the role of a small forest gnome who, thanks to a magical flute, travels aboard a spaceship between strange planets to uncover the origin of a mysterious object affecting his home forest. Each planet visited has its own visual style, fauna and puzzle logic, so the game feels like a collection of small, carefully crafted worlds connected by one story of searching for and righting an old wrong. The transition between planets is accompanied by short travel sequences that give the player time to absorb the chapter just completed before diving into the next one.

As in the studio's previous games, there is no spoken or written text of any kind here either — all understanding of the world and its inhabitants arises purely from visual and audio cues, gestures and facial expressions of the small creatures the player encounters, whether a trusting bug or a mysterious trader in strange artifacts. The hand-drawn graphics, combined with organic, almost biological shapes, create a unique surrealist atmosphere, complemented by ambient music that supports the contemplative pace of play. The puzzles are more intuitive and exploratory than strictly logical, which sets the game apart from classic adventures based on combining objects, and the player is often rewarded simply for carefully examining the scenery.

Samorost 3 confirmed Amanita Design's reputation as one of the most distinctive European independent studios, and even years later it is praised above all for its visual inventiveness and its ability to create a sense of discovering an unknown world that no other game can quite claim for itself. Players remember the game above all for the feeling of calm and wonder it can evoke without a single line of dialogue.
pc-modern__samorost-3.teaser: A more expansive sequel in the Amanita Design series; a forest gnome travels between planets by ship.

pc-modern__botanicula.article:
**Botanicula** from 2012 is a point-and-click adventure from studio Amanita Design, in which the player controls five small plant-like creatures trying to save the last seed of their home tree from parasitic pests. Unlike most adventure games, the player does not control a single character here but switches between five distinct companions, each with their own ability useful for solving puzzles and overcoming obstacles on a journey through a forest world full of small creatures and plant beings. The five heroes must cooperate to escape the dark spiders threatening their home, and the game often resolves this cooperation through simple but inventive puzzles built on combining the individual characters' abilities.

The game is characterized by its playful, almost childlike humor and lush imagination, where almost every element of the environment is interactive and rewards the player with a small sound or animation gag, whether it's tapping a mushroom or waking a sleeping little bug. The visual style follows the studio's signature look known from previous titles but pushes it into an even more colorful and playful world full of strange creatures, where even the smallest root or seed has its own character. The music was provided by the band DVA, whose experimental sounds perfectly match the bizarre yet friendly atmosphere of the game and underscore its gently comedic tone.

Thanks to its positive mood, originality and thoughtful, non-violent puzzles, Botanicula won favor with both children and adult players, and together with Machinarium it ranks among the titles that helped establish the reputation of Czech independent adventure game development on an international scale. The game still serves as an example that even without violence, text or complex storytelling, one can create an emotionally rich and memorable experience that even very young children can be safely guided through.
pc-modern__botanicula.teaser: Five plant-like creatures, five abilities, no single main character; an adventure game from Amanita.

pc-modern__factorio.article:
**Factorio** is a construction and automation simulation whose first complete versions appeared in early access around the mid-2010s, with the full release arriving in 2020. After a spaceship crash on an alien planet, the player starts with bare hands and gradually builds ever more complex factories – from manually gathering raw materials through the first belts and machines to sprawling automated complexes producing rockets capable of leaving the planet. The key element of the game is the constant refinement of production chains and the solving of logistical bottlenecks, which grow more and more complex as the empire expands, forcing the player to think more like an engineer than an adventurer. The gradual unlocking of new technologies, resources, and machines gives the game a clear sense of progression, even though the actual goal – building a rocket and leaving the planet – remains in the background until the very end.

The game is complicated by the presence of local fauna called biters, aggressive creatures irritated by the pollution produced by factories, which become more and more dangerous as production grows, making it necessary to build defensive lines and dedicated military production as well. Besides optimizing production, the player must therefore also handle base defense, which adds a subtle element of tension to an otherwise meditative building experience. The game also supports mods and custom scenarios, thanks to which the community has managed to extend the game by dozens of additional hours beyond the base campaign. Technically, the game is remarkable for its extremely efficient optimization, which allows it to simulate even enormous complexes built over hours of play without significant performance drops.

Factorio, from the Czech studio Wube Software, has become a phenomenon among fans of automation games; it is famous for its addictiveness, nicknamed the so-called engineering spiral, and to this day it remains one of the highest-rated games of its genre.
pc-modern__factorio.teaser: From gathering resources by hand to launching rockets; automation so compelling you can't stop playing.

pc-modern__beat-saber.article:
**Beat Saber**, from 2018, is a rhythm game for virtual reality in which the player uses two controllers representing lightsabers to slice blocks flying in time with the music, while simultaneously dodging obstacles and following the correct cutting direction indicated by the color and orientation of each block. A simple, instantly understandable concept combined with energetic electronic music and intuitive physical movement quickly made it one of the most recognizable titles of the emerging era of consumer virtual reality, understandable at a glance even to people seeing a VR headset for the very first time.

The game places emphasis on fluid movement of the whole body, so it functions simultaneously as entertainment and as a form of physical activity, which contributed to its reach beyond the traditional gaming community, including people using it as a form of home exercise. Game modes gradually increased in number, along with difficulty levels aimed both at complete beginners and at players seeking a genuine challenge for their hands and reflexes. The visually minimalist but strikingly lit environment, combined with precisely synchronized music, creates the feeling that the player is themselves part of the song's rhythm, while higher difficulties add obstacles and faster sequences of blocks requiring almost dance-like precise movements. Over time, official music packs were added along with support for custom community-made tracks, which significantly extended the game's lifespan beyond the original song selection and allowed players to practice their favorite tracks from a wide range of musical genres.

Beat Saber, from studio Beat Games, became one of the proofs that virtual reality can offer entertainment understandable even to people with no other gaming experience, and to this day it remains among the best-selling and most highly praised VR titles ever made. For many people, this very game was the first reason to buy a virtual reality headset at all.
pc-modern__beat-saber.teaser: Slicing blocks to the beat of music with lightsabers; a VR hit that clicks on the first try.

pc-modern__euro-truck-simulator-2.article:
**Euro Truck Simulator 2**, from 2012, offers content that seems unassuming at first glance but is unexpectedly absorbing – driving a truck along the roads of European countries, hauling cargo between cities, and gradually building your own trucking company. The player starts as a hired driver and gradually earns enough to buy their own vehicles, hire additional drivers, and expand a network of garages, turning a simple driving simulator into a light economic strategy game as well, in which routes, fleet maintenance, and staff hiring all need to be planned. The vehicle fleet can also be customized both visually and mechanically to personal taste, from the color of the cab to a more powerful engine.

The game's charm lies in the combination of a calm, meditative driving pace, a faithfully rendered network of European roads and cities, and the satisfying feeling of gradually growing your own business. The driving respects the basic physics of a heavy vehicle, so the player has to account for braking distance, body roll while cornering, and fatigue during long night drives. Over the course of its existence, the game has gone through numerous expansions adding further countries and regions, gradually growing the map to cover most of Europe and offering faithfully depicted highways, border crossings, and the typical architecture of individual countries. The multiplayer mode also lets players meet each other on virtual roads and share the same stretch of asphalt together, whether as fellow travelers or just random passers-by. The ambient radio soundtrack, engine sound, and changing weather and time of day create an atmosphere that can calm the player much like an actual long journey.

Euro Truck Simulator 2, from the Czech studio SCS Software, unexpectedly became a phenomenon even beyond the circle of simulator fans, a popular streamed title, and proof that even a seemingly mundane activity can be tremendously addictive and relaxing in a game, whether the player treats it as a challenge or as a digital counterpart to a long walk.
pc-modern__euro-truck-simulator-2.teaser: Seemingly modest truck driving across Europe that turns into an absorbing transport business.

pc-modern__hidden-and-dangerous-2.article:
**Hidden & Dangerous 2**, from 2003, is a tactical action game set during the Second World War, in which the player commands a small commando team operating behind enemy lines. Between missions, the player can switch control between up to four soldiers, each with their own equipment and role, ranging from sniper through demolition expert to a heavily armed machine gunner, which calls for careful planning of the advance rather than frontal assaults. The player can give basic orders to their squadmates and split them into smaller groups in order to cover several directions of attack at once, turning individual missions into small tactical puzzles rather than straightforward firefights.

The missions take the player across several battlefields of the Second World War, from the European countryside to more distant fronts, combining stealthy infiltration, sabotage, and firefights, and the game rewards patience and the use of terrain cover over reckless shooting. A shortage of ammunition and limited equipment force the player to approach combat cautiously and not waste rounds on targets that can be avoided. The graphical rendering of the landscape and battlefield was solid for its time and helped convey the harsh atmosphere of wartime conflict, reinforced by the fact that characters can easily be wounded or killed and must be given first aid during combat. The game builds on the successful first installment from 1999 and expands its concept with more modern presentation, a more elaborate environment, and smoother squad control, making tactical decision-making more accessible without the game losing its demanding nature.

Hidden & Dangerous 2, from the Czech studio Illusion Softworks, ranks among the respected representatives of the tactical war game genre, and thanks to its demanding nature and emphasis on realistic tactical approaches, it still maintains a circle of loyal fans even years later who appreciate that the game never slips into simplistic action solutions.
pc-modern__hidden-and-dangerous-2.teaser: Up to four soldiers, each with their own role - sniper, demolitions, machine gunner; tactics over assault.

pc-modern__space-engineers.teaser: A block-based space building game with honest physics; blocks can be controlled with your own scripts.
pc-modern__space-engineers.article:
**Space Engineers** is a space construction simulation from Keen Software House, a Czech development team founded by Marek Rosa. The game put a block-based building kit into players' hands, letting them build their own spaceship, mining base, or entire orbital station, all with honestly simulated physics of mass, engine thrust, and structural integrity. It is not just a creative toy - the game also offers a survival mode, where you need to mine ores, smelt them, and build increasingly complex machines, all while facing potential shortages of oxygen or power. Particular attention was earned by the so-called programmable blocks, which can be controlled with the player's own scripts, turning the game into a popular tool for experimenting with automation and simple machine logic.

On PC the game runs on its own VRAGE engine, which handles destruction and physics in real time across a huge number of blocks, which was technically ambitious at the time of release and remains demanding on hardware to this day. The atmosphere is rounded out by quiet space music and sounds that emphasize the loneliness of open space, where the only sound is often the hum of your own ship. Space Engineers gradually built up a loyal community of builders and modders, who created thousands of workshop creations for the game, from replicas of real rockets to fantasy cruisers. The game also supports multiplayer and dedicated servers, on which entire cooperative economies and survival scenarios emerge, and later added support for virtual reality, letting players explore their own creations from a first-person perspective with a much stronger sense of scale.

The game spent a long time in Early Access, which allowed the studio to listen to the community and gradually improve the building system before it reached its full release form. Today Space Engineers is considered one of the most complete building simulations of the genre and has inspired a number of other titles built around block construction, from smaller indie projects to more ambitious sci-fi sandboxes. The studio supported the game long-term with paid expansions adding new planets and technologies, and even years after release it remains actively played thanks to mods and regular updates.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its elaborate building system and long-term support through mods and paid expansions, Space Engineers remains to this day one of the most complete building simulations of the genre.

pc-modern__medieval-engineers.teaser: Space Engineers' sister title set in the Middle Ages; castles and catapults with proper collapse physics.
pc-modern__medieval-engineers.article:
**Medieval Engineers** is a construction simulation from Keen Software House, a sister title to Space Engineers that transplants the same block-building principle from the sci-fi setting of space into a medieval environment. The player builds castles, catapults, bridges, and mills out of individual blocks and must respect the physics of weight, material strength, and structural load - a poorly designed tower can collapse just as it would in reality. The game also works with deformable terrain, so you can dig trenches, mine stone from a quarry, or level a path for building fortifications, which sets it apart from many other construction titles.

The game runs on a modified version of the VRAGE engine and builds technically on the experience gained developing Space Engineers, including destruction physics and simulation of moving mechanisms such as water wheels, treadmills, or drawbridges. The visual style is warmer and more down-to-earth than its sci-fi predecessor, with an emphasis on wood, stone, and blacksmithing, and the sound design leans toward a calm, folk-inspired atmosphere of village life. However, the game never quite stepped out of the shadow of Space Engineers, and player attention focused mainly on the circle of builders who appreciated the ability to build a functioning medieval village, a water-powered mill, or a siege engine with a realistically simulated impact trajectory.

Unlike its space-set sibling, Medieval Engineers never gained as broad a player base, and development was slower, yet it remained popular among creators who wanted to explore historical construction in a game environment without having to deal with space technology. Keen Software House kept maintaining it with updates, and today the game serves as an interesting example of how a single game system and technological base can be carried over into a completely different thematic setting while preserving the same depth of construction physics.

**Why play it:** For players who want to explore historical construction without space technology, Medieval Engineers offers the same depth of construction physics as its space-set sibling, just with a smaller player base.

pc-modern__mashinky.teaser: A railway building game from a Czech developer, who single-handedly coded a century of transport history.
pc-modern__mashinky.article:
**Mashinky** is a strategic building game about constructing a railway network, programmed single-handedly by Czech developer Jan Zeleny. The player starts with a single steam locomotive and gradually builds tracks, stations, depots, and connects mines and factories to the network in order to get raw materials to buyers as efficiently as possible. As the years pass, more modern locomotives and wagons unlock, from steam engines to electric units, pushing the game across more than a century of railway history and forcing the player to rebuild older lines so they can handle faster and heavier trains. Besides railways, players can also build road transport with trucks and buses, gradually turning the logistics network into a truly multi-layered transport system.

Visually the game relies on a cozy low-poly style with bright colors, which contrasts with a fairly deep economic and logistics core - the player has to deal with track capacity, train routing, crossing tracks, and gradually expanding the network so that no bottlenecks form and trains don't fall behind schedule. The music and train sounds create a calm, meditative atmosphere typical of building strategy games of this type, and players spend a lot of time simply watching a train wind smoothly through the landscape between hills and bridges. Mashinky was especially appreciated by fans of building and transport simulation genres as a smaller but honestly crafted alternative to bigger series like Transport Tycoon or Railway Empire, with its own clearly readable visual language. The game also offers generated maps as well as hand-crafted scenarios, so each player can choose between free-form building and completing predefined challenges with specific goals.

The game spent a long time in Early Access, and even after release its author kept supporting it with further updates, new locomotives, and improvements to the building tools, so the content kept expanding even after reaching the full version. Even today Mashinky is valued as an example that a polished and playable building strategy game can be created by a single independent developer without the backing of a large studio, and thanks to that the game earned respect within the community of train simulation fans around the world.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its elaborate building strategy, created single-handedly by an independent developer, Mashinky has earned respect among fans of train simulations around the world.

pc-modern__someday-you-ll-return.teaser: A dark psychological adventure about searching for a lost daughter in a misty Czech forest.
pc-modern__someday-you-ll-return.article:
**Someday You'll Return** is a psychological adventure from the Czech studio CBE Software, in which the player, as the father Daniel, walks through the dark forest of Soul Mountain while searching for his missing daughter. The game combines exploration of a more open landscape from a first-person perspective with adventure puzzles, gathering supplies for camping, surviving in the forest overnight, and a dialogue system in which the player's past and decisions influence how both characters and the forest itself react to him. Part of the gameplay is also the need to keep basic needs met, such as hunger or warmth at the campfire, which pushes the game closer to a survival adventure. The path through the forest is not straightforward either - the player often has to return to already-visited places as they gradually find new memories and keys to further parts of the story.

The game's atmosphere is carried by a dense, dark, and misty forest full of symbolism and supernatural phenomena, accompanied by oppressive music and sound design that heightens the feeling of anxiety and disorientation, especially during night passages, when the player must rely only on the light of the fire. The game is not afraid to tackle themes such as guilt, addiction, or family breakdown, and tells its story non-linearly through memories, dreams, and beliefs, so the player pieces together the true shape of events gradually. On PC the game benefited from a finely detailed environment and full voiced localization including well-known voices, which represented a fairly demanding and costly project for a smaller Czech studio.

Someday You'll Return appealed mainly to fans of darker, story-focused adventure games and became one of the most visible Czech achievements in the genre of psychological horror with a more open world, one that combines exploration of nature with an intimate family drama. Even years after release it is still referenced as an example of an ambitious smaller production that was not afraid to experiment with narrative form and to uncompromisingly pursue uncomfortable themes.

**Why play it:** For fans of darker, story-focused adventure games, Someday You'll Return offers an uncompromising psychological horror that is not afraid to pursue uncomfortable themes.

pc-modern__chuchel.teaser: An absurd point-and-click comedy from Amanita Design; a chase for a cherry full of slapstick.
pc-modern__chuchel.article:
**CHUCHEL** is a comic point-and-click adventure from Amanita Design in which a hairy black character named Chuchel goes through a series of funny, grotesque minigames to reach the cherry he desperately craves. Each scene is a self-contained puzzle built on absurd humor, exaggerated character expressions and unexpected twists, where the player often just tries clicking on different objects and watching what comical situation it triggers. Chuchel is also constantly hindered by his small rival Kekel, who keeps stealing the cherry from him or otherwise complicating his path, which creates the game's central comic conflict. Their rivalry is further joined by other supporting characters and animals who complicate the situation with further unexpected twists, adding another layer of grotesqueness to the game. The environment in which the game takes place also changes fundamentally with each chapter, from a cozy cottage through bizarre landscapes to entirely abstract scenes.

The game is typical of Amanita Design's signature style - hand-drawn graphics with distinctive, caricatured characters, no spoken or written text, and all storytelling carried purely by facial expressions, sounds and music. The soundtrack, full of crazy melodies and sound effects, underscores the game's slapstick tone, which differs markedly from more contemplative titles like Machinarium or Samorost, and feels more like a farce in the style of old cartoons. CHUCHEL is a deliberately short and lighthearted piece of entertainment, aimed at quick amusement without the need to solve complex logic puzzles, with individual chapters connected by little more than a loose storyline of chasing the cherry.

The game earned its popularity thanks to its unmistakable humor and visual style, which appeals even to players outside the traditional adventure game circle, including children and family audiences. For Amanita Design it was a detour from more serious, atmospheric games toward pure farce, and CHUCHEL became one of the studio's most accessible titles for the widest possible audience, able to entertain even without any knowledge of language.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its unmistakable humor and visual style that's understandable even without knowing the language, this is one of Amanita Design's most accessible games for the whole family.

pc-modern__creaks.teaser: A puzzle platformer about light and shadow; a lamp turns monsters into furniture.
pc-modern__creaks.article:
**Creaks** is a puzzle platformer from Amanita Design in which the main character discovers a mysterious underground world full of shadow creatures behind the wall of his room. When lit up, these beings turn into solid, harmless furniture, but when the light goes out they set off after the player again - and this principle of light and shadow forms the basis of most of the puzzles, where the player must time the lighting of lamps, the moving of furniture and jumps between platforms to get further. New types of creatures and switches are gradually added, forcing the player to combine light and shadow in increasingly elaborate ways. The game progresses through individual chapters, each of which introduces new mechanisms and rules of light and shadow, so the player never feels like the game's principles are repeating without progression. The controls remain simple and intuitive throughout, making the game accessible even to players with little experience with puzzle platformers.

Visually, the game combines a dark, painterly environment with strong color accents and characters reminiscent of the studio's classic adventure-game art, just shifted into platformer mechanics with fluid animation and full background parallax. The music and sound design create a mysterious, dreamlike atmosphere of an underground labyrinth, where silence alternates with creaking wood and the footsteps of shadow creatures, and the player moves the entire time along the edge between fairy-tale coziness and quiet tension. The difficulty of the puzzles gradually increases as the game introduces new types of furniture and mechanisms, without unnecessarily overwhelming the player with explanations or text.

Creaks built on Amanita Design's reputation as a studio with a distinctive visual style and clever but never frustrating puzzles that respect the player's pace. The game showed that the shift from a classic adventure to a platformer suits the studio well, and became another example of how atmosphere, visual style and game mechanics can be fused into one indivisible whole, without one element pulling away from another.

**Why play it:** For players who love clever but never frustrating puzzles set in a strong visual atmosphere, Creaks shows that Amanita Design's adventure-game style works brilliantly in a platformer too.

pc-modern__happy-game.teaser: A cheerful childhood dream that quickly twists into a bizarre nightmare.
pc-modern__happy-game.article:
**Happy Game** is a dark surrealist adventure from Amanita Design that seemingly starts out as a cheerful childhood dream before quickly plunging into a disturbing nightmare full of bizarre creatures and unpleasant imagery. The player moves through a dreamlike landscape made up of grotesque, often disturbingly overgrown heads, teeth and other bodily motifs, solving simple point-and-click puzzles that allow progress through this strange world. The interactions are deliberately simple and direct, so all of the player's attention is focused on what's currently happening on screen rather than on mechanical complexity. Transitions between individual scenes are smooth and often unpredictable, so the player is never sure what strange scene will appear around the next corner.

The contrast between the seemingly playful, colorful graphics and their genuinely nerve-wracking content is the game's main asset - Happy Game toys with the expectation that a game from a studio known mainly for contemplative titles like Machinarium or Samorost will again be pleasant, and instead offers an unpleasant, at times oppressive experience. The sound design and music deepen the sense of anxiety without the game reaching for a classic horror jumpscare - the tension is more atmospheric and psychological, built slowly through recurring motifs and deformed shapes. The short playtime, meanwhile, allows the entire unpleasant experience to be completed in one closed sitting, which only heightens the feeling of a dark dream from which the player eventually wakes up.

Happy Game divided players thanks to its uncompromising style and its willingness to go against the pleasant expectations Amanita Design had built up with its previous games. Even so, it is valued as a bold artistic experiment that shows a point-and-click adventure can also work as a tool for evoking genuinely strong and unpleasant emotions, and that even an established studio isn't afraid to abandon its own safe, beloved tone.

**Why play it:** If you're after a bold artistic experiment that goes against pleasant expectations, Happy Game proves that a point-and-click adventure can evoke genuinely unpleasant emotions too.

pc-modern__attentat-1942.teaser: An educational adventure about the assassination of Heydrich; digging through family history under the Protectorate.
pc-modern__attentat-1942.article:
**Attentat 1942** is an educational adventure from Charles Games, a studio founded at Charles University, which takes the player into a family history set during the Nazi occupation and the assassination of Reinhard Heydrich. As the grandson, the player investigates his grandfather's fate during the Second World War, and through interviews with witnesses, documents and period records gradually uncovers what actually happened to him at the time, and why he preferred never to talk about certain parts of his life; individual chapters take place in different periods of the occupation and complement one another so that the resulting picture of the family history makes sense as a whole. The player moves between the present, where they conduct interviews with living witnesses, and the past, which they experience through flashback sequences.

The game combines drawn graphics and animated sequences with real documentary footage and testimonies from actual witnesses, blurring the line between game and historical document. Mechanically it's an adventure with dialogue trees and puzzles built on connecting information, where the player pieces together the mosaic of the past from fragments of memories that the characters often remember differently or incompletely, and must judge for themselves which version of the story to believe. The game's tone is serious and sensitive, without unnecessary dramatization, emphasizing how historical trauma affects the generations of descendants and how difficult it is to retroactively reconstruct the truth about one's own family.

Attentat 1942 was praised precisely for connecting the game format with genuine historical education, and became a resource used even in schools, where it served as a supplement to teaching about the occupation period. For Charles Games it was their first major project to show that a game can serve as a fully-fledged tool of historical memory, and it opened the way to their further historical titles focused on sensitive periods of Czechoslovak history, a direction the studio continued to pursue in later years.

**Why play it:** For anyone interested in history, and as a supplement to teaching, Attentat 1942 offers a game as a fully-fledged tool of historical memory, which is why it's genuinely used in schools.

pc-modern__svoboda-1945-liberation.teaser: A sequel to Attentat 1942; conflicting memories of the war's end in postwar Czechoslovakia.
pc-modern__svoboda-1945-liberation.article:
**Svoboda 1945: Liberation** is an adventure game from Charles Games that follows on from Attentat 1942 and moves the player to a small Czechoslovak town at the end of the Second World War and in the first postwar years. Playing a present-day character, the player explores the town residents' memories of the liberation, the postwar expulsion of the German population and the arrival of the new regime; different witnesses remember the same events differently and often contradictorily, so their testimonies must be compared and their agreements and discrepancies sought out, which in themselves say something about the character of the narrator and about how people come to terms with a difficult era, or instead push it out of their own memory.

The game again combines drawn graphics with documentary materials and real testimonies, but this time works with an even more open narrative structure, where the player themselves pieces together whose version of the story is more plausible, without the game clearly hinting at a single, unambiguous truth. Mechanically it's a classic dialogue-driven adventure with an emphasis on listening to and comparing testimonies, without action elements or classic logic puzzles, which keeps the focus mainly on the content of the stories rather than on gameplay challenges. The atmosphere is completed by sensitive, subdued music and authentic period photographs and recordings, which give the game documentary weight and remind the player that this is a real historical period.

Svoboda 1945: Liberation continues Charles Games' line of educational games and again shows how sensitive chapters of national history can be handled in interactive form without simplifying them into clear heroes and villains. The game is particularly valued for how it manages to show the many layers of the postwar period, when the line between victim and perpetrator wasn't always clear, and how strongly the emotions of the time influenced the decisions of ordinary people at a moment when the entire society around them was suddenly changing.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its sensitive, unsimplified treatment of the postwar period without clear heroes and villains, this is a valuable probe into a morally ambiguous chapter of Czechoslovak history.

pc-modern__kingdom-come-deliverance-ii.teaser: Warhorse's sprawling RPG; Henry continues his journey through a historically faithful 15th-century Bohemia.
pc-modern__kingdom-come-deliverance-ii.article:
**Kingdom Come: Deliverance II** is an open-world action RPG from Warhorse Studios that continues the story of Henry of Skalitz in a historically faithful reconstruction of early 15th-century Bohemia. The game expands the world of the first installment with new regions, more elaborate melee combat, deeper RPG skill systems and a broader network of side quests that react to the player's decisions and reputation among the inhabitants of individual villages and towns. Henry, meanwhile, continues to move on from being an inexperienced young man toward a hardened fighter caught up in political intrigue amid the Hussite unrest.

Warhorse Studios once again emphasizes historical authenticity - period clothing, architecture, crafts and combat methods are drawn from historical sources, which sets the game apart from most fantasy medieval RPGs and gives it an almost documentary approach to history. Technically, on PC the game offers significantly improved graphics, a denser and livelier world with NPCs who have their own daily rhythm and react to the player's clothing and cleanliness, and a more elaborate combat system using directional strikes, blocking and combinations of melee and ranged weapons. The music draws on a similarly historicizing aesthetic as the first game and rounds out the atmosphere of the early Renaissance amid wartime events, between burned-out villages and bustling marketplaces. Like the first game, it builds on crafts, alchemy, cooking and other side activities that give the world the feeling of a truly lived-in medieval countryside, not just a backdrop for combat.

Kingdom Come: Deliverance II built on the good reputation of the first installment and expanded its fan base thanks to an improved, more accessible yet still demanding system of play that retains a realistic approach to combat and survival. The game ranks among the most significant Czech game projects and is considered one of the most ambitious returns to a realistic historical RPG on PC, one that managed to further expand the scope and craftsmanship of the first game.

**Why play it:** For fans of realistic historical RPGs, Kingdom Come: Deliverance II represents one of the most ambitious Czech game projects, one that further expanded the scope and craftsmanship of the first installment.

pc-modern__euro-truck-simulator.teaser: A calm trucking simulator of European highways; the foundation of SCS Software's whole series.
pc-modern__euro-truck-simulator.article:
**Euro Truck Simulator** is a long-haul trucking simulator from SCS Software in which the player, as a truck driver, hauls freight between European cities, earns money, buys new trucks and gradually builds up their own trucking company with hired drivers. The game focuses on calm, realistic driving along highways and roads, with the player having to monitor driver fatigue, vehicle condition, fuel and traffic regulations, and deliver cargo on time to maintain a good reputation with clients and be able to accept more lucrative and demanding routes.

On PC, the game offered a simplified but fairly faithful map of Western Europe with recognizable cities and a road network, accompanied by models of several truck brands that the player could gradually buy and customize. The soundtrack consists mainly of ambient radio and engine noise, underscoring the meditative, calming pace of play without the time pressure typical of racing games, and the driving itself feels more relaxing than adrenaline-fueled, which won the game players who otherwise don't seek out racing or action games at all. Euro Truck Simulator was SCS Software's first major entry into the truck simulator genre after previously making similar games focused on other regions and smaller budgets, and so it focused on a simpler, more accessible driving model than harder-edged, competing professional simulators.

The game laid the foundations for a successful series and a style that SCS Software later developed into a much more expansive sequel with a more elaborate driving model and a larger map. Even years later, Euro Truck Simulator is seen as a pioneering title that showed how even a seemingly unexciting activity like driving a truck can, in game form, be engaging, relaxing and surprisingly addictive, even for players who otherwise have no interest in real trucks.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its pioneering standing, it's worth trying even today - the game showed that driving a truck can, in game form, be engaging and relaxing even for players with no interest in real trucks.

pc-modern__american-truck-simulator.teaser: Euro Truck Simulator transplanted to the USA; licensed Kenworth and Peterbilt tractors.
pc-modern__american-truck-simulator.article:
**American Truck Simulator** is a trucking simulator from SCS Software that brings the proven concept of Euro Truck Simulator to the setting of the United States. As a truck driver, the player hauls cargo between American states, builds their own trucking company, hires other drivers, buys garages in multiple cities and gradually expands their fleet with licensed models of American tractor units from brands like Kenworth or Peterbilt, whose distinctive look is unmistakable for American highway hauling and sets it apart at a glance from the European tractor units of the sister series.

The game differs from the European series mainly in the character of the landscape - vast deserts, mountains, canyons and endless highways give the gameplay a different, more open sense of space, accompanied by a different rhythm of traffic regulations, weigh stations and the style of American highways. SCS Software gradually expanded the map with further states through paid expansions, so the game developed over the long term in a way similar to its European predecessor, and the map today covers a significant portion of the continental USA, from the Pacific coast to the central plains. The soundtrack, with radio stations, country music and the calm atmosphere of the highway, continues the series' proven, relaxing tone.

American Truck Simulator built up its own loyal community, partly distinct from the European series, and became further proof that the truck simulator genre has a stable, dedicated audience willing to spend hours on virtual highways just for the feeling of calm and smooth travel through the landscape. For many players, the game became a favorite way to relax after a demanding day, similarly to the European series, just with a different, more open scenery of the American countryside. For SCS Software it was an important step toward international expansion of the brand beyond the European market and toward further cementing its position as the genre leader of truck simulators in general.

**Why play it:** If you're drawn to the more open, varied scenery of the American countryside, American Truck Simulator offers a relaxing experience just as much as the European series, only with its own loyal community.

pc-modern__vietcong-2.teaser: Tactical war action from Pterodon; commanding a squad in the Vietnamese jungle.
pc-modern__vietcong-2.article:
**Vietcong 2** is a tactical war action game from the Czech studio Pterodon, which builds on the success of the first Vietcong and once again puts players into the American army's battles in the Vietnam War. The game follows a rookie who joins a special forces unit, and combines direct shootouts in dense tropical terrain with tactical command of a small squad of soldiers, who can be given basic orders to advance, provide cover, or attack a specific target, letting the player choose between a cautious advance or a more direct assault depending on the situation in the field.

Compared to the first installment, the game simplified some systems toward a more straightforward, action-oriented experience with a more linear mission structure, which earned it mixed reactions from part of the fanbase, who appreciated the predecessor's tactical depth and more open missions. The setting of Vietnamese jungle, villages, and rivers nevertheless remains the atmospheric core of the game, backed by the sound of gunfire, insects, and distant explosions, which creates a tense, claustrophobic atmosphere of combat in dense vegetation, where the enemy is often not seen before they fire, making orientation in the terrain just as important as an accurate aim. The dense vegetation also limits visibility so much that firefights often take place at very short range, which increases the tension and the feeling of vulnerability. The PC version also offered cooperative and multiplayer modes with several maps and game types, which extended the title's lifespan beyond the single-player campaign.

Vietcong 2 didn't achieve quite the same acclaim as the first installment, yet it remains a significant part of Czech war-action game development and proves that Pterodon was able to tackle the theme of the Vietnam War repeatedly and with its own recognizable style, even with less emphasis on tactical freedom. Today the game is seen mainly as a dignified, if less ambitious, sequel to one of the most distinctive Czech game titles of the nineties and early 2000s.

**Why play it:** For fans of the first installment, Vietcong 2 is a dignified, if less ambitious, sequel that proves Pterodon knew how to tackle the theme of the Vietnam War repeatedly with its own style.

pc-modern__arma-3.teaser: A military simulation focused on realism; ballistics, fatigue, and radio chatter instead of action.
pc-modern__arma-3.article:
**Arma 3** is a military simulation from the studio Bohemia Interactive, continuing a long line of games starting with Operation Flashpoint and continuing through Arma 1 and Arma 2. The game puts the player in the role of a soldier in a fictional Mediterranean setting and offers a huge open world that can be traversed on foot, in armored vehicles, on ships, and in airplanes and helicopters. The foundation is a maximum emphasis on realism – ballistics affected by distance and wind, long-range visibility, fatigue, injuries, and tactics are much closer to military training than to an action shooter, and the player has to learn to work with a map, compass, azimuth, and radio communication between squad members.

The campaign follows a fictional conflict on the islands of Altis and Stratis, but Arma 3's greatest strength lies in its mission editor and its huge modding community, which to this day creates extensive multiplayer scenarios, new maps, vehicles, and entire game mods – the best-known derivative project is the survival game DayZ, alongside dozens of other community modes such as Zeus, King of the Hill, or extensive roleplay mods. The sound is detailed down to the last nuance, gunshots and explosions sound different depending on distance and environment, the music is rather ambient and subordinate to the atmosphere of endless fields, forests, and abandoned villages, which makes the game feel raw and believable even after hours of play.

At release, Arma 3 earned recognition as one of the most ambitious military simulations on PC and to this day remains a genre standard thanks to regular expansions, paid and community DLC, and an active player base that regularly gathers for large organized operations. For players looking for arcade action, it can be demanding and inaccessible, with a long learning curve for the basic mechanics, but for fans of realistic tactics it remains one of the deepest experiences PC has to offer, and its influence can be seen in a number of later military simulators and battle royale titles.

**Why play it:** For fans of realistic military tactics, Arma 3 remains one of the deepest experiences PC has to offer, even though newcomers face a steep learning curve compared to arcade shooters.

pc-modern__dayz.teaser: Originally an Arma 2 mod that kicked off the survival genre; permanent death and mutual distrust.
pc-modern__dayz.article:
**DayZ** originally emerged as a mod for Arma 2 and became one of the catalysts that launched the entire genre of open-world survival games. The standalone version by Bohemia Interactive places the player on the vast post-apocalyptic island of Chernarus, overrun by the infected as well as other survivors, where one must search for food, water, weapons, clothing, and medical supplies while also dealing with injuries, fractures, illnesses, or dehydration through an elaborate health system. The most distinctive feature is permanent death and an uncompromising approach to other players – meeting a stranger can end in cooperation for survival, but just as often in betrayal, an ambush, or a sudden firefight over meager supplies.

The game spent a long time in early access, gradually replacing its engine, animations, and looting, building, and hunting mechanics, which led the community to alternate between patience and repeated frustration until the game reached a full release as a standalone title separate from Arma 2. The atmosphere is completed by a quiet, inhospitable landscape, changeable weather, the alternation of day and night, forest sounds, and the tension of not knowing who is hiding behind the next hill or in an abandoned building – the music is minimalist, and the game relies mainly on silence, footsteps, and ambient sound effects that deepen the feeling of constant threat and loneliness in an inhospitable land.

DayZ fundamentally influenced the battle royale genre as well as survival games in general and inspired dozens of other titles that adopted its system of looting, hunger, illness, and permanent death, from PUBG to a number of smaller sandbox games. Even after years, it remains unique in its rawness and the unpredictability of multiplayer encounters, where you can rely only on your own judgment and vigilance, even though compared to more modern competition it can feel mechanically clunkier and less polished in places. For many players it remains a memory of a time when meeting a stranger on a server was a genuine source of tension, not just a game statistic, and when the uncertainty of how the other side would act formed the very core of the experience.

**Why play it:** Because of its raw and unpredictable multiplayer experience, where everything depends on your own vigilance, DayZ remains unique even after all these years, even though it feels mechanically clunkier than more modern competition.

pc-modern__pilgrims.teaser: A wordless point-and-click adventure from Amanita Design; cards offer more than one way to solve things.
pc-modern__pilgrims.article:
**Pilgrims** is a short point-and-click adventure from the studio Amanita Design, the creators of Machinarium and Samorost, built on their tried-and-true style of hand-drawn worlds and puzzle-solving without a single word of text. The player accompanies a small wandering character who, on a journey through a land full of strange creatures and situations, meets a number of characters – from a lost knight to peculiar animals – and must help them or outwit them in order to move on. The most distinctive feature is a card-based system of options, where the player chooses from several cards with items or actions, and the same situation can often be resolved in several different, often funny and surprising ways, which invites repeated exploration.

The visual style is typically Amanita – illustrated, colorful, and playful, complemented by gentle music and precisely timed sound effects that build a fairy-tale-like, slightly absurd atmosphere without a single written word. Thanks to its short length, simple mouse-only controls, and the absence of a language barrier, the game is accessible even to players with no experience with classic adventure games, and it works as a smaller, experimental project among the studio's larger titles, meant more for a single sitting than for long-term play.

Pilgrims was received as a charming, funny little piece that shows Amanita Design can offer inventive gameplay and distinctive humor even in a small format and with limited resources, without losing quality. It still serves today as a pleasant, undemanding introduction to the studio's style for new players and confirms the reputation of Czech indie development as one of the most creative and recognizable in Europe. The game also shows how, even with minimal resources and a short runtime, one can build a memorable world with its own characters and rules, without the player feeling that anything is missing. The short runtime thus paradoxically works as an advantage, since it forces the creators to concentrate every idea into a single, well-executed scene.

**Why play it:** If you're looking for an undemanding and funny introduction to Amanita Design's style, Pilgrims, despite its short runtime, offers a memorable world where every idea is concentrated into one well-executed scene.

pc-modern__chaser.teaser: A sci-fi shooter with memory lapses; an unexpected detour into World War II.
pc-modern__chaser.article:
**Chaser** is an action shooter from 2003 by the Slovak studio Cauldron, which takes the player into a sci-fi future where the main character, suffering from memory loss, gradually learns the truth about his origins amid a large-scale conflict between powerful corporations and resistance factions fighting for independence. The gameplay combines classic corridor-based shooting with a fairly wide range of weapons and environments, which shift throughout the game between industrial complexes, futuristic cities, and exotic locations, including an unexpected and inventive detour into the past during World War II, where the hero relives memories tied to his own identity.

The game relied on a cinematic narrative style with cutscenes, voiced dialogue, and a fairly branching story, which at the time of release set it apart from a number of competing shooters focused purely on action without deeper context. Technically, it was a solidly crafted title with detailed environments for its time and varied locations; the music accompanied the action sequences with dynamic tracks, while the quieter, exploratory sections built on a tense, mysterious atmosphere of uncovering the hero's past.

Chaser didn't achieve the same acclaim as its big foreign competitors and remained a rather marginal title on the international scale, but among players in Central Europe it is still remembered as a quality homegrown effort that showed a Slovak development team could hold its own against the action blockbusters of its time. It remains an interesting reminder of a period when the region established itself as a respected source of quality FPS titles with the ambition to tell a real story. The game also tried to tie its individual chapters into a meaningful whole, in which the player gradually understands why the main character is passing through these particular places and memories. In its time, Chaser was one of the few homegrown projects that dared to be compared with big-budget foreign shooters in terms of both storytelling and scope.

**Why play it:** For fans of retro shooters, it's a reminder of a time when a Slovak team managed to hold its own alongside big foreign competitors with a well-thought-out story.

pc-modern__ufo-aftermath.teaser: A turn-based strategy game carrying on X-COM's legacy; fighting an alien invasion for humanity's remains.
pc-modern__ufo-aftermath.article:
**UFO: Aftermath** is a turn-based strategy game from 2003 by the Czech studio ALTAR Interactive, which pays homage to the legacy of the classic X-COM and transposes its concept into its own world, whose humanity has been nearly wiped out by an alien invasion and a mutagenic virus. The player commands a group of surviving fighters who, on turn-based maps full of ruined cities and wilderness, fight mutated creatures and alien forces, while at the strategic level building and expanding bases, researching new technologies and weapons, and deciding how to divide noticeably limited resources between defense, research, and saving the remnants of humanity.

The game retains the tense, uncompromising tone of its predecessor – losing a unit is permanent, and a bad decision on the strategic map can mean a slow, hard-to-reverse decline of the entire campaign and the loss of key bases. The graphics were functional and clear for their time, focused mainly on the readability of the battlefield and the individual enemy types, and the music accompanied the rather grim, post-apocalyptic atmosphere of a ravaged, feral Earth without a single safe place.

UFO: Aftermath became the first installment of a loose trilogy continued by UFO: Aftershock and UFO: Afterlight, and among fans of turn-based strategy it earned a reputation as a dignified, if less polished and less finely tuned, successor to the X-COM series. To this day it is valued as one of the most ambitious Czech attempts to revive the genre at a time when it was rather marginal in the main gaming market's interest among major publishers. The series also differed from classic X-COM in its emphasis on the story behind the invasion and the gradual revelation of the enemy's origin, which gave players motivation to keep pushing through the campaign despite its difficulty. The game also demanded careful expedition planning from the player, since a shortage of fuel, ammunition, or medicine could easily ruin even a well-progressed campaign. It was precisely this uncompromising resource management that gave the game its tension even outside the turn-based battles themselves and set it apart from simpler strategy games of its time.

**Why play it:** For fans of turn-based strategy and the X-COM legacy, it offers demanding expedition planning and a compelling story about an invasion, albeit with less polished execution than the legendary original.

pc-modern__vaporum.teaser: A grid-based dungeon crawler; mechanical puzzles inside an abandoned steampunk tower.
pc-modern__vaporum.article:
**Vaporum** is a dungeon crawler from 2017 by the Czech studio Fatbot Games, which puts the player in the role of a nameless character waking up on a beach in front of a huge, abandoned steam-powered tower in the middle of the ocean, into which they must venture to find out what happened to them. The game takes place in first-person perspective on a square grid, where the player moves room by room, solves mechanical puzzles involving levers, elevators, and pressure plates, collects equipment, and fights robots and other creatures using a system of weapons and implants that can be gradually upgraded and combined throughout the game according to one's own strategy.

The steampunk aesthetic of the tower, combining metal, steam, gears, and electrical devices, gives the game a distinctive and consistent visual style that clearly sets it apart from the typical fantasy setting of most dungeon crawlers. The puzzles require careful examination of the environment and searching for hidden switches and working with mechanisms, while the turn-based combat system relies on tactical movement across the grid, retreating, flanking the enemy, and correctly timing attacks and the use of special abilities.

Vaporum was received favorably as a carefully crafted, honest return to the classic style of dungeon crawlers, one whose atmosphere and design managed to appeal even to players outside the genre's narrow fanbase. Thanks to it, the studio Fatbot Games built a reputation as a creator of quality, atmospheric games with a distinctive visual signature of their own, and later built on that success with further installments set in the same world. The story of the tower and its mysterious owner is pieced together gradually by the player from diaries, notes, and found items, which gives even a purely mechanical game a sense of progress and discovery. The absence of any randomly generated environments also allowed the creators to carefully design each room so that both the puzzle and the combat within it made sense and built on the player's previous experience.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for an honest, carefully designed dungeon crawler without randomly generated levels and with the captivating atmosphere of a steampunk tower will find a genre benchmark here.

pc-modern__ylands.teaser: A colorful sandbox alternative to Arma and DayZ; building and exploring tropical islands.
pc-modern__ylands.article:
**Ylands** is a sandbox building and adventure game from Bohemia Interactive, offering a markedly more colorful, friendlier, and more accessible alternative to their military simulations like Arma or DayZ. Players find themselves on procedurally generated tropical islands, where they can build houses and ships, mine raw materials, hunt and fish, sail the seas, explore underwater caves and ancient ruins full of puzzles, or use extensive built-in tools to create their own scenarios, missions, and minigames, which can then be shared with other players directly within the game.

The visual style is stylized, brightly colored, and simpler in shape, which deliberately sets the game apart from the realistic look of Arma or DayZ, even though it runs on a similar, further modified technology developed by the studio. The emphasis is on creativity, experimentation, and learning – the editor allows players to build their own islands, puzzles, quests, and entire game mods using visual scripting without any need for programming, which brings the game closer to a creative platform than a classic survival title.

Thanks to its accessibility and safer, less bloody tone, Ylands has also found use in education and among younger players, while building a smaller but loyal community of content creators who appreciated the flexibility of the editor compared to the studio's complex simulations. For Bohemia Interactive, it represents a successful step outside the military genre and a demonstration that the studio can offer a more family-friendly, more creative, and more accessible experience for a wider audience alongside its raw simulations. The game also allows hosting your own server and playing in a small group of friends, which makes it a popular choice for family or casual play without having to deal with complex setup. The developers have also long supported community creation through a workshop, thanks to which hundreds of maps and scenarios made by the players themselves have gradually appeared in the game, ranging from simple puzzles to extensive adventures.

**Why play it:** For families and small groups of friends drawn to a creative and safe sandbox without Bohemia Interactive's usual raw military tone, easy self-hosting of your own server is a major plus.

pc-modern__arma-armed-assault.teaser: The direct successor to Operation Flashpoint; the island of Sahrani, where a single bullet decides life.
pc-modern__arma-armed-assault.article:
**Arma: Armed Assault** is a military simulation from Bohemia Interactive and the direct successor to Operation Flashpoint, the game that made the studio's name. Because of a trademark dispute with publisher Codemasters, the studio couldn't use the original name, so the new Arma series was born — one that still follows the same philosophy: a huge open island, complete freedom of movement, and combat where a single bullet means the end. The player lands on the fictional archipelago of Sahrani in the middle of a conflict between north and south, gradually taking on the roles of infantryman, tank commander, pilot, and guerrilla leader.

Compared to Flashpoint, the new engine brought considerably longer view distances, more detailed terrain, and far more elaborate ballistics — at long range you have to account for bullet drop and aim above the target. The controls remained demanding, and the game still holds a reputation as a title that forgives nothing: the health system distinguishes injuries by limb, vehicles have realistic inertia, and you navigate by map and compass bearing rather than an on-screen arrow. Alongside the campaign, the game offered a mission editor that let anyone build their own battle within minutes, and it was this editor that kept Arma alive long after release — the community around it produced thousands of missions, mods, and new maps.

At launch the game suffered from unpolished performance and bugs that Bohemia fixed in later patches and the Queen's Gambit expansion, so reviews were mixed. In hindsight, though, Armed Assault is an important link in the chain — a technical bridge between Operation Flashpoint and the far more polished Arma 2, on which the studio tested out the Real Virtuality 2 engine and the format of an open military sandbox. For fans of the series it's a title played mostly out of historical interest, but its influence on the current shape of Arma 3, and on the whole Czech games scene, is impossible to overlook.

**Why play it:** With its unpolished performance and bugs, it mainly makes sense for fans interested in the series' history — as the technical bridge between Operation Flashpoint and the more polished Arma 2.

pc-modern__witcher.teaser: A mature RPG based on Sapkowski's books; Geralt faces choices with no purely good option and delayed consequences.
pc-modern__witcher.article:
