Both critically and commercially, the game was well received and is often referred to as the spiritual predecessor of Red Dead Redemption, even though the development history of the two games differs and it was originally developed by a different studio than the one that ultimately finished the project under the Rockstar banner. Today, Red Dead Revolver is interesting mainly for fans of the series who want to see where some of its iconic mechanics came from, and even after all these years it still offers functional, enjoyable action with a distinctive style that holds back from a modern open-world approach and focuses on straightforward fun.

**Why play:** Fans of the Red Dead series will enjoy the look at the roots of its iconic mechanics, and even after all these years it offers functional, straightforward western action without the ambitions of a modern open world.

xbox__conflict-desert-storm.teaser: A tactical shooter set in the Gulf War; switch between four soldiers, each with their own specialty.
xbox__conflict-desert-storm.article:
**Conflict: Desert Storm** transports the player to the setting of the Gulf War in the early 1990s and offers a tactical shooter from the perspective of a four-member team of elite soldiers. During a mission, the player can switch between the individual squad members, each of whom has their own specialty – sniper, heavy machine gunner, demolitions expert, and all-around rifleman. This approach forced players to think about the deployment of forces and make use of each character's strengths while advancing through the terrain.

Missions take place in deserts, urban ruins, and military installations, and place emphasis on taking cover, coordinating fire, and carefully planning each advance, which was relatively unusual for consoles at the time of release – most shooters back then relied mainly on straightforward action. On Xbox, the game could rely on a solid technical execution with decent textures and pleasantly smooth controls that tried to translate the complexity of PC tactical shooters onto a gamepad.

Contemporary reception was mostly positive; the game was praised for the idea of switching between soldiers and for the authenticity of the military setting, although some critics pointed to overly high difficulty and to the behavior of the AI-controlled teammates, who sometimes required more frequent micromanagement than players would expect. Its success led to a number of sequels that further developed the concept of squad tactics in various war conflicts, from Vietnam to more modern battlefields, and cemented the Conflict brand as one of the recognizable military series of its generation.

Today, Conflict: Desert Storm feels like an interesting transitional link between the arcade shooters of the nineties and the later, more elaborate tactical games like Rainbow Six or Ghost Recon. For fans of military shooters with an emphasis on teamwork, it remains a pleasant and still playable experience that, even after all these years, can deliver the tension that comes from having to cooperate and carefully plan every advance through military terrain full of lurking enemies.

**Why play:** For fans of team-based military shooters with an emphasis on tactics and cooperation, it remains a playable transitional link today between nineties arcade action and the later Rainbow Six or Ghost Recon.

xbox__bloodrayne.teaser: Half vampire, half human, against Nazi occultists; combat built around draining blood.
xbox__bloodrayne.article:
**BloodRayne** presents one of the most distinctive heroines of action games of its time – Rayne, half vampire, half human, who works for a secret organization fighting supernatural threats and Nazi occultists in the 1940s. The gameplay combines fast melee combat using a pair of blades with the ability to drain enemies' blood, which replenishes health and unlocks a special ability called blood rage, during which Rayne gains a temporary power boost.

The game openly relies on graphic violence and a dark, exploitation-style atmosphere that clearly places it among titles aimed at an adult audience. Environments range from European villages to secret Nazi laboratories, accompanied by darkly atmospheric music that underscores the game's grim overall tone. On Xbox, the game benefited from the console's better performance compared to PlayStation 2, which showed in smoother combat and more detailed character models.

At the time of release, BloodRayne received a mixed but generally favorable reception – critics praised the distinctive design of the main heroine and the stylish action full of flashy moves and combos, while a more common complaint was the repetitive gameplay loop in the later parts of the game and a camera that, in tighter spaces, sometimes cooperated reluctantly with the fast pace of combat. Thanks to this game, the character of Rayne became a recognizable pop-culture brand and inspired not only further game entries but also a film adaptation and a comic book treatment, extending beyond the original gaming medium.

Today, BloodRayne is interesting mainly as an example of bold, stylized action with a dark atmosphere that wasn't afraid to swim against the current of the more family-friendly Xbox titles of the time and target an adult audience craving more graphic violence and a darker story. For fans of action games with horror and occult elements, BloodRayne remains a reminder of a time when smaller studios could still afford to take risks with bold and controversial concepts.

**Why play:** If you like stylized, dark action aimed at an adult audience, BloodRayne still recalls a time when smaller studios could afford to take risks with bold, controversial concepts.

xbox__metal-arms-glitch-in-system.teaser: A shooter starring the robot Glitch in a resistance against the Konstruct army; a varied cast of enemies.
xbox__metal-arms-glitch-in-system.article:
**Metal Arms: Glitch in the System** is a third-person shooter in which the player takes control of a small combat unit named Glitch, who joins a resistance of robots fighting against the tyrannical Konstruct army. The game relies on a carefully designed range of robotic enemies and allies, from small reconnaissance units to massive war machines, with each type requiring a different approach in combat.

One of the game's biggest draws was the ability to take control of enemy robots using a hacking device and temporarily turn them against their own forces, which opened up room for varied tactical combinations in an otherwise fairly classically designed shooter. The level design plays out across varied environments, from factory halls to deserts and underground complexes, while the humorous tone of the dialogue and characters gave the game a light-hearted atmosphere despite fairly intense action.

On Xbox, the game stood out with surprisingly good graphics and smooth performance, which helped it stand apart from the many similarly focused titles. Critical reception was mostly positive; the game was praised for the variety of its robotic opponents, its humor, and solid game mechanics, with some reviewers calling it one of the pleasant surprises of its time precisely because of its combination of action, hacking puzzles, and engaging storytelling. Even so, as a commercially successful title it ultimately didn't break through as much as it deserved, which some attribute to strong competition in the shooter market at the time of its release.

Today, Metal Arms is regarded as one of the underrated gems of the Xbox library, well worth discovering especially for fans of robotic themes and action shooters with a healthy dose of humor. Its legacy survives mainly among collectors and fans who discover the game retroactively and appreciate how well it has held up in terms of playability over the years, even though it never got a proper sequel or reboot.

**Why play:** For fans of robotic themes and action shooters with a healthy dose of humor, it's one of the underrated gems of the Xbox library, one that has kept very solid playability even after all these years.

xbox__advent-rising.teaser: An ambitious sci-fi shooter whose script was co-written by a renowned science fiction author.
xbox__advent-rising.article:
**Advent Rising** is a sci-fi action shooter set in the distant future, when humanity first encounters the alien Aurorans civilization. The player takes on the role of Gideon Wyeth, an ordinary man who, during a catastrophic chain of events, becomes a key figure in a conflict that decides the fate of the entire human race. The game's script was co-written by a renowned science fiction author, which is reflected in its fairly ambitious story and world-building.

The gameplay combines a classic third-person shooter with telekinetic powers that Gideon gradually acquires - the player can throw enemies around, crush them, or use them as projectiles, which adds dynamism to combat beyond simple trigger-pulling. The settings alternate between urban ruins, space stations, and alien complexes, with the game striving for a cinematic feel through an emphasis on music and the direction of individual scenes.

On Xbox, where the game was exclusive for a time, it received a mixed reception - the ambitious script and the telekinetic power system, which allowed for very effective and visually striking combat, were praised, while the technical side, frequent bugs, camera control issues, and an unfinished impression left by some parts of the game, pointing to a troubled and demanding development process, were criticized. Still, the musical score and the attempt at cinematic storytelling were among the things that set the game apart from ordinary shooters of its time.

Nevertheless, Advent Rising gained a certain cult following among fans who appreciate its bold story, expansive sci-fi universe, and atmosphere that tried to feel more like an interactive film than an ordinary shooter. Today the game is interesting mainly as an example of unfulfilled potential, showing how great ambitions often clashed with the realities of game development of its era, and it remains a reminder of a period when Xbox hosted a number of bold, if not always perfectly executed, sci-fi experiments.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its bold sci-fi story and expansive universe, Advent Rising earned a cult following of fans, even though today it serves more as a showcase of the unfulfilled potential of its era's great ambitions.

xbox__tao-feng-fist-of-lotus.teaser: A fighting game from the creators of Killer Instinct, emphasizing authentic martial arts like kung fu.
xbox__tao-feng-fist-of-lotus.article:
**Tao Feng: Fist of the Lotus** is a fighting game created by the team that had previously been behind the acclaimed Killer Instinct, and from the outset it was conceived as an Xbox-exclusive title. The game moves away from the fantastical battles typical of its creators' previous project and instead blends a realistic approach to martial arts, with an emphasis on authentic styles such as kung fu, judo, or capoeira, which the individual characters practice.

One of the game's most distinctive features was its detailed injury system, in which opponents visibly bled during combat, specific body parts swelled, and damage affected their mobility and attack effectiveness - at the time of release, this was a fairly innovative approach to visualizing combat within the fighting game genre. The game thus placed greater emphasis on the tactical use of specific techniques aimed at weakened body parts of the opponent rather than on simple combo attacks.

On Xbox, the game benefited from good technical execution of the character models and arenas, although the broader content and roster of characters were more limited compared to competing fighting games. Critical reception was mixed - the injury system and realistic approach were praised as a refreshing change from exaggerated fighting games with fantastical characters and special attacks, but the overall content, number of arenas, and depth of the game system were rated as below average compared to established genre franchises such as Tekken or Virtua Fighter. As a result, the game remained more of a niche title than a broad commercial success.

Today, Tao Feng is interesting mainly as an example of a bold experiment with realism in a fighting game and as a historical curiosity for fans of Xbox-exclusive titles who appreciate an attempt at a different approach to a genre that was, at the time, heavily dominated by Japanese franchises. For those looking for an unconventional alternative to traditional fighting games, Tao Feng still offers an interesting, if imperfect, experience.

**Why play it:** For fans looking for an unconventional alternative to the era's Japanese fighting games, Tao Feng offers an interesting, if imperfect, experiment with a more realistic take on the genre.

xbox__x-men-legends.teaser: A cooperative action RPG for four players featuring a team of mutants from the X-Men comics.
xbox__x-men-legends.article:
**X-Men Legends** brought a cooperative action RPG to Xbox, in which the player assembles a team of four mutants from a wide roster of characters known from the X-Men comics, from Wolverine and Cyclops to Storm or Iceman, and takes them through an extensive campaign full of battles against the series' classic villains. The game allowed up to four players to progress through the story together, with each controlling a different character with their own unique abilities and combat style.

The game system combined simple but satisfying combat based on combining attacks and special abilities with RPG elements - characters gained experience, leveled up, and acquired new skills and equipment, giving players room to build their own strategy and team specialization. The settings drew on a variety of locations from the comic universe, from the Danger Room at X-Men headquarters to enemy bases, with destructible environments and the ability effects of individual mutants looking quite impressive by the standards of the time.

On Xbox, the game benefited from support for cooperative play and solid technical execution, which allowed multiple characters with special effects to be displayed simultaneously without major issues. The game was very successful both critically and commercially, praised for its enjoyable cooperative play, its faithfulness to the comic source material, and for how well it managed to translate the feeling of building a superhero team into a game form accessible even to players not deeply familiar with X-Men comic mythology. Its success led to sequels and other similarly conceived games from the same studio, making X-Men Legends a founding entry in an entire subgenre of comic-based action RPGs.

Today, X-Men Legends remains a fondly remembered title for fans of comics and cooperative RPG action alike and is often cited as one of the best comic-based titles of its generation. Its legacy is also evident in later games focused on team-based superhero action, and even after all these years it offers an enjoyable way to work through a story full of familiar characters from the Marvel universe with friends.

**Why play it:** For fans of comics and cooperative RPG action alike, X-Men Legends still offers an enjoyable way to work through a story full of familiar Marvel universe characters with friends.

xbox__mortal-kombat-deadly-alliance.teaser: A series reboot in which every character fluidly switches between several fighting styles.
xbox__mortal-kombat-deadly-alliance.article:
**Mortal Kombat: Deadly Alliance** marked a fundamental reboot of the popular fighting series after several installments that took place in 3D environments but did not receive an unambiguously positive reception. The game brought a completely reworked combat system, in which every character has several distinct fighting styles that can be seamlessly switched between during combat, which greatly expanded the tactical options and depth of individual fights.

The game's story introduced an alliance between two iconic series villains, Shang Tsung and Quan Chi, who together forge a plan to conquer all the realms. The game also reintroduced the legendary finishing Fatality moves, supplemented with new Brutalities and other flashy ways to end a fight, which once again became a central draw of the series for its fans. Graphically, the game looked noticeably better on Xbox than previous installments, with more detailed character models and smoother animation.

Contemporary reception was very positive, and the game was generally seen as a return of the series to the quality that had made it famous in the nineties, when it still consisted of two-dimensional fights with a simple but brutally effective execution. Critics praised in particular the new fighting-style system and the return to a grittier, more hardcore atmosphere that appealed to original fans of the series who were tired of the previous 3D experiments. The sound design and musical score also contributed to the grim, mystical atmosphere that had always been typical of Mortal Kombat.

Today, Deadly Alliance is regarded as an important turning point in the history of Mortal Kombat and as a title that laid the foundation for the successful installments of the series that followed. The Xbox version also benefited from the console's performance, which allowed for more detailed character models and smoother animation than on competing platforms, making it the preferred choice for many players to experience this important chapter of the series.

**Why play it:** For fans of the series, this is an important turning point for Mortal Kombat, and the Xbox version additionally benefited from the console's performance, offering more detailed character models and smoother animation than competing platforms.

xbox__mortal-kombat-deception.teaser: Builds on the series reboot with interactive arenas full of deadly traps for opponents.
xbox__mortal-kombat-deception.article:
**Mortal Kombat: Deception** followed up on the series' successful reboot and expanded the combat system with additional elements, including interactive arenas with traps into which opponents could be thrown for flashy and lethal bonus attacks. The story continues from the previous installment and further develops the intrigue surrounding Shang Tsung and his allies, while adding an extensive Konquest mode that guides the player through the fighting universe via free exploration and quest completion.

The game also introduced the unusual mini-games Chess Kombat and Puzzle Kombat, where the series' characters competed in chess strategy and, respectively, in a logic puzzle game inspired by falling-block puzzles - both variants used the characters and their abilities to influence the course of the match. On Xbox, the game also supported online multiplayer via Xbox Live, allowing players to compete in remote matches, which was still a relatively new and valued feature for console fighting games of its time.

Critical reception was mostly positive, with praise given especially to the variety of content, the number of playable characters, and the abundance of side modes that went beyond the classic one-on-one fight and gave players a reason to return to the game outside of matches against friends or the computer. Some critics, on the other hand, complained that the sheer number of modes distracted from the core of the game - the fights themselves - and that not all the experiments worked equally well, with some lacking deeper polish.

Today, Deception is remembered mainly for its experimental side modes and as one of the most ambitious installments of the series in terms of the content it offered. Xbox Live support also made Deception one of the first entries in the series to allow full-fledged remote online combat, foreshadowing the direction fighting games would gradually take in the following years.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its experimental side modes and one of the first full-fledged implementations of Xbox Live support, this is one of the most ambitious and content-rich installments of the series.

xbox__punisher.teaser: A brutal shooter based on the comic; Thomas Jane lent the Punisher both his face and his voice.
xbox__punisher.article:
**The Punisher** is a third-person action shooter based on the Marvel comics antihero of the same name, who, after the murder of his family, embarks on a merciless campaign against the criminal organizations of New York. Lead actor Thomas Jane, who also portrayed the Punisher in the 2004 film adaptation, lent the character his likeness and voice, giving the game a distinct cinematic authenticity.

The gameplay is built on tough, uncompromising action full of shootouts and close-quarters combat, complemented by a controversial interrogation system - the player can question and intimidate captured enemies in various ways to obtain information, and these sequences were among the most discussed and graphically rawest parts of the game. The settings take place in seedy alleyways, warehouses, and criminal dens that faithfully evoke the dark atmosphere of the comic source material.

On Xbox, the game benefited from pleasantly smooth action and honest technical execution, which allowed for a large number of enemies fighting on screen simultaneously. Critical reception was largely positive, with the credibility of the main character, high-quality voice acting, and intensity of the action praised in particular, although the controversial interrogation system also drew criticism regarding the acceptable level of violence in the game and, in some countries, affected its adults-only classification. The criminal neighborhoods and docks were complemented by dark, atmospheric music that underscored the grim, hopeless tone of the entire game.

Today, The Punisher is remembered as one of the rawest and most mature comic-based titles of its generation, unafraid to push right up to the limits of acceptability and thereby distinguish itself from most more family-friendly superhero games. For fans of the character and of grittier action alike, it remains an interesting glimpse into the darker side of the Marvel comic universe, crafted with an eye toward its film counterpart.

**Why play it:** It will appeal to fans of the character and of grittier action alike as one of the rawest and most mature comic-based titles of its generation, crafted with an eye toward its film counterpart.

xbox__return-to-castle-wolfenstein-tides.teaser: A console version of an acclaimed FPS blending World War II with the occult horrors of the Nazis.
xbox__return-to-castle-wolfenstein-tides.article:
**Return to Castle Wolfenstein: Tides of War** is a console version of the acclaimed FPS that revived the Wolfenstein franchise, taking the player back to the period of World War II, where, as United States agent B.J. Blazkowicz, they fight not only the regular German army but also the secret SS Paranormal Division organization experimenting with occult and supernatural powers. The combination of a historical wartime conflict with horror and supernatural elements gave the game a distinctive character that set it apart from ordinary war shooters.

The gameplay offers a classic FPS experience with a varied arsenal of weapons ranging from standard rifles to experimental German technology, with missions taking place in German fortresses, catacombs, and secret laboratories. The Xbox version adapted the controls for a gamepad and adjusted the multiplayer mode to the console's capabilities, while still retaining the team modes known from the original PC version of the game.

Contemporary reception of the console version was solid, although it never quite reached the acclaim given to the original 2001 PC version, which was widely regarded as one of the best shooters of its time and became one of the defining titles of the genre on computers. Critics praised the atmosphere, the variety of weapons, and the variability of missions combining a stealth approach with direct action, while criticizing the minor technical compromises necessary for the console conversion, especially the controls and, at times, a slower frame rate in more demanding scenes.

Today, Tides of War is interesting mainly for players who want to experience the classic Wolfenstein experience directly on Xbox without needing to use a keyboard and mouse. The combination of a historical wartime backdrop with occult and supernatural elements remains a distinctive contribution of the entire franchise and, even after all these years, gives the game a unique atmosphere that sets it apart from most ordinary war shooters.

**Why play it:** For players who want a classic Wolfenstein experience right on Xbox without a keyboard and mouse, Tides of War offers a distinctive atmosphere born from combining a wartime backdrop with occult elements.

xbox__whacked.teaser: An Xbox launch title; a parody of a TV reality show in the form of an arena shooter.
xbox__whacked.article:
**Whacked!** was one of the Xbox's launch titles and offered an unusual combination of an arena shooter and a parody of a TV reality show. Players, taking on the role of colorful contestants, face off in various arenas full of weapons, traps, and power-ups, with the goal being to survive and take down opponents before one of them does it to them instead - the whole concept is wrapped in an ironic presentation of a TV show, complete with a host commenting on the events in the arena.

The game mechanics are built on fast, chaotic battles for up to four players at once, in which characters collect unconventional and often humorous weapons and power-ups that fundamentally alter the course of combat. The arena settings are designed to support vertical movement and quick shifts in tactics, while the humorous tone of the whole presentation, including character animations and voice acting, gives the game a light-hearted atmosphere typical of party games of its era.

On Xbox, the game benefited from fairly solid technical execution and physics that were decent for its time, which suitably complemented its arcade character. Critical reception was mixed to average - the game was praised for its original TV-show concept, colorful characters, and fun multiplayer for several players on one screen, but criticized for its fairly limited depth and repetitive gameplay loop over longer play sessions, which grew stale over time and did not offer enough long-term motivation. Still, as social entertainment for a few players, it found its place among the console's launch titles.

Today, Whacked! is mainly a curiosity of the early Xbox library, a reminder of how varied the console's launch titles were in their effort to appeal to as broad an audience as possible. For fans of arena shooters with a humorous edge and a party focus, Whacked! still offers an interesting look at what a multiplayer entertainment title could look like at the start of the Xbox generation.

**Why play it:** It will appeal to fans of arena shooters with a humorous edge and a party focus as a curiosity of the early Xbox library, showcasing the diversity of the console's launch titles.

xbox__bard-s-tale.teaser: A parody of classic fantasy RPGs full of sarcasm, fourth-wall breaks, and genre clichés.
xbox__bard-s-tale.article:
**The Bard's Tale** is an action RPG from inXile Entertainment that takes its cue from the legendary series of the same name from the eighties, but turns it on its head — instead of serious fantasy, it tells a parody full of sarcasm, fourth-wall breaks, and jabs at classic genre clichés. The hero is a nameless wandering bard, a cynic and opportunist, who is drawn into adventure not by a desire to save the world but by the prospect of a reward and a full purse of gold. The narrator comments on events directly to the player, characters ironically reflect on typical RPG situations, quip about tired fantasy clichés, and the game pokes fun at itself and the entire genre it nonetheless carries with evident affection.

Gameplay combines an action combat system with RPG elements — the player collects weapons, spells, and companions who accompany them on their travels, summons them even from outside the game world directly from other titles, and continuously upgrades the character through a simple but functional experience system. On Xbox, the game benefited from the console's power when displaying larger locations and crowds of enemies, though technically it was no graphical marvel of its generation, and the animations and character models sometimes felt stiff. The audio side is one of the main draws — the narrator, voiced with pronounced detachment and irony, and music parodying fantasy pathos give the title an unmistakable atmosphere that carries the whole game even in moments when the gameplay falters.

Contemporary reception was mixed to positive; the game found fans thanks to its humor and distinctive narrative style, though there were complaints about repetitive gameplay, shorter playtime, and technical shortcomings such as occasional frame drops. Today it is remembered mainly as one of the few genuinely funny RPGs of its time, one that wasn't afraid to parody the very genre it represented, and it inspired later attempts at comedic RPGs. For players looking for a lighter alternative to the serious fantasy epics that dominated at the time, it remains a pleasant curiosity worth rediscovering even years later.

**Why play it:** For players looking for a lighter alternative to the serious fantasy epics of its time, it remains a funny RPG parody of the genre, even though it's accompanied by repetitive gameplay and technical shortcomings.

xbox__champions-of-norrath.teaser: A dense dungeon crawler set in the world of EverQuest for up to four players on one screen.
xbox__champions-of-norrath.article:
**Champions of Norrath** is an action RPG set in the world of EverQuest that, instead of a sprawling MMO, offered a dense dungeon crawler for one to four players. The player chooses from several classes and races, works through a series of dungeons, castles, and caves full of monsters, collects loot, and improves their character in the spirit of classic action RPGs à la Diablo, but with an emphasis on a cooperative experience on a single screen and fast, straightforward combat without unnecessary text detours.

On Xbox, the game benefited from a steady thirty frames per second and a clear isometric camera that could handle even chaotic battles with dozens of enemies and flashy spells at once without the player getting lost in the melee. Cooperative play for up to four players on a single TV was one of the main draws — friends could split the roles of tank, healer, and damage dealer, share treasure, and progress together through the campaign and additional challenges and randomly generated dungeons with extra replayability that players appreciated when returning repeatedly for better loot. The music and dungeon sound effects created a dark, mysterious atmosphere that complemented the endless waves of enemies well and lent even the repeated plundering of the same corridors a certain tense mood.

Critics and players alike received the title very positively, especially for its adept transfer of the hack-and-slash RPG concept to a console at a time when the genre on PC was dominated by the Diablo series and a similar approach was rather the exception on consoles. Champions of Norrath became one of the proofs that action RPGs can also work as relaxed couch co-op fun, and it influenced later console dungeon crawlers that followed, including its own sequel. Even today it's playable as an undemanding, addictive time-waster, especially in the company of friends, when its simple rules and fast pace still work flawlessly and the game plays practically without needing to explain the controls to anyone.

**Why play it:** As an undemanding and addictive couch co-op time-waster, Champions of Norrath still works flawlessly today, thanks to simple rules and a fast pace that don't require explaining anything to anyone.

xbox__champions-of-norrath-return-to-arm.teaser: A sequel to the EverQuest dungeon crawler with deeper crafting and new abilities.
xbox__champions-of-norrath-return-to-arm.article:
**Champions of Norrath: Return to Arms** builds on the successful action RPG set in the world of EverQuest, expanding it with new areas, additional classes and races, and richer multiplayer content. The structure remains the same — players work through dungeons, fight hordes of monsters, and collect ever-better gear — but the sequel adds a deeper crafting system, more elaborate item management, and new special character abilities, bringing the game closer to players craving longer staying power in a world of loot collecting and experimenting with different gear loadouts.

On Xbox, the title supported up to four players on one screen as well as online multiplayer via Xbox Live, a notable step forward compared to its predecessor at the time, allowing cooperative play with friends remotely as well. The visual presentation was only slightly improved over the first game, but speed and smoothness of the action remained a priority, so even in large battles with dozens of opponents at once the game held a stable frame rate without unnecessary slowdown. The atmosphere is rounded out by gloomy music and careful sound design of the underground corridors, caves, and ancient ruins the player passes through while hunting for ever-rarer gear.

Return to Arms was received as a successful expansion of the proven concept, praised especially for its multiplayer options, the depth of its item system, and its wider roster of characters compared to the first game. For fans of the action RPG genre, it represented one of the most comfortable ways to enjoy hack-and-slash fun on console together with friends and online, without the need for complicated setup. It's still remembered today as the pinnacle of the Xbox Champions of Norrath line, partly thanks to its online cooperative play, which was by no means a given for console games of the kind back then and foreshadowed the later boom of online multiplayer on consoles, whether in big action titles or specifically in the action RPG genre.

**Why play it:** For fans of hack-and-slash RPGs, it's the pinnacle of the Xbox Champions of Norrath line, thanks to a richer item system and online cooperative play that wasn't a given on consoles at the time.

xbox__baldur-s-gate-dark-alliance.teaser: An action RPG from the Forgotten Realms; instead of a tactical party, one character and two-player combat.
xbox__baldur-s-gate-dark-alliance.article:
**Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance** brings the famous computer RPG brand into a more action-oriented, console-friendly form set in the world of the Forgotten Realms. Instead of a complex tactical party, the player controls a single character — a fighter, ranger, or sorceress, each with a distinct playstyle — and moves through linear but visually rich locations, from the harbor streets of Baldur's Gate to dark caves, mines, and tombs full of undead and other monsters, with two-player cooperative play on one screen lending the game a social dimension as well.

Gameplay rests on straightforward action combat, collecting weapons, armor, and magic items, and gradually developing the character through experience points and a simple, clear skill tree. The Xbox version benefited from more powerful hardware compared to the original PlayStation 2 version, offering sharper textures, longer draw distances, fewer loading pauses, and smoother action even in larger battles with many enemies on screen. Music drawing on the fantasy tradition of Dungeons & Dragons, the booming sounds of combat, and a dark, gothic setting gave the game an unmistakable atmosphere that appealed both to RPG fans and players who preferred a more action-oriented, straightforward approach without needing to study extensive rule menus.

Dark Alliance was praised at the time for how elegantly it transferred the atmosphere of the Forgotten Realms into an accessible action package, and it helped open the door to an entire wave of console hack-and-slash RPGs in the first half of the decade, including its own sequel. Even years later it remains a gratifying, quickly playable title that appeals to players looking for an undemanding entry point into the world of Dungeons & Dragons without needing to know the complicated rules of the tabletop game or spend hours on character creation, and its cooperative mode remains a pleasant way to enjoy it together with another player.

**Why play it:** For players who want an undemanding entry into the world of Dungeons & Dragons without knowing the complex rules of the tabletop game, Dark Alliance remains a gratifying, quickly playable title with an enjoyable cooperative mode.

xbox__baldur-s-gate-dark-alliance-ii.teaser: A sequel to the Forgotten Realms action RPG with a wider selection of classes, including the necromancer.
xbox__baldur-s-gate-dark-alliance-ii.article:
**Baldur's Gate: Dark Alliance II** expands the concept of an action RPG set in the Forgotten Realms with a larger story, new characters, and a more elaborate combat system. This time the player can choose from a wider selection of classes, including a necromancer who commands summoned skeletons, and travels across more varied environments, from city streets to underground labyrinths, sewers, and exotic regions far from Baldur's Gate, with this installment also supporting two-player play on one screen.

Compared to the first game, the sequel offered a deeper skill tree, more combo attacks, a more elaborate spell system, and the ability to summon companions into battle, making combat feel less repetitive and offering more tactical options. On Xbox, the game used the console's solid technical foundation to smoothly render larger battles and more spectacular spellcasting animations even in moments when dozens of enemies and visual effects roared across the screen at once, without the game noticeably slowing down. The audio side relied on orchestral music underscoring the epic tone of the story and on quality sound design of both combat and environments, which helped convey the feeling of a long, adventurous journey through a vast fantasy world full of danger.

Reviewers praised especially the more mature combat system and a longer, more satisfying campaign compared to the first game, though there were also complaints about occasional monotony in dungeon design, repeating enemy types, and less distinctive side quests. Dark Alliance II is now seen as the pinnacle of this console offshoot of Baldur's Gate and a pleasant retro experience for players who want to experience an action RPG set in the classic world of Dungeons & Dragons without having to deal with the complicated rules of the tabletop original, and its cooperative play ranks among the best the Xbox version has to offer.

**Why play it:** Thanks to a more mature combat system and a longer campaign, Dark Alliance II is the pinnacle of this console offshoot of Baldur's Gate, and its cooperative play ranks among the best the Xbox version has to offer.

xbox__summoner-2.teaser: An action RPG from Volition about a hero who summons powerful beings into battle in a dark fantasy setting.
xbox__summoner-2.article:
**Summoner 2** is an action RPG from Volition, a sequel to the first game set in the dark fantasy world of Orenia. The player takes on the role of a hero with the ability to summon powerful beings into battle alongside themselves and their companions, moves through a vast, to some extent open world, completes quests, develops the character through a skill system, and gradually uncovers an intricate story about power intrigues, ancient forces, and the fate of an entire realm — a story that follows the events of the first game, though it can also be played independently without knowledge of the previous plot.

Compared to its predecessor, the sequel sped up and streamlined the combat system, reduced lengthy transitions between locations, made navigating the world clearer, and placed greater emphasis on real-time action and clearer control of companions in combat. On Xbox, the game benefited from improved performance when rendering larger landscapes, castles, and cities, though even at release it was not among the graphical elite, and some textures, character models, and animations felt somewhat dated. The music and the dark, melancholic atmosphere of the world of Orenia, full of crumbling kingdoms, religious conflicts, and ancient prophecies, remain among the title's strongest elements, as in the first game.

Critics praised the improved accessibility of the gameplay compared to the more complicated and slower first game, as well as the visual presentation of the sprawling locations, though some longtime fans missed the depth and tactical deliberateness of the original game. Summoner 2 today reads as a typical representative of a transitional period, when console action RPGs were trying to find a balance between narrative depth and accessible, faster action, and for fans of the genre it remains an interesting, though today somewhat forgotten, stop in the history of console RPGs, especially for those who enjoy a darker, more mature narrative tone.

**Why play it:** For fans of the genre with a taste for a darker, more mature narrative tone, Summoner 2 remains an interesting, though today somewhat forgotten, stop in the history of console action RPGs.

xbox__gladius.teaser: A turn-based tactics game from LucasArts that trades space for the arenas of ancient Rome.
xbox__gladius.article:
**Gladius** is a turn-based tactical RPG from LucasArts that, instead of the usual space epics associated with the brand, surprisingly took players into the arenas of ancient Rome and the fictional surrounding lands. The player leads a group of gladiators from several different factions, builds and upgrades their own gladiator school, and gradually prepares them for increasingly demanding battles in arenas across the empire, from modest local tournaments to the ultimate contests before the emperor himself.

The combat system is built on turn-based tactics reminiscent of strategic RPGs like Final Fantasy Tactics — each gladiator has their own set of abilities, weapons, and special attacks, which expand, combine, and specialize as the game progresses depending on the chosen playstyle. Managing the school between fights, training individual fighters, their personal development, rivalry among wards, and concern for their morale gave the game a scope beyond mere arena skirmishes and drew the player into the long-term building of an entire team. On Xbox, the game ran smoothly and offered a clear isometric camera, making even larger battles with more participants on both sides legible and easy to follow, while the arena sound effects lent the fights appropriate rawness.

Gladius was praised at the time for its fresh setting of a tactical RPG in the world of Roman arenas, its clear turn-based tactics, and its elaborate system for developing both individual characters and the entire school, which gave individual fights a meaning beyond a single arena bout. Although it wasn't LucasArts' most commercially successful title and the brand never got a sequel, it earned a reputation among fans of turn-based strategy as a quality, well-thought-out game that still appeals today with its fresh theme, solid tactical depth, and the atmosphere of building a gladiator team from scratch — also thanks to the developers not settling for merely repeating the proven formula of other tactical games.

**Why play it:** Fans of turn-based strategy will be drawn in by its fresh setting in Roman arenas, its well-thought-out system for developing characters and the whole school, and the atmosphere of building a gladiator team from scratch.

xbox__broken-sword-sleeping-dragon.teaser: The fourth installment of the classic adventure series abandons 2D drawing for 3D environments and a free camera.
xbox__broken-sword-sleeping-dragon.article:
**Broken Sword: The Sleeping Dragon** brings back the beloved duo of heroes George Stobbart and Nico Collard in the fourth installment of the classic adventure series. Compared to previous entries, it abandons purely hand-drawn 2D graphics in favor of a three-dimensional environment and a freely controllable camera, but retains the traditional adventure framework — exploring locations, collecting and combining items in an inventory, conversations with characters featuring numerous dialogue branches, and solving puzzles built on logic and observation of the surroundings.

The story links an ancient Mayan prophecy about the end of the world with a modern conspiracy plot full of secret societies, and the player travels with the duo of protagonists across several world locations, from Prague to Central America. On Xbox, the adventure's controls were adapted to the gamepad, which, for a genre traditionally tied to mouse and clicking, required some getting used to and brought minor action sequences, sneaking, and simple combat — though the result remained playable on console, if not always as elegant as mouse control. The music and voiced dialogue carry the characteristic humor and lightness for which the Broken Sword series was always known, even though the tone of the fourth installment shifted at times toward more serious and darker territory.

Reviews were mixed — part of the critical reception welcomed the return of the beloved characters and the honest adventure puzzles, while other reviewers criticized the more awkward 3D controls, a less intuitive camera system, a lower pace, and simplified puzzles compared to the previous, purely two-dimensional entries in the series. Nevertheless, The Sleeping Dragon remains an important testament to the fact that the classic point-and-click adventure could find its way onto consoles and adapt to gamepad controls, and fans of the series still rate it today as a dignified, if not flawless, continuation of the beloved brand, especially thanks to the returning duo of main heroes and their chemistry.

**Why play it:** Fans of the series will be delighted by the return of the beloved duo of heroes and their chemistry, though the more awkward 3D controls and simplified puzzles make Sleeping Dragon only a dignified, not flawless, continuation.

xbox__dreamfall-longest-journey.teaser: A sequel to the cult classic The Longest Journey, blending adventure puzzles with action sequences.
xbox__dreamfall-longest-journey.article:
**Dreamfall: The Longest Journey** is an adventure game by Funcom that follows on from the cult PC title The Longest Journey, bringing its story of the parallel worlds of April Ryan and Zoë Castillo into a three-dimensional, more action-oriented form. The player switches perspective between the new heroine Zoë, searching for a missing friend in a near-future world, and the returning April, now living in the magical world of Arcadia, moving through both settings connected by a mysterious gateway between worlds and solving both classic adventure puzzles and simple action and stealth passages.

Compared to its predecessor, the game noticeably scaled back purely cerebral puzzles and item-hunting, adding instead more cinematic storytelling, larger dialogue trees, tailing and stealth sections, and action sequences, which split long-time fans of the original series into two camps. On Xbox, the controls were adapted for the gamepad, and the game benefited from atmospheric, carefully designed environments connecting the futuristic Stark and the magical Arcadia, two starkly different worlds. The musical score and quality voice acting were among the title's strongest points, helping to build the melancholic, thoughtful atmosphere of the whole story and the relationships between characters, whether old friends or protagonists just getting to know each other.

Critics praised the emotional storytelling, well-crafted characters, and audiovisual treatment of both contrasting worlds, while criticism was directed at the unresolved ending, which left questions open for a planned sequel, and at the noticeably reduced share of classic puzzles compared to the first game. Dreamfall remains one of the respected narrative adventures of its generation, and for players interested in story-rich titles it offers a worthwhile, if emotionally demanding and at times unresolved, experience that will be especially appreciated by those who know and love the previous game.

**Why play it:** For players interested in story-rich titles who know and love the previous game, Dreamfall offers an emotional and audiovisually strong, if at times unresolved, narrative experience.

xbox__suffering-ties-that-bind.teaser: A survival horror where the hero can freely switch between human and monstrous form.
xbox__suffering-ties-that-bind.article:
**The Suffering: Ties That Bind** is a survival horror game with stealth-action elements by Surreal Software, continuing the first game and the dark story of prisoner Tory Higgins, accused of murdering his own family. The player once again moves through dark, unsettling environments full of monstrous beings embodying various forms of violence, guilt, and suffering, while the main character can freely switch between human and monstrous form according to their decision and preferred playstyle, whether they favor stealth tactics or direct, brutal confrontation.

The gameplay builds on a combination of firearm shooting, melee combat, sneaking past enemies, and using the special abilities of the monstrous form, complemented by a morality system that reacts to the player's choices and actions throughout the story and gradually affects both its outcome and the behavior of the characters around Tory. On Xbox, the game benefited from dark, atmospheric lighting and thoughtful sound design that effectively underscored the oppressive, claustrophobic mood of the settings, from the abandoned streets of a ruined island city to underground sewers, docks, and prison cells full of traces of past violence. The music and unsettling ambient sounds contributed to the oppressive, disturbing atmosphere typical of the whole series.

Critics praised the dark, unsettling story, moral decision-making with real consequences, and dense atmosphere, though some reviews pointed to repetitive gameplay mechanics carried over from the first game and a similar level structure. Ties That Bind remains one of the respected horror titles of the sixth console generation, unafraid to combine action with a genuinely unsettling psychological undertone, and fans of the genre still value it for its dark atmosphere, unconventional morality system, and the ability to freely switch between the hero's human and monstrous forms.

**Why play it:** It will appeal to genre fans with its dark atmosphere, unconventional morality system, and the ability to freely switch between the hero's human and monstrous forms, despite mechanics repeated from the first game.

xbox__arx-fatalis.teaser: An underground RPG by Arkane Studios where spells are cast by drawing runes directly on the screen.
xbox__arx-fatalis.article:
**Arx Fatalis** is an RPG by Arkane Studios, set entirely in an underground world where humanity retreated after the sun mysteriously stopped shining on the planet's surface. The player moves through intricate caves, mines, temples, and underground cities of various races, including dwarves and goblins, solving puzzles, trading, gathering resources, and developing their character in a first-person view, with spellcasting done by drawing individual runes directly with the mouse or gamepad on screen.

The game places unusually strong emphasis on world simulation - the player can cook food from hunted ingredients, forge their own weapons and armor, distill potions from herbs, or tame an animal companion, and many puzzles and conflicts can be resolved in multiple ways thanks to an open approach to combat, stealth, and dialogue with characters. The Xbox version, released somewhat later following the success of the original PC game, adapted the controls for the gamepad, simplified rune drawing, and offered players without a computer access to this refreshingly original, systemically deep fantasy world, albeit with minor control compromises compared to mouse and keyboard. The dark, oppressive atmosphere of underground corridors, caves, and ancient ruins, heightened by sparse ambient music, was among the game's strongest points and is still considered one of its defining features.

Arx Fatalis was praised above all for its ambitious systemic approach to world simulation and for an atmosphere deliberately reminiscent of genre classics like Ultima Underworld, which the developers openly cited as an inspiration. Although it wasn't a commercial blockbuster, it earned a reputation as a cult favorite among fans of classic RPGs with an emphasis on freedom and systemic depth, and is still remembered today as an early inspiration for Arkane's later, acclaimed work, including the Dishonored and Prey series.

**Why play it:** For lovers of old-school RPGs with an emphasis on systemic depth and freedom of choice, and for Arkane fans who want to discover the early roots of Dishonored and Prey.

xbox__enter-matrix.teaser: An action-adventure made in collaboration with the film's creators, featuring dozens of minutes of new footage.
xbox__enter-matrix.article:
**Enter the Matrix** is an action-adventure by Shiny Entertainment, created in close collaboration with the makers of the Matrix film trilogy and set in parallel with the events of The Matrix Reloaded. The player takes on the role of one of two supporting characters known from the films, Ghost or Niobe, and follows a story that runs alongside the film and adds its own perspective on key events, including dozens of minutes of new footage shot specifically for the game with the trilogy's original cast.

The gameplay combines gunfights with a wide arsenal of weapons, a combat system inspired by martial arts, hacking minigames unlocking bonus content, and stealth passages where the player must avoid guards and security cameras instead of direct confrontation. On Xbox, the game benefited from better performance than the PlayStation 2 version when displaying larger locations and impressive slow-motion action sequences in the spirit of the iconic bullet-time film aesthetic that the film trilogy made famous. The music and sound design drew on the atmosphere of the source films and helped evoke the characteristic, darkly stylized, coldly metallic mood of the digital world of the Matrix as well as its harsh, industrial real-world counterpart.

Contemporary reviews were mixed - the game benefited from the film brand, an extensive weapon arsenal, and new footage with the lead actors, but suffered from clunkier controls, a problematic camera, and uneven pacing between action and stealth passages. Despite these criticisms, Enter the Matrix remains an interesting artifact of its time, showing how the film universe tried to extend its own storytelling into the gaming medium, and for Matrix fans it represents a remarkable, if imperfect, curiosity from the early part of the decade that offers a look at the story from a different angle than the films themselves.

**Why play it:** For Matrix fans who want to experience the story from the perspective of supporting characters in period footage shot directly with the film's actors, despite the clunkier controls and problematic camera.

xbox__need-for-speed-underground.teaser: The series abandoned official circuits for the nighttime tuning scene; an icon of tuning culture.
xbox__need-for-speed-underground.article:
**Need for Speed Underground** marked a fundamental shift in the Need for Speed series - it abandoned official licensed circuits and moved to neon-lit night streets, where races take place in modified tuning cars. The player builds a career from street duels up to prestigious underground races, gradually earning money to buy parts, engines, and above all visual bodywork upgrades. It was precisely this emphasis on a car's looks - neon lights, spoilers, vinyls, and hydraulics - that made the game an icon of tuning culture at the start of the millennium and inspired a whole wave of similar titles. Alongside classic circuit races, the game also offered drift disciplines and direct one-on-one duels, so the player had several racing styles to choose from depending on their mood.

On Xbox, the game ran smoothly, using the console's power to display reflections on car bodies, motion blur at high speed, and dense city traffic that had to be dodged at full speed. The controls were accessible and arcade-like, allowing quick access to drifting and nitro boosts without the player having to master the simulation-level nuances of real vehicle physics. The soundtrack, made up mostly of hip-hop and rock, rounded out the atmosphere of the underground subculture and became, for many players, an inseparable part of the experience, along with the evening lighting of streets full of neon signs.

The game achieved great critical and commercial success, launching a series of sequels that made Need for Speed one of the best-selling racing series of all time. Today, Underground is remembered as a defining moment for the street racing genre, one that influenced later titles like Midnight Club and Juiced and set the visual standard for tuning games for years to come. Even years later, the game remains playable thanks to its energy and clearly readable style, though the graphics and physics naturally show their age and may feel simplified to today's player.

**Why play it:** For fans of street tuning races and nostalgics for the neon aesthetic of the early 2000s, even though the graphics and physics naturally show their age today.

xbox__need-for-speed-underground-2.teaser: Nighttime tuning moved into an open city that can be freely driven through between races.
xbox__need-for-speed-underground-2.article:
**Need for Speed Underground 2** built on the series' successful reboot and expanded the nighttime tuning concept with an open city where the player could freely drive between individual races. Instead of picking events from a menu, it was enough to drive to the relevant spot on the map, which gave the game a sense of a living space and career flow that the previous game's menu-based selection didn't offer. The range of disciplines grew to include drift races, sprints, and night circuits, and the player could modify the car not only visually but also mechanically, through a clearer parts system divided into several performance categories.

The Xbox version benefited from the hardware when rendering the sprawling city with dynamic lighting, rain, and reflections on polished car bodies, which were a direct trademark of the series and gave the night scenery a cinematic touch. The game also offered a vinyl editor, letting players create and share their own decals, which, in an era before internet content was widespread on consoles, was a pleasant bit of variety that extended gameplay. The controls remained arcade-like and accessible, with an emphasis on drifting and nitro, making the game suitable even for less experienced racing game players looking for quick fun. The range of licensed cars expanded, and the player could gradually turn their favorite model into a completely unique machine to their own taste.

Underground 2 was among the commercially most successful entries in the entire series and cemented Need for Speed's position as a synonym for tuning races in the streets of big cities. The open city later became a model for subsequent entries in the series as well as competing titles that tried to offer similar freedom of movement between races. Today the game feels like a typical artifact of the mid-decade, with pronounced visual stylization, an exaggerated neon effect, and a period hip-hop soundtrack that still evokes the atmosphere of the underground tuning scene of that era.

**Why play it:** For the open city, the pronounced neon stylization, and the period hip-hop soundtrack, which still faithfully evoke the atmosphere of the mid-decade tuning scene.

xbox__need-for-speed-most-wanted.teaser: Brought police chases back into the series, making them the core of the entire gameplay.
xbox__need-for-speed-most-wanted.article:
**Need for Speed: Most Wanted** left behind the purely illegal night scene and brought police chases back into the series, making them the core of the whole experience and setting the game apart from previous entries focused mainly on tuning. As the driver, the player tries to fight their way up the ranking of the city's ten most wanted street racers, with every victory bringing increasingly brutal and relentless police pursuits with a higher degree of determination from the law. The chase system, with gradually upgraded police enforcement measures - from patrol cars to helicopters and tightly coordinated roadblocks - was among the best the series has ever offered.

On Xbox, the game ran with an impressive sense of speed, destructible environments, and realistically damaged bodywork, which was still a relative novelty for that console generation and added to the drama of each chase. A storyline shot with live actors between the individual races gave the career a cinematic touch and motivated players to climb the rankings to reach the most powerful and best-equipped rivals. The combination of tuning, arcade driving, and adrenaline-fueled chases created a balanced mix that appealed to both fans of previous entries and entirely new players of the genre. The open city also offered side challenges and hidden shortcuts, discovering which paid off when fleeing an overwhelming number of police cars.

Most Wanted became one of the highest-rated entries in the series and is still considered by many fans to be the peak of Need for Speed before the arrival of a newer console generation and the graphical and gameplay changes that came with it. Police chases defined the game's style so strongly that they became a model for the series' later reboot many years afterward. Even years later, this entry remains a favorite for its energy, excellent soundtrack, and the unforgettable feeling of fleeing justice through the streets of the fictional Rockport.

**Why play it:** For fans of police chases and an energetic atmosphere, thanks to which many players still consider this entry the peak of the entire Need for Speed series.

xbox__midnight-club-ii.teaser: Street racing across three big cities, including motorcycles and one-on-one duels.
xbox__midnight-club-ii.article:
**Midnight Club II** carried the street racing of the first game over into three genuinely inspired big cities - Los Angeles, Paris, and Tokyo - and gave players the freedom to move freely between illegal races, bets, and a one-on-one duel called Battle. Besides cars, motorcycles also returned to the game, which, together with the variety of settings, gave the series a unique character compared to competing tuning games focused solely on automobiles. The player could choose between several game modes, from classic sprints to endurance races across the whole city, gradually unlocking new vehicles and locations as they built up enough reputation among local racers.

The Xbox version benefited from the console's power when rendering sprawling city districts, night lighting, and reflections on wet asphalt, which rounded out the atmosphere of illegal night races taking place out of the police's sight. The controls were fast and arcade-like, emphasizing drifting through sharp corners and the tactical use of shortcuts, which were key to victory in dense traffic full of civilian vehicles. The musical accompaniment, made up of electronic music and rock, underscored the energy and pace of driving across all three metropolises, which differed from each other not only in architecture but also in the behavior of the virtual traffic.

Midnight Club II was critically praised for its sense of speed and big-city atmosphere and helped the Rockstar Games series establish itself as a full-fledged competitor to Need for Speed in the field of street racing. The more open approach to cities and emphasis on exploratory driving influenced the following entry as well as a number of other street racing games that tried to offer similar freedom. Today the game stands out as a notable example of an early generation of open-world racing titles, though technically it naturally lags behind later sequels in its own series.

**Why play it:** For fans of early open-world racing through big-city streets who will appreciate the atmosphere and sense of speed, even though it naturally lags behind later series entries technically.

xbox__midnight-club-3-dub-edition.teaser: Collaboration with DUB magazine brought deep car customization including hydraulics.
xbox__midnight-club-3-dub-edition.article:
**Midnight Club 3: DUB Edition** pushed the series a step further through its collaboration with the tuning magazine DUB, reflected in a strong emphasis on deep vehicle customization - from rims and paint jobs to hydraulics and sound systems pumping bass tones into the streets. The game offered three American cities, between which players could travel freely by plane, and expanded the vehicle roster with motorcycles and off-road specials alongside classic sports cars. The career was built around building reputation through races, duels, and side missions, giving the gameplay a solid and well-considered pace of progression from rookie to a respected star of the underground scene.

On Xbox, the game looked visually rich, with intricately detailed vehicle interiors and a wide range of visual customizations that could be shared with other players through the online community. The reward system encouraged replaying individual races for better times and new parts, while the soundtrack of licensed artists rounded out an authentic atmosphere of mid-decade tuning culture. The controls remained accessible and arcade-like, ideal for fast and intense duels both in the streets and beyond, while the flights between cities gave the career an unusual dynamic.

DUB Edition was among the most successful entries in the series and cemented its position alongside Need for Speed as a key representative of the street tuning racing genre on sixth-generation consoles. The depth of customization influenced competing titles as well and became one of the hallmarks of the entire Midnight Club brand for years to come, as the series tried to keep pace with players' growing demands for vehicle personalization. Today, the game serves as a vivid time capsule of the mid-2000s, when tuning culture fully permeated the gaming industry and defined the visual language of an entire generation of racing games.

**Why play it:** For the depth of vehicle customization and the pronounced mid-2000s tuning culture that this entry captures as a vivid time capsule of its era.

xbox__colin-mcrae-rally-04.teaser: Realistic rally driving on asphalt, gravel, and snow; the co-driver's calls are essential.
xbox__colin-mcrae-rally-04.article:
**Colin McRae Rally 04** was among the flagship rally simulations of the early 2000s, and unlike its more arcade-like competitors, it emphasized realistic car behavior on various surface types - from asphalt through gravel to snow and muddy roads. The player went through seasons inspired by the real World Rally Championship, having to master not only the driving itself but also strategic decisions about car setup based on the conditions and length of each stage. The co-driver's pace notes were an integral part of the experience, and following them was key to a successful and safe run through the special stage, since a single missed corner could mean the end of the stage in a ditch.

On Xbox, the game benefited from intricately detailed tracks with variable weather and visible vehicle damage, which was also reflected in the cars' handling and could decide the outcome of an entire stage. The physics model was considered one of the most sophisticated on the market at the time and demanded patience from players, as well as gradually mastering each car's distinct behavior at the edge of grip. The sound design of the engines and surrounding environment contributed to an immersive atmosphere of fast and dangerous mountain and forest tracks, where every stone on the road could spell trouble.

Colin McRae Rally 04 was very well received critically and cemented the series' position as a reference point for rally simulations on consoles of that generation. Its demanding nature and authenticity influenced later entries in the series as well as competing rally and off-road racing titles in general. Today, the game remains an interesting glimpse into the state of simulation racing games before the arrival of the next console generation, though the controls, lacking the analog conveniences of today's titles, require a certain degree of getting used to and patience from anyone returning to it after all these years.

**Why play it:** For fans of demanding rally simulations who don't mind getting used to controls without modern conveniences in exchange for the authenticity that still defines the genre today.

xbox__mx-vs-atv-unleashed.teaser: Motocross, ATVs and buggies in one game; open terrain offers unusual freedom of movement.
xbox__mx-vs-atv-unleashed.article:
**MX vs. ATV Unleashed** combined motocross bikes, ATVs, buggies, and snowmobiles into a single game, offering a more varied vehicle roster than competing titles focused purely on motocross. Players could race on closed tracks as well as in vast open terrain full of ramps, jumps, and natural obstacles, giving the game an unusual freedom of movement for the off-road racing genre and inviting free exploration. The trick system during jumps allowed players to earn points and unlock further content, encouraging experimentation with individual jumps and their combinations rather than simply racing through tracks as fast as possible.

On Xbox, the game excelled with vast open maps featuring varied terrain, where players could freely explore the surroundings outside marked tracks and discover hidden shortcuts and challenges. The vehicle physics model accounted for terrain type and machine weight, so handling a motorcycle differed markedly from riding a heavy ATV or a bulky buggy, and players had to adopt a different approach for each type of machine. Multiplayer races and the ability to compete with friends in various disciplines extended the game's lifespan well beyond the career mode alone and also offered freestyle jumping competitions.

MX vs. ATV Unleashed was well received, particularly for its variety of vehicles and open approach to terrain, which set it apart from the era's competition focused on classic motocross tracks and closed circuits. The game's success led to a long line of sequels that remain staples of the off-road racing genre on consoles and computers to this day, establishing the MX vs. ATV brand as one of the best known in the entire off-road segment. From today's perspective, the game feels like a pleasantly open and playful title that offers both serious racing and pure fun in open terrain without pressure to perform, whether that means jumping across canyons or a leisurely ride through the countryside.

**Why play it:** For players craving open terrain and vehicle variety instead of closed circuits, whether that means jumping across canyons or a leisurely ride through the countryside.

xbox__tony-hawk-s-pro-skater-4.teaser: Abandoned the series' strict time limit; free movement across the level foreshadowed later entries.
xbox__tony-hawk-s-pro-skater-4.article:
**Tony Hawk's Pro Skater 4** abandoned the strict time limit of previous entries and replaced it with free movement across individual locations, where the player completed tasks in any order and at their own pace. This change gave the series a new dimension of exploration and gradually brought it closer to the more open skateboarding games that followed in the years ahead. The trick roster grew with customizable move combinations and the so-called Nail the Trick, which allowed detailed control over the execution of a jump using both analog sticks at once, requiring precise coordination of both hands.

On Xbox, the game ran smoothly and offered varied locations from city streets to fictional environments like an amusement park, with the graphics taking advantage of the console's power to display more detailed textures and smoother rider animation. The roster of professional skateboarders and hidden characters remained one of the series' main draws, and the soundtrack of punk and rock music rounded out the characteristic atmosphere of turn-of-the-millennium skate subculture. Minigames and side tasks scattered across the locations extended playtime well beyond the main career and encouraged repeated playthroughs of favorite levels.

Pro Skater 4 was very well received critically and is still considered by many players to be one of the high points of the entire series before it was replaced by the Underground brand with its emphasis on story and open cities. Free movement across locations influenced the direction of later entries as well as competing skateboarding games for a long time to come and became a standard that players came to expect from the series going forward. Today, the game remains playable thanks to its straightforward fun and catchy scoring system, even though the graphics naturally bear obvious traces of their era, and the controls may take newcomers a while to fully get used to and master all the nuances of the tricks.

**Why play it:** For fans of straightforward arcade fun and a catchy scoring system who will appreciate the free movement across locations that many still consider the high point of the entire Tony Hawk series.

xbox__tony-hawk-s-underground.teaser: Gave the series its own character, a story, and the ability to hop off the board and walk.
xbox__tony-hawk-s-underground.article:
**Tony Hawk's Underground** marked a fundamental shift for the series toward story - the player created their own character and progressed through a career from amateur to professional skateboarder, accompanied by cutscenes and collaboration with real riders from the actual scene. It was now possible to hop off the board and move around on foot, opening up new possibilities for interacting with the environment and completing tasks beyond classic skateboard tricks and competitions. More open cities replaced the earlier closed levels, giving players a genuine sense of traveling between the career's individual locations, including nighttime outings for tagging and minor vandalism.

On Xbox, the game offered vast city environments like New York or Tampa that could be freely traversed not just on a skateboard but also by car during special tasks and nighttime excursions. A character and trick editor let players customize the appearance and moves of their own character, extending the game's lifespan well beyond the main career alone. The soundtrack again drew on punk and hip-hop music, which became an inseparable part of the series' atmosphere and accompanied players through every attempt at a new trick.

Underground was both a commercial and critical success and confirmed that the series could grow beyond a purely sports-focused approach toward a more pronounced plot and the player's personal career. The emphasis on story and a more open environment influenced the direction of the entire brand for several years to come, as well as competing sports titles that tried to use a similar formula to reach a younger audience. Today, the game stands as an interesting milestone in the history of skateboarding games, when the genre tried to find a balance between arcade fun and deeper player investment in a character and their story, and many players remember it as their first contact with the skateboarding genre altogether.

**Why play it:** For players who want to experience the moment when the skateboarding genre first combined arcade fun with story and a personal career, offering many their first contact with the skateboarding genre.

xbox__tony-hawk-s-underground-2.teaser: Deepened the humor and buddy co-op; World Destruction Tour parodies competitions.
xbox__tony-hawk-s-underground-2.article:
**Tony Hawk's Underground 2** built on its successful predecessor and further deepened the emphasis on story, humor, and cooperation with the player's buddy, with whom they went through a series of absurd missions across several world destinations. The new World Destruction Tour mode parodied competitive circuits and let players sabotage opponents as well as complete comically exaggerated tasks outside classic skateboarding disciplines and fair-play rules, with the game openly embracing its own exaggeration and departure from realism. The trick system was further expanded, giving players even greater control over move combinations and their smooth linking into long, flashy sequences.

On Xbox, the game benefited visually from colorful and varied locations, from desert cities to European metropolises full of historic architecture, while the technical presentation remained on par with the previous entry in the series. A character, trick, and custom level editor gave players plenty of room for creativity and extended the game's lifespan well beyond the campaign alone, since the community could share their creations further. A humorous tone and exaggeration set Underground 2 apart from more seriously toned competitors and became one of its main hallmarks.

Underground 2 was well received, though some reviewers saw it as less groundbreaking than its predecessor, more of an extension and fine-tuning of the existing mechanics. Still, it retained a strong fan base thanks to its humor and the variety of content on offer, as well as the number of hidden references to previous entries in the series. Today, the game serves as a nostalgic reminder of the era when the Tony Hawk series experimented with story and an open world, before later returning to simpler professional tours without an overblown plot and with an emphasis on pure gameplay, free of unnecessary detours from the skateboarding itself.

**Why play it:** For fans of humor, hidden references to previous entries, and varied content, even though it's more a fine-tuning of the first Underground than a fundamental step forward.

xbox__amped-2.teaser: More open mountains and more tricks than the first Amped; free riding and specific challenges.
xbox__amped-2.article:
**Amped 2** built on the successful snowboarding title Amped: Freestyle Snowboarding and expanded its concept with larger open mountains, more playable riders, and a more elaborate trick system. Players could freely ride down vast slopes full of jumps, rails, and natural obstacles, with combining tricks and stylish landings being key to earning points and unlocking new gear and clothing. The career mode offered progressive competition across various mountains around the world, each with different terrain, weather, and track difficulty, and players could choose between riding freely in their own style and completing specific challenges.

On Xbox, the game excelled with vast snowy scenery and a smooth sense of descent, taking advantage of the console's power to display more detailed terrain and distant views of the surrounding landscape full of mountains and forests.
