**Why play it:** For players on the couch, the Xbox 360 version offers the same campaign and factions as the PC, just with controls reworked into circular menus operated by gamepad instead of precise mouse selection.

xbox-360__far-cry-2.teaser: An open Africa with fire spreading according to the wind, decaying weapons, and the hero's malaria.
xbox-360__far-cry-2.article:
Far Cry 2 places the player in a vast open African landscape ravaged by civil war, where as a mercenary they try to track down an arms dealer known as the Jackal. The game is known for the dynamic spread of fire across dried-out vegetation, which spreads according to wind direction and can drive off both enemies and the player themselves, for decaying weapons that jam and have to be continually swapped for new ones, and for malaria, which occasionally drops the main character to the ground and forces them to take medicine so as not to pass out in the middle of a firefight. The open world is also populated by dozens of armed patrols, checkpoints, and so-called buddies, who can save the player directly in combat if they're wounded, giving the game an unusually raw, unpredictable feel to every encounter.

The Xbox 360 version launched on the same day as the PC version in 2008 and offers the same open world, the same main storyline, and the same side quests scattered across the map, including the need to travel between missions under one's own power through desert, savanna, and rivers instead of fast travel on the map. The graphics were slightly simplified compared to the PC version, with lower-resolution textures and shorter draw distance, and the game runs at a fixed resolution with a target frame rate of around 30 frames per second, whereas the PC version could scale detail and performance according to the computer's configuration, from weaker rigs up to the era's top-end hardware. Controls moved to the gamepad instead of mouse and keyboard, which changes the feel of shooting and long-range aiming, and the game lacks modding support, which PC players later made extensive use of for tweaking the game, fixing bugs, and adding their own content extensions. Cooperative and competitive multiplayer nonetheless work on the console the same way as on PC, just via Xbox Live instead of computer servers, with the same game modes and maps as on the other platforms released the same day, so console players didn't come away with content diminished compared to PC, just adjusted controls.

**Why play it:** For players who prefer a gamepad, the Xbox 360 version offers the same open world and story as the PC, just with slightly simplified graphics, a fixed resolution, and no modding support.

xbox-360__assassin-s-creed.teaser: A pioneer of stealthy movement through the city; the sci-fi framing device with the Animus defined the entire series.
xbox-360__assassin-s-creed.article:
Assassin's Creed, released in 2007, took place in three historical cities of the Third Crusade - Jerusalem, Damascus, and Acre - where the player, in the role of the secret assassin Altaïr, engaged in tailing targets, stealth, and free movement across rooftops and city walls. Between individual assassinations, the player returned to the present, where a character named Desmond Miles relived his ancestor's memories through a device called the Animus - a framing story that became a defining trait of the entire series. At the time, the game was among the first to show what a truly living virtual city full of crowds, guards, and side quests could look like, though the repetitive structure of those side missions was among the most common criticisms from reviewers.

The Xbox 360 version launched on the same day as the PlayStation 3 version, and in terms of content and graphics both console editions were practically identical, including the same frame rate and resolution. The difference lay in online service support: Xbox Live offered a working achievement system from day one, so Xbox 360 players could earn points for completed challenges from the very start. PlayStation 3 didn't yet have a trophy system at the time - Sony didn't introduce it until mid-2008, and Assassin's Creed only received it via a later update. The Xbox 360 version was therefore, at the moment of release, the more complete choice for achievement hunters, even though this changed nothing about the actual playable content, game length, or difficulty - it really was just a difference in the two platforms' supporting online systems.

Assassin's Creed launched one of the generation's most significant action series on both Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3, and a year later also received a PC version, which, however, came with its own set of technical quirks, including a then-discussed anti-piracy protection requiring a constant internet connection. Thanks to this, the console versions maintained a reputation as the more convenient choice for players who wanted to avoid such complications.

**Why play it:** For players who wanted to avoid the much-discussed anti-piracy protection requiring a constant internet connection on the later PC version, the console version remained the more convenient way to start one of the generation's most significant action series.

xbox-360__beatles-rock-band.teaser: An interactive band biography instead of an ordinary playlist; you can even tackle vocal harmonies.
xbox-360__beatles-rock-band.article:
The Beatles: Rock Band (2009) was among the most ambitious music games of its time - instead of an ordinary playlist, it delivered a comprehensive biography of The Beatles using archival photographs, period recordings, and stylized visual sequences accompanying each song. Players with a guitar, bass, drums, or microphone worked through the discography chronologically, from club performances in Hamburg and Liverpool to the late studio albums, and the game thus functioned both as an interactive tribute to the band and as a classic party game for four players at once. A system supporting up to three-part vocal harmonies also rewarded players who could sing secondary melodic lines, not just the lead vocal.

The Xbox 360 edition launched alongside the PlayStation 3 and Wii versions and contained the same songs and the same game content. Unlike the Wii version, however, it offered full-fledged online multiplayer via Xbox Live, allowing players to compete or cooperate remotely - something the Wii of that era did not allow for Rock Band series titles. Thanks to the more powerful hardware, the visual presentation of the musical "dream" sequences was also more detailed than on Wii, with sharper textures for the archival photographs and smoother transitions between the individual scenes.

In terms of gameplay and content, the Xbox 360 version remained identical to the parallel PlayStation 3 edition - only technical details tied to the platforms differed, such as the achievement system instead of trophies and slightly different support for wireless instruments. The instrument peripherals also weren't compatible between consoles due to different connectors, so owners of multiple systems had to buy a separate set of instruments for each platform. For fans of the Beatles and rhythm games, the choice of console therefore didn't really matter - the experience was practically identical on both HD platforms, just noticeably richer than the Wii variant, and after finishing career mode players could freely replay any unlocked song.

**Why play it:** For fans of the Beatles and rhythm games, the choice between Xbox 360 and PlayStation 3 didn't matter - the experience was practically identical on both HD platforms and noticeably richer than the Wii variant.

xbox-360__ace-combat-6-fires-of-liberati.teaser: An arcade flight simulator set in the fictional Strangereal with dozens of licensed aircraft.
xbox-360__ace-combat-6-fires-of-liberati.article:
**Ace Combat 6: Fires of Liberation** is an arcade flight simulator set in the fictional country of Strangereal, telling the story of a war of liberation from the perspective of a fighter pilot. In the campaign, the player gradually gains access to dozens of licensed and fictional aircraft, from classic fighters through bombers to experimental machines, and each mission presents a different tactical situation - from escorting convoys to defending a city to destroying enemy bases. The controls are deliberately accessible and arcade-like, so the game focuses more on flashy dogfights and spectacular explosions than on realistic flight physics.

On Xbox 360, it was one of the platform's few truly exclusive franchises and, at the same time, a technological leap for the whole series - the game was the first in the line to fully exploit the power of the new generation, with expansive battlefields, dense traffic of units on the ground and in the air, and dramatic weather changes that affect both visibility and tactics. The soundtrack was accompanied by orchestral music underscoring the epic tone of each mission, and radio communication between pilots gives the battles a cinematic atmosphere. The game also offered online multiplayer for battles involving multiple players at once, which at the time was rather the exception for flight action games.

Contemporary reviews praised above all the scope and variety of the missions, the number of available aircraft, and the overall audiovisual quality, which was among the best the Xbox 360 offered in the genre. They also highlighted the dynamic battlefield, where the situation in the sky and on the ground changes depending on how the player performs in a mission, so the same scenario can look noticeably different on a second playthrough. It was precisely its exclusivity on this console that made Ace Combat 6 a sought-after title among owners of other platforms who wanted to try the series, and many considered it one of the reasons to get an Xbox 360 in the first place. To this day, the game works as an entertaining, accessible demonstration of how flight action games can play like a blockbuster without burdening players with complicated simulation - and for fans of the series it remains one of the most fondly remembered entries of the whole console generation.

**Why play it:** For owners of other platforms, Xbox 360 exclusivity was one of the reasons to get the console - the dynamic battlefield and scope of missions still work today as an accessible, blockbuster showcase of flight action games.

xbox-360__call-of-duty-3.teaser: Battles for France 1944 seen through four Allied armies; the first game with contextual quick-time actions.
xbox-360__call-of-duty-3.article:
**Call of Duty 3** took players back to World War II, specifically to the battles for the liberation of France in the summer of 1944, told from the perspective of soldiers from several Allied armies — American, British, Canadian, and Polish. The game follows the structure of previous entries: linear missions interspersed with scripted moments, an emphasis on cinematic battle choreography, and switching perspectives between different characters. New to the series were contextual actions requiring quick button presses during close-quarters combat or vehicle sections, meant to add more dynamism to both infantry and vehicle passages.

On the Xbox 360, this was the entry in the series developed specifically for this console generation — development was handled by Treyarch, while Infinity Ward was at the time working on the modern Modern Warfare. The graphics engine delivered denser battlefields, a larger number of units on screen, and more impressive explosion and fire effects, though compared to later entries in the series the game still stuck to a fairly linear, corridor-based level design. The audio side relied on intense gunfire, shouting comrades, and orchestral music that gave period World War II titles their proper sense of gravity.

Reviews rated the title as solid but not a groundbreaking addition to the series — praising the variety of missions and vehicle sections, including riding a motorcycle and operating tanks, but criticizing the worn-out World War II theme, which by that point had appeared quite often in the genre and was starting to blur together across competing series in players' minds. Still, the multiplayer component attracted a decent player base on the Xbox 360 thanks to online combat over Xbox Live, where the game maintained its own community even after later sequels were released. From today's perspective, Call of Duty 3 is interesting mainly as a transitional point in the series between historical wars and the modern setting that would later be defined by Modern Warfare, and as a reminder of a time when World War II was still the main subject for shooters.

**Why play it:** For fans of the series, the game is interesting mainly as a transitional point between historical wars and the modern setting later defined by Modern Warfare, thanks to its varied missions and a decent multiplayer community on Xbox Live.

xbox-360__armored-core-4.teaser: A series restart for the new generation – boost drift turns battles into fast aerial acrobatics.
xbox-360__armored-core-4.article:
**Armored Core 4** brought the long-running series of mech battles to the new console generation while also partially restarting its game systems. The player builds their own mech from dozens of parts — legs, weapons, generators, and other equipment — and fights other mechs and large bosses in arenas and story missions. Compared to older entries in the series, the game sped up the pace of combat by introducing so-called boost drift, which allows for smooth flying maneuvers and quick aerial movement, making the battles feel more like fast aerial acrobatics than the slower ground-based skirmishes of previous generations.

On the Xbox 360, the new generation showed mainly in the scale of the battlefields and the sense of speed — the mechs move more nimbly, the camera reacts to sharp turns, and environmental destruction along with the visual effects of explosions and lasers reached a noticeably higher level compared to previous entries on older consoles. Still, the game retained the steep learning curve typical of the series: assembling a mech requires understanding the relationship between weight, energy, and armament, and it can easily discourage beginners before they grasp the basic principles of building a machine. The audio side is filled out by an electronic and orchestral score that reinforces the feeling of a cold, technological future in which the story takes place.

Contemporary reviews praised the faster, more action-oriented approach to combat and the graphical leap, while also pointing out that the game remained fairly inaccessible to newcomers and that the story is told in the terse, fragmented way typical of the entire brand. For loyal fans of the series, it was nonetheless a welcome restart that paved the way for further entries on this console generation. Today, Armored Core 4 is interesting mainly as a precursor to FromSoftware's later work and as an example of how the mech genre can be adapted to a faster, more action-oriented style of play.

**Why play it:** For fans of mech combat and anyone curious about the roots of FromSoftware's later work, who won't mind swallowing the terse storytelling and the steeper demands placed on newcomers.

ps3__call-of-duty-modern-warfare-2.teaser: A cinematic, controversial campaign featuring the infamous airport mission; a relentless pace with no room to breathe.
ps3__call-of-duty-modern-warfare-2.article:
**Call of Duty: Modern Warfare 2** followed up on the incredible success of its predecessor and pushed the series into an even more sprawling, more cinematic direction. In the campaign, the player switches between several characters and continents — from snowy mountains through Washington to Brazilian favelas — and the game went even further in its storytelling than Modern Warfare, including the controversial airport mission, which sparked widespread discussion about the limits of interactive violence in video games. The story continues with the popular characters Soap MacTavish and Captain Price and expands the conflict between Russia and the United States to even grander proportions, ending on an open note that left players waiting for the next installment. The pace is relentlessly fast, the firefights short and intense, with scripted sequences alternating with adrenaline-fueled action and no unnecessary downtime.

On the PS3, the game ran on a modified IW 4.0 engine and technically kept pace with the competing Xbox 360 version, though minor differences in performance, textures, and loading times were noticeable and became the subject of comparative tests between platforms at the time. The audio was among the game's strongest aspects — gunfire had weight, the voice acting was convincing, and the music gave the campaign an epic feel. The multiplayer brought an improved perk system, killstreaks such as an AC-130 gunship strike or a tactical nuke, and new game modes like Spec Ops, which allowed cooperative play for two players on split screen as well as online.

Reception at the time was enthusiastic, and the game became one of the best-selling titles of the generation, defining the shape of online war shooters for years to come. Today the campaign feels more like a fast, flashy ride than a deep war story, but its influence on the genre is undeniable — without Modern Warfare 2, today's arena and tactical shooters would look different. On the PS3 it remains playable even after all these years, though the multiplayer servers have long since lost their original form and many online features are now missing.

**Why play it:** Because of the fast, flashy campaign and the influence that permanently transformed the shape of online war shooters, Modern Warfare 2 is worth trying, even though the multiplayer no longer runs in its original form.

ps3__call-of-duty-black-ops.teaser: A Cold War thriller full of conspiracies and the question of what's real and what's just a figment of the mind.
ps3__call-of-duty-black-ops.article:
**Call of Duty: Black Ops** moved the series into the Cold War and offered a darker, more paranoid story woven through with secret operations, experiments on the human psyche, and conspiratorial motifs inspired by real historical events. The player takes on the role of agent Alex Mason, whose memories are gradually revealed in flashbacks during an interrogation by an unknown man — from the invasion of Cuba, through the war in Vietnam, to secret operations in the Soviet Union and Hong Kong. The campaign leans on cinematic production with plenty of period detail and tries to keep the player in suspense over what is real and what is just a product of a tortured mind, with the final twist ranking among the most discussed moments in the entire series.

On the PS3, the game ran on an engine derived from previous entries and was technically comparable to the competition, though the PS3 version had minor performance and multiplayer stability issues at launch, which developers gradually addressed with updates. The soundtrack and period music of the sixties, including licensed songs, did a good job underscoring the atmosphere of Cold War paranoia. But the real star was once again the multiplayer, which introduced the CoD Points system for buying weapons, perks, and cosmetic customizations, the popular cooperative Zombies mode on the Kino der Toten map, and the ability to create custom emblems using a simple editor.

Black Ops did very well both commercially and critically, cementing the series' position as a dominant force in online shooters and mainstream pop culture. The Zombies mode founded its own subgenre within the series, one that remains popular to this day and has grown into its own mythology. Looking back, the campaign feels like a dreamlike, at times confusing ride, but it's precisely this ambiguity that gives it a character distinct from the more straightforward entries in the series and still sparks discussion about how to interpret the ending.

**Why play it:** For its dreamlike, at times confusing campaign that still sparks discussion about how to interpret the ending, and for the Zombies mode that founded its own popular subgenre, Black Ops is worth attention even after all these years.

ps3__battlefield-3.teaser: Frostbite 2 gave the generation its best-looking visuals; but the main draw is the massive multiplayer.
ps3__battlefield-3.article:
**Battlefield 3** marked the series' return to modern warfare and brought an impressively good-looking world to the PS3, powered by the Frostbite 2 engine, which in 2011 was among the most technically ambitious titles of the generation thanks to advanced lighting, environmental destruction, and character animations. The shorter single-player campaign led the player through several storylines from a conflict in the Middle East, including the Battle of Paris and an operation in Iran, and built on cinematic firefights inspired by the successful Modern Warfare series, but the true center of gravity was the much larger multiplayer with big maps, vehicles, aircraft, and team play based on four military classes.

On the PS3, compared to the PC version, studio DICE had to limit the number of players per match to twenty-four and reduce some graphical details as well as the extent of environmental destructibility, yet the game still looked and sounded excellent on console — the sound of gunfire and explosions was among the most impressive things the console offered that generation. Destruction of buildings and cover changed tactics on the fly and forced players to constantly improvise and seek new hiding spots, which was one of the main differences from the competing Call of Duty series and its fixed environments.

Battlefield 3 received very positive reviews and cemented the series' position as the main rival to Call of Duty in online war action throughout this console generation. Multiplayer maps like Caspian Border and Operation Firestorm became iconic examples of what large-scale battles with tanks, helicopters, and planes could offer players on an ordinary home console. Today the game still stands as proof that even an older-generation console could deliver a grand, chaotic multiplayer experience, even though the servers have long since ceased operating at full capacity and many players have moved on to newer entries.

**Why play it:** Anyone who wants to experience grand, chaotic battles with tanks and planes, which consoles of that time rarely managed to deliver, will find in Battlefield 3 proof that it was possible, even though full servers are long gone.

ps3__just-cause-2.teaser: A massive open world on the island of Panau; the grappling hook enables absurd physics-driven stunts.
ps3__just-cause-2.article:
**Just Cause 2** sent the player to the fictional Southeast Asian island of Panau and offered one of the largest and most open playgrounds of its generation, in scale far exceeding competing open-world titles of the time. Main character Rico Rodriguez wields a grappling hook and a parachute that can be combined into utterly absurd chains of stunts — pulling himself toward enemies, tethering vehicles to each other, launching himself onto rooftops, or towing himself behind a flying plane. The story about overthrowing Panau's dictator is little more than a pretext for the player to enjoy total physics-based anarchy and complete dozens of side missions for local resistance factions, collect scattered equipment crates, and unlock new weapons and vehicles.

On the PS3, the game ran on its own Avalanche Engine 2.0 and offered a huge, visually varied environment ranging from tropical jungles through deserts to snow-capped mountains, at the cost of occasional frame-rate drops and longer loading times during fast travel across the island. The music and ambient sounds nicely complemented the sense of adventure on an exotic island, while the physics model of explosions and destruction gave the action a comedic, almost cartoonish energy typical of the whole series. Collecting upgrades and unlocking new abilities motivated the player to keep exploring even outside the main storyline.

Critics and players alike praised above all the freedom of movement and the endless ways to take down enemy bases and military convoys, even though the linear story campaign was seen more as a side product to freely roaming the world. Just Cause 2 became a cult favorite and defined the subgenre of open-world action sandboxes built around movement acrobatics, inspiring the creators of other games and gaining an active modding community on PC. Today, players return to it mainly for the sheer joy of moving around with the grappling hook and parachute, something many later games struggled to replicate even with much bigger budgets and more elaborate stories.

**Why play it:** For the sheer joy of moving around with the grappling hook and parachute, which later games with far bigger budgets struggled to replicate, Just Cause 2 remains a cult choice for lovers of free-form destruction.

ps3__saints-row-third.teaser: A self-aware parade of absurdity in Steelport; the Saints gang is already a celebrity brand here.
ps3__saints-row-third.article:
**Saints Row: The Third** abandoned the last remnants of seriousness and turned the series into a parade of absurd, self-aware action in the stylized metropolis of Steelport. The Saints gang is already a celebrity brand here, with its own energy drink, movie, and action figures, and during the campaign the player gets access to all sorts of bizarre weapons, goes through missions full of parody references to other video games and films, and can enjoy completely free movement around the open city on foot, in cars, and in planes. Character creation offers an extreme degree of customization for the gang's appearance and behavior, setting the game apart from more seriously toned competitors, and the player can also buy and upgrade their own businesses throughout Steelport.

On the PS3, the game ran on a modified engine and offered a colorful, legible world with fast pacing and fluid action, though technically it did not reach the level of detail of competing major productions. The soundtrack with licensed songs and the crazy radio stations with their own hosts nicely underscored the wacky atmosphere, while the combat combined shooting, melee, and vehicle driving into a single fast-paced whole full of options for customizing the character, weapons, and the entire Saints gang. Cooperative play for two players also allowed the entire campaign to be played together with a friend.

The game received very favorable reception precisely for its willingness not to take itself seriously and to offer players pure fun without pretensions, which set it noticeably apart from the somewhat darker Saints Row 2. It became the turning point in the series toward the parodic, kitschy aesthetic that was later taken even further by the even more extreme Saints Row IV, with its alien invasion and superpowers. Today, The Third is valued as one of the most entertaining open-world titles of the generation, ideal for players who want to take a break from seriously-toned action games and their terse tone, and it still enjoys an active player base.

**Why play it:** Anyone wanting a break from seriously-toned action games will find in Saints Row: The Third one of the most entertaining open-world titles of the generation, built on pure fun without pretensions.

ps3__prototype.teaser: Alex Mercer turns his body into blades and claws; he steals abilities from the victims he absorbs.
ps3__prototype.article:
**Prototype** placed the player in an infected New York in the skin of Alex Mercer, an amnesiac man with superhuman abilities who tries to figure out what caused the viral outbreak turning residents into monsters and why both the army and a military corporation are after him. The main character can transform parts of his body into blades, claws, and shields, absorb the memories and abilities of his victims, climb buildings, and leap between skyscrapers, which makes moving around the city just as important a part of the game as the actual combat against soldiers and mutated monsters. By gradually completing side missions and consuming further targets, Alex unlocks new mutations and abilities that fundamentally change his combat style.

On the PS3, the game ran on Radical Entertainment's own engine and offered a large, though somewhat visually plain, city full of enemies ranging from civilians and soldiers to giant mutated monsters called Hunters. Combat was fast, brutal, and full of flashy combos, which made the player feel like an unstoppable weapon of mass destruction capable of wiping out an entire military unit, including tanks and helicopters. The atmosphere was rounded out by dark, industrial music and a grim narrative tone interspersed with flashbacks revealing the protagonist's past and his connection to the epidemic that engulfed all of Manhattan.

The game came out the same year as the competing inFamous, which tackled the same theme of open-world superhero action, and the two titles were frequently compared, with Prototype praised especially for its brutality, speed, and aggressive style of play, while criticized for weaker storytelling and a less sympathetic protagonist. Even years later, Prototype remains an interesting example of just how far a feeling of total physical dominance over the surrounding world can be taken, and it earned a loyal following of fans who appreciated its raw, uncompromising action free of unnecessary restrictions and moral dilemmas.

**Why play it:** For the raw feeling of total physical dominance over the surrounding world and a fast, aggressive style of play free of moral dilemmas, Prototype remains an interesting choice despite its weaker storytelling.

ps3__bulletstorm.teaser: Killing as art; the Skillshot system rewards creativity, not just aiming and shooting.
ps3__bulletstorm.article:
**Bulletstorm** is a stylized sci-fi shooter that focused on creative kills instead of plain aiming and shooting. Playing as mercenary Grayson Hunt on the abandoned planet Stygia, the player uses an electric leash, kicks, and the environment itself to send enemies flying into the air, onto spikes, into turbines, or otherwise dispatch them in the most inventive way possible. For this the game awards points called Skillshots, which unlock special weapon abilities and equipment upgrades. Weapons like the drill gun or the flare gun that fires a swarm of darts offered dozens of environmental combinations, turning every fight into an opportunity to invent a new way to finish off an opponent.

On PS3 the game ran on Unreal Engine 3 and offered a colorful, tropical world full of decaying spaceships, ruins, and lush vegetation, complemented by brisk action with no unnecessary downtime or long loading screens. The game's humor was deliberately crude and over the top, with dialogue full of swearing and black comedy underscoring the B-movie, self-aware tone of the whole story about revenge, betrayal, and survival on a hostile planet. The scoring system for creative kills motivated players to experiment with weapons instead of mechanically mowing down enemies, and the game also offered a two-player co-op mode.

Critics praised above all the original combat system, which differed sharply from the cover-and-precision-aiming style that dominated military shooters at the time, even though the game didn't perform commercially as the publisher had hoped. Bulletstorm nonetheless became a cult favorite among action shooter fans and is still cited today as an example of how playfulness and a reward system built around style, rather than mere accuracy, can be brought into the genre. Today it feels like a refreshing reminder of a time when shooters could still poke fun at themselves, didn't take themselves deadly seriously, and weren't afraid to experiment with their own identity.

**Why play it:** Thanks to an original combat system that rewards style over pure accuracy, and the nerve to make fun of itself, Bulletstorm is a refreshing reminder of less self-serious shooters.

ps3__ninja-gaiden-sigma.teaser: An enhanced port of one of the generation's most difficult and precise action titles.
ps3__ninja-gaiden-sigma.article:
**Ninja Gaiden Sigma** is an enhanced version of the Xbox action game Ninja Gaiden, which Team Ninja brought to PS3 with improved graphics, a new playable character, and adjusted difficulty for a new audience. Playing as the ninja Ryu Hayabusa, the player fights through a series of relentless battles against demons, ninjas, and human soldiers using fast, technical combos, dodging, and parrying with a katana and other exotic weapons — the game ranks among the most difficult and precise action titles of its generation. A system for unlocking and upgrading weapons at a merchant between chapters gave the player room to tailor their equipment to their own playstyle.

The PS3 version added the playable character Rachel with her own set of hammer-based weapons, along with several new levels and bosses compared to the original Xbox version. The visuals were polished and ran more smoothly than the original, as Team Ninja used the platform transition to fix a number of technical shortcomings. The combat system demanded precision and knowledge of enemy movement patterns — mindlessly mashing buttons led to a quick death here, setting the game apart from the more accessible action games of the time. The dark, gothic atmosphere and intense soundtrack complemented the bloody, brutal tone of a game full of severed limbs and blood spatter.

Ninja Gaiden Sigma was critically praised as one of the most technically accomplished action titles of its generation and gave PS3 owners a rare chance to play a series that had previously been exclusive to Xbox. Its uncompromising difficulty and deep combat system inspired a number of later action games striving for similarly technical depth and precise controls. Even today it's recommended as a test of a player's true reflexes and patience — for someone willing to learn from their mistakes, retry the same section repeatedly, and gradually refine their technique.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for a test of true reflexes and patience, paired with a deep combat system, will find Ninja Gaiden Sigma one of the most technically accomplished action titles of its generation.

ps3__dante-s-inferno.teaser: Openly borrows from God of War, just sets the scythe combat across the nine circles of hell.
ps3__dante-s-inferno.article:
**Dante's Inferno** is an action game loosely inspired by Dante's Divine Comedy, in which the knight Dante journeys through the nine circles of hell to save the soul of his beloved Beatrice, abducted by Lucifer himself. The game combines fast combat with a death scythe and a holy cross with the option to either forgive enemies through absolution or brutally destroy them, letting the player gradually upgrade either a holy or a demonic branch of abilities — much like the God of War series, which the game openly and unabashedly echoes in both its combat style and camera work. Each of the aforementioned circles of hell — from lust through wrath to treachery — offers its own visual motif, puzzles, and a unique boss symbolizing that particular sin.

On PS3 the game stood out with its visually reworked, grotesque depiction of the nine circles of hell, full of monstrous bosses, deformed bodies, and dark symbolism inspired by medieval religious art and Bosch's paintings. The musical score, with its dark choirs and orchestral music, effectively underscored the grim, at times outright shocking atmosphere, while the combat system offered brisk combinations of attacks, dodges, and magic abilities unlocked as the player progressed through the game and collected the souls of the dead. Animated sequences explaining Dante's past as a crusader also appeared between chapters.

Reviewers couldn't help but notice the strong resemblance to God of War, yet they praised the game's visual boldness and atmosphere, which didn't shy away from depicting extreme violence and nudity as part of its story about sin, temptation, and redemption. Dante's Inferno didn't sell well enough commercially to receive its planned sequel despite an open ending, but it remains an interesting example of combining genre clichés with an unconventional artistic approach. Today it's valued especially by fans of dark fantasy aesthetics and the literary source material, who appreciate the bold visual treatment of its infernal scenes.

**Why play it:** For fans of dark fantasy aesthetics and the literary source material, Dante's Inferno offers a bold visual treatment of infernal scenes, even though its gameplay draws heavily on God of War.

ps3__dead-space-2.teaser: A faster sequel to the horror game set on the Sprawl station; telekinesis can now impale enemies.
ps3__dead-space-2.article:
**Dead Space 2** continued the cult survival horror set in space, bringing engineer Isaac Clarke to a massive space station called the Sprawl, home to thousands of civilians, where he faces a new wave of Necromorphs as well as his own psychological demons from the events aboard the Ishimura. Compared to the first game, this entry picked up the pace, added more action sequences and public spaces like nurseries and churches, but kept the series' signature system of strategically dismembering enemy limbs instead of classic headshot aiming, complemented by new weapons and a telekinesis ability that can now instantly impale an enemy on anything sharp nearby.

On PS3 the game stood out for its impressive sound design, which, combined with the claustrophobic environment of the station and a minimalist interface built directly into Isaac's suit, created an intense sense of tension without the need for distracting on-screen indicators. A new chapter of psychological trauma, which the player experiences alongside the protagonist including hallucinations of his deceased girlfriend, gave the story added psychological depth, while a new cooperative and competitive multiplayer mode extended the game beyond its solo campaign. The famous needle-in-the-eye sequence at the game's opening became one of the most talked-about moments of the entire console generation.

Dead Space 2 received very positive critical reception and is considered by many players and journalists to be the peak of the entire series, deftly balancing horror tension with a faster pace without sacrificing atmosphere. The game further cemented Visceral Games' reputation as the creator of one of the finest survival horror titles of this console generation. Even today Dead Space 2 is recommended as essential playing for sci-fi horror fans thanks to its atmosphere, sound design, and tense, emotionally rich story that ranks among the genre's high points on consoles of its generation.

**Why play it:** For fans of sci-fi horror, Dead Space 2 is essential playing thanks to its atmosphere, sound design, and tense story, which deftly balances horror tension with a faster pace.

ps3__asura-s-wrath.teaser: An action series told in episodes with recaps; battles against gods escalate to cosmic scale.
ps3__asura-s-wrath.article:
**Asura's Wrath** is a one-of-a-kind action game from Japanese studio CyberConnect2 that combines gameplay with a format resembling an animated TV series, split into episodes complete with recaps, credits, and previews of what's coming next. The player takes on the role of the demigod Asura, who is stripped of his divinity and loses his daughter after being betrayed by his own comrades, and who sets out on a path of revenge against his former allies. Combat combines classic close-quarters action with massive quick-time-event sequences that unfold on a cosmic, almost planetary scale. The player gradually faces a pantheon of deities called the Seven Deities, with each final confrontation escalating step by step toward cosmic proportions.

On PS3 the game stood out for its exaggeratedly grandiose visual style, with battles taking place between planets and combatants growing to galactic size — a clear nod to the aesthetic of Japanese action anime series and manga source material. The music and voice acting effectively underscored the emotionally charged moments of the protagonist's fury and despair, while the visual style combined cel shading with intricately detailed environments and massive, monumental enemies. Individual episodes varied in length and pacing, much like episodes of a television series, an unusual approach for the action game genre.

The game divided reviewers due to its heavy emphasis on quick-time events at the expense of more traditional gameplay and room for free-form action, yet thanks to its exceptional presentation and manic energy it found devoted fans around the world. The decision to sell the story's final chapter as paid DLC was also controversial, drawing criticism from players expecting a complete experience in the base game. Today Asura's Wrath is valued as a unique experiment straddling the line between video game and interactive anime, one that's still hard to compare to anything else and has earned a cult reputation.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for a unique experiment straddling the line between video game and interactive anime will find manic energy and exceptional presentation in Asura's Wrath, even though the quick-time events crowd out room for free-form action.

ps3__red-faction-guerrilla.teaser: Destroying buildings with Geo-Mod 2.0 isn't an effect here, it's the core game mechanic.
ps3__red-faction-guerrilla.article:
**Red Faction: Guerrilla** moved the series from linear shooting corridors to an open world on Mars, where the player, as a member of the resistance organization Red Faction, fights against the oppressive mining corporation Ultor that controls the entire planet and its inhabitants. The key new feature was the Geo-Mod 2.0 physics engine, which allowed players to demolish buildings, bridges, and bases almost freely using a sledgehammer, explosives, vehicles, or a rocket launcher, turning environmental destruction into a core gameplay mechanic rather than a mere visual effect as in competing titles. Liberating individual districts from corporate control gradually built up support among the population and opened access to further areas of the Martian colony.

On PS3 the game offered a sprawling, if somewhat desolate, Martian landscape scattered with settlements and military bases, through which the player moved on foot, by vehicle, and using a jetpack that enabled short flights. The sound design and music effectively underscored the harsh, industrial atmosphere of an uprising against overwhelming odds, while missions often centered on sabotage, freeing hostages, and gradually weakening enemy infrastructure through guerrilla-style tactics rather than direct confrontation. The game also offered a cooperative multiplayer mode and a standalone competitive mode focused purely on demolishing buildings.

Critics praised the game especially for its innovative destruction system, which had no equal on the market at the time and functioned as a full-fledged gameplay mechanic, even though the open world was seen as somewhat emptier and more repetitive than in competing titles. Red Faction: Guerrilla became a cult favorite among fans of physics simulations and is still cited today as one of the few titles to elevate environmental destruction into a genuine gameplay mechanic rather than just a flashy backdrop. Even years later its demolition system feels surprisingly satisfying and technically ahead of its time, making it a favorite pick for players looking for something other than a classic shooter.

**Why play it:** Thanks to a demolition system that still feels satisfying and technically ahead of its time, Red Faction: Guerrilla is a favorite pick for players looking for something other than a classic shooter.

ps3__socom-4-u-s-navy-seals.teaser: A tactical shooter from the pioneers of online multiplayer and voice chat on the PS2.
ps3__socom-4-u-s-navy-seals.article:
**SOCOM 4: U.S. Navy SEALs** is a tactical third-person shooter from Zipper Interactive, the studio that made a name for itself with the SOCOM series back in the PlayStation 2 era as a pioneer of online console shooters and voice communication between players. The fourth installment sends a SEAL team commander into a fictional conflict in Southeast Asia, where the player leads a squad of teammates, issuing orders to attack, take cover, or reposition, combining cover-based firefights with tactical planning of advances through insurgent-held territory. The player can issue orders to teammates either through a classic menu or by aiming directly at a target, which was meant to speed up command in hectic firefights.

On PS3 the game supported control via the PlayStation Move controller and the Navy SEALs headset included in a special edition, which allowed voice commands to squadmates, aiming to offer a more immersive alternative to traditional gamepad control. The campaign emphasized taking cover, methodically clearing areas of enemies, and cooperating with AI teammates, while the sound design focused on a realistic weapon roster and authentic military communication solutions between team members in combat. Jungle, village, and port city settings gave the campaign visual variety compared to the more austere military bases of competing shooters.

Multiplayer had traditionally been the heart of the SOCOM series, and the fourth installment offered expansive maps and a varied set of game modes for team battles, although the launch version struggled with technical issues and weapon balance problems that developers gradually patched. SOCOM 4 received a mixed to mildly positive reception and was the last major installment in the series developed by Zipper Interactive before the studio's subsequent closure. For fans of tactical shooters it remains an interesting reminder of a time when consoles were searching for new ways to control military action and experimented with voice command and motion controllers.

**Why play it:** For fans of tactical shooters, SOCOM 4 is an interesting reminder of a time when consoles experimented with voice command and motion controllers, despite its rocky launch technical issues.

ps3__l-noire.teaser: Famous for its interrogations; MotionScan captures suspects' subtle facial reactions.
ps3__l-noire.article:
**L.A. Noire** takes the player to Los Angeles in the late 1940s, casting them as detective Cole Phelps, who gradually works his way through the departments of the LAPD, from Traffic to Homicide. Developed by Team Bondi, the game combines an open world with an investigative adventure, where examining crime scenes, gathering evidence, and above all interrogating suspects and witnesses take center stage. It's the interrogations in particular that made L.A. Noire famous — thanks to the advanced MotionScan facial capture technology, the player watches suspects' subtle facial reactions and decides whether to believe them, doubt them, or confront them outright with a lie. Progression is divided into individual cases organized by department, and as the player's career advances, so does the severity of the crimes, ranging from theft through arson to murder investigations tied to corruption at the highest levels of the city.

On PS3 the game ran smoothly and made use of an extensive recreation of period Los Angeles, complemented by period music and a jazz score that heightens the noir thriller atmosphere. Shooting and action sequences are more of a side element to the detective work, giving the game the feel of an unconventional mix of adventure, action, and driving sim, as the player travels between crime scenes in period automobiles through the city's recreated streets. The individual cases are tied together by a broader story about corruption, postwar trauma, and the dark side of the American metropolis, which gradually unfolds partly through the protagonist's own past.

Upon release, L.A. Noire was praised above all for its facial-capture technology and authentic atmosphere, although the game's pacing and the repetitive structure of its cases divided player opinion. The game became a symbol of how far facial animation technology could be pushed in service of storytelling and inspired later attempts by other studios to more convincingly depict human emotion in games. Even years later it remains a unique experience that has never been fully replicated by any other title, and for fans of detective stories it remains one of the most fascinating experiments of its console generation.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its unique facial-animation technology in service of storytelling, never fully replicated by any other title, L.A. Noire remains one of the most fascinating experiments of its console generation.

ps3__walking-dead-season-one.teaser: Choices with no clearly right answer; the story of Lee and Clementine amid the ruins of civilization.
ps3__walking-dead-season-one.article:
**The Walking Dead: Season One** by Telltale Games builds on Robert Kirkman's comic and tells its own story of Lee Everett, an escaped convict who, in a collapsing world, becomes the protector of a young girl named Clementine. The game is split into five episodes and relies on dialogue choices, fast quick-time action sequences, and simple puzzles, with the main emphasis on relationships between characters and moral decisions that have no clearly right solution. The group of survivors Lee gradually meets faces not only attacks by the infected but also internal conflicts, a lack of resources, and the question of who can still be trusted amid the ruins of civilization, with tension inside the group often proving just as dangerous as threats from outside.

On PlayStation 3, the game worked as an episodic title available through PlayStation Network, and later also as a complete package. The comic-book-inspired art style hid technical limitations well and gave the game a distinctive visual identity, while the restrained, atmospheric soundtrack heightened the tension and sorrow running through the whole story. The player's choices have limited impact on the actual branching of the plot, but thanks to strong character writing and voice performances, every decision feels emotionally weighty, and players remember the consequences of their choices, and who they lost along the way, for a long time.

The Walking Dead: Season One is now considered one of the key titles that popularized the modern choice-based narrative adventure and defined the direction of the whole genre for years to come, including the studio's own further seasons and the work of competing studios. The relationship between Lee and Clementine is among the most talked-about game stories of its time, and even with the years since, the game remains an emotionally powerful experience that showed games can tell dramas comparable to film or literature — and for many players, the ending of the first season has stuck in memory as one of the strongest moments in the history of the genre.

**Why play it:** For the emotionally powerful story of Lee and Clementine, which proved that games can tell dramas comparable to film — The Walking Dead: Season One remains one of the genre's most powerful experiences to this day.

ps3__kingdoms-of-amalur-reckoning.teaser: A fantasy world by R. A. Salvatore and Todd McFarlane; classes can be freely combined.
ps3__kingdoms-of-amalur-reckoning.article:
**Kingdoms of Amalur: Reckoning** is an action RPG set in the vast fantasy world of Amalur, created for the game by writer R. A. Salvatore in collaboration with artist Todd McFarlane. The player takes on the role of a resurrected being with no fixed fate, which allows them to alter the very course of events within the fixed order of destiny the world is built on. The game offers a flexible class system based on combining three skill trees, so the player can build their own combat style, from warrior through rogue to mage, and the skill system allows freely combining elements of multiple classes without being locked into a single fixed class, meaning the player can redirect their character in a completely different direction as the game progresses.

The combat system is one of the game's strongest features — fast, action-packed, and full of flashy combos and special strikes, setting it apart from more traditional, slower Western RPGs. On PS3, the game offered a sprawling open world full of side quests, factions, dungeons, and collectibles, though technically it wasn't the most demanding title of the generation, and loading times and minor technical hiccups were noticeable. The atmosphere is rounded out by a distinctive visual style close to comic-book stylization and orchestral music underscoring the epic tone of a story that plays out against the backdrop of a struggle between mortal realms and immortal fae factions.

Kingdoms of Amalur was made with the involvement of 38 Studios and Big Huge Games, and became well known also because of the complicated fate of the development studio, which went bankrupt shortly after release, ending the planned sequel and further expansion of the game world. Even so, the game gained a number of fans thanks to its wealth of content and enjoyable combat system, and is still seen today as an underrated, honestly crafted piece of fantasy RPG that offers dozens of hours of content for a reasonable price, and many players find it satisfying even as a standalone, self-contained experience regardless of the sequel's fate.

**Why play it:** For fantasy RPG fans who'll appreciate dozens of hours of honest content and an enjoyable combat system at a reasonable price, despite this being an underrated title from a now-defunct studio.

ps3__witcher-2-assassins-of-kings-enhanc.teaser: A mature RPG from CD Projekt RED. The second chapter branches into two different storylines depending on your choice.
ps3__witcher-2-assassins-of-kings-enhanc.article:
**The Witcher 2: Assassins of Kings Enhanced Edition** brought to PlayStation 3 an expanded version of the PC RPG by CD Projekt RED, continuing the story of witcher Geralt of Rivia amid the political intrigue and warfare of the northern kingdoms. The game builds on mature storytelling full of morally ambiguous decisions whose consequences significantly shape the rest of the story, including the pivotal split of the second chapter into two different story branches depending on the choice made, which fundamentally changes which characters and locations the player sees in that passage — so two different players can experience a markedly different second chapter.

The console version adapted the controls of a combat system that combines tactical planning, signs, and alchemy for the gamepad, and added new content, additional quests, and reworked opening tutorial sections that make it easier to enter the complex universe drawn from Andrzej Sapkowski's book series. Visually, it was one of the most striking RPGs of the generation, with a dense, gritty, and believable fantasy aesthetic and distinctive music blending Slavic motifs with an epic orchestral sound, rounding out the harsh, realistic atmosphere of a medieval conflict.

Enhanced Edition proved that a demanding, story-heavy PC RPG could work on console without losing its identity, and opened the door to the world of the Witcher for many players even before the arrival of the third installment. The game was praised for its character writing, moral complexity, and willingness not to give the player easy answers, and along with the rest of the series, it helped build CD Projekt RED's reputation as a studio capable of making world-class RPGs. Even today, Witcher 2 is remembered as an important milestone on the road to the later Witcher 3, and as proof that a European studio can compete with the great Western and Japanese RPG makers.

**Why play it:** For players who want to know the roots of the Witcher before the third installment, and who'll appreciate the character writing and moral complexity that defined CD Projekt RED's reputation.

ps3__white-knight-chronicles.teaser: A JRPG exclusive to PS3 from Level-5; combat with an MMO feel and transformation into a giant knight.
ps3__white-knight-chronicles.article:
**White Knight Chronicles** is a JRPG exclusive to PlayStation 3 from Level-5, combining traditional Japanese storytelling with a combat system inspired by MMOs. The player takes on the role of young Leonard, who, during an attack on his home town, accidentally bonds with legendary armor called the White Knight, gaining the ability to transform into a giant warrior. The story revolves around intrigue between kingdoms, lost magic, and the hero's journey from ordinary townsperson to protector of an entire region, accompanied along the way by Princess Cisna and other companions with their own motivations and secrets, whose fates gradually intertwine with the main plot about a struggle for power between neighboring kingdoms.

Battles take place in real time on a tactical, active-pause basis, where the player selects skills from a prepared list and also directs the behavior of party members. On PS3, the game offered an extensive world to explore as well as an online co-op mode that let players complete quests together outside the main storyline — a fairly unusual feature at the time for a singleplayer-leaning JRPG, and one that foreshadowed the later trend of blending classic JRPGs with online features. Visually, the game leaned on typical Level-5 style with colorful graphics and expressive characters, complemented by orchestral music that underscores both the fairy-tale and adventurous tone of the story.

While White Knight Chronicles did not reach the popularity of other major Level-5 franchises like Ni no Kuni or Dark Cloud, it became one of the titles that helped define Japanese RPGs on PlayStation 3 in the console's early years. The combination of classic storytelling, online co-op, and an active-pause combat system makes it an interesting and still-playable piece for genre fans who appreciate its ambition to connect singleplayer with multiplayer elements at a time when this was more the exception than the rule for major Japanese RPGs.

**Why play it:** For JRPG fans who'll appreciate the combination of classic storytelling with online co-op and an active-pause combat system, at a time when that was more the exception than the rule among major Japanese RPGs.

ps3__star-ocean-last-hope-international.teaser: A space-set prequel to the Star Ocean series from tri-Ace; humanity searches for a new home after a nuclear war.
ps3__star-ocean-last-hope-international.article:
**Star Ocean: The Last Hope International** is the expanded PS3 version of the fourth installment of tri-Ace's Star Ocean series, serving as a prequel to the whole series and following the crew of humanity's first expedition into space after Earth is devastated by nuclear war. The player travels through space full of planets, alien races, and ancient mysteries alongside main hero Edge Maverick and his companions, as the story gradually links the fate of humanity to a wider cosmic conflict and questions about the meaning of humanity's expansion into space, after the crew encounters both more advanced and more primitive alien civilizations.

The combat system continues the series' tradition, built on real-time action battles that take place directly on the game map, where the player switches between characters and combines attacks with dodging and special abilities called Blindside and Rush Mode. The International version for PS3 added, compared to the original Xbox 360 release, improved graphics, new voice acting, additional costumes and scenes, and further content, making it the definitive version of the game. Visually, it was one of the graphically most ambitious JRPGs of its time, though not always fully consistent, complemented by striking orchestral music that accompanies the player from claustrophobic spaceships to sprawling alien planets.

Star Ocean: The Last Hope International is prized especially by the series' devoted fans for its extensive crafting system, deep combat mechanics, and sci-fi-flavored story that sets it apart from the fantasy focus of most competing JRPGs. Although its reception was mixed due to certain design and technical shortcomings, it remains an important title for genre fans and one of the few major sci-fi JRPGs of its generation, offering dozens of hours of content including a rich postgame and an extensive crafting system that rewards patient players.

**Why play it:** For devoted series fans and lovers of sci-fi JRPGs who'll appreciate the extensive crafting, deep combat system, and dozens of hours of content including a rich postgame, despite minor shortcomings.

ps3__el-shaddai-ascension-of-metatron.teaser: An action adventure based on the Book of Enoch; the visuals transform radically as you progress.
ps3__el-shaddai-ascension-of-metatron.article:
**El Shaddai: Ascension of the Metatron** is an action adventure from Japanese studio Crim inspired by the apocryphal Book of Enoch, in which the player, as the angel Enoch, sets out on a mission to stop seven fallen angels threatening humanity. The game combines a fluid combat system based on disarming enemies and taking their weapons with platforming sections whose visual style dramatically transforms as the game progresses, from minimalist white surfaces to psychedelic, colorful worlds. As Enoch descends ever deeper into the fallen heavenly realms on his journey, each new area presents a different visual and mechanical treatment, setting the game apart from most action titles of its time and maintaining a constant sense of discovering something new.

On PS3, the game stood out especially for its thoroughly unique audiovisual style, created by art director Sawaki Takeyasu, who brought influences from modern art, fashion, and architecture into the game. The combat system is deliberately simple and accessible, built around three types of weapons and a rhythmic alternation of attack and defense, giving the game the feel of an interactive work of art rather than a classic action game. The soundtrack blends electronic and orchestral elements and rounds out the unusual, dreamlike atmosphere that accompanies the player across wholly distinct visual chapters.

Even though El Shaddai did not do particularly well commercially, it earned a reputation among players and critics as a cult favorite, precisely because of its visual daring and willingness to take an unconventional artistic direction instead of following established genre conventions. Today the game is valued as an example of how an action adventure can function as a full-fledged artistic experience, and it belongs among the titles worth discovering even years later, precisely for a unique aesthetic that had no equal among PS3 titles of its time.

**Why play it:** For players open to unconventional artistic aesthetics, it's worth discovering even years later thanks to a visual daring that had no equal among PS3 titles of its time.

ps3__beyond-good-and-evil-hd.teaser: An HD remaster of the cult adventure about journalist Jade and the conspiracy of the military organization DomZ.
ps3__beyond-good-and-evil-hd.article:
**Beyond Good & Evil HD** is an HD remaster of Ubisoft Montpellier's cult action-adventure, bringing to PlayStation 3 improved graphics and steadier performance for the original 2003 game. The player takes on the role of journalist and fighter Jade, who, together with her uncle Pey'j, runs an orphanage on the planet Hillys and gradually uncovers a conspiracy by the military organization DomZ, which terrorizes the country under the pretext of defending against an alien invasion.

The game combines open-world exploration, simple combat sections, stealth sequences, and photographing wildlife, which serves as a secondary but strongly character-defining activity — Jade documents the world around her as an investigative photographer, sending her photos to alternative media outlets exposing the truth. On PS3, the remaster preserved the original gameplay and distinctive visual style with bold, cartoonishly rendered characters, complemented by atmospheric, genre-spanning music that underscores both the adventurous and conspiratorial tone of the story. The environments of the planet Hillys, from the harbor town to underwater bases and industrial complexes, are among the things that still give the game its reputation as a carefully and cohesively built world.

Beyond Good & Evil has long been considered one of the most underrated titles of its generation, one that failed commercially on its original release but gradually built a cult-classic status prized for its originality, strong lead heroine, and well-thought-out world. The HD version on PS3 let a new generation of players discover this title and served as a reminder of why it's still cited as an example of a game that was in many ways ahead of its time, and why fans have long called for a full sequel, whose development has since been announced, delayed, and revived again over the following years without ever reaching a certain release.

**Why play it:** For players who missed the original, the HD version offers a chance to discover a strong heroine and a well-thought-out world in a title that was ahead of its time, and for which fans have long called for a sequel.

ps3__south-park-stick-of-truth.teaser: An RPG written by the show's own creators, Parker and Stone; South Park humor in full force.
ps3__south-park-stick-of-truth.article:
**South Park: The Stick of Truth** is an RPG made in collaboration between Obsidian Entertainment and South Park creators Trey Parker and Matt Stone, who personally worked on the game's script and visual style. The player creates their own newcomer character who joins the children's war over a wooden stick representing a magical artifact, and the game faithfully mimics the style and humor of the show, including its distinctive animation and vulgar, provocative tone. During the main quest, the player meets almost the entire gallery of familiar characters from the show, from Cartman through Stan and Kyle to the town's other residents, who join the children's war game in their own way and often poke fun at classic RPG clichés.

The combat system draws on classic turn-based RPGs with a focus on timing attacks and defenses, complemented by an item collection, companions drawn from familiar show characters, and exploration of the town of South Park, faithfully recreated in detail for the game. On PS3, the game ran without major technical issues thanks to simple graphics, and focused mainly on content, humor, and faithfulness to the source, with the music and sound effects directly recycling the show's characteristic style, and voice acting handled by the original cast, giving the game the feel of watching an actual episode.

South Park: The Stick of Truth ranks among the best-reviewed games ever based on a TV license, because it doesn't just try to cash in on a well-known brand, but creates a well-thought-out and entertaining RPG with genuine gameplay depth. The combination of genuinely funny writing, a surprisingly functional combat system, and attention to detail made the game one of the most pleasant surprises of its time for players and critics alike, and proof that licensed games can be quality products — something later confirmed by the sequel, The Fractured but Whole, which built further on the same foundation.

**Why play it:** For fans of South Park and RPGs alike, it's proof that licensed games can be quality products — witty writing and a surprisingly functional combat system make it one of the most pleasant surprises of its time.

ps3__assassin-s-creed-iii.teaser: The series moves to the American Revolution with a half-Mohawk hero, Connor Kenway.
ps3__assassin-s-creed-iii.article:
**Assassin's Creed III** shifted the series to the era of the American Revolution and introduced players to Connor Kenway, a young man of half-Mohawk, half-British blood who gets drawn into the conflict between the Assassins and the Templars against the backdrop of the American colonies' fight for independence. On PS3 the game offered a vast open world spanning bustling cities like Boston and New York as well as the wilderness of colonial America, which could be sailed, climbed through the trees, and hunted for game. The story is also framed by parallel modern-day sections featuring Desmond Miles, through which the series' broader mythology tied to an ancient civilization and its influence on human history is revealed, linking every Assassin's Creed entry into one larger whole.

The gameplay expanded the series with new elements such as a naval combat system built around Connor's own ship, the Aquila, a more elaborate crafting and trading system, and improved combat with an emphasis on smoothly chaining counterattacks against multiple enemies. Technically, it was one of the most ambitious titles of the series on PS3, with large crowds, dynamic weather, and changing seasons, accompanied by an epic orchestral soundtrack that underscores the historical, revolutionary tone of the narrative and the atmosphere of colonial America both before and during the war of independence itself.

Assassin's Creed III received a mixed reception from players and critics – while praised for the scope of its world, the naval sequences, and its production values, some players criticized the slow opening and a less charismatic protagonist compared to previous entries. Even so, it remains an important milestone for the series, laying the groundwork for the later naval focus of the sequel Black Flag, and even today it offers one of the most expansive open worlds of the PS3 generation, packed with side activities from hunting and trading to building your own homestead.

**Why play it:** For players craving one of the most expansive open worlds of the PS3 generation, full of hunting, trading, and homestead building, despite a slower start and a less charismatic hero than before.

ps3__wolf-among-us.teaser: A Telltale adventure set in the Fables universe; Sheriff Bigby Wolf, the Big Bad Wolf himself, solves murders.
ps3__wolf-among-us.article:
**The Wolf Among Us** is an episodic adventure game from Telltale Games set in the universe of the Fables comic series, where fairy-tale characters live hidden among humans in New York's Fabletown and try to blend into the human world despite their supernatural nature. The player takes on the role of Sheriff Bigby Wolf, the transformed Big Bad Wolf of classic fairy tales, who investigates a series of brutal murders that reveal a dark secret lurking beneath the surface of an apparently ordinary city. During his investigation, Bigby encounters characters like Snow White, Beast, and Toad, who carry their own, often bittersweet versions of classic fairy-tale fates adapted to the harsh New York setting full of crime, corruption, and lost illusions.

The game builds on the same principle as previous Telltale titles – timed dialogue choices, quick action sequences, and environmental exploration while searching for evidence, with the player's decisions affecting relationships with characters as well as the direction of the investigation. On PS3, the game stood out with a striking visual style inspired by noir comics, featuring contrasting colors and stylized animation, complemented by an atmospheric jazz and electronic soundtrack that perfectly matches the dark, gritty tone of a story set in the streets of 1980s New York.

The Wolf Among Us is considered one of Telltale Games' best-written titles, praised for its strong noir atmosphere, the complex character of Bigby, and its clever blending of fairy-tale archetypes with a brutal crime plot. The game proved that a narrative adventure can work even outside licenses based on films or TV series, and it ranks among the most distinctive representatives of the genre from the PlayStation 3 era, still standing today as a reminder of how powerfully Telltale could work with someone else's license and reshape it in its own storytelling style.

**Why play it:** For fans of narrative adventures and strong noir atmosphere who will appreciate Bigby's complex character and the clever blending of fairy-tale archetypes with a brutal crime plot.

ps3__divinity-ii-dragon-knight-saga.teaser: An RPG from Larian Studios in which a dragon hunter learns to turn into a mighty dragon himself.
ps3__divinity-ii-dragon-knight-saga.article:
**Divinity II: The Dragon Knight Saga** combines two titles from the Belgian studio Larian Studios on PS3 – Divinity II: Ego Draconis and its expansion Flames of Vengeance – into one complete RPG package. The player takes on the role of a dragon hunter who gradually learns to control draconic powers and transform into a mighty dragon himself, giving the game an unusual dual perspective on combat – as a ground-based warrior and as a flying, devastating beast. The Flames of Vengeance expansion then pushes the story further, casting the player as a defender who must face an invasion by the forces the main hero had learned to control, this time from the perspective of a different, newly playable character.

The game offers a vast, open fantasy world full of side quests, puzzles, and a deep skill system that allows experimentation with different playstyles, from melee combat through magic to special abilities such as reading characters' minds, which often opens up unconventional solutions to quests. The PS3 version brought console players the entire complex crafting and combat system, though the technical execution and controls showed their PC roots. The atmosphere is rounded out by a distinctive, at times even humorous narrative tone and an orchestral score underscoring the epic scale of the story about the fight against a dragon cult.

Divinity II: The Dragon Knight Saga expanded Larian's fanbase even before the studio became famous for the Original Sin series, and it showcased the studio's typical approach to gameplay full of freedom, experimentation, and unconventional humor for which Larian is still known today thanks to the later Divinity: Original Sin series. For fans of Western RPGs it represents a hefty, content-packed title that, despite some minor technical flaws, offers dozens of hours of engaging fantasy adventure with an inventive dragon mechanic and a freedom that few console RPGs offered at the time.

**Why play it:** For fans of Western RPGs who will appreciate the freedom, experimentation, and unconventional humor typical of Larian even before the Original Sin series, along with an inventive dragon mechanic and dozens of hours of content.

ps3__sonic-generations.teaser: A celebration of 20 years of Sonic: classic 2D and modern 3D hedgehog across legendary levels.
ps3__sonic-generations.article:
**Sonic Generations** was released in 2011 to celebrate Sonic the Hedgehog's twentieth anniversary, combining two versions of Sonic in one game – the classic 2D Sonic and the modern 3D Sonic. The player progressively works through reimagined versions of iconic levels from across the series' history, from Green Hill Zone to City Escape, with each level having two variants corresponding to both styles of play. Classic Sonic offers a side-scrolling view with an emphasis on fluid movement and jumps, while Modern Sonic adds fast running through 3D space with elements of quick-time events and drifting. The framing story, in which a mysterious force drains the color from Sonic's world and summons his younger self, mainly serves as an excuse to meet characters and bosses from various periods of the series, from Dr. Robotnik to Metal Sonic and Perfect Chaos.

Technically, the game ran smoothly on PS3 and looked great – colorful, detailed environments and a reworked soundtrack with remixes of the original tracks rank among the best the series has offered. Besides the linear story progression, the game also offers side challenges, collectibles, and time leaderboards that extend its lifespan for players chasing a perfect run. The atmosphere is nostalgic yet fresh thanks to modern visual effects and a fast pace. The musical score, combining orchestral arrangements with electronic elements, remains highly regarded among fans to this day.

After a string of less successful entries, Generations was received as a strong return to form, and many consider it one of the best modern Sonic titles overall. Reviewers particularly praised the precision of the controls in the classic 2D sections, while the 3D segments received somewhat more mixed, though still largely positive, reactions. The game showed that combining nostalgia with modern game design can work if it stays true to what made the original games fun. Even today, Generations is a great entry point for new players and a pleasant trip down memory lane for those who grew up with the classic Sega titles.

**Why play it:** For fans of both classic and modern Sonic, it's a great entry point thanks to precise controls in the 2D sections, as well as a pleasant trip down memory lane for those who grew up with the games on Sega.

ps3__sonic-and-all-stars-racing-transfor.teaser: Sega character kart racing where vehicles transform into boats and planes mid-race.
ps3__sonic-and-all-stars-racing-transfor.article:
**Sonic & All-Stars Racing Transformed** from 2012 is a racing game from Sumo Digital that builds on the concept of kart racing with characters from the Sega universe. The key new feature compared to the previous installment is vehicle transformation on the fly – cars turn into boats when crossing water and into planes in the air, giving tracks dynamic variety and forcing the player to constantly adapt their driving style. Besides Sonic, the roster includes characters from Ratchet & Clank, NiGHTS, Shinobi, and other Sega franchises, each with specific abilities and weapons, so choosing a racer affects not just looks but also strategy on the track. The game offers several modes, from classic races through a World Tour career to competitions focused purely on aerial or aquatic sections.

On PlayStation 3 the game ran smoothly and offered colorful, varied tracks inspired by various Sega game worlds, from Skies of Arcadia to Golden Axe, with each track changing its appearance and layout depending on which vehicle type is currently being driven. The controls are accessible to beginners yet deep enough for competitive players thanks to drifting, shortcuts, and combat power-ups that can be combined in various ways depending on the situation on the track. The soundtrack draws on classic Sega melodies rearranged for a modern sound, which heightens the game's nostalgic feel and will please players familiar with older Sega titles.

Reviews praised the title especially for the variety of its tracks and the inventive transformation mechanic, which set it apart from competing kart racers, and many placed it among the best entries in the genre overall. The multiplayer, whether local or online, was one of the main draws, and many players still rank the game among the best non-Mario kart racers. Even years later, Transformed remains a fun and visually timeless choice for fans of arcade racing and for those looking for a great same-screen multiplayer game.

**Why play it:** For fans of arcade racing and players looking for great same-screen multiplayer fun, thanks to an inventive transformation mechanic and track variety among the best in non-Mario kart racing.
