The game's sound design ranked among the best the series had to offer, with realistic weapon sound effects and tense music underscoring the gravity of the depicted conflicts, and even minor characters got room to develop their own motivations, which was unusual for the series up to that point.

The game became a commercial hit and kicked off a new era for the series with a gradual shift to a live-service approach, seasonal content updates, and a tie-in with the battle royale mode Warzone, which turned Modern Warfare into a gateway to one of the most successful free-to-play shooters of the decade. It's still remembered today as a return to a more realistic, more serious tone for the series after years of sci-fi detours, and as a title that noticeably shaped the direction of the entire Call of Duty brand for years to come.

**Why play it:** For players craving a more realistic, more serious tone for the series and the tie-in with the battle royale mode Warzone, Modern Warfare is the title that kicked off a new era for Call of Duty.

ps4__battlefield-4.teaser: The series' move to Frostbite 3; spectacular, destructible battlefields of the new console generation.
ps4__battlefield-4.article:
**Battlefield 4** was the 2013 flagship of the series' transition to the new console generation, showing on PS4 what the Frostbite 3 engine could do in open, destructible battlefields. The singleplayer campaign follows a squad of US Marines caught up in a crisis between China and Russia, and serves mainly as a spectacular, cinematically directed showcase of technology, featuring collapsing skyscrapers, a sinking aircraft carrier, and a tsunami that reshapes the map on the fly.

The real center of gravity of the game, however, was and remains its expansive multiplayer for up to 64 players, built around four soldier classes, ground and air vehicles, and the Levolution system, which let players trigger massive environmental changes right in the middle of a match. Building destruction, collapsing bridges, and shifting map elevations gave battles an unpredictability that no competing series offered at the time. On PS4, the game ran at a solidly high resolution for the era and delivered the visually most ambitious Battlefield experience of the generation, though its launch was marred by technical issues and extensive post-release fixes.

The game also featured an extensive Commander mode, letting one player coordinate the entire team from a bird's-eye view using artillery support and orders, adding another layer of command-level strategy on top of straightforward shooting. Vehicles ranging from tanks and amphibious boats to fighter jets and attack helicopters gave every map its own tactical rhythm and forced players to adapt their loadout to the terrain and match objectives.

Battlefield 4 remains one of the series' most beloved entries thanks to its honest, tactical multiplayer and teamwork built on communication and space control rather than reflexes alone. Even years later it remains a favorite of players craving military authenticity and large-scale vehicle battles, and its influence is visible in every later entry in the series that has tried to balance destruction, tactics, and accessibility.

**Why play it:** For players craving honest tactical multiplayer built on teamwork and large-scale vehicle battles, Battlefield 4 remains, even years later, one of the series' most beloved entries.

ps4__star-wars-battlefront.teaser: A reboot of the classic without a campaign; purely multiplayer battles across the saga's iconic locations.
ps4__star-wars-battlefront.article:
**Star Wars Battlefront** from 2015 was DICE's reboot of the classic series using the Frostbite engine, and instead of a sprawling campaign it bet purely on multiplayer battles set in the saga's iconic locations, from snowy Hoth through the forests of Endor to desert Tatooine. The game offered no classic story-driven singleplayer; instead it had short missions and training scenarios that served mainly as an introduction to the mechanics.

The title's main strength was its audiovisual presentation. DICE created environments that faithfully evoked the atmosphere of the original trilogy, with authentic weapon sounds, music, and vehicle and hero models like Darth Vader or Luke Skywalker, who could randomly appear right in the middle of a match. Gameplay-wise, it consisted of team-based firefights emphasizing the feeling of being part of the film, complemented by X-wing and TIE fighter flight in separate aerial modes. On PS4 the game benefited from visually impressive blaster and explosion effects, though the depth of the weapon system and the launch content were criticized as thinner compared to the series' previous entries produced by Pandemic Studios.

The gameplay was built on relatively simple, accessible soldier classes supplemented with collectible cards granting bonus abilities, making it easy for players who didn't yet know the series of big online shooters to jump into matches. Iconic weapons from the films, such as the E-11 or DL-44 blasters, were designed with emphasis on their distinctive sound and laser effects, so that every firefight retained a strongly cinematic atmosphere even in gameplay terms.

Despite initial criticism over the missing campaign and the smaller number of maps, the game gradually grew through paid and free expansions and remains valued above all as an audiovisual experience that to this day ranks among the most faithful digital renditions of the Star Wars atmosphere. For many players it represented an emotional return to the series after years away, and it paved the way for the more ambitious but controversial sequel, Battlefront II.

**Why play it:** For Star Wars fans who value audiovisual rendering of the saga's atmosphere over content depth, the game offers one of the most faithful digital renditions of the Star Wars universe.

ps4__tom-clancy-s-division.teaser: A cover-based shooter with RPG loot in a New York devastated by epidemic.
ps4__tom-clancy-s-division.article:
**Tom Clancy's The Division** dropped players into a snow-covered, epidemic-devastated New York, where as agents of the secret Strategic Homeland Division organization they fight to restore order amid anarchy, gangs, and collapsing infrastructure. The game combined cover-based third-person shooting with a deep RPG system of loot, skills, and ever-stronger gear, making it an online action RPG with pronounced looter-shooter elements.

Visually, The Division was among the most impressive titles of its generation. A snow-covered Manhattan with elaborate lighting, drifting snow, and finely modeled streets created a dense, believable atmosphere of a city in crisis, further heightened by a melancholic soundtrack. Besides story missions, the game offered an extensive endgame with the so-called Dark Zone, a risky PvPvE area where players could fight each other for the best loot, creating a tension unseen elsewhere in the genre. On PS4 the game ran stably and managed to deliver a detailed open world without noticeable compromises to its atmosphere.

Players could customize their character through gear with randomly generated properties and specialized skills, such as attack drones or healing turrets, allowing distinct playstyles to be built within a cooperative team. The shared world also connected players outside the active team, who could join an ongoing mission through random street encounters or, conversely, compete against each other in higher-risk areas.

After a troubled launch, when Ubisoft grappled with build imbalance and a lack of endgame content, the game improved considerably through a series of updates and became one of the successful examples of a live-service game that managed to hold its community for years to come. The Division helped popularize the genre of online looter shooters with a realistic setting and paved the way for a successful sequel as well as similarly styled titles from other studios.

**Why play it:** For players interested in online looter shooters with a realistic setting, The Division, after a series of improvements, offers one of the successful examples of a live-service game with a long-sustained community.

ps4__tom-clancy-s-ghost-recon-wildlands.teaser: An open world in a fictional Bolivia; fighting a cartel solo or in four-player co-op.
ps4__tom-clancy-s-ghost-recon-wildlands.article:
**Tom Clancy's Ghost Recon Wildlands** brought the series into a sprawling open world set in a fictional Bolivia, where a four-member elite Ghost unit fights the powerful Santa Blanca drug cartel. Players could run the operation solo with AI teammates or in full cooperation with up to four human players, making the game one of the most ambitious attempts of its time at an open tactical action world.

Gameplay-wise, the game was built on freedom of approach. Missions against individual cartel commanders could be completed in any order and with a variety of tactics, from silent infiltration with long-range sniping, through vehicles and drones for reconnaissance, to open firefights. The sprawling map of Bolivia offered a varied range of environments, from mountains and salt flats to rainforests and cities, and on PS4 it managed to render impressive long-distance views, albeit with some compromises in texture detail and vegetation density compared to more powerful platforms. The synchronized-kill and target-marking system allowed for deliberate team coordination that rewarded patience and planning before action.

The audio design and the atmosphere of the South American cartel war, complemented by radio chatter, news broadcasts, and local music, gave the world of Bolivia credibility, although the game deliberately avoided treating the politically sensitive drug issue too literally. Gradually unlocking skills and specializations let players tailor a soldier to the role of sniper, engineer, or support medic, which, in cooperation with three other players, led to a well thought-out division of roles within the team.

Wildlands received mixed reactions at launch due to its at times repetitive mission structure and lighter enemy AI, but thanks to its extensive cooperative content and the genuine joy of moving freely across a huge world it found a loyal community of players. The game showed that the concept of tactical action could be successfully expanded into the open-world format, and this direction later steered the series toward its next entry, Breakpoint.

**Why play it:** For fans of cooperative play and free movement across a huge open world, Wildlands is a showcase of how tactical action can be successfully expanded into the open-world format, despite its more repetitive missions.

ps4__far-cry-4.teaser: The Himalayan kingdom of Kyrat under the rule of the eccentric despot Pagan Min.
ps4__far-cry-4.article:
**Far Cry 4** took players into the fictional Himalayan kingdom of Kyrat, oppressed by the brutal dictatorship of the eccentric despot Pagan Min, one of the series' most memorable villains. The player takes on the role of Ajay Ghale, who, while on a journey to scatter his mother's ashes, gets caught up in a civil war between the government regime and the rebel Golden Path, and must decide which side he ultimately stands on.

The game continued the recipe of the previous entry, an open world full of towers to unlock the map, animal hunting to upgrade gear, and networks of outposts to capture, but enriched it with mountainous verticality, jetpack-like wingsuit gliding, and for the first time a full two-player cooperative mode for story missions. Kyrat, with its temples, villages, and wildlife ranging from tigers to elephants, offered a visually rich and colorful setting on PS4, accompanied by striking music inspired by South Asian culture. The AI of both animals and enemies gave the world a sense of a living, unpredictable place, where a plan to storm an outpost could be ruined at any moment by a wild rhino attack.

Optional co-op let a second player join directly into the host's world and go through story missions and side activities together, a new and welcomed shared-fun element for the series. Side activities ranging from hunting rare animals through rescuing hostages to liberating enemy outposts gave Kyrat the feel of a living, densely layered world that could be explored in many different ways.

Both critics and players praised Far Cry 4 above all for its charismatic villain Pagan Min and for its refined, more accessible gameplay compared to the third entry, though some noted the similarity of its structure to the previous game. The game became a commercial success and cemented the series' position as a synonym for open worlds full of towers, outposts, and emergent moments that defined an entire generation of sandbox action games.

**Why play it:** For fans of open worlds full of towers, outposts, and the charismatic villain Pagan Min, Far Cry 4 offers more accessible and refined gameplay compared to the third entry.

ps4__wolfenstein-new-order.teaser: An alternate history where the Nazis won the war; a story-ambitious shooter.
ps4__wolfenstein-new-order.article:
**Wolfenstein: The New Order** revived a fading series as a deliberate, story-ambitious first-person shooter set in an alternate history in which Nazi Germany won the Second World War and dominated most of the planet using advanced technology. The player returns to the role of veteran B. J. Blazkowicz, who wakes from years in a coma into a devastated world and joins a resistance cell fighting for the last remnants of freedom.

The Swedish studio MachineGames bet on a combination of raw, brutal action with an unexpectedly emotional and human story, full of quiet moments, moral dilemmas, and unusually well-developed side characters. The gameplay was built on a classic old-school shooter approach with dual-wielded weapons, health that only partially regenerated, and the choice between loud infiltration and silent elimination using knives and suppressed weapons. On PS4 the game ran smoothly and technically clean, with a striking art direction full of monumental Nazi architecture and industrial fortresses, accompanied by an intense, synthesizer-driven soundtrack.

Side characters of the resistance were given ample room during downtime between missions so that the player could genuinely experience their fates and build a relationship with them, which was unusual for action shooters of the time. Between missions, the player could freely walk around the resistance base and listen to conversations among its members, deepening the connection to a world that otherwise offered mostly a linear progression through chapters.

The New Order was received, both at launch and in hindsight, as one of the best comebacks of an established franchise, one that managed to combine old-school pacing with modern storytelling and an authorial approach to alternate history. The game launched a new era for the series, with sequels Old Blood, New Colossus, and the spin-off Youngblood, and is still considered one of the best singleplayer shooters of its generation.

**Why play it:** For players craving an honest singleplayer shooter, The New Order combines old-school pacing with modern storytelling and alternate history in one of the best comebacks of an established franchise of its generation.

ps4__mad-max.teaser: A post-apocalyptic wasteland inspired by Miller's films; building the perfect war machine.
ps4__mad-max.article:
**Mad Max** brought the post-apocalyptic world inspired by George Miller's film series into a sprawling open sandbox full of wrecks, gangs, and a waterless wasteland. As the titular Max, the player crosses a parched landscape with the goal of building the perfect war vehicle called the Magnum Opus and escaping territory controlled by the tyrannical warlord Scabrous Scrotus and his henchmen.

The core of the gameplay consisted of vehicular combat full of ramming, harpoons, and explosives, complemented by third-person fistfights and exploration of a desert world full of side activities, from destroying enemy camps through gathering resources to upgrading the car and Max himself. Despite its monotonous desert setting, the open world was surprisingly varied thanks to sandstorms that altered visibility and tactics, as well as the technical detail of vehicles, whose components could be visibly upgraded and damaged. On PS4 the game offered a solidly smooth performance and an atmospheric, visually unified setting steeped in the parched, raw aesthetic of the film source.

The game lacked an official tie-in with the character of Furiosa or other elements of the film Mad Max: Fury Road, which was released in theaters shortly after the game's launch, yet its own post-apocalyptic story of revenge and survival held a consistent tone and visual language with the entire film brand. The extensive Magnum Opus upgrade tree let players gradually turn the car from a fragile wreck into an armored fortress with plating, a harpoon, and a mounted machine gun, giving a sense of tangible progress in an otherwise harsh world.

While reviews praised above all the vehicular combat system and the atmosphere, the game was occasionally criticized for a repetitive side-quest structure typical of Avalanche Studios' open worlds. Even so, Mad Max found its community thanks to a faithful handling of the license and the satisfying feeling of destroying enemy vehicles, and to this day it is valued as one of the best game adaptations of the post-apocalyptic universe.

**Why play it:** For fans of destructive vehicular combat and post-apocalyptic atmosphere, Mad Max offers a faithful handling of the license, even though its side quests suffer from the repetitiveness typical of Avalanche's open-world games.

ps4__just-cause-3.teaser: Physics-driven destruction in the fictional Medici against dictator General Di Ravello.
ps4__just-cause-3.article:
**Just Cause 3** returned players to the role of Rico Rodriguez, an agent fighting to liberate his fictional home Mediterranean republic of Medici from dictator General Di Ravello. The series' signature emphasis on absurd, physics-driven action reached its largest form yet on PS4, with an open world full of mountains, islands, and cities awaiting complete destruction.

The foundation of the gameplay remained the iconic grappling hook, letting players combine parachute, wingsuit, and grapple into fluid uninterrupted movement across the whole map, complemented by an extensive arsenal of weapons and vehicles from tanks to fighter jets. The game focused on liberating villages and towns from the regime's rule by destroying propaganda statues, towers, and military infrastructure, with destruction designed to be spectacular and almost limitless. Buildings collapsed, tanks exploded in chain reactions, and bridges crumbled under the force of explosives. On PS4, the scale of destruction and the open world sometimes hit the console's technical limits, showing up as frame-rate drops during larger explosions, but the overall sense of freedom of movement wasn't fundamentally undermined by this.

The game was rounded out by a challenge editor and a system of unlockable upgrades for the hook, parachute, and wingsuit, which gradually expanded movement abilities and allowed for ever more spectacular cascading traversals across the entire island archipelago. The sprawling map of Medici, made up of a mainland and dozens of smaller islands, offered considerable vertical and horizontal terrain variety, from snow-capped mountain peaks to sunny coastlines full of military ports.

Critics praised above all the joy of movement using the hook and wingsuit and the honest, no-strings-attached fun of destruction, even though the story and side content were seen as secondary to the technical stunts. Just Cause 3 became a symbol of the sandbox destruction-action genre with no pretense of realism, and its movement system influenced later open-world games striving for similarly fluid traversal.

**Why play it:** For players craving no-strings-attached fun from moving with the hook and wingsuit and honest destruction with no emphasis on realism, Just Cause 3 is a symbol of sandbox action whose movement system influenced later open-world games.

ps4__vanquish.teaser: Frenetic action from PlatinumGames featuring rocket-powered ground slides amid firefights.
ps4__vanquish.article:
**Vanquish** is a fast, stylized third-person shooter from PlatinumGames that arrived on PS4 in remastered form, reaffirming its reputation as one of the best-designed action titles of its generation. Players control agent Sam Gideon in an ARS suit equipped with a rocket-powered ground slide that enables lightning-fast moves between cover during intense firefights against a robotic army of Russian separatists aboard a space station.

The game is built on a perfectly tuned rhythm of action. Slow-motion sliding, explosive battles against giant robots, and clever weapon combinations create a sense of ballet amid chaos, typical of director Shinji Mikami's work. The campaign is deliberately short and intense, without unnecessary padding, which sets it apart from most modern shooters, and emphasizes replaying individual sections on higher difficulties for a better score. The remastered PS4 version offered higher resolution and a more stable frame rate, which let the precise controls the entire gameplay is built on truly shine.

Battles against giant robots require spotting weak points and quickly switching between cover, sliding, and precise long-range shooting, with the game constantly pushing players to stay on the move, since standing still is practically a death sentence. A slow-motion module triggered by a near-fatal hit gives players a last-second chance to dodge incoming fire and land a precise shot on the enemy, which became one of the game's most defining features.

At its original release, Vanquish was praised by critics as mechanically brilliant, though commercially less successful, and the remastered edition let it find an audience that had missed it at launch. Today it is regarded as a cult classic of the action shooter genre and is often cited as an example of perfect pacing and movement design that inspired a number of later action games.

**Why play it:** For fans of action shooters with perfect pacing and movement design, Vanquish is a cult classic that the remaster brought to an audience who had missed it at launch.

ps4__metal-gear-rising-revengeance.teaser: PlatinumGames steered Metal Gear away from stealth toward action; Raiden slices through almost everything with his katana.
ps4__metal-gear-rising-revengeance.article:
**Metal Gear Rising: Revengeance** steered the Metal Gear series away from stealth mechanics toward stylized action, courtesy of PlatinumGames, a studio specializing in dense, fast-paced combat systems. Players take on the role of the cyborg Raiden, a former child soldier and katana-wielding ninja who, after leaving government service, works as a private mercenary fighting a private military company spreading chaos across the world.

The game's key mechanic is the so-called Blade Mode, which lets players slice enemies and the environment with precision in any direction in slow motion, resulting in flashy battles and boss fights, quite literally cut to pieces, full of charismatic, over-the-top theatrical villains. The combination of fast parrying, aggressive combos, and the ability to regenerate health by ripping out a defeated enemy's core creates a distinctive identity, quite different from the main series' slower, tactical tone. On PS4 the game ran smoothly and made use of a stylized, metallic-glossy visual style backed by an intense rock and metal soundtrack that underscores the boss fights.

The game also included side VR missions in the style of the series' classic training simulators, plus a chapter-rating system based on speed, style, and accuracy that encouraged repeat playthroughs and honing combat skills. The game world, though told fairly linearly, offers small detours within each chapter with side battles and collectibles that reveal further layers of Raiden's traumatic childhood.

At release, Revengeance was praised chiefly for its precise combat system and unforgettable, over-the-top dramatic moments, despite the campaign's relatively short length. It is still regarded today as one of the best action titles of its generation and a showcase example of Japanese studio collaboration that managed to combine the serious Metal Gear brand with a genuinely tongue-in-cheek yet mechanically deep take on action.

**Why play it:** For fans of precise combat systems and over-the-top dramatic moments, Revengeance offers one of the best action titles of its generation, despite its relatively short campaign.

ps4__sniper-elite-4.teaser: The iconic slow-motion X-ray bullet-hit cams; the fourth game has the series' largest levels.
ps4__sniper-elite-4.article:
**Sniper Elite 4** set the sniper series in sunny Italy during World War II, where agent Karl Fairburne helps the Italian resistance fight the fascist regime and Nazi forces developing new weapons technology. The series is known chiefly for its iconic system of slow-motion X-ray bullet-hit cams, which show an enemy's destroyed organs and bones in detail, and the fourth game develops this feature further with larger, more open levels.

Compared to previous entries, the fourth game offered significantly larger maps with several approach routes, allowing players to plan long-range engagements while accounting for wind, gravity, and heart rate affecting aim precision. The game supports both a purely stealthy approach with close-range takedowns of patrols and a more aggressive approach using sabotage and explosives, and it also offers a cooperative multiplayer mode for the campaign and standalone survival challenges. On PS4 the game rendered sprawling Italian landscapes with views of villages, harbors, and military bases that encourage careful planning of sniper positions, accompanied by atmospheric, understated music.

Alongside the story campaign, the game offered a standalone survival mode for defending a position against waves of enemies, plus competitive challenges focused purely on the accuracy and speed of long-range target elimination. The settings of Italian towns and villages occupied by fascist and Nazi units gave players freedom in choosing approach routes, whether across rooftops, through sewers, or across open fields with tall grass offering natural cover.

Sniper Elite 4 was received by critics as a significant improvement over previous entries thanks to greater freedom and a better balance of stealth and action elements, cementing the series' position as the leading representative of the tactical sniper genre. For fans of precise, deliberate long-range shooting, it remains one of the most complete experiences of its kind on PS4 to this day.

**Why play it:** For fans of precise, deliberate long-range shooting, Sniper Elite 4's balanced stealth and action elements make it one of the most complete tactical sniper experiences on PS4.

ps4__resident-evil-village.teaser: The eighth entry in the series shifts RE7's horror toward a more action-oriented style close to the RE4 classic.
ps4__resident-evil-village.article:
**Resident Evil Village**, the eighth entry in the main series, followed on from the events of Resident Evil 7 and returned players to the role of Ethan Winters, who, after several peaceful years with his family, finds himself amid a snowbound village full of mutants, vampire women, and terrifying cults while trying to find his kidnapped daughter. The game combines the previous entry's first-person perspective with a markedly more action-oriented pace, closer to the style of the classic Resident Evil 4.

The village and its surroundings, including the gothic castle of Lady Dimitrescu, a mill, a fishing village, and underground laboratories, form a series of varied, densely atmospheric settings the player moves through while solving puzzles, managing a limited inventory, and fighting mutated enemies with firearms bought and upgraded from the mysterious merchant Duke. The game skillfully alternates the tension of survival horror with more intense action segments, including major boss fights, and ran technically very solidly on PS4, with detailed lighting and a dense atmosphere heightened by impressive sound design and music.

The game also included a bonus Mercenaries mode for fast, score-based battles against waves of enemies, and offered a short pre-release demo that helped build major anticipation thanks to the sequence set in Lady Dimitrescu's castle. The crafting and weapon-upgrading system at merchant Duke's shop motivated players to explore the environment carefully and gather materials, which linked the game's survival elements to its more action-focused core in a natural, unforced way.

Village received largely positive reception at launch for its varied settings, its return to a more action-oriented yet still tense take on the series, and unforgettable characters like the towering Lady Dimitrescu, who quickly became a pop-culture phenomenon. The game confirmed that Capcom can successfully balance survival horror and action, and it is regarded as one of the high points of the modern Resident Evil era, one that introduced the series to a wider audience in an accessible way.

**Why play it:** For fans of varied settings and a balanced mix of survival horror and action, Village offers one of the high points of the modern Resident Evil era, accessible even to newcomers to the series.

ps4__persona-5-royal.teaser: A polished version of one of the generation's most distinctive JRPGs; its stylization is unmistakable.
ps4__persona-5-royal.article:
**Persona 5 Royal** is an expanded, polished version of one of the generation's most distinctive Japanese RPGs, in which the player leads a group of Tokyo students who transform by night into the Phantom Thieves of Hearts and infiltrate grotesquely stylized "Palaces" - the subconscious of corrupt adults who harbor a warped version of their own desire for power. By day, the protagonist attends school, works part-time jobs, and builds relationships (so-called Confidants) with people around him, which gradually unlock new Persona abilities used by the heroes in turn-based battles built around enemies' weaknesses and resistances. The Royal edition adds a new playable character, an entire third act of story set after the original ending, reworked dungeons, and fresh animations and musical arrangements, so even players familiar with the original Persona 5 get a significantly enriched and longer experience.

On PS4 the game runs smoothly even in more complex battle sequences and visually remains one of the most stylish titles of the generation - the red-and-black menus, Shoji Meguro's jazz-acid music, and the constantly animated interface turn every menu and purchase into an experience full of character. The combat system remains accessible to newcomers but offers considerable depth thanks to Persona fusions, building a personal arsenal of abilities, and tactically exploiting elemental weaknesses and so-called baton touch combos. This time the dungeons are largely hand-designed rather than procedurally generated as in previous entries in the series, which noticeably improves the game's pacing and the feeling of exploration, and rewards attentive players with hidden treasures.

Critically, the Royal edition was received as one of the best versions of the game ever made and cemented Persona's position as the genre's flagship for mainstream audiences outside Japan, reflected in the meteoric rise in the series' popularity in the West. It is still cited today as an example of how to elegantly combine a social simulation of everyday life with a deep turn-based RPG, and it remains the recommended entry point into the entire series for new players and for those who want to experience the definitive version of the story.

**Why play it:** For new players and fans wanting the definitive version of the story, the Royal edition is an elegant blend of social simulation and deep turn-based RPG, and the recommended entry point into the whole series.

ps4__life-is-strange.teaser: An episodic adventure about rewinding time; choices come to fruition episodes later.
ps4__life-is-strange.article:
**Life is Strange** is an episodic adventure from studio Dontnod in which photography student Max Caulfield unexpectedly learns to rewind time and uses this ability to search for her missing friend Chloe in the fictional town of Arcadia Bay, Oregon. The game is built on a slow pace, carefully crafted dialogue, and moral decisions whose consequences often only surface episodes later - a signature feature is also the ability to rewind time and try a different response, which makes decision-making less stressful, yet all the more deliberate and experimental for every player. The five episodes gradually escalate from teenage drama about friendship and first loves to markedly darker themes like bullying, addiction, domestic violence, and mental health, and the game isn't afraid to tackle even more controversial topics such as suicide. The setting of Blackwell Academy high school and the surrounding town feels believable thanks to carefully written side characters, each with their own small storylines independent of the main plot.

On PS4 the title benefited from simple yet atmospheric graphics with a painted, watercolor-like touch, and above all from a soundtrack full of indie and folk music by artists like Jose Gonzalez, which heightened key emotional scenes. The controls are minimalist - walking, interacting with the environment, taking photos, and dialogue wheels - so the main emphasis lies on the story, atmosphere, and the player's relationship to the individual characters, which was a relatively fresh approach at the time of release.

Life is Strange became one of the most influential narrative titles of the mid-decade and helped popularize the episodic adventure genre with an emphasis on choices with long-term impact, similarly to Telltale's earlier work. It is still praised today for its sensitive, honest portrayal of young characters and their problems, and for how naturally it linked the time-travel game mechanic with themes of memory, guilt, and regret over missed opportunities. The game's success subsequently launched an entire series of further entries and spin-offs, but it is the first game that remains the one still cited today as the genre's defining moment.

**Why play it:** For players who appreciate a sensitive portrayal of young characters and a time-travel mechanic tied to themes of memory and regret, the first game remains the defining moment of the episodic adventure genre.

ps4__firewatch.teaser: An atmospheric walking simulator conducted over a radio in the forests of Wyoming.
ps4__firewatch.article:
**Firewatch** is a short, atmospheric first-person adventure in which the player takes on the role of Henry, a man fleeing his own crumbling life to a remote fire lookout post in Wyoming in 1989. Most of the game unfolds through radio conversations with his supervisor Delilah, as the player walks through the forest, completes small lookout duties, and gradually uncovers strange happenings around him that slowly grow from a calm summer stroll into a paranoid thriller with a hint of conspiracy. Mechanically, it's more of a so-called walking simulator with a map, compass, and radio than an action game - the emphasis is on exploring the landscape, naturally written dialogue, and building the relationship between the two main characters. The player sets their own pace for walking through each section of forest, so it's entirely possible to just stop and listen to the surrounding nature, which only heightens the sense of isolation in the wilderness.

On PS4, the title stood out chiefly for its striking visual style with a rich color palette inspired by American national parks, and for its quality voice acting, which carries the entire story without a single face on screen besides Henry's hands. The gameplay is deliberately simple and undemanding on reflexes, but the environment is designed to reward attentive players with small details, notes, and side discoveries scattered across the whole map.

Firewatch became one of the most cited examples of the walking sim genre and showed that even a game without combat, an inventory, or complex mechanics can tell a powerful, emotionally memorable story about loneliness and escaping reality. It is still praised today chiefly for its precise dialogue writing and its ability to evoke a sense of tension and uncertainty using nothing but the environment, the sound of the forest, and a voice on the radio. The game's short length also proved to be an asset, since the story never drags things out and ends before the initial sense of mystery could wear off.

**Why play it:** For players craving an emotionally powerful story without combat or an inventory, Firewatch offers precisely written dialogue and tension created purely by the environment, the sound of the forest, and a voice on the radio, all in a satisfyingly short playtime.

ps4__heavy-rain.teaser: An interactive thriller built on quick-time events; any character can die permanently.
ps4__heavy-rain.article:
**Heavy Rain** is an interactive thriller from studio Quantic Dream that arrived on PS4 as a remastered version of the original PS3-era title with improved graphics and more stable performance. The story follows four distinct characters caught up in the hunt for a serial killer known as the Origami Killer, with the player alternately controlling a desperate father searching for his kidnapped son, a journalist chasing the truth, an aging private detective, and a young FBI agent with a hidden secret. The game plays out mostly through quick-time events and contextual actions tied to analog stick movements, where nearly every decision or failure can lead to a permanent change in the story, including the definitive death of any of the playable characters. The story also offers several different endings depending on how many characters the player manages to keep alive and how they piece together the various clues leading to the killer.

The remastered PS4 version offered higher resolution and smoother frame rates compared to the original release, better highlighting the cinematic camera direction, character expressions, and detailed movements that Quantic Dream has always prided itself on. The music and careful sound design effectively underscore the game's grim, perpetually rainy atmosphere, which, both thematically and in content, is aimed more at an adult audience due to violence, dark themes, and sensitive subjects like the loss of a child.

Heavy Rain is regarded as one of the defining titles of the interactive film genre and significantly influenced later work by studios like Telltale and Dontnod, which took a similar approach emphasizing choice and story. Even years later it remains interesting for its many story branches and its boldness in making players live with the consequences of their own decisions, though some fans of classic adventure games still dispute certain plot twists as overly melodramatic. It was specifically the PS4 remaster that brought the game to a new generation of players who could experience it for the first time without the limitations of the older console.

**Why play it:** For fans of interactive film with the boldness to live with the consequences of their own decisions, the PS4 remaster offers Heavy Rain without the limitations of the older console, even if some twists come across as overly melodramatic.

ps4__beyond-two-souls.teaser: Quantic Dream's interactive drama told non-linearly across fifteen years of the heroine's life.
ps4__beyond-two-souls.article:
**Beyond: Two Souls** is another interactive drama from Quantic Dream, released on PS4 as a remastered version with improved graphics and more stable performance compared to the original 2013 PS3 release. The player follows fifteen years in the life of Jodie Holmes, a woman bonded to an invisible supernatural entity named Aiden, whom she can directly control at key moments to solve puzzles, fight enemies, and make small supernatural interventions in the surrounding world. The story is told deliberately non-linearly, jumping between different periods of Jodie's life from early childhood through adolescence to adulthood, giving the narrative a cinematic, fragmentary, puzzle-like character that the player gradually pieces together like a mosaic of memories.

The game's main draw was the motion-capture performances of Ellen Page as Jodie and Willem Dafoe as researcher Nathan, which on PS4 shine thanks to sharper textures, better lighting, and smoother transitions between scenes, letting the subtle facial expressions of both actors stand out even in quiet, contemplative moments. The gameplay remains simple - contextual actions, quick-time events, and environmental exploration rather than classic puzzles - so the main emphasis is again on story, emotion, and the cinematic visual presentation of the whole experience.

Beyond: Two Souls divided critics and players due to its non-linear structure and less room for genuine decision-making compared to the earlier Heavy Rain, but it still remains a significant experiment on the border between film and game. It's still talked about today as a showcase of how far you can go with Hollywood casting and motion capture technology within interactive storytelling. Aiden's ability to intervene in the world outside the main heroine's body also remains one of the more original gameplay ideas, one Quantic Dream hasn't used in any other game, since it lets players explore surroundings Jodie herself can't reach.

**Why play:** For players curious about Hollywood casting and motion capture on the border between film and game, Beyond offers the original Aiden soul mechanic, despite a non-linear structure with less room for real decisions.

ps4__vampyr.teaser: A dark vampire RPG - for every character you choose whether to kill them for power or spare them.
ps4__vampyr.article:
**Vampyr** is a dark action RPG from Dontnod, in which the player takes on the role of Dr. Jonathan Reid, who is involuntarily turned into a vampire shortly after returning from World War I and must cope with a constant hunger for blood on the streets of London in 1918, amid a raging Spanish flu epidemic. A key element of the game is the moral dilemma reflected in every non-playable character in the city - each can be thoroughly investigated, their personal story, relationships, and secrets uncovered, and ultimately the player decides whether to kill them for a quick boost to vampiric powers or let them live at the cost of slower character progression, though doing so preserves the health and stability of the whole district and its inhabitants for future chapters of the story.

The combat system combines ordinary and surgical weapons infected with vampire blood with supernatural abilities such as turning into mist, blood claws, or hypnotizing opponents, and on PS4 the game ran solidly, albeit with occasional technical shortcomings typical of a smaller independent studio, such as fluctuating frame rates or minor animation glitches. The atmosphere is completed by a gloomy Victorian England shrouded in fog, disease, and poverty, supported by a melancholic musical score and believably written supporting characters from various layers of society.

Vampyr was praised by critics especially for its bold moral system, which gave real weight even to seemingly minor characters and their fates, and for its dense atmosphere despite a not-quite-polished technical execution and combat system. Today it is seen as an interesting and thoughtful alternative to mainstream vampire games, one that places emphasis on ethical decisions and storytelling rather than flashy, mindless action. It is precisely the need to choose between mercy and power that players remember most about Vampyr, even years after release and despite all the technical flaws that accompanied it.

**Why play:** For players who prefer ethical decisions and storytelling over flashy action, Vampyr offers a bold moral system that gives weight even to supporting characters, despite a not-quite-polished combat system.

ps4__greedfall.teaser: A colonial fantasy RPG from Spiders; diplomacy between factions carries as much weight as the sword.
ps4__greedfall.article:
**GreedFall** is an RPG from the French studio Spiders, set in a fictional colonial world strongly inspired by the seventeenth century, where the player, a diplomat of mysterious origin, sets out for the island of Teer Fradee, full of magic, healing nature, an incurable disease, and growing tension between European colonizers, trading companies, and native tribes. The game combines thorough dialogue choices with a real impact on individual factions and their mutual alliances, alongside real-time action combat that can be supplemented with tactical pauses and a choice between several combat styles - sword and shield, firearms, or magical abilities, with the chosen approach also affecting how the player resolves conflicts with individual factions and their representatives.

On PS4, the title impressed especially with the scope of its open world and the number of quests that sensitively reacted to the player's earlier decisions, even though the graphics and overall technical execution didn't match big-budget RPGs from larger publishers - character animations and some environment textures often felt cheap and stiff. Even so, the atmosphere is held together more by the imaginatively designed world, costume design inspired by Baroque fashion, and orchestral music than by the technical precision of the engine itself.

GreedFall was received as a pleasant surprise from a notably smaller studio, one that took clear inspiration from the style of classic BioWare RPGs and, despite a more limited budget, managed to offer an engaging, believably written world full of politics. It is still praised today by fans of classic decision-driven RPGs for not shying away from complex factional politics and morally gray choices, even though it occasionally clearly runs up against the limits of a smaller production and lower budget. The game's success, after all, gave Spiders room and the publisher's trust to work on further, more ambitious projects.

**Why play:** For fans of classic decision-driven RPGs from BioWare who will appreciate complex factional politics and morally gray choices, GreedFall is an engaging surprise from a smaller studio despite the limits of a lower budget.

ps4__salt-and-sanctuary.teaser: A 2D soulslike inspired by Dark Souls; slow combat and exploration of an interconnected island.
ps4__salt-and-sanctuary.article:
**Salt and Sanctuary** is a 2D action RPG clearly inspired by the Dark Souls series, carrying over its combat toughness, stamina system, and risk of losing progress into a side-scrolling view enriched with metroidvania elements and exploration of an interconnected world. As a shipwrecked pilgrim, the player explores a dark, cleverly interconnected island full of monsters, cults, and mythological horrors, gradually collecting weapons, armor, and spells, and building the character through an extensive skill tree that visually resembles a night sky full of constellations. Combat is deliberately slow and methodical, requiring precise timing of dodges, blocks, and parries, and punishes carelessness with the loss of accumulated salt, the local equivalent of souls from soulslike games, which can be recovered by returning to the spot where you died. The choice of weapons is meanwhile very wide, from heavy two-handed weapons through fast daggers to magic staves.

On PS4, where the game originally launched ahead of other platforms, the carefully animated pixel graphics and hand-drawn environments worked very well thanks to the dark, gothic atmosphere and gloomy, choral music underscoring the despair of the whole island. The level design tightly connects individual areas through shortcuts and hidden paths, which rewards thorough and patient exploration just as in the big action RPGs the game openly draws inspiration from.

Salt and Sanctuary is considered one of the most successful combinations of soulslike mechanics with a classic 2D metroidvania, and it inspired a number of later indie titles in the same genre across platforms. It is still praised today for its fair, honest difficulty, dense atmosphere, and depth of possible character builds, without needing the budget of a large studio to achieve it. The optional cooperative and competitive multiplayer, moreover, offered something that wasn't entirely a given in soulslike games of the time.

**Why play:** For soulslike fans craving a dense 2D metroidvania with fair difficulty and depth of character builds, plus the option to play cooperatively or compete with another player.

ps4__remnant-from-ashes.teaser: A third-person soulslike with procedurally generated levels and three-player co-op.
ps4__remnant-from-ashes.article:
**Remnant: From the Ashes** is an action RPG combining ranged, third-person combat with procedurally generated levels and soulslike elements such as limited healing via flasks, harsh punishment for mistakes, and demanding boss fights. Players explore a post-apocalyptic, heavily devastated Earth invaded by a mysterious entity called the Root, with the world laced with portals to other fantasy and sci-fi dimensions, each with its own unique enemies, weapons, and fragments of story hidden in the environment. Co-op for up to three players is the core of the whole experience, letting players share danger and loot in procedurally varied versions of individual levels on each playthrough, so even repeated play through the same area offers a different layout of enemies and side events.

On PS4, the game offered solid and satisfying action shooting with an emphasis on correct positioning and use of cover, complemented by crafting of weapons, mods, and upgrades from materials obtained primarily from defeated bosses, who also serve as the main source of the game's difficulty and progression. The atmosphere combines dark fantasy with pronounced sci-fi elements and a bleak, locally devastated visual style that nicely underscores the feeling of a lonely fight for survival in a ruined world consumed by an alien power, full of abandoned cities and overgrown vegetation.

Remnant: From the Ashes surprisingly succeeded as a project from a smaller studio that managed to elegantly combine soulslike pacing and difficulty with a cooperative shooter for up to three players, and it earned a loyal fanbase despite a fairly modest marketing campaign at launch. Its success eventually led to several sequels, and the title is still praised today as an inventive alternative for fans of demanding action RPGs who want to share the difficulty with friends rather than face the controller alone.

**Why play:** For players who want to share soulslike pacing and difficulty with friends instead of facing it alone - a cooperative shooter for up to three players offers an inventive alternative among demanding action RPGs.

ps4__tales-of-vesperia-definitive-editio.teaser: The Definitive Edition finally united content that had been split between Xbox 360 and the Japan-only PS3 version.
ps4__tales-of-vesperia-definitive-editio.article:
**Tales of Vesperia: Definitive Edition** brought to PS4, for the first time, a complete and visually unified version of the beloved JRPG from the Tales of series, which had previously been available mainly on Xbox 360 and, in an enriched form, only on the Japanese PS3. The story follows Yuri Lowell, a former knight disgusted by the corruption of the nobility, who together with a colorful group of companions sets out across the fantasy world of Terca Lumireis, where technology based on magical crystals called blastia fundamentally influences politics, the economy, and the everyday life of its inhabitants. The combat system follows the series' traditional action combat - the player directly controls one character in real time within an enclosed arena, while the rest of the team is handled by AI according to finely adjustable tactics and priorities, allowing smooth switching between characters depending on the situation in battle.

Definitive Edition added new playable characters, additional quests, and content compared to the older Japanese release, making it, for the first time, a truly complete version of the game for Western audiences as well, who had been waiting for it for over ten years. On PS4 the title ran smoothly and stably, though visually it is clearly a remaster of an older generation, evident in simpler textures and environment models, but the colorful, cel-shaded art style and charismatic characters hold up well even years later.

Tales of Vesperia has long been considered by JRPG fans one of the best entries in the whole extensive series thanks to its strong story about friendship, sacrifice, and moral ambiguity, and its dynamic, action-based combat system. Definitive Edition on PS4 finally allowed a new generation of players to experience a title that had long been only partially available outside Japan and North America. Fans of the series still often rank it right behind the most celebrated entry, Tales of Symphonia.

**Why play:** For JRPG fans looking for a strong story about friendship and sacrifice paired with a dynamic action combat system - Definitive Edition finally made a long hard-to-access title available to a wider audience.

ps4__ni-no-kuni-wrath-of-white-witch-rem.teaser: A JRPG made in collaboration with Studio Ghibli; its fairy-tale styling remains among the best in the genre.
ps4__ni-no-kuni-wrath-of-white-witch-rem.article:
**Ni no Kuni: Wrath of the White Witch Remastered** is a remastered version of the Japanese RPG from Level-5, created in close collaboration with the famous animation studio Ghibli, whose fairy-tale, hand-drawn visual styling remains among the most impressive in the entire genre to this day. The story follows a young boy named Oliver, who, after suddenly losing his mother, travels through a tear cried into a plush teddy bear into a parallel fantasy world, accompanied by a talking and somewhat cheeky wizard named Drippy, in order to save the world and his own family. The combat system combines turn-based elements with free movement in real time and combat companions called familiars, which can be caught in traps, healed, fed, and gradually upgraded similarly to the well-known Pokémon series, while being freely swapped between fights depending on the type of opponent.

The PS4 remaster brought noticeably sharper textures, higher resolution, and more stable framerate compared to the original 2013 PS3 release, which let the hand-drawn environments, character expressions, and smooth animations in the typical Ghibli style shine even more, lending even ordinary battles a fairy-tale lightness. The music for the whole game was composed by Joe Hisaishi, longtime musical collaborator of director Hayao Miyazaki, giving the game a cinematic, almost moving emotional atmosphere that is fairly rare for the JRPG genre.

Ni no Kuni was repeatedly praised, both at its original release and at the PS4 remaster, for its visual side, music, and sensitive fairy-tale storytelling, which managed to appeal to both child and adult players across generations. It is still considered one of the most beautiful JRPGs of its generation and a textbook example of a fruitful collaboration between a game studio and a renowned film animation studio. The PS4 remaster, for the first time, allowed the game to be properly appreciated even by players who had for some reason missed the original PS3 version.

**Why play:** For players of all generations looking for a fairy-tale JRPG with gorgeous visuals and music, thanks to a collaboration with a renowned animation studio - and the remaster finally made it properly accessible to those who missed the PS3 version.

ps4__pillars-of-eternity-complete-editio.teaser: An isometric CRPG from Obsidian born from crowdfunding; a spiritual successor to Baldur's Gate.
ps4__pillars-of-eternity-complete-editio.article:
**Pillars of Eternity: Complete Edition** brought to PS4 a classic isometric CRPG from Obsidian Entertainment, which came into being thanks to a successful crowdfunding campaign as a spiritual successor to classics like Baldur's Gate or Icewind Dale. The player creates their own character from an extensive selection of races and classes, journeys through the vast fantasy world of Eora full of religious disputes and old gods, and gradually gets drawn into a dispute surrounding the mysterious phenomenon called Hollowborn, which afflicts newborn children, with the game's main emphasis placed on deep writing, morally ambiguous factions, and tactical real-time combat that can be paused at any moment to issue orders to an entire party of adventurers at once.

The console port had to solve controls that were originally aimed exclusively at mouse and keyboard, which resulted in a reworked, simplified menu and a newly adapted system for selecting targets and characters for the gamepad, without significantly limiting the player's tactical options in combat. There's an enormous amount of text in the game - extensive journals, dialogue, and detailed item descriptions - so Complete Edition on PS4 will appeal especially to players who don't mind reading as a natural part of the experience, in exchange for an unusually elaborate world, history, and factional politics.

Pillars of Eternity was praised at its original PC release as a successful and credible return of the classic CRPG genre financed directly by players, and the console version allowed even people without a PC to sample this more demanding, story-focused style of play. The game is still praised today especially for its writing and elaborate system of faction reputation, even though gamepad controls remain a noticeable compromise compared to the original mouse control. For players who grew up on old isometric RPGs, it's nevertheless a rare opportunity to experience this style of play comfortably from the couch.

**Why play:** For players who grew up on old isometric CRPGs and will appreciate elaborate writing and a factional reputation system, even at the cost of gamepad controls remaining a noticeable compromise compared to a mouse.

ps4__mass-effect-andromeda.teaser: BioWare left Shepard behind for a new galaxy; the jetpack gives combat vertical dynamism.
ps4__mass-effect-andromeda.article:
**Mass Effect: Andromeda** is an action RPG from BioWare that chose to leave the well-known Commander Shepard trilogy behind and move the story six hundred years and one galaxy forward, to the Andromeda galaxy, where humanity sends a huge colonization fleet called the Ark as part of the ambitious Andromeda Initiative. Playing as Pathfinder Ryder, the player freely explores sprawling open planets using the Nomad all-terrain vehicle, builds and supplies outposts, and deals with growing conflicts between humans, the other races of the Milky Way, and the hostile native Kett, while combat combines cover mechanics, a range of special abilities, and a jetpack that enables dynamic vertical movement directly during firefights, setting the game apart from the slower pace of the series' previous entries.

On PS4, the game offered large, genuinely open planets to explore and a noticeably improved, more dynamic combat system compared to previous entries in the series, but at launch it was unfortunately marred by technical issues, bugs, and unnatural, stiff facial animations that quickly became the target of internet mockery and damaged the game's initial reception. Despite that, the atmosphere is well supported by ambient sci-fi music and an extensive codex describing the new galaxy and its inhabitants, though the story itself was generally viewed by critics as noticeably weaker than the beloved original trilogy.

Mass Effect: Andromeda is judged somewhat more kindly in hindsight than it was at launch - the combat system, character building, and planet exploration have found their defenders among players, even though the title remains permanently in the shadow of the previous trilogy and its influence. It thus serves as a reminder of how easily technical problems and a rushed release can damage the perception of an otherwise sincerely ambitious and costly project, one after which the Mass Effect series went quiet for several years.

**Why play it:** For fans of the series willing to forgive technical issues and a rushed release in exchange for a decent combat system, character building, and planet exploration - a reminder of how easily a rushed release can damage even an ambitious project.

ps4__spyro-reignited-trilogy.teaser: A complete remake of Spyro's first three games with modern graphics and faithful mechanics.
ps4__spyro-reignited-trilogy.article:
**Spyro Reignited Trilogy** brings to PlayStation 4 a complete remake of the first three installments of the purple dragon's adventures from the late nineties, this time in a graphically reworked form with modern lighting, detailed textures, and fully animated characters that were missing from the originals due to the hardware of the time. The player flies through colorful worlds, collects gems, frees imprisoned dragons, and breathes fire at enemies, while the core gameplay mechanics - flying, fire attacks, horn charges, and treasure collecting - remain faithful to the originals from the original PlayStation era. The trilogy includes Spyro the Dragon, Ripto's Rage!, and Year of the Dragon, offering dozens of hours of platforming fun split across many thematically distinct levels, each with its own visual style and small gameplay variations.

On PS4 the game runs smoothly at high resolution and benefits from reworked music that keeps the original composers' melodies, just in richer orchestration and with a stronger emphasis on each world's atmosphere. The level design remained essentially unchanged, which was especially appreciated by players who remember the series from childhood, while offering new players an accessible, undemanding platformer with more open levels than many current genre titles. The atmosphere combines fairy-tale stylization with gentle humor and playfulness typical of late-nineties platformers, and the individual areas differ markedly in theme and color palette.

The remake was well received at launch as a fitting tribute to a classic that managed to appeal to both nostalgic fans and a new generation of players unfamiliar with the originals. It also contributed to renewed interest in the Spyro brand and to further projects from Toys for Bob within Activision, including later follow-ups to the related Crash Bandicoot series. Today the game works as a pleasant entry point into the 3D platformer genre for players of all ages, and as proof that a faithfully executed remake can present old values in an attractive modern coat without losing their original charm.

**Why play it:** For nostalgic fans and newcomers alike looking for a pleasant entry point into the 3D platformer genre - a faithfully executed remake that presents old values in a modern coat without losing their original charm.

ps4__crash-bandicoot-4-it-s-about-time.teaser: A direct sequel to the classic trilogy, bypassing the spin-offs; Quantum Masks alter gravity.
ps4__crash-bandicoot-4-it-s-about-time.article:
**Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time** is a direct sequel to the classic Crash Bandicoot 1-3 games, ignoring all the side titles and continuing the story long after the original nineties trilogy. The player once again returns to fast, precise 3D/2.5D platforming, where perfect timing of jumps, spin attacks, and slides is needed to get Crash and Coco past increasingly demanding traps, chasms, and enemies scattered across several different dimensions and time periods. The new addition is the so-called Quantum Masks, which alter the main character's gravity, mass, or phase of matter, adding new puzzle and movement elements to the established formula that the player gradually unlocks throughout the campaign. The level structure also offers alternate timelines, where the player returns to the same environment but with a different goal and a different route, extending the challenge even after first completing a given chapter.

The graphical presentation on PS4 is clean and colorful, with high resolution and stable performance, while the music continues the series' traditional tone with energetic tracks accompanying the acrobatic runs through each level. The game's difficulty is deliberately high, especially when collecting all the crates and completing bonus challenges or optional retro levels in the style of the original games, which was appreciated by players looking for a genuine challenge comparable to the difficulty of nineties platformers, just with modern technical execution and more precise controls. The game also offers local co-op for a second player in the role of supporting characters, adding a pleasant shared-play option to an otherwise strictly solo platformer.

The game was well received at launch as a successful return to the series' roots after the more experimental titles of previous years, and fans appreciated that the developers at Toys for Bob weren't afraid to return to tough, precise platforming action instead of simplifying things. It is still considered one of the most demanding and elaborately crafted 3D platformers of the PS4 generation, and proof that Crash's classic formula can hold up against more modern genre competitors when approached with respect for its roots.

**Why play it:** For players who want tough, precise platforming action without simplification - one of the most demanding and elaborately crafted 3D platformers of the PS4 generation, faithful to the series' roots.

ps4__sackboy-big-adventure.teaser: Sackboy's first full 3D platformer for up to four players; the musical levels are the highlight.
ps4__sackboy-big-adventure.article:
**Sackboy: A Big Adventure** moves the well-known character from the LittleBigPlanet series away from a focus on building your own levels and into a full-fledged 3D platformer emphasizing precise movement, jumping, and cooperative play for up to four players at once. The player moves through varied, thematically diverse worlds, collects bubbles and materials for crafting costumes, and faces boss fights, while the game smoothly alternates between classic jumping sections and more action-heavy sequences, chases, and music-synchronized levels that rank among the game's most memorable moments. The world structure is divided into separate thematic chapters, each offering a different environment and set of enemies, and the player moves between them via a clear map with optional collectibles.

On PS4 the title looks visually rich, with vivid felt, fabric, and paper textures continuing the LittleBigPlanet brand's characteristic handmade style, just translated into a fully three-dimensional space where the character can freely jump between several depth planes. The musical accompaniment plays an active role in many levels, where the character's movement and obstacles sync to the rhythm of pop and orchestral tracks, giving the gameplay noticeable energy and replay value. The multiplayer co-op mode is designed to work both with friends on a single screen and online, and it also offers small competitive elements between teammates.

Sackboy: A Big Adventure was well received at launch as one of the most accessible and enjoyable platformers of its generation, suitable for family play across age groups. Sumo Digital managed to carry the charm of the LittleBigPlanet series into a more traditional platforming framework without losing its playfulness, attention to detail, and handcrafted aesthetic. Today the game works as a reliable choice for players looking for a colorful, well-crafted family platformer with high production quality.

**Why play it:** For family play across age groups - a colorful, craft-like platformer that carries LittleBigPlanet's playfulness and aesthetic into a more accessible, traditional framework.

ps4__littlebigplanet-3.teaser: A 2.5D platformer expanded with three new characters and an elaborate custom level editor.
ps4__littlebigplanet-3.article:
**LittleBigPlanet 3** expands the series with new characters alongside the classic Sackboy - Oddsock, Toggle, and Swoop - each with their own special abilities used to solve puzzles and overcome obstacles scattered across the levels. The core of the game remains 2.5D platforming built on a physics engine, complemented by an extensive editor where players can create their own levels, minigames, and entire gameplay mechanics using elaborate tools and logic circuits, and then share them with the community around the world, including tools for custom scripted gameplay mechanics and simple minigames.

On PS4 the game offers smoother performance and more detailed textures made of fabric, wood, cardboard, and other materials that have long been characteristic of the series' visual style. The campaign takes the player through varied worlds with their own atmosphere and humor, the soundtrack combines licensed tracks with original compositions to build the series' distinctive fairy-tale mood, accompanied by the typical narrator commentary with English voice acting. Cooperative play for up to four players remains one of the pillars of the experience, whether in the campaign or in user-generated content, of which tens of thousands of levels exist after the game's release, spanning puzzles, platforming challenges, and minigames inspired by other genres.

At launch the game was received as a solid, if not groundbreaking, sequel, with the greatest praise going specifically to the expanded editor capabilities and the endless supply of player-created content. With this installment, Sumo Digital proved that the concept of a shared creative tool set within a platformer still has plenty to offer even years on, both to creators and to players looking for new content. Today the game appeals mainly as a huge archive of community creativity and a nostalgic piece for fans of the series from the first half of the PS4 generation.

**Why play it:** For fans of the series and players looking for a huge archive of community-made content - the greatest value comes from the expanded editor and the endless supply of user levels, rather than the campaign itself.

ps4__sonic-mania.teaser: A celebration of Sonic's classic 2D era with modern physics; old and new zones in one package.
ps4__sonic-mania.article:
**Sonic Mania** is a celebration of Sonic the Hedgehog's classic 2D era, built on an engine that follows on from the Sega Genesis titles, but with modern presentation, new physics, and smoother animation of characters and environments. The game combines reworked levels from the original games - such as Green Hill Zone or Chemical Plant Zone - with original new zones created specifically for this title, while the gameplay is built on fast, fluid movement, ring collecting, and exploring alternate routes through each level in the style of nineties platformers, where route familiarity leads to noticeably faster runs. The levels also frequently hide alternate paths and bonus sections that reward thorough exploration and repeated playthroughs of the same zone.

On PS4 the title runs at a stable high frame rate, which makes the fast, acrobatic sections even more precise and pleasant to control than in many of the original games. The pixel-art graphics are elaborately detailed, and the soundtrack, created with an emphasis on fidelity to the style of classic Sonic titles, ranks among the most praised elements of the game across both reviews and the fan community. The gameplay offers three playable characters with different abilities - Sonic, Tails, and Knuckles - adding variety to repeated playthroughs of the same levels.

Sonic Mania was received at launch as the best 2D installment of the series in many years, and was called by many players and reviewers a return to the qualities that made the series famous in the nineties after a string of divisively received modern entries. The development team gathered around Christian Whitehead, studio Headcannon, and PagodaWest Games proved that respect for a brand's legacy can also produce a commercially successful result. Today the game is considered one of the high points of the 2D platformer genre on PS4, and a model for how to handle nostalgia sensitively without the result feeling like a mere memory.

**Why play it:** For fans of classic Sonic from the nineties - a return to the qualities that made the series famous, created directly by fans with a sensitive relationship to nostalgia, without feeling like a mere memory.

ps4__olliolli-world.teaser: A skateboarding platformer in a fairy-tale world; combo tricks demand precise timing.
ps4__olliolli-world.article:
**OlliOlli World** combines platforming action with the skateboarding sports focus of the OlliOlli series, this time in a colorful, fairy-tale-stylized world full of quirky characters and side quests. The player rides through linear tracks, combining tricks, grinds, and jumps into fluid combos and trying to achieve as high a score as possible or as clean a run as possible without a single mistake, while the game demands precise timing and quick reactions similar to the previous, significantly harder entries in the series. Conversations with characters and completing small side quests open the way to new areas, giving the world its own storyline and a pleasant sense of traveling between individual regions.

On PS4 the game feels visually fresh thanks to hand-drawn environments and bold character stylization, accompanied by an energetic electronic and dance soundtrack that underlines the smooth feel of riding through each level. The game's structure offers both a story campaign and demanding optional challenges for players who want to master perfect runs through the tracks on the highest difficulty, giving the title considerable replay value long after finishing the main storyline. The controls are designed so that tricks arise from combinations of simple analog stick movements, letting the player focus more on the flow and rhythm of the ride than on memorizing complex button combinations.

Critics praised OlliOlli World especially for how accessibly it presents mechanics that were perceived as demanding for newcomers in previous entries in the series, without sacrificing depth for experienced players chasing a perfect score. With this installment, studio Roll7 shifted the series from raw arcade difficulty toward a more narrative-driven, more accessible form with a distinctive visual identity. Today the game works as an excellent choice for fans of skateboarding sports and platforming action alike, looking for a more relaxed yet still skill-demanding experience.

**Why play it:** For fans of skateboarding and platforming action looking for a more relaxed yet still skill-demanding experience - a more accessible presentation of mechanics that were a scarecrow for newcomers in previous entries in the series.

ps4__trine-4-nightmare-prince.teaser: A return to the series' cooperative roots after a divisive entry; four players solve the puzzles.
ps4__trine-4-nightmare-prince.article:
**Trine 4: The Nightmare Prince** returns the series to the beloved cooperative formula of the first two installments after the more experimental and divisively received third entry, taking the form of a 2.5D platformer with strong physics-based puzzle elements. Players control a trio of heroes - the sorceress Amadeus, the knight Pontius, and the thief Zoya - each with unique abilities used to solve environmental puzzles, move objects, levitate things, and overcome traps, either solo by switching between characters, or in co-op with up to four players engaged at once, with the game automatically adjusting puzzle layouts to the number of active characters.

On PS4 the game excels especially visually, with painterly, fairy-tale graphics full of light effects, fog, and elaborately crafted environments that rank among the most impressive in the whole series and in the genre in general. The environments shift smoothly from snowy forests through underground caves to grand castle halls, keeping visual variety throughout the campaign's length. The soundtrack builds a magical, dreamlike atmosphere fitting the theme of nightmares and dark fairy tales that inspire the story of the escaped prince. The puzzles require a combination of all the characters' abilities, and the game sensitively balances difficulty so it works both for solo play switching between roles and for a group playing together.

Trine 4 was received at launch as a successful return to the series' roots, correcting the mixed reception of the third installment and confirming that the combination of hand-painted graphics and physics-based puzzles still holds strong appeal for players. With this title, the Finnish studio Frozenbyte demonstrated maturity in handling the cooperative genre as well as the ability to listen to fan feedback. Today the game is recommended especially as an ideal title for playing together with family or friends thanks to its accessibility, visual beauty, and gentle difficulty.

**Why play it:** For playing together with family or friends - a return to the series' roots after the mixed reception of the third installment, with hand-painted graphics, physics-based puzzles, and gentle difficulty.

ps4__gran-turismo-7.teaser: A return to the series' traditional format with the Café mode; hundreds of cars and deep tuning options.
ps4__gran-turismo-7.article:
**Gran Turismo 7** is a sweeping return to the series' traditional format, combining realistic car simulation with an extensive collector and career mode called Café, which guides the player through the history and technology of various cars in a menu format with progressively unlocked challenges and collection tasks. At the core of the game remains a precise, physics-based driving model, hundreds of licensed cars, and dozens of real and fictional tracks, along with deep vehicle customization and tuning options, from engine performance through the gearbox to tires and chassis aerodynamics. The game also features its own economy, in which the player invests earned money into collector cars, their upgrades, or new models from an extensive virtual car dealership.

On PS4, the game runs stably and fully supports wheels and other peripherals, making it one of the most precise racing simulations available on the console. Visually it offers finely detailed car and track models along with dynamic weather that affects handling and tire grip in real time. Classic circuit championship series as well as drift and rallycross disciplines are also available, so the game covers a wide range of motorsport styles. The soundtrack combines authentic engine sounds with calmer, atmospheric music during menus and the photo mode Scapes, which has long been a popular and widely used part of the series.

Upon release, Gran Turismo 7 was received as a return to the identity fans had missed in the previous installment, which focused more on online services at the expense of single-player content, though it sparked discussion over an economic model tied to real-world currency and gradual content unlocking.
