With this installment, Polyphony Digital once again confirmed its position as one of the most significant racing series in gaming history. Today the game serves as a comprehensive encyclopedia of car culture as well as a respected simulation platform for sim-racing enthusiasts across generations of players.

**Why play it:** For sim-racing enthusiasts and car culture fans alike - a comprehensive return to the identity the previous installment sacrificed for online services, though the real-money economic model sparked discussion.

ps4__crash-team-racing-nitro-fueled.teaser: A remake of the kart classic enriched with content from Crash Nitro Kart and Grand Prix seasons.
ps4__crash-team-racing-nitro-fueled.article:
**Crash Team Racing Nitro-Fueled** is a complete remake of the beloved kart racing game from the original PlayStation era, enriched with content from its sequel Crash Nitro Kart and a range of entirely new characters, tracks, and game modes added through regular seasonal updates called Grand Prix. At its core remains technically more demanding arcade racing than competing kart games, built on a sophisticated drifting and gradual boost-charging system that requires precise timing and rewards experienced players with noticeably faster lap times. The game also includes the classic Adventure mode carried over from the original, in which the player traverses a world map, completes challenges on individual tracks, and collects trophies and keys that unlock further content.

On PS4 the title excels visually, with significantly reworked character models and tracks in high resolution while preserving the original track layouts and game feel from the '90s installments. The music builds on the melodies of the original games in a new arrangement, and the classic tracks are also available as an optional choice for nostalgic players who prefer the original sound. The game supports online racing, seasonal content with unlockable characters and costumes, and cooperative and competitive multiplayer modes on a single screen, including battle arenas with special weapons.

Upon release, Nitro-Fueled was received as one of the finest remakes of the generation, one that managed to combine faithfulness to the original with modern technical execution and long-term post-launch support through additional content. With this title, studio Beenox proved that the precision of the original driving model holds up alongside Mario Kart and other modern competitors in the genre, thanks in part to the high technical difficulty of mastering the drift. Today the game is considered one of the best kart racing games available on PS4, equally praised by newcomers and players who remember the original.

**Why play it:** For fans of kart racing and newcomers alike - one of the finest remakes of the generation, whose demanding driving model with technical drifting holds up alongside Mario Kart.

ps4__need-for-speed-heat.teaser: Legal day races and illegal night races, with the risk of losing reputation if you get arrested.
ps4__need-for-speed-heat.article:
**Need for Speed Heat** places the series in the fictional city of Palm City, inspired by Miami, and builds on the contrast between legal daytime races that earn money for car upgrades and illegal nighttime races that bring the reputation needed to unlock the best parts and more powerful upgrades, while also drawing the attention of a corrupt police force willing to resort to aggressive and dangerous tactics. This day/night cycle gives the game a different dynamic from previous series installments and forces the player to choose between caution and risk on every trip into the open world, since accumulated reputation can be lost if arrested by police. The car roster includes a wide range of sports and luxury cars that can be customized both in terms of performance and visually with wraps, rims, and body kit accessories.

On PS4 the game offers extensive visual and performance tuning options, an open world full of side activities, and a strongly stylized night atmosphere supported by neon lighting and an electronic and hip-hop music selection accompanying both driving and menus. Police chases during night races are among the game's most thrilling moments, requiring quick decisions between fleeing, hiding in side streets, and continuing the ongoing race. The game also allows shared play in the open world with other players, who can join in shared races or chases.

Upon release, Need for Speed Heat was received as a significant improvement over the previous installment, Payback, praised especially for returning emphasis to car customization and a deeper, more thrilling police chase system. With this title, Ghost Games showed that the series still has something to offer fans of arcade street racing even after several weaker installments that had noticeably drifted from the series' roots. Today the game serves as a solid choice for players seeking a stylized, action-packed arcade racing experience with a strong night atmosphere and a heavy emphasis on car customization.

**Why play it:** For fans of stylized arcade street racing - a significant improvement over the weaker Payback, with a return to emphasis on car customization and more thrilling police chases in a night atmosphere.

ps4__f1-2020.teaser: Licensed F1 with the My Team mode - your own outfit, from hiring drivers to developing the car.
ps4__f1-2020.article:
**F1 2020** expands the officially licensed Formula One racing series with an entirely new game mode called My Team, in which the player founds and runs their own team as the eleventh entry in the championship, including hiring drivers, negotiating sponsors, building the team headquarters, and developing the car over the course of multiple seasons. At the core of the game remains a finely detailed, physics-based driving model reflecting the real tracks and cars of the current Formula One season, complemented by the supporting F2 category with its own drivers and cars. The classic single-driver career mode also offers an alternative history of the 2020 F1 season, in which players can race with cars created specifically for this version of the championship.

On PS4 the title offers extensive difficulty and driving assist settings, making it accessible to both newcomers and experienced simulation players who demand more precise car behavior when cornering and at the limit of grip. Visually the game faithfully depicts the real circuits, teams, and drivers of the given season, while the sound design captures the authentic roar of engines and the atmosphere of race weekends, including broadcast-style elements evoking real television coverage with interviews and press conferences. The career mode with long-term car and team development is among the most elaborate and closely followed features of the whole series and also includes strategic decisions about tires and pit stops.

Upon release, F1 2020 was well received, especially thanks to the My Team mode, which added new depth, a management dimension, and long-term motivation to keep replaying the game. With this installment, Codemasters confirmed its position as the leading creator of official Formula One simulations on the market and showed that even a licensed sports series can offer significant creative innovation. Today the game remains a popular choice for motorsport fans who appreciate the combination of management elements with a precise, physics-based racing core reflecting the real Formula One season.

**Why play it:** For motorsport fans who want a management dimension alongside the real Formula One season - the My Team mode added depth and long-term motivation that earlier installments lacked.

ps4__fifa-21.teaser: Another yearly installment of the football series with an improved dribbling system and the beloved Ultimate Team.
ps4__fifa-21.article:
**FIFA 21** is another yearly installment of the most widespread football series, which on PS4 brings a revised player movement system, more agile dribbling, and reworked AI for teammates and opponents that respond to game situations somewhat more convincingly than in previous installments. The game offers a wide range of modes, from single-player or manager career through online matches and seasonal leagues to the immensely popular collector mode Ultimate Team, in which players build dream teams from cards of real footballers and compete against other players worldwide. The career mode also offers a more elaborate transfer system and the ability to simulate the gradual development of young players over multiple seasons.

On PS4 the title benefits from an extensive license base of leagues, clubs, and players worldwide, giving it a high degree of authenticity compared to competing sports series. Match presentation includes commentary, stadium atmosphere, and finely detailed animations that try to approximate a real television broadcast, complete with rituals and details such as fan reactions or player gestures after scoring a goal. Ultimate Team remains a key element of long-term playability thanks to regularly updated content, seasonal challenges, and competitions in which players improve their lineup according to the current form of real footballers.

Upon release, FIFA 21 was received as a solid, if rather evolutionary, yearly entry, with the most attention drawn by adjustments to on-pitch gameplay and further expansions of Ultimate Team with new game modes. In this installment, EA Vancouver continued its long-term refinement of both the football simulation and the social and competitive elements surrounding it. Today the game stands as evidence of the enormous popularity of football simulations and their central role in online sports gaming on PS4, as well as one of the last installments in the series still carrying the FIFA name.

**Why play it:** For fans of football simulations and Ultimate Team looking for a solid, if rather evolutionary, yearly entry - proof of football's central role in online sports gaming on PS4, and one of the last installments still under the FIFA name.

ps4__nba-2k21.teaser: An acclaimed basketball simulation with faithful animation of NBA stars and the MyTeam mode.
ps4__nba-2k21.article:
**NBA 2K21** continues the tradition of the most acclaimed basketball simulation with a sophisticated player movement system, finely detailed ball physics, and a broad range of game modes, from single-player career through club management to online matches and the collector mode MyTeam with cards of current and historical NBA players. The game emphasizes a realistic depiction of basketball duels, the individual style of NBA stars distinguished by unique movement animation, and team strategy requiring cooperation from AI-controlled teammates. The game also captures the small individual quirks of specific stars, from their characteristic dribbling to their signature shooting habits, which fans following the real NBA league will recognize.

On PS4 the title offers finely detailed player models, faithfully rendered arenas, and match atmosphere backed by commentary and a licensed soundtrack spanning a wide range of genres from hip-hop to electronic music selected for that season. The MyCareer career mode combines sports matches with story elements and a social space called Neighborhood, where players can move between various off-court activities, buy gear for their character, and meet other players online. The game also includes a thoroughly developed MyGM/MyLeague management mode for players who prefer strategically running an entire club or league.

Upon release, NBA 2K21 was received with more mixed reactions than previous series installments, partly due to criticism of microtransactions in the MyTeam and MyCareer modes, though the basketball core itself continued to be rated as the most sophisticated on the market. With this installment, Visual Concepts confirmed the series' dominant position in the basketball simulation genre despite the controversy surrounding content monetization. Today the game remains a reference point for basketball simulations and is also remembered as one of the last major titles of the PS4 generation.

**Why play it:** For basketball fans looking for the most sophisticated simulation on the market, though you should expect the criticized microtransactions in the MyTeam and MyCareer modes.

ps4__limbo.teaser: A black-and-white platformer full of deadly traps; an icon of the modern indie art-game scene.
ps4__limbo.article:
**Limbo** is a black-and-white platform adventure by Danish studio Playdead that arrived on PlayStation 4 in 2016 and became one of the pillars of the modern wave of indie art games. The player controls a nameless boy who wakes up on the edge of a dark forest and sets out to find his sister — the story is never explained in words, everything is conveyed through grim atmosphere, silhouettes, and sound. The game functions as a sequence of logic puzzles: traps, pulleys, gravity mechanisms, and dangerous creatures force the player into careful trial-and-error experimentation, with death arriving often and without warning, though respawns are instant and don't break the game's pace. The game leans heavily on subverting expectations — many traps seem harmless, and death comes from an unexpected direction.

On PS4 the game runs at stable framerates and higher resolution, which only further highlights the contrasty black-and-white visuals with minimal color accents, usually limited to a single glowing point that serves as a guide. The sound design is spare and deliberately empty — no music in the traditional sense, just the sound of wind, creaking wood, and a heartbeat, which heightens the feeling of loneliness and danger. The camera and character movement are deliberately slow, underscoring the vulnerability of a small boy in a world full of giant spiders and hazards. This audiovisual austerity is one of the reasons Limbo is still cited today as a pioneer of atmospheric 2D platformers with minimalist storytelling.

Contemporary reception was exceptionally positive, and the game helped kickstart an entire genre that was later expanded upon by titles like Inside or Little Nightmares, incidentally from the same studio. Even today Limbo works flawlessly — it's short, focused, and doesn't have a single wasted scene. For players seeking a dense, art-house experience without unnecessary explanation, it remains one of the best entry points into the genre, even more than ten years after its original release.

**Why play it:** For players seeking a dense, art-house experience without unnecessary explanation - a short, focused game without a single wasted scene, which kickstarted an entire genre of atmospheric platformers.

ps4__ori-and-blind-forest-definitive-edi.teaser: One of the most beautiful 2D stories of its generation; a metroidvania told without words.
ps4__ori-and-blind-forest-definitive-edi.article:
**Ori and the Blind Forest: Definitive Edition** brought to PlayStation 4 in 2019 one of the most beautiful 2D storytelling experiences of its generation. The story of the orphan Ori, who tries to save the dying forest of Nibel, is told with almost no dialogue — only through movement, music, and hand-painted backgrounds that feel like living illustrations from a storybook. In terms of gameplay it's a metroidvania built on precise platforming: the player gradually acquires new abilities (double jump, dash, gliding) that unlock previously inaccessible parts of the map, elegantly linking world exploration with the player's growing dexterity. Enemies and the environment are often lethal to the touch, so the game works both as a calm walk through a landscape and as an uncompromising test of reflexes during escape sequences.

The Definitive Edition added new areas, tougher boss fights, a supplementary map, and faster travel between key points compared to the original release, fine-tuning the game's overall pacing and removing unnecessary padding from the first release. On PS4 the title ran smoothly, and the musical score by Gareth Coker was among the most praised on the entire console — orchestral pieces manage to switch within seconds from calm melancholy to the tension of life-threatening escapes from natural disasters, where a single wrong jump means death. The hand-painted backgrounds with layered parallax remain among the most visually rich the 2D platformer genre has ever offered.

Ori and the Blind Forest is now considered one of the defining titles of the metroidvania genre alongside Hollow Knight, and is often cited as an example of how powerful storytelling can be without a single written word. Despite its fairytale aesthetic, it's a game that can be mercilessly demanding, and it's precisely this combination of beauty and frustrating precision that made and still makes it an experience players remember long after finishing it. The success of the Definitive Edition also paved the way for the sequel, Ori and the Will of the Wisps.

**Why play it:** For fans of metroidvanias alongside Hollow Knight who appreciate storytelling without a single written word - a fairytale aesthetic hiding a mercilessly demanding game whose combination of beauty and precision is remembered long after finishing it.

ps4__shovel-knight-treasure-trove.teaser: A tribute to the 8-bit era with an original "shovel bounce" that lets you bop enemies with a shovel.
ps4__shovel-knight-treasure-trove.article:
**Shovel Knight** arrived on PlayStation 4 in 2015 and instantly became one of the most talked-about tributes to the 8-bit era. The hero, a knight armed with a shovel, journeys through eight themed lands full of enemies drawn from the golden years of platformers — from Mega Man through DuckTales to Zelda — with each area closing on a boss fight against a striking member of the Order of No Quarter. The core of the gameplay is precise jumping and the so-called "shovel bounce," a downward bop off enemies and objects with the shovel that serves both as an attack and as a means of traversal, opening paths to otherwise unreachable treasures and shortcuts. On top of that, the player loses part of their accumulated gold upon death, so the game balances risk and reward much like the classic action platformers of its era.

Visually the game imitates the aesthetic of NES titles but with modern refinements — smoother animation, a richer color palette, and more precise collisions that remove the frustration of the old titles without losing their character. Jake Kaufman's music ranks among the most praised soundtracks of the indie scene, and its chiptune compositions manage to evoke nostalgia without feeling like mere pastiche. Over the years Shovel Knight grew into the full Treasure Trove collection, which added further campaigns with different playable characters — each with its own style of movement and attack — turning the original game into effectively four games in one, tied together by a shared world and cross-references between each hero's story.

Critically and commercially, Shovel Knight was received exceptionally well and became a symbol of a successful crowdfunded indie project that matches or exceeds the quality of the classics that inspired it. The game has also enjoyed numerous guest appearances in other indie titles, which only confirmed how quickly the shovel-wielder became a recognizable icon of the independent gaming scene. To this day it is often recommended as a textbook example of how to do a retro platformer right — with respect for history, but without compromising on controls or level design.

**Why play it:** For fans of retro platformers who want respect for history without any compromise on controls or level design — a textbook example of a successful crowdfunded indie project that became an icon of the independent scene.

ps4__katana-zero.teaser: A lightning-fast action slasher where a single mistake means death; the whole run replays like a movie.
ps4__katana-zero.article:
**Katana ZERO** brought PlayStation 4 in 2019 a combination of lightning-fast action gameplay and a neon-lit neo-noir story that quickly earned a devoted fan base. The hero, a samurai with the ability to manipulate time, moves through rooms full of armed enemies who must be dispatched with a single sword stroke — but any mistake means instant death and a return to the start of the room. The game therefore builds on a principle of rapid memorization and improvisation, as the player gradually assembles the perfect run through a room like a choreography of dodges, deflected shots and precise strikes, after which the complete run through the whole mission plays back as a smooth, seamless action movie scene.

Visually the title combines pixel art with cinematic transitions and colorful neon lights that recall stylized 1980s action films and their visual language full of VHS artifacts and jump-cut editing. The electronic synthwave soundtrack perfectly complements the pace of the action and often shifts in real time according to what's happening on screen, reinforcing the feeling that the player is as much a part of the music as of the combat. The story, told through therapy sessions between missions, gradually reveals the dark and ambiguous background of the main character and engages with themes of addiction, manipulation, paranoia and an unreliable narrator, leaving the player to work out for themselves how much of the depicted memories is actually true.

Katana ZERO was very well received critically and became one of the most frequently mentioned indie titles of its time thanks to its combination of demanding but fair gameplay and a strong authorial style. Dialogue that can be interrupted with quick responses also gave the game an unusually lively, reactive feel even outside the fights themselves. Even years later it remains a reference point for the genre of fast action platformers built on the one-hit, one-death principle.

**Why play it:** For fans of fast action platformers built on the one-hit, one-death principle — demanding but fair gameplay paired with a strong authorial style and lively, interruptible dialogue.

ps4__gris.teaser: A calm platformer with no dying; color returns to the world as the story comes to terms with loss.
ps4__gris.article:
**Gris** came to PlayStation 4 in 2019 as the visually most striking title from the Spanish studio Nomada Studio, which collaborated with illustrator Conrad Roset. The game follows a young girl moving through a landscape that gradually awakens from shades of gray into full color, symbolizing her journey through processing grief and loss. In terms of gameplay it's a calm platformer with no dying and no time pressure — the player solves simple environmental puzzles and gradually gains new movement abilities that open up further parts of the world, much like in classic metroidvanias, just without combat or danger. Each of the four colored chapters adds a new ability as well as a new visual motif — transforming into heavy stone, flying on gusts of wind, or swimming through the depths — and the emotional tone of the whole landscape shifts along with the color.

The game's greatest strength is its visual style — watercolor-painted backgrounds that respond fluidly to the player's movement and change color according to the emotional register of each chapter, while the heroine herself literally falls apart into pieces in moments of despair, pieces that must be put back together. The music, composed by Berlinist, accompanies each scene with a feel for dynamics and quietly builds as the story moves toward resolution. On PS4 the game ran smoothly, and the higher resolution only highlighted the detail of the hand-drawn surfaces, which otherwise feel like a living gallery.

Gris received wide acclaim for its treatment of a heavy subject without a single line of dialogue, and it is often cited as an example of how a game can function as a sensitive artistic statement about sorrow, denial and accepting loss. Thanks to its short length and gentle pace it's accessible even to players who otherwise avoid action titles, and to this day it remains one of the most frequently recommended emotional experiences on the platform, often mentioned in the same breath as titles like Journey.

**Why play it:** For players looking for a short, sensitive artistic experience about sorrow and accepting loss without a single line of dialogue — accessible even to those who otherwise avoid action games, often mentioned in the same breath as Journey.

ps4__spiritfarer.teaser: A management sim about ferrying the souls of the deceased; a moving farewell at the lighthouse at the end of the pier.
ps4__spiritfarer.article:
**Spiritfarer** arrived on PlayStation 4 in 2020 and offered an unusual combination of management simulation and an emotionally charged story about death and farewell. The player takes on the role of Stella, a newly minted ferrymaster of spirits, who carries the ghosts of deceased friends and acquaintances across the sea on her boat toward their final rest. Each character has their own story, personality, needs and favorite foods — the player builds cabins for them, grows crops, cooks meals and completes small tasks for them, until the moment comes to let them go and say goodbye forever with an embrace at the lighthouse at the end of the pier. The boat itself can gradually be expanded with dozens of specialized rooms, turning it into a living, ever-growing home for a whole crowded crew of spirits.

In terms of gameplay it's a broad mix of crafts: fishing, mining, farming, cooking and upgrading the boat blend with platforming sections while exploring islands, where the player gradually finds new materials, recipes and companions. The hand-drawn graphics have a warm, fairy-tale look that contrasts with the heavy themes the game deals with, and it's precisely this contrast that gives the story its power — sorrow is handled here with kindness and without fear of feeling. The musical accompaniment supports the game's meditative pace and gives the player room to fully feel each character's departure without the game ever pushing them to rush, and the player chooses for themselves whether to spend the day on productive work aboard the ship or in a quiet conversation with one of its residents.

Spiritfarer was very well received for its sensitive handling of the themes of dying and caregiving, which rarely appears this directly in the games industry, and many players and journalists praised the game's ability to be comforting and honestly sad at the same time. Its long playtime, which gives room for gradually building relationships with the characters, makes it an experience that's often recommended more as an emotional journey than as a classic game about challenge, and it remains to this day one of the most frequently mentioned indie titles of its generation on the theme of loss and acceptance.

**Why play it:** For players open to an emotional journey rather than a classic challenge — a sensitive and honestly sad take on the themes of dying and caregiving that gives plenty of room to gradually build relationships with the characters.

ps4__return-of-obra-dinn.teaser: A detective puzzle where a magic pocket watch replays the scene of a death; guess three fates at once.
ps4__return-of-obra-dinn.article:
**Return of the Obra Dinn** released on PlayStation 4 in 2020, two years after its original PC release, bringing to the console one of the most original detective concepts in the history of games. Playing an insurance investigator, the player boards the abandoned ship Obra Dinn, which returned after years without its crew, and uses a magic pocket watch to replay, at the site of each person's last cry, the frozen moment of their death and freely walk through it as if among statues. The task is to deduce, from these frozen scenes, sounds and tiny clues, the name, fate and cause of death of all sixty people aboard, with the game confirming findings only when the player correctly guesses all three parts of a fate at once.

The whole title runs in a striking monochrome style inspired by old computer monitors and a technique known as 1-bit dithering, which gives the investigation a specific, almost archival character while still allowing detailed reading of faces and scenes without unnecessary visual noise. The game has no hints in the traditional sense — the player must connect accents, uniforms, dialogue and the context of individual snapshots and build an extensive system of deduction themselves in the accompanying logbook, which makes the satisfaction of each correctly guessed identity all the greater. The sound design, built on real voice recordings rather than text, gives the individual scenes surprising emotional weight despite the sparse graphics, and even small details like a sailor's accent or an officer's tone of voice often turn out to be the key clue.

Return of the Obra Dinn received extraordinary acclaim for its utterly unique narrative and gameplay concept, which barely resembles any other game on the market, and it is often cited as one of the best-designed logic titles of its time, compared even to the author's previous game Papers, Please. On PS4 it found a further audience that appreciated just how patient and rewarding pure detective thinking can be without action or time pressure.

**Why play it:** For players who want to savor pure detective thinking without time pressure or action — a unique narrative concept from the creators of Papers, Please that has no equal on the market.

ps4__hyper-light-drifter.teaser: A visually distinctive tribute to Zelda: A Link to the Past, its story told only through images and music.
ps4__hyper-light-drifter.article:
**Hyper Light Drifter** arrived on PlayStation 4 in 2018 as a visually distinctive tribute to classic action-adventures in the style of The Legend of Zelda: A Link to the Past. The player controls the mysterious Drifter, afflicted by an unknown illness, who moves through a decayed world full of remnants of an ancient, advanced civilization, searching for a cure through technological artifacts. The story is told almost entirely through images and short, silent memories, without a single spoken word, leaving the reader plenty of room for their own interpretation of events and of the Drifter's relationship to his deceased companions, who appear only in fragments of dreamlike memories.

Combat is built on fast, precise movement — dash dodges, combinations of ranged and melee attacks, and careful timing are necessary to survive against enemies who show no mercy for mistakes, and the game demands a level of skill comparable to more demanding action titles even though it outwardly looks like a leisurely platformer. Pixel-art graphics with a striking color palette and neon accents create a melancholic, almost dreamlike atmosphere, underscored by an ambient electronic soundtrack composed by Disasterpeace. The level design is non-linear and encourages personal exploration, with individual areas of the world unlocking further abilities and weapons needed for progress, and the player chooses for themselves the order in which to explore the four main areas.

Hyper Light Drifter was very well received critically and became a frequently cited example of how strong an impression a game can leave when built purely on atmosphere, visuals and pure gameplay without any textual exposition. To this day it ranks among the titles held up as a model of aesthetically consistent and mechanically tense indie design, and its influence can be seen in a number of later action platformers with similarly stylized graphics.

**Why play it:** For fans of atmospheric action platformers where the story is told only through visuals and music — an aesthetically tight and mechanically tense experience that inspired a number of later indie titles.

ps4__messenger.teaser: A tribute to 8-bit ninja platformers that cleverly turns into something far bigger.
ps4__messenger.article:
**The Messenger** released on PlayStation 4 in 2018 as a tribute to 8-bit ninja platformers of the Ninja Gaiden type, one that surprisingly and cleverly transforms during play into something far bigger. The player controls a young ninja from a clan whose village has been wiped out by demons and must deliver an important message across dangerous lands full of enemies and traps, with combat built around precise timing of strikes and bouncing off enemies, projectiles and chasms with a sword, allowing the player to reach otherwise inaccessible places and chain long combos of jumps over pits and lava.

Roughly halfway through the game there's a surprising twist, where the linear action platformer turns into a sprawling metroidvania with backtracking through already-visited areas and new abilities that let players discover hidden parts of the map, radically changing the pace and structure of the rest of the playthrough. The game also plays elegantly with a shift between an 8-bit and 16-bit graphical aesthetic, which unlocks new parts of the world, changes the musical arrangement and the look of the environment, and symbolizes a shift in time within the story. Both chiptune and more modern music alternate the same way and complement the humorous, self-deprecating tone of a narrative full of references to retro gaming classics, including a shopkeeper character who is well aware of his own role in the story and regularly breaks the fourth wall with remarks about the platformer genre itself.

The Messenger was very well received critically precisely thanks to its bold structural transformation over the course of play and its carefully tuned controls, which respect the difficulty of the original games while removing their unfair elements. Studio Sabotage built a reputation with this title as creators who can combine sincere reverence for the past with the courage to break the genre's expectations. To this day the game is often cited as an example of how a tribute to the past can also be innovative game design, thanks in part to a wealth of optional side quests and collectibles that reward thorough exploration.

**Why play it:** For fans of retro platformers unafraid to break their own rules midway through — a bold structural transformation and fairly tuned difficulty make The Messenger an exceptional tribute to the past.

ps4__enter-gungeon.teaser: A fast roguelike with four Gungeoneers and a bizarre fortress full of armed chests.
ps4__enter-gungeon.article:
**Enter the Gungeon** released on PlayStation 4 in 2016 and quickly became one of the most popular roguelike shooters of its generation thanks to its combination of fast action, humor and randomly generated dungeons. The player controls one of four characters called Gungeoneers, each with their own backstory and starting loadout, who descend into the Gungeon — a bizarre underground fortress full of anthropomorphic bullets and armed chests — seeking a gun capable of killing the past. Each run offers differently laid-out rooms and new combinations of weapons and items, ensuring high replayability, while narrative layers gradually reveal each character's past across many attempts.

Combat is built around a dodge roll system that lets the player pass directly through enemy shots, so the game rewards precise timing and a feel for space in rooms full of bullet-hell fire patterns inspired by classic Japanese shmups. A collection of dozens to hundreds of different, often absurd weapons — from classic pistols to guns that fire other, smaller guns — gives each run its own character and encourages experimentation as well as sharing favorite combinations among players. Pixel-art graphics with a bold color style and light-hearted humor contrast with the game's fairly high difficulty, which is eased by a two-player co-op system and the ability to unlock permanent upgrades between runs, including new rooms and merchants within the Gungeon fortress itself.

Enter the Gungeon was very well received critically and became one of the most frequently cited representatives of the roguelike shooter genre alongside titles like Nuclear Throne. Thanks to its endless replayability and ever-fresh combinations of items, it remains a popular choice for both short and long play sessions to this day, and it's among the titles players kept coming back to on PS4 even years after first finishing it.

**Why play it:** For fans of roguelike shooting that never gets old thanks to endless item combinations — Enter the Gungeon stands alongside Nuclear Throne among the genre's classics.

ps4__superhot.teaser: FPS puzzle where time only passes when the player moves; standing still gives you time to plan your next move.
ps4__superhot.article:
**Superhot** arrived on PlayStation 4 in 2017 with its remarkable central mechanic summed up right in the subtitle: time only passes when the player moves. This simple idea turns a classic first-person shooter into a thoughtful puzzle, where every step, turn, or shot pushes the world forward, while standing still gives the player time to think about the next move amid a fight against dozens of enemies and flying bullets that, in slowed-down time, become almost statues waiting to be hit.

Visually, the game uses a stark style with red, glassy enemy figures against a white background, which clearly separates the important scene elements from the surroundings while giving the game a recognizable, minimalist aesthetic without a single extra texture. The levels are short but densely designed so that each one requires precise planning of the order of attacks, dodges, and picking up weapons from fallen enemies, so every playthrough feels more like solved choreography than a traditional firefight, and repeated attempts to pull off a perfect, smooth clear of a room without a single hesitation are one of the main sources of fun and motivation to keep playing. The story, delivered through a fictional computer interface and conversations outside the game, adds a meta-element that questions the relationship between the player and the game itself, and gradually takes on an increasingly unsettling self-referential tone.

Superhot was very well received critically for its originality and became a frequently cited example of how one well-thought-out mechanical idea can carry an entire title. On PS4, the game also later inspired its own VR version, which translated the same principle into fully physical controls. The short playtime is balanced by a high density of ideas, and the game remains a beloved showcase of how innovation in controlling time can transform even such an established genre as the first-person shooter.

**Why play it:** Thanks to a single, brilliantly conceived idea — time only passes when you move — Superhot is worth trying despite its short playtime, which it makes up for with a density of ideas.

ps5__grand-theft-auto-v.teaser: Enhanced edition with higher resolution and 60 fps; three heroes, chases and big heists.
ps5__grand-theft-auto-v.article:
**Grand Theft Auto V** arrived on PlayStation 5 in 2022 in an enhanced and improved edition offering higher resolution, 60 frames-per-second support, and faster loading thanks to the SSD. The game remains a vast open world set in the fictional Los Santos and its surroundings, where the player alternately takes control of three characters — Michael, Franklin, and Trevor — moving through an interwoven story of heists, betrayal, and life on the fringes of the law. The core of the gameplay is cover-based shooting, car chases, and planning big heists that unfold in several phases from preparation to execution, with the player switching between the three heroes on the fly and tackling situations from different points of view.

The PS5 version adds a range of graphical improvements — denser traffic, better lighting and shadows, and support for 3D audio through headphones, which heightens the atmosphere of a city full of neon, traffic, and radio stations with their own selection of music ranging from electronic to hip-hop to country. The DualSense controller uses adaptive triggers and haptic feedback when shooting or driving various vehicles, giving the action a tactile dimension on the new generation of consoles. The online multiplayer mode GTA Online is also present, running more smoothly on the new-generation consoles, with shorter wait times and a steady stream of new content. Technically, it's one of the best-optimized versions of the game, even though the core gameplay remains unchanged since 2013.

Grand Theft Auto V was critically praised on its original release for the scope of its world, its dark humor, and the sophistication of its three parallel storylines, and this acclaim carried over with the arrival on PS5. The game influenced the direction of the entire open-world action genre and is still often cited as an example of what a living virtual world with a believable daily rhythm, traffic, and inhabitant behavior should look like. Even more than a decade after its PS3 debut, GTA V remains, thanks to updates, an active online community, and its media reach as a satire of American society, one of the most-played titles on PlayStation 5.

**Why play it:** Even more than a decade after its debut, Grand Theft Auto V is worth playing for the scope of its world, its dark humor, and its lively online community, which make it one of the most-played titles on PS5.

ps5__like-dragon-gaiden-man-who-erased-h.teaser: A Yakuza spin-off serving as a bridge between storylines; Kiryu returns from years spent in hiding.
ps5__like-dragon-gaiden-man-who-erased-h.article:
**Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name** is a spin-off from the main Yakuza/Like a Dragon series, released in 2023 by Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio as a bridge between the stories of earlier entries and Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth. The player returns to the role of Kazuma Kiryu, who, after years in hiding as "Joryu," once again enters the underworld of Tokyo and Yokohama to protect those he cares about and unravel a conspiracy reaching all the way to the top of the yakuza clans. The story deliberately picks up the loose threads left by previous entries and explains what happened to Kiryu during the years he was officially presumed dead.

In terms of gameplay, the game returns to the action-based combat system closer to the series' earlier entries, meaning real-time combat with several fighting styles that the player switches between on the fly depending on the situation and number of opponents. Besides the main storyline, the game also offers side content in the form of the Akame mini-game island, spy-agency mechanics with gadgets like a hidden camera or a remote-controlled drone, and the classic side quests full of bizarre humor typical of the series. On PS5, the game runs smoothly at high resolution with fast-loading support, which comes in especially handy when traveling between the sprawling and finely detailed districts of Kamurocho and Sotenbori.

The game's atmosphere draws on the contrast between the serious, almost melancholic main story about an aging hero and the lighthearted side activities, accompanied by the series' characteristic musical score combining orchestral motifs with electronic elements and energetic battle themes. Critics and fans alike praised it as a shorter but emotionally dense title that works as a dignified farewell to Kiryu's character as it has existed so far, without losing the series' characteristic melancholic-comic tone. Today it's seen as an important connecting piece in the saga, worth attention also for its self-contained nature, sparing players the need to invest dozens of hours as with the main entries in the series.

**Why play it:** For fans of Kiryu who want a dignified and emotionally dense farewell without having to invest dozens of hours, Like a Dragon Gaiden is an ideal, shorter chapter in the saga.

ps5__like-dragon-ishin.teaser: A remake of the 2014 original set at the end of the shogunate; Sakamoto Ryoma in alternate history.
ps5__like-dragon-ishin.article:
**Like a Dragon: Ishin!** is a remake of the 2014 original, which Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio rebuilt on a modern engine and released on PlayStation 5 in 2023 as well. The story is set at the end of the shogunate era in the 19th century and follows Sakamoto Ryoma, a historical figure from Japanese history, in an alternate version of events full of intrigue, betrayal, and a struggle over the future shape of Japan. The player moves through a reconstructed Kyoto, tackles side quests, and builds relationships with other characters in the spirit of the series' classic entries, with many familiar faces from the Like a Dragon series appearing here in period-appropriate roles.

The combat system combines close-quarters swordplay with the firearms of the era and offers several fighting styles that can be switched between depending on the situation and the number of opponents surrounding the player. Besides the main story, the game offers a wealth of side content — from growing rice, to running your own weapons shop, to minigames typical of the Like a Dragon series, including card games and guard duty duels. The PS5 version brings improved graphics, a higher frame rate, and faster loading compared to the original Japanese version from 2014, which never made it to the West at the time.

Thanks to the remake, European and American players got their first chance to experience a title that had long been valued in Japan as one of the series' best spin-offs. The atmosphere is rounded out by music blending traditional Japanese instruments with a dramatic orchestral score that underscores both the gravity of the historical period and the protagonist's personal drama. Ishin! was received as a successful fusion of a historical setting with the series' proven mechanics, and today it serves as an excellent entry point for new players as well as a pleasant reminder for those already familiar with the game. Also worth praising is the care with which the creators translated period costumes, architecture, and social conventions into interactive form, without sacrificing the characteristic humor and over-the-top situations that made the series famous.

**Why play it:** For newcomers and longtime series fans alike, Like a Dragon: Ishin! offers a great entry into historical Japan thanks to its carefully rendered period setting and the series' proven mechanics.

ps5__diablo-iv.teaser: A return to the series' darker tone after the lighter Diablo III; gathering builds against Lilith.
ps5__diablo-iv.article:
**Diablo IV** was released by Blizzard Entertainment in 2023, also for PlayStation 5, and marks a return to the series' darker, grimmer tone after the lighter Diablo III. The player chooses one of several characters — for example a Barbarian, Sorceress, Necromancer, or Druid — and moves through the open, dark world of Sanctuary, fighting demonic forces and eventually Lilith herself, daughter of Mephisto. Gameplay is built on collecting items, building character builds, and endlessly upgrading the character through a system of skills and legendary items, all typical of the action RPG genre.

Unlike previous entries, Diablo IV offers a truly open world with free movement between regions, a shared online environment for chance encounters with other players during world bosses or live events, and seasonal content that regularly expands the game with new mechanics, leaderboards, and storylines. On PS5, the game takes advantage of the SSD for fast loading between areas and offers controls tailored to a gamepad, including a clear quick skill-select wheel and support for DualSense haptic feedback. The visuals lean on a dark, gothic aesthetic and the dense atmosphere of cursed lands, heightened by somber music from composers associated with the series.

Diablo IV was received on release as a successful return to the series' roots, with an emphasis on a dark story and a refined combat system, though discussions among players later raised questions about the endgame content, difficulty, and online features requiring a constant connection. Over time, the game went through a series of updates and paid expansions that brought new areas, classes, and a system of time-limited seasons. Today it's seen as one of the flagship titles of the action RPG genre for the current generation and a continuation of the legacy that made the series famous back in the nineties.

**Why play it:** For fans of action RPGs who want a dark story and a refined combat system, Diablo IV continues the legacy of a series famous since the nineties, even though the endgame and online features have sparked debate.

ps5__balatro.teaser: A card roguelike that blends poker with deckbuilding; jokers change the rules and the score.
ps5__balatro.article:
**Balatro** is a card roguelike that blends poker with deckbuilder mechanics, and it arrived on PlayStation 5 in 2024 as well. The player builds poker hands from a standard deck of cards, which changes over the course of the game thanks to so-called joker cards — special modifiers that multiply the score earned, change how hands are evaluated, or add unusual effects. The goal of each round is to reach a predetermined point total before running out of hands, with the difficulty gradually rising as the player must assemble dozens of jokers, tarot, and planet cards into working synergies that shuffle and change with every run. A system of bets and blinds also forces the player to constantly weigh whether to risk a higher score for better rewards or play it safe and survive to the next level of the deck.

On PS5, the game runs completely smoothly and visually draws on a simple but distinctive style reminiscent of old casino tables and felt playing mats, complemented by hypnotic electronic music that underscores the rhythm of decision-making. Controlling the game with the DualSense is, despite its original PC roots controlled by mouse, surprisingly comfortable and quick to pick up, with a clear menu adapted for couch play.

Balatro became one of the most talked-about indie titles of the year after release, praised for the genius of combining poker with the roguelike "one more round" loop, as well as for the depth of its synergy system, which reveals new layers of strategy even after dozens of hours played. In the field of card roguelikes, it raised the bar and inspired a whole wave of similar projects. Even today it's one of the titles players love to return to for quick but immensely addictive gaming sessions, whether on the big screen or via portable play on other platforms. Its simple barrier to entry combined with nearly endless depth of synergies makes it a game that can be recommended equally to complete newcomers and to players looking for a demanding strategic challenge.

**Why play it:** For complete newcomers and players seeking a demanding strategic challenge alike, Balatro is that rare game that combines a simple barrier to entry with nearly endless depth of synergies, luring players into quick but immensely addictive gaming sessions.

ps5__inscryption.teaser: A card horror game that gradually twists from a deckbuilder into a much darker story.
ps5__inscryption.article:
**Inscryption** is a card roguelike wrapped in a dark horror atmosphere, which arrived on PlayStation consoles some time after its original PC release. The player finds themselves in a mysterious cabin across from an enigmatic opponent and must build a deck of cards, sacrifice their own creatures on altars, and use card after card to survive battles whose rules keep changing as the game progresses. Behind what seems like a classic deckbuilder lies a much bigger and darker story, which the game gradually reveals through fourth-wall breaks, hidden mechanics, and transitions between entirely different game layers. The card battles themselves function as a full-fledged tactical system with animal cards of varying strength, sacrifice mechanics, and gradually unlocked abilities that would hold up even without its narrative depth.

On PS5, the game benefits from its atmospheric audiovisual presentation — dim lighting, creaking wood, and an uncomfortably intimate camera that keeps the player close to the card table. The sound design and the voice of the mysterious opponent are among the things that make Inscryption an experience that works best in silence, with headphones on, and the DualSense controls manage to carry over even the small interactive elements outside the card battles themselves.

Upon its original release, the game earned great acclaim for its courage to break genre expectations and for how it managed to combine card strategy with narrative horror and puzzle elements into one unforgettable whole. Inscryption's influence is evident in a number of later card and horror indie titles that tried to emulate its unexpected twists. Even years later, this title remains one of the most original entries in its genre, and its console version lets you replay the experience comfortably on the big screen. Precisely because the game relies heavily on first impressions for much of its charm, it's recommended to go into it with as little prior information as possible.

**Why play it:** Because of the originality with which it combines card strategy, narrative horror, and puzzle elements, Inscryption is worth playing with as little prior information as possible, so its unexpected twists can land at full force.

ps5__vampire-survivors.teaser: A bullet heaven where the player themselves becomes the source of the bullets; half-hour runs full of synergies.
ps5__vampire-survivors.article:
**Vampire Survivors** is an action roguelite that, with its simple yet immensely addictive premise, popularized the genre nicknamed "bullet heaven" — instead of dodging a flood of bullets, the player themselves becomes the source of them. The character moves around the screen with automatically firing weapons, while the player only chooses the direction of movement and collects experience from defeated enemies, who pour in ever-larger waves as time goes on. The combination of dozens of weapons and passive items creates a huge number of synergies, thanks to which a tiny character can become, within a few minutes, a devastating force capable of filling the whole screen with effects. Individual runs typically last around half an hour, making the game an ideal title for both short and long gaming sessions, and unlocking new characters and items keeps motivating players to run it again and again.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs completely smoothly at full frame rate even when the screen is literally flooded with hundreds of enemies and projectiles, which is crucial for this type of game. The pixel-art graphics, combined with a simple but effective chiptune soundtrack, evoke the nostalgic atmosphere of eight- and sixteen-bit games, while the modern game loop offers the typical roguelite pull of "just one more run."

Vampire Survivors became a phenomenon already on PC and mobile platforms, and its console versions have extended the game's reach to players who prefer playing on the couch with a controller in hand. The low price, the huge amount of unlockable content, and frequent updates with new characters and maps have made it one of the most influential indie titles of the last decade, defining an entire genre that has since followed in a wave of similar games. Even today it's considered a textbook example of how a simple mechanic can create a deeply addictive experience, and its success has prompted a number of other studios to experiment with a similar kind of automated action survival gameplay.

**Why play it:** For players on the couch with a controller in hand, Vampire Survivors offers a textbook example of how a simple mechanic and a low price can create a deeply addictive experience that defined an entire genre.

ps5__cult-of-lamb.teaser: A combination of dungeon crawler and life-sim; a sacrificed lamb founds its own dark cult.
ps5__cult-of-lamb.article:
**Cult of the Lamb** is an original combination of an action roguelike dungeon crawler and a base-building life-sim, in which the player takes on the role of a sacrificed lamb rescued by a dark god and founds their own cult of worshippers. Between expeditions into procedurally generated dungeons full of fast-paced combat, weapons, and curses, the player returns to their camp, where they must feed, house, and manage loyal followers, build structures, plant crops, and strengthen faith through sermons as well as dubious rituals. Followers also remember how the player treats them, and their satisfaction or dissatisfaction directly affects the strength and stability of the whole cult.

On PlayStation 5 the game excels with its striking, cutely grotesque visual style, which contrasts with the darker themes of sacrifice, manipulation, and religious cults that it treats with exaggeration and black humor. The combat system in the dungeons is fast and clear, and the DualSense controls respond precisely even in more hectic boss fights, while managing camp life proceeds at a more relaxed pace, creating a pleasant alternation of intensity. The soundtrack shifts smoothly between playful melodies of camp life and darker, tenser tracks accompanying dungeon expeditions, underscoring the game's dual nature.

Cult of the Lamb received a very positive reception upon release precisely for its fresh blend of two seemingly incompatible genres and for a style that instantly won fans across platforms. The game continued to expand its content through free updates that added new areas, cult-management mechanics, and social activities among followers. It is still regarded today as one of the most distinctive indie titles of its generation, one that proved combining survival-sim management with roguelike action can work surprisingly harmoniously, and its cute visuals contrasting with its dark theme became a striking part of its marketing identity as well.

**Why play it:** For players seeking a fresh combination of survival-sim management and roguelike action, Cult of the Lamb is one of the most distinctive indie titles of its generation, where cute visuals contrast with a dark theme.

ps5__slay-spire.teaser: The title that defined the deckbuilding roguelike genre; each character has its own deck and playstyle.
ps5__slay-spire.article:
**Slay the Spire** is the title that defined the modern deckbuilding roguelike genre on PC in 2019 and arrived on PlayStation 5 in 2023. The player advances through a procedurally generated spire full of enemies, building a card deck for one of their characters, choosing a new card, relic, or upgrade after every winning fight that shapes their strategy for the rest of the run. The combination of attack, defense, and mana cards creates a well-thought-out turn-based combat system in which players must plan several turns ahead and react to changing enemy patterns. Each playable character has its own set of cards and mechanics, so strategy and playstyle differ substantially between runs.

On PS5 the game runs stably, and the interface clearly displays all information about enemies, their intentions, and card effects, which is key to the game's strategic depth. Controller support works surprisingly naturally despite the game having originated as a typically mouse-driven PC title, and the menus have been noticeably adapted for consoles. The minimalist visual style and understated, atmospheric soundtrack reinforce the focused, meditative pace of each run.

Upon its original release, Slay the Spire essentially kick-started the deckbuilding roguelike genre on its own and became the reference point against which later titles like Balatro or Monster Train are measured. Its deep system of synergies between cards and relics, high difficulty, and near-endless replayability earned it consistently excellent reception from both players and critics. Even years after release, Slay the Spire remains regarded as one of the best-tuned deckbuilders ever made, and its console version lets players enjoy the experience comfortably on the big screen with a controller in hand — something especially appreciated by players discovering the genre through its newer successors.

**Why play it:** For players discovering the deckbuilding roguelike genre through its newer successors, Slay the Spire is the reference point with a deep system of synergies and near-endless replayability, this time comfortably on the big screen.

ps5__marvel-s-spider-man-2.teaser: Switch between Peter and Miles on the fly with no loading; the dark Venom suit changes the rules of combat.
ps5__marvel-s-spider-man-2.article:
**Marvel's Spider-Man 2** follows on from Insomniac Games' previous entries and brings a pair of playable heroes — Peter Parker and Miles Morales — between whom players can switch at any time on the fly, without the game needing to load anything. New York is once again an open playground full of skyscrapers, between which the heroes swing on webs faster and more fluidly than ever thanks to the newly added wing suit, and the map has also expanded to include the Brooklyn and Queens boroughs. Combat builds on a combination of acrobatics, gadgets, and symbiotic abilities that Peter gains after bonding with an alien entity called Venom, while Miles retains his electric and invisibility-based skill set from the first game.

The game fully leverages the power of the PlayStation 5 — loading between locations practically disappears, ray tracing reflects off skyscraper glass, and DualSense haptic feedback lets players feel the difference between different types of web shots. The story focuses on a darker thread involving Venom and the hunter Kraven, who runs his own hunt for superheroes across Manhattan, while simultaneously resolving Miles's personal drama, giving the game an emotional depth the first entry was only building toward. The soundtrack underscores dramatic moments and, together with cinematic camera direction and elaborate side quests, creates the impression of an almost blockbuster experience, even though the main story is shorter than in its predecessors.

Critics and players alike embraced the game as one of the technical and gameplay high points of the PS5 generation and confirmation that Insomniac can keep pushing the series forward without losing its identity, and the title took home numerous awards for best action game of the year. Today the title is still considered a showcase example of what a big-budget superhero game should look like — accessible, visually stunning, and with a solid core for comic-book fans and casual players alike, who especially appreciate the fluidity of moving through the city.

**Why play it:** For comic-book fans and casual players who especially appreciate the fluidity of moving through the city, Marvel's Spider-Man 2 is a showcase example of a big-budget superhero game that is both accessible and visually stunning.

ps5__helldivers-2.teaser: Cooperative carnage for four, where you call in stratagems directly under enemy fire.
ps5__helldivers-2.article:
**Helldivers 2** turned the successful cooperative concept of the first game, previously viewed from a top-down perspective, into three-dimensional third-person action and became one of the biggest surprises of 2024. Players head out as Super Earth soldiers to fight the robotic Automatons or the insectoid Terminids, with a squad of up to four players needing to coordinate fire support, artillery, and airstrikes called in via so-called stratagems — combinations of directional inputs entered literally on the move under enemy fire.

The game revels in black humor and exaggerated patriotic propaganda that mocks war games and itself alike, while chaos on the battlefield can turn a heroic mission into a grotesque fiasco within seconds, when friendly fire or a poorly aimed orbital strike wipes out your own team instead of the enemy. This unpredictability, and the ability to tell your own absurd war stories, is one of the main reasons the game quickly built a devoted community. On PS5 the game benefits from fast loading and stable performance even with dozens of enemies and explosions on screen at once, though in the first weeks after release it struggled with server load due to unexpectedly high player interest, leading to temporary matchmaking queues.

The game's living world also evolves based on the collective results of players across platforms, so the outcomes of individual battles influence events in the so-called Galactic War and unlock new weapons, enemy factions, and story twists for the entire community at once. Developers also regularly add new factions, weapons, and so-called Warbonds with cosmetic rewards, which keeps player interest high for months after release. Helldivers 2 quickly became a phenomenon thanks to its combination of tactical cooperation, self-irony, and satisfying weapon-fueled carnage, and it is now cited as an example of how to revive a live-service game with compelling design, regular content, and a sense of humor.

**Why play it:** For players craving tactical cooperation with self-irony and satisfying weapon-fueled carnage, Helldivers 2 is a phenomenon whose living world evolves based on the collective results of the entire community across platforms.

ps5__street-fighter-6.teaser: Capcom's return to form; World Tour teaches techniques from legends like Ryu and Chun-Li.
ps5__street-fighter-6.article:
**Street Fighter 6** marked Capcom's return to form after years in which the previous entry, Street Fighter V, was hampered by a slow pace of content. The game offers three distinct modes — the classic Fighting Ground for training and matches, an online Battle Hub resembling a virtual arcade with avatars, and an extensive story mode called World Tour, in which the player creates their own character, roams an open city full of side quests, and gradually learns techniques from legendary masters throughout the series, including Ryu and Chun-Li.

The combat system is built around a new mechanic called the Drive Gauge, which links defensive and offensive techniques into a single shared resource and forces players to constantly choose between aggression and caution, pushing the game closer to modern, more accessible fighting games. The system also includes powerful Drive Impact strikes capable of breaking through an opponent's guard, and so-called Perfect Parries, which, when timed precisely, open up room for a devastating counterattack. The visual style combines more realistic character models with bold color effects and a street-graffiti aesthetic, giving the game a fresh identity compared to its more austerely styled predecessor. On PS5 the game runs smoothly at high resolution and uses an online infrastructure with quality rollback netcode, making long-distance matches nearly imperceptibly lag-free.

Critics particularly praised the depth of the combat system, the elaborate World Tour mode, and its accessibility for newcomers thanks to the simplified Modern control scheme, without that limiting players who prefer classic controls with all the traditional command inputs. The Battle Hub also earned praise for successfully bringing the feeling of a shared arcade, familiar to players from the arcade halls of past decades, back into an online environment. Street Fighter 6 became one of the pillars of the competitive fighting game scene and remains a regular tournament title at major esports events to this day, confirming its lasting influence on the entire genre.

**Why play it:** For both newcomers and fighting game veterans, Street Fighter 6 offers the depth of classic controls as well as the accessibility of the Modern scheme, complemented by a Battle Hub that brings back the feeling of a shared arcade from the halls of past decades.

ps5__mortal-kombat-1.teaser: A reboot of the series' mythology; Kameo fighters add a second character to every match.
ps5__mortal-kombat-1.article:
**Mortal Kombat 1** presents a reboot of the series' timeline following the events of the previous entry, Aftermath, in which the god Liu Kang recreated the entire universe in a new image, giving the series a chance at a clean start. The game thus features familiar characters like Scorpion, Sub-Zero, and Raiden in new roles and relationships, which creates room for surprising twists even for players intimately familiar with the series' previous mythology, while also allowing easy entry for complete newcomers. The combat system introduces so-called Kameo fighters — a second character summoned during a match for supporting strikes, combos, and rescue maneuvers, adding another layer of tactics beyond the classic one-on-one fights.

The series stays true to its most iconic feature — brutal Fatalities, complemented by new Fatal Blows and interactive arenas full of destructible background animations, which leverage the power of the PS5 for more detailed and fluid character movement. The graphics engine delivers realistic skin and clothing textures and blood effects that are a typical, if long-controversial, hallmark of the series, distinguishing it from competing fighting games. The story mode once again relies on cinematic direction with several hours of cutscenes that tell a cohesive narrative arc full of betrayals, alliances, and surprising fates for well-known characters.

Reception at launch was mixed due to technical problems at release and more aggressive monetization through cosmetic items, but the core of the game — satisfying, brutal combat with a deep combo system — remains essential for fans of the series. Over time, developers fixed many of the criticized issues and expanded the game with the extensive Khaos Reigns expansion, adding further characters and story chapters. Mortal Kombat 1 remains among the most-played fighting games on PS5 to this day, regularly receiving new characters, seasonal content, and balance updates.

**Why play it:** For fans of the series, Mortal Kombat 1 remains an essential choice thanks to its satisfying, brutal combat with a deep combo system, even though its launch was marred by technical problems and more aggressive monetization.

ps5__tekken-8.teaser: A more aggressive, faster Tekken thanks to the Heat mechanic; the Mishima clan's vendetta continues.
ps5__tekken-8.article:
**Tekken 8** continues the long-running saga of the Mishima clan's family vendetta, adding the son of the series' main hero, Jin Kazama, as the central character in a story about stopping an apocalyptic conflict between father and son. The combat system is built around a new mechanic called Heat, which temporarily strengthens attacking options, enables special moves, and allows for more aggressive, more fluid combat than in previous entries, which were known more for cautious, technical play focused on spacing and waiting for the opponent's mistake. The classic roster of twenty-plus characters is further rounded out by newcomers as well as the return of fan-favorite fighters from earlier entries in the series.

The graphics engine, built on Unreal Engine, looks visually stunning on PlayStation 5 — from realistic faces to destructible environments and dynamic weather and rain that changes arena behavior mid-match and gives the setting a cinematic feel. The game also includes an extensive story mode called Arcade Quest, which guides newcomers through the basics of the combat system and the series' history via stylized comic-book-style storytelling. The soundtrack combines electronic and orchestral elements, and together with elaborate character animation gives the series a sense of drama without sacrificing the speed and readability needed for competitive play at the highest level.

Tekken 8 was received by critics as one of the most accessible entries in the series thanks to assist control schemes and training tools for newcomers, without sacrificing depth for advanced players accustomed to complex combos and mix-ups. The extensive roster of characters, many of whom have accompanied the series since the nineties, also gives players the chance to find their own style among dozens of distinct fighters. It quickly established itself as a pillar of the competitive fighting-game esports scene alongside Street Fighter and continues to receive regular updates and new fighters to this day, confirming its status as one of the genre's key franchises on the current console generation.

**Why play it:** For newcomers and advanced players alike, Tekken 8 offers assist control schemes and training tools without sacrificing depth for complex combos, making it one of the genre's key franchises of the current generation.

ps5__guilty-gear-strive.teaser: An anime fighting game with cel-shaded graphics; a slower pace opened the door to newcomers.
ps5__guilty-gear-strive.article:
**Guilty Gear Strive** is the latest entry in Arc System Works' long-running fighting game series, known for its extremely stylized graphics reminiscent of hand-drawn anime animation, even though the characters are actually fully three-dimensional models rendered using cel-shading. Strive noticeably slowed the pace compared to the series' previous, extremely fast entries and simplified the control scheme and combo system, opening the door to newcomers without alienating longtime fans of the technical, combo-oriented gameplay built on precisely reading the opponent.

On PlayStation 5 the game excels above all visually — dynamic lighting, exaggeratedly expressive hit effects, and fluid character animation create the impression that the player is controlling characters straight out of a premium anime series' battle scene. Each character also has a markedly distinct archetype and rhythm of play, from slow heavy hitters to fast technical fighters with intricate combinations, so every player can find a character matching their own style. The music is no less important: composer Daisuke Ishiwatari's aggressive metal soundtrack is among the most distinctive in the entire genre and reinforces the energetic atmosphere of each match and character. The online infrastructure, with quality rollback netcode, also enables smooth long-distance matches, which had long been a problem for previous entries in the series and had noticeably held back the growth of its competitive scene.

Guilty Gear Strive was embraced by critics and the community alike as one of the most accessible and visually striking fighting titles of its generation, also praised for its striking gallery of charismatic characters and their elaborate personal stories. Thanks to regular seasonal updates with new fighters and a balanced yet still deep system, it has become a mainstay of the competitive scene and is still cited today as proof that a fighting game can be beautiful and deep at the same time.

**Why play it:** For players who want a fighting game that is beautiful and deep at the same time, Guilty Gear Strive is one of the most accessible and visually striking titles of its genre, with a charismatic gallery of characters.

ps5__lies-of-p.teaser: A dark steampunk Pinocchio as a soulslike; you assemble your sword from blades and hilts.
ps5__lies-of-p.article:
**Lies of P** is a soulslike action game that reimagines the classic story of Pinocchio as a dark, steampunk version of turn-of-the-century Belgian Paris, overrun by mad, aggressive puppets after a mysterious catastrophe. The player takes on the role of the puppet Pinocchio, who must become a real human by the end of the journey, and must face deadly enemies using swords that can be modularly assembled from various blades and hilts, plus a mechanical arm loaded with special abilities such as a flamethrower, a chain trap, or an electric discharge, freely switchable as needed.

The combat system emphasizes precise parry timing, called Guard Regain, which lets you return deflected damage back to the enemy, giving the game its own identity compared to other soulslike titles built more around dodging. Weapons are also subject to wear, and Pinocchio's mechanical arm offers optional modules that let the player tailor their combat style to their own preferences. On PlayStation 5 the game runs stably with elaborate graphics, a gothic atmosphere, and a gloomy industrial soundtrack that heightens the sense of decay in the explored city of Krat, full of rusted mechanisms. The visual style combines Victorian elegance with mechanical horrors and grotesque bosses, creating a distinctive atmosphere different from the Japanese templates of the genre that the game otherwise openly builds on.

Critics particularly praised how the Korean development studio managed to meet the high expectations of demanding genre fans without losing its own artistic signature and literary inspiration. Lies of P is today considered one of the best soulslike titles outside FromSoftware's output, and proof that the genre still has room for new, original interpretations of classic literary motifs and stories, even from a previously lesser-known development studio.

**Why play it:** For soulslike fans looking for new interpretations of classic literary motifs, Lies of P proves that even a lesser-known studio can meet the high expectations of demanding players without losing its own signature.

ps5__armored-core-vi-fires-of-rubicon.teaser: The mech series from FromSoftware returns after ten years; you build your mech from dozens of parts.
ps5__armored-core-vi-fires-of-rubicon.article:
**Armored Core VI: Fires of Rubicon** marked the return of FromSoftware's mech action series after more than ten years away, combining fast, vertical action with a deep customization system for combat machines called Armored Cores. The player becomes a mercenary pilot hired by corporations competing for a rare mineral on the planet Rubicon, assembling their own mech from dozens of parts — legs, weapons, core, and generator — where each combination fundamentally changes the playstyle, from lumbering tanks to nimble bipedal machines capable of long airborne flight.

Battles are fast and vertical, emphasizing energy management, weapon overheating, and the so-called stagger system, which allows a devastating critical attack once the opponent's gauge is filled. The bosses are among the most demanding and memorable elements of the game and require repeated experimentation with the mech's loadout as well as mastery of the core game mechanics — several of them can also fundamentally change tactics mid-fight. The campaign also offers several different endings depending on which contracts the pilot accepts throughout the game, encouraging repeated playthroughs to uncover the whole story. On PlayStation 5 the game benefits from fast mission loading and smooth frame rates even in hectic battles with dozens of visual effects on screen at once.

Reception was very positive — critics praised how FromSoftware managed to carry over its philosophy of demanding but fair design from its renowned soulslike games into a completely different mech genre without losing the studio's recognizable signature. Armored Core VI is today seen as a successful revival of a once-niche series and an entry point for a new generation of mech action fans as well as longtime soulslike players, who appreciated the similarly honest difficulty in the game.

**Why play it:** For longtime soulslike players and newcomers to the mech genre alike, Armored Core VI carries FromSoftware's philosophy of demanding but fair design into a completely different setting of battle robots.

ps5__rise-of-ronin.teaser: Open-world action set at the end of the shogunate era; dialogue choices change the outcome of the story.
ps5__rise-of-ronin.article:
