**Rise of the Ronin** is a sprawling open-world action game from Team Ninja, set in the turbulent period at the end of the shogunate era in nineteenth-century Japan, as the country is forcibly opened to Western influence and internal factions fight over the future direction of the entire island nation. The player takes on the role of a nameless ronin trained by a secret order, whose fate becomes intertwined with real historical events and figures of the Bakumatsu era, while choices made in dialogue and missions influence which faction the hero ultimately sides with and how the story ultimately ends, giving the game room for repeated playthroughs with different outcomes.

The combat system builds on Team Ninja's earlier experience with games like Nioh — combining various weapon combat styles from katana to naginata, which can be switched on the fly, with an emphasis on parrying called Counterspark and exploiting the specific weaknesses of individual opponents based on their own combat school. The open world offers a horse for fast travel across the landscape, a glider for descending from heights, and plenty of side activities from photographing period landmarks to building personal relationships with companion characters, which affect available equipment as well as alternative paths through the story. On PlayStation 5 the game makes use of expansive environments in Yokohama, Kyoto, and Edo with detailed period architecture and changeable weather that alters both visibility and enemy behavior.

Critics praised the ambitious scope, the combat system, and the unconventional historical setting, though they pointed out technical shortcomings and a less refined open world compared to competing titles in the genre. Rise of the Ronin nonetheless represents a significant step by Team Ninja toward large open worlds and offers a unique look at a less commonly portrayed historical era within the action samurai genre, which is otherwise dominated by more fictional stories.

**Why play it:** For fans of action samurai games set in a less common historical era, who can forgive technical rough edges in exchange for a vast world and a stylish combat system.

ps5__star-wars-jedi-survivor.teaser: Cal Kestis searches for the hidden city of Tanalorr; five lightsaber stances to switch between.
ps5__star-wars-jedi-survivor.article:
**Star Wars Jedi: Survivor** continues Cal Kestis's story from Fallen Order, taking the player five years later, when the hardened Jedi hides from the Empire and tries to find refuge in the form of the legendary hidden city of Tanalorr, about which little is known and whose existence most of the galaxy considers a mere legend. The game expands the lightsaber combat system with new fighting stances — from a heavy two-handed style through dual blades to a fast crossguard style and a standalone blaster — freely switchable on the fly depending on the situation and the type of enemy on screen, giving battles considerable tactical depth.

A more open level design offers more paths to explore and return to older locations with newly gained abilities, in the spirit of the metroidvania design that strongly characterized the first installment of the series as well, rewarding patient players with rare equipment and cosmetic items. On PlayStation 5 the game offers noticeably larger and more detailed environments, denser vegetation, and larger crowds of characters in cities, which, however, took a technical toll on the console in the form of frame rate fluctuations at launch, later partially addressed by patches. The film score again builds on the long-standing tradition of the Star Wars saga and heightens the most epic moments of the story as well as the battles against iconic villains.

Critics praised the deepened combat system, the more elaborate world, and an emotionally stronger story compared to the first installment, even though technical issues at launch noticeably detracted from an otherwise excellent overall impression. Star Wars Jedi: Survivor is today considered one of the best modern Star Wars titles and proof that the brand can work even outside the linear action-adventure format of the previous console generation, thanks to a compelling protagonist and an elaborate world.

**Why play it:** For fans of Star Wars and action-adventures alike, offering a deepened combat system and a stronger story than the first installment, despite the technical issues that plagued the series at launch.

ps5__resident-evil-2.teaser: A remake of the 1998 classic, free as an upgrade; Leon and Claire each offer a different night of horror.
ps5__resident-evil-2.article:
**Resident Evil 2** is a complete remake of the 1998 classic, which Capcom offered on PlayStation 5 as a free technical update with support for higher resolution, shorter loading times, and a more stable frame rate. The player finds themselves in a Raccoon City police station overrun by zombies shortly after the outbreak of a viral infection called the T-virus, and in the shoes of rookie Leon Kennedy or student Claire Redfield, moves through cramped corridors full of scarce ammunition and constant tension, with both scenarios offering a different perspective on the same night of horror.

The shift from the original's fixed camera to an over-the-shoulder camera fundamentally transformed the game's pacing — both combat and exploration are noticeably more tense, since the player sees danger up close and has a harder time judging a safe attack distance. Managing a limited inventory and solving puzzles with keys and items scattered throughout the station gives the game a more deliberate pace compared to purely action-oriented horror games and forces the player to plan every step ahead. Sound design is one of the game's strongest points: creaking doors, distant footsteps, and sudden silences build the horror atmosphere just as effectively as the immortal monster known as Mr. X, who relentlessly pursues the player throughout the entire station no matter where they hide. On PS5 the game runs smoothly even in scenes with a high number of enemies on screen and uses fast loading for near-instant restarts after death.

The remake was received by critics as a model example of how to sensitively rework an older classic without losing its identity and horror atmosphere, and it still ranks among the best-rated horror games of all time. Resident Evil 2 confirmed that survival horror can be just as frightening and tense on modern consoles as in the era of the first PlayStations, only with noticeably more modern, precise, and cinematic gameplay.

**Why play it:** For anyone who wants to experience how sensitively an older classic can be reworked without losing its atmosphere — one of the best-rated horror games ever made.

ps5__wo-long-fallen-dynasty.teaser: A fantasy China from the makers of Nioh; the Deflect mechanic rewards precise, bold parrying.
ps5__wo-long-fallen-dynasty.article:
**Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty** places the player in a fictional, fantasy version of Chinese history at the end of the Han dynasty, when the vast empire is convulsed by the Yellow Turban Rebellion and supernatural forces that turn dying people into monstrous demons. Team Ninja, the longtime creators of the Nioh series, replaced the slower, stamina-driven combat system here with a considerably faster approach built around the so-called Morale system and the Deflect mechanic, which allows parrying almost any attack, including magical ones, and rewards the player for bold, precisely timed actions.

The game emphasizes an aggressive, attack-oriented playstyle that rewards taking risks over cautiously waiting for the opponent's mistake, which clearly sets it apart from the more typical, defensively oriented soulslike titles. The story loosely follows the Chinese classic novel Romance of the Three Kingdoms, and during the campaign the player encounters characters inspired by real historical generals and rulers of the era. Five elemental magic paths let you tailor your character to different combat styles, from fiery offensive spells to bolstering your own stance and resilience in battle. On PlayStation 5 the game offers smooth combat even in hectic battles with dozens of characters on screen at once, which was a technical challenge for earlier entries in the series on older hardware, adding to the epic feel of the large battle scenes.

Critics praised the faster, more aggressive pace and the innovative approach to the parrying system, although the story and overall atmosphere were seen as less distinctive and less tightly constructed than in competing titles in the genre. Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty expanded the soulslike genre with a new perspective on what combat built purely around attacking and deflecting the enemy can look like, and cemented Team Ninja's position as specialists in demanding, historically themed action games.

**Why play it:** For soulslike fans craving a faster pace built around attacking and deflecting the enemy, even though the story and atmosphere remain overshadowed by the combat system.

ps5__uncharted-legacy-of-thieves-collect.teaser: A remaster of Nathan Drake's two finales at 60 fps; Naughty Dog's direction shines even brighter.
ps5__uncharted-legacy-of-thieves-collect.article:
**Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection** brings to PlayStation 5 a remastered version of the two final installments in the adventure series about treasure hunter Nathan Drake — the extensive Uncharted 4: A Thief's End and the standalone expansion The Lost Legacy, starring Chloe Frazer alongside the mercenary Nadine. Both games were reworked with support for higher resolution, smoother frame rates of up to 60 frames per second, and noticeably faster loading, which makes the cinematic direction that Naughty Dog has always been famous for stand out even more.

The gameplay combines third-person cover shooting with acrobatic climbing across cliffs and ancient ruins and elaborate puzzles inspired by historical mysteries and long-lost civilizations. Effective vehicle chases, entire buildings collapsing during battles, and carefully choreographed action sequences give the game a pace comparable to major adventure blockbusters. Cover-based combat and dynamic shootouts alternate with quieter passages full of dialogue and character interaction, giving the story emotional weight comparable to a great Hollywood adventure film. The visuals on PS5 are among the most technically impressive of the entire generation, with detailed environmental textures ranging from snowy mountains to dense jungles to beautifully lit sunsets.

The collection was received by critics as one of the best ways to experience the culmination of the Uncharted series on modern hardware, confirming the quality of the original titles even years after their initial release. Uncharted: Legacy of Thieves Collection remains a benchmark example of a linear cinematic action-adventure and a reminder of the influence the series has had on the entire genre of third-person adventure games, including many titles that have drawn inspiration from it since.

**Why play it:** For players who want to experience the peak of the Uncharted series in its best available form — a benchmark example of a cinematic third-person action-adventure.

ps5__final-fantasy-vii-remake-intergrade.teaser: A PS5 launch title; turn-based magic gives way to real-time action combat with a tactical pause.
ps5__final-fantasy-vii-remake-intergrade.article:
**Final Fantasy VII Remake Intergrade** is an expanded version of the reimagining of the legendary 1997 RPG, released as a launch title for PlayStation 5. The game retells the story of the mercenary Cloud Strife and the eco-terrorist group Avalanche, fighting against the megacorporation Shinra that controls the city of Midgar, but instead of a turn-based system it offers dynamic real-time action combat supplemented by a tactical pause and a clear command menu for individual characters. The player switches between party members, combining regular attacks with magic, special abilities, and summoning eidolons, with each character having their own combat style, so Tifa attacks up close with fast combos while Aerith wields a staff and magic at range. The original linear story is expanded with new characters, side quests, and a longer, more elaborate rendition of Midgar, turning the first installment into a standalone, many-hours-long game.

On PS5 the game runs at high resolution with support for 60 frames per second and shorter loading times, significantly changing the experience compared to the original PS4 version. Visually it is one of the most elaborate reconstructions of Midgar, with music reworking Nobuo Uematsu's classic themes into orchestral and rock arrangements that shift dynamically depending on the combat situation and the environment. The edition also includes an episode featuring Yuffie Kisaragi, which expands the story with a standalone storyline taking place in parallel with the main adventure and offers a different combat style built around materia and shuriken.

The remake attracted major attention from both fans and newcomers upon release, as it dared to enrich the well-known story with new plotlines and philosophical questions about fate and memory without betraying the emotional core of the original. Critics and players alike praised the combat in particular, which successfully combined action dynamics with the tactical depth of classic Final Fantasy games. Today it is seen as an example of how sensitively a classic can be modernized without losing its character, and serves as an introduction to the trilogy continuing with Rebirth.

**Why play it:** For fans of the original and newcomers alike, who will appreciate a sensitively modernized story and combat combining action dynamics with the tactical depth of classic Final Fantasy games.

ps5__persona-3-reload.teaser: A remake of the 2006 classic; high-school social sim meets the Tartarus tower.
ps5__persona-3-reload.article:
**Persona 3 Reload** is a complete remake of the 2006 JRPG that brings to PlayStation 5 the story of students secretly fighting Shadows during the Dark Hour, a hidden period that appears between one day and the next and that most people are not even aware of. The game combines a high-school social simulation, building relationships known as Social Links, and exploration of the endless, procedurally shifting Tartarus tower with turn-based combat in which the player assembles Personas representing the characters' psyches and exploits enemies' elemental weaknesses for effective combos and bonus All-Out Attacks. During the daily schedule the player divides limited free time between studying, hobbies, part-time jobs, and building friendships, which directly affects the strength and variety of their Personas and opens up new conversations with characters outside the main story.

Reload preserves the atmosphere of the original but completely reworks the graphics, animations, and part of the music into a modern form, while the iconic soundtrack remains the core of the game's melancholic yet energetic atmosphere, supplemented with newly recorded versions of some tracks and a reworked combat soundscape. On PS5 the title benefits from fast loading and smooth performance even in Tartarus's large interiors, which makes long play sessions easier between school, dating characters, and nightly expeditions into the tower, where the player gradually descends into ever more dangerous floors full of stronger Shadows.

At launch the remake was received very positively, as it made the acclaimed installment accessible to new players who had not experienced the original on PlayStation 2, while also confirming that the concept of alternating ordinary student life with a dark fight for survival still works flawlessly today. Persona 3 Reload is considered one of the most notable JRPG remakes of recent times and shows how strongly the series has influenced the entire genre, including many later games built on the combination of social simulation and combat system.

**Why play it:** For players who missed the original on PlayStation 2 — one of the most notable JRPG remakes of recent times, combining student life with a dark fight for survival.

ps5__persona-5-tactica.teaser: The Phantom Thieves in grid-based tactics reminiscent of XCOM; cover decides the battle.
ps5__persona-5-tactica.article:
**Persona 5 Tactica** is a tactical spin-off from the main series that shifts the Phantom Thieves from turn-based combat into a grid-based tactics genre reminiscent of XCOM. The player controls Joker and his companions from Persona 5 in a new, self-contained kingdom, where they must advance using cover, exploit height advantages, and combine Persona abilities to trigger flashy group attacks called All-Out Attacks. The party is also joined by a new ally whose special ability opens up further tactical options for flanking enemies and taking over their positions on the map, while the player plans equipment and character placement between battles according to the type of upcoming fight and the terrain available on the map.

The game retains the series' stylized comic-book art and jazzy, pop-inflected music, and on PS5 it runs smoothly, with short transitions between exploration, dialogue, and battles divided into individual chapters. Compared to the main entries, Tactica is significantly shorter and more accessible, with simpler maps and fewer combat variables, making it a good entry point for players who were intimidated by the scope of the classic Persona games but want to experience the same visual style, characters, and atmosphere of rebellion against authority. Outside the main story, the game also offers side challenges and costume collecting that reference previous entries in the series.

Critics praised the title especially for its elegant blend of the tactics genre with the series' identity, and for the fact that, despite being a spin-off with a shorter playtime, it offers a meaningful story about freedom and rebellion against an oppressive regime. Today it is seen as a successful, if smaller, experiment that shows the Persona brand can work even outside its traditional gameplay framework and reach fans of different genres who might not have picked up the series' larger entries on their own.

**Why play it:** For Persona fans willing to try the series outside its traditional framework — an elegant tactical spin-off with a shorter playtime but a meaningful story about rebellion against oppression.

ps5__granblue-fantasy-relink.teaser: Action JRPG based on the mobile game Granblue; up to three players co-op against massive bosses.
ps5__granblue-fantasy-relink.article:
**Granblue Fantasy: Relink** is an action JRPG set in the world of the popular mobile game Granblue Fantasy, offering on PlayStation 5 a fast-paced combat system with combos, special abilities, and flashy full-party finishing attacks. The player travels on a flying ship between islands floating in the sky and, together with a band of mercenaries, fights enemies and massive bosses, with co-op play for up to three additional players being a key part of the experience. Choosing a character from the rich roster of available heroes, each with a distinct set of abilities and their own special-attack gauge, gives combat plenty of room for experimentation and personal playstyle, and characters can be freely swapped between expeditions and have their skill trees developed using gathered materials and experience points.

Visually the game combines an anime style with richly animated attacks and colorful environments, which on PS5 stands out thanks to stable framerates even in hectic battles with many enemies and effects on screen at once. The orchestral music supports well the epic tone of a story about friendship and adventure among the sky islands drifting in an eternal sky, and it also accompanies long post-game battles with the toughest bosses, which require well-coordinated teamwork, well-executed dodging, and a deep understanding of the combat mechanics.

After years of delays and several renamings during development, Relink was warmly received at launch, largely thanks to its satisfying combat system and post-game content that entices players to keep playing with friends long after finishing the main story. Today the title is valued as one of the most accessible entry points into the world of Granblue Fantasy for players outside Japan, and as an example of how a long-running mobile IP with a rich history can be successfully converted into a full-fledged console game.

**Why play it:** For players looking for satisfying action combat and hours of content to enjoy with friends — one of the most accessible entry points into the world of Granblue Fantasy outside Japan.

ps5__unicorn-overlord.teaser: Tactical RPG from Vanillaware; assembled units fight automatically according to your rules.
ps5__unicorn-overlord.article:
**Unicorn Overlord** is a tactical RPG from Vanillaware that offers on PlayStation 5 warfare on a large map, where the player, as exiled prince Alain, assembles units made up of several fighters and sends them against enemy squads in battles that play out automatically but are deeply customizable. The key mechanic is building formations, choosing positions, skills, and equipment for each character so that the unit functions as a well-coordinated team even without direct control in combat, while the player can pause the battle at any time and adjust tactics as the situation on the map develops, or set unit behavior using simple conditional commands, which also makes the game function as a well-thought-out puzzle about the optimal squad composition.

The game benefits from Vanillaware's distinctive hand-drawn visual style, which on PS5 stands out with detailed character animations and colorfully rich environments of the liberated continent of Fevrith, divided into several regions each with its own character, culture, and politics. The orchestral music underscores the epic tone of the campaign, and together with an elaborate system of bonds between units, which gradually strengthen their ties and unlock new shared skills and personal conversations, it creates a game that can be played for dozens of hours without feeling repetitive, especially thanks to the large number of classes and equipment.

Unicorn Overlord was praised at launch for the depth of its strategic options, its wide range of classes, and for how elegantly it makes an otherwise complex tactical-RPG genre accessible even to less experienced players thanks to a clear interface and gradual introduction of mechanics. Today it ranks among the most notable titles of its genre for the entire generation and confirms Vanillaware's reputation as a studio with a distinctive visual and gameplay signature, able to maintain its own identity even against much larger publishers.

**Why play it:** For fans of tactical RPGs as well as newcomers to the genre thanks to a clear interface and gradual introduction of mechanics — one of the most notable titles of its generation.

ps5__eiyuden-chronicle-hundred-heroes.teaser: Spiritual successor to Suikoden from its former creators; over a hundred recruitable heroes.
ps5__eiyuden-chronicle-hundred-heroes.article:
**Eiyuden Chronicle: Hundred Heroes** is a spiritual successor to the classic Suikoden series, created by many of its former developers, offering on PlayStation 5 a turn-based JRPG with a huge cast of over a hundred recruitable characters. The player builds their own fortress, gradually gaining specialists with various skills from blacksmiths to alchemists, leads an army into large-scale war campaigns that play out in a separate strategy mode, and at the same time resolves the personal stories of individual heroes in smaller, more intimate battles fought in parties of six, where the choice of lineup and the characters' relative positions on the battle line significantly affects the course of combat and which abilities get to come into play.

The visual style combines hand-drawn 2D characters with 3D environments, evoking classic 1990s JRPGs, but on PS5 it adds smoother animations, sharper textures, and faster loading between the many locations of the sprawling world and inside the ever-growing fortress, which gradually gains shops, minigames, and other amenities depending on how many specialists the player manages to recruit. The music lends the game a nostalgic yet fresh tone befitting a sprawling fantasy world full of political intrigue and rival factions, among which the player, as the young mercenary Nowa, seeks their own place and gradually builds a resistance movement against a powerful empire that rules the surrounding kingdoms with an iron fist.

The game was partly funded through crowdfunding, and fans had awaited it for years as a spiritual continuation of the beloved but long-discontinued Suikoden series. Upon release it received a mixed-to-positive reception, as the technical side and some animations fell slightly short of the project's ambitions, but the story, music, and scale of the cast confirmed that the Suikoden legacy still has its place — and its loyal, devoted audience — on modern consoles.

**Why play it:** For loyal fans of the Suikoden series who will appreciate the huge cast, the music, and the story despite minor technical shortcomings that fall slightly short of the project's ambitions.

ps5__octopath-traveler-ii.teaser: HD-2D graphics blend pixel art with 3D depth; eight stories intertwine in a single world.
ps5__octopath-traveler-ii.article:
**Octopath Traveler II** is a JRPG with so-called HD-2D graphics, combining pixel-art characters with a three-dimensional environment, depth of field, and lighting effects that on PlayStation 5 stand out with a sharp image even in detailed night scenes accompanied by dynamic weather. The game offers eight independent main characters with their own storylines that intertwine across a shared world and can temporarily join one another's parties, along with a turn-based combat system built around exploiting enemies' elemental and weapon weaknesses and the so-called Boost system, which lets players stockpile points for a devastating chain of attacks or empower a single strike for a decisive blow against bosses, turning every battle into a question of properly timed risk and reward.

Beyond combat, the game places emphasis on interacting with town residents using each character's unique abilities, such as challenging someone to a duel, stealing items, gathering information, or hiring helpers into the party, which gives the world a sense of reactivity and offers several ways to resolve the same situation depending on which character the player is currently leading. Composer Yasunori Nishiki once again delivered both melancholic and energetic pieces that rank among the most praised parts of the game and beautifully complement the atmosphere of eight interconnected adventures unfolding across the sprawling continent of Solistia, with its distinct biomes and cultures.

At launch the second installment was received as a refinement of the first Octopath Traveler thanks to better interwoven storylines, a fine-tuned combat system, and new day-and-night mechanics that affect available shops and the behavior of townspeople. Today it is considered one of the most visually distinctive modern JRPGs and proof that retro-inspired graphics can look thoroughly fresh on current hardware while remaining legible even after dozens of hours of play.

**Why play it:** For JRPG lovers who appreciate the genre's most visually distinctive titles, it offers a refined sequel with more thoughtfully interwoven stories and a day-and-night mechanic.

ps5__star-ocean-divine-force.teaser: A sci-fi and fantasy JRPG with flight across the battlefield; Blindside turns evasion into an opening.
ps5__star-ocean-divine-force.article:
**Star Ocean The Divine Force** is an action JRPG blending sci-fi and fantasy elements, in which the player switches perspective between the earthbound captain Raymond and Princess Laeticia from a technologically underdeveloped planet, who, after a ship crash, find themselves forced to cooperate to save her world from an impending war. The combat system plays out in real time on open battlefields, where characters fly freely using a special device, combine physical attacks with special abilities called Blindside that allow them to effectively dodge attacks and open up an opponent's defenses, and use synergy actions with other party members for devastating combined finishers. Characters can also be equipped with a range of weapons and accessories that affect their stats and available combat techniques.

On PlayStation 5 the game offers sprawling environments to freely explore, including vertical movement above the ground thanks to a short-flight ability, and the option to freely switch between two protagonists with different perspectives on the same story, which also affects which scenes, dialogues, and side quests the player experiences during their playthrough. The technological and magical sides of the Star Ocean world create a distinctive genre blend the series has cultivated since the nineties, accompanied by orchestral music typical of the whole series, alternating epic battle themes with calmer melodies during free exploration of the planets and their distinct civilizations.

Divine Force was received as a return to a more action-oriented and open take on the series after previous, more linear entries, and it was praised especially by loyal fans for its ambitious storytelling from two different points of view on the same events. Today it serves as a reminder that, even after all these years, Star Ocean keeps its own identity on the border between JRPG and sci-fi adventure, though it remains more a matter for the series' devoted fans than a mass-market hit.

**Why play it:** For devoted fans of the series longing for a more action-oriented and open take, with ambitious storytelling from two points of view, rather than for those seeking a mass-market hit.

ps5__remnant-ii.teaser: A soulslike shooter for up to three players; procedural worlds and Archetypes to combine.
ps5__remnant-ii.article:
**Remnant II** is an action RPG blending elements of the soulslike genre with a third-person shooter, in which players, alone or with up to two others, make their way through procedurally generated worlds full of dangerous creatures and massive bosses threatening the last remnants of humanity. The character selects and combines so-called Archetypes representing character classes, such as healer, hunter, or engineer with their own automated turret, and gathers weapons, mods, rings, and relics that allow for dozens of distinct playstyles depending on the preferred approach to combat, which can be freely combined with one another for synergistic effects and a personalized approach to every enemy and boss.

On PlayStation 5 the game offers varied environments spread across several interconnected worlds, from dark lands reminiscent of medieval Europe through alien deserts to gothic, decaying cities, with procedural generation ensuring that the placement of enemies, side quests, and secret areas differs slightly with each playthrough, so no two players' runs are ever quite the same, even on repeated playthroughs. Atmospheric sound design and the combination of ranged shooting with melee combat give the game a different feel from classic soulslike titles built purely around melee weapons, and that holds true even in co-op for up to three players at once, who can freely complement one another with their own assembled combat loadouts and strategies.

Remnant II was received at launch as a marked improvement over the first game thanks to more varied and expansive worlds, deeper character progression, and better co-op for more players. Today it ranks among the most successful mid-budget RPGs of the generation and shows that combining a third-person action shooter with soulslike depth can work very convincingly even without the marketing budget of the very largest publishers.

**Why play it:** For fans of cooperative action RPGs who will appreciate more varied worlds and deeper progression than in the first game — a convincing blend of third-person shooting with soulslike depth.

ps5__dragon-age-veilguard.teaser: Fourth installment in the BioWare series; faster combat built on combos with two companions.
ps5__dragon-age-veilguard.article:
**Dragon Age: The Veilguard** is an action RPG from BioWare, the fourth installment in the long-running fantasy series, in which the player, as the leader of the Veilguard group, confronts the awakening of two ancient gods who have escaped their prison and threaten the entire world of Thedas as well as the connected realm of spirits. The combat system is faster and significantly more action-oriented than in previous entries, built on combos between the player's abilities and those of the two actively selected companions from a roster of seven party members overall, who can be combined with each other in battle for effective cooperation and special joint attacks, while the player's own character combines one of three classes with an optional skill specialization and equipment tailored to their preferred combat style.

On PlayStation 5, the game offers visually elaborate environments and characters with an emphasis on bold, stylized graphics that move away from the more realistic approach of previous series entries, a branching dialogue system with the ability to influence relationships with the party, and decisions that affect the fate of individual factions and cities across the continent of Thedas. At the start, the player creates their own character, including their origin and profession, which is reflected both in the reactions of the surrounding world and in the available dialogue options during conversations. The music and sound design underscore the epic scope of the story, which follows on from the events of the series' previous entries as well as the companion animated series Absolution.

Veilguard sparked mixed reactions among long-time fans upon release due to its departure from the darker tone of previous entries toward a more accessible and more colorful action-oriented approach, while new audiences appreciated the fluidity of combat and the quality of the written companions. Today it is seen as a distinctive, if debated, attempt by BioWare to revive the Dragon Age brand for a new generation of players after years of protracted and repeatedly redirected development of the entire project.

**Why play it:** For players open to a more accessible and more colorful take on the series with fluid combat and well-written companions, even though long-time fans may miss the darker tone of previous entries.

ps5__dragon-quest-iii-hd-2d-remake.teaser: HD-2D remake of the 1988 classic; turn-based combat stays faithful, just faster.
ps5__dragon-quest-iii-hd-2d-remake.article:
**Dragon Quest III HD-2D Remake** is a modern reimagining of one of the most influential JRPGs in history from 1988, which on PlayStation 5 uses the same HD-2D graphics as previous Dragon Quest remakes, combining pixel-art characters with the depth of three-dimensional environments, dramatic lighting, and distance blur. The game follows a young hero who, on his sixteenth birthday, sets out into a world full of monsters to complete the legacy of his father, a warrior named Ortega, while the series' classic turn-based combat system remains faithful to the original, only streamlined and sped up for today's players accustomed to a more modern pace of play. The player assembles a party of their own, nameable characters, whose appearance and abilities are determined by their chosen vocation, and can retrain them into a different vocation at any time in the capital city, allowing the party's composition to be adjusted to the current needs of the expedition.

The remake preserves the series' iconic music in new orchestral arrangements and adds modernized spell and combat animations, making the game look noticeably livelier on PS5 than the technically simple original from the 1980s. The open world with the option to choose day or night, which affects character behavior and available shops, and the elaborate vocation system, which determines the skills and appearance of individual party members, are among the elements that made Dragon Quest III famous upon its original release and that the remake carefully preserves while slightly expanding with new content.

Upon release, the remake was received as a sensitive and faithful modernization of a classic that shows the roots of many mechanics found in today's JRPGs directly at one of their founders and reminds us how fundamentally this entry shaped the entire genre. Today it serves as an ideal entry point for players who want to discover the history of the genre without having to play a technically outdated version from the 1980s.

**Why play it:** For players wanting to discover the roots of many mechanics in today's JRPGs without having to reach for a technically outdated 1980s version — a sensitive and faithful modernization of a classic.

ps5__quarry.teaser: Spiritual successor to Until Dawn; nine teenagers, dozens of endings, one night at camp.
ps5__quarry.article:
**The Quarry** is an interactive horror drama from Supermassive Games, the creators of Until Dawn, which brings the studio's proven formula to the big screen with nine playable teenagers stranded on the last night at a summer camp. The player makes choices through branching dialogues and quick quick-time events, where every decision and even a minute's delay in pressing a button can send a member of the group to their death — the game offers dozens of different endings depending on who survives. The structure resembles an episodic horror series with transitions reminiscent of comments from an experienced narrator, who occasionally deals out tarot cards hinting at future events and suggests what kind of horror awaits the player in the next chapter.

On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from photorealistic actor models captured via performance capture, and the cast includes several well-known Hollywood faces, lending the story a cinematic level of acting. The atmosphere is enhanced by dense music and the sound backdrop of a forest where something unnatural is awakening under the full moon, and the game skillfully alternates quiet dread with bursts of action. An optional local multiplayer mode for multiple players on one TV allows players to take turns making decisions, turning the game into a form of social entertainment similar to a board game, where players take turns arguing over each subsequent decision.

Contemporary reception was largely positive, with critics praising the production values and the experience of playing with friends, though some noted excessive similarity to the studio's previous titles. For genre fans, it offers a comfortable entry point thanks to accessible controls and the option to follow the story more like an interactive film than a demanding game. To this day it functions primarily as an entertaining experience for one evening with friends, where the tension of decision-making is heightened by a group of people gathered around one couch, arguing about who to sacrifice next and who to save instead.

**Why play it:** For a group of friends looking for a thrilling evening on one couch — an accessible interactive horror that works more like a film you watch together than a demanding game.

ps5__until-dawn.teaser: Survival horror with a butterfly effect: a small decision can cost a life.
ps5__until-dawn.article:
**Until Dawn** is a survival horror interactive drama that arrived on PlayStation 5 in 2024 as a completely rebuilt remake of the original 2015 title, this time with improved graphics, new lighting, and expanded scenes. A group of young people returns to a remote mountain lodge a year after a tragedy, only to find themselves at dawn face to face with an ancient evil hidden in an abandoned mine. The player switches between the perspectives of individual characters and decides their fate through dialogue choices and quick reactions to quick-time events, while the butterfly effect system links seemingly innocent decisions to far-reaching consequences later in the game, so that even a small detail noted in the first few minutes can come back in the final act.

The remake uses the DualSense controller for haptic feedback and adaptive triggers that heighten the tension during a chase or quiet movement through the dark, and newly recorded facial animations elevate the acting performances a notch above the original. The musical score relies on oppressive string motifs and silence interrupted by sudden jump scares, which is typical for the genre but is particularly effective here thanks to spatial audio. The level design of the lodge and the snowy forests combines claustrophobic interiors with more open outdoor sections, where the player searches for totems that predict future scenes and scattered memorabilia that flesh out the story's background.

The original 2015 game became one of the most influential titles in the interactive horror genre and paved the way for further Supermassive Games projects, and the remake has now let a new generation of players experience the story in a modern technical package. Reception of the remake was more mixed than for the original, with some players criticizing the high price for essentially the same content, yet Until Dawn remains valued for its gripping story, memorable characters, and nerve-wracking decision-making, where no choice comes for free and even a seemingly insignificant decision from the first hour can determine who lives to see the morning.

**Why play it:** For fans of gripping storytelling where even a seemingly insignificant choice can cost someone their life, though the remake is worth considering mainly on sale given its high price for essentially the same content.

ps5__alan-wake-remastered.teaser: Psychological horror where you must first scatter the darkness with a flashlight, then shoot.
ps5__alan-wake-remastered.article:
**Alan Wake Remastered** brings the original psychological horror game from Finnish studio Remedy Entertainment to PlayStation 5 in full glory, this time in a reworked visual form with improved textures, character models, and lighting running at higher resolution and frame rate. The player takes on the role of writer Alan Wake, who, while searching for his missing wife in the fictional town of Bright Falls, discovers that the pages of his unfinished manuscript are coming true and the darkness around him is coming alive as a hostile Taken horde. Fighting these shadow enemies requires first dispelling the protective darkness with a flashlight and only then neutralizing them with a firearm, creating a distinctive combat rhythm based on light as the main weapon and forcing the player to constantly monitor dwindling flashlight batteries and other light sources.

The game is structured into episodes resembling a television series, complete with previously-on recaps and cliffhangers, matched by cinematic camerawork and an emphasis on the atmosphere of a fog-shrouded pine forest and nighttime drives along deserted roads. The musical backdrop combines ambient dread with licensed songs playing at the end of each chapter, giving the narrative an unusually personal tone. On PS5, the remaster also includes bonus content in the form of two episodes taking place after the end of the main storyline, expanding the view of the characters' fates and the mythology of Bright Falls.

The 2010 original is still considered one of the most significant psychological horror games of its generation, and its influence is evident in the subsequent sequel Alan Wake II. The remaster has allowed players who missed it on older consoles to discover the game, and thanks to a steady 60 frames per second on PS5, the controls feel more precise than ever. Even years later, the dense atmosphere, the literary ambition of the script, and the distinctive blend of action and horror still captivate, keeping Alan Wake deservedly regarded as a genre classic and essential playing for anyone wanting to understand the context of the second game.

**Why play it:** For fans of psychological horror and future Alan Wake II players, the remaster is essential — its dense atmosphere and the script's literary ambitions have held up even years later.

ps5__little-nightmares-ii.teaser: Dark puzzle platformer about a small boy among giant, terrifying figures.
ps5__little-nightmares-ii.article:
**Little Nightmares II** is an atmospheric puzzle platformer from Tarsier Studios, in which the player takes on the role of a boy named Mono as he journeys through a warped world full of giant, unsettling figures and dark secrets. The core mechanics involve sneaking, jumping, and solving physics-based puzzles with the help of a rescued girl named Six, as the two work together to manipulate the environment, open locked doors, or distract enemies who are always disproportionately larger and more frightening than the players' tiny characters. The game emphasizes quiet observation and quick evasive steps away from danger, since direct confrontation almost always means instant death, forcing the player to rely on patience rather than reflexes.

The visual style relies on a striking art design reminiscent of a dark fairy tale, where the deformed proportions of characters and households heighten the sense of helplessness of a small child in a hostile adult world. On PlayStation 5, the game runs smoothly with detailed textures and dense lighting that deepens the claustrophobic feel of narrow corridors, attics, and television broadcasts spreading a strange static threat. The soundtrack is sparse, which makes the creaking floors, the characters' breathing, and sudden dissonant tones signaling nearby danger stand out even more, while the absence of spoken dialogue forces the player to focus on every visual detail.

The game follows on from the first installment, expanding its world with new locations, including a school and a city, without losing the characteristic silent storytelling method that features not a single spoken line. Critics praised especially the visual style and the breathtaking finale, which raises questions for the continuing story. Little Nightmares II still stands today as an example of how strong atmosphere and tension can be built purely on visuals, sound, and clever level design, without the need for the explicit violence that previous generations of horror games often relied on.

**Why play it:** For lovers of atmospheric platformers, it shows how tension can be built purely through visuals, sound, and clever level design without any unnecessary explicit violence.

ps5__dark-pictures-anthology-house-of-as.teaser: Third entry in the Dark Pictures anthology: a siege by ancient evil amid the Iraq war.
ps5__dark-pictures-anthology-house-of-as.article:
**The Dark Pictures Anthology: House of Ashes** is the third installment of the horror anthology from Supermassive Games, this time set in 2003 during the Iraq War, where a group of American soldiers and Iraqi civilians accidentally uncovers an ancient underground temple hiding something far older than human civilization. The gameplay builds on the series' well-known formula: the player moves through a linear story full of branching dialogues and quick-time events, where decisions and failed reactions can lead to the deaths of individual characters and different variations of the ending. The novelty here is the emphasis on the tense relationships between hostile soldiers who are forced to cooperate in order to survive, and their mutual distrust is reflected in how easily they decide to sacrifice one another.

The underground setting, full of excavations and ancient architecture, gives the game a claustrophobic character different from previous entries, which took place mostly outdoors, and dark corridors lit only by flashlights heighten the tension from unseen creatures lurking in the shadows. On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from detailed motion-capture acting and cinematic camera direction, making it feel like an interactive horror film. The music combines Middle Eastern instrumental motifs with a dark orchestral backdrop that underscores the feeling of being lost deep underground, far from any help on the surface.

The entry continued the popular format of the series' previous games and expanded the option for cooperative play and online multiplayer, allowing players to follow different versions of the story with friends. Critics praised the more gripping pace and better character relationships compared to the previous entry, Little Hope, even though some mechanics have remained part of the series since its first title. House of Ashes remains one of the anthology's stronger entries thanks to its untraditional setting and the tension to which the combination of wartime conflict and supernatural threat significantly contributes, forcing hostile sides to seek a common enemy.

**Why play it:** For fans of interactive horror played with friends, it offers an untraditional wartime setting steeped in supernatural threat and a more gripping pace than the previous entry in the series.

ps5__dark-pictures-anthology-devil-in-me.teaser: Conclusion of the Dark Pictures first season: a hotel inspired by real-life killer H. H. Holmes.
ps5__dark-pictures-anthology-devil-in-me.article:
**The Dark Pictures Anthology: The Devil in Me** concludes the first season of Supermassive Games' horror anthology with the story of a film crew shooting a documentary about serial killers, who are invited to a remote hotel inspired by the real historical figure of the murderer H. H. Holmes. The gameplay again builds on branching dialogues, quick-time events, and decisions affecting the survival of individual characters, but this time with the novelty of free movement around the rooms and interaction with objects that can be collected, photographed, and used to resolve situations or to unlock shortcuts for further playthroughs.

The hotel, full of hidden traps, secret passages, and mechanical devices, references the real inventions of its historical inspiration and gives the setting a morbid, playful sense of dread, where the player must learn to read warning signs before a trap springs shut. On PlayStation 5, the game offers detailed Victorian-style interiors and carefully lit scenes, where the interplay of light and shadow both reveals and conceals danger, and the sound design skillfully works with the creaking of gears, distant cracking of wood, and the quiet clicking of trigger mechanisms. Cooperative modes allow the story to be followed from multiple angles at once with other players, with each character having access to different parts of the hotel.

Devil in Me was received as a fitting conclusion to the series' first season thanks to its return to a more explicit slasher style after the more psychological previous entries and its greater emphasis on exploring the environment. Critics praised the inventive mechanical hotel as a game setting, although some pointed to technical issues at launch. Today the game is interesting mainly as a demonstration of how classic slasher clichés can be transformed into interactive storytelling with a real risk of losing a favorite character at any point during play.

**Why play it:** For fans of the classic slasher, the inventive mechanical hotel and the real risk of losing a favorite character make for an interesting conclusion to the anthology's first season, despite minor technical issues.

ps5__outlast-trials.teaser: A co-op survival horror without weapons — the only way to survive is running and hiding.
ps5__outlast-trials.article:
**The Outlast Trials** is a co-op survival horror game from Red Barrels, set during the Cold War in secret facilities of the sinister Murkoff Corporation, which is testing new mind-control methods on involuntary volunteers. Unlike previous entries in the series, the game is built around repeatable missions for one to four players, where the goal is to complete assigned tasks in a closed environment full of traps, guards, and experimental monsters, while the player has no weapon available and the only defense remaining is running, hiding, and distracting teammates and enemies alike.

Between missions, players upgrade their character in a central hub called the Sleep Room, where they acquire new abilities, cures for insanity, and cosmetic customizations, pushing the game closer to the structures of games-as-a-service than to traditional linear horror. On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from fast loading and stable performance even with four players at once, while the atmosphere is completed by the industrial environment of laboratories and dark underground corridors, complemented by the unsettlingly calm advertising aesthetic of the fictional corporation. The sound design relies on the character's breathing and the footsteps of pursuers as key danger indicators, making headphones practically essential gear here.

The game expands the Outlast universe with a new perspective on the Murkoff organization and brings an unconventional co-op format to the survival horror genre, which has proven to be a viable alternative to solo experiences. Reception was positive, especially among players seeking shared tension with friends, although purebred horror fans sometimes missed the intensity of the isolated experience from previous entries. To this day it works best as social horror entertainment, where fear is both amplified and softened by the presence of teammates, with whom you can share both the panic and the relief of a successful escape.

**Why play it:** For a group of players looking for shared tension, the co-op format of survival horror is a refreshing alternative to solo experiences, even if purebred fans might miss the intensity of isolation.

ps5__immortality.teaser: An interactive film from Sam Barlow: click on details and jump between scenes.
ps5__immortality.article:
**Immortality** is an interactive film from creator Sam Barlow, which presents the player with hundreds of film clips from three never-finished films by the fictional actress Marissa Marcel, and lets them investigate what actually happened to her. The gameplay is based on the principle of visual search, where the player clicks on any object or face on screen to jump to another scene in which the same element appears, gradually piecing together a fragmented story from dozens of seemingly unrelated clips shot across different decades of the actress's career, from screen tests to never-released final cuts of the films.

This unconventional storytelling method demands active detective work and patience from the player, since no scene provides answers directly, only further clues leading to an understanding of the hidden conspiracy running through all three fictional films. On PlayStation 5, the game excels through the quality of the digitized film material and the authentic period style of the camera work and editing matching the individual decades in which the films are set, from grainy celluloid to the sharper digital image of the nineties. The absence of traditional game music and the emphasis on cinematic sound heighten the feeling that the player is truly digging through an archive of lost film material with their own hands.

Immortality builds on Sam Barlow's previous projects and pushes the concept of interactive film toward an even more abstract and demanding form of storytelling, without any hint or progress map. Critics praised the bold structure and the surprising final reveal, earning the game several awards in the best narrative category. To this day it is considered one of the most original experiments with narrative form in modern games, rewarding above all players willing to devote time to their own investigation and piecing together connections without any hints.

**Why play it:** For players willing to devote time to their own investigation without any hints, it offers one of the most original experiments with narrative form in modern games.

ps5__alone-in-dark.teaser: A remake of the 90s classic: Lovecraftian horror in a crumbling mansion in Louisiana.
ps5__alone-in-dark.article:
**Alone in the Dark** is a survival horror game from Pieces Interactive, which in 2024 revived the legendary series from the nineties with a story set in the crumbling Derceto mansion, shrouded in the atmosphere of American Louisiana. The player can choose to play as private detective Edward Carnby or mansion resident Emily Hartwood, both characters are fully voiced with their own unique game content, and both experience the story slightly differently, revealing a different perspective on the family secret intertwined with cosmic horror in the spirit of H. P. Lovecraft, whose influence is felt in every corner of the mansion's atmosphere.

The gameplay combines exploration of the sprawling mansion and its strange dreamlike detours with light combat elements and puzzle-solving based on key items, letters, and symbols scattered throughout the mansion and its surrounding grounds. On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from a detailed, richly modeled Victorian mansion with lush surrounding swamp vegetation and changing weather that underscores the breakdown of the boundary between reality and the main characters' nightmares. The musical score and the sound backdrop of cicadas and creaking wood evoke the sultry atmosphere of the American South, while the narrative rests on the vocal performances of well-known actors lending the characters believable humanity amid the horror.

The series restart faced comparisons with the 1992 original, considered one of the pioneers of the survival horror genre, and reviews were mixed, mainly due to the uneven combat side of the game. Even so, critics praised the atmosphere, the visual style, and the effort to return to a slower, story-focused horror instead of the action pace of many current titles. For fans of classic psychological horror, Alone in the Dark offers a pleasant return to the atmosphere of the genre's old roots in a modern technical package, even if it is more of a tribute to the classic than a revolution of the genre.

**Why play it:** For fans of classic psychological horror, it's a pleasant return to a slower, story-focused pace in a modern coat, though the uneven combat is a reminder that it's more a tribute to the classic than a revolution of the genre.

ps5__plague-tale-requiem.teaser: The continuation of the story of siblings fleeing the plague and swarms of thousands of rats.
ps5__plague-tale-requiem.article:
**A Plague Tale: Requiem** is a narrative action-adventure from the French studio Asobo Studio, a continuation of the story of siblings Amicia and Hugo de Rune, who in fictional medieval France flee from the plague, the Inquisition, and a dark curse awakening in the boy a supernatural power over rats, which is slowly consuming him at the same time. The gameplay combines stealthy movement through the environment, solving environmental puzzles, and combat with slings, crossbows, and alchemical concoctions that can be combined for various tactical effects, while swarms of thousands of rats remain a key visual and gameplay element capable of engulfing an entire battlefield in an instant and sweeping away everything living that stands in its way.

On PlayStation 5, the game excels with sprawling environments of the Mediterranean coast, sunny vineyards, and dark catacombs, between which it transitions seamlessly without loading screens, and the massive number of simulated rats on screen together with sophisticated lighting demonstrates the console's technical capabilities. The music is once again composed by Olivier Deriviere, whose combination of orchestral and electronic elements underscores both the emotional and horror passages, from quiet conversations to a desperate escape from the sea of rats, while the relationship between the siblings remains the emotional core of the entire story and the motivation for all their decisions.

Requiem builds on the acclaimed first entry Innocence and expands its world with a darker tone and higher production values, while also addressing the price that Hugo's supernatural ability carries for his and Amicia's souls. Critics praised the emotional storytelling, the visual side, and the courage to head in a darker direction at the end than many similar family adventures. To this day, the game is valued as an example of how a narrative adventure can combine a touching sibling relationship with horror elements and the merciless world of medieval Europe gripped by plague and fear of the unknown.

**Why play it:** For players seeking an emotionally powerful narrative experience, it offers a darker continuation of Innocence with horror elements and the merciless world of plague-stricken medieval Europe.

ps5__slitterhead.teaser: Action horror from the creator of Silent Hill: the player jumps from body to body mid-fight.
ps5__slitterhead.article:
**Slitterhead** is an action horror game from Bokeh Game Studio, founded by Keiichiro Toyama, creator of the original Silent Hill and Gravity Rush, and the game is set in the fictional Asian metropolis of Kowlong, plagued by parasitic monsters hiding in human bodies. The player controls a bodiless entity capable of entering the bodies of random passersby, called Rasid, and using their unique abilities in combat against the monsters, and when the host is seriously injured, the entity can instantly jump into another nearby person, so the fight continues seamlessly in a new body without a single pause in the action, while the abandoned body collapses lifelessly to the ground.

Combat combines fast melee attacks with hemoprove, blood turned into a weapon, and tactical switching between several permanent playable characters with different abilities and personal stories, which makes it feel more like a B-movie action horror than a classic survival horror. On PlayStation 5, the game builds on a neon, rain-soaked metropolis inspired by Asian cities and dense, atmospheric music by Akira Yamaoka, known primarily for the sound of the Silent Hill series. The visual style combines a realistic environment with grotesquely transformed monsters emerging from human bodies, giving the game a distinctly visceral, organic character.

The game represents a return of key creators of Japanese survival horror to the genre they themselves helped shape years ago, this time with an emphasis on a more action-driven and rawer approach to combat. Reception was mixed to positive, with critics praising the originality of the body-possession concept and the music, while some pointed out the repetitive mission structure. Slitterhead is interesting above all as a new voice in the genre of Japanese horror from the people who stood at its birth, and as a demonstration of where the classic horror legacy can be taken when its own founders take it on.

**Why play it:** For fans of Japanese horror, it's an interesting, rawer action alternative from creators who helped shape the genre themselves, even if the missions get repetitive at times.

ps5__chants-of-sennaar.teaser: A language puzzle without a single word: you decipher the pictograms of the Tower of Babel's levels.
ps5__chants-of-sennaar.article:
**Chants of Sennaar** is a logic adventure from the French studio Rundisc, in which the player travels between the isolated levels of a giant Tower of Babel and gradually deciphers the distinct pictographic languages of the individual communities inhabiting each level, without the game ever offering a single word in English or any other real language. The gameplay rests on observing recurring symbols in the context of gestures, images, and situations, from which the player builds their own dictionary and gradually comes to understand dialogues, inscriptions, and puzzle mechanics needed to progress to the higher levels of the tower, without anyone literally translating anything for them.

Each level of the tower represents a distinct culture with its own visual identity, color palette, and type of puzzles, from a religiously-tinged community of monks through a military order and a merchant bureaucracy to a civilization obsessed with technology, and the player gradually discovers the connections and shared history among them that the tower's inhabitants themselves are unaware of. On PlayStation 5, the game presents a clean, illustrative visual style reminiscent of a moving book illustration and simple, meditative music, which lets the process of deciphering the language stand out as the main gameplay and emotional experience of the entire journey through the tower.

The game's concept draws on the biblical story of the Tower of Babel and turns the language barrier between civilizations into the central gameplay mechanic instead of mere set dressing, which was received by critics as an inventive and refreshing approach to the logic game genre. The game earned recognition for its originality and sensitive treatment of the theme of communication and understanding between different cultures. To this day, Chants of Sennaar is a valued example of how language itself can be turned into a fascinating game system that entertains precisely because the player never gets an easy explanation for free but must earn it through their own observation.

**Why play it:** For lovers of logic games built on solving the language itself, it's an original puzzle that rewards patient observation without unnecessary hints.

ps5__cocoon.teaser: A minimalist puzzle adventure from the designer of Limbo — worlds nested one inside another.
ps5__cocoon.article:
**Cocoon** is a minimalist logic adventure from the Danish studio Geometric Interactive, involving Jeppe Carlsen, a former game designer at Playdead, the studio behind Limbo and Inside, and the game builds on a simple yet profound concept of mutually nested worlds hidden inside portable orbs. The player controls a small insect-like creature that carries and switches between several such worlds, where entering an orb transports the player inside a smaller universe with its own puzzles, while changes made inside affect the world outside and vice versa, creating an elegant puzzle system of interconnected levels.

The game contains no text, dialogue, or tutorial; all understanding of the mechanics arises purely through observation and experimentation with the environment, an approach typical of the creators' previous projects. On PlayStation 5, the game excels with a clean graphic style featuring distinct color accents for each world against an otherwise dark, industrial backdrop, and gentle ambient music underscores the meditative pace without unnecessary haste. The gradual revelation of how the individual orb-worlds fit inside one another like a Russian matryoshka doll is among the most striking moments of the whole game and rewards the player with a feeling of pure understanding of the system.

Cocoon builds on the legacy of atmospheric, textless logic platformers made famous by titles like Limbo or Inside, but pushes it forward with its own original mechanism of nested worlds, which critics repeatedly called one of the smartest game ideas of the year. The game earned numerous nominations and awards in the best logic game category and was praised for its elegant design without a single unnecessary element. To this day, Cocoon is a showcase example of how a single game idea can be built into a compact, perfectly tuned experience from start to finish, without a single wasted minute.

**Why play it:** For fans of elegant, textless puzzle platformers, it's a compact, perfectly tuned experience built on the clever idea of nested worlds, without a single wasted minute.

ps5__destruction-allstars.teaser: A PS5 launch title: a demolition arena where you also fight on foot after crashing your car.
ps5__destruction-allstars.article:
**Destruction AllStars** was among the flagship titles with which Sony demonstrated the capabilities of the freshly launched PlayStation 5. It's an original mix of a vehicular demolition arena and battle royale elements – players try to smash opponents' cars and score points in enclosed arenas, but at any moment they can bail out of the wreck and continue fighting on foot until they find a new vehicle. Each character also has a unique special ability, whether a short teleport, temporary invisibility, or the ability to summon a heavier vehicle, which makes the game feel more like a hybrid of a hero shooter and an auto-destruction sport than a classic demolition derby. The individual game modes also differ in their objective – in some, points are scored for destruction, while others are purely about the last crew standing.

Technically, it was a showcase next-gen title: lightning-fast loading thanks to the SSD enabled an almost instant transition between menu and arena, switching smoothly between vehicle and on-foot action happened without the slightest hitch, and above all the precisely implemented haptic feedback of the DualSense let you literally feel the difference between asphalt, sand, or a deformed car body panel on impact. The visual side relied on bold colors, stylized characters with strong personalities, and energetic electronic music, which pushed the game toward the feel of a sports esports broadcast, including virtual commentators describing the action in the arena in real time similar to an online shooter.

The game was released free for PlayStation Plus subscribers, which secured it a huge initial player base, but in the long run it failed to maintain interest comparable to competing online titles, and support from the studio gradually waned until the servers were shut down after a few years of operation. Even so, it remains an interesting and, in players' memory, still vivid example of how the racing genre can be combined with multiplayer action and the possibilities of a new console generation, and for fans of car destruction it offered a fresh, original experience you simply won't find on other platforms.

**Why play it:** For fans of car destruction it was a fresh combination of racing and multiplayer action; today it's worth remembering mostly as an interesting chapter in the early days of PS5, since the servers have since been shut down.

ps5__dirt-5.teaser: A launch arcade racer: mud, snow and ice, career narrated by real drivers.
ps5__dirt-5.article:
**Dirt 5** was among the PlayStation 5 launch titles, and compared to the previous, more simulation-focused entries in the series, it deliberately shifted toward lighter, more arcade-style fun. Instead of a strict driving model, it offers wild off-road races across snow, desert, ice and city streets, complemented by flashy drifting, jumps and environmental destruction elements such as falling barrels or collapsing fences. The career mode, subtitled Playgrounds, is told through short narrated segments voiced by real figures from the motorsport world, guiding the player through various disciplines from rallycross to ice racing to freestyle exhibitions and stunt challenges on specially designed arenas.

On PlayStation 5, the game fully leveraged the power of the new console — running at high resolution with support for a higher frame rate, significantly shorter loading times compared to the previous-generation version, and support for DualSense haptic feedback and adaptive triggers, which let players distinguish the different surface under the wheels as well as the car's behavior during a skid or wheel slip on ice. Visually, it's a colorful, stylized title with dynamic weather that changes mid-race, and striking lighting during the transition between day and night, accompanied by an energetic soundtrack made up mostly of electronic, rock and hip-hop music.

At release, Dirt 5 was seen as a fun, accessible alternative to more seriously pitched racing simulations and one of the first showcases of the new console generation's capabilities, though it didn't fully overshadow the critical acclaim of previous entries in the series. From today's perspective, it's a brisk, undemanding choice for players who want fast arcade fun without having to study complex car setups, and as one of the first truly next-gen titles it remains a pleasant reminder of the early days of the PlayStation 5.

**Why play it:** Anyone wanting brisk, undemanding arcade fun without fiddling with car setup will find a pleasant reminder of the early days of the PlayStation 5.

ps5__ea-sports-wrc.teaser: The WRC license returns to Codemasters: track surface changes with the weather and rivals' tire marks.
ps5__ea-sports-wrc.article:
**EA Sports WRC** marked the return of the World Rally Championship license to Codemasters studio, this time under the EA Sports banner, and also a noticeable shift toward a more sophisticated simulation compared to earlier, more arcade-oriented rally titles. Players drive real tracks from the entire WRC calendar with cars matching current and historical categories, and the game emphasizes a physics model for how the car behaves on changing surfaces — from gravel to asphalt to snow and mud — which also changes dynamically over the course of a stage depending on weather and the tire marks left by earlier drivers, so the same track behaves differently in the day's last run than in the first.

On PlayStation 5, the game offers a career mode called Moment of Your Own Team, where the player gradually builds a team, hires a co-driver and engineers, and develops vehicles between seasons according to available budget and results. Technically, the title benefits from the console's power through detailed track models created using laser scanning of real stages, real-time changing weather, and support for DualSense haptic feedback, which can convey the difference between slippery gravel and firm asphalt directly through the controller. The audio side is rounded out by the authentic roar of engines across the different classes and the co-driver's pace notes read from the track, which are an essential part of the atmosphere for the rally genre.

The game was received as a solid, if not flawless, return to the series' simulation roots, with critics and players praising especially the driving physics and variety of tracks, while criticism was aimed more at technical shortcomings at launch. For motorsport fans, EA Sports WRC represents one of the most comprehensive rally simulations available on PS5 and shows well how a traditional license can be modernized for the current console generation after years away.

**Why play it:** For motorsport fans, it's one of the most comprehensive rally simulations on PS5, even though technical rough edges accompanied its release.

ps5__f1-24.teaser: The official F1 game with a driving model built on "car feel".
ps5__f1-24.article:
**F1 24** is the latest installment in the official series of games based on the Formula 1 World Championship, developed for EA Sports by Codemasters studio. Compared to previous entries, it brings a reworked driving physics model built around the concept of "car feel," which aims to more faithfully simulate the behavior of the season's real single-seaters, including reactions to tire wear, fuel strategy and changing track conditions during a rainy race. It also includes the story-driven Driver's Career mode, in which the player goes through a season as part of both a fictional team and the real teams on the grid, deals with engineers, and gradually builds a reputation in the paddock.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs at high resolution with support for higher frame rates, which is crucial for accurately reading the track and rivals in corners given the fast single-seaters reaching over three hundred kilometers per hour. DualSense haptic feedback conveys engine vibrations and how the chassis behaves when losing grip on curbs or wet asphalt, while the adaptive triggers simulate brake and throttle pedal resistance based on how hard they're pressed. The race presentation mimics Formula 1 television broadcasts, including results graphics, commentary, and the authentic sounds of each team's engines as well as the surrounding grandstand atmosphere.

The F1 series has long been considered the standard for official motorsport racing simulations, and its yearly installments, F1 24 included, tend to be judged mainly on how faithfully and enjoyably they capture the feel of driving a real single-seater, and on the small improvements to the career mode compared to the previous year. For Formula 1 fans, it's a natural choice on PS5, whether they want to play purely as a simulation with all driving assists turned off, or enjoy a more accessible, arcade-style difficulty setting. The offering also includes online multiplayer, where players compete in full championships with real scoring rules, collision penalties, and strategic pit-stop decisions, which keeps the game alive long-term beyond one-off career experiences.

**Why play it:** For Formula 1 fans, it's a natural choice on PS5, offering both a demanding simulation and a more accessible arcade setting, plus online championships with real rules.

ps5__grid-legends.teaser: Arcade racing with the cinematic Driven to Glory story mode and live-action actors.
ps5__grid-legends.article:
**Grid Legends** continues the long-running Grid series, combining accessible arcade racing with a fairly extensive story mode called Driven to Glory, in which we follow a fictional team and its drivers through live-action sequences filmed with real actors. The player fights their way through various motorsport disciplines, from circuit races to drift challenges to an ice track and electric vehicles, with a car roster that includes a wide range of vehicles from sports specials to large trucks and stock cars, which differ significantly in how they behave on track.

On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from fast loading and a stable high frame rate, which contributes to a smooth and legible experience even in hectic moments given the dense starting grids of dozens of cars and destructible track environments. A distinctive feature is the dynamic track storytelling system, which generates unique race moments in real time based on car positions and incidents, so every race plays out a bit differently and the commentator reacts to what's currently happening. Visually, it's a colorful, energetic title with striking body damage, dynamic weather, and a range of real and fictional locations around the world.

Critics praised especially the fun and accessible driving side and the ambitious story mode, though the latter was at times seen as overly theatrical, with some dialogue coming across as clunky. Grid Legends thus fits into the tradition of more arcade-oriented racing titles that prioritize fun and variety of disciplines over hardcore simulation, and on PS5 it offers a brisk, accessible alternative to more seriously pitched competing series focused on simulation. The multiplayer portion also benefits from fast matchmaking and a variety of disciplines, so players aren't limited to just one type of car or track and can switch between circuit, drift and offroad according to their mood.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for a brisk, accessible alternative to hardcore racing simulations and a variety of disciplines from circuits to drifting will also appreciate the fast matchmaking in online multiplayer.
