ps5__test-drive-unlimited-solar-crown.teaser: A return after ten years: an open Hong Kong Island and the fight between two rival factions.
ps5__test-drive-unlimited-solar-crown.article:
**Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown** revives the Test Drive Unlimited brand after more than ten years of silence, a series known for its open world and its emphasis on the social side of racing rather than pure competition. The game places the player on the open island of Hong Kong Island, where they move freely between asphalt roads, mountain switchbacks and dense urban development, collect and buy luxury cars from sports specials to premium SUVs, and gradually build a reputation in one of two rival factions, Sharp and Street, which compete against each other for the prestigious Solar Crown title.

On PlayStation 5, the game builds on a sprawling, densely populated open world with a smooth transition between free driving, races, car dealerships and social activities without loading screens between individual activities. Emphasis is placed on collecting and deeply customizing the car roster, which includes dozens of licensed brands including luxury and exotic manufacturers, and on multiplayer sharing of the open world with other players, who can encounter each other directly during free driving similarly to the legendary earlier entries in the series from the previous decade.

The brand's return was awaited with great hopes among fans of the original games, but the launch was accompanied by performance issues, server stability problems and missing content, which noticeably affected the game's initial reception among critics and players. Even so, Solar Crown remains an interesting attempt to revive the concept of an open world focused on luxury cars and social racing, and for fans of the original entries it represents the closest available alternative on PlayStation 5 to the spirit of the classic Test Drive Unlimited, albeit with the need to tolerate initial technical shortcomings. The developers gradually released fix updates and new content, so the state of the game improved over time, even though it carried the reputation of a troubled comeback for a long while after launch.

**Why play it:** For fans of the original Test Drive Unlimited, it's the closest available alternative on PS5, though you need to reckon with technical shortcomings, even as the game's state gradually improved.

ps5__ride-5.teaser: A motorcycle simulation from Milestone with an extensive lineup spanning history to circuits.
ps5__ride-5.article:
**Ride 5** is another installment in the motorcycle simulation series from the Italian studio Milestone, which has long specialized in licensed motorsport titles across disciplines from MotoGP to motocross. The game offers an exceptionally extensive selection of motorcycles, from classic historical machines to modern sport models to specials modified for circuit racing, with an emphasis on a detailed physics model of how the bike behaves under braking, leaning into corners and applying throttle out of a turn. The career mode takes the player through various disciplines and championships, from circuit races to time trials to special themed events dedicated to specific manufacturers.

On PlayStation 5, the game leverages the console's power for detailed track and motorcycle models, including faithfully rendered cockpit views, and for a stable high frame rate, which is important for accurately perceiving traction and the bike's lean angle in corners during fast motorcycle riding. DualSense haptic feedback can simulate engine vibrations as well as loss of grip on the front or rear wheel during more aggressive riding, contributing to a more realistic feel than purely arcade competitors. The sound design of the engines from individual brands, faithfully distinguishing the sound of a twin-cylinder from a four-cylinder, is something Milestone has long prided itself on.

The Ride series is regarded within the motorcycle simulation genre as a solid, technically proficient choice for players who want more of a simulation approach than the light arcade fun known from competing motorcycle titles. Ride 5 builds on this reputation and offers one of the most comprehensive motorcycle simulations available on the market on PlayStation 5, though it primarily targets already devoted motorsport fans rather than casual players. A track and livery editor lets the community share custom motorcycle and rider appearance edits, which keeps the series' active base going long-term between yearly releases.

**Why play it:** For devoted motorsport fans, it offers one of the most comprehensive motorcycle simulations on the market, complemented by a track and livery editor for sharing with the community.

ps5__motogp-24.teaser: The official MotoGP game with the full starting grid and tire wear.
ps5__motogp-24.article:
**MotoGP 24** is the official game based on the MotoGP championship and another yearly addition to the long-running series from the Italian studio Milestone, which has held the license for this series for many years now. The game features the full starting grid of the current season, including the Moto2 and Moto3 classes, licensed riders, teams and all tracks from the current calendar, and it emphasizes a simulation-style riding model in which working the brake, throttle and lean angle in corners, as well as how the tires behave as they wear over time, play a key role. The career mode lets players go through an entire riding career from the lower classes up to the premier category, including negotiating contracts with teams based on results achieved.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs at high resolution with a stable frame rate, which is essential for reading rivals' lines and precise braking points at high speeds exceeding three hundred kilometers per hour. DualSense haptic feedback conveys engine vibrations and signals loss of traction on the front and rear wheel while leaning, while the adaptive triggers simulate brake lever resistance based on how hard it's squeezed. The race presentation tries to mimic MotoGP television broadcasts, including results graphics, commentary and the authentic sound of engines from individual manufacturers such as Ducati, Yamaha or Honda.

The MotoGP series has long been considered the standard licensed motorcycle racing simulation, and the individual yearly installments tend to be judged mainly on small improvements to the riding model, opponent AI and career mode compared to the previous year. For fans of the MotoGP series, it's a natural choice on PlayStation 5, offering both a demanding simulation for advanced players and more accessible assist settings for less experienced ones. Besides the main career, the game also offers online championships and time trials, where players from around the world compare themselves on identical tracks and conditions.

**Why play it:** For fans of the MotoGP series, it's a natural choice on PS5 with a demanding simulation as well as more accessible settings, plus online championships against players from around the world.

ps5__nba-2k24.teaser: The market's most successful basketball simulation with the popular MyCareer mode.
ps5__nba-2k24.article:
**NBA 2K24** is another installment in the market's long-standing most successful basketball simulation, developed by Visual Concepts studio under publisher 2K. The game offers the full NBA and WNBA license, detailed gameplay mechanics built around precise timing in shooting and defense, and an extensive selection of game modes, from classic games and exhibition matches to the management-focused MyGM and MyNBA to the immensely popular MyCareer, in which the player builds their own basketball career from college league through the draft to becoming an NBA star and potentially a legend of the sport.

On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from the console's power especially in player animations, which are captured via motion capture directly from professional basketball players and connected through a sophisticated system of smooth transitions, making movement on the court feel natural and believable even during rapid changes of direction. DualSense haptic feedback complements the feel of dribbling and physical contact during battles under the basket, while the online social space The City lets players walk through a virtual city and play matches together with other players in a shared environment.

The NBA 2K series has long been regarded as the technical standard for sports simulations and a reference point for basketball presentation in video games, though it regularly faces criticism over the aggressive microtransaction model in MyCareer mode, built around the virtual currency VC. Despite these controversies, NBA 2K24 remains the most comprehensive basketball experience available on the console on PlayStation 5, with content that, thanks to regularly updated online seasons, can keep players entertained for tens to hundreds of hours. Besides basketball itself, the game also offers its own music soundtrack curated in collaboration with musicians across genres, which has long been one of the recognizable hallmarks of the whole series.

**Why play it:** Despite the controversial microtransactions in MyCareer mode, it remains the most comprehensive basketball experience on PS5, with content for hundreds of hours and its own music soundtrack.

ps5__madden-nfl-24.teaser: The official NFL simulation with a new on-field duel system called FieldSENSE.
ps5__madden-nfl-24.article:
**Madden NFL 24** is the latest entry in the long-running official NFL-licensed American football simulation, developed for EA Sports by studio EA Tiburon since the turn of the millennium. The 2024 edition introduced a reworked movement and duel system called FieldSENSE, aiming to more faithfully simulate one-on-one battles between offensive and defensive players at the moment of a pass, run, or block on the line. The game offers a wide range of modes, from a franchise management mode where the player runs an entire club including the draft and budget, through the card-collecting online Ultimate Team, to the career-focused Face of the Franchise in the style of a professional athlete.

On PlayStation 5, the game leverages the console's power for detailed player and stadium animations as well as smooth handling of large-scale on-field battles, where up to twenty-two characters converge at once into complex blocking schemes. DualSense haptic feedback adds to the feel of hard hits and blocks during line-of-scrimmage duels, while match presentation strives to closely mirror NFL television broadcasts, including graphics, commentary, and the atmosphere of a sold-out stadium.

The Madden series has long been the only officially NFL-licensed game, securing it a stable position among sports titles without direct competition, though it regularly faces criticism for the slower pace of gameplay innovation between yearly editions. For American football fans, Madden NFL 24 on PlayStation 5 is a natural choice with hundreds of hours of content thanks to regular online seasons and rosters updated to match real events in the league. Match presentation also changes according to the importance of the game, so playoff clashes and the Super Bowl final feel more ceremonial than a regular-season game, with distinct graphics for intros, celebrations, and crowd shots.

**Why play:** For American football fans, this is the only officially licensed choice on PS5, with hundreds of hours of content and a more ceremonial presentation for playoff games and the Super Bowl.

ps5__fifa-23.teaser: The last entry under the FIFA name, and the first to feature women's football in career mode.
ps5__fifa-23.article:
**FIFA 23** was the final installment of the long-running football series to carry the FIFA name, before the brand was renamed to EA Sports FC following publisher EA's split from the International Federation of Association Football. The game was the first to bring women's football into the main club career mode, added licenses for both the men's and women's top-tier world championships held that year, and technically improved the movement and duel system called HyperMotion2, based on motion data captured directly from real professional matches.

On PlayStation 5, the game ran at high resolution with a stable frame rate, featuring detailed stadiums, roaring crowds, and player animations that, thanks to advanced motion capture, felt smoother and more natural than on the previous console generation. It included fan-favorite modes such as club and player career, Volta Football focused on lighthearted small-sided street football, and the online Ultimate Team, long the series' most lucrative and most-played mode, built around collecting and trading player cards.

FIFA 23 was received as a solid, if not revolutionary, farewell to the old brand, with most of the media's and players' attention drawn to the upcoming renaming of the series for the following year. For fans of football simulations, it is the last entry to carry the historic FIFA name, and on PlayStation 5 it offers a content-rich title with thousands of licensed teams and players, still serving today as a solid choice for those who prefer the series' traditional name over the new brand. The atmosphere is rounded out by licensed leagues from dozens of countries, authentic stadiums with faithfully scanned details, and voice commentary in many languages, together creating the impression of watching a genuine televised football broadcast, even on older hardware carried over via backward compatibility.

**Why play:** For fans who prefer the series' traditional name over the new brand, it offers the last entry to carry the FIFA name, with thousands of licensed teams and an authentic stadium atmosphere.

ps5__pga-tour-2k23.teaser: A golf simulation, for the first time in years again featuring Tiger Woods on the cover.
ps5__pga-tour-2k23.article:
**PGA Tour 2K23** is a golf simulation by the Canadian studio HB Studios, published under the 2K label and featuring, for the first time in years, ambassador Tiger Woods, whose name returns to the series after years associated with rival golf brands. The game offers a realistic golf swing model controlled by moving the analog stick, licensed professional courses and real PGA Tour players, and an extensive MyCareer mode, in which the player gradually builds their own golfer from amateur tournaments through qualifiers up to the major championships.

On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from detailed golf courses with faithfully modeled terrain, dynamic weather and wind affecting ball flight, and smooth transitions between holes without lengthy loading. DualSense haptic feedback can subtly convey the quality of a shot based on the precision of the executed swing, adding another layer of feedback to otherwise largely visual, timing-based golf controls. Also included is the popular course editor, letting the community create and share their own courses to their imagination's content.

The 2K Golf series, formerly known as The Golf Club, has long been praised especially for its well-crafted course-creation system and honest, simulation-focused approach to the game itself, without unnecessary arcade compromises. PGA Tour 2K23 builds on that tradition and on PlayStation 5 offers one of the most complete golf simulations of its time, suited both to casual players and to fans seeking a deeper, longer-term career experience. The slower pace of play and lack of time pressure also make it a welcome, relaxing alternative to more action-packed sports titles available on the same console, further aided by online tournaments where players compete for leaderboard standings on the same courses under the same conditions.

**Why play:** For players seeking a calmer, honest golf simulation without time pressure, this is one of the most complete golf games of its time, including online tournaments for leaderboard standing.

ps5__snowrunner.teaser: An off-road simulation with no racing: the goal is simply to get cargo through mud and snow to its destination.
ps5__snowrunner.article:
**SnowRunner** is a rough-terrain driving simulation by studio Saber Interactive, in which the player operates trucks and off-road vehicles to haul cargo, rescue stuck machines, and build infrastructure across vast, open regions full of mud, snow, flooded rivers, and rutted unpaved roads. Unlike classic racing games, the goal here is neither speed nor competing against other vehicles, but rather mastering the terrain, choosing the right drivetrain and all-wheel-drive setup, selecting tires, and patiently planning a route between points of interest scattered across the sprawling map.

On PlayStation 5, the game received an enhanced next-gen version with higher resolution and a more stable frame rate, which shows especially in the simulation of mud, water, and dynamically deformable terrain — the central element of the entire gameplay concept, changing based on where vehicles have driven. The vehicle physics model accounts for cargo weight, weight distribution, and the type of drivetrain and differential, so the same vehicle behaves completely differently loaded with heavy cargo than it does empty on a firm road. The open world, split into several sprawling regions in Russia, Alaska, and elsewhere, offers dozens of vehicles ranging from ordinary pickups to massive Russian and American heavy-duty trucks and cranes.

SnowRunner built on the success of the previous game, MudRunner, and was received as one of the most elaborate off-road driving simulations on the market, praised especially for its authentic sense of struggle against the terrain and the satisfaction of successfully freeing a deeply stuck vehicle. On PlayStation 5, it offers dozens to hundreds of hours of content thanks to regularly added paid and free regions and vehicles, and it remains a favorite choice for players seeking a meditative, unhurried type of driving simulation without pressure to be fast or competitive. Cooperative multiplayer additionally lets players plan logistics together and rescue heavy cargo with others, making the game a pleasantly shared experience for a small group of friends.

**Why play:** For players seeking a meditative, unhurried driving simulation, it offers dozens to hundreds of hours of content and cooperative multiplayer for rescuing heavy cargo together with friends.

ps5__it-takes-two.teaser: Playable only with two players; nearly every chapter introduces a new mechanic.
ps5__it-takes-two.article:
**It Takes Two** is a cooperative action-adventure by Hazelight Studios that cannot be played any other way than with two players — whether on one screen or online via a free access code for the second player. The story follows a divorcing couple, Cody and May, who are magically transformed by their daughter's spell into living dolls and must journey together through a fantastically overgrown world of their family home, garden, and workshop in order to return to their own bodies. A key feature of the game is its constant shift in mechanics — nearly every chapter introduces a new tool, whether magnets, jump springs, time control, or transforming into a squirrel, so the gameplay never settles on a single idea and keeps surprising the player.

On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from fast loading and a smooth frame rate, which makes the action sequences and boss fights feel brisk and clear. The DualSense controller adds haptic feedback that enhances the feel of the varied tools and environments. Visually, it is a colorful, stylized world full of detail, where each location functions as a self-contained chapter with its own rules, puzzles, and combat sequences, placing emphasis on communication and cooperation between the two players. The whole story is further accompanied by commentary from an ever-present narrator character, a book about love, adding a layer of ironic humor to an otherwise action-focused game.

Upon release, the game received exceptionally positive reception and became one of the most acclaimed titles of its generation, winning several Game of the Year awards. It showed that cooperative games can be just as ambitious and inventive as major single-player productions, and it significantly influenced the direction of both couch co-op and online cooperative genres. To this day it is considered a must-play experience for anyone playing with a partner or friend, and many later cooperative games openly take inspiration from its design.

**Why play:** For anyone playing with a partner or friend, this is a must-play experience and one of the most acclaimed cooperative titles of its generation, still inspiring other games today.

ps5__split-fiction.teaser: Another purely cooperative game from Hazelight; it alternates sci-fi and fantasy within a single playthrough.
ps5__split-fiction.article:
**Split Fiction** is another purely cooperative title from Hazelight Studios, which after the success of It Takes Two once again bet on a game made exclusively for two players. The story revolves around two writers, sci-fi author Mio and fantasy author Zoe, who become accidentally trapped inside a simulation of their own unfinished stories. The game therefore constantly alternates between two distinct visual and gameplay styles — futuristic sci-fi segments featuring robots and technology blend with fairy-tale fantasy passages full of dragons and magic, giving the designers room to experiment with wildly different mechanics within a single playthrough.

On PlayStation 5, the game shines with smooth transitions between the individual genre segments and grand action sequences that would be difficult to keep stable on older hardware. Like the studio's previous title, it emphasizes giving both players an active and distinct role, with mechanics changing in practically every chapter — from chases and platforming passages to unconventional puzzles requiring the two characters to work together. DualSense haptic feedback and fast loading further enhance the sense of rapid transitions between worlds and allow for smooth handling even of the most visually demanding combat arenas. The sound design and character voice acting also help distinguish the two genre threads and keep players engaged in the pace even during sudden shifts in style.

The game lived up to the high expectations set by the studio's previous title and was received as further proof that Hazelight ranks among the best in designing cooperative experiences. Combining two genres in one package, along with a constant stream of new ideas, makes it a title worth trying for anyone looking for a quality game to share with a partner, and it cements the studio's position as a leader in its field. The creators once again proved that limiting gameplay to two players can be a strength rather than a handicap, provided there are enough ideas to sustain the entire playtime.

**Why play:** Anyone looking for a quality game to share with a partner will find further proof here that Hazelight ranks among the best in designing cooperative experiences.

ps5__sackboy-big-adventure.teaser: A charming 3D platformer starring Sackboy, with no user-generated content — just pure jumping.
ps5__sackboy-big-adventure.article:
**Sackboy: A Big Adventure** is a 3D platformer by studio Sumo Digital that brings the beloved character from the LittleBigPlanet series into a full-fledged jumping adventure without an emphasis on creating your own content. Sackboy sets out to save his friends and home island from the villain Vex, who has kidnapped the inhabitants of Craftworld using a giant machine. The player makes their way through dozens of vibrant levels split into themed worlds, from snowy plains to underwater scenery, collecting bubbles and cosmetic items to customize their character. Besides linear jumping levels, the game also offers special musical passages where the character's movement is synced to the rhythm of the track, plus bonus challenges focused on the fastest possible run-through or maximum bubble collection.

The game was designed as one of the showcase titles for the launch of PlayStation 5 and fully exploits its technical capabilities — fast loading between levels, adaptive triggers, and DualSense haptic feedback that responds to surfaces and in-game actions. The graphics are colorful, plush, and full of detail, which combined with a smooth frame rate makes every level a visually rich experience. Many passages are also designed for up to four players in local co-op, where teamwork and dividing tasks become a key part of progression. The sound design relies on energetic, cinematically composed music that accompanies nearly every level and helps create the celebratory, festive tone of the whole game.

At launch, the game was praised for the precision of its controls, clever level design, and skillful use of rhythmic musical passages where jumping syncs with the music. Although not a revolutionary breakthrough for the genre, it proved that a traditional 3D platformer can work as dignified fun for the whole family on a new console. It remains a popular choice today for players of all ages looking for an undemanding yet honestly well-crafted platformer, whether in single-player or shared family play.

**Why play:** For families looking for an undemanding yet honestly well-crafted platformer with precise controls and rhythm-synced musical passages, it's a popular choice for players of all ages.

ps5__crash-bandicoot-4-it-s-about-time.teaser: A direct sequel to the '90s trilogy; new masks alter gravity and mass.
ps5__crash-bandicoot-4-it-s-about-time.article:
**Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time** is a direct sequel to the classic trilogy from the 1990s, picking up the story after the events of the third game and ignoring the spin-offs released in between. The game was developed by studio Toys for Bob, and on PlayStation 5 it arrived as an enhanced version with a subtitle, bringing improved graphics, a higher frame rate, and additional new content compared to the original release from the previous console generation. The gameplay stays true to the series' legacy — linear running and jumping through levels full of traps, crates, and wumpa fruit to collect, complemented by new mask abilities that alter gravity, mass, or phase state. The game also offers alternate playable characters with their own movesets, allowing selected levels to be experienced from a different perspective and unlocking further collectible content.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs at high resolution with a smooth frame rate, which is essential for the notoriously demanding platforming built on pixel-perfect timing. The level design is intricate and often mercilessly difficult, with elaborately hidden paths and alternate routes through levels for completionists. Visually, the game combines colorful stylization with detailed environments and fluid animation, while the sound design carries forward the iconic atmosphere of the previous entries, including the characteristic sound effects of collecting fruit and smashing crates.

At launch, the game was especially praised by players who grew up on the original trilogy, for its faithfulness to the legacy and its honest, if demanding, challenge. Critics occasionally noted the high difficulty as a barrier for newcomers, while also praising the scope of content and the inventiveness of the new mechanics. Today it stands as a reliable choice for fans of classic 3D platformers who want a pure, nostalgically toned challenge with no compromises in design, and the enhanced PS5 version remains the technically best way to play it.

**Why play:** For fans of classic 3D platformers who want a pure, nostalgically toned challenge with no compromises in design, the enhanced PS5 version remains the technically best way to play it.

ps5__psychonauts-2.teaser: Surreal character minds as game levels; the long-awaited sequel to the 2005 game.
ps5__psychonauts-2.article:
**Psychonauts 2** is the long-awaited sequel to the cult 2005 platformer, developed by Double Fine Productions. The player once again steps into the role of young psychic agent Razputin, who this time finds himself right inside the headquarters of the Psychonauts organization and must uncover a conspiracy threatening the organization itself. Most of the game takes place in surreal levels representing the minds of various characters, each world featuring its own visual style, rules, and puzzles reflecting that character's psyche, ranging from a circus setting to a hellish kitchen. The narrative carries the game beyond these surreal passages too, with elaborate dialogue and characters that give the story emotional weight even between jumps into other characters' minds.

On PlayStation 5, the game stands out with detailed graphics, smooth animation, and fast loading between individual mental worlds, which are often extremely stylized and technically demanding in terms of lighting and effects processing. The platforming sections combine precise jumping with psychic abilities such as telekinesis, pyrokinesis, or gliding, and the game gradually unlocks increasingly complex combinations of these abilities for solving puzzles and fighting. The musical score flexibly reacts to the mood of each world, and together with the striking visual stylization helps every location feel like a self-contained work of art.

Upon release, the game was met with great enthusiasm from critics and players alike, who praised the inventiveness of the individual worlds, the narrative humor, and the emotional depth of certain themes, including its sensitive handling of mental health. It confirmed that a long-in-development sequel can exceed expectations, and cemented Double Fine's reputation as a creator of games with an unmistakable visual and narrative signature. Today it ranks among the finest examples of the story-driven, original 3D platformer genre and is often held up as a model of how to combine playful mechanics with a sensitive topic without losing any fun.

**Why play it:** For fans of inventive 3D platformers with narrative depth and sensitive handling of mental health, this is a peak example of the genre with Double Fine's unmistakable storytelling signature.

ps5__prince-of-persia-lost-crown.teaser: The series returns to acrobatic platforming, this time as a full-blooded metroidvania.
ps5__prince-of-persia-lost-crown.article:
**Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown** marks the series' return to its acrobatic platforming roots, this time in the form of a metroidvania from Ubisoft Montpellier. The player takes on the role of Sargon, a young warrior of the elite Immortals unit, who sets out to rescue the kidnapped prince within the legendary Mount Qaf, a space distorted by time where past and present constantly intertwine. The gameplay is built on precise, acrobatic movement interwoven with a fast combat system, with gradually acquired abilities opening up previously inaccessible areas of the sprawling interconnected map. The combat system combines a sword, bow, and special abilities gained throughout the game, so battles with regular enemies and striking bosses alike keep evolving and demand thoughtful tactics.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs at a high frame rate, which is essential given its emphasis on precisely timed jumps, dodges, and combos. The level design offers a densely interconnected world full of shortcuts, hidden treasures, and demanding challenges, while also offering mapping tools that make orientation easier for players just starting out with the metroidvania genre. Visually, it combines a stylized Persian aesthetic with striking color accents and fluid character animation, while the musical score draws on Middle Eastern motifs to complete the unique atmosphere of Mount Qaf.

Upon release, the game was received exceptionally well and was named by many players and critics as one of the best titles in the genre in recent years, one that holds its own against established metroidvania franchises. It showed that a traditional action series can successfully transition to modern, interconnected level design without losing its own identity, and brought Prince of Persia back into the spotlight as a respected gaming brand that players are eager to follow even after years of silence, now expecting further quality sequels.

**Why play it:** For fans of metroidvanias and returns to classic action series alike, it offers interconnected level design without losing its own identity and ranks among the best titles of the genre in recent years.

ps5__blasphemous-2.teaser: A dark pixel-art metroidvania steeped in Spanish iconography; three weapons to switch between.
ps5__blasphemous-2.article:
**Blasphemous 2** is the sequel to the dark, pixel-art metroidvania inspired by Spanish Catholic iconography and Baroque art, developed by The Game Kitchen. The player once again controls the Penitent One, a silent warrior cursed with an endless cycle of suffering, who awakens back in the world of Cvstodia to face a new threat endangering the very existence of his curse. Compared to the first game, the sequel brings a more flexible combat system built around three distinct weapons that can be switched between on the fly, giving players more approaches to combat and to solving environmental puzzles. The environment is steeped in symbolism of guilt, penance, and physical suffering, while supporting characters and fragmentary dialogue flesh out the grim mythological world of Cvstodia without needing extensive text exposition.

On PlayStation 5, the game stands out with detailed pixel graphics, rich animations, and a dark, religiously charged atmosphere heightened by rich sound design and atmospheric music. The level design offers a densely interconnected world full of shortcuts and hidden areas typical of the metroidvania genre, while ability progression gradually opens up new paths and alternative approaches to boss fights. The demanding combat system requires precise timing of dodges and parries, placing the game among the more challenging entries in the genre. The map is divided into several strikingly different regions, each with its own visual identity and set of enemies, keeping exploration engaging throughout the entire playthrough.

Upon release, the game was well received as a worthy and in many ways improved sequel to the first game, one that retained its unique visual identity and oppressive atmosphere. Thanks to its raw, violent depiction and religious symbolism, it is clearly a title aimed at an older audience. To this day it remains a respected member of the metroidvania genre with a distinctly European, artistic signature that managed to stand out clearly in a crowded genre.

**Why play it:** Because of its raw, violent depiction and religious symbolism, it targets an older audience who will appreciate an improved, distinctly European, and artistically distinctive metroidvania sequel.

ps5__jusant.teaser: Contemplative climbing up a giant tower; each of the character's hands has its own controller button.
ps5__jusant.article:
**Jusant** is a contemplative climbing platformer from studio DON'T NOD, in which the player scales a giant, sky-reaching tower formed from the remnants of a dried-up ocean. The core mechanic is realistic climbing using rope and ice axes, where each of the character's hands corresponds to one controller button, so the player must alternately secure holds, plan a route, and manage stamina. On the way up, they discover traces of a vanished civilization and a small companion in the form of a mollusk, while the narrative remains almost wordless, with the story unfolding through the environment and found fragments of memories. During the ascent, the player also has to manage a limited water supply, replenished from springs and reservoirs, which brings a gentle element of planning and resource management into the game's otherwise calm pace.

On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from detailed rock formation graphics, dynamic lighting, and above all from the DualSense controller's haptic feedback, which faithfully simulates the tension of the rope and the strain of climbing. The audio side is understated and meditative, with gentle music and wind sounds that heighten the feeling of solitude and calm on the way up. The puzzle sections are more spatial than logical — the player must judge the direction of progress and make use of the environment, such as water currents that ease climbing. The visual style combines realistically rendered rock formations with the remnants of a vanished civilization's architecture, which, together with the gradual reveal of the tower's height, gives the game a strong sense of progress and discovery.

The game was praised for its original gameplay mechanic, calming atmosphere, and thoughtful environmental storytelling without the need for explicit dialogue. Although it is a shorter, more intimate experience than most platformers, it showed that climbing can work as a full-fledged foundation for an entire game. To this day it is valued as an example of how an unassuming indie title can offer a unique and memorable gaming experience without needing to rely on action or violence.

**Why play it:** For players seeking a calmer, more intimate experience without violence, it offers an original climbing mechanic and thoughtful environmental storytelling, even though it is a shorter adventure.

ps5__sonic-frontiers.teaser: Sonic in an open world for the first time; classic speed sections remain hidden within temples.
ps5__sonic-frontiers.article:
**Sonic Frontiers** marks a significant departure for the series from traditional linear levels toward an open world, developed by the internal Sonic Team studio. Sonic the Hedgehog finds himself on the mysterious Starfall Islands, where he must explore vast open areas, collect keys to unlock ancient temples, and face mysterious mechanical adversaries while uncovering the fate of his lost friends. The open world is divided into several islands, each with its own visual identity and increasing difficulty, with progress between them conditioned on unlocking the abilities and keys needed for the gates to each temple. The open world is interspersed with classic high-speed platforming sections hidden within temples that recall traditional Sonic tracks full of loops and speed ramps.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs smoothly even at high speeds, which is essential for a series built on instant, momentum-driven movement — frame rate drops would undermine the very core of the gameplay. The open world is visually contrasting, featuring sprawling meadows alongside futuristic mechanical structures, and offers a combination of exploration, light puzzles, and a combat system significantly expanded compared to previous entries in the series with combinations of dodges and special attacks. The musical score combines the series' classic orchestral motifs with more modern electronic tracks that dynamically respond to the intensity of battles against massive mechanical bosses.

The game provoked mixed but predominantly positive reactions — many players praised the courage to try a new direction and the quality of the speed sections, while part of the open world was seen as less polished. Nevertheless, it became one of the highest-rated entries in the series in a long time and hinted at a possible direction future installments could take. Today it is regarded as an important experiment that helped the series find a new voice after years of uncertainty and set a direction for future sequels.

**Why play it:** For Sonic fans looking for a bold, not entirely perfect experiment with an open world and phenomenal speed sections that hint at where the series could head next.

ps5__overcooked-all-you-can-eat.teaser: A compilation edition of the frantic kitchen co-op; kitchens catch fire and ride on islands all by themselves.
ps5__overcooked-all-you-can-eat.article:
**Overcooked! All You Can Eat** is a compilation edition of the popular cooperative cooking series, prepared for PlayStation 5 by studios Ghost Town Games and Team17. The package combines the content of both the first and second games, including all expansions, into a single enhanced version with support for higher resolution and a smoother frame rate. Players together run a chaotic kitchen — chopping ingredients, cooking dishes, and serving them to customers, while the kitchens themselves keep changing, riding on moving platforms, catching fire, or splitting into moving islands. The pace of the game accelerates with every level and adds new obstacles, so even experienced teams of players must constantly adapt their division of roles and communication under the pressure of a ticking clock.

On PlayStation 5, the game supports cooperative play for up to four players, both locally and online, while fast loading allows for smooth transitions between levels without unnecessary waiting. The visual style is colorful, cartoonish, and readable even in hectic moments, when the screen is bursting with motion and time pressure. The emphasis on communication, division of roles, and quick decision-making turns every level into a small test of teamwork between players, which is the main draw of the entire series. Cheerful music and exaggeratedly comical chef animations lend even the most stressful moments a lighthearted, jokey edge.

The compilation was received as a convenient and complete way to enjoy both games along with all their additional content in one place, confirming the series' lasting popularity among players looking for fun yet demanding cooperative challenges. Thanks to its simple rules and immediate clarity, it remains an ideal choice for family or party play, where chaos and laughter become a central part of the experience, whether played by a well-coordinated group or complete newcomers who grasp the rules within the first minute of playing.

**Why play it:** For families and groups of friends looking for chaotic cooperative fun that's clear within the first minute — the compilation offers both games and all expansions in one place.

ps5__lego-star-wars-skywalker-saga.teaser: All nine Star Wars episodes in one LEGO package, with an open galaxy to explore.
ps5__lego-star-wars-skywalker-saga.article:
**LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga** is a sprawling family action-adventure from Traveller's Tales, which for the first time retold all nine episodes of the Star Wars saga in one package using the series' characteristic LEGO humor. Players work through key scenes from all three trilogies, solving simple environmental puzzles, building from bricks, and fighting enemies using dozens of different characters and their unique abilities, from Jedi Force powers to droids' technical skills. The game also offers a sprawling open galaxy with dozens of planets to freely explore outside the main story missions. Players can freely switch between the nine episodes in any order, collecting characters, bricks, and ship upgrades, gradually unlocking further content for repeated playthroughs of favorite scenes.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs smoothly even in sprawling open areas, with fast loading enabling near-instant travel between planets. Visually, it is one of the most detailed LEGO games released to date, featuring elaborate effects, dynamic lighting, and faithful recreations of iconic scenes and locations from every entry in the saga. Local two-player cooperation remains a key feature of the series, enabling shared story playthroughs as well as free exploration modes. John Williams' famous film scores accompany practically every scene and, together with the series' characteristic wordless humor, form the core of the game's overall atmosphere.

Upon release, the game was received very positively, with critics particularly praising the scope of the content, the quality of the humor, and the technical execution of the open world, which represented a significant step forward compared to previous LEGO titles. It became one of the most successful games built on the Star Wars brand and within the entire LEGO video game lineup. To this day it is considered a showcase example of how to combine fan service with accessible, family-friendly gameplay for players of all ages, regardless of whether they know the saga in detail or simply take the game as a fun opportunity to play together.

**Why play it:** For Star Wars fans and families alike looking for accessible fun full of humor and content from the entire saga, set in a sprawling, technically accomplished open world.

ps5__party-animals.teaser: A physics-driven, clumsy animal brawler; characters fall over and stumble on their own, and it's hilarious.
ps5__party-animals.article:
**Party Animals** is a chaotic physics-based multiplayer brawler in which adorable animals clash in grotesque battles across a variety of arenas, from kitchens to pirate ships. Developed by studio Recreate Games with an emphasis on utterly unpredictable, physics-driven character animation, the characters fall over, tumble, and flail their weapons clumsily in a way that draws laughs on its own, regardless of the player's skill level. Besides combat modes, the game also offers minigames focused on cooperation, animal soccer, and capture-the-flag variants. Matches take place in short, intense rounds where players can grab weapons from the surroundings, throw objects at each other, and knock one another off platforms, so the outcome is often decided more by chance and improvisation than by precise skill.

On PlayStation 5, the game supports local and online cooperation and competition for several players at once, with simple colorful graphics and stylized animal character designs ensuring instant readability even amid hectic brawls. The controls are deliberately simple and accessible, but it's precisely the unpredictability of the physics engine that makes it an entertaining challenge even for more experienced players who are looking for fun rather than precise control. The adorable design of the animal characters combined with clumsy movement creates comical situations in nearly every match, setting the game apart from more seriously toned fighting games.

Thanks to its accessibility, adorable visuals, and chaotic fun, the game quickly gained popularity as an ideal title for playing with friends or family, whether in short sessions or longer evening marathons. Like other physics-based party games, it thrives on unpredictability, where even a seemingly lost situation can unexpectedly turn into a win. Today it ranks among the popular choices for casual, laughter-filled multiplayer sessions that require no experience with fighting games whatsoever.

**Why play it:** For casual multiplayer evenings where all you need is the will to laugh — physics-driven chaos and unpredictability make every match fun regardless of players' skill level.

ps5__death-s-door.teaser: A tiny crow works as a clerk of Death collecting souls; a melancholic palette with a horror-tinged edge.
ps5__death-s-door.article:
**Death's Door** casts the player as a small crow working as a reaper of souls for a bureaucratic office of Death, where humans and mythical beings alike must be processed after passing on just like at any other office — with queues and paperwork. When the soul the crow was sent to collect gets stolen, it sets out across strange kingdoms to reclaim it, uncovering along the way a dark story about immortality, power, and the cycle of life and death. Visually, the game combines a muted, almost melancholic palette with bold character stylization, giving it a distinctive, faintly horror-tinged, almost fairy-tale feel.

In terms of gameplay, it's an isometric action-adventure inspired by classics like Zelda and by soulslike games — combat demands precise dodge timing and combines melee attacks with spells such as fire or ice projectiles, while the world is full of environmental puzzles and hidden shortcuts linking the individual areas into one compact whole. Gradually acquiring new abilities and weapons opens up previously inaccessible places, encouraging the player to return to already explored locations in search of optional secrets. Boss fights, among which the eccentric Lord of Doors stands out, rank among the most highly praised elements of the game thanks to their readable attack patterns and a balanced yet genuinely challenging difficulty.

On PS5, Death's Door boasts a crisp image and stable performance that underline its carefully crafted atmosphere, accompanied by understated yet very effective music. The game from the small studio Acid Nerve, published under the Devolver Digital banner, was received upon release as one of the most delightful surprises of that year and is still held up today as an example of how limited resources can produce a game with perfectly balanced design, humor, and emotion, without the player ever feeling like the playtime is being artificially padded with unnecessary content.

**Why play it:** Anyone who appreciates a compact adventure free of unnecessary padding will find in Death's Door a perfectly balanced design, atmosphere, and humor from the small studio Acid Nerve.

ps5__solar-ash.teaser: From the makers of Hyper Light Drifter, this time in 3D; riding a gravitational vortex instead of pixel art.
ps5__solar-ash.article:
**Solar Ash** is an action-adventure from Heart Machine, the studio behind the acclaimed Hyper Light Drifter, this time moving from pixel art into vast three-dimensional worlds. The player takes on the role of Rei, a Voidrunner who ventures into a giant gravitational vortex called the Void to save her planet, which has been swallowed by this cosmic anomaly. Along the way she discovers the remnants of vanished civilizations, meets strange characters trapped between realities, and battles massive, geometric beings called Remnants.

At the core of the gameplay is fluid movement — the character glides on invisible skates across curved surfaces, performing trick jumps, dashes, and grinds, creating a sense of speed more reminiscent of a racing game or skateboarding than a classic platformer. Fights against giant bosses work on the principle of climbing across their body while in motion and destroying specific weak points, similar to Shadow of the Colossus, only in a much faster and more acrobatic form, where failing a jump means falling back to the start. Between combat sequences, the player explores floating islands, collects memories, and solves simple spatial puzzles that function more as a calmer breather between the more acrobatic and combat-heavy passages.

Visually, the game combines vivid neon colors with a dark, cosmic backdrop, and on PS5 it runs smoothly even in large open spaces, heightening the sense of fast movement and long glides. The electronic, atmospheric soundtrack beautifully underscores the game's meditative yet urgent mood. Solar Ash was received as an impressive, stylistically distinctive title that showed Heart Machine could carry its signature visual language into a larger, more open, and mechanically different game world, without sacrificing the feeling of agility and weightlessness that earned Hyper Light Drifter its reputation.

**Why play it:** For fans of fast, fluid movement and bold visual stylization who want to see how the makers of Hyper Light Drifter translated their signature language into a bigger, more open world.

ps5__tunic.teaser: A fox knight with no guidance; the only key to the game is a manual written in an invented language.
ps5__tunic.article:
**TUNIC** casts the player as a small fox in armor who wakes up on an unfamiliar shore with no memories and no guidance — except for scraps of pages from an instruction manual written in an invented language, which the player gradually finds scattered across the world. This idea is the heart of the whole game: the manual isn't just a cosmetic extra but a genuine key to understanding the combat system, the map, items, and hidden mechanics that the game otherwise never explains, and without its pages the player is left quite literally groping in the dark.

The game is visually inspired by classic isometric Zelda titles, but beneath its charming surface hides surprisingly demanding, thoughtful combat and layered puzzles that often require combining information from different parts of the manual and different corners of the world, without the game ever explicitly pointing the way. Discovering hidden paths, secret rooms, codes, and alternate endings ranks among the most praised elements of the game, as it rewards patient, observant players far more than is typical for the genre. The level design is full of shortcuts and portals that gradually connect into one surprisingly compact and well-thought-out whole, one that can be traversed in many different directions and rediscovered even after completion thanks to new information found in the manual.

On PlayStation 5, where the game arrived roughly a year after its debut on other platforms, TUNIC runs without a hitch, and its gentle, watercolor-like graphics and melancholic music truly shine on a big screen. The game was received with great enthusiasm upon release, with many players and journalists calling it one of the smartest adventure designs of recent times, one that elegantly blends nostalgia for old games with a modern, player-respecting approach to storytelling and discovery, where each player ultimately builds their own uniquely incomplete understanding of the world based on what they found themselves.

**Why play it:** For players who want to piece together their own understanding of the world without being led by the hand — TUNIC ranks among the smartest adventure designs of recent times and runs flawlessly on PS5.

ps5__cuphead.teaser: A run-and-gun with hand-drawn 1930s-style animation and jazz recorded by a live orchestra.
ps5__cuphead.article:
**Cuphead** is a run-and-gun platformer renowned above all for its unique visual style, which faithfully imitates the hand-drawn, rubber-hose animation of American cartoons from the 1930s, complete with period film-reel imperfections and a jazz score recorded by a live orchestra. Playing as Cuphead or his brother Mugman, the player tries to pay off a gambling debt to the devil by defeating a gallery of bizarre bosses scattered across a storybook island map, where giant frogs, carrots, and rowdy circus characters await.

The core of the game consists almost entirely of boss fights, each with several distinct phases and unique attack patterns that the player must learn through observation and repetition before being able to survive them without losing all three lives. Shooting in every direction, dodging, the parry mechanic on pink objects, and a quick dash all demand precision and flawless timing, and the game is deliberately designed to be very demanding, which has made it a favorite title among fans of old-school arcade difficulty. Besides the boss fights, the game also includes several classic platforming levels with their own enemies and jumps between platforms, as well as a two-player co-op mode in which both players face the same boss and must coordinate their attacks and movement.

On PlayStation 5, where the game arrived several years after its original release on other platforms, Cuphead runs perfectly smoothly, and its hand-painted graphics look just as stunning as they did at its 2017 debut. The game had already been praised as a technical and artistic gem from the moment it came out, and its later arrival on PlayStation let a new generation of players experience a title that has since become an icon of independent game development and even inspired a full animated Netflix series that brought its art style to an even wider audience beyond gamers.

**Why play it:** For nostalgics and newcomers alike who want to experience hand-painted graphics and an uncompromising difficulty in a title that has since become an icon of independent development and the basis for a Netflix series.

ps5__rollerdrome.teaser: Retro eighties, skates, and shooting as a bloody television sport in an enclosed arena.
ps5__rollerdrome.article:
**Rollerdrome** places the player in a stylized retro-futuristic version of the 1980s, where a bloody but publicly beloved sport combines roller skating with shooting armed opponents inside an enclosed arena. Player character Kara Hassan takes part in a tournament run by a powerful corporation and, through conversations and memories, gradually uncovers the darker side of the entertainment industry that sustains her — one that turns violence into a mass-watched spectacle for crowds hungry for an ever bloodier show.

The gameplay hinges on a tight link between movement and shooting — all ammunition and health are replenished only through tricks performed on ramps, grinds, and jumps, forcing the player to stay constantly in motion and combine acrobatics with combat, as if a skateboarding sim had been merged with a third-person arena shooter. This system creates a distinctive, almost dance-like rhythm, where chaining tricks and precise hits fluidly together brings a satisfying sense of flow, and the player is rewarded for taking risks rather than playing it safe. Each arena has a different layout of ramps, railings, and platforms that rewards creative use of the terrain, and as the levels progress, new enemy types appear that demand a different approach.

Visually, the game relies on clean cel-shaded colors and a poster-like aesthetic reminiscent of period sci-fi illustrations and comic book covers, which on PS5 stands out thanks to a crisp image and stable frame rate necessary for precise control during fast movement. Rollerdrome, from studio Roll7, known for the OlliOlli series, was praised on release above all for its original combination of two seemingly unrelated genres and for a visual style that immediately carved out its own identity among the indie games of its time, even though commercially it was a much smaller title than the studio's later work.

**Why play it:** For fans of original genre combinations and a bold cel-shaded style — Rollerdrome fuses skating and shooting in a way that earned studio Roll7 its own distinct identity.

ps5__planet-of-lana.teaser: A fragile story of a girl and her feline companion against robots; a hand-painted world.
ps5__planet-of-lana.article:
**Planet of Lana** tells a fairy-tale-like yet emotionally urgent story of a girl named Lana who, together with a small feline companion named Mui, sets out to save her sister and her village from an invasion of robotic alien forces. The game unfolds in a picturesque, hand-painted world inspired by Asian nature and architecture, and from its very first minutes emphasizes the fragile but firm bond between the two main characters, who must learn to trust each other just to survive their first encounter with the machines.

Mechanically, it's a 2.5D puzzle platformer in which the player directly controls Lana, while Mui reacts to simple commands and helps solve puzzles — for instance by distracting patrolling robots, opening up paths, or helping with acrobatic passages across chasms and precarious ledges above the void. The puzzles largely rely on timing, stealth passages around the machines, and cooperation between the two characters, while the game deliberately avoids violence, building instead on the tension of silent pursuit and escape from an overwhelming force. Gradually, other animal companions join Lana and Mui's bond, bringing new mechanical possibilities and expanding the range of solvable puzzles as the pair ventures deeper into machine-controlled territory.

On PlayStation 5, where the game arrived roughly a year after its debut on other platforms, the finely rendered scenery and the fluid, hand-animated movement of the main characters, reminiscent of film animation, truly stand out. The accompanying orchestral score heightens the emotional tone of the whole narrative. Planet of Lana was received as a visually stunning and emotionally affecting title that showed the small studio Wishfully could deliver a cinematic experience comparable to much bigger productions in the genre — and do so without a single spoken line of dialogue in the entire game.

**Why play it:** For lovers of cinematically told stories without a single spoken word, where hand-drawn animation and an orchestral score can strike just as powerfully as much bigger productions.

ps5__tchia.teaser: An open world inspired by New Caledonia; the Soul-Jump ability links her to the soul of nature.
ps5__tchia.article:
**Tchia** is an open-world adventure inspired by the nature, culture, and rich folklore of New Caledonia, the very homeland of the development team at studio Awaceb. The player takes on the role of the girl Tchia, who, after her father is kidnapped by a local tyrant, sets out across an archipelago full of tropical islands, caves, and villages to rescue him, discovering along the way a magical ability called Soul-Jump, inherited from her deceased mother, which connects her to the spiritual world of nature.

This ability lets Tchia temporarily take control of almost any animal or inanimate object she comes into contact with — she can turn into a bird and fly through the air, into a fish and swim through the depths, or even take control of a piece of cloth, a boulder, or a small boat to solve environmental puzzles. This system gives the player enormous freedom in how they approach exploring a sprawling yet compact world full of small side activities, such as playing the ukulele, cooking local dishes, gathering resources, or taking photographs with a camera. The game also includes stealth passages and lighter combat sequences against hostile factories polluting the pristine islands with soot, and the player can also simply sit down at any time and watch the sunset over the ocean.

On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from open, colorful landscapes and quick travel between islands with no noticeable delays thanks to fast loading. Music drawing on local musical traditions and authentic instruments gives the whole world a very distinctive and unmistakable atmosphere. Tchia was praised upon release above all for its distinctiveness, cultural authenticity, and for how effortlessly it manages to combine open-world exploration with an intimate family story about loss and belonging, which makes the game feel far more personal than most open-world adventures of similar scale.

**Why play it:** For players craving a distinctive, culturally authentic open-world adventure that links exploration of colorful islands with an intimate story about loss and belonging.

ps5__signalis.teaser: A survival horror in the spirit of Resident Evil and Silent Hill, set in a totalitarian sci-fi future.
ps5__signalis.article:
**Signalis** is a survival horror heavily inspired by classics like Resident Evil and Silent Hill, set in a dark sci-fi future ruled by a totalitarian regime that evokes a combination of East German aesthetics and 1980s Japanese pop culture. The player takes on the role of Elster, a technical android known as a Replika, who wakes up on a crashed space station and searches for her lost companion Ariane, to whom she is bound by a deep and unclear connection that goes beyond the usual relationship between a machine and its crew.

The gameplay preserves the spirit of old-school survival horror — a limited inventory forces the player to constantly weigh which items and weapons to carry, ammunition is scarce, and fights against deformed, once-human enemies are deliberately unpleasant and risky rather than fun. The game emphasizes solving puzzles, finding codes for vaults, and piecing together fragmentary information, journals, and records scattered around the station, with the narrative delivered non-linearly and leaving plenty of room for the player's own interpretation. The atmosphere draws on claustrophobic corridors, a recurring motif of distorted, glitching broadcasts, and dreamlike sequences in which reality and Elster's memories gradually blur together.

Visually, the game combines pixel-art environments with finely painted, almost anime-style character portraits, creating on PlayStation 5 an unmistakable contrast between retro stylization and an almost painterly expressiveness. The dark, industrial sound design and oppressive ambient tones heighten the sense of isolation and anxiety. Signalis was received upon release as one of the most striking horror games in recent memory, praised above all for its atmosphere, visual style, and the courage to tell a dark story without simplistic explanations, which quickly earned it a reputation among genre fans as a horror game for those who want to keep piecing together what actually happened long after finishing it.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for a dark horror game with an unmistakable blend of pixel art and painted portraits will also appreciate Signalis for a story that leaves players piecing together explanations long after the credits roll.

ps5__chicory-colorful-tale.teaser: A world stripped of color and a magic paintbrush in a dog's paws; painting as the core game mechanic.
ps5__chicory-colorful-tale.article:
**Chicory: A Colorful Tale** takes place in an entire world that has suddenly lost all its color after its longtime guardian, a legendary painting brush, mysteriously vanished without a trace. Playing as a dog named Pizza, the player finds this magic brush and must use it to restore color to the world, all while uncovering along the way what happened to its previous holder, the beloved artist Chicory, and why she gave up her duty so suddenly and without a word.

The brush works as a universal tool — it paints colors into the surrounding environment, but it's also the core mechanic for solving puzzles, opening paths, and creating temporary platforms, ladders, or reflections needed to progress, much like in classic Zelda-style games. Yet the game doesn't present itself merely as a cute children's fairy tale; it gradually reveals a surprisingly deep reflection on creative anxiety, impostor syndrome, and the pressure artists place on themselves trying to live up to their own past successes, making it a title that resonates with adult players who have creative work experience and the fear that their ideas aren't good enough anymore. An optional multiplayer mode also lets a second player paint together in the open world and complete the townsfolk's side quests.

On PlayStation 5, the game boasts bright, saturated colors that are the central motif of the entire experience, and it responds fluidly to brush strokes in real time thanks to precise analog-stick control. Lighthearted, cheerful music contrasts with the story's more serious themes, underscoring its remarkably sensitive and honest tone. Chicory: A Colorful Tale was received upon release as a fresh and emotionally honest title, praised especially for how elegantly it ties the painting mechanic to the theme of creative confidence, aided by a free-drawing tool that lets players decorate the world entirely their own way.

**Why play it:** For players open to an unconventional painting mechanic, through which Chicory sensitively ties its game system to the theme of creative confidence and offers free drawing to decorate the whole world.

ps5__last-of-us-part-ii-remastered.teaser: A remaster of the morally polarizing revenge story, now with full DualSense support.
ps5__last-of-us-part-ii-remastered.article:
**The Last of Us Part II Remastered** is an enhanced version of the original 2020 game, tailored specifically for PS5 with higher resolution, faster loading, and full DualSense feature support, such as haptic feedback and adaptive triggers that heighten the tension of both combat and quiet stealth among enemies. The game continues the story of Ellie and Joel from the first installment, telling a dark, morally complicated tale of revenge and its consequences, one whose narrative shifts midway through to a different lead character — a choice that provoked strongly polarized reactions among players and critics alike upon the original release.

The remaster also adds entirely new content called No Return, a roguelike mode offering replayable combat encounters with randomized challenges, adjustable conditions, and various playable characters from the game, substantially extending playtime beyond the main campaign alone. It also includes a set of non-playable lost levels accompanied by developer commentary, and the option to play the entire campaign with unlocked audio logs that shed light on the game's development process and the decisions behind its story.

Technically, thanks to the remaster, the title remains one of the most impressive on PS5, long praised for its enemy and ally AI design, its sound work, and the visual detail of its environments. Given its violent and emotionally demanding content, it is unambiguously a game made for adult players, yet at the same time one of the most technically and narratively ambitious titles of the entire PS4 and PS5 generation. An optional accessibility support mode also opens the game up to players who would otherwise struggle with its tougher combat and stealth sections, without diminishing the dramatic power of its story — and even years after release, it remains perhaps the most discussed title when it comes to storytelling in the games medium.

**Why play it:** It's the most technically and narratively ambitious title of the PS4/PS5 generation, made explicitly for adult players — and thanks to its extensive accessibility options, it's manageable even for those who otherwise struggle with tough combat.

ps5__crisis-core-final-fantasy-vii-reuni.teaser: A prequel to Final Fantasy VII about Zack Fair; battles are spiced up by a slot-machine wheel of chance.
ps5__crisis-core-final-fantasy-vii-reuni.article:
**Crisis Core -Final Fantasy VII- Reunion** is a reworked version of the 2007 PSP title that tells the prequel to the legendary Final Fantasy VII from the perspective of Zack Fair, a young and ambitious SOLDIER trooper striving for the same reputation as his idol, Sephiroth. The game combines a real-time action battle system with an element of chance through the Digital Mind Wave mechanic, a constantly spinning slot wheel that unlocks special abilities, spells, and limit breaks as you play, setting it apart in gameplay terms from the rest of the series' more traditional turn-based battles.

For current platforms including PS5, Reunion has been completely reworked graphically — characters, environments, and battles all received a modern visual makeover closer in style to Final Fantasy VII Remake, while the original story, dialogue, and overall structure remain faithful to the PSP source material. Players once again relive Zack's fate, his friendship with Angeal and Sephiroth, and his relationship with Cloud and Aerith, gaining crucial emotional context for the events that follow in the main game and the Remake series.

Reunion's reception upon its 2022 release was largely positive, with particular praise for modernizing the visually dated original and making accessible a story long tied to the PSP handheld and thus out of reach for many players. For Final Fantasy VII fans, it's an important piece of the puzzle that lends emotional weight to events hinted at in the Remake series, and also one of the best-received modernizations of an older Square Enix title. Its short playtime compared to the series' larger entries also makes it a suitable entry point for players who want to dive into the world of Final Fantasy VII before the main game without investing dozens of hours, while the emotionally powerful ending remains to this day one of the most cited moments in the entire Final Fantasy VII saga.

**Why play it:** For Final Fantasy VII fans wanting to understand the emotional backdrop of events from the Remake series, and for newcomers looking for a shorter, accessible entry point into its world without the extra dozens of hours.

ps5__horizon-zero-dawn-remastered.teaser: Aloy hunts machines in a post-apocalypse; a remaster with denser vegetation and DualSense haptics.
ps5__horizon-zero-dawn-remastered.article:
**Horizon Zero Dawn Remastered** brings back to PS5 the story of huntress Aloy, who in a post-apocalyptic world ruled by robotic creatures searches for her own origins and the causes of the fall of an old technological civilization that turned the world into a wilderness full of machines. The remaster builds on the foundation of the original 2017 game and adds upgraded textures, dynamic lighting, more detailed character models, and denser vegetation, faster-loading support thanks to SSD, and DualSense haptic feedback that makes hunting mechanical beasts with bows, spears, and set traps feel more immediate and tactile.

The core gameplay remains unchanged — an open world full of distinct types of machine creatures that must be observed, whose weak points must be analyzed, and which must be tactically overcome through a combination of weapons, elemental attacks, and traps, complemented by exploration of the ruins of an ancient technological civilization and a branching story tree that gradually reveals the full mythology of this world. The remaster also adds select enhancements and technical solutions carried over from the later entry, Horizon Forbidden West.

After its 2024 release, the remaster met with a more mixed reception than the original game did on its debut — some players and reviewers pointed out that it's a fairly costly update to an already visually timeless title whose differences from the PS4 version aren't always dramatic. Still, Horizon Zero Dawn remains one of the standout open-world stories of its generation and a great entry point for players who haven't yet experienced the series in its best-available technical form. An optional photo mode, added difficulty accessibility settings, and full controller support also make the remaster a comfortable choice for rediscovering one of the previous generation's key open-world titles, thanks in part to a more straightforward entry into the game than the 2017 version offered on period hardware.

**Why play it:** Anyone who hasn't yet experienced the series will find a comfortable entry point in the remaster, complete with photo mode and difficulty accessibility — veterans should expect a subtle enhancement rather than a dramatic leap for an already timeless game.

ps5__metal-gear-solid-delta-snake-eater.teaser: A faithful remake of Kojima's classic about Naked Snake; camouflage, CQC, and cooking food in the jungle.
ps5__metal-gear-solid-delta-snake-eater.article:
**Metal Gear Solid Delta: Snake Eater** is a faithful reworking of Hideo Kojima's legendary series' third entry from 2004, telling the story of agent Naked Snake, sent into the Soviet jungle during the Cold War on a mission that gradually turns into a personal betrayal and a fight for survival. The remake preserves the original story, dialogue, and key gameplay mechanics, such as camouflage adapted to the surrounding environment, close-quarters combat (CQC), hunting and preparing food to maintain stamina, or treating sustained injuries, but completely rebuilds the graphics on a modern engine and offers a choice between classic and new camera controls.

On PS5, the game stands out with a richly detailed jungle full of dense vegetation and wildlife, which can also be hunted as a food source, and with technical work that makes full use of the console's power for smooth performance and visual fidelity of the environment. The stealth system remains built around careful observation of the surroundings, patient camouflage, and improvisation with available resources, thanks to which the game, even two decades after the original, still feels like a thoughtful and functional alternative to the series' more action-oriented entries.

The remake launched in 2025 and was received as a respectful and technically accomplished tribute to one of the most acclaimed entries in the Metal Gear Solid series, making the classic title accessible to an entirely new generation of players. Thanks to preserving the original story, music, and atmosphere, and only carefully adjusting the gameplay, it's one of the most notable remakes in recent memory and a reminder of why Snake Eater is still considered one of the series' high points. The choice between the classic and new interface also allows for both a nostalgic reliving of the original and a more comfortable experience for players used to current action games, giving the remake a broad appeal across generations of Metal Gear Solid fans.

**Why play it:** For fans and newcomers alike who want to experience one of the Metal Gear Solid series' high points in a respectful remake — the choice between classic and modern interface offers both nostalgia and a more comfortable approach to the action.

ps5__tomb-raider-i-iii-remastered.teaser: A remaster of the first three Lara Croft games; switch between the old and new visuals on the fly.
ps5__tomb-raider-i-iii-remastered.article:
**Tomb Raider I-III Remastered** brings together the first three entries of the classic series about archaeologist Lara Croft from the nineties — Tomb Raider, Tomb Raider II, and Tomb Raider III — into a single collection with upgraded graphics, modern controls, and a range of period bonus materials. Players can switch on the fly at any time between the original, blockier nineties-era graphics and the reworked textures, models, and lighting, allowing a direct comparison of just how much the remaster has transformed the original look while keeping the exact same level design for each stage.

Gameplay-wise, the collection remains faithful to the original games — an emphasis on precise platforming acrobatics, solving spatial puzzles in vast tombs and temples, and combat against wildlife and human opponents alike, complemented by Lara Croft's signature rigid, grid-locked movement that still defines the survival-adventure genre to this day. On PS5, the remaster benefits from smooth performance and fast loading, eliminating the long pauses between levels that were typical of the original releases on older hardware.

After its 2024 release, the collection received largely positive reviews for its sensitive approach to the source material and the scope of the included period content, including soundtracks, artwork, and other materials straight from the games' development. For players who already know the classic entries, it's a nostalgic reminder of the genre's beginnings; for new audiences, it's an accessible gateway to understanding why Tomb Raider became one of the most influential series in the history of action-adventure games. Making all three classic entries available in a single collection also lets players trace the series' evolution from its origins through the first sequel to the more ambitious, technically demanding third installment in one continuous stretch, without having to hunt down the original, now hard-to-find releases.

**Why play it:** For players wanting to trace the series' evolution from its origins to the third entry in one continuous stretch, with rich period bonus content and no need to hunt down now hard-to-find originals.

ps5__diablo-ii-resurrected.teaser: A remaster of the 2000 action RPG in modern 3D, with the same legendary gameplay.
ps5__diablo-ii-resurrected.article:
**Diablo II: Resurrected** is a remaster of the classic 2000 action RPG that completely rebuilds the graphics into a modern 3D look while preserving the original isometric perspective, game systems, and the careful balance on which the hack-and-slash genre built its still-enduring reputation.
