Players choose from several character classes — from the Barbarian and Sorceress to the Necromancer, Paladin, Amazon, or Druid — and journey through the dark world of Sanctuary across four acts, gathering ever more powerful gear and battling hordes of demons led by the Prime Evil and its lieutenants.

On PS5, the remaster offers smooth performance, support for higher resolutions, and the ability to switch between classic and reworked graphics at any time with a single button press, allowing for direct, instant comparison with the original. The game also includes the original Lord of Destruction expansion, with its fifth act and another pair of playable character classes, so the remaster offers the complete content on which the series built its reputation as one of the most influential titles in the entire genre.

Diablo II: Resurrected was received upon its 2021 release as an accomplished and faithful modernization that consistently respects the original gameplay and merely updates the visuals and control comfort for modern screens. Thanks to regular seasonal content and an active community, the game remains alive on PS5 even years after release and is prized as one of the best-executed remasters in the action RPG genre, one that shows why Diablo II still shapes expectations for the entire genre to this day. Co-op play for several players, an extensive trading system, and endless replayability thanks to randomly generated levels and items also make it a title players keep returning to even after dozens of hours spent in the world of Sanctuary, whether solo or with friends.

**Why play it:** For action RPG fans who'll appreciate a faithful modernization of a classic, with co-op for several players and endless replayability thanks to randomly generated levels and items.

ps5__death-stranding-2-on-beach.teaser: Kojima's distinctive sequel; Sam Bridges this time delivers packages across sun-scorched Mexico.
ps5__death-stranding-2-on-beach.article:
**Death Stranding 2: On the Beach** continues Hideo Kojima's controversial yet strikingly distinctive 2019 debut, carrying Sam Bridges and his delivery mission into sun-scorched Mexico and other parts of the Americas. The gameplay remains faithful to the original concept — the player traverses a vast, inhospitable landscape, plans routes according to terrain and weather, balances cargo on their back, and gradually builds a network of roads, bridges, and postal stations that connects isolated survivors into a single community. Compared to the first game, new tools for moving through demanding terrain have been added, along with a wider range of combat options against both human and supernatural opponents and an improved cooperation system between players, through which one player's structures help everyone else in their own world.

On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from fast data loading and high resolution, which fully showcase its elaborate, often almost melancholic environments, from dusty deserts to rain-lashed coastlines. The visual style combines photorealistic landscapes with the strange, supernatural phenomena typical of the series, such as the invisible beings called BTs or rain that accelerates time, and together with an atmospheric, cinematically composed musical score it creates an experience that feels more like a meditative pilgrimage than a conventional action game. The story further develops themes of isolation, connection, and reconciliation and features an extensive cast of actors along with numerous cinematic sequences.

The sequel was anticipated as one of the key exclusive titles for PlayStation 5 and built on the reputation of the first game as one that splits players between enthusiasts and those who don't get its slow pace. Even with some distance from its release, Death Stranding 2 remains a demonstration of how mainstream, high-budget action games can be approached at a completely different — slower and more introspective — rhythm than is typical for big productions, while still retaining its own unmistakable identity.

**Why play it:** For players open to the unconventional, slow, and introspective pace of a big-budget action game — even in its sequel, Death Stranding 2 keeps its own unmistakable identity.

ps5__ghost-of-yotei.teaser: Spiritual successor to Ghost of Tsushima; this time the protagonist is the warrior Atsu.
ps5__ghost-of-yotei.article:
**Ghost of Yotei** is the spiritual successor to Ghost of Tsushima from the same studio, Sucker Punch Productions, moving the story centuries later to the mountainous region around Mount Yotei on Hokkaido. The protagonist is samurai warrior Atsu, who after the murder of her family sets out on a long journey of revenge against a group of raiders, exploring along the way an open world full of snow-covered plains, dense forests, mountain shrines, and remote villages. The combat system builds on the proven foundation of the previous game but expands the selection of weapons and fighting styles, letting the player adapt their approach to the type of opponent and situation, whether that means a direct face-to-face duel or a silent elimination from the shadows.

On PlayStation 5, the game harnesses the console's power to render a vast, visually stunning landscape with dynamic weather and changing seasons that heighten the atmosphere of a lonely journey across the wilderness. The soundtrack again combines traditional Japanese instruments with cinematic orchestration, and together with the emphasis on composition — where the wind itself points the way to the next objective — supports the studio's intent to evoke the feel of a classic samurai film. The game also offers the popular black-and-white cinematic mode with period-appropriate sound, which further heightens the cinematic impression and nods to inspirations from last century's Japanese cinema.

Ghost of Yotei was one of the most anticipated exclusive titles for PlayStation 5 and built on the success of its predecessor both in the scope of its open world and in the craftsmanship of its environments and story. During their journey, the player encounters side stories of villagers, merchants, and travelers who flesh out the picture of a shattered land, and the side content is designed to complement the main revenge storyline rather than needlessly padding it out with empty tasks. Despite the different setting and an entirely new heroine, the game retains the tone, pacing, and focus on atmosphere that made the first entry one of the most beloved samurai action titles of the entire console generation, and the sequel builds further on that reputation.

**Why play it:** For fans of the previous entry and newcomers alike looking for a sprawling samurai open world, where side stories complement the heroine's revenge without needlessly padding it out with empty tasks.

ps5__lost-judgment.teaser: Detective spin-off of the Yakuza series; this time with the dark theme of high school bullying.
ps5__lost-judgment.article:
**Lost Judgment** is the sequel to the detective spin-off of the Yakuza series from Ryu Ga Gotoku Studio, once again casting the player as former lawyer and now private detective Takayuki Yagami. The player roams the streets of the Tokyo district of Kamurocho as well as the newly added Isezaki Ijincho area in Yokohama, solving cases through tailing suspects, disguises, hacking devices, and classic hand-to-hand combat, and between the main storyline completes dozens of side quests, minigames, and detours that together form a substantial amount of side content. This time the story centers on bullying at a high school and the darker themes connected to it, such as manipulation, peer pressure, and systemic failure, which the game handles with surprising seriousness and sensitivity.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs smoothly at high resolution, which particularly shows in combat that combines two distinct fighting styles selectable depending on the situation and type of opponent. The sound design and musical score continue the series' proven quality, and together with a wealth of side content — from board games through a dance minigame, a school robotics club, to your own detective agency with assistants — they create a world in which you could spend dozens of hours outside the main story alone. The atmosphere skillfully alternates between serious, dramatic passages and the series' typically over-the-top, situational humor.

Lost Judgment was critically well received as one of the studio's most polished works, even though it was later pulled from digital sale on all platforms due to licensing disputes. The investigation segments also offer logical evidence assembly and reconstruction of events, so the game combines elements of a classic detective story with hard-hitting action and an open city. For fans of the series and of the action-adventure genre alike, it remains an example of how a detective story can be woven together with an open city full of side activities, side stories, and unexpectedly powerful emotional moments.

**Why play it:** For fans of detective plots and open-world action alike, it's one of the studio's most polished works, though due to licensing disputes you can no longer buy the title in digital distribution today.

ps5__forspoken.teaser: Action RPG from the creators of Final Fantasy XV; phenomenal magic-powered parkour movement.
ps5__forspoken.article:
**Forspoken** is an action RPG from Luminous Productions, a studio previously associated with the development of Final Fantasy XV, telling the story of New York heroine Frey Holland, transported by a mysterious magical bracelet into the fantasy world of Athia, ravaged by a curse called the Break. The game's main draw is its movement system — the heroine can parkour, glide across terrain, and cover distances using magic woven directly into her running and jumping, which makes traveling through the open world one of the smoothest and fastest experiences of its kind. Combat combines elemental magic of fire, ice, earth, and lightning with dodging, and attack combinations can be freely tailored to your preferred playstyle.

On PlayStation 5, the game makes full use of the fast storage and graphics processing power to render an expansive landscape with virtually no perceptible loading, and offers both a performance mode and a graphics mode with higher resolution. Visually the game feels lavish, with varied biomes ranging from open plains and deserts to corrupted, darkness-stricken areas full of strange growths. The soundtrack underscores the contrast between the world's beauty and its gradual decay, though the heroine's dialogue, full of modern slang, split players between those who found the humor fitting and those who found it jarring and out of place.

Forspoken met with a mixed reception at launch, mainly because of its character writing and dialogue, even though the movement system and the technical execution of the open world were repeatedly praised as among the best on the platform. Later updates and a paid expansion attempted to fine-tune the story's pacing and combat balance, which partly reconciled part of the audience with its initial shortcomings. Today the game is often remembered as an example of a title where the individual components — movement, graphics, combat — each work excellently on their own but never quite fit into a fully convincing, cohesive whole.

**Why play it:** The movement system and technical execution rank among the best on the platform, but due to weaker character writing it's more of a title for players who can tolerate the individual pieces not fitting into a fully cohesive whole.

ps5__suicide-squad-kill-justice-league.teaser: Looter shooter from the creators of the Arkham trilogy; each character has their own movement style.
ps5__suicide-squad-kill-justice-league.article:
**Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League** is a cooperative looter shooter from Rocksteady Studios, known for the previous Batman: Arkham trilogy, casting the player as Harley Quinn, Deadshot, Captain Boomerang, and King Shark, who must stop a brainwashed Justice League threatening to destroy Metropolis. The game combines cover-based shooting with fast, acrobatic movement across the open city — each character has their own, distinctly different way of getting around, from flying to a grappling hook to sliding across buildings — and offers an elaborate loot system with ongoing upgrades to weapons, armor, and special abilities.

On PlayStation 5, the game supports online co-op for up to four players and renders the expansive, vertical city of Metropolis with visible callbacks to the world of the previous Arkham games, including familiar locations and supporting characters. The graphical treatment of both superheroes and villains is detailed, and the music and sound effects match the grandiose, self-aware action tone, though the game places heavy emphasis on live-service elements such as seasonal content, ongoing updates, and repeated loot farming to progress through further story phases.

Suicide Squad: Kill the Justice League drew mixed reactions at launch, because many players and critics had expected Rocksteady Studios to deliver a polished single-player game in the style of the Arkham series rather than a live-service shooter built around repeat play. The plot also disrupts several established Justice League heroes in a way that sparked heated discussions among fans of both the comic source material and the film adaptations, since it touches on the fate of Batman himself. Nevertheless, the characters' humor, voice acting, and individual action mechanics earned praise, and the game remains a striking example of the risk that the live-service format poses even for long-established and respected studios.

**Why play it:** For players who enjoy open-world live-service action with humor and quality voice acting, rather than those expecting Rocksteady Studios to deliver a polished single-player game in the style of the Arkham series.

ps5__atomic-heart.teaser: Action RPG set in an alternate Soviet utopia; rebelling robots, a telekinetic glove.
ps5__atomic-heart.article:
**Atomic Heart** is an action RPG with shooting elements from Mundfish studio, set in an alternate Soviet utopia of the 1950s, where humanity relies on an army of obedient robots for everyday labor and defense thanks to advanced cybernetics and artificial intelligence. Playing as agent P-3, the player moves through a sealed-off research complex and the surrounding open landscape after the robots unexpectedly rebel, fighting the crazed machines with firearms as well as improvised melee weapons, while also solving environmental puzzles using a special glove with telekinetic, electric, and freezing abilities.

On PlayStation 5, the game stands out for its striking art design, which combines Soviet propaganda aesthetics, posters, and architecture with a bizarre, at times almost horror-tinged vision of a bright yet corrupted future. The graphical treatment of both interiors and open exteriors is detailed, and the atmospheric soundtrack, partly built on period Soviet songs rearranged into electronic form, heightens the contrast between optimistic propaganda and the dark reality beneath the surface. The game contains dark humor and raw, violent sequences, which mark it as intended strictly for a mature audience.

Atomic Heart divided players and critics alike at launch — praised especially for its visual style, world, and atmosphere, while the shooting, puzzles, and storytelling received more mixed reception. The studio's very origins and its ties to Russia also sparked discussion, which affected how the game and its marketing were perceived in some countries shortly after release. A mysterious, ironically commenting artificial intelligence that the protagonist communicates with throughout the game also became a narrative draw. The studio further expanded the game with several paid add-ons that deepen the world's mythology and add new areas, and thanks to the controversial context of its creation, the game earned considerable media attention throughout its entire period of support.

**Why play it:** For players drawn in by its striking visual style and an ironically commenting artificial intelligence as a companion, who can handle a more mixed reception of its shooting and storytelling along with the studio's controversial background.

ps5__trek-to-yomi.teaser: Black-and-white samurai adventure in the style of Japanese films; camerawork straight off the cinema screen.
ps5__trek-to-yomi.article:
**Trek to Yomi** is a black-and-white action adventure inspired by classic Japanese samurai films, which studio Flying Wild Hog developed together with Leonard Menchiari as the author of the original concept and visual direction. The player takes on the role of the samurai Hiroki, who after a tragic attack on his home town sets out on a long journey of vengeance that gradually leads him into the supernatural realms of Japanese mythology, among spirits and demons. Combat is built on simple but precise combo attacks and parrying, while the camera holds to fixed, cinematically composed shots that render three-dimensional space almost like a two-dimensional platformer with carefully chosen viewing angles.

On PlayStation 5, the game benefits from sharp black-and-white visuals reminiscent of classic Akira Kurosawa films, complemented by film grain, static shot composition, and dynamic lighting that shifts the mood of individual scenes. The Japanese-language sound design, together with a traditional musical arrangement, heightens the authentic atmosphere of historical Japan, while the game's shorter overall length keeps it in a tight, well-paced format free of unnecessary padding and repetition.

Trek to Yomi was praised above all for its striking visual style, shot composition, and atmosphere, though critics saw the combat system as somewhat less refined and more repetitive than its visual side. The game gradually shifts between the real world and a spiritual plane, where the rules of movement and the appearance of the entire environment change, adding another dimension beyond plain linear combat. The journey is further accompanied by short environmental puzzles and exploration of side paths with chests and upgrades, which vary the gradual trek. As a smaller digital title, it showed that even with a limited budget it's possible to create a game on PlayStation 5 with a distinctly personal aesthetic and strong craftsmanship in both visuals and sound.

**Why play it:** For players drawn to the black-and-white aesthetic of samurai films and careful shot composition rather than combat-system depth — a shorter, aesthetically exceptional experience at a reasonable price.

ps5__aliens-dark-descent.teaser: Real-time tactics set in the Alien universe; command marines against hordes of xenomorphs.
ps5__aliens-dark-descent.article:
**Aliens: Dark Descent** is a real-time tactics game from Tindalos Interactive, set in the universe of the Alien film series, in which the player commands a squad of marines defending against hordes of xenomorphs on a colonized planet after a space station crash. Unlike turn-based tactics games, combat unfolds continuously in real time, with the ability to pause at any moment to issue orders, and the game places strong emphasis on managing unit stress, limited ammunition, soldiers' health, and the constant threat of invisible danger lurking in vents and dark corridors nearby.

On PlayStation 5, the game renders the cramped, industrial environments typical of the series with an emphasis on dynamic lighting, flickering fluorescent lights, and deep shadows that heighten the constant sense of threat. The sound design — from the motion tracker's characteristic beeping to the distant thud of xenomorph footsteps around the corner — is a key part of the tension, and the score draws on the atmosphere of the original films by Ridley Scott and James Cameron. Between individual missions, the player manages the mothership, treats wounded soldiers, and decides on equipment for the next dangerous mission to the surface.

Aliens: Dark Descent was received as one of the better game adaptations of the Alien license in recent years, praised especially for its tense atmosphere and tactical depth of decision-making. The game also pulls no punches and can wipe out an entire squad of soldiers without warning, forcing the player to approach units carefully and accept that not every mission has to end in success. Lost soldiers, moreover, remain permanently dead, and the player must command new recruits with lower experience, which adds weight to decision-making even beyond combat itself. For fans of sci-fi horror and tactics games alike, it offers a combination that stands out sharply from most action adaptations of the license through its emphasis on unit vulnerability and careful planning of each individual mission.

**Why play it:** For fans of sci-fi horror and tactics games who appreciate the tense atmosphere of the Alien license and permanent unit death that forces careful, deliberate command.

ps5__robocop-rogue-city.teaser: FPS based on the RoboCop film saga; the crushing power of the Auto-9 pistol on the streets of Detroit.
ps5__robocop-rogue-city.article:
**RoboCop: Rogue City** is a first-person shooter from Teyon studio that continues the story of the RoboCop film saga, set shortly after the events of the second film in the streets of a corrupt Detroit. Playing as RoboCop, the player moves through the city, handling side tasks tied to upholding the law — from domestic disputes to petty crime — as well as the main investigation into a sprawling criminal organization, combining the massive firepower of his Auto-9 pistol with the slowed, heavy movement befitting the character's robotic nature.

On PlayStation 5, the game faithfully recreates the visual style of the late-1980s films, including the characteristic design of weapons, police uniforms, vehicles, and the overall atmosphere of a decaying metropolis. RoboCop's voice was performed by Peter Weller, the actor who played the character in the original films, which together with a musical theme inspired by the film source material lends the game a strong nostalgic atmosphere for fans of the series. Combat is straightforward but rewards the player for tactically using cover, different ammo types, and the environment against street gangs.

RoboCop: Rogue City surprised many players and critics with the quality of its execution as a smaller but honestly crafted licensed game with an emphasis on atmosphere, humor, and fan service. The player also repeatedly has to decide whether to act by the strict letter of the law or choose a faster, more forceful solution, which at least partly reflects the moral dilemmas that made the original film famous. Gradual ability upgrades and new weapons give the player a sense of growing power without the game losing the straightforward, action-oriented character typical of the entire film series. It showed that even a studio without a large budget can handle a beloved film license with respect and create a game that appeals both to fans of the original films and to players of classic first-person action shooters.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its honest handling of the film's atmosphere, humor, and moral dilemmas, it's a surprisingly solid licensed shooter that will please fans of the original as well as players looking for straightforward action.

ps5__ghostrunner-2.teaser: Fast one-hit-kill cyberpunk platformer; now with a motorcycle for riding sequences.
ps5__ghostrunner-2.article:
**Ghostrunner 2** is the sequel to the fast first-person action platformer from Polish studio One More Level, in which the player, as a cybernetically enhanced katana-wielding warrior, races through the vertical cyberpunk metropolis of Dharma Tower a year after the events of the first game. The gameplay is built on a one-hit-kill principle - a single strike means instant death for both the player and enemies - which demands quick reflexes, precise timing, and a fluid combination of wall running, double jumps, dodges, and brief time slowdowns. New this time is a motorcycle for fast riding sections between the action sequences.

On PlayStation 5, the game runs at a high frame rate, which is absolutely essential for this type of game - fluidity of movement and instant control response determine success in the most demanding sections full of traps and enemies. Visually, the game combines neon cyberpunk environments with dark, industrial interiors, and the electronic soundtrack heightens the constant sense of speed and tension during the action. The game also expands on the story elements, characters, and world established by the first installment.

Ghostrunner 2 was received as a successful expansion of the first game's successful concept, praised for its fluid movement, balanced difficulty, and newly added mechanics like the motorcycle. The game gradually unlocks further abilities and tools, so the pace and complexity of combat situations steadily increase as playtime accumulates, without overwhelming the player right from the start. Individual levels also contain hidden shortcuts and alternative routes that reward repeated playthroughs and experimentation with movement abilities. For fans of fast, reflex-demanding action games, it ranks among the standout representatives of the genre on PlayStation 5, though it remains more of a demanding, niche title than a mainstream affair for the broader gaming public.

**Why play it:** For fans of fast, reflex-demanding action games, it offers fluid movement, a motorcycle, and gradually escalating difficulty - though it's more of a demanding, niche title than a mainstream affair.

ps5__pacific-drive.teaser: Survival in an anomaly-ridden zone; your car is both a tool and a cared-for companion on the road.
ps5__pacific-drive.article:
**Pacific Drive** is a survival and vehicle-maintenance game from Ironwood Studios, in which the player takes charge of an abandoned car stranded in a mysterious, anomaly-ridden region of the US Pacific Northwest known as the Olympic Exclusion Zone. The core of the game is careful vehicle upkeep - repairing bodywork after collisions, replacing worn parts, and gradually installing upgrades in the garage - combined with excursions into the surrounding area, where the player gathers resources and confronts supernatural phenomena such as lightning storms, radiation, or spatial anomalies that reshape the landscape around them.

On PlayStation 5, the game depicts a bleak, misty, rain-soaked landscape of the US Northwest with a strong emphasis on vehicle sound effects - creaking bodywork, crackling electronics, rattling loose parts - which turn the car into an almost independent, living character of the story. The atmosphere combines the claustrophobia of the car's enclosed space with the tension of the open, dangerous surroundings beyond the glass, and the sparse, ambient soundtrack effectively underscores the sense of isolation and solitude. Between expeditions, the player also upgrades their home garage and resource storage.

Pacific Drive was praised by critics for its original combination of the survival genre with vehicle care and for its dense, tight atmosphere, though the repetitiveness of some expeditions was repeatedly cited as a weakness. As the game progresses, the player develops a genuine emotional bond with the car, since its condition often determines whether a dangerous excursion can even make it back safely to the garage. Each expedition also proceeds under the pressure of limited time and unpredictable anomalies, so even a seemingly routine trip for resources can quickly turn into a fight for survival. As a smaller independent game, it showed that an unconventional combination of at-first-glance mismatched mechanics can find a grateful audience on PlayStation 5 even without the extensive marketing of major publishers.

**Why play it:** For fans of unconventional survival games, it offers a dense atmosphere and a genuine emotional bond with the vehicle, though the repetitiveness of some expeditions may dull the tension over time.

ps5__fort-solis.teaser: A short interactive sci-fi drama on Mars; no combat, just tension and cinematic storytelling.
ps5__fort-solis.article:
**Fort Solis** is a short interactive sci-fi adventure from British studio Fallen Leaf Studios, set at a remote mining base on Mars, which the player, as security technician Jack Leary, explores after picking up an urgent distress call from its deserted corridors. The game is built on slowly, deliberately unveiling the story, exploring empty, eerily abandoned spaces, and solving simple interactive sequences, entirely without traditional combat or action elements - the emphasis is on tension, atmosphere, and cinematic storytelling throughout.

On PlayStation 5, the game uses motion-capture technology and detailed character models that make the protagonist and supporting characters feel believable and natural, further reinforced by professional acting performances with quality voice work. The sound design - the creaking of the base's metal structures, the hissing of the ventilation system, the utter silence of the Martian desert beyond the walls - creates a claustrophobic, unsettling atmosphere, heightened by a sparse, ambient musical score throughout the playthrough.

Fort Solis was received as a solidly crafted example of the cinematic adventure genre, praised especially for its character visuals, voice performances, and atmosphere, though some players criticized its slow pace and fairly short overall length. The story gradually reveals what actually happened at the base through found recordings, voice messages, and clues in abandoned rooms, so much of the tension comes from the investigation itself rather than direct encounters with a threat. Dialogue choices and small action sequences, such as quick reaction tests, meanwhile give the player a sense of direct influence over how Jack responds to the information he uncovers. As a smaller digital title, it fits into the tradition of similar narrative games that on PlayStation 5 target players seeking a cinematic experience rather than any action-oriented challenge.

**Why play it:** For fans of cinematic adventures with an emphasis on atmosphere and voice performances who don't mind a slower pace and a fairly short playtime.

ps5__neon-white.teaser: A fast platformer for speedrunners; cards serve as both weapons and movement abilities.
ps5__neon-white.article:
**Neon White** is a fast action platformer with shooter and speedrun elements from studio Angel Matrix, in which the player, as a former assassin named Neon White, finds themselves in heaven with the task of hunting down fleeing demons in order to earn a coveted shot at redemption. Each level is a short, precisely designed run in which the player collects cards that function as both weapons and movement abilities - discarding them enables a double jump, sprint, teleport, or explosion - with the goal of achieving the fastest possible time and earning the highest medal.

On PlayStation 5, the game boasts smooth performance and instant control response, which is absolutely essential for a genre built on millisecond precision and repeated attempts at routes. Visually, it combines a bright, stylized anime character design with minimalist level design, and the energetic electronic soundtrack reinforces the sense of constant forward momentum without stopping. Between levels, the game also offers lighthearted visual-novel segments that develop the characters' relationships and backstories.

Neon White received very positive reviews upon its original release on PC and Switch thanks to its original fusion of platformer, shooter, and speedrun, and its later arrival on PlayStation 5 allowed fans of fast-paced games to try the title on a Sony console as well. What players enjoy most is the chase for the perfect run through each level, where the same short route is repeated dozens of times until all the jumps, card discards, and shortcuts finally line up into a single fluid sequence of movements. The game also gradually unlocks weaker cards with simple effects as well as rarer, more powerful variants as the story progresses, so the movement options keep expanding throughout the playthrough. As a smaller digital title, it belongs among the games that prove innovative gameplay mechanics can emerge even outside large publisher budgets and extensive marketing campaigns.

**Why play it:** For fans of fast platformers and speedrunning, Neon White on PlayStation 5 offers the same addictive chase for the perfect run that players came to love on PC and Switch.

ps5__silent-hill-f.teaser: The first Silent Hill set in 1960s Japan; the script was written by Ryukishi07, creator of Higurashi.
ps5__silent-hill-f.article:
**Silent Hill f** takes Konami's legendary horror franchise outside the American small town that made the series famous for the first time, setting the story in rural Japan in the 1960s. The protagonist is a high school girl whose hometown transforms one foggy night into a dark, flower-overgrown version of itself, filled with disfigured beings. Choosing historical Japan over contemporary America gives the horror a different rhythm - alongside the series' traditional motifs of fog, garbled radio, and psychological dread, it adds period cultural pressures, family relationships, and a visual language drawing on Japanese grotesquerie and the symbolism of flowers as both decay and beauty at once.

Gameplay-wise, this is a classic survival horror with an emphasis on exploration, item collection, and puzzle-solving, but combat takes place exclusively in melee - the protagonist has no firearms on hand, only improvised tools, dodges, and timed blocks. The lack of ammunition is thus replaced by the risk of close-quarters skirmishes and the need to carefully consider when to even engage in a fight at all. The environment is deliberately claustrophobic and visually dense, with fog and overgrown vegetation replacing the cold steel of previous entries, and the atmosphere relies mainly on silence broken by fragments of sound.

The game was developed by studio NeoBards Entertainment, but the script was written by Ryukishi07, author of the visual novel Higurashi no Naku Koro ni, which explains the emphasis on gradually revealed trauma and the protagonist's unreliable narration. Silent Hill f arrives at a time when the franchise, after years of spin-offs and the remake of the second game, is returning to its original games, and it is the first entry in the main series not set in the titular town of Silent Hill itself - a gamble that divides fans between those who appreciate the refresh and those who miss the familiar streets and old fog.

**Why play it:** It will appeal to fans of psychological horror and Japanese grotesquerie who appreciate a new cultural context and a combat system without firearms, rather than those expecting the classic streets of Silent Hill.

xbox-one__tom-clancy-s-division.teaser: A snow-covered, quarantine-ravaged Manhattan as a fully fledged character of the whole story.
xbox-one__tom-clancy-s-division.article:
**Tom Clancy's The Division** brought players into a snow-covered, quarantine-ravaged New York, where an epidemic had, within a few days, broken civilization down into factions of looters, soldiers, and desperate survivors. The player takes on the role of an agent of a secret unit tasked with restoring order and tracking down the source of the outbreak, moving through streets full of snow, looted shops, and abandoned apartments bearing traces of what happened in the city. The game did not depict Manhattan merely as a backdrop but as a fully fledged character of the story, whose streets, subway stations, and underground tunnels carried their own narrative of a society's collapse.

The game combined a third-person cover shooter with looter-shooter and light RPG elements - weapons and gear had levels, stats, and rarity tiers, so the hunt for better loot formed the core of long-term motivation just as it does in full-blooded RPG titles. On Xbox One, the game benefited from a meticulously modeled Manhattan and a quiet, ambient score that heightened the sense of isolation amid a crowd of enemies. Co-op play for up to four players and a risky PvP zone called the Dark Zone added tension, since a player could lose their collected loot in an instant if attacked by other agents - or if they themselves chose to turn allies into adversaries.

After release, the game faced mixed reactions regarding the amount of content available to players who had already completed the story, which Ubisoft gradually addressed through extensive free updates and expansions that transformed the endgame beyond recognition. Even so, The Division showed that the looter-shooter genre could work outside a sci-fi setting, and it paved the way for its sequel as well as an entire wave of similar online shooters set in the real world. It is still remembered today mainly for its atmosphere, weighty gun sound, and visually striking snowbound city, which even years later feels chillingly believable and stands among the best-realized virtual depictions of New York in video games - something also appreciated by players who kept returning to its New York streets simply for the atmosphere alone.

**Why play it:** Its chillingly believable snowbound New York and weighty gunplay make it worth revisiting even today, though the endgame only truly came alive thanks to later updates.

xbox-one__tom-clancy-s-division-2.teaser: The battle for Washington, D.C. after the outbreak; iconic landmarks overgrown by wild nature.
xbox-one__tom-clancy-s-division-2.article:
**Tom Clancy's The Division 2** moved the fight to rebuild civilization from New York to Washington, D.C., where seven months after the outbreak of the epidemic, military militias, bandits, and the last remnants of government are fighting for control of the capital. The player once again embodies an agent of the special unit, moving through iconic locations such as the White House, the Capitol, or the Smithsonian museums, which the game transformed into overgrown, nature-reclaimed ruins breathing with their own oppressive summer heat.

Compared to the first game, this installment offered a more elaborate specialization system with unique back-mounted weapons, more distinctive enemy factions with their own combat tactics and behavior, and a more expansive endgame with seven-player raids that ranked among the most demanding co-op content of the generation. On Xbox One, the game ran smoothly even in hectic firefights against many opponents at once and offered a richly detailed environment where lush summer vegetation mixed with the remains of government buildings and abandoned equipment. The sound design, radio chatter from the surviving factions, and the city's ambient noise rounded out the impression of a metropolis falling apart yet still desperately fighting on.

The Division 2 was received considerably better than its predecessor, especially thanks to content that was ready right from launch and ongoing support through seasonal updates and new areas. The game proved that Ubisoft had learned from the first game's mistakes and cemented the series' position as one of the established looter shooters of the generation. Even years later, it offers a functional and still-active co-op experience for players seeking a more tactical, somewhat slower alternative to faster arena shooters, and thanks to continued support it remains, even after years, among the titles with an active community of players returning for new seasons and content. Moving the action to recognizable Washington landmarks also gave the game a symbolic weight that the first game, set in New York, lacked.

**Why play it:** For players seeking a more tactical, slower co-op alternative to fast arena shooters, it still offers, even years later, an active community and regular new content.

xbox-one__far-cry-4.teaser: Fictional Himalayas ruled by the flamboyant dictator Pagan Min; the series' finest villain.
xbox-one__far-cry-4.article:
**Far Cry 4** took players to the fictional Himalayan country of Kyrat, ruled by the flamboyant and unpredictable dictator Pagan Min. Playing as Ajay Ghale, the player arrives to scatter his mother's ashes, but is quickly drawn into a civil war between the government army and the rebel Golden Path movement, with Pagan Min himself remaining one of the most compellingly written characters in the entire series thanks to his unpredictable, almost affable malice.

The gameplay built on the series' proven open-world formula full of towers to unlock the map, outposts to capture, and wildlife that could intervene in battles just as dangerously as human enemies - tigers, elephants, and other animals introduced unpredictability into every firefight and forced the player to improvise. On Xbox One, the game offered sprawling mountain scenery, caves, Buddhist temples, and villages with vivid coloring, complemented by a varied soundtrack drawing on local folklore alongside electronic elements that heightened the tension of assaulting enemy bases. The new option to ride an elephant or glide with a wingsuit gave movement across Kyrat its own distinctive character, different from the series' previous tropical entries.

Far Cry 4 was praised at release especially for its world and its villain, although critics noted the similarity of its game structure to the previous entry and the repetitive nature of its map activities. Nevertheless, it became one of the most successful Far Cry entries and cemented the formula the series would follow in the years that followed. It is still praised today as a title with one of the best-written main villains in open-world gaming and as a solid, well-polished action experience that still plays well even with today's hindsight, with the dialogue exchanges with Pagan Min remaining among the most quoted moments in the entire Far Cry series. An optional two-player co-op mode and a rich map editor also gave the game a long lifespan even after finishing the main storyline.

**Why play it:** Thanks to one of the best-written villains in open-world gaming and optional two-player co-op, it still plays solidly and well even with the passage of years.

xbox-one__far-cry-5.teaser: A religious cult has taken over Montana; Joseph Seed is one of the series' best villains.
xbox-one__far-cry-5.article:
**Far Cry 5** moved the series to the United States for the first time, specifically to the fictional Hope County, Montana, where the religious cult Eden's Gate, led by the charismatic Joseph Seed, has seized control of the entire county and is preparing its followers for an approaching apocalypse. As an unnamed deputy sheriff, the player must liberate individual areas controlled by Seed's siblings and gradually confront the prophet himself, whose calm, almost fatherly demeanor contrasts with the brutality of his cult.

The game kept the series' traditional open-world formula, this time without towers to unlock the map and with a greater emphasis on allies the player could recruit, including animal companions such as a bear or a cougar. The American countryside on Xbox One offered varied environments from forests and farms to lakes and cave systems, complemented by distinctive country and gospel music that underscored the unsettlingly ordinary facade hiding fanaticism and violence. Two-player co-op allowed the entire campaign to be played together, a first for the series.

Far Cry 5 earned praise for its bold take on religious extremism and for its commercial success within the series, even though the story's ending divided both players and critics with its controversial resolution. Even years later, the game remains notable for how it transplanted the series' proven formula into an American setting and how it handled themes of manipulation and fanaticism, and it ranks among the best-selling Far Cry titles ever, confirming that the brand can work outside the exotic destinations of previous entries. Thanks to its finely detailed depiction of American rural life and the disturbingly convincing cult characters, Hope County kept its reputation as one of the strongest settings the series has ever offered, and even years later it is cited as one of the franchise's bolder entries in terms of how it handles its theme and its willingness to portray a society collapsing from within.

**Why play it:** Its bold take on religious extremism and the convincingly rendered Hope County make it worth your attention, even though the story's ending divided players.

xbox-one__just-cause-3.teaser: A return to the Mediterranean island of Medici; the story is just an excuse for bombastic destruction.
xbox-one__just-cause-3.article:
**Just Cause 3** brought agent Rico Rodriguez back to his native Mediterranean island of Medici, which has fallen under the rule of dictator General Di Ravello. The goal of the game is to liberate the island's individual regions from military control, while the story serves mainly as an excuse for a series of increasingly bombastic acts of destruction and stunts, the foundation the series has always built its reputation on.

The core of the gameplay remained the iconic grappling hook, which let players pull themselves toward any object, tether two things together, or launch themselves high into the air, combined with a parachute and a new wingsuit for smooth flight over the landscape without having to break the pace of play. On Xbox One the game offered a vast island world with distant vistas, explosive effects, and a physics system that turned every military base into a playground for chain reactions of exploding fuel tanks, bridges, and statues reminiscent of the dictator's personality cult. The sunny Mediterranean atmosphere and lighthearted tone were underscored by energetic cinematic music accompanying chases and aerial stunt sequences.

Just Cause 3 was received as an entertaining, if not always technically flawless, game, with reviewers occasionally criticizing frame-rate drops during larger explosions and long loading times. Even so, it became a favorite for its pure destructive humor and the feeling of complete freedom of movement through the air, where a player could fly across half the island without ever touching the ground. It is still remembered today as one of the finest examples of playful, carefree open-world action, where story takes a back seat to the pure joy of chaos and improvised destruction, and even years later it remains a popular pick for players seeking purely relaxing, undemanding fun without unnecessary overthinking. The combination of grappling hook, parachute, and wingsuit also became a reference point that later games with a similar focus on free aerial movement were compared to.

**Why play it:** If you're looking for undemanding, purely destructive fun without unnecessary overthinking, the combination of grappling hook, parachute, and wingsuit offers a genuine feeling of freedom of movement through the air.

xbox-one__vanquish.teaser: A blazing-fast sci-fi third-person shooter; sliding on your knees and slowing down time.
xbox-one__vanquish.article:
**Vanquish** is a fast-paced sci-fi third-person shooter in which the player, as agent Sam Gideon, dons the futuristic ARS suit that allows for lightning-fast knee-sliding movement and temporary time deceleration at moments of greatest danger. The story about a Russian space station threatening the United States with an energy weapon serves mainly as a framework for a string of breathless action sequences taking place both aboard the station and amid the ruins of a devastated New York.

The game, originally released for the previous console generation, arrived on Xbox One as part of a remastered collection that highlighted its emphasis on speed and aggressive, offensive-minded play, rewarding players for constant movement, risky close-quarters engagement with enemies, and precisely timed weapon reloads. The combination of cover-based shooting with acrobatic sliding and massive robotic enemies created a distinctive rhythm, backed by an electronic soundtrack and an over-the-top, grandiose Japanese direction of action scenes full of dramatic slow-motion moments and cinematic camera angles.

Vanquish was praised on its original release mainly by a narrow circle of action-genre fans as mechanically brilliant, if commercially not very successful, and the remastered Xbox One version only confirmed that status to a new audience. Years later it is considered a cult classic from developer PlatinumGames and one of the best-designed action titles of its decade, one that significantly influenced later games built around fluid, almost dance-like movement in combat and rewarding aggressive rather than cautious play. Its short playtime is offset by a high density of ideas per hour of play, so the game still feels like a remarkably concentrated demonstration of what the action genre is capable of. Many reviewers today retrospectively rank it among the best-paced action games of its entire console generation, one well worth discovering even at a great remove.

**Why play it:** For fans of the action genre who appreciate fluid, almost dance-like movement in combat, it's a short but remarkably concentrated demonstration of what the genre is capable of.

xbox-one__bulletstorm-full-clip-edition.teaser: Remaster of a self-aware, over-the-top vulgar shooter with bizarre enemies.
xbox-one__bulletstorm-full-clip-edition.article:
**Bulletstorm: Full Clip Edition** is a remastered version of the first-person shooter in which former mercenary Grayson Hunt, along with his band of castaways, survives on a planet full of mutants after taking revenge on his former commander. Excessively vulgar dialogue and bizarre enemies gave the game a distinctive, self-aware tone that stood out sharply from the more seriously toned shooters of its era and never took itself too seriously.

The key gameplay element was the so-called "skillshot" system — a scoring system for creative kills using an energy whip that could pull enemies toward the player or throw them into traps, combined with a kick and environments full of cacti, chasms, and other lethal objects that turned every arena into a playground for devising ever more bizarre ways to dispatch enemies. On Xbox One, the remaster offered improved graphics, a higher frame rate, and, new to this version, the ability to play as Duke Nukem in one of the game's campaigns, a nod to a crossover with another shooter legend and its trademark humor.

Full Clip Edition received a mixed but generally welcoming reception — praise focused mainly on the return of the game's original inventiveness, while criticism pointed out that at its core it was an older title without major gameplay innovations over the previous-generation version. Even so, the remaster reminded players how refreshing a shooter focused on style of killing rather than mere hit count could be, and it kept the game's legacy alive for a new console generation that might have missed the original. The game thus remains a popular choice for players who just want to relax and dispatch enemies in the most inventive way possible, without an overly serious tone. The skillshot system remains a frequently cited example of how to motivate players toward creativity instead of simply pulling the trigger.

**Why play it:** Thanks to the skillshot system rewarding inventiveness over sheer hit count, it's ideal for relaxed, lighthearted shooting of enemies.

xbox-one__star-wars-battlefront.teaser: A cinematic multiplayer Star Wars battle; take command of Vader or Han Solo for a while.
xbox-one__star-wars-battlefront.article:
**Star Wars Battlefront** revived the multiplayer shooter series set in the classic Star Wars trilogy, this time emphasizing cinematic audiovisual presentation over depth of game systems. On familiar planets like Hoth, Endor, or Tatooine, players clashed in infantry and vehicle battles between the Empire and the Alliance, with the option to temporarily take control of iconic heroes such as Darth Vader or Han Solo at the moments when it mattered most on the battlefield.

The game lacked a traditional single-player campaign and focused purely on online multiplayer across various game modes, from large battles for dozens of players to smaller skirmishes on more enclosed maps. On Xbox One the game featured an exceptionally faithful visual reconstruction of the environments from the Star Wars films, accompanied by John Williams's iconic score and authentic blaster and starship sound effects, which made the game feel like an interactive gateway into the film universe rather than an ordinary military shooter.

Star Wars Battlefront received a mixed reception at launch — the visual and audio presentation was praised almost universally, while criticism pointed to a lack of content and the absence of a campaign, which Electronic Arts partly addressed with a subsequent paid expansion adding new maps and heroes. Despite these reservations, the game's atmosphere earned it a substantial player base and paved the way for a more ambitious, content-richer sequel two years later that tried to learn from the first game's shortcomings. For many players, it's still the first installment they remember most fondly, thanks to the immediate feeling of finally holding a real cinematic battle in their hands. The Battle of Hoth, with its giant AT-ATs striding through the snow, remains to this day one of the most memorable moments in the entire multiplayer series, and it's often the first scene many players picture when the game's name comes up.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its atmosphere and the Battle of Hoth with its giant AT-ATs striding through the snow, it remains the installment many players remember most fondly, despite the missing campaign and thinner content.

xbox-one__star-wars-battlefront-ii.teaser: Expanded the series with an Iden Versio campaign spanning all three film trilogies.
xbox-one__star-wars-battlefront-ii.article:
**Star Wars Battlefront II** expanded the series' scope with a single-player campaign following imperial special-forces commander Iden Versio, and across all three film trilogies it offered battles ranging from the Clone Wars through the classic era to the age of the new trilogy. The multiplayer component remained the main draw, with expansive maps, heroes, and starship space battles running in parallel with the ground combat.

On Xbox One the game excelled in visual quality and variety of settings, whether the forested moon of Kashyyyk, the elegant planet Naboo, or space battles above the mining planet Kessel, all accompanied by cinematic music and convincing weapon and ship sound effects drawn from all three Star Wars eras. In terms of gameplay, the game offered a more elaborate class system and hero units with their own abilities that changed the dynamics of every engagement and forced teams to react to their deployment.

The launch was accompanied by extensive controversy over microtransactions and a pay-to-win progression system affecting in-game stats, which sparked a strong reaction from the player community and regulators in several countries and forced Electronic Arts to hastily overhaul the system before release. Despite its turbulent start, the game gradually transformed, through subsequent free updates and a reworked rewards system, into a respected, content-rich title, and it is now often cited as an example of a game that managed to significantly repair its reputation through long-term support. The campaign and the elaborate space multiplayer are today rated among the best parts of the entire Battlefront series. The gradual addition of content from the new trilogy and the prequel films also expanded the roster of playable characters and locations to a scope no previous entry in the series had offered, turning the game into one of the most comprehensive celebrations of the entire film saga ever produced in video game form.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its elaborate space multiplayer and campaign, today rated among the best in the series, it's worth a second chance despite its turbulent, microtransaction-plagued start.

xbox-one__warframe.teaser: A free-to-play action shooter; biomechanical warframes with perfectly fluid movement.
xbox-one__warframe.article:
**Warframe** is a free-to-play online third-person action shooter in which players, as mysterious warriors called Tenno, don biomechanical exoskeletons called warframes, each offering distinct abilities and a different fighting style. The game combines fast melee combat with gunfights and acrobatic movement along walls and ziplines, making it one of the most fluidly moving shooters on the market even years after release.

On Xbox One, the game gradually built its reputation through regular, extensive updates that added new warframes, weapons, planets, and entire game systems, from open-world areas to players' own spacecraft serving as a mobile base. Visually the game leaned on the contrast between organic and technological shapes belonging to alien factions, backed by atmospheric electronic music, and as a free-to-play title it offered deep content without requiring payment, though with the option to speed up progress through microtransactions for cosmetic items and time savings.

Over its lifetime, Warframe transformed from an unassuming launch into one of the longest-running and most conscientiously supported online titles of its generation, praised for its generosity toward non-paying players and for a constant stream of extensive content without shutting down previous updates. On Xbox One it stood as an example of how a free-to-play model can be implemented without aggressive pressure to spend, and it still maintains an active, devoted community of players returning for new expansions and story chapters. The gradual layering of storylines transformed what began as a straightforward shooter into one of the most extensive and surprisingly ambitious online worlds on the market. The development team also communicated openly with the community, which helped the game build an exceptionally loyal player base even after more than a decade of operation.

**Why play it:** For players looking for a free-to-play model without aggressive spending pressure, it offers generous, consistently well-supported content over the years and an active community.

xbox-one__borderlands-3.teaser: A cartoonish looter shooter; the quartet of Vault Hunters leaves their home planet Pandora behind.
xbox-one__borderlands-3.article:
**Borderlands 3** continued the series of cartoonishly stylized looter shooters set across several planets of the galaxy, where a new quartet of Vault Hunters travels to stop the fanatical Calypso siblings from seizing ancient alien treasures and the power they conceal. The game expanded the game world beyond the home planet of Pandora to several other visually distinct moons and planets, each with its own fauna and factions.

The shooting system, long a celebrated strength of the series, received further refinement with billions of procedurally generated weapons with bizarre properties, new character abilities, and a deeper skill tree allowing for distinctly different playstyles. On Xbox One the game featured striking cel-shaded graphics, energetic electronic-rock music, and the series' trademark sarcastic humor, complemented by four-player co-op letting players progress through the same campaign regardless of differing story progress.

Borderlands 3 was one of the series' most commercially successful entries, and critics praised especially the refined shooting and the sheer volume of content, though some reviews noted that the humor occasionally felt stale or overly forced. Thanks to extensive post-launch support in the form of paid and free expansions, the game continued to grow even after release, cementing Borderlands' position as one of the longest-running and most influential brands in the looter-shooter genre. For many players it became the entry point into the whole series, and it remains a title they return to repeatedly in pursuit of ever-better combinations of weapon and character ability. The quartet of playable characters with distinct playstyles also gives the game notable replay value even for players who have already finished the campaign once, encouraging them to try the same challenges with a completely different approach to combat.

**Why play it:** For looter-shooter fans craving an endless pursuit of the best combination of weapons and character abilities, the four distinct characters and generous post-launch support guarantee dozens of hours of fun.

xbox-one__rage-2.teaser: Post-apocalyptic open-world shooter with superhuman nanite abilities and a quest for revenge.
xbox-one__rage-2.article:
**Rage 2** drops players into a post-apocalyptic wasteland full of mutants, bandit gangs, and bizarre factions, where the protagonist Walker sets out for revenge after her home settlement is destroyed, aided by nanite abilities that grant her superhuman strength, speed, and special ranged attacks that tear enemies apart. The open world combined exploration of a motorized desert with intense firefights in enemy camps scattered across the map.

Behind the shooting stood id Software, which shows in the dense, precise gunplay comparable to their Doom series, while Avalanche Studios contributed the sprawling open world and vehicle systems drawn from their experience with the Just Cause series. On Xbox One the game offered a vividly colored, sun-drenched desert, an aggressive rock-tinged soundtrack, and fluid movement combining jumps, dashes, and devastating superhuman-like abilities that could be chained together into deadly combos.

Rage 2 earned praise above all for the shooting itself, which reviewers ranked among the best in the genre, while criticism was aimed at the open world's sparse content and a weaker story that felt like mere filler between firefights. The game thus remained an example of a title where excellent gameplay mechanics outweighed the structure around them, and it is still sought out today mainly by players who want purely adrenaline-fueled, quality gunplay without needing to engage with a deeper story. The unusual pairing of two different studios shows in the result as a fusion of two distinct yet complementary traditions of action design. The ability called Overdrive, which temporarily turns weapons into more devastating versions of themselves, ranks among the most beloved elements of the whole ability system, and is still cited today as one of the reasons to try the game even years later.

**Why play it:** For players who want purely adrenaline-fueled, superbly tuned shooting without needing to deal with a deeper story, Rage 2 offers fun from the combination of id Software's and Avalanche Studios' styles.

xbox-one__shadow-of-tomb-raider.teaser: The finale of the rebooted Lara Croft trilogy; a darker Lara amid a Mayan apocalypse.
xbox-one__shadow-of-tomb-raider.article:
**Shadow of the Tomb Raider** closed out the rebooted Lara Croft trilogy, this time set in the dense jungles of Central America, where Lara tries to stop the organization Trinity from triggering an ancient Mayan apocalypse that she herself partly and unwittingly set in motion. The story placed greater emphasis on Lara's transformation into a seasoned, but also darker and more conflicted character, who must bear the weight of her own decisions.

The game deepened the elements that made the series famous — climbing rock faces and temples, solving environmental puzzles in vast tombs, and stealthy action in dense terrain, complemented by new options for mud camouflage and underwater exploration of sprawling cave systems. On Xbox One the game excelled with dense jungle vegetation, elaborate underground complexes, and atmospheric music underscoring Mayan mythology and the sanctity of the visited sites, while gunfight sequences receded further into the background in favor of exploration and puzzles.

Shadow of the Tomb Raider was received as a dignified, if not revolutionary, conclusion to the trilogy, with reviewers particularly praising the tombs and atmosphere but noting a slower action pace compared to previous entries. The game thus closed out the series reboot on a positive, if calmer, note and confirmed that an emphasis on exploration and puzzles can work just as well as the pure action the series had foregrounded earlier, offering a more balanced conclusion to the whole story arc. The elaborate tombs rank among the largest and most inventive in the entire rebooted trilogy and alone form a large part of the value the game offers players. An optional higher puzzle difficulty setting further gave more experienced players a chance to face a genuine challenge without relying on hints, meeting the needs of longtime fans of adventure platformers built around logic.

**Why play it:** Thanks to the largest and most inventive tombs of the entire rebooted trilogy and a more balanced emphasis on exploration and puzzles, it's worth finishing Lara Croft's story with a calmer but honest conclusion.

xbox-one__mass-effect-andromeda.teaser: An action RPG in a new galaxy far from Shepard's trilogy; free mixing of abilities without classes.
xbox-one__mass-effect-andromeda.article:
**Mass Effect: Andromeda** took players into an entirely new galaxy, far from the known trilogy about Shepard, and offered a story about colonization as Pathfinder Ryder. The game builds on an action-RPG system with a collection of abilities combining biotics, tech, and combat upgrades, and the player could freely switch between them without being locked into a strict character class — a marked change compared to previous entries. Exploring planets took place largely aboard the wheeled Nomad vehicle, with more open environments offering side quests, resource gathering, and outpost building as part of the main storyline about finding a new home for humanity.

On Xbox One the game ran technically solidly, though the launch was marred by criticism of facial animations and some technical issues, which later patches significantly improved. The music score carried on the series' ambient sci-fi style, and the atmosphere of space exploration worked well, even though the story and characters didn't reach the quality of the original trilogy. Contemporary reception was mixed, with critics praising the combat system and the sheer amount of content but faulting the dialogue writing and technical bugs, which led to the cancellation of planned sequels and a long hiatus for the brand. Today the game is viewed more favorably, as a solid, if imperfect, expansion of the Mass Effect universe with a generous amount of content for genre fans and an open, endlessly explorable universe full of planets.

The package also included a cooperative multiplayer mode called APEX, in which a squad of four players completed missions against waves of enemies while gradually unlocking new characters, weapons, and gear, giving the Xbox One version an unexpectedly long lifespan even after finishing the campaign. The combat system also introduced, for the first time in the series, active dodges and short bursts of flight powered by back-mounted thrusters, making firefights feel snappier and more vertical than in previous entries. Even years later, Andromeda remains an interesting detour for fans of the sci-fi RPG genre who are looking for dozens of hours of content and a welcoming entry point into the Mass Effect universe even without knowledge of the previous trilogy.

**Why play it:** For sci-fi RPG fans looking for dozens of hours of content, snappier combat with dodges and thrusters, and the cooperative APEX mode, Andromeda offers a welcoming entry point into the Mass Effect universe even without knowing the trilogy.

xbox-one__elder-scrolls-v-skyrim-special.teaser: A remastered legendary open-world RPG from Bethesda; mods on console for the first time.
xbox-one__elder-scrolls-v-skyrim-special.article:
**The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Special Edition** brought to Xbox One a completely remastered version of Bethesda's legendary open-world RPG, enriched with improved graphics, new lighting, weather effects, and mod support directly on console. Playing as the Dovahkiin, the last living person able to absorb dragon souls, players set out into the sprawling fantasy world of Skyrim, where they can freely choose between the main storyline about the return of dragons and a vast number of side quests, faction questlines, and exploration of caves, cities, and mountains. The character progression system is based on skill use rather than traditional levels, so the hero develops exactly according to their playstyle, whether that's sword-and-shield combat, spellcasting, or stealthy sneaking.

On Xbox One the game ran at higher resolution and with a better frame rate than the original 2011 release, and mod support from Bethesda.net allowed console players for the first time to experience community-made modifications directly on their console. The atmosphere is completed by the iconic music of Jeremy Soule, whose choral themes and raw Nordic tones became synonymous with the entire series. Contemporary reception was enthusiastic, as Special Edition confirmed the timelessness of the original game and expanded its audience to a new generation of players. Even years later, Skyrim remains one of the most influential RPGs of all time, and its continual re-releases on new platforms only confirm how strongly it shaped the genre of open fantasy worlds.

Freedom of movement is heightened by the fact that almost any mountain can be climbed on foot, every village visited, and nearly every character exchanged a few words with, which at release gave a sense of a truly living world. Faction questlines, whether the Dark Brotherhood, the Companions, or the College of Winterhold, offer their own story arcs that the player can freely switch between depending on mood. On Xbox One, the Special Edition also served as console players' first full-fledged entry into the world of mods, from cosmetic tweaks to sprawling community-made quest packs, turning a single game into a practically endlessly expanding platform.

**Why play it:** Thanks to the freedom to climb practically any mountain and visit every village, interconnected faction questlines, and its role as console players' first full-fledged entry into the world of mods, Special Edition remains a nearly endlessly expanding platform.

xbox-one__diablo-iii-ultimate-evil-editi.teaser: The complete Diablo III with Reaper of Souls; loot hunting for up to four players on the couch.
xbox-one__diablo-iii-ultimate-evil-editi.article:
**Diablo III: Ultimate Evil Edition** brought to Xbox One a complete package of Blizzard Entertainment's action RPG, including both the base game and the Reaper of Souls expansion, tailored specifically for controller play and split-screen co-op for up to four players on a single console. Players choose from several classes such as barbarian, witch doctor, or monk and journey through the dark fantasy world of Sanctuary, hunting demons, collecting ever-better gear, and building up their character through a system of runes and legendary items. At the core of the game is the addictive loop of killing enemies and gathering loot, complemented by Adventure Mode with randomly generated bounties for endless replayability.

Gamepad controls were reworked to naturally replace mouse and keyboard, with auto-targeting and quick access to abilities via a radial menu, which proved to be a surprisingly effective solution. Visually the game drew on a dark, gothic atmosphere combined with colorful spell effects, and the music underscored the tension of dark dungeons and epic boss fights alike. The console version earned praise for how well the controls and co-op translated from PC to gamepad, and for many players it became a favorite way to enjoy a two-player session in front of one TV. Even today, Diablo III on Xbox One is a great choice for quick, satisfying RPG sessions without unnecessary complications and with a huge amount of collectible content.

The seasons system, which Blizzard gradually added to consoles as well, motivates players to repeatedly start over with a new character and compete on leaderboards, giving the game long-term replayability even years after release. Its ties to the classic Diablo trilogy are apparent in enemy design, musical motifs, and the overall grim mythology of angels and demons, so the series won over both new players and veterans of the PC versions from the nineties and 2000s. Thanks to easy access on gamepad and the ability to play a short dungeon run in just half an hour, Diablo III became a popular draw specifically for console audiences who had previously passed on the series for system reasons.

**Why play it:** For players looking for easily accessible action on a gamepad even for just half an hour, Diablo III offers a seasonal system with long-term replayability and an atmosphere that won over both new players and PC veterans.

xbox-one__wasteland-3.teaser: An isometric turn-based RPG in frozen Colorado; dark humor and choices that always cost something.
xbox-one__wasteland-3.article:
**Wasteland 3** is an isometric tactical RPG from inXile Entertainment that takes players to a frozen post-apocalyptic Colorado as members of the Desert Rangers, sent from Arizona to restore an alliance with a local warlord. The game builds on turn-based combat with an emphasis on building a squad of four to six characters, base management, and an extensive dialogue-choice system that genuinely affects the story's development and the fate of the world's factions. A prominent feature is the dark humor and morally ambiguous decisions, where almost every choice comes with some sacrifice or compromise, giving the game a sense of real weight to its consequences.

On Xbox One the game offered full two-player online co-op, quite rare in the isometric RPG genre, allowing the whole campaign to be played together with a friend from start to finish. The visual style combines snowy wastelands with the ruins of an old civilization and industrial complexes, while the music rounds out the grim, but at times also grotesque, atmosphere of Colorado as a whole. Contemporary reception was very positive, with critics praising the depth of its systems, the writing, and the amount of content, placing Wasteland 3 among the best-reviewed turn-based RPGs of its generation. It remains a celebrated return to the traditional CRPG style, offering dozens of hours of thoughtful content and freedom in how to shape the Wasteland according to one's own values.

Base management in the form of an abandoned prison building gradually turned into a functioning Desert Rangers headquarters gives players a sense of building their own stronghold amid a hostile world, similar to previous entries in the Wasteland series. The combat system relies on cover, a wide range of weapon types from pistols to heavy machine guns, and the special abilities of individual squad members, so assembling a balanced team is key to overcoming tougher encounters. The choice between diplomacy and violence also shapes relations with factions such as the Patriarch's family or a religious sect worshipping an element, and the game never lets players forget that even a seemingly good decision can carry an unexpectedly cruel price.

**Why play it:** Anyone who wants to build their own base and assemble a balanced squad around cover and special abilities will appreciate the thoughtful combat system and the morally ambiguous decisions that shape relations with the game's factions.

xbox-one__greedfall.teaser: Colonial fantasy RPG from French studio Spiders; diplomacy, magic, and choices between factions.
xbox-one__greedfall.article:
**GreedFall** from the French studio Spiders places players in the colonial fantasy world of the island of Teer Fradee, where the protagonist travels as a diplomatic envoy amid tensions between European powers, the native inhabitants, and the island's mysterious magic. The game combines real-time action combat with RPG elements such as character progression through skills, crafting equipment, and an extensive dialogue system where the player's choices affect relations between factions as well as the final shape of the story. It also features a group of companions with their own storylines, who accompany the player on expeditions and react to their decisions.

On Xbox One the game lived up to its ambitions despite the limited budget of a smaller studio, which showed in simpler textures and animations, but it nonetheless offered a surprisingly elaborate world with convincingly written factions and their politics. The atmosphere is rounded out by music inspired by baroque and colonial seventeenth-century aesthetics, which together with misty forests and Victorian-styled towns creates a distinctive visual style. Contemporary reviews praised the ambition and inventiveness of the world, though they pointed out technical shortcomings befitting the studio's size. GreedFall thus became a pleasant surprise for fans of Western RPGs looking for an alternative to big-budget titles, and it is still valued today for its fresh colonial fantasy setting and its well-thought-out faction politics.

The island of Teer Fradee is steeped in mysterious magic and nature spirits, with whom both the colonizers and native inhabitants must somehow coexist, and the game uses this supernatural layer as a source of both conflict and resolution, from healing rituals to a mysterious curse afflicting the main character. Players can choose between diplomatic persuasion, bribery, or force, with each faction — whether a trading company, a scientific academy, or native tribes — reacting differently to the player's dealings and opening different paths through the story. This interweaving of politics, exploration, and companions' personal relationships makes GreedFall one of the more honest smaller-scale RPGs of its generation.

**Why play it:** For fans of smaller but honest RPGs, GreedFall offers a blend of politics, exploration of a mysterious island, and companions' personal relationships, where the choice between diplomacy, bribery, and force genuinely changes the story.

xbox-one__vampyr.teaser: An action RPG from Dontnod; a moral dilemma between healing the sick and preying on your own patients.
xbox-one__vampyr.article:
**Vampyr** from Dontnod Entertainment is an action RPG set in a London ravaged by the Spanish flu in 1918, where the player takes on the role of Dr. Jonathan Reid, turned into a vampire against his will. At the heart of the game is a moral dilemma between healing the sick residents and preying on them as a source of blood, where killing a particular character can irreversibly affect the state of an entire district as well as the side quests available. The combat system combines melee weapons with vampiric abilities such as turning into mist or blood attacks, and the character develops precisely according to how much the player chooses to feed on London's inhabitants.

On Xbox One the game suffered from certain technical shortcomings, such as a lower frame rate and longer loading times, which somewhat spoiled the otherwise strong impression of its atmosphere for some players.
