By day the player builds social bonds, studies, and spends time with characters through the so-called Social Links system; by night the party explores the endless Tartarus tower and fights turn-based battles using the Persona system – summoned beings that reflect the characters' inner psyche and their ability to face their own demons. This dual rhythm of everyday life and nighttime combat is a defining trait of the entire Persona series, and Reload delivers it in a noticeably smoother form.

On Xbox Series X/S the game runs in high resolution with stylized graphics, and the modern user interface preserves the series' distinctive visual identity, just in a considerably clearer and smoother form than the original from the PlayStation 2 era. Shoji Meguro's music, rearranged for this remake, ranks among the game's strongest points and, together with the melancholic atmosphere of the Tokyo suburb of Iwatodai, creates a unique feeling both while exploring and during social interactions with classmates. Battles are faster and clearer than in the original while retaining the strategic depth built on exploiting enemies' elemental weaknesses and teamwork.

Reload was received as one of the most accomplished JRPG remakes of recent times, one that made a title now two decades old accessible to a new generation of players without sacrificing its distinctiveness, its darker tone, or its central theme of death and coming to terms with it. For many fans of the series it represents a return to the work that in 2006 set the direction for the entire Persona brand and introduced the format of a social simulator combined with a dungeon crawler. Its release on Xbox Series X/S also marked the first official arrival of a mainline series entry on Microsoft's platforms, making the game accessible to a much wider audience than had previously known the series.

**Why play it:** Anyone who wants to get to know the work that in 2006 set the direction for the entire Persona series will find in Reload a distinctive, dark story about death and coming to terms with it, wrapped in a modern and accessible package.

xbox-series__persona-5-royal.teaser: An expanded version of the acclaimed JRPG about the Phantom Thieves; Royal adds Kasumi and a new dungeon.
xbox-series__persona-5-royal.article:
**Persona 5 Royal** is an expanded version of the acclaimed JRPG about a group of Tokyo students who transform by night into the so-called Phantom Thieves of Hearts and infiltrate the symbolic underworlds of corrupt adults in order to steal their distorted hearts and force them to publicly confess their sins. The game combines a social simulation, in which the player spends time with friends, studies for exams, and develops the skills needed to progress through the story, with tactical turn-based battles in elaborate dungeons built on the Persona system and exploiting enemies' elemental weaknesses. The Royal edition adds a new playable character, Kasumi, an entire new spring semester period, and another extensive dungeon on top of the original 2016 content, extending the playtime by dozens of hours.

The Xbox Series X/S version, released in 2022, brought the game officially to Microsoft's platforms for the first time and offered smooth performance and fast loading, which shows especially during quick transitions between the open city of Tokyo and the individual floors of the dungeons. The game's art style, built on a striking black-and-red palette and stylized animated transitions between menus and battles, ranks among the most distinctive in the entire genre and, together with Shoji Meguro's jazz-inflected music, creates an unmistakable atmosphere of urban rebellion against adult hypocrisy. The daily routine alternates with nighttime forays into dungeons at a pace the player themselves controls, deciding how much risk they are willing to take before the next school day.

Persona 5 Royal is now commonly ranked among the best JRPGs of its generation, and its arrival on Xbox Series X/S and Game Pass significantly broadened the circle of players who encountered the series for the first time. Its elaborate story about rebellion against a corrupt system, memorable characters, and dozens of hours of content make it a title that, even years after release, holds a reputation as one of the pinnacles of the genre. It also serves as a textbook example of what an expanded edition of a game should look like, rather than merely padding out the playtime cosmetically.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its elaborate story about rebellion against a corrupt system, unforgettable characters, and dozens of hours of content, it ranks among the best that the JRPG genre offered this generation.

xbox-series__gears-5.teaser: Cover-based tactical shooting against the Locust and the Swarm, this time from Kait Diaz's perspective.
xbox-series__gears-5.article:
**Gears 5** is a continuation of the long-running series of third-person cover shooters set on the war-ravaged planet Sera, and it arrived on Xbox Series X/S as a technically enhanced version supporting higher resolution and frame rate. The game builds on the tried-and-tested system of cover-based tactical shooting against the alien Locust race and now also the Swarm, this time from the perspective of Kait Diaz, whose personal story and unexpected connection to the enemy race gives the series a new emotional dimension compared to earlier entries focused primarily on Marcus Fenix. The campaign also offers more open sections on a snow vehicle called the Skiff, a fairly new, more relaxed element for an otherwise linearly structured series.

The enhanced version for Xbox Series X/S brought faster loading, a more stable frame rate during action sequences, and support for higher resolution, which highlighted the elaborately detailed environments ranging from snowy plains to industrial complexes and underground laboratories. Besides the campaign, the game offers an extensive cooperative Horde mode for defending against growing waves of enemies and a competitive multiplayer with a range of classes, which together form a substantial part of the overall gameplay and long-term appeal of the title. The audio side, with the heavy sounds of the Lancer chainsaw rifle and orchestral music, remains true to the series' identity.

Gears 5 was praised on release especially for its courage in telling a more personal story and for the technical quality of its execution, while the new-generation console version showed just how significantly extra power can improve an already solid action game. Within the series, Gears 5 is considered one of its most mature entries in terms of storytelling and character work, and it still serves as a demonstration of how strongly Xbox Series X/S can boost older multiplatform titles without the need to completely remake them.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its boldly personal story, strong character work, and the technical quality that the new-generation version further amplifies, it ranks among the most mature entries in the entire Gears series.

xbox-series__halo-master-chief-collectio.teaser: Six entries of the legendary sci-fi series in one package; the entire saga of the Master Chief together.
xbox-series__halo-master-chief-collectio.article:
**Halo: The Master Chief Collection** gathers six mainline entries of the cult sci-fi series about humanity's fight against the alien Covenant alliance, and on Xbox Series X/S it offers an optimized version with higher resolution and a smoother frame rate. The collection includes remastered versions of the first two games, reworked Halo 3 and ODST, Halo 4, and Halo: Reach, so the player can go through the entire chronology of the Master Chief's story and the supporting cast in one package and switch between campaigns without having to buy them separately or hunt down old consoles. The legendary combination of shooting, grenades, and melee combat that made the series famous back on the original Xbox remains the core of the gameplay across all the entries and holds up surprisingly well, though it's noticeable how the pacing and level design gradually shifted between the series' different eras.

The Xbox Series X/S version brought support for higher resolution and higher frame rates, up to 120 frames per second in multiplayer, which made a substantial difference especially in competitive modes where smoothness and responsiveness play a key role. The collection also includes the extensive Halo: Reach campaign telling the story of the fall of the planet Reach, which players who only know the later entries will appreciate as a missing piece of the puzzle. The collection also features extensive online multiplayer across all the entries with crossplay support between consoles and PC, thanks to which the community remains active years after the individual games' original release. The audio side, from Martin O'Donnell's iconic musical theme to the distinctive sounds of weapons like the battle rifle, ranks among the most recognizable in the entire gaming industry.

The Master Chief Collection was initially plagued by technical problems when it launched on PC in 2019, but these were gradually resolved, and the collection became the definitive way to enjoy the Halo series on a single platform. On Xbox Series X/S it offers an ideal entry point for new players as well as a nostalgic ride for veterans, and it still serves as a reminder of how fundamentally the first game in 2001 shaped the genre of console first-person shooters for years to come.

**Why play it:** For new players and nostalgic veterans alike, it's the definitive way to go through the history of the series on a single platform, a series that shaped console first-person shooters.

xbox-series__doom-eternal.teaser: An extremely fast shooter where attacking restores health and ammo; passive cover has no place here.
xbox-series__doom-eternal.article:
**Doom Eternal** is a continuation of the legendary series' 2016 reboot, and on Xbox Series X/S it delivers an extremely fast, aggressive shooter in which constant movement matters just as much as an accurate aim. The game expands on the so-called "push forward combat" system, where the player must actively attack demons using specific weapons and abilities to get ammo, health, or armor from them, meaning the game rejects passive cover and forces the player into constant risky movement through an arena full of enemies. The arsenal of weapons and mobility options, including the grappling hook, double jump, and brutal finishing animations, makes Doom Eternal one of the fastest and most demanding shooters of its entire generation.

On Xbox Series X/S the game runs in high resolution with a high, stable frame rate, which is absolutely essential for a title built on precision and speed of movement. Visually the game combines an industrial, hellish aesthetic with futuristic elements of an Earth base and distant planets, accompanied by Mick Gordon's intense metal score, which reinforces the feeling of the unstoppable power of the main hero, the Doom Slayer. The level design also offers hidden collectibles, secret rooms, and platforming sections that vary the game between individual, extremely intense battles, and the rune system for upgrading weapons and abilities lets the player gradually tailor the game's pace to their own style.

Doom Eternal was praised on release for its courage in pushing action shooters to even greater intensity and speed, though some players needed longer to get used to its more demanding, less forgiving system than the more accessible previous entry. On Xbox Series X/S the game received smooth technical execution that fully exploits the console's potential, and it still ranks among the titles used as an example of what a modern, technically polished first-person action shooter built on speed and aggression should look like.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for a technically polished action shooter built on speed and aggression will get a boldly intense sequel, though its more demanding system does take some getting used to.

xbox-series__remnant-ii.teaser: Souls-like action with guns instead of swords, playable with up to three players in a shared world.
xbox-series__remnant-ii.article:
**Remnant II** is a continuation of the action shooter that combines elements of souls-like design with cooperative play for up to three players, who together make their way through procedurally generated worlds full of dangerous creatures across several distinct dimensions. The player picks a character archetype with its own abilities, and over the course of the game combines firearms, magical abilities, and tactical dodging, while battles against sprawling bosses demand the same patience and pattern reading as classic soulslikes, just from a third-person perspective and with guns instead of swords and shields. The archetype system also allows combining two different playstyles on a single character.

On Xbox Series X/S the game benefits from fast loading during transitions between procedurally generated worlds and offers stable performance even in hectic battles against dozens of enemies at once. Visually the game alternates between completely different environments, from dark gothic locations through flooded swamps to alien, biomechanical landscapes, giving it a surprising genre and aesthetic variety compared to the first game. Procedural generation ensures that each playthrough slightly differs in room layout and boss order, and together with plenty of hidden content and alternative paths it supports repeated playthroughs across multiple characters and builds. Weapons can also be upgraded using mods obtained from bosses, which motivates players to experiment even with less conventional equipment combinations.

Remnant II was praised on release for its difficulty, the depth of its builds, and for working equally well in solo play and full cooperation, which made it one of the most successful smaller action titles of 2023. On Xbox Series X/S the game offers an experience comparable to smooth performance on other platforms, and together with the previous entry, Remnant: From the Ashes, it cements the reputation of Gunfire Games as specialists in demanding cooperative action games with soulslike elements, a reputation that continues to grow.

**Why play it:** Thanks to the depth of its builds and a difficulty that works equally well solo or in full cooperation, Remnant II ranks among the most successful smaller action titles of 2023 with soulslike elements.

xbox-series__dead-space.teaser: A remake of the 2008 survival horror; severing limbs instead of aiming for the head is a certainty.
xbox-series__dead-space.article:
**Dead Space** is a complete remake of the classic 2008 survival horror that brings to Xbox Series X/S the story of engineer Isaac Clarke, trapped on the mining ship USG Ishimura, which has been overrun by mutated corpses called Necromorphs. The game builds on the well-thought-out system of strategic dismemberment, where instead of aiming for the head the player shoots off individual limbs using improvised mining tools, and on the claustrophobic atmosphere of the ship's narrow corridors, where every sound can be a warning of an incoming attack. The remake also connected the entire ship into one continuous whole without hidden loading screens, and it expanded the side content and character work, including new crew conversations and additional logs fleshing out the ship's fate before the main hero's arrival.

On Xbox Series X/S the game uses the fast SSD for perfectly smooth transitions between decks without breaking the atmosphere, and it offers high resolution and improved volumetric lighting, which heightens the feeling of claustrophobia and constant threat in the dark corridors. The sound design, built on the ship's metallic creaking, the main character's heavy breathing, and unexpected audio ambushes from around a corner, ranks among the most elaborate in the genre and is one of the reasons the game works best with headphones and the lights off.

The remake was received by fans and critics alike as a model example of how to sensitively approach reviving an older classic – it preserves the core of the original game while also modernizing it on both the gameplay and technical side, including the previously silent main character, who speaks for the first time in the remake. On Xbox Series X/S, where the game was released as an exclusively next-gen title with no version for older consoles, the remake fully demonstrated what the new generation of hardware can do with atmospheric horror, and it reminded everyone why the original Dead Space is considered one of the best horror games of its generation.

**Why play it:** For survival horror fans who will appreciate a sensitively modernized remake with a main character who finally speaks, it's one of the best reasons to give the original classic a chance.

xbox-series__scarlet-nexus.teaser: Anime action RPG with two intertwined storylines; telekinesis hurls cars and lampposts alike.
xbox-series__scarlet-nexus.article:
**Scarlet Nexus** is an action RPG with a striking anime visual style that, on Xbox Series X/S, tells a story set in a future world plagued by alien creatures called Others, against whom players gifted with psychokinetic powers fight as part of a special organization called OSF. The game offers two distinct storylines told from the perspective of two main characters, Yuito and Kasane, which intertwine throughout the narrative and offer different views of the same events, while combat combines fast melee attacks with telekinetically hurling objects from the environment, such as wrecked cars or street lamps, and the ability to temporarily borrow the powers of teammates. This system makes battles a visually striking and strategically varied spectacle, in which the player constantly switches between their own arsenal of abilities and temporarily borrowed team powers.

On Xbox Series X/S, the game runs at high resolution and a high frame rate, which is essential for readability during fast, acrobatic battles filled with on-screen effects. Alongside combat, the game also offers a social element in the form of messages from supporting characters that develop relationships among OSF team members between missions. The art style combines cel-shaded graphics with a bold pink and red color palette, creating a distinctive visual identity, complemented by electronic-orchestral music that underscores the futuristic atmosphere of the city of Suoh and its neighborhoods devastated by the Others' attacks.

Upon release, Scarlet Nexus was praised above all for its distinctive visual style, its refined combat system, and its boldness in offering two different perspectives on the same story, which increases the motivation to complete the game multiple times and piece the whole story together. Although it is a smaller production compared to major Japanese RPG series, Scarlet Nexus managed to build a loyal fanbase, and on Xbox Series X/S it ranks among the titles that show how well a fast, action-oriented take on the JRPG can work on modern hardware without compromising smoothness.

**Why play it:** For its distinctive visual style, brisk combat system, and the boldness to show two different perspectives on the same story, which is enticing to piece together on a second playthrough.

xbox-series__immortals-of-aveum.teaser: A shooter where firearms are replaced by colorful magic of three elements.
xbox-series__immortals-of-aveum.article:
**Immortals of Aveum** is a first-person shooter that, instead of classic weapons, builds on magic — the player, as young mage Jak, fights using three color-coded types of magical attacks, blue, red, and green, which functionally replace conventional firearms from shotguns to sniper rifles, and gradually combines them with additional abilities and upgrades. The story takes place in a fantasy world torn by an eternal war over a magical resource called the Fount, and combines linear action sequences with exploration of larger locations full of collectibles and side quests that expand the main storyline and the relationships between characters. The player also gradually unlocks upgrades for magical weapons, called Sigils, which adds another layer of customization to combat.

On Xbox Series X/S, the game visually benefits from richly detailed environments and spectacular magical battles that take advantage of the new-generation consoles' power to display a large number of particle effects at once without losing smoothness during hectic firefights. The musical and sound design underscores the epic tone of the narrative and, together with cinematic cutscenes and motion-capture animations, gives the game a blockbuster feel that Ascendant Studios evidently aimed for in its first major production.

Immortals of Aveum was received as an ambitious attempt to bring the energy of modern shooters into a fantasy setting, with the idea of replacing weapons with magic while retaining the same speed and precision of aiming that players are used to from classic FPS games earning the most praise. As the debut title of a newly founded studio, Immortals of Aveum showed that the first-person shooter genre still has room for unconventional ideas, and on Xbox Series X/S it offered a technically accomplished showcase of what the new console generation is capable of.

**Why play it:** Thanks to the idea of replacing weapons with magic while retaining the speed and precision of classic shooters, it's an interesting choice for FPS fans looking for a technically accomplished new-generation spectacle.

xbox-series__sea-of-stars.teaser: A pixel-art JRPG inspired by 90s classics; turn-based combat is spiced up by timed hits.
xbox-series__sea-of-stars.article:
**Sea of Stars** is a pixel-art JRPG inspired by classics of the nineties that, on Xbox Series X/S, tells the story of two Solstice Warriors, Valere and Zale, fighting against the alchemist Fleshmancer and his monstrous creations scattered across the world. Combat is turn-based, but enriched with a system of timed strikes and blocks that increase or decrease damage, combining attacks against specific types of enemy magic to disrupt their abilities, and the ability to combine the two main characters' abilities into stronger joint attacks, which lets the game pair a nostalgic look with modern, well-thought-out mechanics that keep battles exciting even after dozens of hours played. The party also gradually grows with additional companions with their own personalities and abilities, adding another strategic layer to combat.

On Xbox Series X/S, the game runs smoothly at high resolution, and the hand-drawn pixel-art environments, from sunny coastlines through dense forests to dark caves, stand out thanks to detailed lighting, dynamic weather, and fluid character animations. The music was composed by Eric W. Brown, partly in collaboration with Yasunori Mitsuda, composer of the legendary Chrono Trigger, to which Sea of Stars openly acknowledges itself, both visually and tonally, as one of its main inspirations. Exploring the world also offers logic puzzles, platforming sections, and hidden treasures that set the game apart from purely combat-focused JRPGs.

Upon release, Sea of Stars was received as one of the best independent JRPGs of recent times, and day-one availability on Xbox Game Pass helped it reach a wide audience that might otherwise have overlooked a smaller title. Today the game is often cited as proof that the genre of pixel-art JRPGs inspired by the classics can still offer fresh and well-considered gameplay mechanics, not just a nostalgic memory, and for many players it represents an ideal entry point into the JRPG genre as a whole.

**Why play it:** For a well-considered pixel-art JRPG that, thanks to day-one availability on Game Pass, works as an ideal entry point into the genre even for players with no prior experience.

xbox-series__wo-long-fallen-dynasty.teaser: A souls-like from Team Ninja set in fantasy China of the Three Kingdoms. Faster and more aggressive than Nioh.
xbox-series__wo-long-fallen-dynasty.article:
**Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty** is an action RPG from Team Ninja set in a fantastically reimagined China of the Three Kingdoms period, where the historical Yellow Turban rebellion against the Han dynasty mixes with demonic forces and supernatural enemies inhabiting a devastated landscape. The game builds on a combat system based on a so-called "morale" system and precise parry timing called Deflect, in which the player must deflect enemy attacks at just the right moment to disrupt their balance and open up a window for a devastating counterattack — a mechanic reminiscent of the studio's previous titles like Nioh, but here faster, more aggressive, and less dependent on stamina. Magical elements of five elements are also available, which the player assigns to their character and combines with a combat style of their own choosing.

On Xbox Series X/S, the game offers a choice between a resolution-focused mode and a mode with a higher frame rate, which plays a crucial role for comfortable and fair play in a title dependent on precise combat timing. Visually, it combines realistically depicted environments of a war-torn China, from burning villages to snow-covered mountains, with fantastical, demonic elements, and music drawing on traditional Chinese instruments rounds out a unique atmosphere that sets the title apart from other soulslike games set in a Japanese environment.

Upon release, Wo Long: Fallen Dynasty was praised for its fast, aggressive combat system and for its day-and-date availability on Xbox Game Pass, which brought the title to a much wider audience than is usual for demanding soulslike games. The game continues Team Ninja's reputation as one of the leading creators of demanding action RPGs, and on Xbox Series X/S it offers a technically polished experience that proves the genre still has room for new variations on tried-and-true foundations built on precise timing and risky aggression.

**Why play it:** For its fast, aggressive combat system built on precise timing, which thanks to day-one Game Pass availability made a demanding souls-like accessible to a much wider audience than is usual for the genre.

xbox-series__f1-23.teaser: The official Formula 1 game with the Braking Point story mode and the return of F2 cars.
xbox-series__f1-23.article:
**F1 23** is the official Formula 1 game for the 2023 season, developed by Codemasters in collaboration with EA Sports. On Xbox Series X and S, it offers the complete starting grid of all teams and drivers, faithfully rendered circuits, and a driving physics model that tries to combine realism with accessibility for a wider audience. A new feature is the Braking Point story mode, which continues the successful narrative format from previous installments and adds a dramatic human dimension of the paddock and racing behind-the-scenes to the technical simulation. The game also brings back two-seater F2 cars to the lineup for the first time in years, letting players try out the lower single-seater category as a stepping stone to real F1.

Gameplay rests on elaborate team management, the My Team career mode, and online races, where players can compete across platforms thanks to network support. On the new console generation, the game benefits from faster loading, higher resolution, and more stable frame rates, which lets the rendering of reflections, weather, and dynamic track lighting shine. The sound design faithfully reproduces the roar of engines and pit radio communication, which, together with tense music, heightens the sense of racing adrenaline during a Grand Prix weekend. Support for shifters and racing wheels also gives the game a more demanding dimension for players seeking the most authentic cockpit experience possible.

Contemporary reviews praised above all the balance between simulation depth and accessibility for newcomers, though there were also reservations about opponent AI and slightly repetitive career elements. In the context of the genre, it is a well-crafted annual update that cemented the series' position as the reference point for official F1 racing on current consoles. The series is also accompanied long-term by the official F1 Esports Series scene, which turns the game into a platform for competitive play at a professional level. Even with the passage of time, it remains a reliable choice for fans of top-tier motorsport.

**Why play it:** For its balance of simulation depth and accessibility for newcomers, and support for the official F1 Esports Series scene, it remains a reliable choice for fans of top-tier motorsport, despite minor reservations about opponent AI.

xbox-series__ea-sports-wrc.teaser: A rally simulation to which Codemasters returned after years away; weather changes the track surface.
xbox-series__ea-sports-wrc.article:
**EA Sports WRC** is an official rally simulation created by Codemasters, which after years took over the World Rally Championship license from another publisher. On Xbox Series X and S, the game offers dozens of real tracks from various countries, faithfully rendered cars and teams, and a dynamic weather system that gradually changes surface conditions and visibility over the course of a single rally. The main draw is the Career mode, in which the player builds their own team from small races up to the top competition, chooses a co-driver, and gradually upgrades both the vehicle fleet and the team's facilities.

Driving is built on a physics model that emphasizes sensitive handling of throttle, brakes, and sliding on gravel, snow, or tarmac, making the game a more demanding experience than arcade racing titles. On the new console generation, the game particularly benefits from high-quality environment rendering, dynamic weather, and real-time shadows, which, together with a precise co-driver voice in the cockpit, create the atmosphere of a genuine rally race. Sound design and the tension of racing against the clock are among the game's strongest points, as is the noticeable difference between how a car behaves on dry versus muddy surfaces.

Reception at launch was mixed, as technical problems, missing features from previous installments, and a less extensive car roster compared to earlier series entries drew criticism from longtime fans, though subsequent free updates gradually fixed a number of shortcomings and expanded the selection of cars and tracks. Even so, the game earned recognition for returning to an authentic and demanding rally simulation on consoles, one built on honest driving rather than arcade accessibility. Today it represents, for rally fans, one of the few ways to experience the official World Rally Championship on Xbox and measure themselves against other players on the same real tracks they know from television broadcasts.

**Why play it:** For returning to an authentic, demanding rally simulation built on honest driving rather than arcade accessibility, it's one of the few ways to experience the official World Rally Championship on Xbox.

xbox-series__grid-legends.teaser: Arcade racing with the live-action Driven to Glory story mode, styled like a sports documentary.
xbox-series__grid-legends.article:
**Grid Legends** is an arcade racing game from Codemasters that continues the long tradition of the Grid series and combines spectacular racing with the live-action Driven to Glory story mode. Using live-action sequences with actors, it tells the story of a team fighting its way to the top of the motorsport world, an approach reminiscent of a televised sports documentary. On Xbox Series X and S, the game offers a wide range of vehicles from open-wheel racers through stock cars to demolition derby, and players can freely move between the various disciplines within a single season.

At the core of the gameplay is aggressive, contact-heavy racing, where collisions between cars are commonplace and opponents actively react to the player's behavior thanks to a system called Livrivalries, which remembers previous confrontations and carries them over into future races. On the new console generation, the game benefits from a high frame rate and fast loading, which, together with destructible environments and dynamic weather, give the races visual punch. The musical score and commentator voices round out the impression of a grand sporting spectacle that strives to be accessible even to less experienced players, among other things thanks to an extensive range of driving assists.

Reviews praised above all the variety of content, quality sound design, and entertaining, if occasionally predictable, storytelling built on live-action characters. Criticism was directed mainly at the somewhat stereotypical dialogue and a slightly superficial damage system. Grid Legends nonetheless confirmed that arcade racing focused on spectacle and accessibility still has its solid place on current consoles alongside simulation titles, and it offers an entertaining alternative for players who mainly want a fast, carefree ride without having to master complex simulation physics and lengthy learning of how to handle individual cars.

**Why play it:** For its varied content, quality sound, and spectacular arcade racing, it's an entertaining alternative for players who want a fast ride without having to master complex simulation physics.

xbox-series__crew-motorfest.teaser: An open world on the fictional Hawaiian island of O'ahu; more compact than the earlier The Crew games.
xbox-series__crew-motorfest.article:
**The Crew Motorfest** is an openly designed racing title from the French studio Ivory Tower that takes players to the fictional Hawaiian island of O'ahu, where a grand automotive festival is taking place. Instead of the sprawling scaled-down model of the United States that players were used to from previous entries in The Crew series, this time the developers focused on a more compact, but denser and more detailed open world full of varied terrain, from beaches to mountain roads and volcanic regions, inspired by the real geography of the Hawaiian archipelago.

The game is divided into so-called Playlists, thematic collections of races linking specific brands, eras, or driving styles, from classic sports cars through off-road quad bikes to boats and planes, between which the player freely switches on the fly, without having to go through menus. On Xbox Series X and S, the open world loads with virtually no delay, and the game benefits from a high density of detail, day-night cycles, and pronounced weather that affects both visibility and vehicle grip on the road. The sound design, with an extensive selection of licensed music spanning genres, contributes to the impression of a continuous festival mood and celebratory atmosphere, further heightened by regular live in-game events.

Critical reception praised above all the variety of content, the return to the qualities of the original series, and a generous offering of vehicles and activities for both single and multiplayer. A minor drawback remains the smaller size of the game world compared to previous entries, which the developers offset with greater content density per square kilometer. Motorfest nonetheless confirmed that the concept of a vacation automotive festival works as a fresh and accessible alternative to simulation racing games, offering dozens of hours of fun for players of all experience levels, from casual cruising to collecting every vehicle and completing every challenge in the individual playlists.

**Why play it:** For its generous offering of vehicles and activities for both single and multiplayer, it delivers dozens of hours of fun, from casual cruising to collecting every vehicle and completing every playlist challenge.

xbox-series__hot-wheels-unleashed.teaser: Miniature Hot Wheels cars on orange tracks running through kids' bedrooms and garages.
xbox-series__hot-wheels-unleashed.article:
**Hot Wheels Unleashed** brings the popular Hot Wheels die-cast toy cars and their signature orange tracks full of loops, jumps, and stunts into video game form. Italian studio Milestone, known primarily for its motorcycle simulations, shows here that it can also deliver lighthearted arcade fun built on fast pacing and spectacular trick tracks winding through toy-scale bedrooms, garages, and living rooms, where obstacles lurk in the form of toys, furniture, and household appliances.

The gameplay is built on simple but precise controls that emphasize proper timing of drifts, jumps, and power-ups, which players earn by driving and can use to slow down rivals or speed themselves up. The game includes a track editor where players can build their own routes from dozens of pieces and elements, plus an extensive collection of licensed vehicles ranging from classic Hot Wheels models to popular brands from film and gaming. On Xbox Series X and S the game runs smoothly, with the extra power showing most in demanding effects such as reflections on glossy surfaces and larger numbers of rivals on track at once.

Reviews particularly praised the accessible gameplay for all age groups, the quality track editor, and the visible love for the license reflected in the models' details, glossy paint jobs, and small cosmetic touches on individual tracks. The game subsequently gained support through regular expansions adding more vehicles, tracks, and game modes. Hot Wheels Unleashed thus confirmed that even an undemanding arcade racer built on a well-known toy concept can find a broad and grateful audience across generations of players on current consoles, from children to nostalgic adult collectors who know the brand from childhood and appreciate its careful digital treatment and the many hidden references to favorite models.

**Why play it:** With accessible gameplay for all age groups, a quality track editor, and visible love for the license, it's a great choice for both kids and nostalgic adult Hot Wheels collectors.

xbox-series__motogp-23.teaser: The official MotoGP simulation; the Rivals mode revives legendary duels from the nineties.
xbox-series__motogp-23.article:
**MotoGP 23** is the official simulation of the motorcycle Grand Prix, traditionally developed by Italian studio Milestone, which specializes in motorsport titles. The game features the complete starting grid of the current MotoGP, Moto2, and Moto3 season with licensed riders, teams, and circuits from around the world. The new addition is the Rivals mode, offering unlockable challenges built around real historical duels between famous riders, which adds a narrative dimension beyond the standard career mode and brings less experienced players closer to the championship's older history, including legendary battles from the nineties and 2000s that produced some of the most famous rivalries in the history of motorcycle racing.

Riding a motorcycle emphasizes fine control of lean angle, braking, and throttle, which together with a realistic tire and wear model creates a more demanding, simulation-focused experience compared to arcade racing games. On Xbox Series X and S there's greater frame-rate stability and higher-quality rendering of tracks and weather, which at a motorcycle's high speeds is especially important for readability and precise cornering timing. The sound design faithfully reproduces the characteristic sound of racing engines and the ambient noise of the grandstands, rounding out the impression of a genuine race weekend.

Critical reception praises the series' long-standing consistency and depth of simulation, though it often points out that the yearly update brings more incremental improvements than fundamental changes from previous entries. For motorcycle racing fans, MotoGP nonetheless remains one of the few significant official alternatives on current consoles, since competing licensed motorcycle simulations are fairly rare on the market. The game thus plays the role of a reliable, honestly crafted rendition of the license for a more demanding audience seeking an authentic two-wheeled racing experience, whether that's a short weekend race or a multi-year career across all three rider classes of the championship.

**Why play it:** For motorcycle racing fans it remains one of the few significant licensed alternatives on current consoles, whether for a short weekend race or a multi-year career across the championship classes.

xbox-series__nba-2k24.teaser: The most elaborate basketball simulation on the market; career, franchise, and collectible MyTeam.
xbox-series__nba-2k24.article:
**NBA 2K24** is the current entry in the long-running basketball series from Visual Concepts studio, which has long held the position of the most elaborate and best-selling basketball simulation on the market. The game continues the tradition of the MyCareer and MyNBA career modes, in which the player either builds their own athlete from the start of their career to star status, or runs an entire organization including trades, the draft, the budget, and the coaching staff. Also included is the online MyTeam mode built around collectible player cards, plus a social space in the form of a virtual city, blending career and multiplayer content where players spend time between matches.

On Xbox Series X and S the game benefits from motion-capture technology recorded from real players and a high level of animation aiming to replicate real basketball as faithfully as possible, including the individual dribbling and shooting styles of the league's stars. The console's extra power shows in smoother transitions between animations and faster loading of the extensive menus and game modes, which matters a lot for a title with this much content. The sound design, with commentator voices and licensed music, rounds out the atmosphere of a real NBA game, including crowd reactions to key moments and loud support from the home crowd.

Reviews consistently praise the depth of the simulation and the quality of the presentation, though criticism repeatedly surfaces regarding microtransactions in the MyTeam and MyCareer modes, which many players say affect the pace of progression without additional spending. Even so, NBA 2K24 confirms the series' status as the standard in basketball games, offering dozens to hundreds of hours of content for players interested in career and online modes of a professional-level sports simulation, including the ability to follow their player's development across multiple NBA seasons.

**Why play it:** With deep simulation and quality presentation it offers dozens to hundreds of hours of career and online modes, even though microtransactions in MyTeam and MyCareer remain a frequent target of criticism.

xbox-series__ea-sports-fc-24.teaser: The first entry after the split from FIFA; women's football reaches the same technical level for the first time.
xbox-series__ea-sports-fc-24.article:
**EA Sports FC 24** is the first entry in the football series after publisher Electronic Arts split from the international federation FIFA, taking over from the original FIFA brand and continuing its long tradition dating back to the nineties. The game offers an extensive licensed database of clubs, leagues, and players, plus new HyperMotionV technology, which uses footage from real matches to more faithfully capture player movement and ball duels on the pitch, including player reactions to unexpected in-game situations. For the first time, women's football competitions and national teams are also rendered at the same technical level, expanding the overall scope of the game's licensed content.

The core of the content remains the popular Ultimate Team mode built on collecting and upgrading player cards, alongside a career mode as manager or player, a club mode for creating your own virtual footballer, and online competitions across skill-based ladders. On Xbox Series X and S the extra power shows especially in stadium crowd detail, animation quality, and faster loading between matches, which together with realistic lighting and weather contribute to a broadcast-like feel. Commentary and the musical score further enhance the atmosphere of a big match, whether it's a league fixture or a cup final watched down to the last minute.

Critical reception praised the smoother, more dynamic player movement enabled by the new technology, though discussion repeatedly arose about balance and microtransactions in the Ultimate Team mode, which remains the game's main source of post-launch revenue. As the first entry under the new FC 24 brand, it also confirmed that the name change didn't break the series' continuity, cementing the game's position as the most widely played football simulation on current consoles for millions of players around the world who typically don't miss the annual new installment.

**Why play it:** With smoother, more dynamic player movement thanks to the new technology, it remains the most widely played football simulation on current consoles, even though microtransactions in Ultimate Team remain a controversial aspect of the game.

xbox-series__madden-nfl-24.teaser: The official American football simulation from EA Tiburon, with Franchise and Superstar modes.
xbox-series__madden-nfl-24.article:
**Madden NFL 24** is the current annual entry in the long-running American football simulation from EA Tiburon studio, which holds the official license for the NFL and its teams, players, and stadiums. The game continues the tradition of the Franchise career mode, in which the player runs a team over multiple seasons including the draft, trades, and budget, and Superstar mode, focused on an individual player's career from college through the professional league and possibly stardom on the team, where the player gradually builds their reputation and abilities based on how they play. Also included is the online Ultimate Team mode with collectible player cards and a regularly updated slate of challenges throughout the season.

The main new feature is the FieldSENSE system, which aims to more faithfully capture one-on-one battles between offensive and defensive players as well as physical struggles for the ball after it lands, replacing the older, less detailed player-contact model from previous entries in the series. On Xbox Series X and S the extra power shows in smoother player animations, faster loading between quarters, and more detailed rendering of the stadium and crowd. The commentator and authentic presentation, with graphics resembling NFL broadcasts, round out the feel of a real Sunday game, including halftime recaps, statistics, and individual player graphics.

Critical reception praised the improved physics of ball duels and enhanced artificial intelligence, though there were also frequent remarks that the yearly update brings more gradual improvements than a fundamental transformation of the series. Even so, Madden remains the only officially licensed American football game on current consoles, and thanks to that it holds a significant position among sports simulations for NFL fans around the world and beyond North America, where the sport's popularity is traditionally highest and where the game also serves as a gateway to understanding its rules.

**Why play it:** For NFL fans around the world, it's the only officially licensed American football game on current consoles, and it also serves as a gateway to understanding the sport's rules.

xbox-series__rocket-league.teaser: Football with rocket-powered cars from Psyonix; on Series X|S it runs at up to 120 frames per second.
xbox-series__rocket-league.article:
**Rocket League** combines football with racing cars into a unique concept, in which teams of rocket-powered cars on an enclosed pitch knock a giant ball toward the opponent's goal. The game was originally created by Psyonix studio for a previous console generation, and only over the years did it become one of the most-played titles of its era; on Xbox Series X and S it received dedicated optimization at the console's launch, bringing higher resolution and frame rates up to 120 frames per second for a maximally smooth and precise driving feel, even in fast duels near the goal.

The core of the gameplay is deceptively simple controls built on acceleration, jumping, and aerial flight, which in the hands of experienced players turns into an acrobatic, almost balletic sport full of spectacular volley strikes and goal-line saves right under the crossbar. The game has been free to play since 2020 and offers cross-platform play, which together with regular seasons, cosmetic items, and an esports scene keeps an active and extensive community of players engaged years after release. Alongside standard three-versus-three matches it offers smaller and larger game formats, ranked competitive matches, and occasional themed game modes tied to holidays or collaborations with other brands.

Rocket League is widely regarded as one of the most original and best-tuned multiplayer concepts of its generation, combining accessibility for new players with an almost endless space for improvement for experienced veterans. On Xbox Series X and S it offers one of the smoothest and most responsive versions of the game around, and so, even years later, it remains a clear choice for anyone looking for an addictive, socially oriented action sports experience, whether playing casually or pursuing competitive ladders and following the professional esports tournaments that have grown up around the game over the years.

**Why play it:** With an addictive, socially oriented mix of action and sport in one of the smoothest versions of the game around, it's a clear choice whether you play casually or follow competitive esports tournaments.

xbox-series__age-of-empires-iv.teaser: A real-time strategy game from Relic Entertainment, ported to console gamepad controls.
xbox-series__age-of-empires-iv.article:
**Age of Empires IV** is a real-time strategy game from Relic Entertainment and Microsoft, which originally launched on PC in 2021 and arrived on Xbox Series X and S in 2023 as a port adapted for gamepad control. The game continues the series' tradition based on building medieval civilizations, gathering resources, developing technologies, and waging wars across historical periods from the early Middle Ages through later eras with gunpowder, siege engines, and early artillery.

Each of the playable civilizations, from the English through the Mongols to China or Delhi, has its own units, buildings, and strategic advantages drawn from real history, which sets the game apart from pure fantasy fiction and gives it an educational dimension supported by accompanying historical documents and short documentary videos. The console controls translate a genre traditionally played with mouse and keyboard into a form suited to a gamepad using radial menus and smart unit selection, a nontrivial task for strategy games on consoles that many earlier console adaptations of the genre failed to solve satisfactorily, which is one reason real-time strategy games have long appeared only rarely on consoles.

Critical reception praised the successful adaptation of a complex strategy game to gamepad controls and the preservation of the campaigns' depth and multiplayer competition, including the ability to play against PC players thanks to shared online infrastructure connecting both platforms into a single community. Age of Empires IV is thus one of only a handful of quality real-time strategy games available directly on consoles, giving genre fans without a PC full access to one of the most significant historical RTS titles on current-generation hardware, without having to compromise on the game's depth and scope.

**Why play it:** For real-time strategy fans without a PC, it offers full access to the depth of the campaigns and multiplayer thanks to shared online infrastructure connecting console and PC players into a single community.

xbox-series__age-of-empires-ii-definitiv.teaser: A modernized version of the legendary strategy game from the late nineties, with all expansions included.
xbox-series__age-of-empires-ii-definitiv.article:
**Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition** is a modernized version of the legendary real-time strategy game from the late nineties, prepared for current platforms by Forgotten Empires studio in collaboration with Microsoft. On Xbox Series X and S the game arrived in 2022 as a full console port including every expansion released so far and dozens of civilizations from medieval Europe through Asia to the Americas, each with its own units and strategies, supplemented by years of expansions and campaigns based on real historical events and figures such as Joan of Arc or Genghis Khan.

The game keeps the original concept of building a settlement, gathering resources, developing technologies, and waging wars against opponents, which in its time defined the entire real-time strategy genre and inspired dozens of later titles across the whole games industry. On console the controls are adapted using radial menus and smart group commands, aiming to compensate for the absence of a mouse and keyboard, a considerable technical achievement for such a complex genre. Visually the game benefits from recreated models and environments in high resolution, which nonetheless preserve the original, readable stylization and color palette that longtime series fans are used to from the very first release in the late nineties.

Critical reception especially praised the fact that the depth and balance of the original game were preserved even when adapted for a gamepad, which is the exception rather than the rule for strategy games. Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition thus opened up one of the most significant and influential titles in the history of the strategy genre to console players as well, who previously didn't have easy access to this classic, and confirmed that even after decades the game remains thoroughly playable and enjoyable for new and returning players alike.

**Why play it:** By preserving the depth and balance of a legendary strategy game even after adapting it for a gamepad, which is the exception rather than the rule for the genre, it opens the game up to console players who previously lacked access to it.

xbox-series__neon-white.teaser: A fast platformer from the creator of Donut County; cards are either weapons or movement.
xbox-series__neon-white.article:
**Neon White** is a fast-paced action platformer from Angel Matrix, designed by Ben Esposito, creator of the earlier game Donut County, blending freerunning movement mechanics with card-game elements. The player takes on the role of White in heaven as one of the "demon hunters," tasked with clearing each level as fast as possible, while collected cards can either be used as one-shot weapons against demons or discarded for special movement abilities such as a double jump, dash, or teleport straight to the goal, turning every level into a puzzle of movement decisions. The game encourages repeated playthroughs with a medal system for speed as well as for finding hidden doves tucked into the corners of levels, so even short levels offer considerable replay value.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs at a high frame rate, which is absolutely essential for this kind of gameplay built on millisecond precision and constant level replays chasing a better time. The sharp, stylized anime visuals and an energetic electronic soundtrack underscore the sense of speed and precision, while the story sequences between levels offer a lighter, dialogue-driven contrast full of dark humor to the otherwise fully focused action.

The game was released in 2022 on PC and PlayStation consoles, and it arrived on Xbox Series X|S and into Game Pass later, where its combination of speedrun precision, imaginative level design, and a clear rating system quickly earned it a devoted audience. Neon White is now regarded as one of the best-designed titles focused on repeatedly refining a level run, even among players who don't otherwise seek out fast platformers and speedruns, because the game explains its reward and rating system clearly enough to remain accessible to newcomers to the genre.

**Why play it:** For speedrun precision, imaginative level design, and a clear rating system, it's one of the best-designed titles even for players who otherwise don't seek out fast platformers and speedruns.

xbox-series__dredge.teaser: A fishing adventure with horror elements; fatigue at night warps both the map and the player's perception.
xbox-series__dredge.article:
**Dredge** is an atmospheric adventure with fishing-simulation elements from the New Zealand studio Black Salt Games, in which the player sails a small boat across fog-shrouded waters, fishing to pay off debts and uncover the mystery of a vanished fisherman in a remote harbor town. As dusk falls, however, the waters change, and unsettling phenomena and creatures appear in the dark, while the player also has to contend with a fatigue mechanic that, if they stay out at sea too long, begins to distort their perception of the surrounding world and conjure hallucinations that even affect the layout of the map. The player gradually upgrades their boat with new tools and components found at sea, allowing them to venture into more distant and dangerous areas of the map.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly and at a crisp resolution, which stands out especially on the dark water surfaces and in dense fog, where the game relies on slowly building atmosphere rather than direct action. A melancholic, faintly unsettling musical score and a stark, illustrative visual style with striking silhouettes support a narrative inspired by Lovecraftian horror and sea legends about things best left in the depths.

Dredge was released in 2023 and was very well received by critics for its inventive combination of a relaxing fishing loop with gradually escalating tension and horror elements, a combination not many games had attempted at this scale before it. The game is now often cited as a textbook example of how genre elements from seemingly incompatible styles can be woven into a single coherent, atmospheric whole, and it's one of the beloved smaller titles in the Game Pass catalog for players with weaker nerves as well as for those looking for a quieter kind of horror built more on oppressive atmosphere and uncertainty about what lurks beneath the surface than on direct scares and cheap jump-scares.

**Why play it:** For players who want a quieter horror built on oppressive atmosphere and uncertainty rather than jump-scares, this blend of relaxing fishing and escalating tension is an ideal choice.

xbox-series__astroneer.teaser: Soothing building on alien planets; a terrain deformer shapes the world to your liking.
xbox-series__astroneer.article:
**Astroneer** is an exploration building game from System Era Softworks, set on distant planets that the player explores, mines, and literally reshapes using a tool called the terrain deformer, which can dig tunnels, level hills, or build artificial platforms. The game's core loop is gathering resources, processing them in increasingly complex machines, and then building ever more extensive bases, vehicles, and research facilities; it can be played solo or in co-op with other players who jointly build shared infrastructure across several planets of the solar system. New technologies, automated production lines, and transport vehicles gradually become available, so what starts as basic survival on a single planet can grow into a sprawling interstellar operation.

On Xbox Series X|S the game benefits from improved performance and smoother rendering of large-scale terrain modifications, which are central to the gameplay, especially when building large bases with dozens of interconnected machines and pipes. A colorful, playful visual style and a calm, ambient musical score create a relaxed atmosphere of exploration free of unnecessary pressure on the player, which noticeably sets the game apart from many survival titles with a stronger focus on hunger, thirst, and constant survival.

Since its release, Astroneer has built a stable and loyal community of players who value the combination of creative building, cooperative play, and the gentle, meditative pace of space exploration. Thanks to regular content updates adding new planets, machines, and automation options, the game remains alive many years after release, and in the Game Pass catalog it's one of the titles suited to long-term, repeated returns rather than a single playthrough over a weekend, while its co-op easily finds a place among groups of friends who play together regularly.

**Why play it:** For fans of creative building, cooperation, and a meditative pace of space exploration, it's a title more for long-term, repeated returns than for one quick weekend playthrough.

xbox-series__death-s-door.teaser: Zelda for crows; polished timing-based combat and clever unlocking of shortcuts.
xbox-series__death-s-door.article:
**Death's Door** is an action adventure from Acid Nerve that draws on the design of classic games in The Legend of Zelda series, including its emphasis on polished timing-based combat, exploration of interconnected locations, and the gradual unlocking of new abilities needed to return to previously inaccessible places. The player takes on the role of a crow working as a soul collector, whose routine assignment goes wrong after the soul she was meant to deliver is stolen from her, and she sets out to reclaim it through a series of dangerous, thematically distinct worlds full of puzzles and enemies. Along the way she meets other soul collectors, whose fates and conversations lend surprising depth to an outwardly simple story, along with plenty of dark humor.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly with fast loading between areas, which stands out especially when returning to previously visited locations with newly acquired abilities, such as a bomb attack or a grappling hook. A melancholic visual style with a muted, almost autumnal color palette and orchestral music underscore the themes of death and impermanence the game repeatedly explores, without losing its lightness and the dry humor in the dialogue of supporting characters.

Death's Door was released in 2021 and was received by critics as one of the most polished smaller titles of its time, praised especially for its precise combat system, challenging boss fights, and thoughtful level design in the metroidvania spirit. The game is often cited today as an example of how a small team can, with limited resources, create a game comparable in quality to larger productions, and in the Game Pass catalog it's a regularly recommended title for fans of action adventures who appreciate a game that can be completed in a reasonable time without unnecessary padding or filler content, yet still leaves a strong and lasting impression.

**Why play it:** For metroidvania fans who appreciate precise boss fights and thoughtful level design, it's proof that a small team can create a game comparable to big productions, and one that can be finished in a reasonable amount of time.

xbox-series__chicory-colorful-tale.teaser: Painting as the core mechanic; the brush restores color to a faded world and to your own style.
xbox-series__chicory-colorful-tale.article:
**Chicory: A Colorful Tale** is an adventure with platforming and painting elements from creator Greg Lobanov, published under the Finji label, in which the player controls a dog named Chicory who inherits a magic brush capable of restoring color to a faded, literally colorless world. Most of the game's puzzles and exploration are built around creative use of the brush – the player paints paths across chasms with it, solves environmental puzzles, and freely expresses personal style with their own patterns and color combinations across the map, which makes every playthrough a slightly different, personal visual experience. The game also offers an extensive photo and painting mode in which players can freely edit saved scenery even after completing the main story.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly and at a crisp resolution, which shows off the finely drawn environments and the ability to freely paint over most surfaces in the game without noticeable slowdown. The game openly engages with themes of anxiety, impostor syndrome, and the pressure of expectations tied to creativity, through sensitively written dialogue with supporting characters who experience these themes as intimately as the protagonist Chicory herself.

Chicory was released in 2021 on PC and PlayStation and arrived on Xbox platforms somewhat later, where the combination of its original painting mechanic, sensitive storytelling, and cute yet imaginative visuals earned it a devoted audience even beyond the traditional circle of platformer fans. The game tends to be praised as one of the most distinctive indie titles of its time, one that managed to artistically portray difficult themes of creativity and self-doubt without losing its playfulness, colorfulness, and accessibility to a wide range of players, including those who don't usually play platformers or adventure games regularly and were drawn to it specifically by its themes of creativity and self-expression.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its original painting mechanic, sensitive storytelling, and cute visuals, it will appeal even to players who don't usually play platformers and adventure games but are drawn to its themes of creativity and self-expression.

xbox-series__resident-evil-village.teaser: Gothic horror with Lady Dimitrescu; survival pacing blends tension with more action-heavy sections.
xbox-series__resident-evil-village.article:
**Resident Evil Village** picks up directly from the events of Resident Evil 7 and transports the player to a snow-covered village surrounded by a gothic castle, swamps, and ancient buildings, ruled over by supernatural beings led by the mysterious Lady Dimitrescu. The game combines first-person exploration, combat with firearms and knives, and puzzle-solving, gradually alternating dark horror atmosphere with more action-heavy sections that recall survival action more than the pure horror of the previous entry. A crafting system, trading with a mysterious merchant named Duke, and exploring a castle full of locked doors and hidden treasures keep the pacing balanced between tension and the reward of careful exploration. The game gradually leads the player through several strikingly different locations, from the aforementioned castle through a swampy lake to an industrial factory, each offering its own type of enemies and puzzles.

On Xbox Series X and S the game runs smoothly at high resolution with fast loading, allowing for nearly seamless transitions between locations without noticeable delays. The sound design and music round out the depressing, yet at times almost baroquely opulent atmosphere of the village and its inhabitants, while the graphics were among the most technically advanced on consoles at the time of release. The reception at launch was very positive, with players and reviewers praising the series' willingness to move toward more varied environments and more diverse enemies compared to the claustrophobic interiors of the seventh installment.

Village still works today as an entry point into the series for new players thanks to its accessible controls and clearly readable goals, while also serving as a celebration of classic survival horror with a modern polish. Additional content in the form of expansions and an alternative third-person perspective further extended the game's lifespan after launch. Its influence on the genre shows especially in how naturally it blends fast action shootouts with slower, tense exploration of the environment. Even years later, it remains one of the most accessible entry points into the Resident Evil universe, both visually and in terms of gameplay.

**Why play it:** For newcomers to the series, it's an accessible entry point with clearly readable goals; for veterans, it's a celebration of classic survival horror with a modern polish and a natural blend of action and tense exploration.

xbox-series__mortal-kombat-1.teaser: A reboot of the series' timeline; the Kameo system adds summonable helpers to fights.
xbox-series__mortal-kombat-1.article:
**Mortal Kombat 1** presents a reboot of the series' timeline through the intervention of the fire god Liu Kang, who created a new universe with altered versions of iconic fighters such as Scorpion, Sub-Zero, and Raiden. The gameplay builds on the series' established system of special attacks and brutal finishers, along with a newly introduced Kameo mechanic, where the player picks a helper for their main character who can be summoned during a fight to add extra combinations and playstyle options. The story mode again offers a cinematically presented narrative full of twists, while the Invasions mode adds more extensive single-player content with gradual unlocking of cosmetic items. The roster includes both longtime pillars of the series and newly reimagined versions of classic characters, as well as several guest fighters from other franchises.

On Xbox Series X and S the game runs smoothly at high resolution, with fast loading for both local and online matches, underscoring the emphasis on responsive controls that's essential for a competitive fighting game. Visually detailed character models and extremely gory fatalities remain a hallmark of the series, accompanied by intense music and sound design that heightens the impact of every hit. Reviewers praised the inventive handling of the alternate timeline as well as the new Kameo fighter system, which opened up room for new combinations of playstyles, though the scope of microtransactions and the cosmetic item store sparked some discussion.

Mortal Kombat 1 thus continues the series' long tradition as one of the most violent, yet also one of the most mechanically refined fighting games on the market, with subsequent expansions further enriching the roster with additional characters and content. The combination of a nostalgic reboot with an innovative helper system showed that even an established brand can push the genre forward without abandoning what has earned Mortal Kombat its loyal audience since the nineties.

**Why play it:** Fans of violent yet mechanically refined fighting games will appreciate a nostalgic reboot paired with an innovative helper system and a gradually expanding character roster.

xbox-series__street-fighter-6.teaser: Three distinct modes in one; World Tour is its own RPG odyssey through Metro City.
xbox-series__street-fighter-6.article:
**Street Fighter 6** arrives with a trio of distinct game modes that make it one of the most comprehensive entries in the series. World Tour offers a single-player RPG odyssey through Metro City with your own customizable character, Battle Hub serves as an online space for matches and tournaments against other players, and the classic Fighting Ground brings traditional fights with familiar and new fighters alike. The character created in World Tour mode can also learn techniques from individual masters, which can then be deployed in your own hybrid fighting style. The new Modern control scheme simplifies performing special moves for new players, while the classic Classic scheme preserves the depth valued by experienced veterans, making the game an accessible yet still demanding competitive title. The fighter roster combines longtime series icons like Ryu and Chun-Li with newly introduced characters, each with their own fighting style and set of special moves.

On Xbox Series X and S the game stands out with clean visuals using a modified RE Engine, a smooth frame rate crucial for precise combat, and fast online matchmaking thanks to robust rollback netcode. The visual style combines bold, graffiti-inspired environments with finely animated characters, backed by an energetic soundtrack leaning toward hip hop and electronic music. Reviews after release were exceptionally positive, with the game praised for its balance between accessibility and depth as well as for the quality of its online infrastructure, which lets matches between players from different parts of the world run with almost no noticeable lag.

Street Fighter 6 is now considered one of the best-received entries in the series and is often cited as a model of the modern approach to fighting games, successfully appealing to both newcomers and longtime genre fans. The combination of World Tour, Battle Hub, and a well-balanced fighting system gives it long-lasting appeal even several years after release.

**Why play it:** Thanks to World Tour, Battle Hub, and a well-balanced fighting system, it appeals to both newcomers and longtime genre fans, and offers lasting appeal even years after release.

xbox-series__like-dragon-infinite-wealth.teaser: Kasuga moves the series from Kamurocho to Hawaii; tactical combat and absurd humor.
xbox-series__like-dragon-infinite-wealth.article:
**Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth** continues the story of Ichiban Kasuga and moves part of the plot from the traditional Japanese setting to sunny Hawaii, without abandoning the series' signature districts of Kamurocho and Isezaki Ijincho. The game combines a tactical combat system with RPG elements, where characters switch between jobs that affect their available abilities, alongside a vast open world full of side activities, minigames, and the absurd humor typical of the Yakuza series. The combat party features a wide range of characters from both Kasuga's older and newer circle, each bringing their own repertoire of abilities and jobs. Alongside Kasuga, the player also controls the returning Kazuma Kiryu, whose parallel storyline links the new and older eras of the series into one cohesive narrative. The Hawaiian portion of the game also adds extensive side content in the form of managing your own Dondoko Island, which serves as a relaxed downtime activity between main quests.

On Xbox Series X and S, the game stands out with the vivid colors of the Hawaiian setting as well as the finely detailed Tokyo district of Kamurocho, with transitions between exploration and combat running smoothly without noticeable slowdown. The soundtrack alternates energetic battle tracks with the more relaxed atmosphere of beaches and bars, underscoring the contrast between serious dramatic passages and lighthearted side stories. Upon release, the game received widespread praise for its scope of content, depth of combat system, and the emotional culmination of both main characters' storylines, with many reviewers ranking it among the best entries in the entire series.

Infinite Wealth confirms that the series can successfully combine a serious theme of organized crime with lighthearted entertainment and experimentation with gameplay mechanics, without losing its identity. In terms of content scope and character depth, it ranks among the most ambitious entries in the entire series and is considered one of the highlights of the action RPG genre in recent years.

**Why play it:** For fans of the series and newcomers alike, this is one of the most ambitious entries, one that manages to combine a serious theme of organized crime with lighthearted fun without losing its own identity.

xbox-series__like-dragon-gaiden-man-who-.teaser: A shorter spin-off between Yakuza 6 and Infinite Wealth; a return to Kazuma's faster combat style.
xbox-series__like-dragon-gaiden-man-who-.article:
**Like a Dragon Gaiden: The Man Who Erased His Name** is a shorter spin-off set between the stories of Yakuza 6 and Like a Dragon: Infinite Wealth, focusing on Kazuma Kiryu, who secretly works for a government agency under a new identity. The player returns to the faster, more action-oriented combat system of the series' earlier style, complemented by new gadgets such as drones and concealed weapons that expand the possibilities for combat and for handling side situations in the Kamurocho district. Although the game is shorter than the series' main entries, and players typically complete it in less than half the time needed for a main title, it offers a full-fledged story with emotional weight as well as a range of the series' signature side stories and minigames, including the return of beloved arcade activities.

On Xbox Series X and S, the title runs smoothly with fast loading between locations, suiting its more action-driven, less sprawling pace compared to the series' larger main entries. Visually, it builds on the series' established style, with detailed nighttime streets of Kamurocho and a distinctive, atmospheric soundtrack accompanying both dramatic and humorous moments. Critics praised the return to more action-oriented combat and the way the game functions as an emotional bridge between two major entries without unnecessarily padding its playtime, also commending it for retaining the main series' high production quality despite its shorter runtime.

Gaiden shows that even smaller, supplementary projects can enrich the sprawling Kiryu saga with a fresh perspective, without needing to match the scope of the series' main entries. Its focused structure also lets the writers dwell on the emotional details of Kiryu's character in a way that a larger main entry might not have room for. Thanks to its compact length and focused storytelling, it's a suitable entry point for players who want to get to know the series without diving into dozens of hours of content.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its compact length and focused storytelling, it's an ideal entry point for players who want to experience Kiryu's story without diving into dozens of hours of the main entries.

xbox-series__mass-effect-legendary-editi.teaser: The entire Shepard trilogy in one package with nearly all DLC content.
xbox-series__mass-effect-legendary-editi.article:
**Mass Effect Legendary Edition** brings together all three entries of the original trilogy about Commander Shepard and their fight against an alien threat called the Reapers into a single package with graphically and mechanically updated versions of each game. The collection includes nearly all of the additionally released content, so the player experiences the entire sprawling story—from the first game, through the politically charged second entry, to the epic conclusion of the third game—as one continuous experience. The combat system of the first game has been noticeably refined toward smoother shooting, while the narrative, the decisions that carry over into later entries, and building relationships with the crew remain at the heart of the series. The collection also includes most of the supplementary content released over the years, including expansions that deepen the side characters and their fates.

On Xbox Series X and S, the edition runs at a higher resolution and frame rate than the original versions, with shorter loading times that ease transitions between planets and missions. The cinematic score and dialogue voice acting remain among the series' strongest elements, and in remastered form they stand out even more thanks to an improved audio mix that comes through even better on modern surround sound systems. Legendary Edition was received as a nearly ideal way to experience the entire trilogy for the first time or all over again, praised especially for its sensitive unification of visual quality across the individual games, though the collection does not include the third game's competitive multiplayer mode.
