The edition confirms why the Mass Effect trilogy is still considered one of the pinnacles of sci-fi storytelling in video games, thanks to its complex world, unforgettable Normandy crew members, and the impact of player decisions across the entire saga. For new players, it's an ideal entry point; for veterans, a reason to relive Shepard's story in its best available form.

**Why play it:** For new players, it's an ideal entry point into one of the pinnacles of sci-fi storytelling in video games; for veterans, a reason to relive Shepard's story in its best available form.

xbox-series__tekken-8.teaser: The culmination of the Mishima clan saga; the Heat system rewards an aggressive offensive style.
xbox-series__tekken-8.article:
**Tekken 8** continues the family saga of the Mishima clan and delivers the culmination of the long-running conflict between Kazuya and Jin Kazama, complemented by an extensive roster of returning and new fighters. The new Heat system mechanically enriches the fights with more aggressive attack options that reward an offensive playstyle, while the single-player Arcade Quest mode serves as an interactive tutorial introducing new players to the series' fundamentals through a stylized digital environment. The fighter roster includes both the longstanding Mishima and Kazama clans as well as newly introduced characters with their own fighting styles drawn from real martial arts. The classic combat system based on combining hand and leg strikes from different stances remains the core of gameplay in this entry as well.

On Xbox Series X and S, the game runs at a high frame rate crucial for precise, responsive fighting, with finely detailed character models and stages that react to environmental destruction during battles. The soundtrack combines energetic electronic and rock tracks that underscore the drama of individual fights, while the cinematically staged character intros continue the series' tradition of elaborate storytelling. Reviewers particularly praised the depth of the new combat system and the quality of the online infrastructure that facilitates competitive play across platforms, while also commending the lighthearted Tekken Ball minigame as a fun alternative to the more serious fights.

Tekken 8 confirms the series' standing among the most respected fighting games of today, thanks to its combination of technical depth, elaborate storytelling, and accessible tutorials for newcomers. The Heat system represents one of the series' most notable mechanical innovations in recent years, showing that even an established brand can offer a fresh take on a traditional combat system.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its technical depth, elaborate storytelling, and accessible tutorials for newcomers, combined with the innovative Heat system, it ranks among the most respected fighting games of today.

xbox-series__call-of-duty-modern-warfare.teaser: Task Force 141 hunts terrorists armed with missiles; cinematic direction and detailed sound.
xbox-series__call-of-duty-modern-warfare.article:
**Call of Duty: Modern Warfare II** follows up on the series' 2019 reboot, and on Xbox Series X|S it delivers the most significant technical leap of recent years. The campaign follows the elite Task Force 141 unit hunting a terrorist cartel that has seized long-range missiles, alternating highly choreographed action sequences with silent infiltrations using night vision and underwater submarine passages. Infinity Ward committed to cinematic camera direction and detailed sound design, making individual missions feel more like a war thriller than a classic shooter. Weapons react to touch and water more realistically than before, and a new cover and corner-peeking system gives firefights a more tactical pace, appreciated especially by players who prefer a slower, more deliberate approach.

The core of the game, however, remains its multiplayer, which on the new console generation runs at high resolution and with stable frame rates even in large modes like Ground War with vehicles and dozens of players on the map. The maps are designed with an emphasis on verticality and cover, and the weapon system has been reworked with a new Gunsmith attachment system that allows for fine-tuning of every gun, including building custom weapon platforms and sharing favorite loadouts with friends. Also added was the cooperative DMZ mode, an extraction shooter inspired by battle royale titles, where players complete contracts, gather equipment, and try to survive and extract with their loot before rival teams or hostile AI-controlled factions can stop them.

Contemporary reception was mixed—the campaign earned praise for its production values and atmosphere, while part of the community criticized changes to movement controls and the multiplayer economy, especially the need to purchase weapon bundles. Still, the game quickly became one of the most-played titles on Xbox Game Pass and beyond, and it maintained a stable player base for months after release. With hindsight, Modern Warfare II is seen as an important milestone that set the visual and technical direction for the series for several years to come, including a direct sequel a year later and a follow-up Warzone update.

**Why play it:** Despite the mixed reception of the campaign and changes to the multiplayer economy, this is a title that set the visual and technical direction for the series for years to come and ranked among the most-played titles on Game Pass.

xbox-series__call-of-duty-modern-warfare.teaser: Makarov returns with a nuclear threat; more open missions let you choose your approach.
xbox-series__call-of-duty-modern-warfare.article:
**Call of Duty: Modern Warfare III** is a direct sequel to the previous entry, and on Xbox Series X|S it runs on an improved version of the IW 9.0 engine, resulting in denser effects, better environmental lighting, and smoother behavior of enemy crowds and civilians during missions. Sledgehammer Games took over as lead developer and built the campaign around the return of the villain Vladimir Makarov, who threatens the world with nuclear terrorism and chemical weapons stolen from former Soviet stockpiles scattered across Europe. Some missions return to the principle of open operations, where the player chooses the order in which to complete objectives, their approach to the target, and their loadout—a deliberate departure from the strictly linear storytelling of previous series entries.

Multiplayer offers a completely reworked lineup of maps, many of which are remastered from the twelve-year-old Modern Warfare 2 (2009)—a nostalgic move that earned a warm reception from longtime series fans. The weapon system builds on Gunsmith but adds deeper progression, new killstreak sets, and a faster movement pace reminiscent of older entries, including the ability to slide along the ground and climb over obstacles while moving. There's also an expanded Zombies mode, this time conceived as an open extraction world with cooperative tasks, side missions, merchants, and the ability to upgrade equipment for four-player teams trying to safely evacuate with their loot.

Reviews particularly praised the nostalgic maps, technical stability on next-gen consoles, and the fast movement controls, while criticism once again focused on the short and unambitious campaign, which many players completed in a single evening, as well as the repetitive mission structure. Even so, thanks to its extensive multiplayer, popular Zombies mode, and presence on Game Pass, the game retained a large and loyal player base, and it confirmed the annual release cycle as a commercially viable model for the series and its future entries.

**Why play it:** Fans of nostalgic maps and fast movement will appreciate the technically stable presentation, and while the short and unambitious campaign can safely be skipped, the extensive multiplayer and Zombies mode make up for it.

xbox-series__marvel-s-spider-man-remaste.teaser: The best-swinging Spider-Man on the market; civilian worries carry as much weight as combat.
xbox-series__marvel-s-spider-man-remaste.article:
**Marvel's Spider-Man Remastered** arrived on Xbox Series X|S years after its original release for PlayStation, yet it remains one of the best-crafted open-world action-adventures on the market to this day. The player steps into the role of Peter Parker, who as an experienced but weary Spider-Man fights New York's underworld led by the mysterious organization Sinister Six, while also dealing with personal problems in his civilian life and relationships with the people close to him, including a complicated relationship with Aunt May. Swinging through the city using webs is one of the genre's best-executed mechanics—fast, fluid, and carrying a real sense of weight, momentum, and acrobatic freedom while leaping between Manhattan's skyscrapers.

The combat system builds on fluidly chaining strikes, dodges, and improvised use of the environment, somewhat similar to the Batman: Arkham series, but with its own acrobatic identity full of web gadgets and flashy enemy finishing moves. On Xbox Series X|S, the game runs with ray-traced reflections in skyscraper windows, and in performance mode it hits a high frame rate, which comes through strongly during fast combat as well as while flying through a city full of detail and sky reflections. New York is rendered in fine detail, packed with side activities, research stations, pigeon quests, and smaller story vignettes that flesh out side characters and their fates in the New York underworld.

The game was already critically acclaimed at its original release, and even years later it remains among the titles that best define the superhero game genre and set the standard for open-world movement mechanics. On the new console generation it particularly shines through its smoothness, shorter loading times, and visual quality, making it one of the essential stops for any Xbox Series X|S owner interested in action-adventures and stories about superheroes with a human face.

**Why play it:** Its smoothness, shorter loading times, and visual quality on the new generation make it one of the essential stops for any Xbox Series X|S owner interested in superhero action-adventures.

xbox-series__ghostwire-tokyo.teaser: A depopulated Tokyo shrouded in ghostly fog; hand-gesture combat from the creators of The Evil Within.
xbox-series__ghostwire-tokyo.article:
**Ghostwire: Tokyo** places the player in a depopulated Tokyo, whose inhabitants have vanished without a trace after a mysterious masked entity opened a gate to the spirit world and shrouded the entire city in thick, supernatural fog. The main character, Akito, possessed by the spirit of detective KK, fights using supernatural abilities—instead of firearms, he uses elemental energy shaped by hand gestures, giving combat an unusual, almost dance-like fluid rhythm unlike classic action games on the market. Tango Gameworks, the studio also behind The Evil Within series, blends Japanese folklore here with modern action design and open-world exploration full of mysteries and hidden shrines.

The open world is dotted with dozens of yokai inspired by real Japanese legends, ranging from harmless apparitions of faceless schoolgirls to dangerous enemies hidden in side alleys and abandoned buildings. The atmosphere is enhanced by thick fog shrouding unexplored districts, the neon glow of empty streets, rain-soaked sidewalks, and inventive sound design that turns every step through the city into an unsettling yet fascinating experience full of tension and surprise. On Xbox Series X|S, the game arrived a year after its original release for PlayStation and PC, with support for higher resolution and smoother frame rates even in densely fogged areas of the city.

Reviews praised the atmosphere, visual style, and original combat system above all, while criticizing the repetitiveness of side activities in an otherwise imaginatively designed open world full of side content and collectibles. Even so, Ghostwire: Tokyo ranks among the most distinctive action titles of its generation and shows that Japanese mythology and folklore can serve as a full-fledged foundation for a modern open-world game with its own striking tone and atmosphere, unlike anything offered by any competing title.

**Why play it:** The atmosphere, striking visual style, and original combat system drawing on Japanese mythology make up for the repetitive side activities in an otherwise imaginative open world.

xbox-series__metal-hellsinger.teaser: A shooter set to the rhythm of metal; the more precisely you fire on the beat, the higher the damage.
xbox-series__metal-hellsinger.article:
**Metal: Hellsinger** combines a first-person shooter with a rhythm game, and the result is one of the most distinctive titles of the generation on Xbox Series X|S. In a hellish setting, the player controls the Bride, a cursed being seeking revenge on the Red Judge of Hell, fighting hordes of demons to the rhythm of metal tracks composed for the game by respected heavy metal musicians, including singers from famous bands from around the world. A key element is the so-called combo system tied to the musical beat – the more precisely the player shoots in time with the track, the higher the damage multiplier and the louder the song's vocals become, turning the game into an adrenaline-fueled dance with death and music at once, where hearing becomes just as important as sight.

The weapon arsenal is limited, but each piece is designed to work differently in sync with the rhythm – from revolvers and shotguns to crossbows and even fiery boomerangs that return to your hand after hitting a target. The level design draws on Dante's vision of hell divided into several circles, with each level bringing its own visual motif, musical theme, and a distinctive boss with its own accompanying track composed specifically for that stage of the fight. On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly even in intense battles with dozens of enemies on screen at once, which is absolutely crucial – and technically demanding – for maintaining the game's rhythmic precision.

Critics embraced the game enthusiastically, praising in particular its original genre fusion and high-quality soundtrack, which works on its own as a full-fledged metal album released separately from the game on streaming services. Despite its smaller scope and shorter playtime, Metal: Hellsinger became a cult favorite and an inspiration for other rhythm-action games that tried to replicate the fusion of music and shooting with their own twist and musical style.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its original fusion of rhythm and shooting and a soundtrack that works as a full-fledged metal album, it's worth your attention despite the shorter playtime.

xbox-series__gotham-knights.teaser: Batman is dead; the four members of the Batman Family defend Gotham in a co-op RPG.
xbox-series__gotham-knights.article:
**Gotham Knights** takes place in Gotham after Batman's death and puts the player in the role of one of four members of the Batman Family – Nightwing, Red Hood, Batgirl, or Robin – who must learn to protect the city without their mentor, his years of experience, or his strict oversight. WB Games Montréal built on the legacy of the Arkham series but shifted the concept toward an action RPG with two-player co-op, a leveling system, gear, crafting, and specialized skills for each playable character, each with a distinct combat style and personality.

Compared to the Arkham games, the combat system relies more heavily on RPG elements – enemies have levels and resistances that must be overcome with better gear, upgrades, and a more tactical approach to combat, which changes the pacing compared to the fluid combo system of the earlier Rocksteady games. The open Gotham is divided into several districts, and the player travels around it on the Batcycle motorcycle or swings across rooftops with a grappling hook, while the main story follows a clash with the Court of Owls, a secret order of wealthy families that has controlled the city from the shadows for generations.

On Xbox Series X|S the game offers both a performance and a quality mode, though technical issues with performance and lower frame rates plagued it especially in the first weeks after launch, before developers partially fixed them with subsequent patches and updates. Reviews were mixed – praising the story and character design but criticizing the repetitive mission structure and persistent technical shortcomings in the open world. Even so, the game found a loyal fanbase, particularly thanks to two-player co-op and extensive ongoing post-launch content support. The game also features a day-night cycle with changing weather that affects gang behavior and visibility on Gotham's rooftops. Despite its rocky start, the game gradually found its firm place in the Xbox Series X|S library.

**Why play it:** Anyone who appreciates the story, character design, and two-player co-op will overlook the repetitive mission structure and the technical hiccups that plagued Gotham's open world in the first weeks after launch.

xbox-series__deathloop.teaser: A hitman trapped in a time loop; eight targets, one day, from the creators of Dishonored.
xbox-series__deathloop.article:
**Deathloop** casts the player as the hitman Colt, trapped in a time loop on the island of Blackreef, where he must eliminate eight targets in a single day before time resets at midnight and everything repeats exactly from the start, unchanged. Arkane Lyon, the creators of the Dishonored series, put their experience with immersive simulations to good use here – the island is divided into four locations across four times of day, with the targets' behavior, the number of guards, and the available routes all changing depending on when and where the player decides to strike, requiring careful planning, observation, and repeated experimentation with different approaches.

The game combines a first-person shooter with supernatural abilities reminiscent of Dishonored – short-range teleportation, linking enemies together to share damage, or temporarily freezing an entire room of enemies at once. A special twist is the asynchronous multiplayer, in which another player can invade Colt's loop at any time as Julianna, an assassin hired to stop him, turning every playthrough into an unpredictable cat-and-mouse game full of tension and improvisation for both sides.

Deathloop arrived on Xbox Series X|S a year after its timed exclusivity on PlayStation 5, with support for high resolution and smooth framerates even in hectic fights against multiple opponents at once. Reviews praised the game for its inventive level design, dark humor, striking 1960s visual style, and the original way it combined loop mechanics with immersive-sim design and freedom of approach. Deathloop is now considered one of the most original action titles of its generation and proof that Arkane can bring its craft beyond the established world of Dishonored. The visual style draws on 1960s pop art and period interiors, giving Blackreef Island a distinctive retro atmosphere full of colorful contrasts.

**Why play it:** For fans of inventive level design, dark humor, and freedom of approach, it's proof that Arkane can carry its craft beyond the world of Dishonored – with smooth performance on Series X|S to boot.

xbox-series__redfall.teaser: A vampire invasion in Massachusetts; a four-player co-op shooter from Arkane.
xbox-series__redfall.article:
**Redfall** places the player in a fictional coastal town in Massachusetts that has been cut off from the rest of the world after being taken over by vampires created by secret genetic experiments conducted by a local corporation hidden beneath the town's surface. Arkane Austin, the second studio behind the Dishonored and Prey series, bet for the first time on a co-op shooter for up to four players, each controlling one of four characters with unique abilities – ranging from telekinesis to sniping talent to temporary invisibility from enemies and their packs.

The game combines shooting with weapons specially adapted against vampires, such as rifles that fire wooden stakes and lamps emitting ultraviolet radiation, with character abilities and an open world full of side quests, abandoned houses to explore, and vampire nests filled with loot and recordings from missing residents. The atmosphere thrives on the contrast between an idyllic, seemingly peaceful New England town and horror elements such as giant vampire bosses capable of controlling the weather and shrouding the entire region in permanent darkness without any sunlight.

The Xbox Series X|S launch was marred by significant technical problems – low and unstable framerates, a missing split-screen mode, and unbalanced difficulty for solo play, which led to a very cold reception from both critics and players despite the studio's strong reputation and its previous successful titles. Although the developers tried to gradually improve the game with additional updates and fixes, Redfall remains remembered more as a cautionary example of a failed live-service experiment than as a solid entry in Arkane's otherwise strong portfolio. Even though the game later received a substantial update removing paid microtransactions, it never achieved full rehabilitation with critics or the player community.

**Why play it:** Given the persistent technical problems with solo play, it makes more sense to pick this up with two to four players in full co-op – and even then, go in aware that it's one of Arkane's weaker titles.

xbox-series__evil-west.teaser: An alternate Wild West with vampires; pistols and a rifle backed up by an electric gauntlet.
xbox-series__evil-west.article:
**Evil West** is a third-person action game set in an alternate Wild West, where gunslinger Jesse Rentier joins a secret organization of vampire hunters battling a gothic horror spreading across the American prairie in the late nineteenth century, while the government tries to keep the threat under wraps. Flying Wild Hog, the Polish studio known for the Shadow Warrior series, combined a brutal combat system built around pistols and rifles with an electric gauntlet, which the player uses to stun enemies, knock them into environmental traps, and periodically recharge at special generators scattered across the arenas throughout the map.

The game openly embraces the legacy of titles like Devil May Cry or the older God of War games – linear levels, elaborate arenas filled with gradually escalating waves of enemies, and rewarding combinations of ranged and melee attacks, their impact heightened by electric effects, slow-motion charge animations, and flashy finishing moves that quickly dispatch opponents. Visually, the game leans on a stylized, comic-book-inspired take on western aesthetics combined with gothic horror, giving it a distinctive visual identity that sets it apart from more realistic competitors in the genre.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs stably at high resolution, prioritizing smooth action over photorealistic environments and characters in the story. Reviews praised above all its return to straightforward, honestly crafted action without unnecessarily open worlds or microtransactions, which felt refreshing and sincere to players in an era saturated with live-service titles. Evil West thus became a pleasant surprise for old-school action fans craving simple but honest fun without unnecessary complications or detours. Progressing through the game also unlocks new upgrades for the gauntlet and weapons through a simple skill tree that gives the player a constant sense of growing power.

**Why play it:** Old-school fans of straightforward action without open worlds or microtransactions will appreciate the honest craftsmanship, stable performance, and gradually growing skill tree for both gauntlet and weapons.

xbox-series__ghostrunner.teaser: Uncompromising cyberpunk action; one hit means death for either side.
xbox-series__ghostrunner.article:
**Ghostrunner** is a fast-paced first-person action game set in the vertical cyberpunk tower Dharma Tower, the last bastion of humanity after a civilizational catastrophe, ruled from its peak by the tyrannical Keymaster along with her fanatical guards and her own army of machines. The player takes on the role of a cybernetic warrior armed with a katana, whose only defense and attack alike is a single precise strike – one hit means instant death for both enemy and player, making the game an extremely uncompromising yet immensely satisfying real-time action puzzle with no room for error.

One More Level built the game around rapidly repeating short, brutally difficult segments where the player combines parkour, temporary time slowdown, and precisely deflecting projectiles back at enemies, with absolutely minimal room for error or hesitation. The level design fully exploits the tower's verticality – wall-running, double jumps, and ziplines pull the player upward toward a final confrontation with the tower's ruler, while a pulsing electronic soundtrack underscores the pace and synthetic atmosphere of the entire dark cyberpunk world full of neon colors.

On Xbox Series X|S, where the game launched as one of the new generation's launch titles, it benefits above all from lightning-fast loading after frequent deaths and the stable framerate needed for the player's precise, split-second reactions. Reviews praised the adrenaline-fueled feeling of gradually gained mastery and a surprisingly satisfying learning curve despite the game's high difficulty and its occasionally merciless traps. Ghostrunner became a cult title in its genre and received a successful, more expansive sequel two years later. The difficulty is eased by a fast respawn system right at the point of death, so even frequent repetition of difficult passages feels smooth and never comes across as frustrating.

**Why play it:** Anyone who can handle the high difficulty will appreciate the lightning-fast loading after every death, respawning right where you fell, and a satisfying learning curve that keeps the game from ever feeling frustrating.

xbox-series__alan-wake-ii.teaser: A survival horror sequel thirteen years later; two storylines linked by the Dark Place and Bright Falls.
xbox-series__alan-wake-ii.article:
**Alan Wake II** is a survival horror sequel to the cult original, arriving thirteen years later, and on Xbox Series X|S it makes full use of next-generation power for photorealistic environments and elaborate dynamic lighting that is absolutely essential to the atmosphere of the entire game and simply couldn't have been achieved on older hardware. The story unfolds along two parallel lines – FBI agent Saga Anderson investigates a series of ritual murders in the town of Bright Falls, while writer Alan Wake has remained trapped for thirteen years in a dark version of New York called the Dark Place, from which he tries to escape by rewriting his own unfinished story on an old typewriter.

Remedy Entertainment combined tense investigative segments, in which Saga connects clues and builds theories about the perpetrator on an imagined mind-map board, with a classic horror combat system where flashlight beams weaken shadow enemies before a finishing shot from a weapon. Visually, the game blends live-action footage with the game engine so seamlessly that the line between film and game nearly disappears, reinforcing a dark, unsettling atmosphere inspired by American horror, television series, and 1940s noir aesthetics.

Critics received the game as one of the pinnacles of the genre, praising in particular its bold narrative structure, unforgettable musical numbers, and technical execution on the new generation of consoles. Despite more modest commercial success owing to the game's demanding nature and specific tone, Alan Wake II is now regarded as one of the most ambitious horror titles of its generation and has cemented Remedy's reputation as a studio with a distinctive, unmistakable authorial voice. Optional connections to previous Remedy titles, including references to Control, further hint at a shared fictional universe the studio has been building across its games for years.

**Why play it:** For fans of bold storytelling, unforgettable musical numbers, and Remedy's connected universe, it's one of the most ambitious horror titles of its generation, despite its demanding and distinctive tone.

xbox-series__outer-worlds-spacer-s-choic.teaser: A satire on corporate space from the creators of Fallout: New Vegas; choose diplomacy or force.
xbox-series__outer-worlds-spacer-s-choic.article:
**The Outer Worlds: Spacer's Choice Edition** is an enhanced version of the action RPG from Obsidian Entertainment, which in 2019 showed how a satirical corporate space dream could be turned inside out. The player wakes from a hundred years of cryosleep aboard a colonization ship to discover that the entire Halcyon system is controlled by rival megacorporations indifferent to the fate of ordinary people. Planetary exploration, dialogue trees with real consequences, and the option to resolve quests through diplomacy, sabotage, or brute force give the game the signature freedom of choice that Obsidian had already refined with Fallout: New Vegas. A crew of eccentric companions, each carrying their own mini-story and moral dilemma, makes the journey across Halcyon just as much a social experience as an action one.

On Xbox Series X and S, the Spacer's Choice Edition brings reworked lighting, higher resolution, and a more stable frame rate, letting the colorful, almost cartoon-styled environments stand out far better than in the original version. The combat system, combining shooting with tactical time slowdown, remains simple but functional, and the game's main draw — sarcastic dialogue and characterful companions — works just as well as it did at launch. The music and sound design underscore the ironic tone with which the game comments on late-stage capitalism, and even small conversations with side characters often conceal surprisingly sharp social satire.

At launch, the game earned praise mainly for its writing and atmosphere, although critics faulted it for its smaller scope compared to big open-world RPGs. Today that length is viewed more as an advantage — The Outer Worlds can be finished in a reasonable amount of time while still delivering a complete, self-contained story, without the player getting lost in dozens of hours of filler content. On Xbox Series, the remastered edition is the most convenient way to enjoy the game, and for fans of RPGs that emphasize choice and writing, it remains a strong experience even years later.

**Why play it:** The shorter length that critics faulted at launch will now be appreciated by anyone who wants to finish a self-contained story in a reasonable amount of time without dozens of hours of filler content, and the remastered edition is the most convenient way to do it.

xbox-series__fallout-4.teaser: Post-war Boston and the search for a kidnapped child; the S.P.E.C.I.A.L. RPG system and settlement building.
xbox-series__fallout-4.article:
**Fallout 4** brought Bethesda Game Studios' series into a sprawling post-war Boston, where the player, cast as a lone parent, sets out to find a kidnapped child across a parched wasteland full of factions, mutants, and morally ambiguous choices. The game combines open-world exploration with the S.P.E.C.I.A.L. RPG system and extensive crafting and settlement building, letting players build their own bases, manage resources, and defend them against raids. The dialogue system was simplified compared to previous entries, which split fans, but the depth of quests and side stories remained characteristic of the whole series, whether it's a decision between warring factions or the small personal stories of wandering wasteland dwellers.

The next-gen update for Xbox Series X and S from 2023 brought native support for both consoles, including a choice between a performance mode with a higher frame rate and a quality mode with 4K resolution, shorter load times, and a number of minor fixes. The sprawling, densely detailed wasteland now finally runs more smoothly, letting players enjoy the atmosphere of a decaying Massachusetts even years after release, underscored by period radio broadcasts and an unmistakable soundtrack that accompanies the journey across the ruins of pre-war America. The settlement-building system, though initially criticized as an add-on to the main game, has over the years become one of the most engaging ways to spend free time within the Fallout universe.

At its original release in 2015, Fallout 4 became one of the best-selling titles of its generation and defined what a modern post-apocalyptic RPG with base building looks like. Critics praised its freedom and atmosphere, though less so its simplified dialogue writing compared to New Vegas. On Xbox Series, the game today serves as a comfortable entry point into the whole universe, and thanks to a huge amount of expansions (Far Harbor, Nuka-World) it offers dozens of hours of content even to those who already played it before and want to return to the devastated Boston in its smoothest form yet.

**Why play it:** Thanks to a huge amount of expansions like Far Harbor and Nuka-World, it offers dozens of hours of content even to those who want to return to the devastated Boston in its smoothest form to date.

xbox-series__elder-scrolls-v-skyrim.teaser: The fantasy open world that defined the genre; Dovahkiin absorbs the souls of dragons.
xbox-series__elder-scrolls-v-skyrim.article:
**The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim** is a fantasy RPG from Bethesda Game Studios that, since its 2011 release, has become synonymous with an endlessly expandable open world. The player takes on the role of the Dovahkiin, a prophesied hero capable of absorbing dragon souls and using powerful Shouts, while traveling through the snowy province of Skyrim full of factions, caves, cities, and side stories that together add up to hundreds of hours of content. The free character-development system without fixed classes allows players to combine melee combat, magic, and thieving skills as they please, gradually crafting a hero to their own liking without the risk of choosing wrong.

The Anniversary Edition, which arrived on Xbox Series X and S in 2021, combines the base game with all its expansions (Dawnguard, Hearthfire, Dragonborn) and dozens of previously paid and new creation-club contents. On the new generation of consoles, the game runs in native 4K resolution with improved lighting and smoother performance, so the snowy mountain peaks and dungeon depths look significantly better than on Xbox One. Jeremy Soule's atmospheric soundtrack remains one of the most recognizable in the genre, and together with the sound of wind and wolves it completes the feeling of a lonely journey through a wilderness full of dragon shrines and ancient ruins. The faction quest lines, from the Dark Brotherhood to the Companions, also offer entirely different playstyles and tones of storytelling within a single world.

Skyrim has probably had more re-releases than any other game during its existence, and its influence on the open-world RPG genre is hard to overstate — it set the bar for freedom of exploration, the modding community, and the longevity of a single title. Even nearly fifteen years after the original, it remains a game on Xbox Series that players keep coming back to, whether out of nostalgia, for the additional content, or simply because it offers so many paths to walk.

**Why play it:** Almost fifteen years after release, it still offers so many paths to freedom of exploration, modding, and length of play that players keep coming back to it, whether out of nostalgia, new content, or the urge to lose themselves once again in their own adventure.

xbox-series__disco-elysium-final-cut.teaser: A detective RPG without combat; progress is driven by dialogue and bickering inner voices.
xbox-series__disco-elysium-final-cut.article:
**Disco Elysium: The Final Cut** is a detective RPG from the Estonian studio ZA/UM that, instead of sword-and-magic combat, focuses entirely on dialogue, thought, and the inner voices of its protagonist. The player wakes up as an amnesiac detective in the decaying port city of Revachol and must solve a murder, while his actions are shaped by a colorful palette of personality traits that literally converse with him and comment on the world around him. There is no traditional combat system — all progress happens through text-based skill checks and conversations, and even a single conversation can fundamentally change the direction of the entire investigation.

The Final Cut, which arrived on Xbox Series X and S in 2021, added full voice acting for nearly all characters, new quest lines, and political factions, opening the text-heavy game even further to players who might otherwise be intimidated by the amount of reading. A visual style reminiscent of oil paintings and melancholic, jazz-tinged music round out the depressing yet fascinating atmosphere of a crumbling city that still bears the scars of a long-lost revolution. On top of that, the detective character is capable of sabotaging himself through his own vices, giving the game an unexpectedly comic yet also tragic dimension, and the decision whether he tries to redeem himself or sinks further into self-destruction is one of the strongest moments in the whole story.

Upon release, Disco Elysium received exceptionally positive reception and was repeatedly called one of the best-written RPGs, thanks to the depth of its writing, dark humor, and the courage to tackle political themes without oversimplifying them. Its influence can be seen in a number of later narrative RPGs that attempt to imitate its system of inner voices. On Xbox Series, the game remains just as powerful an experience as it was on release — it's a title that proves genuinely good writing can replace even the most elaborate combat mechanics.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for an RPG where writing and dialogue matter more than combat will find in Disco Elysium one of the best-written titles in the genre, period.

xbox-series__as-dusk-falls.teaser: An interactive drama about a fateful motel robbery, playable with up to eight people.
xbox-series__as-dusk-falls.article:
**As Dusk Falls** is an interactive narrative adventure from INTERIOR/NIGHT that tells the branching story of two families bound together by a fateful robbery at a motel in the Arizona desert. The player moves through events spanning thirty years and decides the fates of the characters through quick decisions that shape relationships, trust, and tragedies across generations. The game supports co-op play for up to eight people via controllers on a mobile phone, making it an ideal title for shared evenings with family or friends, where the group must agree on a single joint decision or let the choice be decided by a vote.

Visually, the game relies on an unusual style resembling illustrated comic-book panels with subtle animation, which on Xbox Series X and S, where the game launched as a console exclusive in 2022, runs smoothly and without technical hitches. This approach allowed the team to focus all its attention on writing and voice performances, while the emotive music and sensitively recorded voices give the story cinematic weight despite the stylized visuals. At critical moments the characters change expressions and gestures in a way that resembles an animated series more than a classic video game, and the transitions between the different timelines of the story help maintain tension despite its nonlinear structure.

Critics particularly praised the courage to tell a civilian drama without the action elements typical of the genre, and the elaborate decision-making system where small choices gradually build into major consequences for entire families' fates. As Dusk Falls thus took its place alongside titles like Detroit: Become Human or the games of Quantic Dream, even though it is a more intimate, family-focused story. On Xbox Series it remains to this day a showcase of how powerfully interactive storytelling can work when it focuses on ordinary people in an extraordinary situation.

**Why play it:** For players who crave an intimate family drama instead of action, As Dusk Falls offers a well-crafted decision-making system whose consequences stretch across generations.

xbox-series__alan-wake-2.teaser: A return after 13 years; a survival horror blending light and gunplay with two interwoven storylines.
xbox-series__alan-wake-2.article:
**Alan Wake 2** is a narrative-driven survival horror from the Finnish studio Remedy Entertainment, which after thirteen years returned to the character of a writer trapped in a dark alternate reality called the Dark Place. The player alternates between two storylines — FBI detective Saga Anderson, investigating ritual murders in the town of Bright Falls, and Alan Wake himself, who in a horror-tinged version of New York tries to finish writing the story that would let him escape. Combat against the mysterious darkness combines light and gunplay, but the main emphasis lies on atmosphere, puzzles, and psychological tension, with the player gradually piecing together the so-called Mind Place, connecting clues from both storylines.

On Xbox Series X and S, where the game launched directly in 2023 with no version for the previous generation, Remedy makes full use of the new console's power — dense lighting, cinematic transitions between live-action sequences and gameplay, and elaborate sound design that turns a walk through a dark forest into an unpleasant experience in the best sense of the word. The music and live musical numbers that regularly interrupt the game are among the most striking moments of the entire generation of games and give the otherwise anxious game unexpectedly cathartic peaks. The chapters set in the New York district called the Dark Place also change the rules of reality according to what Alan is writing at that moment, setting the game apart from a classic survival horror.

Alan Wake 2 was showered with praise on release for the courage with which it combines survival horror with an almost television-like narrative structure and metafictional layers referencing Remedy's earlier games as well as Control. The game's influence on the psychological horror genre is noticeable in how it shows that even a story-heavy, slow-paced game can succeed commercially. On Xbox Series it remains to this day one of the technically most impressive showcases of what the new generation of consoles can do, and at the same time a reminder that narrative courage pays off in the horror genre.

**Why play it:** Fans of psychological horror and lovers of layered storytelling alike will be rewarded by Alan Wake 2, one of the technically most impressive and boldest games of the generation.

xbox-series__life-is-strange-true-colors.teaser: An adventure about reading emotions as colored auras; for the first time released whole, without episodes.
xbox-series__life-is-strange-true-colors.article:
**Life is Strange: True Colors** is a narrative adventure from Deck Nine, in which the player, as Alex Chen, possesses an empathic ability to literally see and feel other people's emotions as colored auras. After moving to the mountain town of Haven Springs following the mysterious death of her brother, Alex sets out on an investigation that gradually uncovers dark secrets hidden beneath the surface of a seemingly idyllic community. Unlike previous entries in the series, this game was released in full, without an episodic structure, allowing for smoother storytelling and a more focused dramatic arc for the whole story.

On Xbox Series X and S, where the game launched in 2021, it benefits from higher resolution and stable performance, letting the detailed facial animations and subtle expressions that narrative games of this kind rely on truly shine. Alex's emotional ability is also reflected in the gameplay — the player can amplify other characters' emotions or use them to resolve conflicts, giving what is otherwise a classic adventure a clear gameplay mechanic and allowing the player to actively intervene in the fates of side characters instead of merely observing their stories. The setting of a mountain town with a brewery that forms the economic heart of the community also serves as a closed stage where the past of all its inhabitants and their connection to the tragedy that struck the community is gradually revealed.

Critics praised above all the strong voice performances and the sensitive treatment of themes such as grief, community solidarity, and hidden violence, even though some players missed the tension typical of previous entries in the series. True Colors confirmed that Deck Nine, after taking over the series from Dontnod, can preserve its emotional core and offer a full, self-contained continuation without losing the distinctive tone of the previous entries. On Xbox Series it is one of the most accessible entry points into the series for players looking for an emotionally driven story rather than action.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for an emotionally driven story rather than action will find True Colors one of the most accessible and emotionally powerful entry points into the Life is Strange series.

xbox-series__forgotten-city.teaser: A time loop in ancient Rome, grown out of a Skyrim mod. No one is allowed to sin.
xbox-series__forgotten-city.article:
**The Forgotten City** is a mystery-laced adventure from Modern Storyteller that grew out of a concept originally created as a mod for Skyrim and later evolved into a standalone game. The player is drawn into an ancient Roman city trapped in a loop, governed by a cruel golden rule — if a single inhabitant commits a sin, the whole city is cursed and everyone perishes. Through time travel, the player must untangle a complicated web of motives, alliances, and lies among the city's earlier inhabitants in order to break the curse, all without getting stuck in the loop forever, with each new pass through the loop bringing new information that can be used in earlier stages of the story.

On Xbox Series X and S, where the standalone version of the game launched in 2021, it runs smoothly and clearly, which is essential for a genre built on dialogue and logically connecting clues. The system of repeatedly living through the same stretch of time with gradually growing knowledge recalls detective games like Outer Wilds, but with a markedly more grounded, historical framework and an emphasis on moral dilemmas without a clearly correct answer. The characters also only remember what happened during the current run of the loop, so the player must apply their findings repeatedly and with a sense of timing, while a peaceful resolution to conflicts is almost always possible if the player finds the right words.

The game was praised on release for its inventive use of the time loop and writing unafraid of philosophical questions about guilt, justice, and free will, despite having been made on a relatively modest budget. Its success proved that even a smaller studio can build an entire title around a single ingenious mechanism and still offer a depth comparable to much more expensive productions. On Xbox Series it is a great choice for players who love puzzles built on logic and story rather than reflexes.

**Why play it:** Fans of logic-based puzzles built on story and philosophical questions will appreciate how The Forgotten City wrings from a single ingenious idea a depth comparable to far more expensive games.

xbox-series__tales-of-arise.teaser: A JRPG about an enslaved planet; real-time combat without the tedious menus of earlier entries.
xbox-series__tales-of-arise.article:
**Tales of Arise** is a JRPG from Bandai Namco Studios and the newest major entry in the long-running Tales of series, telling the story of the enslaved planet Dahna and its inhabitants, oppressed by rulers from the neighboring world of Rena. The player takes on the roles of two main heroes — a nameless man in a mask and the rebel Shionne — who fight together to free their people. The combat system combines fluid real-time action with switching between characters and their unique abilities called Artes, giving battles fast pacing and tactical depth without burdening the player with the excess of menus and waiting queues typical of earlier entries in the series.

On Xbox Series X and S, where the game launched in 2021, it runs at high resolution and a stable frame rate, letting the new visual style, reminiscent of painted canvases, truly shine — the series has abandoned its traditional anime look in favor of softer, more painterly colors. The orchestral and vocal tracks accompanying key story moments are among the game's strongest elements, heightening the emotional impact of the relationship between the main characters, while exploring the more open areas rewards players with side stories and materials for upgrading their gear. A cooking system that lets characters prepare meals with temporary bonuses adds a pleasantly relaxed dimension even to ordinary travel across the land, as do the bonding conversations at the group's camp, which deepen the ties between the individual heroes.

Tales of Arise received some of the best reviews in the series' history on release and was called by many the best entry since Tales of Vesperia. Critics praised the visual redesign, the well-crafted characters, and the combat, which finally shed the outdated mechanics of previous entries, as well as an emotive story unafraid to tackle themes of oppression and prejudice. On Xbox Series it is an ideal entry point into the series for new players and a reward for longtime fans of the JRPG genre alike.

**Why play it:** For both newcomers and longtime JRPG fans, Tales of Arise is an ideal entry point thanks to its reworked combat, strong characters, and some of the best reviews in the series' history.

xbox-series__dragon-s-dogma-2.teaser: Action RPG with Pawns sharing experience between players. Climbing monsters instead of combos.
xbox-series__dragon-s-dogma-2.article:
**Dragon's Dogma 2** is an action RPG from Capcom and a direct sequel to the cult classic from 2012, expanding on the concept of the Pawn — an AI-controlled companion who exchanges gathered knowledge and advice between different players' games. The player, in the role of the Arisen, journeys through a vast fantasy world, forges a pact with a dragon, and battles giant monsters in a way that resembles physical interaction — climbing onto beasts — more than the classic turn-based or combo systems of other RPGs. Nighttime travel through a landscape full of ghouls and dangerous werewolves adds tension to exploration that you barely feel during the day.

On Xbox Series X and S, where the game launched simultaneously with other platforms in 2024, it benefits from the advanced RE Engine, which makes the open world look detailed and dynamic, though even on the new generation of consoles the game occasionally takes a toll on frame rate in busy cities. The music and sound design emphasize a sense of danger and majesty when encountering large enemies, one of the defining traits of the whole series. Nine distinct vocations, from the classic Fighter to the mysterious Mystic Archer, also let you completely transform your playstyle with a single visit to the right guild.

Dragon's Dogma 2 was received on release as a faithful yet modernized sequel that retained the series' distinctive, mildly inconvenient approach to quests and travel, without free fast travel. Fans of the first game appreciated the return of the Pawn system and the greater freedom in character building through vocations, though there was also discussion about microtransactions offering minor convenience items, as well as technical dips in large cities. On Xbox Series, it's one of the most distinctive action RPGs of the generation, unafraid to go against the grain of modern genre convenience.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for an action RPG unafraid to go against the grain of modern genre convenience will appreciate Dragon's Dogma 2's return of the Pawn system and its distinctive freedom in character building.

xbox-series__kena-bridge-of-spirits.teaser: Adventure from animated-film makers; cute Rot helpers solve puzzles.
xbox-series__kena-bridge-of-spirits.article:
**Kena: Bridge of Spirits** is an action-adventure from the small studio Ember Lab, which previously worked mainly on animated films — something very evident in the game's visual side. The player takes on the role of young spirit guide Kena, whose task is to help trapped souls find peace and overcome their unresolved ties to the world of the living, while traveling through a stylized forest environment inspired by Southeast Asia. The combat system combines nimble staff-based fighting with an army of cute helpers called Rot, who help solve environmental puzzles and are gradually collected across the map as a reward for careful exploration.

On Xbox Series X and S, where the game arrived in 2022 after originally launching exclusively for PlayStation and PC, it stands out with elaborate graphics in richly fairy-tale colors and smooth animation that holds its own against productions from much larger studios. The orchestral music accompanying key moments amplifies the emotional theme of coming to terms with loss and death that runs through the whole story, while each resolved chapter transforms the corrupted environment back into colorful, blooming nature, visually underscoring the central theme of making peace with the past and letting go of old grievances.

Kena was praised on its original release especially for its visual presentation and the adorable Rot creatures, although some of the boss fights turned out to be surprisingly demanding parts of an otherwise more family-friendly game. With this title, Ember Lab earned comparisons to productions from film animation studios transposed into the gaming medium, even though it was their very first game project. On Xbox Series, Kena is a pleasant, visually captivating trip for players of all ages who will appreciate a story about coming to terms with the loss of loved ones and the gentle yet emotionally honest way the game tells it without unnecessary pathos.

**Why play it:** Visually captivating Kena is a great choice for players of all ages who will appreciate a sensitive story about coming to terms with loss, even though it comes with surprisingly demanding boss fights.

xbox-series__alan-wake-remastered.teaser: Remake of the pioneering 2010 thriller about fighting with light and darkness.
xbox-series__alan-wake-remastered.article:
**Alan Wake Remastered** is a remake of the psychological thriller from studio Remedy Entertainment, originally released in 2010, which tells the story of a writer suffering from creative block and insomnia who retreats with his wife to the mountain town of Bright Falls. After his wife disappears, Alan discovers he has found himself in the middle of a terrifying scenario he unknowingly wrote himself, and must fight beings possessed by darkness using a combination of flashlight and gunfire — a mechanic that was innovative on original release and still defines the game's identity and its distinctive approach to horror.

On Xbox Series X and S, where the remaster launched in 2021, the game received improved textures, reworked character models, and fully rebuilt lighting, making the dense forests and foggy atmosphere of Bright Falls stand out far better than on the original Xbox 360. The episodic structure with recaps and radio and TV segments has been preserved and still feels like a tribute to the television series that inspired the game, including references to Twin Peaks. Fighting shadows illuminated by a flashlight beam before you can even shoot them remains one of the most imitated horror ideas of its time.

Alan Wake was praised on its first release for its atmosphere, gripping chapter-based storytelling, and unforgettable soundtrack, even though it didn't commercially succeed the way Remedy had hoped. Only with time, and thanks to the remaster and the sequel Alan Wake 2, did the game become a cult favorite and an integral part of the so-called Remedy Connected Universe, also linked to the game Control, with many hints and details making sense only in hindsight. On Xbox Series, it's an ideal way to enjoy the original story before diving into the much larger sequel, and to get to know the character who shaped Remedy's entire distinctive storytelling style.

**Why play it:** Before diving into the much larger sequel, it's worth getting to know the story that shaped Remedy's distinctive storytelling style — Alan Wake Remastered is the ideal way to do it.

xbox-series__f1-24.teaser: Official F1 simulation with reworked handling and the story mode Braking Point.
xbox-series__f1-24.article:
**F1 24** continues the long tradition of official Formula 1 simulators from studio Codemasters, which has released a new installment every season since EA Sports took over the brand in 2021. On Xbox Series X/S, the game offers a reworked driving model, called by the developers dynamic handling, which attempts to more faithfully reflect the behavior of current single-seaters with downforce generated by the ground-effect, including a more sensitive response to suspension, brake, and weight-distribution settings. Alongside the classic Grand Prix mode, time trials, and online races, the story mode Braking Point returns, this time in its third episode, which through cinematic cutscenes and fictional characters tells a dramatic paddock story linked to the real drivers of the starting grid.

The career mode has been expanded with testing programs, daily scenarios, and deeper car development across the season, while the MyTeam mode lets you run your own team from scratch, including negotiating with sponsors and hiring staff. On Series X/S the game benefits from fast loading thanks to Smart Delivery and stable frame rates even in large starting grids, something that wasn't always a given on previous console generations. A range of assist features, from braking to shifting, makes the game accessible even to players without simulator experience, while experienced players can turn everything off and rely purely on their own feel for the track. Engine sound design and grandstand atmosphere add appropriate intensity to the races, especially in the rain or at dusk on tracks like Suzuka or Silverstone.

The F1 series has long managed to balance accessibility for casual players with depth for simulation enthusiasts, and F1 24 continues along this proven path more through evolution than revolution. For fans of the series, it's a reliable yearly addition, best appreciated by those who also follow real Formula 1 and want to experience the season from the cockpit's point of view, whether in a short weekend race or a multi-season career.

**Why play it:** For fans who also follow real Formula 1, F1 24 offers a reliable season from the cockpit's point of view, whether in a short weekend race or a multi-season career.

xbox-series__nhl-24.teaser: Hockey on Frostbite; boarding battles are now driven by player physics, not scripts.
xbox-series__nhl-24.article:
**NHL 24** is a continuation of EA Sports' long-running hockey series, which on Xbox Series X/S builds on the Frostbite engine and next-gen performance for smoother and faster matches. The game introduced a reworked boarding-battle system and improved puck physics, making the action around the net and in the corners of the rink feel less scripted and more dependent on the actual position, speed, and orientation of the players. The special X-Factor abilities, which give star players significant in-game bonuses, return in this installment as well and influence roster-building strategy. The Be A Pro career mode continues to follow one hockey player's journey from the draft to the NHL, while World of Chel remains a popular choice for players who want to build their own character in online 3-on-3 matches as well as classic games.

The graphics on the new console generation brought more detailed player models, more faithful arena lighting, and smoother transition animations between faceoffs, passes, and shots, including finer details of equipment and jerseys of individual NHL clubs. The sound design with a roaring crowd and arena announcements simulates the match atmosphere well, especially during the playoffs, when the stands react to every scoring chance. The controls remain accessible to newcomers but offer enough depth for players who want to master the nuances of forechecking, power plays, and precise breakaway finishing. Hockey Ultimate Team, that is collecting cards of players and legends to build your own lineup, remains the most-played online mode of the series in NHL 24 and regularly receives new seasonal content waves.

The NHL series' annual cycle means that changes between individual installments tend to be gradual rather than fundamental, and this holds true for NHL 24 as well. Still, it's one of the few truly faithful hockey simulations available on consoles, and for ice hockey fans it remains the natural choice for enjoying the season off the ice too, whether in standalone matches, the long-term Franchise mode, or an online league with friends.

**Why play it:** For ice hockey fans, NHL 24 remains one of the few truly faithful hockey simulations on consoles, whether in standalone matches, career mode, or an online league with friends.

xbox-series__madden-nfl-25.teaser: American football with the FieldSENSE system for more realistic line battles.
xbox-series__madden-nfl-25.article:
**Madden NFL 25** brought a more pronounced technological leap to Xbox Series X/S thanks to the FieldSENSE animation system, further improved since previous years, meant to deliver more realistic battles on the line of scrimmage, more accurate tackle physics, and more faithful passes between quarterback and receivers. The game emphasizes tactical depth in offensive and defensive formations, letting players choose from an extensive library of playbooks inspired by real NFL teams. The Franchise career mode lets you manage a team for several seasons ahead, from the draft through training and player development to contract negotiations and the salary cap, while the Superstar mode offers a story-driven journey of one player from college football to winning the Super Bowl, with decisions affecting relationships with teammates and coaches and gradually building personal reputation in the league.

On the new console generation, Madden NFL 25 benefits from faster loading and steadier performance even with a fully packed stadium, where crowds, pyrotechnics during team entrances, and dynamic weather add appropriate atmosphere to matches. The control scheme remains traditionally complex, with hundreds of possible passing and running plays as well as sophisticated defensive signaling, making the game more of a simulation for sports fans than a lighthearted arcade experience. The online Ultimate Team mode offers collecting player cards and building your own team for matches against other players around the world.

The Madden series has long been the only official NFL video game license, so this installment too serves primarily as an annual update for loyal fans of American football. For those who follow the league regularly, Madden NFL 25 offers the most complete season simulation available on current-generation consoles, including licensed stadiums, jerseys, current team rosters, and commentator voices accompanying every match.

**Why play it:** Anyone who regularly follows the NFL will find in Madden NFL 25 the most complete season simulation available on the current console generation, including licensed stadiums and current rosters.

xbox-series__nba-2k25.teaser: The most elaborate basketball simulation; MyCareer and collecting legends in MyTeam.
xbox-series__nba-2k25.article:
**NBA 2K25** continues the tradition of the most elaborate basketball simulation on the market and on Xbox Series X/S makes full use of the console's power for detailed player models and smooth movement animations across the court. The game introduced an improved dribbling and post-play system that attempts to better reflect physical clashes between players and offer more faithful controller feedback on both offense and defense. The MyCareer career mode again follows your own player from rookie to league star, with its own storyline and decisions made off the court, while MyTeam lets you collect cards of legends and current NBA stars and build them into your dream team for online matches. The MyNBA mode offers in-depth management of the entire league, including trades, the draft, and franchise development many seasons into the future, letting the player act as both general manager and club owner, including decisions about relocating a franchise to another city or building a new arena.

The game presentation, with commentary, halftime shows, and finely modeled arenas, gives the series a cinematic feel that has long set it apart from the competition. On the new console generation, the details in jersey textures, sweat on players' skin, and lighting effects on the court are especially noticeable, together creating a convincing image of an NBA television broadcast, complemented by faithful dance teams and mascots of individual clubs as well as realistically lit arena interiors during evening games, where even minor imperfections in the floor and lighting are reflected.

The series' annual cycle also brings criticism aimed at microtransactions in modes like MyTeam, something that has accompanied the series for a long time and remains the most common complaint about this installment too. Even so, NBA 2K25 remains the reference choice for basketball fans on consoles, because no other game offers a comparable depth of simulation of an NBA season, its characters, and the personalities around the basketball hoop.

**Why play it:** Despite long-standing criticism of microtransactions in the MyTeam mode, NBA 2K25 remains the reference choice for basketball fans thanks to its unmatched depth of NBA season simulation.

xbox-series__ea-sports-fc-25.teaser: Football after the split from FIFA; the HyperMotionV engine and the new fast-paced Rush mode.
xbox-series__ea-sports-fc-25.article:
**EA Sports FC 25** is the second installment of the football series that took over the baton from the long-running FIFA brand after EA and the international football federation parted ways in 2023, and on Xbox Series X/S it builds on the HyperMotionV engine, which uses footage from real matches to generate more faithful animations of movement, ball duels, dribbling, and passing between players on the pitch. New to this installment is the Rush mode, a faster variant of small-sided football for fewer players on the pitch, aiming to offer a more fun and accessible alternative to traditional eleven-a-side matches. The career mode continues to let you manage a club and an individual player across seasons, with a reworked system of tactics, individual on-field roles, and a more precise chemistry model between teammates, while Ultimate Team remains the series' most-played online mode, collecting cards and building a dream team from stars of present and past football.

On the new console generation, the smoothness of animations and detailed depiction of stadiums and licensed teams stand out especially, including faithful jerseys, crests, and player faces at leading European and world leagues. The sound design with commentary and grandstand atmosphere, fan chants, and cheers helps convey the feeling of watching a real match live from the stadium, whether it's a domestic league fixture or a major European cup match.

EA Sports FC 25 continues the series' established standard as the most widespread football simulation on consoles, though like previous installments it faces criticism regarding microtransactions in Ultimate Team and the balance of online matches. Still, for football fans it remains the natural choice thanks to the scope of its licenses, the wide range of game modes, and regular seasonal updates to rosters, transfers, and individual player form based on real events on the pitches of Europe and around the world.

**Why play it:** Thanks to the scope of its licenses and regular roster updates, EA Sports FC 25 remains the natural choice for football fans, despite repeated criticism of microtransactions in Ultimate Team.

xbox-series__wwe-2k24.teaser: Wrestling for WrestleMania's 40th anniversary with an expanded historical Showcase mode.
xbox-series__wwe-2k24.article:
**WWE 2K24** is the current entry in Visual Concepts' wrestling series, offering on Xbox Series X/S an extensive selection of match types, from classic one-on-one bouts to multiplayer brawls in cages, on ladders, through tables, or in extreme conditions with foreign objects like chairs and hammers. To mark the fortieth anniversary, the game expanded the legendary Showcase mode, which uses archival footage and recreations of famous WrestleMania matches to guide players through WWE history, and added new modes such as Bloodlines, dedicated to the legendary Anoa'i wrestling family. The MyGM editor lets you run your own show, build match cards, sign wrestlers, and compete with other general managers for ratings, while MyRise offers a story-driven career for your own wrestler, from amateur training through smaller arenas to main-event stardom and championship gold.

On the new generation of consoles, the game benefits from more detailed wrestler models and smoother animations during matches, most noticeable in flashy finishers and interactions with the ring, ladders, or the crowd around ringside. The extensive roster includes both current WWE stars and legends from past decades across the promotion's history, and the expansive Creation Suite lets you design custom wrestlers, arenas, outfits, and entire shows, then share them with the wider community of players.

After some rockier entries at the end of the last decade, the WWE 2K series has returned to higher production quality in recent years, and WWE 2K24 confirms that trend with more polished animations, a more stable technical performance, and broader content than earlier installments. For wrestling fans, it's the most comprehensive show simulation WWE currently offers, with enough content for many long hours of play and a faithful presentation of the atmosphere of major pay-per-view events.

**Why play it:** Wrestling fans will find in WWE 2K24 the most comprehensive show simulation available, with more polished animations and a faithful atmosphere of major pay-per-view events.

xbox-series__pga-tour-2k23.teaser: Golf with the first official PGA Tour license and famous courses like TPC Sawgrass.
xbox-series__pga-tour-2k23.article:
**PGA Tour 2K23** is a golf simulation from HB Studios that, on Xbox Series X/S, brought the series its first official PGA Tour license along with the likenesses and names of real professional golfers, including famous courses like TPC Sawgrass. The game builds on the swing-control system proven in earlier entries of the series that grew out of the former The Golf Club brand, combining precision with a degree of tolerance for players still learning golf mechanics. The MyPLAYER career mode lets you create your own golfer, upgrade their equipment and sponsorship deals, and gradually climb the tournament rankings, while a sophisticated course editor gives the community the ability to design and share their own golf courses — of which players have created thousands over the series' history, from faithful replicas to fantastical layouts.

On the new generation of consoles, what stands out most are the finely modeled courses with realistic lighting, terrain undulation, and weather conditions that affect ball flight and green behavior just as in reality. A sound design with hushed commentary and the calm atmosphere of golf tournaments does a good job of evoking the feel of watching a real contest on the greens, complemented by more lighthearted side modes beyond classic golf, such as quick tournaments with modified rules or accuracy-driving challenges.

Under the PGA Tour banner, the 2K golf series has gradually established itself as one of the few serious golf simulations on current-generation consoles, where competition among golf titles has remained limited for a long time. For golf fans, PGA Tour 2K23 offers a solid combination of realism and accessibility, though the game will appeal mainly to those with a close relationship to the sport who also want to try designing their own courses or following professional PGA Tour tournaments from the player's own perspective.

**Why play it:** Players with a close relationship to golf will appreciate PGA Tour 2K23's solid combination of realism and accessibility, plus the ability to design their own courses, in one of the few serious golf simulations on current-generation consoles.

xbox-series__test-drive-unlimited-solar-.teaser: The open-world driving series returns after ten years, set in Hong Kong with social MMO elements.
xbox-series__test-drive-unlimited-solar-.article:
**Test Drive Unlimited Solar Crown** marks the return of the open-world car series after more than ten years away, offering on Xbox Series X/S a sprawling open world inspired by the island of Hong Kong, published under the Nacon label. The game blends racing with social-simulation elements in an MMO style, where players encounter other drivers on the roads, trade cars on a virtual marketplace, and build their reputation within two rival factions, Sharp and Street, each representing a different strain of the island's car culture. The car roster spans a wide range of licensed vehicles from sports cars to luxury sedans and off-roaders, all of which can be customized, tuned, and upgraded in the garage as you like, including visual paint and bodywork changes as well as mechanical parts affecting performance.

The open world, split between day and night versions of the island, offers both city circuits full of traffic and winding mountain roads and coastal highways, and on the new generation of consoles the game aims to draw on a detailed environment and dynamic weather that affects grip on both wet and dry roads. Social features like club activities, shared challenges, and group convoys are meant to keep players coming back long after finishing the main racing series and the initial excitement over new content has worn off.

The return of the Test Drive Unlimited brand was awaited with high hopes, since the original entries from the last decade helped define the genre of open-world racing games even before the arrival of Forza Horizon. Solar Crown therefore faces comparisons with both its own legacy and today's competition, its ambition being to return to the series' original philosophy of free-roaming road trips alongside other players, building your own car collection, and gradually climbing the virtual hierarchy of the island's car subculture.

**Why play it:** Anyone who remembers the original Test Drive Unlimited games will appreciate Solar Crown's attempt to return to free-roaming road trips and collecting cars, even as it faces tough comparisons with today's competition.

xbox-series__motogp-24.teaser: The official motorcycle racing simulation with demanding tire physics and cornering lean angles.
xbox-series__motogp-24.article:
**MotoGP 24** is the current entry in the official motorcycle racing simulation from the Italian studio Milestone, which has long devoted itself to the MotoGP series while also developing the motocross series MXGP and the road-racing series Ride, so it draws on a wealth of accumulated experience with the genre of motorcycle simulations and shares it across its different brands. On Xbox Series X/S it offers a complete licensed MotoGP season including riders, teams, tracks, and the supporting Moto2, Moto3, and electric MotoE classes. The game prides itself on a demanding physics model of riding, in which players must watch tire temperature, tire wear, and the motorcycle's stability while leaning through corners, making it more of a simulation for motorsport fans than a lightweight arcade racer. The career mode takes players from the lower classes through their own team all the way to the premier MotoGP class itself, with the option to negotiate sponsorship deals and upgrade the motorcycle between races throughout the season.

On the new generation of consoles, what stands out most is the smoothness of rider and motorcycle animations and the detailed rendering of the circuits, including variable weather that significantly affects riding style, tire choice, and pit-stop strategy. The sound design of roaring engines and gear shifts underscores the intensity of races on circuits like Mugello, Assen, or Phillip Island, where even a small mistake in a lean angle or late braking before a corner means a crash and the loss of precious seconds.

The series' annual release cycle means individual entries tend to differ more in details and updated rider rosters than in major new features, and MotoGP 24 is no exception in this regard. For motorcycle racing fans, though, it remains the most complete official simulation of the MotoGP season available on current-generation consoles, including the chance to live through an entire season from testing through practice sessions all the way to the championship's grand finale.

**Why play it:** Motorcycle racing fans will find in MotoGP 24 the most complete official simulation of the MotoGP season on current-generation consoles, from testing all the way to the championship's grand finale.

xbox-series__mlb-show-24.teaser: A baseball simulation that arrived on Xbox after years of PlayStation exclusivity.
xbox-series__mlb-show-24.article:
**MLB The Show 24** is a baseball simulation developed by San Diego Studio that, since 2021, has also made its way to Xbox consoles after years of exclusivity on PlayStation platforms. On Xbox Series X/S it offers a complete Major League Baseball license including all teams, stadiums, and players, with a sophisticated batting and pitching system that demands precise button timing, reading the type of pitch thrown, its spin, and judging its trajectory over home plate. The Road to the Show career mode follows your own player from the draft through the minor leagues and a gradual rise to major-league stardom, while March to October offers a sped-up simulation of an entire season with an emphasis on key games, decisive moments, and the fight for a playoff spot. The popular Diamond Dynasty mode, meanwhile, is built around collecting cards of players and legends from across the league's history and assembling them into a dream team for online matches against other players.

On the new generation of consoles, the game can rely on smooth player animations and finely rendered stadiums that faithfully recreate the atmosphere of real MLB games, including changing lighting during evening games and crowd reactions to key hits and tense moments with two outs and the bases loaded. The commentary and crowd sound do a good job of conveying the atmosphere of an entire season, from spring training through the long regular season to the tense playoff series and the World Series finale.
