The series' move to multiplatform releases has allowed MLB The Show 24 to reach players who previously had no access to a baseball simulation on consoles. For sports fans, it's the most polished baseball game available today, now accessible beyond Sony platforms too, with support for cross-generation save progression and regular roster updates that reflect real events during the season.

**Why play it:** Thanks to the series' move to multiplatform releases, MLB The Show 24 is the most polished baseball game available today, now accessible beyond Sony platforms too, with support for cross-generation save progression.

xbox-series__farming-simulator-22.teaser: A farming simulation with seasons that, for the first time, affect crop growth and snow.
xbox-series__farming-simulator-22.article:
**Farming Simulator 22** is the current major entry in the farming simulation series from the Austrian studio Giants Software, offering on Xbox Series X/S expansive open environments with changing seasons that, for the first time in the series' history, affect crop growth, snow on the fields, and farm work throughout the entire calendar year. The game covers the complete farming cycle, from plowing, sowing, and fertilizing through spraying and harvesting to storage, livestock breeding, and selling produce on the market, while the vehicle roster includes hundreds of licensed machines from dozens of real farming equipment manufacturers such as John Deere, Case IH, Fendt, and New Holland. A cooperative mode for up to sixteen players lets you share a farm with other people and split up the work across expansive maps such as the default Elmcreek, with one player able to work a field by tractor while another manages storage or livestock.

On the new generation of consoles, the game can rely on more detailed field and vegetation textures, smoother weather simulation, and a more stable frame rate even when operating multiple larger machines at once, which used to be a weak point in earlier console versions. The sound design, with the rumble of tractor and combine engines and the sounds of farm animals, does a good job of conveying the feeling of real farm work on your own land, whether during quiet evening hours or a hectic harvest race against the arrival of rain.

Over the years, the Farming Simulator series has built a surprisingly wide and devoted fanbase that appreciates the meditative pace and depth of the farming simulation with no time pressure. Farming Simulator 22 keeps that tradition alive well on the new generation of consoles and remains the go-to choice for anyone who wants to try virtual life on a farm, from a single field all the way to a sprawling agricultural empire.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for a meditative pace with no time pressure will find in Farming Simulator 22 the go-to choice for virtual farm life, from a single field all the way to a sprawling agricultural empire.

xbox-series__hot-wheels-unleashed-2-turb.teaser: Arcade racing on Hot Wheels tracks; the courses wind through entire households.
xbox-series__hot-wheels-unleashed-2-turb.article:
**Hot Wheels Unleashed 2: Turbocharged** is the sequel to the arcade racing game inspired by the iconic Hot Wheels toy cars, and on Xbox Series X/S it expands the concept of a track built from orange plastic rail with new settings, including giant courses winding through households, shops, garages, offices, and outdoor locations such as gardens or busy streets. The game keeps its arcade-style controls, with an emphasis on drifting, jumps, loops, and boosting, and offers dozens of licensed Hot Wheels car models, from classic shapes to fantastical machines, monster trucks, and movie icons on wheels with bold flame, lightning, and chrome-bodywork motifs. The career mode takes players through a long series of races and challenges, gradually unlocking new cars, tracks, and parts for both visual customization and performance upgrades.

The sequel's new feature is dynamic weather that affects grip on the track, along with an expanded track editor that lets players build and share their own racing circuits complete with custom obstacles, loops, jumps, and shortcuts, sharing them with other players around the world. On the new generation of consoles, the game benefits from vivid, saturated colors and a smooth frame rate even with a large number of opponents on screen at once, which heightens the sense of speed on miniature tracks built at a giant scale across ordinary household settings, from the kitchen counter to the garden pool.

Since its very first entry, the Hot Wheels Unleashed series has enjoyed a warm reception thanks to its combination of nostalgia for the toy brand and honest arcade fun accessible even to younger players. Turbocharged expands on that formula with more content, settings, and track variety, cementing the series' position as one of the most enjoyable arcade racing games of the current console generation, suited to both solo play and family split-screen duels.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its nostalgia for the toy brand and honest arcade fun, Turbocharged ranks among the most enjoyable arcade racing games of this generation, suited to both solo play and family split-screen duels.

xbox-series__ea-sports-ufc-5.teaser: MMA on Frostbite with the Real Impact system — injuries visibly build up over the course of a fight.
xbox-series__ea-sports-ufc-5.article:
**EA Sports UFC 5** is a mixed martial arts combat simulation that, on Xbox Series X/S, moved to the Frostbite engine for more lifelike fighter models and more detailed animations of strikes, kicks, throws, and ground grappling. The game introduced a new real-time face and body damage system called Real Impact, which visibly manifests on the fighters' models during a bout through swelling, redness, and cuts that gradually worsen based on the strikes taken, and it expanded the mechanics of transitions between stances, the clinch, takedowns, and ground positions to better match the real dynamics of MMA fights. The career mode follows your own fighter from amateur bouts through smaller organizations all the way to the UFC championship belt, including negotiating contracts, building rivalries, and camp preparation ahead of every fight.

The extensive roster includes licensed current and former UFC champions across men's and women's weight classes, from flyweight to heavyweight, and on the new generation of consoles what stands out most is the smoothness of transitions between the different phases of a fight and the detailed rendering of the arena, the cage, and the reactive crowd around it, which roars in response to every well-landed strike. The sound atmosphere, with loud crowd cheers, corner coaching one-liners, and the referee's familiar calls, does a good job of evoking the tension of major pay-per-view events.

The EA Sports UFC series remains the only official video game license of the UFC organization, so the fifth entry also serves as the current standard for mixed martial arts fans on consoles. The depth of its combat system makes it a more demanding title, but one that rewards players willing to invest time in practice with a convincing feel for the cage and a believable sense of impact on every hit, whether it's a flurry of ground-and-pound punches or a precisely aimed head kick while standing.

**Why play it:** Players willing to invest time in practice will find in EA Sports UFC 5, the only official UFC video game license, a convincing feel for the cage on current-generation consoles.

xbox-series__cricket-24.teaser: Cricket simulation from the makers of AO Tennis; Tests, ODIs and fast-paced Twenty20 matches.
xbox-series__cricket-24.article:
**Cricket 24** is a current cricket simulation from the Australian studio Big Ant Studios, which has long specialized in sports simulations and is also known for titles like AO Tennis and Rugby, and on Xbox Series X/S it brought an improved batting and bowling system compared to previous entries in the series. The game offers a wide range of formats, from traditional multi-day Test cricket through one-day matches to the faster Twenty20 format with shorter innings, along with licensed teams and players from leading cricket leagues, Australia's Big Bash league, and national teams playing international matches. The career mode lets you take your own player from a rookie in the domestic competition through professional contracts to national team captain and star of international tournaments, with decisions about batting technique and bowling tactics.

On the new generation of consoles, the game benefits from more detailed pitch and player models as well as smoother animations for batting, bowling and fielding, which matters greatly for a sport like cricket that depends on the fine details of swing technique and timing to feel believable. The sound atmosphere of stadiums full of spectators and the commentary accompanying every phase of the match round out the impression of watching a real international tournament, including the tension of the decisive final balls of a close match.

Cricket simulations remain a niche genre in Western gaming markets, yet thanks to its precise handling of mechanics, Cricket 24 has found its audience especially in countries like India, Australia and England, where cricket is the national sport. For fans of the sport, it's the most complete current simulation available on current-generation consoles, with plenty of modes for long-term play, whether in the short Twenty20 format or a multi-day Test match.

**Why play:** Cricket fans, especially from India, Australia or England, will find in Cricket 24 the most complete current simulation of the sport on consoles, whether in short Twenty20 or a multi-day Test match.

xbox-series__unpacking.teaser: A woman's life told without words, through unpacking boxes after every move.
xbox-series__unpacking.article:
**Unpacking** is an unassuming puzzle game in which the player receives no text or dialogue at all, and yet an entire woman's life story unfolds before them. The task is always to unpack boxes after a move and find a fitting place for every item – from a stuffed toy and a diploma to kitchenware – and with each new chapter to watch the character grow up, move out of her parents' house, live with roommates, go through a relationship, and finally settle into her own apartment. The mechanic is seemingly simple: move objects with the mouse or controller into cabinets, onto shelves and tables, but the game carefully tracks logic – a cookbook doesn't belong in the bathroom, and a diploma isn't meant to be hidden under the bed. It's in these small details that the wordless storytelling hides, and the player gradually pieces together for themselves what happened to the heroine in between. The game comes from the Australian studio Witch Beam, previously known for the completely different arcade shooter Assault Android Cactus, and the move to a quiet, introspective genre marked a significant change of direction for the studio.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly in high resolution, and its hand-drawn pixel-art style feels clean and cozy, matched by quiet ambient music underscoring the domestic atmosphere. It launched as one of the titles available on Xbox Game Pass right on release day, which helped it reach a broad audience that might otherwise have passed over such an unusual genre. Both critics and players received the game as an original, sensitively crafted experience, praised especially for the inventiveness with which it tells a personal story purely through the arrangement of objects in space, and it also appeared in nominations for awards devoted to independent and narrative titles.

Even years later, Unpacking demonstrates that a narrative game doesn't need a single spoken or written sentence to strike an emotional chord. Its short playtime and soothing pace make it an ideal title for relaxation, and it remains a frequently cited example of inventive indie design that players like to return to just for its soothing atmosphere and the honest craftsmanship of its details.

**Why play:** Anyone looking for a short, soothing game that tells a story without a single spoken line will find in Unpacking an inventive indie title worth returning to just for its soothing atmosphere.

xbox-series__stray.teaser: A cat wandering a cyberpunk city of robots; jumping, tight gaps and meowing instead of weapons.
xbox-series__stray.article:
**Stray** casts the player as an ordinary cat that gets lost in an underground cybernetic city inhabited only by robots and must find its way back to the surface. The game combines exploratory platforming with gentle logic puzzles – the cat can jump across ledges, squeeze through narrow gaps, knock items off shelves, or meow to draw the attention of the robotic inhabitants. Along the way the player meets the robot B-12, who becomes a companion and helps with translation and storing collected data, while the story gradually reveals what happened to the city and its inhabitants and why they ended up sealed deep below the surface with no trace of the original human population. Besides the main storyline, the game also offers plenty of side nooks and corners where you can simply prowl the streets, rub against robots, or knock cans off tables, which gives the whole experience an unexpectedly playful, feline dimension.

The atmosphere of city streets steeped in neon lighting is heightened by a striking audiovisual style, where the contrast between rusty ruins and glowing advertisements creates a dense cyberpunk mood, backed by an ambient electronic soundtrack. On Xbox Series X|S the game benefits from fast loading and stable performance, so exploring the tangled streets feels smooth and free of unnecessary frame-rate drops. It originally launched exclusively on PlayStation and PC, arriving on Xbox and Switch a year later, which only heightened expectations among players who had in the meantime read nothing but praise and were eagerly waiting to play it on Microsoft's consoles as well.

On release, Stray earned acclaim mainly for its fresh idea of playing as a cat in a world abandoned by humans and for its sensitive storytelling about identity and loss. It is still cited today as an example of how strongly even a relatively short and mechanically undemanding game can impress through atmosphere and story, and it's among the titles that drew new players to the platform precisely because of its originality and widely shared popularity among cat lovers and sci-fi fans alike.

**Why play:** Cat lovers and sci-fi fans alike will appreciate Stray's original idea of playing as a cat in a world abandoned by humans, and its sensitive storytelling about identity that still draws new players to the platform today.

xbox-series__signalis.teaser: Survival horror in the spirit of the original Resident Evil; an android searches for a lost companion.
xbox-series__signalis.article:
**Signalis** is a survival horror inspired by the genre's turn-of-the-millennium classics, set in a dark sci-fi future where the player follows the fate of an android named Elster, searching for her lost companion Ariane aboard an abandoned space station and in the underground spaces of a frozen colony. The game relies on limited ammunition, key-and-code puzzles, and tense inventory management, where every decision about what to carry and what to leave behind can mean the difference between survival and death. The fixed-angle camera and rendered pixel graphics evoke the era of the first Resident Evil and Silent Hill titles, but with its own vision of a grim, bureaucratically cold dystopia steeped in references to both East Asian and Soviet aesthetics. The story unfolds only gradually, in fragments and ambiguously, and the player must piece together for themselves what really happened to the station's crew and to the heroine herself.

The game's sound design is one of its greatest strengths – quiet machine hums, muffled footsteps and unexpected sound effects create constant tension, while the stark retro-futuristic visuals reinforce the feeling of alienation and loneliness. On Xbox Series X|S the game runs without issues, and thanks to fast loading it makes the frequent repeated returns to save points that survival horror demands much easier. The controls translate well to a modern controller despite the originally PC-oriented design, and the game supports a choice between a classic pre-rendered aspect ratio and a wider modern format.

On release, Signalis earned attention as one of the most impressive independent horror games of its generation, praised for its atmosphere, symbolism, and its willingness not to rush the explanation of its story. It is still cited today as a title that proved slow, ammo-conserving survival horror still has a place on modern consoles, and among genre fans it enjoys a reputation as a game worth revisiting for its multiple possible interpretations of its ending.

**Why play:** For fans of atmospheric survival horror who appreciate a slow pace, thick symbolism, and a story with multiple possible interpretations that invites replaying.

xbox-series__cassette-beasts.teaser: Instead of balls, it records monsters onto cassettes and you transform into them yourself; fusing forms adds depth.
xbox-series__cassette-beasts.article:
**Cassette Beasts** is a monster-collecting JRPG inspired by classics like Pokémon, in which the player doesn't trap creatures in balls but instead records their forms onto cassettes and then temporarily transforms into the monster to fight. This idea enables unconventional duo battles, where two forms can be combined into a single fusion with its own abilities, adding depth to the classic turn-based system and forcing the player to constantly think about the type advantages and disadvantages of the combined forms. The game's world, an island inhabited by forgotten people and strange creatures, is explored in platformer fashion; the player collects new forms and gradually uncovers the mystery of a place with no escape, while building relationships with other characters stranded in the same location.

Visually, the game relies on colorful pixel art and playful animation, complemented by a distinctive synth soundtrack that underscores its nostalgic yet fresh atmosphere. On Xbox Series X|S it launched directly on release day on Game Pass as well, which helped it quickly find an audience among players looking for an alternative to the big monster-collecting series. The controls and interface are adapted for a controller, and the game runs smoothly without noticeable performance drops, which matters for a title with such a large world and so many collectible forms.

Critics praised above all the inventive fusion system and the way the game combines familiar genre elements with its own rules without feeling like a mere imitation. Cassette Beasts became an example of how a small team can create a full-fledged, intricate RPG experience with limited resources that holds its own alongside much bigger productions, and it remains popular especially among fans of the monster-collecting genre, who value above all the depth of the fusion-based combat system, as well as the many side challenges and optional battles that give experienced players plenty of room to experiment with unusual form combinations.

**Why play:** For monster-collecting fans seeking depth: an inventive fusion system and plenty of optional battles offer room to experiment even for experienced players.

xbox-series__short-hike.teaser: A calm hike up a mountain in search of signal; it's in no hurry and lets the player discover.
xbox-series__short-hike.article:
**A Short Hike** is a short but remarkably pleasant adventure about a trip up Hawk Peak, undertaken by the young bird heroine Claire so she can catch a signal at the summit and call her aunt. The path to the top isn't linear, though – the player can freely explore the island, collect coins to trade for feathers that improve flying and gliding, swim, fish, or simply chat with the island's odd inhabitants, each of whom has their own small story and often a minor side quest that offers further rewards. The game is in no hurry and gives the player room to discover, at their own pace, everything a single small island has to offer, whether it's hidden caves, treasures at the bottom of ponds, or just the views from the surrounding cliffs.

The low-poly visual style, reminiscent of turn-of-the-millennium games, is deliberately simple yet colorful and cozy, accompanied by a soothing piano-and-strings soundtrack that fits the feeling of a summer trip perfectly. On Xbox Series X|S the game arrived some time after its original release on PC and Switch, but the controller controls feel natural, and technically the game places no demands on the console, running stably in high resolution without any stuttering even during fast flight above the island.

Even at its original release, A Short Hike earned great praise for its sensitive pacing, charming world, and ability to evoke a feeling of calm without artificially padding its playtime. It ranks among the titles that prove even a game lasting just a few hours can leave a strong, lasting impression, and it's often recommended as an ideal relaxing experience for players tired of more demanding titles who miss the space to simply wander aimlessly and take their time. Even years later, A Short Hike is often mentioned as one of the most frequently recommended small titles, one that can send players off after a few hours with a smile and the feeling that they spent their time exactly as they should have.

**Why play:** For players tired of demanding titles who want a relaxing experience without hurry – a few calm hours with a charming world and a lasting impression by the end.

xbox-series__venba.teaser: Cooking from faded family recipes as a metaphor for the search for lost identity.
xbox-series__venba.article:
**Venba** is a short narrative adventure about an Indian immigrant woman who, in a foreign country, tries to preserve family recipes and her relationship with her son, who is gradually drifting away from his roots. The main game mechanic is cooking from partly faded, handwritten recipes – the player must guess the missing steps and ingredients from context, which elegantly ties the game mechanic to the theme of losing and rediscovering cultural identity. The story is told across several decades, from the family's arrival in the new country to the son's adulthood, and focuses on small, honest moments of family life, such as arguments at the kitchen table, holiday celebrations, or the struggle to find work in an unfamiliar environment.

Visually, the game relies on a warm, illustrated style with a bold color palette that evokes the atmosphere of a home kitchen, and music drawing on South Indian motifs reinforces the authenticity of the setting. On Xbox Series X|S it launched directly on release day as part of Game Pass, which allowed it to reach a much wider audience than a small independent title would otherwise attract. It's technically undemanding and runs entirely smoothly, with short chapters designed so they can be finished in a single evening.

On release, Venba was praised for its sensitive, unsentimental treatment of the themes of immigration, language barriers, and intergenerational estrangement, and for how it manages to tell an emotional story through a simple cooking mechanic. Its short playtime makes it an ideal single-sitting experience that stays with you longer than you might expect from such an unassuming game, and for many players without Indian heritage it opened up a view of the immigrant experience they had not encountered in any game before. Despite having minimal game mechanics, its strength lies precisely in how it turns ordinary cooking into a vehicle for a powerful personal story that lingers in the memory long after finishing it.

**Why play:** For anyone interested in an emotional story about immigration and intergenerational estrangement, told through a simple cooking mechanic – short, but memorable for a long time.

xbox-series__turnip-boy-commits-tax-evas.teaser: A cute turnip pays off his taxes to the mayor through absurd chores. Ironic humor about bureaucracy.
xbox-series__turnip-boy-commits-tax-evas.article:
**Turnip Boy Commits Tax Evasion** is a short top-down action adventure in which the player controls a cute turnip character who owes the town's mayor a considerable amount of tax and, instead of paying, must complete strange tasks all over town to somehow settle the debt. The game combines simple combat with a cleaver, destroying the environment, collecting items, and solving small puzzles tied to unlocking new areas, all wrapped in heavily ironic, absurd humor that pokes fun at bureaucracy and social norms. Short quests follow one another quickly, keeping the player constantly moving forward without unnecessary delays, as they gradually visit a museum, the sewers, and neighboring islands connected by a simple travel system.

The pixel-art graphics are colorful and strongly stylized, complemented by light, cheerful music that heightens the absurdity of the situations the main character gets into. On Xbox Series X|S the game runs without any issues thanks to its low performance demands and quick control response, which suits its brisk pace. Its small scope and straightforward structure make it suitable even for casual players or as a lighter break between more demanding games, and it can easily be finished in a single sitting.

On release, the game gained popularity precisely because of its combination of simplicity, catchy humor, and an unexpectedly addictive gameplay loop of collecting and destroying. It's still cited today as an example of how a small team can create, on a limited budget, an entertaining and memorable title that doesn't take itself too seriously yet still offers enough content for a pleasant afternoon, and it also became a starting point for further titles from the same studio continuing in a similar comedic vein. Its undemanding difficulty and clear controls also make it a suitable choice for players just starting out with this type of action adventure.

**Why play:** For players looking for an undemanding, funny action adventure for one afternoon with an addictive collect-and-destroy loop, suitable even for genre newcomers.

xbox-series__planet-of-lana.teaser: An atmospheric platformer where a girl solves puzzles together with her feline companion Mui.
xbox-series__planet-of-lana.article:
**Planet of Lana** is an atmospheric puzzle platformer in which a girl named Lana sets out to rescue her sister and the planet's other inhabitants, abducted by mysterious robotic forces. The key gameplay element is cooperation with a feline companion named Mui, who can be directed to activate mechanisms, lure away enemies, or help overcome obstacles that Lana couldn't manage alone. The puzzles skillfully combine the interplay between the two characters with platforming sections and quiet stealth sequences that require avoiding robotic patrols, while the game gradually introduces further animal companions with their own abilities that enrich the solutions to later puzzles.

The game's visuals are among its greatest strengths – hand-painted environments reminiscent of animated-film illustrations create a sense of a vast, mysterious world, while the orchestral score heightens the story's emotional moments. On Xbox Series X|S it launched day one on Game Pass, runs smoothly at high resolution, and fast loading times cut down the waiting between sections of the game, a welcome detail for a title with many repeated puzzle attempts.

Critics praised especially the visual craftsmanship and the thoughtful puzzle design built around cooperation with Mui, though some players noted that the difficulty stays fairly mild for most of the game. Even so, Planet of Lana has taken its place among the acclaimed atmospheric platformers of recent times and is often cited as an example of how strongly a visual style can carry a game's overall impression, even without extensive dialogue or text explanations. The relationship between Lana and Mui is told purely through animation and small gestures, which gives the game an emotional dimension comparable to other standout platformers of recent years, and that's also why Planet of Lana is often mentioned alongside similarly toned titles like Inside or Ori.

**Why play it:** For the striking visual style and puzzles built around cooperation with Mui, telling their story purely through animation – ideal for fans of Inside or Ori.

xbox-series__bramble-mountain-king.teaser: A dark fairy tale from Norse mythology; no combat, just quiet stealth and fleeing from trolls.
xbox-series__bramble-mountain-king.article:
**Bramble: The Mountain King** is a dark fairy-tale adventure inspired by Nordic and Scandinavian folk tradition, in which a boy named Olle heads into the forest to find his lost sister, abducted by creatures from local legends. The game combines platforming exploration with simple puzzles and stealth sections that require avoiding dangerous creatures such as trolls and other figures drawn straight from European folklore, often portrayed far more terrifyingly than readers of children's fairy tales would know them. Without a classic combat system, the player is forced to rely mainly on quiet movement, hiding, and improvised escape routes through the forest.

Visually, the game feels realistic and dark, with elaborate lighting and atmospheric forest environments that contrast with the young hero's childlike perspective. The music and sound design skillfully alternate calm, almost idyllic passages with sudden horror, letting the game catch players off guard. On Xbox Series X|S it launched day one on Game Pass and makes use of the console's power for detailed lighting and dense forest vegetation without major technical compromises, which lets the nighttime passages lit only by moonlight and torch flame really stand out.

At launch, Bramble was praised especially for its bold treatment of the darker side of Nordic fairy tales and for its atmosphere, though some critics pointed to uneven difficulty in places and technical shortcomings. Even so, it became an interesting entry in the fairy-tale horror adventure genre, drawing on lesser-known folklore and offering a somewhat different take on classic fairy-tale motifs, which in most games tend to be presented in a far more sanitized way. It's precisely this uncompromising depiction of violence and the horror of folkloric monsters that players most often remember long after finishing the game.

**Why play it:** For players craving a darker, uncompromising take on Nordic folklore, though you should expect uneven difficulty and technical rough edges.

xbox-series__trek-to-yomi.teaser: Samurai revenge in black-and-white late-Edo Japan; precise close-quarters sword combat.
xbox-series__trek-to-yomi.article:
**Trek to Yomi** is an action adventure set in Japan at the end of the Edo period, in which the player, as young samurai Hiroki, sets out to avenge his master's death and protect his home town, a journey that eventually leads him into mythical, supernatural realms. Combat is built on simple but precise close-quarters swordplay, where the timing of dodges, blocks, and attack combinations matters, supplemented by limited ranged weapons like a bow or kunai. The game alternates linear progress through the town with short platforming and stealth sections, and as it progresses, Hiroki's combat technique expands with new combos and abilities earned through story progression.

The most striking element is the black-and-white cinematic presentation, inspired by classic Japanese samurai films, with fixed camera angles reminiscent of movie shots and a grainy visual filter that fills out the retro atmosphere. On Xbox Series X|S the game runs smoothly at high resolution, where the play of light and shadow typical of the black-and-white aesthetic really stands out, and it also offers the option to switch to a color mode for players who prefer a more classic look.

At launch, the game earned praise especially for its visual style and atmosphere, while the combat system was rated as functional but less deep than in bigger action titles. Even so, Trek to Yomi remains an interesting experiment in linking gameplay mechanics with a tribute to a specific film genre, one that on Xbox Series X|S makes full use of its visual styling and remains one of the few titles to take that kind of cinematic homage as its central conceit. Its short playtime also means the game doesn't try to artificially pad itself out with repetitive combat, but instead keeps a consistent pace throughout and strives to make the viewing and playing experience feel like one cohesive whole, which will especially please players looking for a shorter but tightly compact and aesthetically unified experience.

**Why play it:** For the striking black-and-white visuals and homage to Japanese cinema rather than combat depth, appreciated by players looking for a shorter but stylistically cohesive experience.

xbox-series__tmnt-shredder-s-revenge.teaser: A pixel-art celebration of the Ninja Turtles in the spirit of '90s beat 'em ups, for up to six players.
xbox-series__tmnt-shredder-s-revenge.article:
**TMNT: Shredder's Revenge** is a celebration of classic beat 'em ups from the turn of the eighties and nineties, bringing the Ninja Turtles back in a pixel-art style faithful to the era's cartoon series. Players make their way through the streets of New York, battling hordes of Foot Clan soldiers and familiar bosses in co-op for up to six players, with each of the four turtles, April O'Neil, Casey Jones, and other characters having their own fighting style and special abilities. The game deliberately mirrors the structure of old arcade beat 'em ups but adds modern touches like an experience system, new combos, and clear bonus stages that liven up the pacing between levels.

Visually, the game perfectly imitates the style of the original cartoon series, with vivid colors and fluid animation, while the soundtrack was composed by the team also behind the music of Streets of Rage 4, lending the fights an energetic, synth-driven undertone. On Xbox Series X|S it launched day one on Game Pass and supports both online and local co-op, running stably even during fights with many enemies on screen at once, which is key for keeping the action readable with more players involved.

At launch, the game was received with great enthusiasm as one of the best modern beat 'em ups, praised by fans of the series and the genre alike for precisely capturing nostalgia while pairing it with modern gameplay comfort. To this day it's considered one of the high points of the beat 'em up genre in recent years and a frequently recommended title for playing with a group, whether with friends in the same room or online across platforms. References to decades-old comics, toys, and earlier Ninja Turtles video games will also delight longtime fans of the brand, while new players will get by just fine on the purely functional and fun combat system alone, which holds up even without knowledge of the earlier comics or animated series.

**Why play it:** For Ninja Turtles fans and anyone looking for a great beat 'em up to play with friends – it works both for readers who remember the old comics and for players with no nostalgia at all.

xbox-series__have-nice-death.teaser: The player is a tired Death running the underworld corporation; a roguelike with witty boss fights.
xbox-series__have-nice-death.article:
**Have a Nice Death** is a 2D roguelike action platformer in which the player takes on the role of Death himself, who, as the weary CEO of an underworld corporation, must restore order among employees who've stopped doing their jobs. The game combines fast melee and ranged combat with procedurally generated floors of the corporate underworld, where each death costs the player their progress but grants permanent upgrades that ease future runs, typical of the roguelike genre. Boss fights against the company's various departments, such as Marketing or Human Resources, rank among the game's most memorable and funniest moments.

The visual style draws on the French comic book tradition, with bold black outlines and a simple but strikingly stylized color palette, complemented by a darkly comedic atmosphere full of corporate satire. On Xbox Series X|S it launched day one on Game Pass, the game runs smoothly even during fast combat sequences, and loading between attempts is nearly instant, which suits the roguelike loop well and lets players quickly try out new weapon and ability combinations.

At launch it was praised especially for its imaginative corporate-underworld premise, style, and satirical humor, while the combat was rated as solid, though not quite groundbreaking within the crowded roguelike action genre. Even so, Have a Nice Death found its audience thanks to its original concept and visual identity, which set it apart from a number of similarly toned titles, and it keeps motivating further runs even after completion through the desire to try out as many of the available weapons as possible. The combination of dark humor, well-readable combat systems, and a gradually unfolding story about the underworld's corporate bureaucracy makes the game a refreshing spin on an already well-explored roguelike genre, in which the corporate setting of the afterlife proves an unexpectedly rewarding backdrop for dark comedy.

**Why play it:** For fans of roguelike action who'll be drawn in by the original corporate-underworld setting and dark humor, plus the drive to try out as many weapons as possible across further runs.

xbox-series__sable.teaser: Calm exploration of a desert inspired by Moebius's comics; a search for one's own mask, without combat.
xbox-series__sable.article:
**Sable** is a calm exploration adventure set in a desert world inspired by the comic art of Moebius, in which a young girl named Sable sets out on a traditional journey called the Gliding, whose purpose is to find her own mask and identity before she permanently settles within her tribe. The player explores a vast desert on an anti-gravity glider, completes small tasks for scattered inhabitants, gathers parts to upgrade the vehicle, and uncovers the remnants of an ancient, mysterious civilization, all without the game placing any emphasis on combat or time pressure. The whole world is open from the very start, and the player decides for themselves which direction to head and in what order to complete the individual tasks.

The distinctive flat, comic-shaded visual style is one of the game's most recognizable elements, and together with the ambient, synth-driven soundtrack it creates a meditative, dreamlike atmosphere for the desert wandering. On Xbox Series X|S the game benefits from better performance compared to its original release on the older console generation, running more stably and with shorter loading times, which at launch on older machines were one of the main complaints and noticeably disrupted the otherwise relaxed pacing.

Critics praised especially the unique visual style and the sense of freedom in exploring the world without artificial barriers, while technical shortcomings in early versions dampened the overall enthusiasm somewhat. On Xbox Series X|S, though, most of these problems were fixed, making the console version regarded as one of the better ways to truly enjoy Sable's unusual atmosphere and art style to the fullest. The absence of combat and time pressure makes the game a suitable choice for players seeking a purely contemplative experience of exploring a world that's alien yet somehow familiar, where the reward is the sheer feeling of freedom and the aesthetic experience of the landscape itself, rather than points or achievements.

**Why play it:** For players seeking purely contemplative exploration without combat or time pressure – the console version also fixes the technical shortcomings of the early releases.

xbox-series__company-of-heroes-3.teaser: A strategy game from Relic Entertainment with destructible terrain that changes the battle on the fly.
xbox-series__company-of-heroes-3.article:
**Company of Heroes 3** is a real-time strategy game from Relic Entertainment, continuing the studio's long tradition of battle strategy games set during the Second World War. The player commands a column of units through the Italian campaign and the North African theater, with the game placing emphasis on making use of terrain, taking cover behind walls, and flanking enemy positions. Destructible environments also play a major role – buildings crumble under artillery fire, which changes the tactical situation from minute to minute during a battle and forces the player to constantly reassess where a unit can still safely take cover. Part of the campaign is a dynamic operational map of Italy, on which the player manages territory between individual engagements, replenishes supplies, builds up infrastructure, and decides which direction to push the advance – the game thus combines real-time battles with elements of turn-based strategy and adds a layer of long-term planning that was missing from previous entries.

The Xbox Series X|S version launched several months after the original PC release and brought a controller-adapted control scheme that tries to replace the classic keyboard-and-mouse combination with radial menus and smart target marking. Thanks to Series X's power, the game handles even larger engagements with dozens of units and destructible surroundings without major frame-rate drops, although controlling it with a gamepad is naturally not as precise and fast as on PC when micromanaging a large number of units at once.

Reception at launch was mixed – players appreciated the return to a tactical emphasis on cover and destructible environments, but some fans were bothered by the simplification of certain mechanics compared to the second entry, as well as by technical problems after release, which the studio gradually addressed in subsequent updates. Even so, Company of Heroes remains a major name in the war-strategy genre, and the third installment proves that even a demanding tactical RTS can work on a console with a gamepad in hand, albeit with certain compromises compared to the original mouse-and-keyboard controls.

**Why play it:** For fans of tactical RTS games who value cover mechanics and destructible environments, and who can accept that gamepad controls bring certain compromises compared to mouse and keyboard.

xbox-series__age-of-wonders-4.teaser: A turn-based 4X strategy game where the player mixes races and cultures into a fully custom civilization.
xbox-series__age-of-wonders-4.article:
**Age of Wonders 4** is a turn-based 4X strategy game from the Dutch studio Triumph Studios, sending the player into a fantasy world full of distinct races, magic, and branching ruling factions. The core of the game is building your own race using so-called forms and cultures – the player can, for instance, combine dwarves with necromancy or elves with an industrial culture, creating entirely original civilizations with their own units, appearance, and abilities. Besides managing cities and the economy, the game also offers turn-based tactical battles on separate maps, where terrain, spells, unit positioning, and the proper use of heroes all matter, with heroes developing over the course of the game and gaining new abilities much like in role-playing games.

On Xbox Series X|S the game launched simultaneously with the PlayStation console version, with controls adapted for the gamepad – the menus and research tree are neatly divided into tabs that can be navigated with the triggers, which partially compensates for the speed of a mouse on PC when scrolling through dozens of research and upgrade options. Graphically, the game leans more toward readability of the map and units than photorealism, which works well on a console viewed on a TV from a greater distance, where clarity matters more than texture detail.

Critically, the game was received very positively, especially for the depth of its custom-race creation system and for reviving the older Age of Wonders brand for a new generation of players who may never have encountered the original entries. The story mode was also praised, guiding the player through a series of connected scenarios and gradually revealing the rules and possibilities of the system, which eases entry into an otherwise fairly complex game. For fans of turn-based strategy, it's one of the most interesting additions of recent years, and thanks to its clear controls it also ranks among the better things the 4X genre has to offer outside of PC on console, though managing a large empire in more depth will suit a player with the patience and appetite for working through several layers of menus.

**Why play it:** For fans of turn-based strategy who'll appreciate a story mode with a series of connected scenarios that eases entry into an otherwise complex system for creating custom races.

xbox-series__anno-1800-console-edition.teaser: A sprawling PC building giant comes to console with complex production chains.
xbox-series__anno-1800-console-edition.article:
**Anno 1800: Console Edition** brings the sprawling city-building strategy originally released on PC to Xbox Series X|S, set in a fictional version of the nineteenth century on the threshold of the industrial revolution. The player founds and expands a network of island settlements, plans production chains from raw materials to complex goods, addresses the needs of inhabitants from various social classes, and simultaneously engages in diplomacy, trade, and military clashes with neighbors. The depth of the economic systems, where each new tier of inhabitants requires new types of production and raw materials, ranks among the most complex things to appear in the city-builder genre on consoles, and the game also offers expeditions to exotic regions beyond the main map.

The console version arrived with completely reworked gamepad controls - radial menus, contextual hints, and smart switching between map layers are meant to replace mouse precision, which succeeded surprisingly well given the amount of information the game displays on screen at once. On Series X the game benefits from fast loading and stable framerates even in sprawling cities with thousands of buildings and dense transport networks between islands.

Contemporary reviews praised above all the fact that such a complex strategy game was successfully adapted to a controller without a fundamental loss of functionality, even though some advanced operations like mass-reconnecting production chains remain faster on PC. For console players, this is one of few opportunities to try a truly deep economic city-builder without needing a keyboard and mouse, and Anno 1800 thus expanded the franchise's audience with a new generation of players who never tried the PC version. The large amount of additional content the game gained on PC over the years through expansions was also carried over into the console edition, so players get a practically complete experience including later story chapters and new biomes.

**Why play it:** For console players wanting to try a deep economic city-builder without a keyboard and mouse, who also get all the later add-on content included.

xbox-series__wargroove-2.teaser: Turn-based strategy inspired by the nineties; commanders mix units across factions.
xbox-series__wargroove-2.article:
**Wargroove 2** is a turn-based strategy game from Chucklefish that follows up the beloved first entry inspired by classic turn-based strategy games from the nineties. The player commands an army made up of various unit types on grid-based maps, where terrain advantages, unit combinations, and correct attack timing all matter - each turn can decide the whole battle, and misplaced units can quickly turn the tide of a fight. The second game's new feature is the commander system, which allows mixing units from different factions into a single army, bringing greater variability to strategy building before each engagement and rewarding experimentation with unusual combinations.

The game launched on Xbox Series X|S simultaneously with the other platforms and was available in Game Pass from the start, which helped it quickly reach a wider audience beyond traditional genre fans. Visually it continues the pixel-art style of the previous entry, which looks clean and legible on modern TVs, and loading times and smoothness on Series X are problem-free even on larger maps with multiple factions at once.

Critical reception was largely positive - particularly praised were the depth of tactical options and the map editor, which lets players create and share their own scenarios and even entire campaigns with their own story. Wargroove 2 confirms that the turn-based strategy genre inspired by older titles still has its place on modern consoles, especially for players seeking a more deliberate pace of play than real-time strategy offers and who want to carefully think through every move. The campaign is also filled out with smaller narrative missions featuring various commanders who have their own personality and special abilities, adding needed variety to the story portion and a reason to work through the chapters one by one.

**Why play it:** For fans of deliberate turn-based strategy who will appreciate a map editor letting them share their own scenarios and campaigns, and who don't mind taking their time over every move.

xbox-series__crash-bandicoot-4-it-s-abou.teaser: A direct sequel to the original trilogy, with new masks changing traversal of familiar levels.
xbox-series__crash-bandicoot-4-it-s-abou.article:
**Crash Bandicoot 4: It's About Time** is a platformer from Toys for Bob that follows directly on from the original nineties trilogy, ignoring every entry made in between. The player guides both Crash and Coco through intricate levels full of precise jumping, timing, and item collecting, while the game gradually adds new masks with special abilities - such as slowing down time, phasing through obstacles, or reversing gravity - that change how already-familiar levels are traversed and force players to adapt their technique. The difficulty ranks among the higher end of the genre, and the game also offers alternate paths, hidden secrets, and bonus levels for players who want to squeeze every last bit out of each level.

On Xbox Series X|S the game released as a free next-gen upgrade to the original version, bringing faster loading, higher resolution, and a smoother framerate, which is very welcome during fast platforming sections requiring precise timing and reduces frustration during repeated attempts. The colorful, cartoonish graphics look vivid and sharp on modern TVs, and the soundtrack continues the series' distinctive style familiar since the nineties entries.

Critically the game was received positively, praised especially for returning to the demanding but fair difficulty of the classic entries and for the amount of content, including playable characters with their own movement styles and abilities. For fans of the original trilogy, this is a dignified continuation that retains precise controls on next-gen consoles along with the demanding but rewarding feeling of overcoming levels they remember from the earlier entries on older consoles. The game also offers an optional mode with a limited number of lives for players who want to experience the original, harsher nineties feel, as well as more accessible settings for those who mainly want to get through the story without unnecessary frustration. Individual levels often also offer sections seen through the eyes of characters other than Crash and Coco, bringing pleasant variety to the established gameplay formula and breaking up the repetitive rhythm of jumping across platforms.

**Why play it:** For fans of the classic trilogy craving a demanding but fair platformer with a large roster of playable characters - with an optional mode for both a harsher and a more relaxed experience.

xbox-series__prince-of-persia-lost-crown.teaser: A return to the franchise's roots in metroidvania form; abilities gradually unlock the whole map.
xbox-series__prince-of-persia-lost-crown.article:
**Prince of Persia: The Lost Crown** is an action platformer from Ubisoft Montpellier that returns the Prince of Persia brand to its roots in agility and combat mechanics, this time in a metroidvania format. The player takes on the role of the young warrior Sargon and traverses an interconnected world full of acrobatic movement, sword combat, and gradually acquired abilities that unlock new paths into previously inaccessible parts of the map - a double jump, teleportation, or slowing down time change how already-visited areas can be traversed. A key mechanic is also the ability to mark a spot on the map for fast travel back to it, which eases navigation through the intricately interconnected level structure and addresses one of the frequently criticized problems of older metroidvanias.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs in high resolution with a smooth framerate, which is crucial during the demanding combat and precise jumping - the game often requires quick reactions and precise timing of dodges and attacks, or death comes quickly even against an ordinary enemy. Visually it combines hand-painted backgrounds with dynamic action, and the soundtrack draws on Middle Eastern inspiration typical of the franchise since its original entries.

Contemporary reception was very positive, with the game praised for its well-thought-out combat, quality level design, and how elegantly it combines the series' tradition with modern metroidvania mechanics without feeling like a mere imitation of other well-known genre titles. Many critics ranked it among the best platformers of its year, and for the Prince of Persia brand, which had long been searching for a new direction, it represents a very successful return to its platforming roots. The extensive map with many optional side areas also offers plenty of content for players who want to get more out of the world than just the main story, and various difficulty settings make the game accessible to a wider range of players without diminishing the challenge for more experienced audiences.

**Why play it:** For fans of metroidvanias and the old series alike, who will appreciate the well-thought-out combat, quality level design, and an expansive map with plenty of optional content.

xbox-series__blasphemous-2.teaser: A dark metroidvania steeped in blood and symbolism from Spain; three weapons, demanding combat.
xbox-series__blasphemous-2.article:
**Blasphemous 2** is a metroidvania platformer from the Spanish studio The Game Kitchen that continues the dark, religiously-themed world of the first entry, full of gothic architecture, bloody symbolism, and religious motifs inspired by Spanish tradition. The player again takes on the role of the Penitent One and traverses an interconnected world where they gradually gain three distinct weapons, each with its own combat style and special abilities needed to progress into new areas and unlock shortcuts between already-visited places. Combat is more demanding and thought-out than in the first entry, with an emphasis on precise dodge timing, parrying, and using the right weapon against a given type of enemy.

On Xbox Series X|S the game launched simultaneously with all other platforms and runs in high resolution with a smooth framerate, which matters for the demanding combat and precise platforming sections. The hand-drawn pixel-art graphics, with detailed character and environment animations, look very striking on modern TVs, and the dark, religiously-inspired music does a good job of reinforcing the whole game's grim atmosphere.

Contemporary reception was very positive, with critics praising above all the improved combat, richer level design, and greater build variety compared to the first entry, where the player's options were somewhat more limited. Blasphemous 2 ranks among the best-reviewed metroidvanias of its year and confirms that a smaller Spanish studio can keep pace with the best in this extremely competitive genre even after releasing only one previous entry. The distinctive visual style inspired by Spanish baroque and religious iconography also gives the game a strong identity that's easy to recognize among dozens of other recent metroidvanias. The branching map, connected by shortcuts and gradually unlocked abilities, also rewards careful exploration and returning to previously inaccessible parts of the world.

**Why play it:** For fans of metroidvanias craving the improved combat and richer level design of the first entry, now in a distinctive visual style inspired by Spanish baroque.

xbox-series__little-nightmares-ii.teaser: A horror platformer about Mono and Six in an enlarged, terrifying world full of silent sneaking.
xbox-series__little-nightmares-ii.article:
**Little Nightmares II** is a horror platformer from Tarsier Studios that expands the dark, unsettling world of the first entry with a new main character named Mono and his companion Six, familiar from the original game. The player traverses an enlarged, unsettling world full of enormous, deformed figures and solves environmental puzzles based on hiding, moving quietly, and cooperation between the two characters to overcome obstacles that neither one could get past alone. The atmosphere rests on the contrast between the tiny character and the disproportionately large, menacing surroundings, creating a sense of ever-present threat without the game needing to rely on direct jump scares or excessive violence.

On Xbox Series X|S the game launched as an improved next-gen version with higher resolution and better lighting, which further emphasizes the contrasts of light and shadow typical of the whole series' visual style. The music and sound design, partly built on silence broken by sudden sounds, rank among the game's strongest aspects and contribute significantly to the tension while making one's way through the chapters.

Contemporary reception was very positive, with critics praising above all the visual style, level design, and the game's ability to create tension without using classic horror jump scares or graphic violence. Little Nightmares II confirms that a combination of platforming and psychological horror can work even without direct violence, and on Xbox Series it offers one of the visually most striking experiences of its genre to this day. The character Six and her distinctive yellow raincoat have also become a recognizable symbol of the whole franchise, appearing even in promotional materials and merchandise tied to the game. The shorter length of play also means the tension doesn't fade and the game doesn't bore even players who otherwise aren't inclined toward slower titles full of atmosphere. The first entry in the series had already laid the groundwork for this success several years earlier, so the second entry could build on a clearly defined visual and gameplay language for the whole franchise.

**Why play it:** For fans of psychological horror that creates tension without cheap jump scares or graphic violence, with a shorter length that keeps the tension high from start to finish.

xbox-series__lego-star-wars-skywalker-sa.teaser: All nine saga episodes in LEGO style for the first time; open planets and two-player co-op.
xbox-series__lego-star-wars-skywalker-sa.article:
**LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga** is a family action-adventure game from Traveller's Tales that for the first time brings all nine episodes of the main Star Wars saga into LEGO style within a single game, from The Phantom Menace to The Rise of Skywalker. The player goes through key scenes from all three trilogies, solves simple environmental puzzles, fights in lighthearted combat with lightsabers and blasters, and can freely move between levels across open planets full of side quests, collectibles, and unlockable characters. The game is built so that even younger or less experienced players can manage it, and the two-player split-screen co-op mode ranks among its greatest strengths.

On Xbox Series X|S the game runs in high resolution with a smooth framerate even on sprawling open planets, where multiple characters and vehicles can move at once without noticeable slowdown. The humor typical of the LEGO series, built on silent parody of well-known scenes without dialogue, works well even for players unfamiliar with the original films or for younger viewers.

Both critical and audience reception was very positive, with the scope of content, quality of the humor, and how well the game plays two-player on a single screen without a split display all being especially praised. LEGO Star Wars: The Skywalker Saga ranks among the most ambitious entries in the whole LEGO games franchise, and on Xbox Series it offers one of the best family experiences set in the Star Wars universe. The large number of unlockable characters, including minor and lesser-known figures from all three trilogies, also gives the game long-lasting appeal even after finishing the main story of all nine episodes. The open planets with side quests and collectibles can also keep players entertained for dozens of hours even after completing all nine main episodes. The ability to freely switch between characters with different abilities also adds a light puzzle-solving element even to otherwise fairly straightforward combat sections.

**Why play it:** For families and Star Wars fans looking for fun to share two-player on one screen, with a huge number of unlockable characters from all three trilogies.

xbox-series__powerwash-simulator.teaser: Meditative pressure-washing away grime with no win or lose condition; a calming end-of-day routine.
xbox-series__powerwash-simulator.article:
**PowerWash Simulator** is a relaxing simulation from the British studio FuturLab whose core is a surprisingly satisfying activity - washing dirty surfaces with a pressure washer. The player gradually cleans houses, vehicles, playgrounds, and entire locations inspired by a town, with each object having its own geometry and specific grime that must be removed by systematically running the water jet over it down to the last corner. The game offers no win or lose condition in the traditional sense - its goal is to provide a meditative, results-oriented activity that functions as a form of rest and a calming routine after a demanding day.

On Xbox Series X|S the game launched in Game Pass on day one, which greatly contributed to its popularity with a wide audience, including players who otherwise don't play many video games and discovered the title precisely through the service. The visually simple but legible graphics and satisfying visual and sound effects of the spraying water make playing an almost therapeutic experience, one that can also be played cooperatively with other players cleaning together.

Contemporary reception was very positive, and the game quickly built up a loyal community of players who appreciated its undemanding nature and its ability to function as a counterweight to more demanding, stressful titles full of combat. PowerWash Simulator shows that even a seemingly mundane activity can, with the right execution, create an unusually addictive and widely accessible experience suitable for the whole family regardless of gaming experience. Over time the game also gained locations inspired by well-known brands and films, giving long-term players another reason to repeatedly return to already-cleaned spots. The simplicity of the controls and the absence of any time pressure also make the game a suitable choice even for completely inexperienced players or younger children under parental supervision. The ability to play together with another person on one account also makes the cleaning a pleasant shared activity rather than a solitary chore.

**Why play it:** For anyone looking for an undemanding counterweight to stressful titles - simple controls and no time pressure make it an ideal choice for both kids and newcomers.

xbox-series__disney-dreamlight-valley.teaser: A farming life-sim starring Disney and Pixar characters; building up the valley and friendships with Mickey.
xbox-series__disney-dreamlight-valley.article:
**Disney Dreamlight Valley** is a life simulation from Gameloft that combines farming and life-sim mechanics with characters and settings familiar from Disney and Pixar films and series. The player builds and customizes their own valley, grows crops, hunts and fishes, completes quests for characters like Mickey Mouse, Elsa, or WALL-E, and gradually unlocks new areas of the valley inspired by various Disney worlds, from classic landscapes to futuristic locations. Social interactions with the characters, building friendships by gifting items, and collectible elements are among the core gameplay loops that motivate players to return to the game every day.

On Xbox Series X|S, the game runs smoothly even with the large, gradually unlocked valley full of detail and the colorful graphics typical of the Disney aesthetic known from animated films. The game first launched in early access on multiple platforms, including Xbox Series, with additional areas, characters, and seasonal events added over time until its full release a year later.

Contemporary reception was mostly positive, with players praising the pleasant atmosphere, the quality treatment of well-known characters, and the undemanding yet addictive gameplay loops suited to long-term play. Disney Dreamlight Valley became a popular choice for families and younger players seeking a calm, non-violent alternative to more demanding titles, and on Xbox Series it offers convenient access to extensive, ever-growing content. The continuously added seasonal events and new characters also keep the player community active long after first completing the main quests in the valley. The ability to freely customize the appearance of the character, the house, and the whole valley also gives the game a strong creative dimension that many players enjoy just as much as completing the quests themselves. The gradual expansion of the roster of Disney and Pixar characters also keeps the game current even for players who have followed it since its original launch.

**Why play it:** For families and younger players looking for a calm, non-violent life sim with familiar Disney characters and steadily growing content.

xbox-series__grand-theft-auto-trilogy-de.teaser: Three classics on one engine; faithful to the originals, just with more modern controls.
xbox-series__grand-theft-auto-trilogy-de.article:
**Grand Theft Auto: The Trilogy – The Definitive Edition** brings to Xbox Series X and S reworked versions of three classics – GTA III, Vice City, and San Andreas – built on a new, unified engine. Players can once again roam the streets of Liberty City, Vice City, and San Andreas, complete missions for street gangs and mob bosses, flee the police in chases, and enjoy an open world full of vehicles, weapons, and side activities, this time with modern controls closer to later entries in the series. The core gameplay mechanics – shooting, driving, and completing missions triggered by phone calls and map markers – remain faithful to the originals, just supplemented with a more convenient camera system, navigation, easier aiming, and autosave, which makes it easier to return to unfinished tasks.

Technically, the collection runs on Xbox Series at a higher resolution and with improved lighting, new character models, and reworked weather and water reflection effects, while retaining the distinctive soundtrack and radio stations featuring period hits that were key to the atmosphere of all three games. The release was, however, accompanied by technical problems, crashes, missing rain in San Andreas, and inaccuracies in the graphical treatment of some characters, which sparked significant criticism from the player community shortly after launch and were gradually fixed by additional updates in the following months.

Despite its rocky start, the collection has real significance – it makes three groundbreaking games that defined the open-world action genre at the turn of the millennium accessible to new players who would otherwise struggle to reach the originals on old hardware. San Andreas, with its vast map of three cities and countryside, still offers dozens of hours of content today, including side minigames; Vice City remains valued for its eighties Miami atmosphere and accompanying radio stations; and GTA III laid the foundations of the entire 3D open world on which almost all later entries in the series were built, so the collection primarily functions as a convenient and accessible archive of the genre's history.

**Why play it:** For players who can no longer reach the originals on old hardware – San Andreas, Vice City, and GTA III still offer dozens of hours of the genre's key open-world history today.

xbox-series__metal-gear-solid-master-col.teaser: Five key entries in Konami's stealth series together in one package, including development materials.
xbox-series__metal-gear-solid-master-col.article:
**Metal Gear Solid: Master Collection Vol. 1** gathers on Xbox Series X and S the key entries in Konami's stealth series – Metal Gear, Metal Gear 2: Solid Snake, Metal Gear Solid, Metal Gear Solid 2: Sons of Liberty, and Metal Gear Solid 3: Snake Eater – along with related documents, artbooks, and development materials. Playing as agent Snake, the player sneaks through enemy bases, avoids patrols and cameras, resolves situations without unnecessary violence, and gradually uncovers the intricate story of genetics, war, and manipulation the series is famous for. Stealth mechanics, hiding in shadows, knocking on walls, communicating with the support team via codec, and using the environment and disguises remain the core of gameplay across all titles in the collection, even as they are gradually refined with each entry.

On Xbox Series, the collection offers the option to switch between the original aspect ratio and modern widescreen display, along with a stable frame rate and fast loading, even though the games themselves remain graphically faithful to the originals without any major rework of textures and models. The iconic Metal Gear Solid music, full of tension and pathos, and the distinctive alert sound when the player is spotted work just as powerfully as they did on first release, as do the long, cinematically staged cutscenes with elaborate direction that made the series famous and set it apart from the rest of the genre back in the PlayStation era.

In the nineties, Metal Gear Solid fundamentally shaped the perception of stealth action and cinematic storytelling in games as a whole, and the PlayStation 2 entries then raised the bar for audiovisual production and narrative ambition across the entire genre. The Master Collection thus serves primarily as a historically important archive, giving players on modern consoles the chance to experience Hideo Kojima's original stories in their authentic form, albeit without control modernization to the level of later entries such as Metal Gear Solid V, which may initially feel less comfortable for newcomers to the series.

**Why play it:** For players wanting to experience Hideo Kojima's original stealth classics in their authentic form, even at the cost of less comfortable controls compared to later entries in the series.

xbox-series__tomb-raider-i-iii-remastere.teaser: The original Lara Croft trilogy in new graphics, with a choice between classic and modern controls.
xbox-series__tomb-raider-i-iii-remastere.article:
**Tomb Raider I-III Remastered** brings back to Xbox Series X and S the trio of original Lara Croft adventures from the nineties – Tomb Raider, Tomb Raider II, and Tomb Raider III – in reworked graphical form, while also preserving the accompanying expansions and bonus levels from later releases. The player explores vast tombs, temples, sunken ships, and ancient ruins around the world, solves spatial puzzles based on jumping, climbing, swimming, and pushing blocks, and faces wild animals as well as human enemies, and can switch on the fly at any time between the classic and modern look and between the original tank controls and their more modern variant with free camera movement around the character.

The remaster on Xbox Series brings new lighting, higher-resolution textures, modernized character models, and reworked water effects, while the level design and puzzle placement remain faithful to the originals, so the games retain their tough, at times uncompromising difficulty, demanding trap sequences, and the typical leaps of faith where the player has to guess the right path in advance. The original music and ambient sounds, which built up the mysterious atmosphere of abandoned tombs and dangerous traps, have been preserved unchanged and still work well, as does the iconic sound of a collected artifact and the distinctive creak of Lara's backpack.

The first Tomb Raider from 1996 was among the pioneers of the 3D action-adventure genre, and Lara Croft became one of the most famous video game characters of all time, while the second and third entries expanded the concept with more varied settings, from Venetian canals to Himalayan peaks, vehicles, and more demanding acrobatics. The remastered collection today serves as a convenient way to play these landmark titles without having to fight outdated controls and camera, and it's a reminder of how fundamentally they shaped the action-adventure genre at the turn of the millennium, even more than twenty years later.

**Why play it:** For action-adventure fans wanting to relive Lara Croft's pioneering early days without wrestling with the outdated controls and camera of the original versions.

xbox-series__quake-ii-remastered.teaser: A remaster of id Software's classic by Nightdive Studios, with added expansions and fast-paced action.
xbox-series__quake-ii-remastered.article:
**Quake II Remastered** brings to Xbox Series X and S a restored version of id Software's classic 1997 shooter, remastered by Nightdive Studios in collaboration with the original creators, similar to their earlier remaster of the first Quake. Playing as a soldier fighting the alien Strogg race, the player shoots their way through a series of large, interconnected levels full of hidden passages, keycards, and powerful weapons from the shotgun to the railgun, with the game's pace remaining fast and action-packed, built on exploration, finding secret spots, and thoughtful level progression, very much in the spirit of nineties shooters. The remaster also adds the additional missions and expansions Ground Zero and The Reckoning, which were released separately in the original, as well as a brand-new chapter called Call of the Machine, created specifically for this release.

On Xbox Series, the game runs at high resolution with improved dynamic lighting and a smooth frame rate, which together with support for modern controls, an automap, and a clearer objective system makes the transition easier for players used to today's shooters. The distinctive industrial soundtrack, combining guitars with electronic elements, and the dark, alien atmosphere of the Strogg's metal bases and chemical plants remain unchanged and still effectively convey the feeling of a lone fight on a hostile planet.

In its day, Quake II was praised for its technical sophistication, elaborate 3D environments, and networked multiplayer, which helped shape online shooters for years to come. The remastered version makes this legacy accessible to a new generation of players, and thanks to small quality-of-life improvements and comfortable controls, it shows that the basic recipe of fast, straightforward action without unnecessary complications still works flawlessly, even at a great distance in time from the late-nineties original.

**Why play it:** For fans of fast, straightforward action without unnecessary complications, it's a great chance to experience a title that once helped shape online multiplayer shooters.

xbox-series__elder-scrolls-v-skyrim-anni.teaser: A next-gen version of the legendary RPG; the Anniversary Edition adds dozens of earlier DLC.
xbox-series__elder-scrolls-v-skyrim-anni.article:
**The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim Anniversary Edition** is an expanded next-gen release of Bethesda Game Studios' open-world fantasy RPG, optimized specifically for Xbox Series X and S and continuing a decade-long history of the game's release across numerous platforms. Playing as the Dovahkiin, the last Dragonborn, the player explores the vast province of Skyrim full of mountains, caves, and ancient tombs, completes main and side quests, fights dragons using magic and the Voice, joins factions such as the Companions, the Dark Brotherhood, or the Mages and Thieves Guilds, and freely shapes their character through a skill system that grows with use, without the classic division into classes. The Anniversary Edition also includes dozens of previously paid Creation Club content packs, which add new quests, dungeons, items, companions, and minor gameplay enhancements similar to community mods.

On Xbox Series, the game runs at a higher resolution and with support for 60 frames per second, which significantly improves smoothness compared to the previous-generation console version, and loading times are noticeably shorter even in large cities and densely built-up areas. Jeremy Soule's atmospheric orchestral soundtrack, built on choral motifs, and Skyrim's snowy, harsh landscape with dynamic weather and changing seasons remain unmistakable and are among the most praised and most frequently cited elements of the entire series.

After its 2011 release, Skyrim fundamentally influenced the open-world RPG genre, and thanks to repeated remasters and ports to nearly every platform, it became one of the longest-running and most parodied titles in gaming history. The Anniversary Edition on Xbox Series shows that even more than a decade later, the world of Skyrim can still offer dozens to hundreds of hours of content and continues to attract both new and returning players, who even after all these years keep discovering as-yet-unexplored corners and side stories.

**Why play it:** For anyone wanting to spend dozens to hundreds of hours in an RPG world, Skyrim Anniversary Edition is an ideal entry point into one of the most influential open-world titles in history, even more than a decade after release.

xbox-series__life-is-strange-remastered-.teaser: A remastered duo: Max Caulfield's time-rewinding and Chloe Price's youthful rebellion in one package.
xbox-series__life-is-strange-remastered-.article:
**Life is Strange Remastered Collection** combines on Xbox Series X and S reworked versions of the first Life is Strange game and its prequel, Life is Strange: Before the Storm, into a single Square Enix package, without touching the series' later standalone entries. Playing as student Max Caulfield, gifted with the ability to rewind time, the player unravels both personal and supernatural mysteries in the small American town of Arcadia Bay, with choices in dialogue and key situations influencing the direction of the story, the relationships between characters, and the fates of supporting characters, right up to a dramatic finale branching into two possible endings.
