The return to an emphasis on humor and production quality was received considerably better by players and the domestic games press than the previous entry had been.

Polda 6 is now seen as a successful restart of the series after a weaker period — proof that it paid off for the domestic development team to listen to fan feedback and return to a tried-and-tested recipe. For observers of the Czech adventure game scene it's an interesting example of how trust with an audience can be rebuilt even with limited resources, and for loyal fans it remains one of the more beloved later entries in the whole series.

**Why play it:** For fans of the series it's one of the more beloved later entries — a successful restart proving that it paid off for the domestic team to listen to player feedback.

pc-modern__polda-7.teaser: A case arriving after years of delays and crowdfunding; the last entry with Luděk Sobota's legendary voice.
pc-modern__polda-7.article:
**Polda 7** arrived after long years of preparation and delays, partly funded through a crowdfunding campaign, and delivered another case for policeman Pankrác voiced once again by the legendary Luděk Sobota. The gameplay stays true to the series' classic point-and-click formula — exploring the environment, collecting and combining items in an inventory, and conversations full of wordplay and references to Czech reality, this time from the late 2010s and early 2020s. Release was delayed beyond the original plans, among other reasons because of health issues affecting one of the key creators, which shows just how small and personally dependent the team behind the game still is, and how hard it is to keep the series alive after so many years. The game's creation was also preceded by a successful crowdfunding campaign among fans, who thus decided for themselves whether a seventh entry would even go into production.

Graphically and technically, Polda 7 moves the series closer to current standards, while keeping the recognizable style of caricatured characters and settings the series has cultivated since its beginnings in the late 1990s. Voice acting remains the key ingredient of the humor, and the musical accompaniment rounds out the lighthearted atmosphere fans have long come to expect from Polda, and without which the series would feel different. The game later also released on macOS and mobile platforms, showing the creators' effort to reach an audience beyond the traditional circle of PC players and secure the series more years of existence.

The release was welcomed mainly by loyal fans who had followed the series since the 1990s, but commercially the game was hurt by widespread piracy, which led the creators to think about the future of the whole brand and its continuation. Still, Polda 7 stands as proof of the remarkable longevity of a domestic game series and the lasting loyalty of its audience to the character of Pankrác, even more than two decades after the release of the first entry.

**Why play it:** For loyal fans who have followed Pankrác since the 1990s, it's proof of the remarkable longevity of a domestic game series, even more than two decades after the first entry.

pc-modern__black-mirror.teaser: A horror adventure from Future Games; one of the most successful Czech games ever.
pc-modern__black-mirror.article:
**Posel smrti**, released abroad as The Black Mirror, is a horror adventure by studio Future Games, one of the most successful and highly regarded Czech games ever. The story follows young nobleman Samuel Gordon, who returns after years to the family estate of Black Mirror after being forced to do so by his grandfather's death, and gradually uncovers dark family secrets and the circumstances of his wife's death, who perished in a fire. The gameplay is classic adventure fare - exploring the environment, collecting and combining items in the inventory, and solving puzzles, all set across roughly a hundred and fifty locations through which the player gradually works from one chamber of the estate to the next, uncovering increasingly dark connections between the family members.

At the time, the game captivated players with an exceptionally chilling, gothic atmosphere, enhanced by carefully crafted music and sound design, as well as intricate, darkly toned puzzles without unnecessary comic relief, which was less common for domestic adventure games up to that point. Technically, it was a very ambitious project for 2003 - the game was released fully voiced in several language versions including English, German, and French, an unusual scope of localization for domestic production, supplemented with subtitles in additional languages. Visually, it relied on beautifully rendered static scenes that still feel atmospheric today despite their age and the limited technical capabilities of the computers of the time, on which the game ran at a fairly low resolution.

Posel smrti became an internationally successful export of the Czech gaming scene and is still mentioned today as one of the best domestic games, proving that even a small local team could create a title competitive abroad. Its success launched the entire Black Mirror series and cemented Future Games' reputation as a key player in the horror adventure genre, not only at home but abroad as well, where the game gained its own loyal fanbase.

**Why play it:** For fans of horror adventure games, it's one of the best domestic games ever - a title that launched an entire series and succeeded abroad as well.

pc-modern__black-mirror-ii-reigning-evil.teaser: A loose sequel without Future Games; taken up by the German studio Cranberry Productions.
pc-modern__black-mirror-ii-reigning-evil.article:
**Posel smrti 2**, known abroad as Black Mirror II, is a loose sequel to the successful horror adventure, but unlike the first installment it was not created by the Czech studio Future Games, but rather by the German team Cranberry Productions, which bought the rights to the brand and the license for a sequel from the German publisher dtp. The story takes place twelve years later, and its main character is Darren Michaels, son of Samuel Gordon from the first game, who in a small American town grapples with his own dark secrets, a family curse, and mysterious deaths in the area, which ultimately lead him back to the legacy of the Gordon family.

In terms of gameplay, the game sticks to the established adventure formula - exploring locations, collecting and combining items in the inventory, solving puzzles, and conversations with characters that gradually guide the player toward uncovering the truth about the Gordon family curse and its impact on later generations. Technically, it was a more modern production than the previous installment, with more current graphics matching the standards of the end of the decade and smoother character animations, but according to some players and reviews the horror atmosphere did not reach the intensity and cohesion of the 2003 original. The music and sound effects try to follow up on the dark tone of the first game and the atmosphere of an isolated manor, yet according to many the game lacks its gothic tightness and sense of constant threat.

The reception of Posel smrti 2 was more mixed than that of the first installment - the game was seen as a solid but less exceptional attempt to keep the brand alive after the change of development team and country of origin. For fans of the series, it remains an interesting addition to the Black Mirror story, even though it failed to recreate the extraordinary impression left years earlier by the 2003 Posel smrti, and in players' memory it thus remains rather in the shadow of the original.

**Why play it:** Fans of the series will enjoy it as an interesting addition to the Black Mirror story, even though in atmosphere and overall impression it doesn't reach the quality of the 2003 original.

pc-modern__nibiru-age-of-secrets.teaser: A reworked and graphically modernized version of the older Posel bohů with the same story.
pc-modern__nibiru-age-of-secrets.article:
**Nibiru: Posel bohů**, released abroad as NiBiRu: Age of Secrets, is an adventure game by studio Future Games representing a substantially reworked and graphically modernized version of the older title Posel bohů from the late nineties, with the story and characters preserved. The player takes on the role of archaeologist Martin Holan, who, while exploring a discovered German tunnel complex near Prague, comes across clues leading to the secret of the unknown planet Nibiru and an ancient conspiracy connected to it, reaching deep into humanity's past.

The gameplay rests on the classic adventure foundation - the player moves through dozens of locations divided into several chapters, collects and combines items in the inventory, and solves puzzles tied to the archaeological and mythological motifs of the story. The game features 3D animated characters, extensive dialogue with numerous supporting characters, and atmospheric visual effects and music that together create a mysterious, adventurous atmosphere reminiscent of popular archaeological thrillers and adventure films. Compared to the original version from the nineties, it represented a noticeable technical and visual leap that made the game accessible to an entirely new generation of players, without touching the story itself or its main characters. Underground complexes, ancient ruins, and secret laboratories form a varied range of settings that Martin Holan gradually works his way through during his investigation.

Nibiru: Posel bohů became one of Future Games studio's most commercially successful titles and was also released abroad under a foreign publisher, extending the reputation of the Czech adventure game scene far beyond the domestic market. To this day it is regarded as a quality representative of the archaeological-adventure genre and proof that a carefully executed remake of an older concept can work better with players and critics alike than the original from the late nineties.

**Why play it:** For fans of archaeological adventure games, it's a quality remake of an older concept that works better than the original from the late nineties and succeeded abroad as well.

pc-modern__command-and-conquer-generals.teaser: The series abandoned sci-fi and fantasy and moved the fighting to the present day; three distinct factions.
pc-modern__command-and-conquer-generals.article:
**Command & Conquer: Generals** abandoned the series' previous sci-fi and fantasy universe and moved the conflict between three superpowers into the present day: the United States, China, and the terrorist organization GLA pit armies against each other with markedly different gameplay philosophies. The Americans rely on expensive high-tech equipment, air strikes, and precision-guided munitions; China on masses of tanks and infantry backed by a nuclear package of bonuses and base power overcharging; GLA improvises with cheap but dangerous units, suicide bombers, vehicle hijacking, and chemical weapons. This asymmetric design gave each faction its own pace of play and became one of the most interesting and most discussed elements of the title.

Technically, it was the first installment in the series built on the fully three-dimensional SAGE engine, which enabled destructible environments, dynamic explosions, collapsing buildings, and detailed unit models - for its time it was a visually very impressive strategy game capable of displaying hundreds of units at once without major performance drops. The gameplay stayed true to the legacy of its predecessors: fast pace, emphasis on resource economy, base building, and mass battles, but newly supplemented with general's powers that were unlocked through progress in the campaign and online games, giving the series a light element of long-term progression between individual matches. Multiplayer was among the most played parts of the game and kept an active community around the title for years, later supported by the Zero Hour expansion.

Reception at the time was largely positive; players and reviewers praised the pace, graphics, and asymmetry of the factions, though there was also criticism over the sensitive theme of modern terrorism and Middle Eastern conflict coming so soon after the real events of the early 2000s. Generals influenced the direction real-time strategy games took in the middle of the decade, and it is still remembered today as one of the high points of the genre before its gradual decline in favor of other game styles. Even with the years that have passed, it offers straightforward, dynamic fun, and for fans of classic RTS games it remains a must-play, kept alive to this day by a loyal community of modders and online players.

**Why play it:** For fans of classic RTS games, it offers straightforward, dynamic fun and asymmetric factions still kept alive today by a loyal community of modders and online players.

pc-modern__command-and-conquer-3-tiberiu.teaser: A return to the series' sci-fi roots; the campaign is interspersed with live-action sequences featuring actors.
pc-modern__command-and-conquer-3-tiberiu.article:
**Command & Conquer 3: Tiberium Wars** returned the series to its sci-fi roots and picked up the story of the Tiberium universe after years during which it had been pushed aside by spin-off titles focused on other genres. The player once again finds themselves in the middle of a three-way conflict between the Global Defense Initiative, the Brotherhood of Nod, and the newly introduced alien faction Scrin, whose entry into the plot opened an entirely new dimension to the story about the origin of the mysterious, contaminating substance Tiberium and its cosmic origin. The campaigns of both human factions were interwoven with live-action sequences featuring actors, a return to the tradition fans of the series had loved since the nineties, which gave the story a cinematic, almost TV-series quality.

The gameplay built on the tried-and-tested foundation of base building, Tiberium harvesting, and mass battles, but the pace was even faster and more aggressive than in its predecessors - the developers openly admitted to being inspired by StarCraft's combat style, with an emphasis on constant action without delays or dead time. Each faction had a markedly different approach: GDI relied on robust technology and heavy weaponry, Nod on speed, stealth, and cheap expendable units supported by a tunnel network, while Scrin brought exotic, technologically superior units with their own mechanics, such as resource drain or teleportation. The SAGE graphics engine was significantly improved, and for its time the game offered a large, clear battlefield even during hectic battles with dozens of units on screen at once.

Reviewers and players alike received the title very positively, praising the return of a quality cinematic component, the balanced design of three distinct factions, and lively multiplayer, which for a long time was among the most active in the genre and was further developed by the Kane's Wrath expansion. Tiberium Wars is seen today as one of the last great high points of classic RTS games before the genre began to give way to other game styles, and for many fans it remains the definitive return to the Command & Conquer universe after the detours of previous years.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for the return of a quality cinematic component, balanced three-faction design, and lively multiplayer will find here the definitive return to the Command & Conquer universe.

pc-modern__command-and-conquer-red-alert.teaser: An absurd alternate cold war expanded with the Japanese Empire of the Rising Sun.
pc-modern__command-and-conquer-red-alert.article:
**Command & Conquer: Red Alert 3** took the alternate history of the cold war to an absurd but immensely entertaining level, adding a third side to the existing Allied and Soviet factions - the Japanese Empire of the Rising Sun with technologically advanced, transforming units. The story continues from previous installments in a branching, comic-book-exaggerated tone full of live-action cutscenes with film and TV stars, which gave the game the series' typical ironic humor and never took itself too seriously, even though the theme still involved battles for the fate of the world.

The game system introduced a novelty in the form of a naval component, which became a third domain on equal footing with ground and air units - many maps featured extensive bodies of water where separate battles took place and where amphibious units played a key role. A cooperative mode for two players going through one campaign together was also introduced, an unusual and very welcome feature for the RTS genre at the time, allowing the experience to be shared with a friend from start to finish. Each of the three factions had a markedly different visual and gameplay style: the Soviets relied on brute force, bears, and cheap units; the Allies on technology, mobility, and manipulation of time and gravity; the Empire on elegant, transforming machines combining multiple roles in a single unit as the situation required.

The game was valued especially for its entertainment value, humor, and accessibility - the pace was tailored even to less experienced strategy players, which prompted mixed reactions among hardcore fans of the series, who missed the complexity of the older installments and deeper strategic planning. Even so, thanks to its atmosphere, exaggeration, distinctive visual stylization, and cooperative mode, Red Alert 3 earned a place among the favorite strategy games of the end of the decade, and today it is remembered as a lighthearted, entertaining departure from the more serious tone of the Tiberium series, one embraced even by players who otherwise aren't close to the RTS genre.

**Why play it:** For players who appreciate humor, accessibility, and cooperative mode more than deep strategic complexity, it's an entertaining departure even for those otherwise not close to RTS games.

pc-modern__age-of-empires-iii.teaser: A strategy game about the colonization of the New World; the campaign follows the Black family across generations.
pc-modern__age-of-empires-iii.article:
**Age of Empires III** moved the famous strategy series into the era of colonial expansion between the 15th and 19th centuries, when European powers competed for dominance over the New World and its riches. The campaign followed the fictional Black family across generations and continents, from voyages of discovery through the colonization of America to the fight for independence, tying the individual missions together with a compelling long-term story that was fairly unusual for the series and gave it a more cinematic narrative dimension.

A major new feature was the home city system, which developed as the player progressed across individual matches and sent cards with bonuses, units, or resources to the battlefield - a mechanic linking games together and giving the series a light element of long-term progression that players knew more from other genres. The game also introduced native nations and European trading posts as neutral points of interest on the map, along with a new experience resource that was gathered instead of classic gold and encouraged active movement around the map. The graphics engine was very impressive for its time, with detailed lighting, destructible environments, dynamic weather, and smooth unit animation, making the game one of the technically most advanced strategy games of its era and a showcase of how far the genre could be pushed visually.

The game was received as a dignified and innovative continuation of the series; the graphical presentation, the atmosphere of the colonial era, and the home city system were praised in particular, though there were also reservations about slightly simplified micromanagement compared to the second installment. Age of Empires III remains to this day among the most played titles of the genre thanks to an active community and the The WarChiefs and The Asian Dynasties expansions, and its influence is visible in later strategy games that adopted similar meta-progression mechanics between individual players' matches.

**Why play it:** For fans of the genre, it offers the atmosphere of the colonial era, the home city system, and an active community around the The WarChiefs and The Asian Dynasties expansions.

pc-modern__age-of-empires-iv.teaser: A return to a medieval setting with gameplay inspired by the beloved second installment of the series.
pc-modern__age-of-empires-iv.article:
**Age of Empires IV**, after a long hiatus, returned to the historical, medieval setting that made the series famous, combining a modern graphics engine with gameplay that deliberately draws inspiration from the beloved second installment. Players choose from a range of civilizations, from England and France through the Mongols and the Rus to the Abbasid Caliphate and the Song dynasty, each with specific units, buildings, and bonuses reflecting its historical context, giving individual matches a distinct identity and forcing players to adapt their tactics according to the chosen nation and its unique units.

The game system builds on the tried-and-tested formula of settlement building, harvesting four basic resources, and advancing through the ages, but enriches it with more detailed siege mechanics, historically accurate tactics such as storming walls with ladders and siege towers, and documentary sequences between campaigns that bring real historical events closer and give the game an almost educational dimension. The campaigns guide players through key moments of the Middle Ages, from the Norman invasion of England through the Crusades to the rise of the Mongol Empire, with each one focusing on a different civilization and a different style of warfare. The graphics combine a stylized, legible look with modern lighting effects, and the game was designed to run well on a wide range of computers, from powerful gaming rigs to more modest configurations. Multiplayer and ranked games quickly became the backbone of an active community, supported by regular updates, new civilizations, and balance improvements responding to player feedback.

Critics and players alike praised the return to clear, balanced gameplay and the quality historical context, which gives the game an almost educational feel without sacrificing depth of strategic decision-making. Age of Empires IV is today considered a successful revival of the brand for a new generation of players as well as loyal fans, who find in it a balance between nostalgia for the classic installments and a modern take on the strategy genre, which in recent years had been giving way to other game styles.

**Why play it:** For a new generation of players as well as loyal fans, it offers clear, balanced gameplay and quality historical context without losing strategic depth.

pc-modern__age-of-empires-ii-definitive-.teaser: A remaster of one of the most beloved strategy games of all time; the same gameplay, a new look.
pc-modern__age-of-empires-ii-definitive-.article:
**Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition** is a modern remaster of one of the most beloved strategy games of all time, preserving the original gameplay virtually unchanged while giving it an entirely new high-resolution visual look, reworked musical recordings, and a range of under-the-hood quality improvements. The core principle remains the same as in 1999 – the player leads a civilization from a humble village through four historical ages to a mighty empire, gathering resources, building armies, and waging medieval battles full of siege engines, cavalry, archers, and infantry on carefully designed maps.

The edition brought not only a graphical upgrade but also new civilizations and campaigns that were missing from the original game and its expansions, broadening the historical scope to include regions such as Central Asia, Southeast Asia, and the Scandinavian north, along with their distinctive rulers and battles. In terms of gameplay, an improved hint system was added, along with modern netcode for multiplayer and full support for high resolutions and modern monitors, meaning the game runs smoothly on current hardware without the need for complicated compatibility tweaks. The classic emphasis on unit micromanagement, economic planning, rapid villager production, and map reading remains untouched, which is exactly what drew a generation of old fans back and brought in new players as well.

The edition was received very warmly, especially for how sensitively it preserved the essence of the original while removing the technical barriers that had prevented the older version from being played online and in tournaments in the modern era. Age of Empires II: Definitive Edition has become the official platform for a lively and active community, including a professional esports scene followable on streaming platforms, and is still considered one of the best-executed remastered strategy games, proving the timelessness of the original design from the late nineties.

**Why play:** Anyone who loves the classic Age of Empires II will appreciate how sensitively the edition preserved the essence of the original while also opening the game up to a modern online community and esports scene.

pc-modern__homeworld-deserts-of-kharak.teaser: A prequel to the Homeworld series that surprisingly sets its battles on the sands of the planet Kharak.
pc-modern__homeworld-deserts-of-kharak.article:
**Homeworld: Deserts of Kharak** is a prequel to the renowned space strategy series Homeworld, which surprisingly sets its action on land – on the scorching sands of the home planet Kharak, long before humanity set out for the stars. The player commands a mobile desert fleet led by the enormous tracked carrier Kapisi, around which all strategic operations take place, including resource gathering, research, and unit construction directly within the moving base that serves as the heart of the entire campaign.

Transferring the series from three-dimensional space to the two-dimensional surface of the desert was a bold design choice that preserved the typical emphasis on tactical command of unit groups, formations, and use of terrain, but fundamentally transformed the way space is handled – elevation differences and visibility across the dunes replaced the third dimension of space battles. The battlefield is vast and open, with dunes and valleys affecting visibility and maneuvering, while the entire campaign, featuring a gripping story about uncovering humanity's ancient past and mysterious artifacts, smoothly connects the individual missions into a coherent narrative. Visually, the game feels highly atmospheric, almost melancholic, thanks to the combination of desert landscape, dust storms, and industrial vehicle design, accompanied by music that carries on the series' characteristic orchestral sound.

Critics particularly praised the courage to bring a familiar brand into a new setting without losing its strategic soul, as well as the quality storytelling and dense atmosphere the game managed to build even without a space backdrop. Deserts of Kharak is today regarded as a successful and thoughtful entry point into the world of Homeworld for new players, and proof that the developers managed to create a fresh and distinctive strategic experience with respect for the series' legacy – one that holds up well even on its own, without knowledge of the later installments.

**Why play:** For both series fans and newcomers, it offers a fresh, thoughtful entry into the world of Homeworld – dense storytelling and strategic skill without a space backdrop, holding up well on its own.

pc-modern__homeworld-3.teaser: The return of the legendary space strategy series after years of waiting; commanding fleets in 3D space.
pc-modern__homeworld-3.article:
**Homeworld 3** continued the story of the legendary space strategy series after years of waiting, bringing players back to commanding massive fleets in open, three-dimensional space, where the angle of attack, altitude, and formations all matter. The story takes place generations after the previous installments, when the hyperspace network built by humanity begins to fail, and the player once again finds themselves at the center of a conflict that tests the legacy of the Kushan and their homeworld fleet, journeying across the galaxy in search of traces of an ancient civilization.

The gameplay remains true to the series' principle – units move and fight in all three dimensions, correctly reading the space and using formations is key, and fleet construction combines heavy capital ships with swarms of smaller fighters, bombers, and frigates that complement each other in combined arms. New to this installment are expansive maps with fixed, destructible structures, derelict wrecks, and tight spaces that force the player to think about ambush and reserve tactics differently than in the traditionally empty space plains of previous installments. The graphics engine delivered significantly more detailed ship models, dramatic lighting, and explosion effects that give the battles a cinematic impact, accompanied by music continuing the atmospheric, melancholic tone of the original games, which was always one of the strongest experiences for fans and remains a hallmark of the series even in the third installment.

Reception was more mixed than for previous entries in the series – some players praised the return to visually spectacular space battles and atmosphere, while others pointed out that the game was still being fine-tuned after release, particularly in terms of content and technical polish. Even so, Homeworld 3 once again reminded players why the series was valued for its unique approach to spatial strategy, and for fans of the original games it represents an anticipated, if debated, continuation of a long-dormant legacy that had only rarely returned to the space strategy genre.

**Why play:** For fans of the original games, it's an anticipated, if debated, continuation of a long-dormant legacy – visually spectacular battles, but with technical rough edges after launch.

pc-modern__homeworld-remastered-collecti.teaser: Reworked graphics for two cult classics of the Homeworld series; gameplay faithful to the originals.
pc-modern__homeworld-remastered-collecti.article:
**Homeworld Remastered Collection** brought back to modern PCs two key installments of the cult space strategy series, Homeworld and Homeworld 2, with reworked graphics, improved ship models, and a modern interface, but with gameplay faithful to the originals from the late nineties and early two-thousands. The collection allowed a new generation of players to discover the story of the Kushan, a wandering people searching for their lost home planet, which was praised at the time as one of the most ambitious sci-fi stories in the strategy genre.

The core gameplay system remained untouched – the player commands fleets in genuinely three-dimensional space, where altitude, angle of attack, and unit formations matter, which was utterly groundbreaking at the time of the original and to this day few strategy games match it for depth of spatial thinking. The remaster added higher-resolution textures, new ship models preserving the original design, reworked explosion and lighting effects, and also an updated multiplayer using modern network infrastructure, allowing the online community around the game to come back to life after years of silence. The audio and music, one of the strongest elements of the original games, were preserved in full glory and still shape the characteristic melancholic atmosphere of traveling through space that players remember to this day.

The game was received very positively as a sensitively executed return of a classic that respects the legacy of the originals while making them accessible on current hardware without the need to hunt down old drivers and compatible systems. Homeworld Remastered Collection is today the standard gateway for new players who want to discover the roots of spatial strategy, and a reminder of how innovative Relic's approach to three-dimensional fleet command was at the end of the nineties, long before similar ideas became common in the genre.

**Why play:** For new players wanting to discover the roots of spatial strategy, it's the standard, hassle-free gateway to a classic, with no need to hunt down old drivers and compatible systems.

pc-modern__halo-combat-evolved.teaser: Bungie's sci-fi FPS arrived on PC two years later; Master Chief versus the Covenant.
pc-modern__halo-combat-evolved.article:
**Halo: Combat Evolved** arrived on PC in 2003, two years after its original release on Xbox, bringing Bungie's classic to players without a console as well. The player takes on the role of Master Chief, a genetically enhanced soldier who, after the crash of the spaceship Pillar of Autumn, fights on the mysterious ring world Halo against the invading Covenant race and later against the far more dangerous threat of the parasitic Flood. The gameplay is built on a combination of infantry shooting, vehicle combat with the Warthog or Banshee, and tactical management of the limited endurance of a regenerating shield, which at the time represented a significant innovation compared to shooters of the era based on collecting health packs. The level design alternates between enclosed interiors and more expansive outdoor areas, where the player chooses whether to go around enemies, run them over with a vehicle, or shoot them up close.

The PC version, worked on by Gearbox Software, added mouse and keyboard support, higher-resolution textures and models, and multiplayer over LAN and the internet, which made the game a rewarding starting point for modding and competitive community play around classic maps like Blood Gulch. Martin O'Donnell's music, with its distinctive chant and dense weapon sound design, gave the levels an epic, almost mythic tone that contrasted with the open battlefields allowing different tactical approaches to the same situation, and with the gradually unfolding story of the ancient Forerunner civilization.

The period reception of the PC version was more mixed compared to the enthusiastic console response – some players criticized the delayed port and minor differences from the original, while others simply appreciated finally having the legendary title available on computer with solid technical quality. Looking back, Halo: Combat Evolved is considered one of the key titles that showed a console shooter could have depth comparable to the PC classics of the time such as Half-Life, and its influence on the design conventions of sci-fi action games, from regenerating shields to sandbox combat arenas, is still evident today.

**Why play:** For fans of sci-fi shooters, it's a key title whose influence on genre conventions – from regenerating shields to sandbox combat arenas – is still evident today.

pc-modern__halo-master-chief-collection.teaser: A collection bringing together six of Master Chief's campaigns, gradually ported by 343 Industries.
pc-modern__halo-master-chief-collection.article:
**Halo: The Master Chief Collection** came to PC in 2019 as a gradually expanded collection, ported for Steam and Windows Store by studio 343 Industries. The package gradually brought together the campaigns of Halo: Reach, Halo: Combat Evolved Anniversary, Halo 2: Anniversary, Halo 3, Halo 3: ODST, and Halo 4, so players can trace the entire arc of Master Chief's story and its side branches in one place, from the defense of the planet Reach through the war with the Covenant to the encounter with the Forerunners and the artificial intelligence Cortana. Each installment retains its own pace and mechanics, from the classic shield-and-grenade combat to the more advanced movement and armament of later entries, allowing players to observe how the series' design evolved over the years from simple arenas to more expansive battlefields.

The PC version was built with modern hardware in mind – it supports high frame rates, widescreen resolutions, reworked textures, and full mouse and keyboard support, a notable change in controls and shooting feel for a series previously associated exclusively with the gamepad. The collection also restored crossplay multiplayer, leaderboards, and an extensive selection of maps and game modes, making it a platform for the return of community tournaments and competitive play, appreciated especially by players returning to the older titles after years away. The sound and musical accompaniment of the individual installments, built on the motifs of Martin O'Donnell and his successors, remained untouched and continues to shape the series' characteristic epic atmosphere.

The PC release was received as a long-awaited step, although the gradual delivery of the individual campaigns and technical difficulties at launch sparked discussion about the pace of the porting process. Today, the Master Chief Collection is considered the most accessible way to trace the history of one of the most influential sci-fi series in the games industry on a computer, without the need to reach for old consoles.

**Why play:** For players without an old console, it's today the most convenient way to play through the complete campaigns across the entire Halo series on PC in one package.

pc-modern__gears-5.teaser: A third-person shooter with cover mechanics and a chainsaw bayonet; Kait's story on the planet Sera.
pc-modern__gears-5.article:
**Gears 5** was released in 2019 by The Coalition and arrived on PC simultaneously with Xbox as part of the Xbox Play Anywhere platform. The game continues the story of soldier Kait Diaz and her fellow COG faction fighters, who on the planet Sera face not only the alien Swarm threat but also Kait's personal search into her own past connected to the mysterious Locust faction. The core gameplay remains the proven cover system, tactical third-person firefights, and brutal melee attacks with the chainsaw bayonet built into the Lancer rifle, complemented by newly opened-up areas to explore on skiff and on foot, giving the player greater freedom in how they advance and in choosing tactics against hordes of enemies.

On PC, the game offered support for high resolution, widescreen monitors, and variable frame rates, with the graphics engine able to render expansive snowy and desert locations with striking depth of detail and effect density. The campaign can be played in co-op with up to three players, with the third character being the robot Jack, who brings his own support abilities, hacking of enemy technology, and a variable playstyle depending on equipment. The sound design of heavy weapons and music underscoring epic moments remain traditionally strong points of the series, and the atmosphere is further shaped by a darker, more introspective story tone compared to previous installments, complemented by side quests and collectibles.

Critics and players alike praised especially the expansion of gameplay with more open segments, the ability to choose mission order, and the depth of relationships between characters, though some changes sparked discussion among fans of the series' classic linear approach. Gears 5 established itself on PC as a fully-fledged alternative to the Xbox version and confirmed that the Gears of War brand has a firm place on computers even in the modern era full of competing action titles.

**Why play:** With more open missions, a choice of chapter order, and deeper character relationships, it's a fully-fledged choice for Gears of War fans and newcomers alike on PC.

pc-modern__gears-tactics.teaser: The brutal world of Gears of War turned into turn-based strategy; interrupting turns speeds up combat.
pc-modern__gears-tactics.article:
**Gears Tactics** was released in 2020, bringing the brutal world of Gears of War into turn-based strategy, developed by studio Splash Damage under the supervision of The Coalition. The story takes place before the events of the first game and follows veteran Gabe Diaz, father of later hero Kait, at a time when humanity on the planet Sera is desperately defending itself against a Locust invasion led by the giant monster Ukkon. The player assembles and upgrades a four-member squad of mercenaries, plans moves on dynamically generated battlefields, and must consider cover, position, and order of actions, while a system for interrupting enemy turns gives combat a faster pace than is typical for traditional representatives of the turn-based strategy genre.

On PC, the game presented itself as a fully-fledged tactical title built on the Unreal engine, which preserved the series' typical brutality and visual style – from the chainsaw bayonet built into the Lancer rifle to intricately rendered mechs and monsters. The interface was designed with precise mouse control in mind, easing unit micromanagement even in more demanding battles against stronger enemy variants and bosses with special abilities and combat phases. The music and sound effects carry the series' characteristic dense tone and, together with the dark setting of a ruined planet, help build an atmosphere of permanent threat and exhaustion from a long, seemingly endless war.

The game was received as a successful attempt to bring a familiar brand into a different genre, earning praise especially for the depth of unit equipment, the damage system, and the clarity of tactical decisions, even for players with no experience in the turn-based strategy genre. For fans of Gears of War as well as fans of turn-based strategies like XCOM, Gears Tactics presents an interesting combination of two gaming traditions that feels natural on PC thanks to precise mouse and keyboard controls and a clear user interface.

**Why play:** Fans of Gears of War as well as fans of turn-based strategies like XCOM will appreciate the precise mouse-and-keyboard controls and the clear tactical system of equipment and damage.

pc-modern__need-for-speed-underground.teaser: A major turn for the series toward nighttime street tuning; transforming the car became the defining feature of the game.
pc-modern__need-for-speed-underground.article:
**Need for Speed: Underground** was released on PC in 2003 and represented a major turn for the series, away from classic circuit racing toward the nighttime world of street tuning. The player works their way up the street ranking of cities, racing in circuit and sprint races, direct drag race duels, and drift challenges, investing the money earned into visual and performance upgrades for their car — new bumpers, spoilers, paint jobs, neon underglow, or a more powerful engine and turbo. This emphasis on personal identification with the car and its visible transformation became a defining feature of the series for a long time and inspired an entire wave of tuning games that tried to imitate a similar feeling on other platforms in the following years.

Technically, the PC version was built on an engine that was modern for its time, with effective motion blur at high speed and dense night lighting of the streets, giving the races a cinematic, underground character distinct from previous entries in the series set in daylight and on open circuits. The soundtrack, made up of electronic music and nu-metal, underscored the youthful, street atmosphere and became, for many players, an inseparable part of the experience even many years after the game's release. The AI of opponents and the drift physics were tuned more toward arcade than simulation, which made the game accessible to a wide audience regardless of experience with racing games.

Underground became a commercial and critical milestone that steered the series toward tuning themes for more than a decade and inspired a number of competing racing games as well as films connected to street racing and tuning subculture. Today it's seen as a nostalgic reminder of the era of tuning films and turn-of-the-millennium culture, even though its arcade gameplay feels simpler and more straightforward compared to later entries in the series than today's racing games.

**Why play it:** For lovers of turn-of-the-millennium tuning culture, this is a nostalgic visit to the game that kicked off the entire genre, even though today's players might be caught off guard by its arcade simplicity.

pc-modern__need-for-speed-carbon.teaser: A return to nighttime streets enriched with control over city districts and boss battles against gang leaders.
pc-modern__need-for-speed-carbon.article:
**Need for Speed: Carbon** was released in 2006 and on PC built on the success of Most Wanted with a return to nighttime streets, this time enriched with control over the territory of individual districts of the fictional city of Palmont City. The player leads their own crew, fights for control of canyon roads and city districts against rival gangs, and gradually faces the bosses of individual areas in intense duels on winding mountain roads, which became one of the most distinctive new features of this installment. Alongside classic body tuning, the game also introduced assembling a crew of wingmen with their own abilities, such as blocking opponents, navigation, or mechanical repair of the car on the fly, in the middle of a race against rivals and the police.

On PC, the game ran on an engine that, even a year later, retained cinematic handling of police chases, striking night lighting of the streets, and smooth transitions between driving and camera sequences when catching up to opponents on highways and in city streets. Canyon duels, with their own scoring system for proximity to the opponent and safely taking corners, brought a new adrenaline element to the series, distinct from straight sprints down flat streets and highways. The music selection again combined electronic and rock music and completed the nighttime, competitive atmosphere of streets full of rivals, police patrols, and competing gangs vying for their own territory.

Carbon was received as a solid, if less groundbreaking, sequel to the successful Most Wanted, with canyon races and the territory-control mechanic among the most frequently praised new features of this installment even among fans of the series. Within the series' history, Carbon remains remembered as the last major entry of the classic era of street tuning before the brand headed in a different direction, with a different setting and a different narrative tone, for several years.

**Why play it:** Fans of the series will enjoy the canyon races and territory-control mechanic as the last major entry of the classic era of Need for Speed street tuning.

pc-modern__need-for-speed-shift.teaser: A shift away from arcade toward racing simulation; the game distinguishes an aggressive and a precise driving style.
pc-modern__need-for-speed-shift.article:
**Need for Speed: Shift** was released in 2009 by the British studio Slightly Mad Studios and on PC marked a significant shift away from the arcade approach of previous entries toward racing simulation. The player works through a career across championship rankings, from lower car classes up to prototypes and formula cars, with the game tracking not only results but also driving style — distinguishing between an aggressive and a precise approach and unlocking different sponsors, more sophisticated tracks, and vehicle upgrades accordingly. The physics model placed greater emphasis on the car's weight, behavior during a skid, and body damage than in the series' previous arcade entries, requiring a more cautious and precise line through corners as well as better management of brakes and throttle on long straights.

On PC, the game offered support for steering wheels and other peripherals, adjustable difficulty of driving aids, and a technically elaborate body deformation system that could highlight the consequences of demanding driving both on and off the track after an impact with a barrier or an opponent. A distinctive feature was the camera simulating the physical jolts of the driver's head during impacts and fast maneuvers, meant to strengthen the sense of immersion in the cockpit and the intensity of high speed during races on well-known circuits. The engine sound design and licensed soundtrack spanning various genres rounded out the intense, adrenaline-fueled atmosphere of circuit races on real and fictional tracks around the world, from Europe to America.

Shift was received as a successful attempt to bring the series closer back to the simulation core of the genre and paved the way for the sequel Shift 2: Unleashed, released two years later. For fans of the series, it represented a pleasant change of pace after years of street tuning, and it is still remembered today as one of the technically most ambitious and most simulation-focused entries in Need for Speed of its time, even with the years of hindsight.

**Why play it:** For players craving a more simulation-focused experience than the series' classic entries, Shift offers a technically ambitious driving model that still holds up today.

pc-modern__need-for-speed-heat.teaser: The tuning series returns with a day/night cycle; legal races by day, illegal ones by night.
pc-modern__need-for-speed-heat.article:
**Need for Speed Heat** was released in 2019 under the direction of Ghost Games and on PC brought a return to tuning themes with a pronounced day-night cycle in the fictional city of Palm City, inspired by Miami. By day, the player drives legal circuit and sprint races for money needed to buy and upgrade cars, while by night they take part in illegal street races that bring reputation but also attract the attention of aggressive police willing to use harsher measures, including ramming vehicles and nighttime roadblocks in the streets. This division of day and night into two distinct game rhythms and economies was among the main new features of this installment and noticeably affected the risk level of individual activities.

Technically, the PC version used a more advanced version of the Frostbite engine, capable of rendering atmospheric transitions between sunset and neon-lit streets, as well as realistic reflections on painted bodywork in the rain on wet asphalt. The tuning system offered extensive options for visual and performance upgrades, and players could invest earned money and reputation separately, which supported different playstyles depending on the player's preference between caution and risk. A soundtrack made up of electronic and hip-hop music complemented the nighttime chases and underscored the contrast between safe daytime races and risky nighttime chases with police and rival racers from the area.

Heat was received as a successful return to the beloved tuning formula after previous entries that had moved away from the series' classic approach toward cinematic storytelling and a linear plot. The combination of daytime and nighttime activities and the emphasis on thrilling police chases placed it among the more popular entries of the series' last decade and showed that the tuning identity of Need for Speed still has a firm place with players today.

**Why play it:** The combination of daytime races and nighttime chases with the police makes it one of the most successful returns to the series' tuning identity in the past decade.

pc-modern__need-for-speed.teaser: A series reboot with an emphasis on cinematic storytelling; live-action footage blends with the racing.
pc-modern__need-for-speed.article:
**Need for Speed**, released in 2015 by Ghost Games, brought a reboot of the series to PC with a strong emphasis on cinematic storytelling and the theme of the underground street scene in the fictional city of Ventura Bay. The game blends nighttime driving sequences with live-action cinematic footage, in which the player's character meets a group of five charismatic characters representing different disciplines — drift, drag, circuit racing, police chases, and street-style driving. The player gradually builds a reputation with all five and thereby unlocks access to their specific challenges, sponsors, and rewards in the form of parts for tuning the vehicle fleet, as well as new bodies and accessories for individual cars.

On PC, the game ran exclusively at night, an unusual choice at the time that supported the atmosphere of damp, neon-lit streets full of reflections on painted bodywork and wet asphalt after rain. The tuning system built on the series' classic entries and allowed for extensive visual and performance modifications to cars, including visible transformations of the bodywork matching the individual player's chosen driving style and their favorite discipline out of the five on offer. A musical accompaniment made up mostly of electronic music, and collaborations with real figures from the tuning scene, reinforced the impression of a return to the underground roots of the series from the early 2000s and its first major entry from 2003.

Reception was mixed — players appreciated the return to the tuning identity and the attractive nighttime atmosphere, but the technical shortcomings of the PC version at launch and the requirement for a constant online connection, even outside multiplayer races against real opponents from around the world, were criticized. Today, this reboot is seen as a transitional but important step toward later entries such as Payback and Heat, which further built on its foundations and developed its ideas and game mechanics further in the following years.

**Why play it:** Due to its technical shortcomings at launch and the requirement for a constant connection, it's worth attention more as a transitional step toward the later entries Payback and Heat than as a standalone highlight of the series.

pc-modern__elder-scrolls-iii-morrowind.teaser: The sprawling world of Vvardenfell with no markers on the map; the character's path is entirely up to the player.
pc-modern__elder-scrolls-iii-morrowind.article:
**The Elder Scrolls III: Morrowind** transported players to the island of Vvardenfell, where, instead of a linear story, a sprawling world opens up, full of factions, supernatural cults, and ancient mythology. The game builds on a system of choice: the character develops according to what they actually do, skills grow through use, and the player can choose almost any path, from a wandering beggar to the leader of a vampire clan. The player can join one of the powerful Great Houses, such as Hlaalu, Redoran, or Telvanni, the Imperial Legion, the Mages Guild, or the secret brotherhood of the Morag Tong, and each choice opens up a different perspective on the island's politics and the conflict between the native Dunmer and the Empire. Quests offer no markers on the map, only verbal descriptions and orientation by the landscape, which felt unusual at the time and is something many players return to today for the feeling of genuine discovery.

Technically, this was a big leap from previous entries in the series, with a 3D world with changeable weather, time of day, and architecture that differed from region to region, from mushroom-like Telvanni houses to the volcanic wastelands around Red Mountain. The music was composed by Jeremy Soule, and its melancholic, ambient tones became an inseparable part of the atmosphere, as did the strange, alien aesthetic of Vvardenfell, sharply different from the later, more accessible entries in the series.

After release, the game gathered praise for its freedom and depth of systems, even though combat and the interface felt archaic. Morrowind significantly influenced the direction open-world RPGs later took, and even with the need for modernizing mods, it remains playable and cherished today for an atmosphere that no later Elder Scrolls entry has fully replicated. The game was later expanded by the Tribunal and Bloodmoon expansions, which added new areas and quest lines and became a standard part of later compilation releases, and even decades after release, community projects such as OpenMW or extensive graphical overhauls continue to extend its lifespan on modern PCs.

**Why play it:** Anyone longing for an atmosphere no later Elder Scrolls entry has fully replicated will appreciate Morrowind even with its archaic combat, especially with the help of community projects like OpenMW.

pc-modern__elder-scrolls-iv-oblivion.teaser: A struggle for the throne at the heart of the empire, Cyrodiil; Shivering Isles offered the domain of a mad god.
pc-modern__elder-scrolls-iv-oblivion.article:
**The Elder Scrolls IV: Oblivion** moved the series to the province of Cyrodiil, the heart of the empire, where the player, after a prologue in the sewers of the Imperial Palace, becomes the mover of fate deciding the outcome of the struggle for the throne after the assassination of the emperor. The main storyline about closing the gates to the plane of Oblivion and fighting the Mythic Dawn cult is just one of many layers, alongside which stand factions such as the Thieves Guild, the Dark Brotherhood, or the Arena, each with its own tone and morality. The Shivering Isles expansion then took the player into the bizarre domain of the mad god Sheogorath, which offered a markedly different visual and thematic atmosphere from the main game.

The game brought a visually much more civilized world than the desolate Vvardenfell, with forests, farms, and towns connected by roads, and the Radiant AI system, meant to give characters their own daily routines and decision-making. Combat was more accessible than in Morrowind, magic and alchemy allowed for wide experimentation, and the player could freely combine occupations without fixed classes, while voice acting, though of uneven quality, gave the world a new dimension. Jeremy Soule's music again was among the most distinctive elements of the atmosphere and, together with Havok physics technology for objects, gave the game an unusual tangibility for its time.

Oblivion became one of the most successful RPGs of its generation and, for many players, was the gateway into the entire series. It was often criticized for repetitive dungeons and a simplified level compared to its predecessor, but its openness, the humor of its side quests, and the breadth of its content still make it a popular target for the modding community and nostalgic returns today. The Knights of the Nine expansion added a shorter, standalone quest line with its own equipment and rewards. On PC, the game was also accompanied from the start by the official Construction Set, thanks to which an extensive modding community emerged, whose fixes and expansions keep the game playable even on modern hardware to this day.

**Why play it:** Thanks to its enormous amount of content and the extensive modding community it supported from the start with the official Construction Set, Oblivion remains a popular gateway into the series even today.

pc-modern__elder-scrolls-v-skyrim.teaser: The Dovahkiin mastering the Thu'um in snowy Skyrim; most of the content lies outside the main storyline.
pc-modern__elder-scrolls-v-skyrim.article:
**The Elder Scrolls V: Skyrim** placed the player in a northern province full of icy mountains, Viking-styled settlements, and dragon mythology, where the main character turns out to be the Dovahkiin, the Dragonborn capable of wielding the ancient magic of the Thu'um, the Shout. The conflict between the Imperial army and the rebel Stormcloaks forms the political backdrop, while the return of dragons to the world gives the main storyline an epic sweep, even though the vast majority of the content lies in side quests, factions such as the Companions, the Thieves Guild, or the Dark Brotherhood, and simple wandering through the landscape. The Dawnguard, Hearthfire, and Dragonborn expansions later added further quest lines, the ability to build and furnish your own house, and a trip to the island of Solstheim, known from previous entries in the series.

Bethesda simplified the character system compared to Oblivion, replacing classes with free combination of skills and introducing perk trees, which opened the game to a wider audience. Skyrim's world, from snow-covered peaks to dragon temples, is accompanied by music from Jeremy Soule, whose main theme became one of the most recognizable in game music altogether. On PC, the game was further popularized by an enormous modding scene that continues to expand its graphics, content, and mechanics far beyond the original scope, with Steam Workshop integration making mod installation easier even for less technically savvy players.

Skyrim became a phenomenon after release that transcended genre and platform, was repeatedly re-released in expanded and remastered versions, and ranks among the best-selling RPGs in history. Even with the years of hindsight, it remains for many players synonymous with the open-world fantasy RPG genre and an example of how strongly a modding community can extend the life of a single game. The game was gradually released in a remastered Special Edition and other updates that improved the graphics and brought mod support to consoles as well, keeping Skyrim in active player attention for more than a decade since its original release.

**Why play it:** For anyone looking for the definition of the open-world fantasy RPG, Skyrim, thanks to its remastered versions and endless modding support, remains a relevant choice even more than a decade after release.

pc-modern__fallout-4.teaser: Post-apocalyptic Boston with settlement building and power armor crafting; VATS remains faithful.
pc-modern__fallout-4.article:
**Fallout 4** dropped players into post-apocalyptic Boston and its surroundings, where the player, as the sole survivor of cryonic sleep in Vault 111, sets out to find their kidnapped son across the irradiated Commonwealth. This installment leaned more heavily into action-oriented combat and base-building, with the Settlement system letting players build and upgrade their own settlements, while weapon and armor crafting, including modular power armor, gave players an unprecedented degree of control over their gear. The series' signature VATS system for pausing combat and targeting specific enemy body parts remained intact, as did the companionship of the loyal dog Dogmeat and other companions with their own personal stories.

The game kept the series' characteristic dark humor and moral ambivalence, with factions such as the Brotherhood of Steel, the Institute, and the Minutemen offering different perspectives on rebuilding civilization. Visually and technically it was a significant step up from Fallout 3, with a smoother blend of RPG-shooter mechanics and a simplified dialogue wheel with four brief response options, which drew mixed reactions from fans of earlier entries used to more detailed dialogue trees. Period music from the radio and an ambient score, typical of the whole series, rounded out the atmosphere.

Fallout 4 became commercially very successful and expanded the series' player base thanks to more accessible combat and building, though some longtime fans missed the depth of decision-making and writing from earlier entries. To this day the game is supported by an extensive modding community on PC and remains one of the most-played titles of the genre on that platform, aided by tools for creating mods directly through Steam Workshop. Expansions like Far Harbor and Nuka-World later added further large areas and quest lines, giving the game new content long after release.

**Why play it:** More accessible combat, settlement building, and a huge modding community on Steam Workshop make it one of the most-played titles of the genre on PC to this day, especially with expansions like Far Harbor.

pc-modern__fallout-76.teaser: The first online Fallout; instead of people, just robots and holotapes in an irradiated Virginia.
pc-modern__fallout-76.article:
**Fallout 76** introduced the series for the first time as an online multiplayer game, set in West Virginia shortly after a nuclear war, where players, as residents of Vault 76, emerge into the irradiated world as the first ones tasked with rebuilding civilization. Instead of human NPCs, the player initially encounters mostly robots, holotapes, and traces of the past, a fundamental departure from the series' previous structure built around dialogue with characters. The game's map is based on the real geography of West Virginia and includes stylized versions of well-known landmarks, such as the New River Gorge Bridge or the Appalachian Mountains.

The game combines open-world exploration, crafting, C.A.M.P. base building, and survival elements with both PvP and cooperative play, to which factions and quests featuring human characters were later added through updates. The survival elements include tracking hunger, thirst, and radiation exposure, forcing players to regularly seek out supplies and safe places to rest. After release the game faced widespread criticism for technical issues, missing content, and the absence of NPCs, prompting the developers into long-term support and the gradual addition of content, including the paid Fallout 1st subscription. The atmosphere remained true to the series' style, with period music and an ironic take on 1950s American culture, though the emptiness of the world in the launch version initially undercut that tone.

Over the years, Fallout 76 transformed through fixes and expansions into a much more complete experience, and part of the community gave it a second chance, yet for many series fans it remains more of a spin-off than a full-fledged successor to the singleplayer entries. On PC it now functions as a stable online world with an active, if smaller, player base. The Wastelanders expansion was a key milestone, as it finally brought human characters with dialogue and branching quests into the world, moving the game closer to the series' traditional style.

**Why play it:** If you're looking for a stable online post-apocalyptic world with an active community, the game's much-improved state after the Wastelanders expansion is worth a second chance.

pc-modern__fallout-tactics-brotherhood-o.teaser: A branch off into turn-based tactics; you command a Brotherhood of Steel squad against mutants.
pc-modern__fallout-tactics-brotherhood-o.article:
**Fallout Tactics: Brotherhood of Steel** branched off from the isometric RPGs of the series' earlier entries toward turn-based tactical strategy, in which the player commands a Brotherhood of Steel squad fighting mutants, raiders, and other threats across the post-apocalyptic American Midwest. Instead of the free exploration and dialogue-driven decisions of classic Fallout games, the focus here is on selecting units, equipping them, and battlefield tactics, resembling the tactical strategy genre more than the series' RPG heritage. The game also let players choose between classic turn-based combat and a real-time-with-pause mode, and offered multiplayer missions for players who wanted to test their tactics against each other.

The game offered a wide range of weapons, armor, and unit special abilities, with missions tied together by a simple campaign and a base where the squad's equipment could be upgraded. The visual style and dark humor of the series were retained, albeit with less emphasis on written content and morally consequential decisions, a noticeable difference for fans of earlier entries. It was developed by Micro Forte, which attempted to offer a different take on the Fallout universe with this departure from Interplay's format.

Reception was mixed; players looking for a sequel to the classic RPG were often disappointed by the departure from the established style, while fans of turn-based strategy found solid enjoyment in the combat system. Today, Fallout Tactics is seen as a curious and somewhat underappreciated detour in the series' history, more of a side chapter than a key entry, but for those interested in tactical RPGs in a post-apocalyptic setting it remains an interesting experience. The game takes place in areas around the American Midwest and Chicago, further from California than the classic entries, giving it its own, less-explored part of the Fallout universe map.

**Why play it:** For those interested in tactical RPGs in a post-apocalyptic setting, rather than seekers of a direct sequel to classic Fallout, it offers an interesting and little-explored branch of the series.

pc-modern__gothic.teaser: A nameless convict must carve out a place among the camps in the magically sealed Colony.
pc-modern__gothic.article:
**Gothic** dropped the player into the closed world of the Colony, a penal territory sealed off by a magic barrier, where the nameless hero has been imprisoned and must earn his standing among three warring camps of prisoners. Instead of a traditional leveling system with readily available skills, the player must seek out teachers who will train them in combat techniques, spells, or crafts, giving character progression a noticeably more organic feel than most RPGs of its time. The three rival camps, the Old Camp of miners, the New Camp, and the Swamp Camp, have differing values and ways of surviving, and the player's decision about which one to join fundamentally shapes the rest of the game.

The world of the Colony is small but densely interconnected, with NPCs that have their own daily routines, and a palpable sense of danger, even weak enemies can be lethal to a low-level character. This unforgiving difficulty and physicality of combat, combined with a dark, raw atmosphere underscored by the music, gave the game from German studio Piranha Bytes a distinct identity, different from Western RPGs of the time. Technically it was a modest production, but thanks to the world design and depth of its systems it overcame its limitations. The game runs on the proprietary ZenGin engine, developed in-house by Piranha Bytes, which allowed for a detailed simulation of the environment and character behavior within what was then a modest budget.

Gothic became the founding title for the entire line of Piranha Bytes games and achieved cult status in Europe, especially in Germany, though it was initially less known outside it. It is still valued today for its atmosphere, skill-teaching system, and the sense of a truly dangerous and believable world, which inspired later open-world RPGs focused on simulation and unforgiving design. The success of the first game led to the sequel Gothic II, which continued the story of the Nameless Hero, and to a whole series of further Piranha Bytes games built on similar principles of world and progression.

**Why play it:** Anyone craving a truly dangerous and believable world with a thoughtful skill-teaching system will find in Gothic a founding title that inspired a whole generation of open-world RPGs.

pc-modern__divine-divinity.teaser: An isometric action RPG from Larian in the Diablo mold, but with a heavier focus on story and quests.
pc-modern__divine-divinity.article:
**Divine Divinity** is an isometric action RPG by Belgian studio Larian Studios, which dropped the player into a fantasy world threatened by a dark lord and his armies, while the main hero gradually uncovers their own connection to divine power. The game combined real-time action combat with a deep system of skills, spells, and items, similar to isometric RPGs of the Diablo type at the time, but with a significantly greater emphasis on written content, side quests, and exploration. The player could shape their character through a combination of melee combat, ranged attacks, and magic schools, while the main storyline gradually revealed the hero's connection to the deities and forces behind the world's conflict.

The game world was unusually densely packed with detail and humor, with the ability to interact with nearly every object and character, which was unusual for its time and showed the studio's ambition to go beyond genre conventions. The graphical style and music matched the standards of isometric RPGs of the era, but the sheer amount of content and the number of hidden details made it an unusually rich experience for an independent production of the time. The environment combined sprawling outdoor areas with elaborate underground dungeons and catacombs, which offered self-contained side stories and rewards separate from the main storyline.

Divine Divinity laid the foundation for the later Divinity series, which Larian Studios gradually developed all the way to the internationally acclaimed Original Sin titles. At the time of release it was a smaller, European production without major marketing, but among fans of isometric RPGs it earned respect for the depth of its systems and breadth of content, and in retrospect is seen as an important step on the studio's path to its later successes. The game was later re-released on digital distribution platforms, allowing a new generation of players who discovered the Divinity series only through its later, much better-known entries to come back to it.

**Why play it:** Fans of isometric RPGs and admirers of the later Divinity series alike will find it a lesser-known but surprisingly rich, systems-deep foundation of Larian's entire body of work.

pc-modern__divinity-original-sin-ii.teaser: A turn-based RPG with elemental interaction; choose between origin heroes like Ifan or Sebille.
pc-modern__divinity-original-sin-ii.article:
**Divinity: Original Sin II** expanded the turn-based tactics and elemental interaction system from the first game into a sprawling RPG, in which the player, or a party of up to four characters, chooses among several pre-made heroes or creates their own, each with a different standing in a world that is prejudiced against other races and factions. The story takes place in the Rivellon archipelago, where the player, as one of the so-called Sourcerers, tries to escape a church that considers their magic heresy, while resolving a conflict between divine powers. Among the pre-made heroes, known as origin characters, are the former mercenary Ifan ben-Mezd and the former slave Sebille, each with their own personal goal intertwined with the main story.

The combat system builds on combining elements, fire, water, electricity, or poison interact with one another, and players can use terrain to their tactical advantage, while the RPG system allows for extremely wide character customization. The game stands out for its sheer amount of reactivity, dialogues, quests, and battles can be resolved in dozens of different ways, and cooperative play among multiple players brings its own dynamic, as the group can even come into disagreement over how to proceed, with the game supporting cooperative play for up to four players at once. Visually and musically it was a significant step up from its predecessor, with fully voiced dialogue and more cinematic presentation.

Original Sin II received very positive reception after release and is considered one of the best-designed turn-based RPGs of its generation, which also influenced Larian Studios' later work, including their subsequent Baldur's Gate 3. For fans of classic, systemically deep RPGs it remains one of the genre's essential titles to this day. The game also features a standalone Game Master mode, which lets one player run the others like in a classic tabletop RPG and create custom scenarios directly within the game's engine.

**Why play it:** Anyone looking for a systemically deep turn-based RPG will still find in Original Sin II one of the genre's essential titles, including the unique Game Master mode for custom scenarios.

pc-modern__mass-effect-2.teaser: Assembling a team of specialists against the Collectors culminates in the legendary suicide mission.
pc-modern__mass-effect-2.article:
**Mass Effect 2** continued the story of Commander Shepard, who, following the events of the first game, finds themselves in the service of the mysterious organization Cerberus, tasked with assembling a team of specialists against a threat known as the Collectors, who are abducting entire human colonies. Compared to the first game, this entry simplified the RPG elements in favor of more action-oriented cover-based combat and focused heavily on building relationships with crew members, whose personal quests and loyalty directly affect the outcome of the final mission, nicknamed by fans the suicide mission, in which an insufficiently prepared team risks losing even key characters. The game allowed importing saved characters from the first game, so decisions from the previous game affected dialogue and available options in the sequel.

Structurally, this was a major shift for the series toward cinematic, dialogue-driven storytelling with a dialogue wheel and the Paragon and Renegade system, which allowed players to shape Shepard's morality and approach to resolving conflicts. The Mass Effect sci-fi world, full of different races, politics, and ethical dilemmas, took on a darker and more urgent tone in this entry, underscored by atmospheric music and cinematic direction of the conversations. With this installment, BioWare strengthened its focus on a connected story across the trilogy, where choices from the previous game affected the world in the sequel.

Mass Effect 2 is often cited as the peak of the trilogy thanks to its balanced mix of action, story, and attention to crew characters, and its final mission ranks among the most-cited moments in the genre. On PC the game benefited from more intuitive controls and improved graphics compared to the console versions, and it is still considered one of the most significant sci-fi RPG titles of its time. Expansions such as Lair of the Shadow Broker and Overlord later added further story missions and expanded the background of both supporting crew members and the Mass Effect universe itself.

**Why play it:** A balanced mix of action, story, and attention to crew characters makes it the peak of the trilogy and one of the most significant sci-fi RPG titles of its time, especially with expansions like Lair of the Shadow Broker.

pc-modern__dragon-age-inquisition.teaser: The first open-world Dragon Age; as leader of the Inquisition you face a rift unleashing demons.
pc-modern__dragon-age-inquisition.article:
**Dragon Age: Inquisition** returned BioWare's series to the sprawling fantasy world of Thedas, conceived for the first time as open-world, with several large regions to explore, while the player, as leader of the Inquisition, confronts a rift in reality unleashing demons and navigates intrigue among mages, templars, and noble factions. The player creates their own character from several races and classes and, over the course of the game, decides on political alliances that affect the balance of power across the entire continent. The party is joined by both returning and new characters, such as the storyteller Varric Tethras and former templar Cassandra Pentaghast, whose personal quests and relationships with the player's character are among the strongest parts of the game.

Combat combines more action-oriented direct control with a tactical top-down view that lets players pause the game and issue commands to individual party members, similar to previous entries in the series. The open world brought sprawling maps full of side quests, collectibles, and a camp system, a significant change compared to the more linear predecessors Origins and Dragon Age II, and one some players saw as an unnecessary padding of content at the expense of pacing. The game also included a cooperative multiplayer mode with its own separate characters and missions, apart from the main singleplayer campaign.
